# Frequently Asked Questions

_Banner Image: Chansons Piaf, Brel & Me - Musical Cabaret About France. Photo: Anastasia Comelli, Adelaide Fringe 2024_

## Poster Competition

Can I enter if I'm not from Australia?

Yes you can! We encourage entries from all over the world. Please note that the prize money will be paid in Australian dollars.

Can we add the Adelaide Fringe logo?

Yes you can add our logo, but it’s not compulsory. If you want to add the Adelaide Fringe logo, you can download it [**here**](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1SLhPwTHl3CwgI-CrEqccOPelxTfpa3Va?usp=drive_link).  
  
Please do not add any other logos (including Adelaide Fringe partners) to your poster.

Are there sizing guidelines or requirements for the poster competition?

Please design your poster in portrait. Preferable sizing is A3 (29.7cm x 42 cm).

Will you be announcing a shortlist like previous years or just a winner?

We will be doing a shortlist of entries in October and then will announce the winner.

## General

When is the next Adelaide Fringe?

Adelaide Fringe 2027 will be held from Friday 19 February to Sunday 21 March 2027. Where is Adelaide Fringe?

Adelaide Fringe takes place in more than 500 venues across South Australia, from the Adelaide CBD and suburbs, to regional areas spanning Whyalla in the West all the way over to Naracoorte in the East. As Adelaide Fringe is an open access festival, we do not run or operate these venues. Interested in registering a venue for Adelaide Fringe? Venue registrations will open in July/August. Find out more [here](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/as-a-venue). Where is my venue?

Unsure where your show is? Check out the [Venue map](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/fringetix/venues/map) to find your venue.  
  
You can also check out [The Garden of Unearthly Delights map here](https://www.gardenofunearthlydelights.com.au/map/) and [the Gluttony map here](https://gluttony.net.au/pages/map).

How can I stay in the loop?

Subscribe to the Fringe e-news for the full wrap up of what’s happening all year round.

[adelaidefringe.com.au/subscribe](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/subscribe)

Like us for event news and competitions

[facebook.com/ADLfringe](http://www.facebook.com/ADLfringe)

Follow us for on Blue Sky for the latest news and insights

[bsky.app/profile/adlfrin.ge](https://bsky.app/profile/adlfrin.ge)

Subscribe to the Fringe YouTube channel to see snippets of Fringe events

[youtube.com.au/adelaidefringeinc](http://www.youtube.com.au/adelaidefringeinc)

Find interesting ways to explore the program, behind the scenes pics and things that inspire us

[instagram.com/adlfringe/](https://instagram.com/adlfringe/)  
Connect with us on LinkedIn  
[linkedin.com/AdelaideFringe](https://www.linkedin.com/company/139585/admin/feed/posts/)  
Follow us on TikTok for fun video content  
[tiktok.com/@adlfringe](https://www.tiktok.com/@adlfringe)  
  

Use the #ADLfringe hashtag to tag your tweets, Instagram posts and Facebook posts and follow the hashtag to see what others are saying.

Where can I get a Fringe Guide?

The Official Fringe Guide will be avaible to pick up at Foodland stores across SA, as well as other venues and businesses. Check out the map to find your nearest Foodland store or BankSA branch [here](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/adelaide-fringe-guide).  
  
A digital copy of the 2026 Official Fringe Guide can be viewed [here](https://issuu.com/adelaidefringe/docs/2026_adelaide_fringe_official_guide).  
  
If you can't find a guide near you, please contact us by emailing [customerservice@adelaidefringe.com.au](mailto:customerservice@adelaidefringe.com.au)

Can I get into a venue without a ticket?

Most Fringe shows require a ticket for entry. Some venues may have areas accessible to the general public, without a ticket. However, for the full Fringe experience, we strongly encourage you to buy a ticket to the show of your choice and spend the evening at the venue enjoying the show (or shows!) food, wine and hospitality on offer at the venue.  
  
The best way to plan your night is to [view shows by Sessions](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/fringetix/sessions), you can filter by the date you want to go out, filter by the venue of your choice and browse all show by time.

Can you sponsor my event or donate to my fundraiser?

Unfortunately we are not able to sponsor your event, organisation or fundraiser. Adelaide Fringe is a not-for-profit that operates as an umbrella organisation for artists.

As an open-access festival, independent artists pay a fee to be registered in Adelaide Fringe, and use their own funds to stage their productions and/or run their venues. Although Adelaide Fringe retains a small servicing and transaction fee, the majority of the ticket sales income goes directly back to the artists.

Help! I’ve lost something at an Adelaide Fringe venue!

Adelaide Fringe is an open access festival. Every year, hundreds of venues all over the state register to be a part of Fringe; all of these venues are independently run. If you've lost something at a Fringe venue, you will need to contact that venue directly. Venue contact information can be found on our [here](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/fringetix/venues).

How do I apply to have a stall at next year’s Fringe?

Adelaide Fringe is an open access arts festival; we don’t run our own venues and, therefore, don’t coordinate any stalls for catering or goods for sale.

Venues make their own arrangements for stalls and catering. If you're interested in having a stall at a Fringe venue, you will need to contact that venue directly.

How do I enable location services for Safari on my Apple device?

To ensure our website can access your location information through Safari, follow these steps:  
  

1.  **Open your device's Settings app.**  
    Navigate to your home screen and tap on the "Settings" icon.
2.  **Scroll down and tap on "Privacy."**  
    Here, you'll find various privacy settings for your device.
3.  **Tap on "Location Services."**  
    Ensure that Location Services is turned on. If it's off, toggle the switch to enable it.
4.  **Scroll down to find "Safari Websites" and tap on it.**  
    This will show you the settings for websites accessed through Safari.
5.  **Adjust the permission to "While Using the App" or "Ask Next Time."**  
    This setting allows Safari to access your location when you are using the app or prompts you each time a website requests your location.
6.  **Return to our website and try the "Show Near You" feature again.**  
    A prompt should appear asking for location access; select "Allow" to proceed.

## Ticketing

I haven't received my tickets via email

If you have purchased tickets but don't receive a confirmation email, we recommend updating your email address to another one via your [account](https://staging.adelaidefringe.com.au/my-fringe/profile/edit). After updating your account and need your email confirmation resent, please email [customerservice@adelaidefringe.com.au](mailto:customerservice@adelaidefringe.com.au) with your Transaction ID.  
  
You can also access your tickets at anytime via [My Tickets](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/my-fringe/tickets). When can I buy tickets to Adelaide Fringe?

Tickets for 2026 Adelaide Fringe will be on sale from December 2025!   
  
For any other enquiries please send an email to **customerservice@adelaidefringe.com.au** or give us a call on **1300 621 255** and we will be happy to help. What are the different types of ticket?

 Want to know more about our ticket types? Head [**here**](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/ticket-types-explained).  Where is the Rundle Mall Box Office?

Tickets for 2026 Adelaide Fringe are now on sale!  
  
From 20 February 2026, you will be able to book tickets in-person at our Fringe Corner Box Office (located cnr Rundle St and East Tce).   
  

Can't get down to Fringe Corner? You can call one of our customer service team on **1300 621 255** to place your order over the phone. If you are looking for printed vouchers, merchandise or tickets, you can also use our 'Call and Collect' service and collect your order free of charge from HQ at 136 Frome Street, Adelaide. We are open 10:00am until 5:00pm Monday to Friday.

How do I get my tickets?

**Purchasing your tickets  
**You can purchase your tickets directly through our website or by calling **1300 621 255.** Alternatively, you can visit our Fringe Corner Box Office. Find out the opening hours [here](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/purchasing-tickets#fringetix-box-office).  
  

**Check your email!  
**Your order confirmation / tax invoice will be sent straight to your inbox and will contain a QR code – this is your e-ticket. All Fringe venues will accept your digital confirmation for proof of entry. If you have booked multiple seats or performances in one order, you will be admitted using the same e-ticket. Lumo Energy is the official Ticketing Partner for Adelaide Fringe.

  
**MyFringe Account**  
You can also access your e-ticket via your [MyFringe account](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/my-fringe/tickets).

What is the difference between Dress Circle and Stalls?

Stalls are ground level seating – the bottom tier of an auditorium, closest to the stage and the action!  
  

The Dress Circle is the balcony or mezzanine above the stalls.

Can I get an exchange or refund?

We may be able to offer exchanges for your tickets up to 24 hours before a performance, if you meet the terms and conditions for an exchange. All exchanges incur a $10 exchange fee. Fringe Fanatic Members benefit from free exchanges. We do **not** offer refunds on tickets, vouchers, memberships or merchandise.  
  

Please check out our refund and exchange policy in our [**terms and conditions**](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/terms-conditions-and-privacy-policy#exchange-policy) to find out more.  
  
If you believe you are eligible for an exchange, please contact our customer service team by calling **1300 621 255** who can process your payment over the phone. We cannot action exchanges via email or in person.

Are seats General Admission or Reserved?

Most Adelaide Fringe shows do not have allocated seating and therefore are general admission.   
  

If your show is at an allocated seating venue, the system will auto generate the next best available seat for you.  
  

Don't want to sit in the seat the system is generating you? Give us a call and we will do our best to give you the seat you are after!

Age Suitability

**How can I check the age suitability of a show so that I can take my children?  
**  

We will do our best to provide you with warnings about show content and age suitability, where the artist or presenter has passed that information onto us. Artists self-rate their shows, and as we are an open access festival, we can’t guarantee the content and suitability. Please use your discretion when determining suitability for your child, as there will be no exchanges or refunds on tickets purchased.  
  

**  
Audience Suitability Ratings**   
G - Suitable for all ages   
PG - Parental guidance recommended    
M - Recommended for audiences 15 years and over   
MA15+ - Restricted to 15 years and over   
18+ - Restricted to 18 years and over   
  

_All events are self-rated. Adelaide Fringe is not liable for any incorrect rating._ Do I need to buy a ticket for my child?

For most Adelaide Fringe shows, children aged 24 months and younger can attend Fringe events without a ticket, provided they do not take up a seat of their own. Some children's shows may require an infant (aged 24 months or younger) to have a ticket. This information will be provided on their show listing.  
  

I have a question about Accessibility

For information regarding access at Adelaide Fringe, please [**click here**](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/accessibility-bookings) or call our dedicated Accessibility line on **8100 2089**.  
  
For more information on Companion Card verification, please click [here](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/companion_cards).

General Troubleshooting

**My computer crashed while I was trying to book! How do I know if my payment went through?  
**Please contact Adelaide Fringe on **1300 621 255** and we can assist you. If your payment has not gone through, we’re happy to help you book your tickets over the phone. Please note, we do not offer refunds for duplicate bookings, so it's always best to check.  
  

**I can’t navigate to the Adelaide Fringe website. How long will it be down for?  
**It’s probably just a glitch and we’ll have everything back up and running very soon. In the meantime, please call Adelaide Fringe on **1300 621 255** and we can assist with your booking and/or enquiry.  
  

**I’m having trouble logging into my account online. Can you help?**  
Please call Adelaide Fringe on **1300 621 255** and we can have a look at why you might be having trouble logging in. We can also help you with any enquiries relating to your bookings. If you’ve already booked tickets to this Fringe and forgotten your password, you’ll need to have it reset and emailed to you, you can do this online.   
  

**I can’t browse on my mobile device. Is there a problem with the site or is it my phone?  
**Please call Adelaide Fringe on **1300 621 255** and we will assist with your booking and/or enquiry. To assist us in identifying and resolving problems please email **customerservice@adelaidefringe.com.au** with the details of the problem you experienced – including what make and model your mobile device is, what software version you are running, what you were doing at the time of the problem, and any screenshots you were able to capture.  
  

**I need to pay for my purchase using more than one voucher or credit card. Can I do this on the mobile site?  
**Split payments can only be made on our desktop website, or over the phone on **1300 621 255.  
**  

**My session timed out, but I need to buy lots of tickets—help!**  
Your cart will expire 15 minutes after you last updated your cart. We suggest you use the Fringe Planner tool to save a short list of your tickets while you are finding the shows you want, and then add them to your cart at the end. Alternatively, if you know the shows, dates, times and number of people attending, call Adelaide Fringe on **1300 621 255** or visit one of our outlets, and we’ll be able to assist you with the purchase.   
  

**I entered my payment details and nothing happened. How do I know if I’ve been charged or my tickets have been booked?  
**Please call Adelaide Fringe on **1300 621 255** as soon as you can and we will check if your payment has been processed and your tickets booked. Please don’t attempt to purchase again, as it may result in a double charge to your credit card, which we will not offer a refund for.  
  

**What does allocation exhausted mean?**   
Allocation exhausted means the show has sold out, or that the ticket type you have selected is no longer available. Must have been a popular choice! Don’t worry there are plenty of others for you to see.

Tell me about e-ticketing!

**What is an e-ticket?  
**An e-ticket (electronic ticket) is the digital equivalent of a paper ticket, and a more efficient method of ticket entry. A QR code will be displayed in your order confirmation which will be emailed to you after you purchase your tickets. Some venues will be scanning your QR code and other venues will continue to mark you off a door list or issue you with a raffle-style ticket once you get to the venue. Basically, your order confirmation / tax invoice email will suffice as your ticket and you won't need to queue for collection! Lumo Energy SA is the official Ticketing Partner for Adelaide Fringe.  
  

**Do I have to e-ticket?  
**Yes! In 2019, Adelaide Fringe introduced e-ticketing for the first time and each year we have continued to reduce the amount of physical tickets as we progress further into a digital world. In alignment with our sustainability practices, Adelaide Fringe will be a paperless festival with E-tickets being our standard option. Lumo Energy SA is the official Ticketing Partner for Adelaide Fringe.  
  
**What if I can’t access the emailed e-ticket?  
**You can access your QR code by logging into your MyFringe account and finding your QR code in the My Orders section of your account. You can also call us on **08 8100 2000** or email us at [customerservice@adelaidefringe.com.au](mailto:customerservice@adelaidefringe.com.au) and we can resend your email.  
  

**Am I able to transfer my e-ticket to a friend if I choose not to attend?  
**If so, how would I give/ transfer my ticket to my friend? You can forward your e-ticket on but keep in mind if you have purchased multiple tickets in one transaction, the QR code will allow anyone with the QR code entry to all shows in the transaction.  
  

**Will I need any form of identification with the e-ticket?  
**It is handy to carry your ID on you at all times. Venues will ask to sight your applicable form of ID if you have purchased a concession ticket and some venues will need to sight ID for their Liquor Licence requirements.  
  

**How fast is the transaction? How close to a show's start time can I book?  
**The transaction is instant. You can book up until the show starts at selected venues. This means that you can be standing at a venue and buy a ticket without having to visit a Box Office!  
  
There are some events that are durational in nature, that allow you to book after the start time.  
  

**Do you need to have a smartphone or can I use any device that has access to my emails?  
**You can use any device that has access to your email/screenshot of your order confirmation so that we can sight the booking information or QR code.  
  

**What if I delete my email or the email doesn't arrive?**   
Always check your junk folder if you don't think you have received an email from us. If the email doesn't arrive or you accidentally delete your email, never fear! You can access your QR code by logging into your MyFringe account and finding your QR code in the My Orders section of your account. You can also call us on 08 8100 2000 and we can resend your email.

## Fringe Membership

What is Fringe Membership?

It's Fringe... with benefits! Membership is your secret pass to the festival. You join thousands of fun-lovers and unlock exclusive perks, early access, and of course, a stack of discounted tickets.  
  
There are two tiers to choose from: the Fringe Mate ($35) for those who want to dip their toes in to the world of Fringe, and the Fringe Fanatic ($49) for maximum savings and maximum fun. How much does it cost?

Honestly, it pays for itself almost instantly! Both tiers are designed to stay affordable despite rising living costs so you don't have to miss out on those magical Fringe nights.  
  
Fringe Mate ($35) gets you 5 sets of 2for1 tickets.  
  
Fringe Fanatic ($49) loads you up with 10 sets of 2for1 tickets plus the exclusive perk of FREE exchanges on all tickets.  
  
If you run out of your allocation but still need your Fringe fix, both tiers offer an upgrade to an unlimited allocation for an additional fee. A Fringe Mate upgrade costs $30 and the Fringe Fanatic costs $20.  
_All transactions are subject to a $4.80 transaction fee._ How do I sign up as a member?

The easiest way to sign up as a member is right here on the Adelaide Fringe website! Seeing as you're already here, may as well, right? Click [**here**](https://www.adelaidefringe.com.au/fringe-membership) to sign in or create your MyFringe account and add a Fringe Membership to your cart. You can also sign up by calling us on (08) 8100 2000. I've signed up as a member. What now?

Congratulations on joining Fringe Membership!

Our memberships are digital and you can access all [**Member Offers**](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/deals) and benefits immediately after signing up via your MyFringe account. 

You will receive a welcome email explaining your membership and benefits. If you don’t see it, just double check your junk mail.

When does my membership expire?

All Fringe Memberships now run within a fixed term. Your membership can be purchased anytime between 1st November and closing night of the festival.  
  
Your main saving perk - the 2for1 tickets - is valid for the **festival season only** that it was purchased for, expiring on closing night,   
  
Your other member perks (exclusive news, offers, and competition giveaways) stick around much longer. All membership benefits expire on 31st October of the year following purchase. Does my Fringe Membership give me discounts/express entry to The Garden of Unearthly Delights or Gluttony?

Although the Garden of Unearthly Delights and Gluttony are synonymous with Fringe, they are run completely independently of Fringe!  
  
Like the hundreds of other wonderful venues around the state that host our Fringe goers (you!), we do not own or run them, and therefore cannot offer any discounts on their products.   
  
What you might know is that having a ticket to a show at The Garden or Gluttony WILL get you express entry into those respective venues. So go ahead and support the artists that make this festival come alive and get your tix for entry! What is the Fringe Member discount on Fringe tickets?

Fringe Members can book 2for1 tickets to any show participating in the membership offer. Fringe Fanatics can access up to 10 sets of 2for 1, while Fringe Mates can book up to 5 sets.   
  
Fringe Member 2for1 is now a selectable ticket type when you check out. This means you choose exactly which shows to apply your discount to, ensuring you maximise your savings.   
  
Used up all your sets? No drama! Both Fringe Fanatics and Mates can easily purchase an Unlimited 2for1 Upgrade for the rest of the season and keep the party going.  
  
Click [**here**](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/my-fringe/sign-in/new) to sign into your MyFringe account and get the most of your membership.   
  

Please note: the discount is deducted from the ticket price and excludes the transaction fee. Fringe Member tickets are a selectable ticket type. Once you redeem a 2for1 ticket offer to a specific event they cannot book another 2for1 ticket for that same event. For all other terms and conditions regarding Membership and the 2for1 ticket offer click [**here.  
**](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/terms-conditions-and-privacy-policy)  

Why are there changes to Fringe Fanatic benefits?

We get it - change can be annoying! We made a choice to adjust the Fanatic tier to protect the one thing our members love most: the affordable price.   
  
With rising operational costs, keeping the 2for1 tickets completely unlimited meant we would have had to hike the membership price for everyone. Instead, we decided to put a generous cap of 10 sets on the base Fanatic pass. This changes allows us to offer the same low price while still providing incredible value, plus Fanatics exclusively benefit from free exchanges on all tickets. For the super fans you can still upgrade to an unlimited allocation for a small additional fee. Do I get access to the Fringe Club by being a Fringe Member/Fringe Fanatic?

To ensure we are supporting our Fringe venues and the hospitality industry in the best way, Adelaide Fringe will no longer be operating the Fringe Club.   
 Through our Membership program we are working with participating venues to provide Members offers and deals to encourage a vibrant nightlife during Fringe and we encourage our Members to support our local hospitality industry.   
We hope you can understand this decision and can help support South Australian venues far and wide.  How do I prove I'm a member?

We are able to look you up at the Box Office when you purchase your tickets, or you can access your digital membership card in your MyFringe account. To do this, head to [**MyFringe**](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/my-fringe/membership) page in your MyFringe account and then click 'Show membership card'. Can I gift a membership to my family and friends?

You sure can! Your loved ones will be stoked with a year full of magical Fringe-ness, and hey, they might even shout you a discounted ticket or two to thank you for it.  
  

 Gift Memberships can be purchased [**here.**](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/shop/vouchers)

I've been gifted a membership! How do I redeem it?

Lucky you!

Redeem your Fringe Membership during the festival using the voucher code by calling 1300 621 255, or online. To redeem it online, simply click [**here**](http://adelaidefringe.com.au/fringe-membership), add the membership you want to your cart and then by provide the voucher code number at the checkout. Easy as pie! 

Please note: if you redeem your gift membership online, it will incur a $4.80 transaction fee. Do Fringe Member benefits apply to my partner and family as well?

During Fringe, you can buy up one lot of 2for1 tix per participating event (unless otherwise stipulated). So if you're going out for date night, you get two tickets for the price of one!

However, if your partner or other family members want to access **all** of the awesome member benefits, they'll need to purchase their own membership. How do I update my contact details?

Just log in to your [**MyFringe**](https://www.adelaidefringe.com.au/my-fringe/sign-in/new) account where you can update your billing and postal address details, add your DOB, change your password and also update your email account. Otherwise, give us a buzz on 08 8100 2000 and we'll help you out!  My Fringe Membership question isn't here! Who can I contact?

Hit up our Membership team by calling **08 8100 2088** during office hours, or by emailing [**membership@adelaidefringe.com.au  
**](mailto:membership@adelaidefringe.com.au)

## About Adelaide Fringe

_Adelaide Fringe acknowledges that we were not the first to walk this Country, we are all visitors to these Lands.  
  
We recognise First Nations peoples as the oldest living cultures in the world and acknowledge their deep spiritual and cultural connection to these Lands, Waters, Skies, Animals and Plants. They are our first Storytellers, first Educators, first Dancers, first Artists, first Custodians, and the first to welcome all to these Lands.  
  
We recognise Kauran Miyurna (Adelaide Plains People), who made the first footprints across Kaurna Yarta-ana (Lands on the Adelaide Plains and Hills regions). Adelaide Fringe acknowledges that the footprints we leave should tread lightly, following those who have cared for and walked this Country for more than 65,000 years.  
  
_**Adelaide Fringe 2027 will be held from 19 February to 21 March. See you there!**

#### _Who We Are_

Adelaide Fringe is a world-renowned, annual arts festival that celebrates culture, place and artists from across the globe. Bringing 8,000+ independent artists far and wide to South Australia, Adelaide Fringe is a destination for culture seekers in search for a hive of activity.  
  
For 66 years, Fringe's innovative and inclusive approach as an open access arts festival has made it a hub for emerging talent, as well as a destination for established artists from around the world. Among the audiences at Adelaide Fringe are hundreds of industry professionals from around the world, scouting for shows to book for future touring. This makes Adelaide Fringe a thriving marketplace for artists as well as a public facing festival.  
  
Adelaide Fringe is a not-for-profit organisation that celebrates diversity and encourages a social cohesion through cultural exchange, bringing people together and providing a platform for artists to share their unique perspectives with a global audience.  
  
Adelaide Fringe's popularity has led to significant growth in ticket sales year-on-year, making it Australia's biggest arts festival and must-visit destination for travellers seeking out cultural experiences.

[Meet the Fringe Team](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/team)

#### _What We Do_

Held over four weeks during February and March each year, Adelaide Fringe is an open access festival that welcomes anyone with an event to participate. 

  

What does open access mean? Fringe doesn't edit or limit the program, we don’t curate any events or run any venues, but there are hundreds of curators and venues that operate under the umbrella of Adelaide Fringe annually. Adelaide Fringe provides a platform to support this unique ecosystem. The Fringe team is a highly accessible support network available to artists, producers and venues year-round.

  

Adelaide Fringe supports those participating at the festival by providing a customer-friendly ticketing service, connecting artists with the various stakeholders to support their venture, and driving tourism to the state of South Australia to enjoy the magic of Fringe.

#### _How We Do It_

Presenting Adelaide Fringe is a $35 million activity each year, 13% of which is provided by the State Government. The remainder is earned through Partnerships, ticketing fees, registrations and other business activity, as well [Adelaide Fringe Foundation](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/adelaide-fringe-foundation), Adelaide Fringe's Foundation.  
  

$25.6 million in box office from ticket sales is paid out directly to artists and venues.

**2029** – 16 February to 18 March 

**2030** – 15 February to 17 March 

**2031** – 21 February to 23 March

### WE'RE EQUAL

Adelaide Fringe has joined [WE’RE EQUAL](https://www.equalopportunity.sa.gov.au/equal) - an initiative demonstrating the commitment of South Australian businesses and organisations to treat everyone equally.

  

Adelaide Fringe is the first major festival or event in South Australia to make this commitment to anti-discrimination.   
  
This means Adelaide Fringe will make sure their premises are a safe space for all people. Adelaide Fringe has zero tolerance for discrimination or disrespectful behaviours, whether to or by their customers, staff, or suppliers and contractors.

## Board   

![Person wearing glasses and a dark suit jacket against a light background.](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6NzI4NjAsInB1ciI6ImJsb2JfaWQifX0=--14d9d0353a1f6e4bfc64063dcf8b80046e0e5226/16.png) Paul Hamra

_Chair  
  
_Having trained as a journalist and working in public relations in Australia and the US, Paul established a national public relations company, Hamra Management, over 13 years which was sold to Young & Rubicam in 2000. Following this, in 2004, Paul established Solstice Media - a company creating Australian news products including, InDaily, InQueensland, The Lead, SALIFE, CityMag and The New Daily, through its subsidiary, Motion Publishing. Paul is also Publisher at The New Daily. The company operates out of Melbourne, Adelaide and Brisbane and employs over 90 people. In 2017 Paul was a finalist in The EY Entrepreneur of the Year Award.  
  
Paul was appointed deputy chair of Australia’s film agency, The Australian Film Commission (now Screen Australia) in 1999 for six years and was chair of The Fleurieu Art Prize for four years. Paul has also served as a Trustee of the Flinders Medical Centre Foundation, committee member of the SA Press Club and University of Adelaide Media Advisory Board.

![Smiling person with curly hair wearing a yellow blouse against a dark background.](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6NzI4NjEsInB1ciI6ImJsb2JfaWQifX0=--c627a95274bffba827cde9c3e3a4cd6755fe1dbe/21.png) Cathy Parker_Deputy Chair  
  
_With a broad ranging career, Cathy brings a mixed skill set spanning media, communications, policy, stakeholder engagement, government relations, politics, project delivery, crisis management, negotiation and events. After almost 15 years in broadcast journalism at the ABC and print at AAP, Cathy worked in a women’s NGO in Jakarta before taking up Comms and Media Management in SA Government.  
  
Cathy then moved into politics as an adviser to a Minister and a former Premier, which included, among others, advising on the Arts portfolio. Cathy has also worked in Stakeholder Engagement at the University of Adelaide, and she managed SA’s COVID-19 Vaccination Program during the pandemic. A career break as a food rescue driver with OzHarvest, she’s now back in Government as Director, Reform and Strategy. 

![Smiling person wearing a suit and tie against a black background.  19:](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6NzI4NjIsInB1ciI6ImJsb2JfaWQifX0=--7d5aab9ae83a0cbe60bee281564054fab4d1ceda/18.png) Jamie Dreckow

_Treasurer  
  
_Jamie Dreckow is a Partner in Audit & Assurance at Nexia Edwards Marshall, bringing deep experience across external audit, risk management, accounting system reviews, financial reporting and technical advice, International Financial Reporting Standards and corporate governance. Jamie works with organisations across finance, education, healthcare, wholesale and retail trade, manufacturing and community services, pairing rigorous assurance with practical insights.   
   
Beyond audit, Jamie is an experienced company secretary. He spent many years as company secretary for an ASX-listed entity, providing governance and financial guidance, and has served on audit committees for major SA Government departments in health and family services. Today, Jamie is Company Secretary for the Energy & Water Ombudsman (SA) Ltd and a member of the Department for Health and Wellbeing’s Audit and Risk Committee.

![Person wearing a suit jacket and white shirt against a neutral background.](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6NzI4NjMsInB1ciI6ImJsb2JfaWQifX0=--b66cddee6941b16cc0e58b4f657ce8b28ece79b2/17.png) David O'Loughlin

_Board Member  
_  
David O'Loughlin, CEO and Chair of kwp, has a rich background in creative leadership across the advertising and communications industry. Beginning with Young & Rubicam in Adelaide, he expanded his expertise internationally, working at BHO London on major brands like Walt Disney and Waitrose. He then led strategic planning at Dentsu Canada for Toyota, Lexus and Canon before moving to Ogilvy & Mather in Chicago to work on TD Ameritrade.  
  
Returning to Australia in 2002, David held senior roles at TBWA and Saatchi & Saatchi, driving strategy for high-profile clients including Sony, Lion Nathan and Toyota Australia. In 2011, he returned to South Australia to join the South Australian Tourism Commission, creating award-winning campaigns like Barossa - Be Consumed. David joined kwp in 2014 and now serves as a Director of multiple non-for-profit organisations, including the South Australian Business Chamber and the Jodi Lee Foundation.

![Smiling person with short dark hair against a bright white background.](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6NzI4NjQsInB1ciI6ImJsb2JfaWQifX0=--614fdbb105ed16315123b2c749051482828f806a/19.png) Emily Farrell

_Board Member  
  
_Born and raised in Adelaide, Emily earned a Bachelor of Laws from the University of Adelaide before moving to New York, where she lived and worked for six years. She began her time in New York working at a nonprofit legal advocacy organisation promoting justice in the workplace for women and caregivers, before moving to a leading U.S. immigration law firm. There, she worked with high-profile artists, designers, entrepreneurs, and entertainers on complex U.S. visa matters.  
  
While at university, she developed her love of theatre as a member of the Adelaide University Law Revue from 2014 to 2017, a passion she continues to nurture as a regular (and nostalgic) audience member.

![Person wearing glasses and a checkered blazer against a dark background.](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6NzI4NjUsInB1ciI6ImJsb2JfaWQifX0=--179300e9fa3e08aacb83c06e59859b7be9667f41/22.png) Matt Tarrant

_Board Member_  
  
Matt Tarrant is an internationally recognised magician, mentalist and producer with over 20 years of experience creating and touring independent productions across Australia and beyond. He is the founder of MindBlown Productions, a not-for-profit run Talent Agency. He has built a reputation as one of the most successful self-produced artists in the history of Adelaide Fringe, selling over 100,000 tickets and winning multiple awards, including Pick of the Fringe and People’s Choice.  
   
Matt has toured extensively with his original shows, worked with major brands globally, and mentored dozens of emerging performers in branding, marketing, and production. He is a passionate advocate for accessibility and sustainability in the arts. He also serves as a board member of the Adelaide Fringe Foundation, which supports grants for artists and ticket access for underrepresented communities.

![Smiling person with a read sweater standing in front o a grey background](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6NzI4MjQsInB1ciI6ImJsb2JfaWQifX0=--ca2849f48aa6056569b2c682900cf75ccbe88feb/Odette%20Pearson%20headshot.jpg) Odette Pearson

_Board Member_  
  
Odette Pearson is a Kuku Yalanji and Torres Strait Islander women from Far North Queensland who has lived on Kaurna Country for the last 13 years. Odette has worked as a health researcher at the South Australian Health and Medical Research Institute since 2013. Through research Odette informs health system and service improvements and supports self-determination of Aboriginal communities.   
  
Odette has been on the Fringe Board since 2018 and contributes her research skills and lived experience as an Aboriginal person to supporting and developing the fringe to be a diverse and thriving festival in South Australia, Australia and across the globe. Odette, her husband Steve and Golden Retriever Pipi, live in Adelaide. Their families live interstate (QLD & WA) and abroad (England) which sometimes has it benefits but overall, it means (or meant) a lot of travel and cherishing those moments.

![Smiling person wearing glasses and a dark jacket against a grey background.](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6NzI4NjYsInB1ciI6ImJsb2JfaWQifX0=--96ffda8f0f8f795236758f0023ea9263ada5dc5a/20.png) Van Tang_Board Member_  
  
Van is the CEO Asia Pacific for GHD Limited responsible for the strategic and transformational growth and performance of the region. She is a civil engineer (however having also graduated with an Arts degree) and over her career, Van has successfully led the delivery of high profile, complex and large projects across Australia and internationally. Having grown up in Adelaide, Van has enjoyed the vibrancy of the city, the Arts Community and firmly believes in the lasting benefits the Arts sector brings to all communities. She is a huge supporter of STEAM, and a strong advocate for delivering positive sustainable Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander outcomes.  
  
Van has held numerous positions on boards, advisory boards, subsidiary boards, and board committees across a range of sectors both private and public from education, the arts, social impact and business. 

![](https://d2cudhp9dwbqkd.cloudfront.net/release-20261019/assets/footer-desktop-bird-de72ad6a.png) ![](https://d2cudhp9dwbqkd.cloudfront.net/release-20261019/assets/footer-mobile-bird-ac9b40ef.png)

Adelaide Fringe acknowledges that we are visitors on Country nurtured by First Nations peoples for more than 65,000 years. We honour their enduring cultural and spiritual connection to these Lands, Waters and Skies, and recognise them as the first storytellers and custodians. We pay our respects to Kaurna Miyurna and all Elders past and present.

# Work at Adelaide Fringe

[Jump to current positions available](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/join-our-team#positions-available)

Adelaide Fringe employs a team of year round staff who work in marketing, partnerships, program operations, production, finance and ticketing. As we come closer to festival season, we also advertise a wide range of short-term contract roles and casual positions.

  

Adelaide  Fringe  supports  flexible  and  accessible  working  arrangements  for  all.  This  includes  people  with  a disability,  Aboriginal  and  Torres  Strait  Islanders,  culturally, religiously  and  linguistically  diverse  people,  young people, older people, women, and people who identify as gay, lesbian, bisexual, transgender, intersex or queer. We draw pride and strength from our diversity, remain open to new approaches and actively foster an inclusive workplace that celebrates the contribution made by all our people.  
  
  
**Benefits of working at Adelaide Fringe:**

*   1 week bonus (post) festival leave for year round staff (in addition to 4 weeks annual leave)
*   Employee Assistance Program
*   9 day working fortnight for year round staff
*   2 days of Volunteer Leave for all full year and seasonal salaried staff
*   Ongoing training opportunities
*   Staff development days and opportunities
*   An Adelaide Fringe Membership
*   Flexible work environment
*   An optional social calendar and events
*   Study leave.

### Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

Our [**Disability Access and Inclusion Plan**](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/accessibility-at-fringe#disability-access-and-inclusion-plan) outlines ways that Fringe is working to make workplaces, services and products more accessible and inclusive to people living with a disability.   
  

Our [**Reconciliation Action Plan**](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/reconciliation) outlines practical plans of action for Fringe to actively contribute to reconciliation, creating space to listen and celebrate Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander voices and support First Nations artists, staff and volunteers.   
  

Our [**Sustainability Action Plan**](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/sustainability) outlines a commitment to seven of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, to utilise Fringe’s influence to generate positive social and environmental change.   
  

Our [**Multicultural Inclusion Action Plan**](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/multicultural-inclusion) (in development) will outline actions to ensure the cultural diversity of South Australia is reflected in Fringe participation, and provide opportunities for refugee and migrant communities.

## [Customer Experience Assistant (Box Office)](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/join-our-team/customer-experience-assistant-box-office-26)

**Applications close:** 8 Nov 2026

Customer Experience Assistants are the public face of Adelaide Fringe, based in our Fringe operated box offices, and also providing box office and front of house support at venues and activations across the city. You’ll help audiences purchase tickets, get answers, and navigate the festival with confidence. Whether it’s a packed night at Fringe Corner or you’re scanning tickets at a quiet session in a small venue, you’ll help keep things running smoothly with a calm, friendly approach.

In this role, you’ll use Red61, Adelaide Fringe’s ticketing system, to handle sales, exchanges and refunds. You’ll also manage merchandise and materials, maintain your box office space, and help resolve issues on the spot with the support of your Supervisors and Coordinators. This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys being in the action, solving problems quickly, and making the festival a great experience for anyone who wants to be part of it.

## [Customer Experience Assistant (Fringe HQ)](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/join-our-team/customer-experience-assistant-fringe-hq-26)

**Applications close:** 8 Nov 2026

Customer Experience Assistants are the first point of contact for Adelaide Fringe audiences. Whether you are on the phones, replying to enquiries, or providing ad-hoc support at physical locations, you help make the Fringe experience seamless, friendly and stress-free. You’ll work in our call centre based at Fringe HQ, using Red61 to manage sales, process exchanges, and support access bookings. You’ll be part of a fast paced, supportive team that takes pride in clear communication, inclusive service and solving problems on the spot. You don’t need to know everything on day one. All we ask is you bring energy, initiative, and a genuine care for our customers. This is a great role for someone who thrives in live environments, enjoys connecting with people and is up for the organised chaos that comes with festival life.

## [Email Marketing Coordinator](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/join-our-team/crm-edm-coordinator)

**Applications close:** 2 Nov 2026

Email Marketing Coordinator supports the delivery and day-to-day coordination of Adelaide Fringe’s marketing communications and email marketing (eDM) activity, delivered through Salesforce Marketing Cloud. Working under the direction of the Marketing and Commercial Manager, this role coordinates the eDM content calendar, builds and maintains audience segmentation and automated customer journeys, and monitors performance across all Adelaide Fringe audiences, including patrons, artists, venues, partners and Adelaide Fringe Foundation donors and supporters.

This is a hands-on role, building personalised, data-driven marketing and donor communication journeys that improve engagement, retention and lifetime value, while maintaining database health, consent compliance and sender reputation. The role works closely with the Marketing and Commercial Manager, Head of Marketing and Adelaide Fringe Foundation team to ensure marketing and Foundation CRM and eDM activity is coordinated and delivered in line with broader marketing, ticketing and fundraising objectives.

## [Event & Production Crew](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/join-our-team/event-production-crew)

**Applications close:** 8 Nov 2026

Working under the direction of the Events, Production & Volunteer Lead and Events & Production Coordinator, the Casual Event & Production Crew support the delivery of Adelaide Fringe-managed events, activations and festival infrastructure.

This hands-on role assists with the transportation, installation, maintenance and pack-down of event equipment and temporary festival sites, as well as providing on-the-ground operational support during Adelaide Fringe events. The role requires a proactive attitude, the ability to work collaboratively within a team, and a willingness to undertake a variety of physical tasks in a fast-paced event environment.

As this is a casual position, shifts will vary depending on operational requirements and may include early mornings, evenings, weekends and public holidays throughout the festival period.

### Partner with WA’s Most Attended Arts Festival

Outranking major sporting and cultural events across WA, FRINGE WORLD is where brands come to life. Connecting with a diverse and engaged audience, with ticket buyers from every postcode in metro Perth, FRINGE WORLD offers brands access to almost every audience imaginable.

[Get in Touch](https://form.asana.com/?k=5YZRG6HgJK1IDt1dWRkPfA&d=94244993155250)

#### Big crowds. Big vibes. Big opportunities for your brand.

#### **Be seen by over 500,000 attendees, unlock $51M+ in media value, and deliver unforgettable brand moments at FRINGE WORLD Festival.** 

### Why FRINGE WORLD?

Every summer since 2012, FRINGE WORLD has lit up the city. We deliver big crowds, bold vibes, and even bigger opportunities for brands ready to show up in creative, meaningful ways.   
  
FRINGE WORLD is a festival that blends community spirit with unforgettable experiences.

_Each season, artists, audiences and stories come together on Whadjuk Noongar boodja to bring FRINGE WORLD to life. We honour the story-telling and art-making at the heart of First Nations’ cultures and the enrichment it gives to the lives of all Australians._ 

  

_We acknowledge the Whadjuk people of the Noongar Nation as the traditional custodians of this land, pay our respects to Elders past and present, and honour their ongoing connection to Country._

### What is FRINGE WORLD?

FRINGE WORLD is a massively popular annual festival held in Perth that is enjoyed by hundreds of thousands of people.  
  

The incredible array of entertainment in FRINGE WORLD offers something for everyone; from comedy, music and musicals, circus and much more. Plus, ticket prices are great value so you can enjoy multiple shows in one night out.  
  

The 2026 Festival brought together more than 3000 artists and nearly 500,000 attendees across 599 events. Over $10.9 million was spent at the Box Office, $8.34 million of which was paid to FRINGE WORLD Artists and Venues.

![People roaming The Woodside Pleasure Garden](https://fringeworld.com.au/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6NSwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--be96ec50a089397afef53cd47b819cf523319730/People%20roaming%20The%20Woodside%20Pleasure%20Garden)

The Pleasure Garden. Photo by Miles Noel.

### What shows are in the Festival?

The Festival operates under an open-access model, enabling events to register as part of the Festival. Embracing this format allows the Festival to host an extensive selection of shows spanning many artforms and genres. The open-access Fringe model is popular with artists, often offering a pathway into the industry, and access to audiences.  
  

As the Festival is open-access, the shows presented may not reflect the views, beliefs or opinions of ARTRAGE (the Festival organiser) or its affiliates; and are not intended to malign any religion, cultural group, club, organisation, company or individual.    
  

Find out more about [participating in FRINGE WORLD](https://fringeworld.com.au/participate) as an artist or venue. 

![The Pleasure Garden entrance.](https://fringeworld.com.au/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6NiwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--1ec71a5d266b38a13e4b5881f42e47c347a65bbd/The%20Pleasure%20Garden%20entrance.)

The Pleasure Garden. Photo by Miles Noel.

### Who presents FRINGE WORLD?

FRINGE WORLD Festival is presented by [ARTRAGE Inc](https://www.artrage.com.au/), a not-for-profit registered charity that is one of the oldest arts organisations in WA.   
  

Alongside FRINGE WORLD Festival, ARTRAGE also currently produces [Rooftop Movies](https://www.rooftopmovies.com.au/) (est. 2012).   
  

The ARTRAGE Strategic Plan and its organisational Purpose, Vision, Mission and The Way We Work statement inform how the Festival is delivered.  
   
**ARTRAGE Purpose:** To bring artists and audiences together to share in extraordinary experiences.  
  

**ARTRAGE Vision:** The arts are embraced as an integral cultural driver.  
  

**ARTRAGE Mission:** To create spaces where creativity thrives and where artists and audiences connect. 

### Impact Report

The producer of FRINGE WORLD, ARTRAGE Inc, annually releases an Impact Report that reveals the massive benefits the Festival delivers to the Western Australian community.  
  

[Click here](https://artrage.com.au/our-impact) to read the latest ARTRAGE Impact Report. 

### More information

 Visit the [FAQ page](https://fringeworld.com.au/faq) for more information about FRINGE WORLD.

## About The Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association

The Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association (MRBTA) is a not-for-profit organisation, with more than 700 members and 150 staff across the Margaret River region.

The MRBTA operates four caves, two lighthouses, an adventure ropes course, a raptor wildlife centre, and manages airport ground handling.

The funds generated by MRBTA allows it to enhance sustainable tourism by marketing the region to visitors, undertaking visitor servicing, providing high quality attractions and investing in the conservation and preservation of its natural and heritage assets, with a resulting contribution to the economy of the region.

For further information, please visit [mrbta.com](https://margaretriverbusseltontourismassociation.createsend1.com/t/i-l-cznty-l-i/).

# Western Australia Margaret River Pro

![pin](https://www.margaretriver.com/wp-content/themes/river/assets/images/icons/icn-blue-pin.svg)

[Surfers Point, Surfers Point Rd, Prevelly WA 6285, Australia](https://www.margaretriver.com/things-to-do/attractions/beaches/surfers-point/)

![calendar](https://www.margaretriver.com/wp-content/themes/river/assets/images/icons/icn-blue-calendar.svg)

Thursday, 16th April 2026 - Sunday, 26th April 2026  

* * *

Description

**The _Western Australia Margaret River Pro_ is one of only three Australian events on the prestigious World Surf League (WSL) World Championship Tour (CT), with the world’s top professional surfers travelling to Margaret River to compete.**

The 2026 tour returns to Margaret River for 10 days from 16 April as stop number two on the championship tour schedule.

The 2026 season will mark the 50th year of professional surfing, featuring 12 stops across nine countries, including a refreshed format, an expanded women’s field, and an all-in Pipe Masters finale. As one of the sport’s most powerful and unpredictable waves, Margaret River continues to play a key role in shaping the World Title race.

Spectators can watch all the action live and free at [Surfers Point](https://www.margaretriver.com/members/surfers-point/), with the bulk of the competition taking place on Main Break and The Box.

The event hub has a true festival vibe with big screens showing replays, expert commentary, food trucks and merchandise stands. But perhaps best of all, young hopefuls can get up close and personal with their surfing stars who take their time after each heat to chat to groms who line the walkway to collect autographs and selfies.

**Important information**

*   **When will the competition be ‘on’?:**  Each morning, the WSL decides when to run the event, based on the forecast and live surf conditions. To check if the event is ‘on’, ‘off’ or ‘on hold’ go to [Instagram @wsl](https://www.instagram.com/wsl/) or sign up for updates through the WSL app.  The surfing action will take place between 7.00am – 5.00pm during ‘on’ days and entry is free to all attendees. The event site is still accessible even when the event isn’t running, but site activations will be set around the competition schedule.
*   **Parking:** Midweek parking will be available at [Riflebutts Reserve](https://www.margaretriver.com/things-to-do/attractions/mazes-parks-gardens/riflebutts-reserve/) on surfing competition days, midweek. Weekend parking will only be available at McLeods Paddock (opposite Margaret River Golf Club) to catch the shuttle bus to Surfers Point.  The Surfers Point car park will **not** be accessible during the event build, activation or pack-down.
*   **Shuttle buses:** Will run on the weekends – leaving from near the [Margaret River Golf Club](https://www.margaretriver.com/things-to-do/attractions/golf/margaret-river-golf-club/) to [Surfers Point.](https://www.margaretriver.com/things-to-do/attractions/beaches/surfers-point/) Buses will run from 8am to 4pm daily depending on how the competition is running. There is no time schedule for buses as they operate on rotation based on competition schedule.
*   **Bike racks:**  There will be extra racking for bikes and scooters on site.
*   **Dogs:** No dogs are allowed at the event site.
*   **Rivermouth access****:** Pedestrians will be able to access the Rivermouth at all times during the event. Vehicles can access the Rivermouth Beach carpark using Rivermouth Road on days the competition is not running.
*   **Accessibility**: There is a designated parking bays (ACROD permits) with accessibility paths of travel and toilets at the event site. Assistance animals are welcome at the event and on the shuttle bus, with identification.

**More about the tour**

The 2026 season is primed to deliver a thrilling World Title race from start to finish, offering a wide array of opportunity for the world’s best surfers to elevate the sport to new heights. Covering nine countries across nine months, the 12 stops offer a diverse mix of surf, from the heavy barrels of waves like Pipeline, Cloudbreak, and Teahupo’o, to high-performance hotspots like Lower Trestles, Punta Roca, and Abu Dhabi. Added to the perfection of Snapper Rocks and Jeffreys Bay is the wild unpredictability of Margaret River, Portugal, and Saquarema, with the storied history of Bells Beach kicking it all off.

The Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association is a self-funded, not-for-profit, incorporated association with over 50 years’ experience in supporting the Margaret River Region to thrive through tourism. ​For further information, please visit [mrbta.com](https://mrbta.com/).

# Visitor Information Centres

Plan and book your holiday with the Margaret River Region local experts

The region’s visitor centres are located at [Busselton](https://www.margaretriver.com/members/busselton-visitor-centre/) and [Margaret River](https://www.margaretriver.com/members/margaret-river-visitor-centre/) and service the region from Busselton to Augusta.

As the local experts, we offer comprehensive information, booking services and advice. Trust us to help you find the best surf breaks, camp sites, top restaurants, award-winning wineries, fishing spots and majestic walking trails. We are available to help 7 days per week in person, by phone and [email](mailto:welcome@margaretriver.com).

![Award](https://media.margaretriver.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Untitled-3413-x-1920-px-1-scaled.jpg)

2025 Silver Award Winner for Visitor Information Services

Margaret River Region visitor centre staff all live locally and between us we’ve been everywhere and seen everything. We are happy to offer free advice on just about any topic relating to the region, and if we don’t know the answer to a question, we find someone who does. Mostly, we focus on delivering the following really well:

*   [Accommodation](https://www.margaretriver.com/plan-your-trip/accommodation/) bookings
*   [Tour](https://www.margaretriver.com/plan-your-trip/tours-experiences/) bookings
*   [Transport](https://www.margaretriver.com/plan-your-trip/getting-here-local-transport/) bookings
*   Group accommodation bookings for [weddings](https://www.margaretriver.com/plan-your-trip/weddings-special-occasions/), conferences, birthdays, family gatherings, sporting events and other special occasions
*   Free regional [map and guide](https://www.margaretriver.com/maps-guides-itineraries/)
*   Itinerary planning & travel packages
*   Detailed maps and guides available for purchase
*   Great shopping: local produce, gifts, clothing, homewares, souvenirs
*   Accommodation and experience gift vouchers
*   Information and tickets for local [events](https://www.margaretriver.com/events/)
*   Information on local weather and travel conditions
*   Safety and security information
*   Information on ATMs, public toilets, laundries, employment agencies – you name it!

# Perth Festival | A Celebration of Perth Arts

### 5 - 28 Feb 2027

## Just announced...

# Empty heading

![](https://cms.perthfestival.com.au/media/kdubti31/rohtko_dailestheatre_latvia-3.jpg?anchor=center&mode=crop&width=800&height=442&quality=90)

Art. Money. Fakery.

## ROHTKO

European blockbuster theatre has arrived. Trailblazing Polish director Łukasz Twarkowski fuses theatre, tech and live cinema to create a monumental, technically dazzling show unlike anything seen before in Australia. _ROHTKO_ is a high-octane theatrical thriller about art, money, truth and fakery. His Majesty’s Theatre 5 – 13 Feb.

[

ROHTKO



](https://www.perthfestival.com.au/program/season-2027/rohtko)

![](https://cms.perthfestival.com.au/media/jhth4dtx/lead-press-shot-resized.png?anchor=center&mode=crop&width=800&height=442&quality=90)

East Perth Power Station

## The Avalanches

Take a cosmic joyride through The Avalanches' universe on our final night at the Power Station. These sampling pioneers bring their latest release _No Bad Memories_, a nostalgia trip through the magical and insidious sounds that stay with you forever. East Perth Power Station Mainstage Sat 27 and Sun 28 Feb.

[

The Avalanches



](https://www.perthfestival.com.au/program/season-2027/the-avalanches)

![A staged scene with multiple figures in black attire and crowns, arranged in rows against a yellow backdrop, some saluting.](https://cms.perthfestival.com.au/media/mtifx22p/f37c3b85-b9b9-44f7-95ba-897dcd24e495.jpg?anchor=center&mode=crop&width=800&height=442&quality=90)

It's Opera, transformed

## Operation:Orfeo

Opera stripped back and radically reimagined. Created by Denmark’s legendary Hotel Pro Forma, _Operation:Orfeo_ is part opera, part visual artwork. Descend into the Underworld from 25 – 27 Feb with this masterpiece of astonishing precision and breathtaking beauty.

[

Operation:Orfeo



](https://www.perthfestival.com.au/program/season-2027/operationorfeo)

![](https://cms.perthfestival.com.au/media/5drgjkib/foy-vance-press-shot-tile.jpg?rxy=0.5,0.5&width=800&height=442&quality=90)

## Foy Vance and The Paper Kites

A night of folk, blues and soul from one of the best in the business. Northern Irish troubadour Foy Vance delivers his unmatched musicianship and all the stories that come with it. Joined by Australian indie folk rock heavyweights The Paper Kites. East Perth Power Station Mainstage Sunday 7 February.

[

Foy Vance and The Paper Kites



](https://www.perthfestival.com.au/program/season-2027/foy-vance-and-the-paper-kites)

![a large crowd of people at a concert](https://cms.perthfestival.com.au/media/gb2njpi1/_bp_0147_webres.jpg?anchor=center&mode=crop&width=800&height=442&quality=90)

Get more from your Festival

## Festival Club on sale now

Our 2027 program drops 29 October! Get priority access to the hottest tickets, exclusive offers, insider updates and invitations to special Festival moments. 

Join the club. Get more from your Festival. 

[

Find out more!



](https://www.perthfestival.com.au/festival-club)

![A hand pours sparkling wine into a glass, with bottles and candles in the background, creating a festive atmosphere.](https://cms.perthfestival.com.au/media/r3jniibf/riftphotography-perthfestivalmoktarvipevent-45.jpg?anchor=center&mode=crop&width=800&height=442&quality=90)

Book our Premium Hospitality Packages

## Let us host you in style!

Align your brand with one of the world’s most renowned cultural festivals. Perth Festival is a prestigious, internationally acclaimed event that draws passionate audiences and creative leaders from across Australia and beyond. Don’t just attend – celebrate, entertain, and make memories that last!

Book a Premium Hospitality Package at one of our unique venues and we'll host you in style at Perth Festival 2027. 

[

Download the info pack



](https://www.perthfestival.com.au/media/m4adoopz/perthfest_premiumhospitalitypackages.pdf)

![A vibrant outdoor festival scene with a lion dance performance, colorful lights, and a large crowd enjoying the event.](https://cms.perthfestival.com.au/media/5szpdgqu/redlanterns_casamusica_epps_pf26_crjessicawyldphotography_lowres_030.jpg?anchor=center&mode=crop&width=800&height=442&quality=90)

Donate today.

## Love Perth Festival?

Did you know that ticket sales account for just 17% of what's needed to bring the Festival to life? We need your financial support to continue to share unforgettable, bold and boundary-pushing Festival experiences for everyone. 

If you've discovered a new favourite artist, seen something unforgettable or found yourself looking at the world a little differently because of Perth Festival, consider making a tax-deductible donation.

# Work with us

Explore exciting career and volunteer opportunities at Perth Festival.

Join our team and be part of Western Australia's premier arts festival. Discover current job openings, internships, and volunteer roles, and learn how you can contribute to delivering an unforgettable Festival experience.

Whether you're passionate about the arts, event production, or community engagement, find out how to work with us.

![Five women pose together in front of a bright yellow backdrop for the Perth Festival, showcasing colorful outfits.](https://cms.perthfestival.com.au/media/z40bu3tc/web_lotterywest-film-opening-perth-fest-5007.jpg?anchor=center&mode=crop&width=800&height=442&quality=90)

## Signage Coordinator

We’re looking for a Signage Coordinator on a fixed-term basis to coordinate the planning, production, installation and maintenance of signage and wayfinding across Festival venues, precincts and event sites.

Working closely with the Production Services Manager and teams across Production, Operations and Marketing & Communications, you will help ensure signage is delivered accurately, safely and on time, while supporting audience navigation, accessibility, operational requirements and Festival brand presentation.

[

Apply now



](https://au.seek.com/job/94552897?type=standard&ref=search-standalone#sol=90ec6385a909c07c38d7bad17d3710c2e93e2e8a)

![A lively outdoor gathering with people socializing at tables, enjoying drinks, and engaging in conversation.](https://cms.perthfestival.com.au/media/dg5gdbmi/005-pf-electric-fields-250207-jwyld.jpg?anchor=center&mode=crop&width=800&height=442&quality=90)

## Finance (Payroll) Officer

We're looking for a Finance Officer on a full-time basis, with a payroll focus to keep our compliance and payroll going all year round, and to make sure it doesn't miss a beat when the Festival comes to life across our casual, fixed term and permanent employees.  
  
You'll work closely with colleagues across the organisation and play a key role in supporting our upcoming payroll and HR platform migration.

[

Apply now



](https://au.seek.com/job/94617397?type=standard&ref=search-standalone#sol=731cd6bf76396878149f34afa2d9ef5ffb24eb1a)

![A vibrant city skyline at dusk, illuminated buildings, and colorful lights in the foreground, showcasing an urban landscape.](https://cms.perthfestival.com.au/media/usagxarc/droneshots_epps_pf26_craguiastudio_lowres_009.jpg?anchor=center&mode=crop&width=800&height=442&quality=90)

## Ground Transport Coordinator

A full-time opportunity to help keep Perth Festival moving! You'll coordinate transport for artists, touring companies, VIP guests and Festival teams, managing schedules, drivers and suppliers to ensure seamless airport and venue transfers. Working across teams and responding to changing logistics, you'll help deliver safe, efficient and reliable transport throughout the Festival.

[

Apply now



](https://au.seek.com/job/95028881?type=standard&ref=search-standalone&origin=cardTitle#sol=23f5eb6139916122e851e9a6a3191c2ea74a5fe5)

# We are Perth Festival

Perth Festival is your summer invitation to otherworldly experiences. We’re a not-for-profit multi-arts festival that brings world class performance, music, film, visual arts and literary events to Perth, Western Australia, every summer.  

We are Australia’s longest-running arts festival and for 70 years we have been celebrating Perth, its people and its culture on the shores of the Derbarl Yerrigan (Swan River). Founded by The University of Western Australia and grounded on Noongar Boodjar, we are uniquely placed to celebrate the oldest living cultures in the world by championing rich Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander traditions and contemporary arts practice.  

We have cultivated decades of cultural growth through commissioning major new works and engaging diverse audiences.  

Festival time is for finding yourself alongside the best artists from here and everywhere else and revisiting that memory throughout the rest of your life.

## 

### Noongar Cultural Authority Council

'The spirit in Aboriginal people is very strong. I look at the world and I also see that I am a child of the universe. We are all children of the universe. All around the world there are people of different colours, from different races and we all make up the framework of the universe. We are the human element of the world. What we have to remember is that the spirit works right through. It comes from the earth. Women get it from the earth. They feel it. It works right through, from the inside out. People need to be more spiritually inclined. I am part of the oldest country in the world and I belong to the oldest culture. I am proud of that. … In terms of what I’d like to see in the future, well, there’s one thing our people have to learn, and that’s how to live with each other. We have to do that first before we can live with other people. Reconcile with ourselves first and then we can move forward together. We need to make a plan, understand we are part of the rest of the world, part of the universe—we belong in the bigger picture. When we understand that, then the gates will open… that’s what we have to do as Nyungar elders, pass the heritage on. That’s always been the ongoing flow of life.'

**Kenneth Desmond Colbung AM MBE also known as Nundjan Djiridjarkan   
2 Sep 1931 – 12 Jan 2010** 

Our Noongar Cultural Authority Council brings together well-respected story holders, performers, language and land caretakers, visual artists and organisation representatives with expert industry knowledge to ensure our respectful connection to this place, its people and the cultural bedrock of Noongar Boodjar remains strong. 

The consultation of our Noongar Cultural Authority Council was integral to developing the Festival's Reconciliation Action Plan. 

The Noongar Cultural Authority Council (NCAC) is made up of members with a range of qualifications and lived experiences in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander arts practice who bring together expert industry knowledge from well-respected story holders, performers, language and land caretakers, visual artists and organisation representatives. 

Our NCAC meet six times a year, once each Noongar season, at the Perth Festival office, to provide cultural leadership and guidance to the Festival and to give advice in the best interests of the Noongar community.  Members are compensated for their valuable time and knowledge – knowledge that collectively spans approximately 185 years.  

The Noongar Cultural Authority Council are: 

*   Dr Roma 'Yibiyung' Winmar AM
*   Vivienne 'Binyarn' Hansen
*   Dr Richard Walley OAM
*   Barry McGuire OAM
*   Mitchella 'Waljin' Hutchins

## 

### Access and Inclusion Advisory Committee

Our Access & Inclusion Advisory Committee was formed to ensure that everything we do considers people with disability, access requirements and relevant service organisations through a consultative process.

This committee was integral in developing our Disability, Access and Inclusion Plan (DAIP).

The Access and Inclusion Advisory Committee is comprised of members with a range of access requirements, disability and/or lived experience, and includes patrons, artists and service organisation representatives. They provide advice and guidance on all aspects of the Festival including our Disability Action and Inclusion Plan, built environments, access services available across our programs and community building. Committee members are paid for their time and meet at four key stages across the year.

## 

### Festival Cultural Ambassadors

![](/media/a0xfweej/260117-pfc-46.jpg?rmode=max&width=500)

Our Festival Cultural Ambassador program invites community leaders to experience a range of Festival events, with a focus on our more traditional Festival shows. Together with our Ambassadors we aim to break down barriers around venues, show genres and the perception that ‘this is not for me’. Each Ambassador is a leader in their own community and is asked to share their experiences with their community, helping provide avenues of access to friends and networks.  

The Ambassador program was piloted in 2022 and co-designed with community leader Aisha Novakovich, founder of Modest Fashion Australia and ex-Chair of Roots TV.

## 

### Community Partner Program

Our Community Partner program invites community groups to attend Festival events and take part in opportunities tailored to their members and staff. Community Partners are offered free access to our shows and transport and we work with organisations to find other ways to reduce barriers to attendance at the Festival. These partnerships help us to have ongoing, meaningful relationships with a diverse cross-section of Western Australia and help us truly be a Festival for everyone. 

'It’s been such a wonderful experience working with Perth Festival…the opportunities provided are opportunities that majority of our clients would not have ever experienced.'  

Community Partners | [CARAD](https://www.carad.org.au/) [Mercy Care](https://www.mercycare.com.au/), [Organisation of African Communities (OACWA)](https://oacwa.com.au/), [Community Arts Network CAN](https://www.can.org.au/), [My Place](https://www.myplace.org.au/) | [The Multiple Sclerosis Society of Western Australia (MSWA)](https://mswa.org.au/neurological-conditions/multiple-sclerorsis?gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=433877948&gbraid=0AAAAADnMeWRAumMJ4ocOp2NOztqb2FLLL&gclid=EAIaIQobChMIgvPeiueKkwMVcKVmAh2xOgkgEAAYASAAEgJeXPD_BwE)

## 

### Perth Festival is for everyone

Perth Festival is a place for bold storytelling, big ideas, and shared experiences. We believe in the power of art to spark conversations, challenge perspectives, and bring people together.

We do not support censorship and are committed to providing a platform for diverse voices and creative expression. However, we have zero tolerance for hate speech, discrimination, racism or any content that promotes harm or unlawful activity.

Perth Festival is for everyone. We invite our audiences to engage with curiosity, respect, and openness as we celebrate the artists and stories that help us see the world, and each other more clearly.

## 

### Social Impact

We take seriously the impact our festival has on our community and place and we acknowledge that festivals have not always been as accessible, inclusive and sustainable as they could be. 

Perth Festival takes a holistic view of sustainability, with a focus on caring for our planet, caring for our people and caring for our community. We do this to ensure we remain relevant, accountable and resilient for generations to come. 

We acknowledge that climate change is happening and that festivals have not traditionally been the most environmentally friendly events to undertake. We aim to be an example in changing this. 

We're currently in consultation with industry professionals to develop a sustainability roadmap to keep us accountable on our journey to minimise our impact on the environment. Things we will address in our five-year plan include greenhouse gas emissions, energy use and waste reduction.  

Once finalised, we will publish our Sustainability Action Plan on this page. Watch this space!

# About the IMA

The Institute of Modern Art (IMA) is one of the Asia-Pacific’s most important, visible, and relevant forums for contemporary visual art. The IMA champions contemporary art, artists, and ideas, connecting local voices to global dialogues via inclusive, sustainable, and innovative institutional practice.

Founded in 1975, the IMA is Australia’s oldest independent public art gallery and has been at the centre of the Queensland arts ecology for over fifty years.

The IMA’s reputation for experimentation, care, and criticality is a legacy we proudly continue. Our exhibitions, events, publications, education program, touring exhibitions, and off-site projects connect us with artists and audiences from Queensland, Australia, and around the world.

Entry to the IMA is always free, offering transformative experiences that amplify voices, ignite curiosity, and inspire change through contemporary art.

The IMA is a registered charity and membership organisation supported by the Queensland Government through [Arts Queensland](http://www.arts.qld.gov.au/), the Australian Government through [Australia Council for the Arts](http://www.australiacouncil.gov.au/), and the Visual Arts and Craft Strategy, an initiative of the Australian Federal, State, and Territory Governments, and many private sponsors and donors. The IMA is a founding member of [Contemporary Art Organisations Australia](http://caoa.com.au/).

# History of the IMA

Launched in 2015, the IMA’s 40th Anniversary online archive brings together a general overview of each of the four decades of the organisation’s history.

Each section is accompanied by an interview with a past director, giving first-hand accounts of their experiences, and offers a selection of images from the 40 year exhibition history largely documented by the photographer Richard Stringer. This platform is intended as an introduction, a place to spark interest and encourage engagement with our contemporary programs and with the extensive primary source material held both in the IMA’s onsite archives and in the State Library of Queensland.

# Off Grid 7: Building Stories with Janina Gosseye

### Architecture discussion

### 21 October 2026  
6pm

*   Share
*   [](http://www.facebook.com/share.php?u=https://www.ima.org.au/ima-events/off-grid-7-building-stories-with-janina-gosseye/&title=Off%20Grid%207:%20Building%20Stories%20with%20Janina%20Gosseye)
*   [](http://twitter.com/intent/tweet?status=Off%20Grid%207:%20Building%20Stories%20with%20Janina%20Gosseye+https://www.ima.org.au/ima-events/off-grid-7-building-stories-with-janina-gosseye/)

*   Location:

*   Event Cost:
    
    Free
    
*   Registration:
    
    [Register Here](https://events.humanitix.com/off-grid-7-building-stories-with-janina-gosseye)
    

The ways we create knowledge shape the worlds we can imagine. Can architecture and the built environment be understood differently through new forms of writing, storytelling, and creative practice. Drawing on feminist thinkers, Netherlands-based academic **Janina Gosseye** asks who gets access to knowledge—and what might be possible when we move beyond familiar ways of producing it. She will share examples of experimental writing by feminist scholars, alongside work from her TUDelft seminar, ‘Building Stories’. There, first-year master’s students use creative methods to question established ideas and imagine alternative ways of understanding and shaping our world.

This event is supported by QUT’s Queensland Architecture Research Group as part of the Off Grid series, a program of architecture discussions led by Andrew Wilson, Senior Lecturer in Architecture at University of Queensland, and Andrew Leach, Professor of Architectural History at Queensland University of Technology, both Meanjin/Brisbane.

Guest Info

*   **Professor Janina Gosseye** is Head of the Building Ideologies Group (BIG) at the TUDelft Faculty of Architecture and the Built Environment, Delft, Netherlands. Her research is situated at the nexus of 20th century architectural and urban history, and social and political history. Her books include Urban Design in the 20th Century: A History (gta Verlag, 2021, with Tom Avermaete) and Speaking of Buildings: Oral History in Architectural Research (Princeton Architectural Press, 2019, with Naomi Stead and Deborah van der Plaat).
    

Max Loeschke, Eva Vlasblom, and Lara Walter, 2024.
