Experience Gold Coast and Gold Coast Airport

## Committed to creating and improving accessible events.

## Arrival

HOTA is a cultural precinct located at 135 Bundall Road, Surfers Paradise, QLD.  
  
We have three major venues onsite, including:  
  
• HOTA Gallery (which is home to our galleries, HOTA Shop, The Studio, The Exhibitionist Bar, and Palette Restaurant).  
  
• HOTA Central (which is home to our theatres, cinemas, Candy Bar, Cafe, Studio 1 and Studio 2, Basement, Panorama Room and Lakeside Room).  
  
• Outdoor Stage.

  

### Accessible Parking

There are accessible parking spaces close to the front of HOTA Central and HOTA Gallery.  
  
For more information about parking click the link below.

[Getting Here](https://hota.com.au/visit/getting-here)

### Drop off/Pick Up

HOTA Central and Outdoor Stage drop off/pick-up area is next to the pedestrian crossing in front of the HOTA Central building.  
  
HOTA Gallery drop off/pick-up area is in front of the HOTA Gallery lower ground entrance.

### Ramp and Lift Access

All venues at HOTA have ramp or lift access, except for Theatre 1 (HOTA Central) Stalls Rows V – AA and all Rows in Theatre 1 balcony. For more information see 'Theatre 1' below.

[Venues and Facilities](https://hota.com.au/visit/accessibility#venues-and-facilities)

## Companion Cards

HOTA is proud to be an affiliate of the [Queensland Government's Companion Card program](https://www.qld.gov.au/disability/out-and-about/subsidies-concessions-passes/companion-card).

The Companion Card is designed for individuals with disabilities who require attendant care support to engage in community activities and visit various venues.

This program allows Companion Card holders to receive a complimentary second ticket for their chosen companion.

To book Companion Card tickets: select them on our website or contact our Box Office by calling (07) 5588 4000 or emailing [ticketbox@hota.com.au.](mailto:ticketbox@hota.com.au)

To collect your Companion Card Ticket, please present your companion card at the Box Office.

## Changing Places

HOTA Gallery has a Changing Places toilet. Located on the Ground Floor, the bathroom has an adult-size change table, hoist, and privacy screen.

## Guide, Hearing or Assistance Animals

  
For the safety and comfort of all our patrons, animals are not permitted inside HOTA Venues, including the HOTA Outdoor Stage when it is activated for an event, except for:

*   Guide, hearing and assistance dogs that are trained and certified in accordance with the Guide, Hearing and Assistance Dogs Act 2009 (Qld) with an identity card issued in accordance with that Act. This includes a guide, hearing and assistance dog under training.

Or:

*   Animals that meet the assistance animal requirements as outlined in the Disability Discrimination Act 1992 (Cth) (“assistance animal”), being animals that assist a person with a disability to alleviate the effect of the disability and meets standards of hygiene and behaviour that are appropriate for an animal in a public place, with an approved assistance animal pass.

  

HOTA accepts documentation and passes for assistance animals that are issued by any of the below:

1.  [Approved trainers and training institutions | People with disability | Queensland Government (opens in new tab)](https://www.qld.gov.au/disability/out-and-about/ghad/handlers/approved-trainers-and-training-institutions) 
2.  [Translink (see note below) (opens in new tab)](https://translink.com.au/tickets-and-fares/ticket-types/disability/assistance-animal-pass)
3.  [Transport for NSW (opens in new tab)](https://transportnsw.info/tickets-opal/ticket-eligibility-concessions/people-with-disabilities/apply-for-assistance-animal)
4.  [Victorian Public Transport (opens in new tab)](https://www.ptv.vic.gov.au/tickets/myki/concessions-and-free-travel/assistance-animal-pass/)
5.  [Government of WA (opens in new tab)](https://www.dlgsc.wa.gov.au/local-government/community/cats-and-dogs/applying-for-assistance-dog-approval)
6.  [Young Diggers (opens in new tab)](https://youngdiggers.com.au/)
7.  [Revolutionary Assistance Dogs Inc (opens in new tab)](https://www.raddogsinc.com.au/)
8.  [mindDog Australia (opens in new tab)](https://www.minddog.org.au/the-process/apply/)
9.  [Assistance Dogs International (opens in new tab)](https://assistancedogsinternational.org/)
10.  [ACT Government Domestic Animals Act 2000 (opens in new tab)](https://www.cityservices.act.gov.au/pets-and-wildlife/domestic-animals/assistance-animals#:~:text=Domestic%20Animal%20Services%20accredits%20assistance,within%20the%20Australian%20Capital%20Territory.)
11.  [South Australian Dog and Cat Management Board (opens in new tab)](https://dogandcatboard.com.au/dogs/assistance-dogs)
12.  [Western Australian Government Dog Act 1976 (opens in new tab)](https://www.dlgsc.wa.gov.au/local-government/community/cats-and-dogs/applying-for-assistance-dog-approval)

More information on Queensland's guide, hearing and assistance dogs, can be found [here](https://www.qld.gov.au/disability/out-and-about/ghad/resources).

## d/Deaf and Hard of Hearing

### HOTA Cinema

**Listening assistive headsets** are available at HOTA Cinema. The audio is delivered through a personal headset with individual left and right volume controls. Audio enhancement is available on all films, every session at HOTA Cinema.  
  
**Closed Caption Headset Receivers** and Gooseneck held caption boxes are available at HOTA Cinema to assist hearing impaired guests. These are glasses with captions and a box that rests in the cup holder that receive caption via Infrared energy. These products are compatible with films that have been encrypted with this technology. This new technology at HOTA Cinema is subject to availability. Be sure to check session times or ask one of the friendly Box Office staff for information on enabled access sessions.

### HOTA Gallery

**Assistive listening carrier devices** (FM system) are available in the gallery. The HOTA Gallery foyer, Children’s Gallery and Studio spaces are all fitted with an Audio Frequency Induction Loop system.  
  
**Auslan interpreted programs**: For information about upcoming Auslan interpreted exhibition tours and programs please contact [hotagallery@experiencegoldcoast.com](mailto:hotagallery@experiencegoldcoast.com) or [hotaeducation@experiencegoldcoast.com](mailto:hotaeducation@experiencegoldcoast.com) or call (07) 5588 4000.

### National Relay Service

Patrons who are d/Deaf, hard of hearing or have a speech/communication difficulty can use the National Relay Service (NRS) at no cost.  
  
Step 1. Make contact through your preferred NRS call channel detailed on NRS call numbers and links(link is external, opens in new tab or window)  
  
Step 2. Provide the NRS with the HOTA Box Office number (07) 5588 4000. [https://www.accesshub.gov.au/about-the-nrs](https://www.accesshub.gov.au/about-the-nrs)

## Neurodivergent

HOTA warmly welcomes neurodivergent visitors to enjoy our facilities and events. We encourage you to bring and use personal noise-cancelling headphones, sunglasses, and audio descriptors.

### Programming themes

If you would like to know more about any themes or technical aspects of our performances, events and exhibitions before attending, please contact our Box Office by calling (07) 5588 4000 or emailing [ticketbox@hota.com.au](mailto:ticketbox@hota.com.au).

### Social Stories

Read the Social Story for HOTA Gallery by clicking the link below.

[Social Story](https://hota.com.au/api/img/05c92aac-03d1-0235-0767-bdf54020d78e/adf5c64d-17fe-44dd-9e0e-1b18d80c3df3/HOTA-ACCESSIBILITY-SOCIAL-STORY-Going-to-the-Gallery.pdf?v=a3ec4e4cae973868b22fce8e289b25ed)

## Programs and Events

### Relaxed Performances, Theatres, HOTA Central

HOTA occasionally hosts relaxed performances.  
  
We want everyone to have a great time when they come to HOTA, but we know that not everyone feels comfortable attending a traditional theatre performance. For some events we will offer a relaxed performance.  
  
A relaxed performance may have:  
• lower sound levels and less special effects (but it will still be an amazing performance!);  
• a designated ‘chill out’ zone in the foyer, if you need to take a moment out;  
• no expectation of how you will enjoy the performance – you can move around the auditorium and making noise is ok – we love hearing people enjoy themselves!; and  
• houselights will be on at all time so there is never complete darkness.  
  
Click the link below to find upcoming relaxed performances on our 'What's on page'.

[Whats On](https://hota.com.au/events)

### Sunroom, HOTA Gallery

First Wednesday, every month  
  
Sunroom is about providing a safe, creative space for art making, creative play and exploration for adults who identify with disability.  
  
For more information and to book tickets click the link below.

[Sunroom](https://hota.com.au/events/sunroom-2026)

### Quiet Hour, HOTA Gallery

9am - 10am on the first Saturday of every month.  
  
Quiet Hour at HOTA Gallery provides relaxed and calm exhibition experiences for anyone who prefers a quieter visitor experience.  
  
Click the link below to read more about Quiet Hour.

[Quiet Hour](https://hota.com.au/events/quiet-hour)

## Hidden Disabilities Sunflower Membership

HOTA is a proud member of the Hidden Disabilities Sunflower initiative.  
  
You can look for HOTA staff wearing the Hidden Disabilities Sunflower pins.  
  
You can get a Hidden Disabilities Sunflower lanyard at HOTA Hello Desk in the foyer in HOTA Central or from the Information Station on Gallery ground floor at HOTA Gallery.  
  
If you already have a Sunflower lanyard I can bring it with me.  
  
It is OK if you don’t have a lanyard, you can still get help if I need.

## Visual Disabilities

HOTA Cinema

HOTA Cinema provides listening assisted headsets so you can listen to audio described movies you might have difficulty seeing with a spoken commentary and enjoy all the parts of a movie, including visual jokes, visual scenes, settings and body language. Films listed as \[CC\] carry this technology.

Cinema 1 and Cinema 2 are located within HOTA Central.

Listening assistive headsets are available at HOTA Cinema. Audio enhancement is available on all films at HOTA Cinema.  
  
**Closed Captions** are available on selected movies. Movies with closed captions will include a \[CC\] symbol or state ‘closed caption available text’ on our website.  
  
**Closed Caption Headset Receivers** and Gooseneck held caption boxes are available at HOTA Cinema (subject to availability). See our website or ask one of our friendly Box Office staff for information on enabled access sessions.  
  
**Visually Disabled**  
HOTA Cinema provides **listening assisted headsets** for **audio described** movies. Films listed as \[CC\] carry this technology.  
  
**Accessible Parking**  
The best Accessible carparks are near the front of HOTA Central.

![cinema 2.jpg](/api/img/05c92aac-03d1-0235-0767-bdf54020d78e/7c66db28-0ddf-4d5d-8821-91bc1fa107c0/cinema%25202.jpg?v=00cecaf29b5f216ebf1c923bc3eb2f97&w=460&fm=webp)

### HOTA Cinema 2

Cinema 1 and Cinema 2 are located within HOTA Central.  
  
**Reserved Seats**  
The following seats are reserved for patrons' accessibility requirements.  
• Row H 4, 5 and 7  
• Row H 11, 13 ad 14  
  
You can reserve an accessible seat by contacting our Box Office by calling (07) 5588 4000 or emailing [ticketbox@hota.com.au](mailto:ticketbox@hota.com.au).  
  
**Limited Steps**  
• All rows in Cinema 2 have at least one step to access the row, Except for Row H.  
  
**The best options for patrons wanting seating with limited steps:**  
• Row G, down one step from back of Cinema 2.  
• Row F, down two steps from back of Cinema 2.  
  
**Wheelchair Seating**  
There are two wheelchair seat spaces.  
• Row H 6 and H 12.  
  
You can reserve a wheelchair seat by contacting our Box Office by calling (07) 5588 4000 or emailing [ticketbox@hota.com.au](mailto:ticketbox@hota.com.au).  
  
**Hard of hearing**  
Listening assistive headsets are available at HOTA Cinema. Audio enhancement is available on all films at HOTA Cinema.  
  
**Closed Captions** are available on selected movies. Movies with closed captions will include a \[CC\] symbol or state ‘closed caption available text’ on our website.  
  
**Closed Caption Headset Receivers** and Gooseneck held caption boxes are available at HOTA Cinema (subject to availability). See our website or ask one of our friendly Box Office staff for information on enabled access sessions.  
  
**Visually Disabled**  
HOTA Cinema provides **listening assisted headsets** for **audio described** movies. Films listed as \[CC\] carry this technology.  
  
**Accessible Parking**  
The best Accessible carparks are near the front of HOTA Central.

![HOTA-Venue-Information-Sheet-FEB-2024-Basement-6.jpeg](/api/img/05c92aac-03d1-0235-0767-bdf54020d78e/c8d81ae0-0f79-4dc8-a57c-0418de8953e0/HOTA-Venue-Information-Sheet-FEB-2024-Basement-6.jpeg?v=51e8c3681cbc2b9fa386075af4b546de&w=460&fm=webp)

### Basement

Located on the lower ground of HOTA Central.  
  
**Wheelchair Access/No Stair Access**  
The main entrance to the Basement has 10 stairs.  
  
For no stair access to the Basement:  
• Enter HOTA Central via the Lakeside Room foyer.  
• Follow signs to The Basement.  
  
**Wheelchair Seats**  
To book wheelchair seats in the Basement, please contact our Box Office by calling (07) 5588 4000 or emailing [ticketbox@hota.com.au](mailto:ticketbox@hota.com.au).  
  
**Accessible Parking**  
The best Accessible carparks are near the front of HOTA Central.

![HOTA-Venue-Information-Sheet-FEB-2024-Lakeside (1)3.jpeg](/api/img/05c92aac-03d1-0235-0767-bdf54020d78e/dfb95349-1ad1-4cc1-b06b-0e03a2189d50/HOTA-Venue-Information-Sheet-FEB-2024-Lakeside%2520%25281%25293.jpeg?v=be7cab75af1a14ee0a365b76d2cdca14&w=460&fm=webp)

### Lakeside Room

This room is on the lower ground level of HOTA Central. It is accessible by the main lift from the foyer.  
  
**Wheelchair Access**  
The room has no fixed seating. If you would like to book a wheelchair seat in the Lakeside Room, please contact our Box Office by calling (07) 5588 4000 or emailing [ticketbox@hota.com.au](mailto:ticketbox@hota.com.au).  
  
**Accessible Parking**  
The best Accessible carparks are near the front of HOTA Central.

![outdoorstage.jpg](/api/img/05c92aac-03d1-0235-0767-bdf54020d78e/ef140ce2-9ef4-48e7-89a3-23c624caabb6/outdoorstage.jpg?v=f3440da3ac9d7979da6f35d9dbd69e6f&w=460&fm=webp)

### Outdoor Stage

The Outdoor Stage is situated in the precinct behind HOTA Central and across from HOTA Gallery.  
  
**Wheelchair Access**  
There are designated spots for wheelchair users and their companions on the level paved walkway which provides good views of the stage.  
  
**Accessible Parking**  
The best Accessible carparks are near the front of HOTA Gallery.

![HOTA Gallery Images.jpeg](/api/img/05c92aac-03d1-0235-0767-bdf54020d78e/227be0cd-a14c-4f9c-a85a-d5e1572e1e9c/HOTA%2520Gallery%2520Images.jpeg?v=1259010fb250aca6648f3bc7b6177c90&w=460&fm=webp)

### HOTA Gallery

Located on the precinct adjacent to the Council Chambers Building and across from the Outdoor Stage.  
  
**Auslan Interpretation**  
For information about upcoming Auslan interpreted exhibition tours and programs please contact [gallery@hota.com.au](mailto:gallery@hota.com.au) or [education@hota.com.au](mailto:education@hota.com.au) or call (07) 5588 4000.  
  
**Hard of hearing**  
Assistive listening carrier devices (FM system) are available in the gallery. The HOTA Gallery foyer, Children’s Gallery and Studio spaces are all fitted with an Audio Frequency Induction Loop system.  
  
**Social Story**  
Your pre-visit information for HOTA Gallery. Find out more information click the link below.  
  
**Quiet Hour**  
On the first Saturday of every month between 9 – 10am we offer Quiet Hour in HOTA Gallery. Our Quiet Hour is provided to ensure a relaxed and calm environment for anyone who prefers a quieter visitor experience.  
  
More details on Quiet Hour and the HOTA Gallery Social Story below.  
  
**Accessible Parking**  
The best Accessible carparks are near the front of HOTA Gallery.

[Social Story](https://hota.com.au/api/img/05c92aac-03d1-0235-0767-bdf54020d78e/a74c6c1f-c21e-48e7-b4c9-865653eda561/HOTA-ACCESSIBILITY-SOCIAL-STORY-Going-to-the-Gallery%2520%25282%2529.pdf?v=a3ec4e4cae973868b22fce8e289b25ed)

![HOTA-ExhibitionistBar-2025\_0Y5A6694.jpg](/api/img/05c92aac-03d1-0235-0767-bdf54020d78e/8e2d743b-955e-4ca7-b133-db7c0035e5fc/HOTA-ExhibitionistBar-2025_0Y5A6694.jpg?v=f25720d2d50416edba8863e5a07dffd1&w=460&fm=webp)

### The Exhibitionist Bar

Located on level 5 of HOTA Gallery, The Exhibitionist Bar is a rooftop bar that serves food and drinks.  
  
The Exhibitionist Bar is table service.  
  
**Accessible Parking**  
The best Accessible carparks are near the front of HOTA Gallery.  
  
Find out more information about The Exhibitionist Bar by clicking the link below.

[Find Out More](https://hota.com.au/dining/exhibitionist)

### Palette Restaurant

Palette is on the ground floor of HOTA Gallery. It is accessible by wheelchair via the ramp outside and entering via Ground. Or you can enter HOTA Gallery via the Lower Ground Entrance and take the elevator up to Ground.  
  
Find out more about Palette Restaurant by clicking the link below.  
  
**Accessible Parking**  
The best Accessible Carparks for Palette are near the front of HOTA Gallery.

[Find Out More](https://hota.com.au/dining/palette)

### HOTA Shop

Located on the ground floor of the HOTA Gallery and is wheelchair accessible.

[Find out More](https://shop.hota.com.au/?_gl=1*1aqanpo*_gcl_au*MTI3Njg1Mzk0NS4xNzgyMjcwMjIz*_ga*Mzg0NDY2OTM3LjE3ODIyNzAyMjM.*_ga_2BSS4CJNQV*czE3ODI3MDM0NjEkbzEwJGcxJHQxNzgyNzA1NTg1JGo2MCRsMCRoMA..)

### HOTA Café

Located outside HOTA Central and accessible by wheelchair. The menu has snacks, light lunches, coffee, drinks (both alcoholic and non-alcoholic) and cakes. Order your food and drinks at the counter. You can sit inside or outside on the deck.  
  
**Accessible Parking**  
The best Accessible Parks are near the front of HOTA Central.  
  
Find out more about HOTA Café by clicking the link below.

[Find out More](https://hota.com.au/dining/cafe)

![hota-400of632-jpg.jpg](/api/img/05c92aac-03d1-0235-0767-bdf54020d78e/94124128-8916-4fda-bd2d-bd72db45f8f4/hota-400of632-jpg.jpg?v=e33093df0e07b82b34baf5735c6136ff&w=460&fm=webp)

### Candy Bar

Located on the ground floor of HOTA Central and is accessible by wheelchair.

![Panorama09.jpg](/api/img/05c92aac-03d1-0235-0767-bdf54020d78e/a1d6655c-5e8e-41fc-ae3f-e2093fb2ab0d/Panorama09.jpg?v=9c48643620e18bb611afbddae6373131&w=460&fm=webp)

### Panorama Room

This room, which is used as primarily as a function space and venue with no fixed seating, is found on level 1 of HOTA Central. It is accessible by a lift from the foyer.

## Wheelchair/Wheelie Walker Users

### Lift and Ramp Access

All venues at HOTA have ramp or lift access, except for Theatre 1 (HOTA Central) Stalls Rows V – AA and all Rows in Theatre 1 balcony. For more information click the link below.

### Limited Steps/No Steps

Theatre 1:  
Limited steps  
• All rows in Theatre 1 (except for Row W) have at least one step to access the row.  
  
The best options for patrons wanting seating with limited steps:  
• Stalls Row V, down two steps from back of Theatre 1 (stalls).  
• Stalls Row U, down four steps from back of Theatre 1 (stalls).  
  
Theatre 2:  
Row Access: No Steps  
• Row A requires no steps to access.  
  
Row Access: Limited Steps:  
• Row B, up 1 step from front of Theatre 2.  
• Row C, up 2 steps from front of Theatre 2.  
  
Cinema 1:  
Row Access: No Steps  
All rows in Cinema 1 are accessible via a sloped ramp.  
  
Cinema 2:  
Row Access: No Steps  
• Row H requires no steps to access.  
  
Row Access: Limited Steps  
• Row G, down one step from back of Cinema 2.  
• Row F, down two steps from back of Cinema 2.

### Wheelchair Seats

All venues at HOTA have Wheelchair Spaces:  
• Theatre 1: 2 wheelchair seats (Row W)  
  
• Theatre 2: 2 wheelchairs seats (Row A)  
  
• Cinema 1: 2 wheelchair seats (Row A 6 and A 12)  
  
• Cinema 2: 2 wheelchair seats (Row H6 and H 12)  
  
• Outdoor stage: There are designated spots for wheelchair users and their companions on the level paved walkway which provides good views of the stage.  
  
• Basement: The Basement has no fixed seating so we can accommodate wheelchairs and wheelie walkers. If you would like to discuss your access requirements with our team please call our Box Office team on (07) 5588 4000 or email [ticketbox@hota.com.au](mailto:ticketbox@hota.com.au).  
  
• Lakeside Room: Lakeside Room has no fixed seating so we can accommodate wheelchairs and wheelie walkers. If you would like to discuss your access requirements with our team please call our Box Office team on (07) 5588 4000 or email [ticketbox@hota.com.au](mailto:ticketbox@hota.com.au).  
  
• Panorama Room: The Panorama room has no fixed seating so we can accommodate wheelchairs and wheelie walkers. If you would like to discuss your access requirements with our team please call our Box Office team on (07) 5588 4000 or email [ticketbox@hota.com.au](mailto:ticketbox@hota.com.au).  
  
You can book wheelchair seats by contacting our Box Office by calling (07) 5588 4000 or emailing [ticketbox@hota.com.au](mailto:ticketbox@hota.com.au).

**HOTA** proudly acknowledges the Traditional Custodians of the land on which we are situated, the Kombumerri families of the Yugambeh Language Region. We pay our respects to their Elders past, present and emerging, and recognise their continuing connections to the lands, waters and their extended communities throughout South East Queensland.

# Volunteer with us

Join the Perth Festival volunteer team and be part of an iconic arts celebration! 

Gain valuable experience, meet new people, and contribute to bringing Perth Festival 2026 to life. Learn how to get involved, explore volunteer roles, and find out how you can help create an unforgettable experience for our audiences. Be a part of something special and make a difference in your community. Please note you must be over 18 years of age to volunteer.

Stay tuned for when we open expressions of interest later this year.

In the meantime you can [email us](https://www.perthfestival.com.au/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#5d2b323128332938382f2e1d2d382f29353b382e29342b3c31733e3230733c28) and we'll make sure you're contacted directly when expressions of interest open.

Perth Makers Market Twilight Series is proud to be supported by the Town of Victoria Park through its Place Grant for our 2026 event series. This funding helps us bring free, family-friendly activities to our Fathers Day, Halloween and Christmas Twilight events, from live entertainment and workshops to interactive experiences, at no cost to visitors.

By partnering with the Town of Victoria Park, we’re able to create vibrant, welcoming spaces where locals and visitors alike can connect, discover local makers and producers, and enjoy a great day out. Supporting local handmade makers by organising popular markets for people to experience and buy their craft.

At Perth Makers Market you will only be able to find beautiful items handmade right here in Western Australia.

### Information for Stallholders

At Perth Makers Market we are always on the lookout for new, talented Western Australian makers to come and showcase their wares at our market.

We are strictly a locally handmade only market. **If you do not make your products yourself, please do not apply to our events as we hate to disappoint when you do not meet our criteria.** If you are unsure if what you do qualifies as handmade please scroll down to our FAQ’s as you will find commonly asked questions there. If you can’t find the answer you seek there, you can always get in touch to ask via our [Contact Us](https://perthmakersmarket.com.au/#contact) section.

New to the world of handmade? Not a problem! Here at Perth Makers Market we are more than happy to help you on your handmade journey and even offer discounts to new and emerging artists\*, students and spaces for not-for-profit organisations (at no cost!). We support our makers by helping them gain exposure and furthering their opportunities to develop their brand.

Perth Makers Market is connected with the local community. We take pride in the location of our market and our connections with this community and as such, we ask that all market representatives (makers included) maintain a professional, positive and approachable image and a sense of community at all times during the market.

Please take the time to read our [Terms and Conditions for Stallholders](https://perthmakersmarket.com.au/terms_and_conditions/) before applying, and if you have any queries please do not hesitate to get in touch.

\* Conditions apply - please read our [Discounts](https://perthmakersmarket.com.au/stallholder_applications/#discounts) section below.

* * *

### Legal

All stallholders must have public liability insurance coverage of $10 million. If you do not have your own insurance, do not despair! We are able to provide coverage under our policy for a small cost per event. We are able to cover all product categories with the exception of the following:

*   Children’s toys
*   Animal feeds (pet treats and food)
*   Beauty (including soap)
*   Food and beverages

Should you be accepted to our market we will ask you to provide us with a copy of your certificate of currency. If this is not received prior to the market (by date indicated by market management) you will not be permitted to attend.

* * *

### How to Apply

You will need to create your own online business profile via our stallholder portal: [https://marketlife.com.au/](https://marketlife.com.au/).

Once you have added all information and images, you will be able to apply for market dates in the section titled “Market Applications – Upcoming Markets”. Click on to the date you are interested in applying for, and then you can apply for the appropriate stall size and any relevant discounts. Once you have completed the application for that date, the date in question will move under the heading “Existing Applications”.

* * *

### Discounts

*   Discounts are only available to handmade artisan stalls, not food vendors.
*   You can only apply for one discount type at a time.
*   You must be able to show that you qualify for the discount in order for it to apply.
*   Please be aware that if we request confirmation of your status of a new/emerging artist or student and you fail to provide evidence you will be charged full stall fees.

###### Student Discount - 50% off

Students can apply for a student discount of 50% to any stall size. There is limited availability for student stalls. Please indicate on your application form your status as a student. You must be able to prove your status as a student for discount to apply by providing proof of enrolment at an educational institution.

###### New/Emerging Artist Discount - 30% off

Emerging artists and makers can apply for an emerging artist discount of 30% to any stall size. There is limited availability for emerging artist stalls. Please indicate on your application form your status as an emerging artist. You must be able to prove your status as an emerging artist for discount to apply, we do check this.

To qualify for a new/emerging artist discount you must meet the following:

*   Have attended no more than 6 markets within the last 12 months
*   If you sell online (including through social media) you must not have been in operation for more than 12 months
*   If you are stocked in a retail store, you must not have been stocked for more than 6 months

Please contact market management for further information if you wish to clarify if you are eligible for a discount.

###### Not-for-Profit - 100% off

Not for profit stalls are provided free of charge. Organisations must be able to prove not for profit status. There are a limited number of not for profit stall spaces. All not for profit stall spaces are 3m x 3m outdoor stalls and you must provide your own complete set up for the space including gazebo and weights.

* * *

### FAQs for Stallholders

###### 1\. Do I need to supply my own gazebo?

Yes, you need to provide your own complete set up for your stall including gazebo.

###### 2\. Do you provide a tables and chairs for stallholders?

No, Perth Makers Market does not provide tables or chairs for your stall. You will need to provide your own complete set up for your stall including tables and chairs.

###### 3\. I’m a student – how do I apply for your student discount?

When applying using our online stallholder portal (https://marketlife.com.au/) make sure you select the 50% student discount. In order for us to apply it to you we need to see proof of enrolment for you. You can either add this as part of your application as an image, or e-mail a copy of your proof of enrolment to erin@perthmakersmarket.com

###### 4\. Is there power available?

We do not offer powered stalls due to poor availability/access to power on site at Heathcote. If you require power in order to attend please include this information as part of your application. We have a limited availability to offer power in certain locations and do not wish to run into issues on market day with accepting stallholders who require power that we are then not able to accommodate. Please be aware that if you need power provided by Perth Makers Market in order to run your stall you are less likely to be accepted to our events due to this issue.

###### 5\. Can I peg my gazebo into the grass?

Under no circumstances can items be pegged/stuck into the grass at Heathcote. This is a very strict requirement by City of Melville and is part of our conditions in making use of the site. Your gazebo must be weighted with appropriate weights (proper weights that are strapped to your gazebo), items such as bricks placed on the base of your gazebo are not acceptable. This is a safety issue and should market staff find you non-compliant on market day you will be asked to take down your stall and leave our event. If you need advice on where to purchase appropriate gazebo weights please contact us.

###### 6\. I design my products however they are handmade by artisans overseas, can I still have a stall at your market?

Perth Makers Market is a strictly locally handmade only market. This means we only accept business who make their own products locally in Western Australia. Unfortunately if you have your products manufactured elsewhere we cannot accept you as a stallholder, regardless of where the products are designed.

###### 7\. I’m a photographer so my products are printed elsewhere but I am the one who took the pictures. Does this count as handmade?

In certain product categories such as photography and artwork we will accept stallholders who have their images and artwork printed on to other mediums (within reason) and have multiple copies of their work for sale (art prints etc.) as we recognise that this still counts as handmade as you are the one who has taken the image/produced the artwork.

###### 8\. You offer shared stalls? I don’t know anyone to share with, can you pair me with someone?

Unfortunately we do not pair businesses together for a shared stall due to previous poor experiences. If you would like to apply for a shared stall you need to be able to nominate someone to share with, and they also need to apply and nominate to share with you.

###### 9\. I make cupcakes/cookies/baked goods, do I apply for a food stall?

Nope! We count pre-made food items as a standard stall type as we acknowledge it is a different type of business with a different price point to those making and serving food on market day. Just apply for a stall and select your category as “food, pre-made”

### Information for Food Vendors

If you make pre-made food such as jams, cupcakes, cookies etc. you do not come under our “Food Vendor” category, but rather a normal stall under the category of “Food, Pre-Made”. Please read the [information for stallholders](https://perthmakersmarket.com.au/stallholder_applications/) for further information.

Please take the time to read our [Terms and Conditions for Stallholders](https://perthmakersmarket.com.au/terms_and_conditions/) before applying, and if you have any queries please do not hesitate to get in touch.

We take a maximum of 10 food vendors per event and as such competition for these places is high. We try our best to rotate food vendors through our events so that everyone has an opportunity to trade with us. To ensure your application is as strong as possible be sure to include the following:

*   A good description of your business, including a listing of your menu
*   As many images as needed to showcase your food, rather than the minimum three required
*   Your images are clear and show your food, rather than something unrelated or that does not allow us to view your products
*   Links to a website, or your social media. If you do not have these, that is ok – it is not a detractor to your application, but we do suggest looking at adding these to your business.

Please be aware that we do not offer powered stalls for food vendors due to the site and inaccessibility to power.

# About Us

Perth Makers Market is an exclusively handmade only market South of the Swan River that makes its home at Heathcote Cultural Precinct in Applecross. All items that you will find at our market have been handcrafted by the stall holders themselves locally in WA. The only exception to this is our non-profit stalls who attend to raise awareness and fundraise for their causes.

* * *

Our goal is to provide a platform for the talented, high quality handmade crafters that call Perth their home in a family focused, friendly location.

* * *

Perth Makers Market’s founder and event manager often found that as a hand-crafter herself it was not only difficult to break into the market scene, but that certain markets within the Perth area no longer cater to the exclusively handmade. What makes Perth Makers Market so great is that you will never find something at one of our stalls that wasn’t made right here in our great state of Western Australia. Not only that, but we are actively assisting both new and emerging artists, as well as talented school students in breaking into the handmade marketplace.

Perth Makers Market is proud to be partnered with the City of Melville to bring the local community a beautiful event location and an opportunity for local residents to participate in a handmade market designed to give back to the community through fundraising opportunities with non-profit organisations. With strong ties to the community and a focus on giving back, Perth Makers Market is unique.

Fall in love with the unique pieces that are passionately and individually hand-crafted in an idyllic location while your kids play on the playground. While you’re here why not stop for lunch at the Bluewater Grill or take a look at the on-site gallery? Come wander the stalls, grab a coffee and take in all that the Perth handmade community has to offer.

# Visitor FAQs

#### 1\. What dates and times are the markets held?

We hold many markets spread throughout the year at different locations around the city. The following markets are upcoming:

#### 2\. Is the market disable access friendly?

Yes! Heathcote Cultural Precinct is a disable access friendly site with pathways and no steps. We allocate the on-site parking to be disabled only. Should you arrive and this parking area be full, we have a drop off area available. There are disabled toilets available on site. If you need assistance locating them please ask market staff.

#### 3\. Am I able to bring my dog to the market?

As much as we would love to say yes, the answer is unfortunately no. Heathcote Cultural Precinct does not allow dogs, and there are signs to that effect on site. We also would not want there to be an incident involving any pooches should they be startled by other dogs, kids and the large crowd on site.

#### 4\. What are my transport/parking options for getting to Heathcote Cultural Precinct?

There is dedicated event parking next to the market on the Heathcote Lower Lands. This parking is managed by Applecross Rotary as a fundraiser for their non-profit organisation. Parking is by donation.

If you are interested in a beautiful walk along the river to get to the market, you can arrive by Public Transport to the Canning Bridge train station on the Mandurah Train Line. The walk is approximately 20 minutes.

#### 5\. Where can I contact the market organiser with any questions?

The best way to reach us is using the [Contact Us](https://perthmakersmarket.com.au/#contact) form on this website or reaching us through our [Facebook page](https://www.facebook.com/perthmakersmarket/). Alternatively, if you would like you can give us a call during office hours.

### Information for Buskers and Musicians

At Perth Makers Market we love having live musicians and have three separate locations at the market where we have buskers throughout the day. We particularly like to foster school students who are interested in making music their career.

If you are interested in busking with us please get in touch via our [Contact Us](https://perthmakersmarket.com.au/#contact) form.

### FAQs for Buskers

#### 1\. Is there shade provided?

Yes, we have a gazebo set up for you to busk under.

#### 2\. Is there access to power for me to use?

Unfortunately due to the age of the site there is no access to power. If you require use of an amp you must be able to operate without power.

#### 3\. Is there a retainer paid to musicians?

No, we are not able to pay a retainer to musicians unfortunately. All money that you raise during your busking is yours to keep and we are happy for you to advertise your music or sell CDs.

#### 4\. Can I just turn up on the day to busk?

No, you must register your interest with us and we put together set times for you to busk in specific locations. This is so there is no overlap of music at the market and you are not playing in competition with other buskers.

### Market Terms and Conditions

**Last Updated 17 October 2026**

Thank you for choosing to apply with Perth Makers Market (PMM). Once a stallholder submits their application, the stallholder agrees to adhere to the terms and conditions as outlined in this document. We strongly encourage you to read through the terms and conditions carefully to ensure compliance and to prevent future disappointment or disputes.

**Perth Makers Market is a strictly locally handmade market, built to support the maker community here in Western Australia.** We only accept stallholders who design and handmake their products themselves, here in WA. Bringing products to this event that are not handmade by you in Western Australia breaches our Terms & Conditions. The only exception to this is registered non-profit organisations, which may be accepted at the discretion of market management.

Applications must be completed clearly and accurately. Specific information is required regarding how your products are made. PMM reserves the right to decline applications we deem unsuitable at our discretion without entering into further correspondence with the applicant due to application volume.

It is of utmost importance to remember that stallholders are to engage only with PMM management and staff to discuss any issues, rather than the managers or staff of any of our host venues.

* * *

### Products

1.  Perth Makers Market is a strictly Locally Handmade Market. This means:
    *   All products must be designed and handmade by you, here in Western Australia.
    *   Your products must be created from your own creative vision and made with your own hands, offering unique items that aren’t mass-produced or available elsewhere.
    *   You must be able to show a high level of hands-on involvement in making your products. Embellishing, altering or decorating existing products is only accepted where the changes to the original product are significant.
    *   The only exception to this is for registered non-profit organisations which may be accepted at the discretion of market management.
2.  Stallholders are only able to sell products approved by market management as per their application. If you have been accepted into an event and wish to sell additional products that were not included as part of your initial application, please submit a request in writing with attached images to PMM for approval. If you have not been accepted to an event, you may update your profile in our stallholder portal at any time.
3.  Stallholders are not permitted to sell goods on behalf of other businesses. Shared stall spaces are available as an option during the application process. PMM requires full details of both businesses and therefore both makers are required to submit an application. Stallholders who do not comply with this condition will not be approved.
4.  PMM does not permit stallholders to use the event for clearance sales unless otherwise stated in the event description, as this devalues the efforts of other stallholders trading at full price.
5.  It is the responsibility of stallholders to ensure their products comply with the relevant safety and labelling standards for their items (see Product Safety and Labelling Standards below). PMM takes no responsibility for products or stallholders who fail to comply with standards and regulations.
6.  Stallholders are not permitted to sell offensive, illegal, prohibited, counterfeit or unauthorised goods, including goods bearing trademarks for which the stallholder does not hold a licence to sell.
7.  It is the stallholder's responsibility to ensure that the products they are selling do not infringe on any third-party rights, including the Intellectual Property rights of other stallholders and businesses. Copying the ideas and work of other stallholders may be in breach of creative copyright and is not in the spirit of the market; any grievances must be raised with PMM in writing.
8.  Loud product promotion or demonstrations by stallholders, including in dedicated demonstration areas, are not permitted where they disrupt neighbouring stallholders or patrons.

### Product Safety and Labelling Standards

9.  Certain product categories are stringently regulated by the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC), including fire warnings on children's sleepwear, choking hazards, items intended for children under three, food products, and combustible candle holders. It is vital that stallholders are aware of, and comply with, the mandatory and legally binding safety standards associated with their products, and that products are labelled accordingly.
10.  The onus is on the stallholder to ensure their products comply with the relevant safety and labelling standards. PMM takes no responsibility for products or stallholders who fail to comply with these standards.

### Stall Applications and Attendance

11.  Acceptance of stallholders for participation in events is at the sole discretion of PMM. PMM reserves the right to reject applications and not enter into correspondence or otherwise explain further.
12.  Stalls cannot be transferred, sublet, franchised or sold to any other person, and cannot be shared, without written approval from market management.
13.  All stallholders will be informed in writing of their stall allocations, bump-in time and location one week prior to market. All stall allocations are final.
14.  The Market Manager reserves the right, at any time, to alter the position or layout of the Market and stalls as may be necessary to maintain grounds, in accordance with directions from the landlord, for safety reasons, risk management and legal requirements.
15.  Acceptance of an application to attend a PMM event does not guarantee ongoing acceptance. Applications from stallholders are assessed on an event-by-event basis.

### Stall Payment, Cancellation and Refunds

16.  Successful applicants will have seven (7) days to make payment of stall fees upon notification of acceptance to the market and issue of invoice, which will occur at the time of acceptance.
17.  Failure to make payment within the 7-day period will result in the offer of a stall being withdrawn.
18.  Stall fees are set on an event-by-event basis and are displayed at the time of application. By submitting an application, you acknowledge and accept the applicable stall fees for the event to which you have applied.
19.  Notification of non-attendance is required in writing, with an explanation provided as to the reason for non-attendance.
20.  If you decline your stall offer, no fees apply.
21.  Once your stall offer is accepted and paid for, should you cancel six (6) or more weeks prior to the market date for which you have been accepted, you will be entitled to a 50% refund of your stall fee.
22.  Cancellations received within six (6) weeks or less, prior to the specified market date for which you have been accepted, are non-refundable with no exceptions.
23.  PMM has the right to withdraw an offer to trade at any time. If PMM withdraws an offer to trade, a refund will be issued in full where payment has been made.

### Event Cancellation

24.  PMM reserves the right to cancel any market event up to 12 hours prior to its scheduled time.
25.  PMM will inform stallholders via e-mail of any event cancellation with as much notice as possible.
26.  Event cancellation by PMM may occur for reasons including but not limited to:
     *   Insufficient stalls booked for the event;
     *   Safety concerns (severe weather);
     *   c) A Force Majeure event (see below);
     *   d) Council or permit issues outside of PMM's control.
27.  If an event is cancelled by PMM due to Safety (severe weather warnings), vendors are entitled to a 50% refund of their stall fee.
28.  If an event is cancelled by PMM for other reasons (excluding force Majeure), vendors are entitled to a full refund of their stall fee.

### Force Majeure

29.  Force Majeure means the happening of an event ("FME") or circumstance which is beyond the reasonable control of a party and prevents or delays that party from performing any of its obligations; could not have been avoided or overcome by that party through the exercise of reasonable foresight, care and due diligence; and includes with the exception of severe weather as per the Event Cancellation Policy, but is not limited to: an Act of God, including earthquake, flood, fire, explosion, landslide, lightning, action of the elements, force of nature, washout, storm or storm warning, or natural disaster; a strike, lockout, boycott, work ban or other labour dispute or difficulty, or a venue owner deciding to cancel, restrict or alter a scheduled event; and acts of terrorism, civil disturbance, blockade, embargo, sabotage, insurrection, riot, malicious damage, epidemic, pandemic, chemical leak, noxious atmosphere, war or acts of Government (State or Federal). Force Majeure excludes hardship due to currency fluctuations and changes in market conditions or market prices.
30.  Should an FME occur: this agreement is terminated from the date of the FME; the parties are released from performing any of their respective obligations under this agreement following the FME; the occurrence of the FME does not affect any of the parties' obligations arising prior to the FME; neither party will be liable for losses incurred by the other as a result of the agreement being terminated; and any payment made by a stallholder to PMM prior to the FME is non-refundable, and the stallholder is not entitled to demand a refund of monies paid.

### Stall Set-up and Presentation

31.  Stallholders bump-in and set up during the hours prior to market opening time, and must be ready to trade by market opening. Pack up and bump-out must be completed within two hours of market closing. Stallholders who are not set up and ready to trade by market opening forfeit their stall for that market date.
32.  Stallholders must comply with the bump-in times and locations provided by PMM. Failure to do so will impact acceptance at future events.
33.  Stallholders must comply with instructions provided by all market staff on the day, not just management staff.
34.  PMM takes no responsibility for the weather. Please come prepared for all weather conditions. Events take place rain or shine unless there are issues of safety.
35.  No stallholder is permitted to fix or adhere anything to pillars or walls. Stallholders are responsible for any damage they incur to host venues.
36.  All stallholders must cover tables with floor-length tablecloths, covering all sides of tables. Boxes, bags, crates and other items not on display for sale must be kept out of sight.
37.  All outdoor stallholders must provide their own gazebo. All gazebos are to be weighted down using appropriate weights prior to commencement of trade. No gazebos are permitted to be pegged into the ground at any time.
38.  Stallholders without weights will not be allowed to erect their gazebo with no exceptions and no refunds.
39.  Stallholders using gas or electrical appliances must have a suitable fire extinguisher and/or fire blanket on site. Electrical leads and equipment must be tagged and tested by a qualified tester at least every three months, in compliance with workplace laws and regulations.
40.  Stallholder displays and materials must stay within their assigned stall space. Failure to comply may result in items being removed by market management for safety reasons.
41.  Stallholders must supply their own complete set-up for the market, including tables and chairs.
42.  Please show consideration for the safety of yourself, your team, fellow stallholders and patrons. Stallholders must clean up all breakages and spills within their stall space. For any safety concerns during the event, please contact PMM staff as soon as possible to prevent injury.

### Stallholder Behaviour

43.  Stallholders and their staff, at all times, are expected to deal with the public, other stallholders, market staff and market management in a professional, respectful and courteous manner. Unacceptable, uncivil or unsafe behaviour or swearing may result in the Market Manager directing the stallholder or their staff to leave the Market immediately.
44.  Stallholders must not at any time insult or intimidate anyone including other stallholders, customers, visitors and staff.
45.  You must not engage in any conduct which is disruptive or inconsistent with the purpose of PMM. This includes but is not limited to online bullying, engaging in false claims in online reviews, or slander of PMM, our stallholders, our venues or our staff.
46.  Stallholders should ensure that they, and their staff, do not give false, deceptive or misleading information, or make misleading claims to customers about the quality, quantity, origin or certification of goods, produce or products they are selling.
47.  Stallholders must comply with instructions provided by all market staff on the day, not just management or office staff. Failure to do so may result in removal from the market.
48.  Where a stallholder is involved in activities that, in the opinion of PMM, bring or will bring PMM into disrepute, discredit the market, or cause reputational damage to the market, the stallholder may be directed to leave the market. PMM has the discretion to suspend a stallholder pending any investigation being undertaken by, or about to be undertaken by, an investigative body.

### Stall Operation

49.  Stallholders agree to trade for the entire duration of the market event they have accepted to participate in.
50.  Raffle tickets may not be sold, and competitions or giveaways may not be run, without prior written approval from PMM.
51.  PMM does not permit stallholders to stand outside their stall space to distribute flyers to passing customers, due to the impact on fellow stallholders.
52.  Stallholders are responsible for the area of their stall and surrounds, and must leave the area clean and tidy.
53.  Boxes and cartons must be removed from the market area. Market bins must not be used for the disposal of stallholder waste or packaging materials.
54.  All stallholders must be respectful and considerate of neighbouring stallholders, their spaces and any shared areas, to ensure the safety of stallholders and patrons and to maintain a courteous, friendly environment for all.
55.  It is the responsibility of the stallholder to trade in accordance with Market, State and Local Council or Shire regulations.

### Stall Close and Pack-up

56.  Stalls must not commence pack-up prior to the advertised closing time. This is both a safety requirement and necessary to meet the advertised market time obligations to patrons.
57.  Stallholders must pack up their stall and transport items to a designated bump-out location prior to collecting their vehicle. Failure to do so may impact future acceptance at events.
58.  Stallholders must follow directions of market staff at all times to ensure safety.
59.  All stallholders are responsible for the removal of their own rubbish and must leave their allocated space in the condition it was found prior to bump-in.

### Regulations and Insurance

60.  Proof of public liability insurance to the value of $10 million must be provided prior to the event. Failure to provide proof of current insurance may result in set-up being refused.
61.  Should a stallholder not hold their own public liability insurance, insurance can be purchased for a fee per market from PMM. Please note that the PMM policy covers public liability only and does not extend to products liability insurance.
62.  Stallholders who employ staff are encouraged to hold appropriate worker's compensation insurance in accordance with applicable laws and regulations. PMM takes no responsibility for any claims, costs or liabilities arising from a stallholder's failure to hold adequate worker's compensation coverage.
63.  Stallholders are encouraged to consider whether product liability insurance is appropriate for their business. PMM takes no responsibility for any claims, costs or liabilities arising from products sold by stallholders at any market event, and stallholders accept full responsibility for any such claims.
64.  PMM has the right to withdraw the right to trade of any stallholder in dispute with PMM or any other person. The right to trade will only be reinstated if the dispute is resolved to PMM's satisfaction.
65.  PMM has the right to reject any stallholder it believes does not comply with the terms and conditions set out in this document.

### Traffic Management and Parking

66.  Strictly no parking or unloading is permitted on footpaths. No driving on grass or non-drop-off areas unless specified in writing by PMM.
67.  Stallholders who are permitted to drive on site to unload vehicles must drive at walking pace, as directed by market staff. Failure to do so may impact future acceptance at events.
68.  Stallholders must use the bump in area allocated to them.
69.  No vehicles are to be left onsite unless by prior arrangement with market management.
70.  Stallholders are required to unload their market supplies at their allocated bump-in location and immediately move their vehicle to the allocated event parking.
71.  Stallholders requiring assistance moving between event parking and the event, for any reason, may apply to Market Management for an exemption.
72.  During Bump Out, stallholders are required to fully pack down their stall and transport goods to a bump out location, prior to getting their vehicle. Failure to do so may impact future acceptance at events.

### Additional Terms for Food/Beverage Vendors

73.  PMM will only allow stalls to trade if their food or beverages are produced in Council-registered food premises and appropriate certification can be produced.
74.  PMM will only allow stalls to trade if they hold a valid permit to sell their food or beverage as a mobile vendor.
75.  Food and beverage stallholders must be registered with the local council where the event is hosted and must pay for the appropriate council permits. Obtaining and paying for this is the stallholder's responsibility and must be completed prior to event application.
76.  For some events local councils may invoice PMM directly for food/beverage permits/inspections and these costs will be included in the invoice from PMM to the stallholder prior to the market.
77.  Where a stallholder is accepted to an event without current permits, no refund will be issued if permits are not issued and provided to PMM before the event.
78.  All certificates of registration and permits must be provided as part of the application process.
79.  Food and beverage vendors are required to produce a copy of their mobile food/beverage vendor's insurance.
80.  Stallholders must comply with current food safety regulations and food standards, including the Australian New Zealand Food Standards Code, the WA Food Act 2008, Local Council Environmental Health Services requirements applicable where the event is held, the Country of Origin Labelling Information Standard 2016, and any other regulations applicable to their goods, produce or products.
81.  All stallholders preparing food on site, particularly those using gas-powered equipment, must have an appropriate fire extinguisher and fire blanket. This also applies to stallholders cooking or heating samples for tastings, who should use a heat shield surrounding three sides of any hot plates or burners in use.
82.  All stallholders using refrigeration, eskies, ice, ovens or warmers should have an appropriate thermometer on hand to monitor temperature control.
83.  Food/beverage vendors must supply their own power to their stall unless discussed prior to the event with Market Management.
84.  Stallholders must comply with any host venue conditions of trade regarding compliance according to the venue. Failure to comply will result in an acceptance to an event being withdrawn.

### Privacy and Data

85.  PMM collects personal and business information from stallholders for the sole purpose of operating and administering its events and related business activities, in accordance with the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) and the Australian Privacy Principles.
86.  Stallholder information will not be shared with, sold to, or used by any third party for commercial purposes.
87.  Where a member of the public requests the contact details of a stallholder, PMM will only provide information that is already publicly available. Where contact details are not publicly available, PMM will pass the member of the public's details directly to the relevant stallholder, so that the stallholder can make contact at their own discretion.
88.  Stallholders have the right to request access to the personal information PMM holds about them, or to request that inaccurate information be corrected, by contacting PMM in writing via e-mail.
89.  PMM takes reasonable steps to protect stallholder information from misuse, interference, loss, and unauthorised access, modification or disclosure.

### Sale of Business

90.  Any stallholder who plans to sell a business that is operating at the Market must inform PMM in writing. The prospective buyer's suitability, and whether they meet the market's criteria, will be assessed by the Market Manager and remains at the Market Manager's discretion.
91.  It is preferred that the outgoing stallholder continue trading at the market until the incoming stallholder is ready to trade; otherwise, the outgoing stallholder may need to continue paying the full stall fee until the incoming stallholder commences trading.
92.  The outgoing stallholder should inform the incoming stallholder of the Market's requirements in relation to insurance, licences and permits, and should ensure the incoming stallholder is familiar with PMM's terms and conditions and application process.

### Use of Artificial Intelligence

93.  PMM does not accept applications from people who create art or products using AI. Products that are designed or generated, in whole or in part, using AI are not eligible for sale at PMM events.
94.  Applications that include AI-generated imagery, including product photos, mock-ups, renders, artwork and logos, may not be considered.
95.  PMM may review an applicant’s or stallholder’s website and social media accounts. Where PMM finds a heavy presence of AI-generated content, this may affect the acceptance of the application.
96.  Stallholders must not use AI tools to make false, misleading or deceptive claims about the quality, quantity, origin, materials or certification of their products.
97.  Products that are designed or generated by AI — for example, AI-generated artwork applied to a manufactured item — are not eligible for sale at PMM events.
98.  A stallholder found to be in breach of this section may be removed from the market and excluded from future events at PMM’s discretion.

### Other

99.  Any complaints are to be directed to PMM in writing via e-mail, unless the matter is urgent in nature. PMM aims to acknowledge complaints within five (5) business days.
100.  Stallholders and their staff are asked to refrain from playing music or other audio from any device before or during the market, out of respect for residents living near the market and to remain consistent with performing rights and APRA requirements.
101.  Images captured at PMM events, including images of stallholders and stallholder products, may be used by PMM as promotional material for media and publicity purposes, both online and in print. By applying to be a stallholder, you agree to images of yourself, your stall and your products being captured and used by PMM for promotional purposes. Stallholders who do not wish to have personal images of themselves used in PMM marketing may submit a written request to PMM, and this preference will be respected.
102.  Images supplied by stallholders to PMM may be used as promotional material by PMM for media and publicity purposes. By supplying images, you confirm that the images are yours, or that you hold an approved photographer's agreement for their use. If permission was not sought, any fees or royalties incurred for use of the image will be invoiced to the relevant stallholder.
103.  Stallholders are welcome to photograph and film their own stall and products during events for their own marketing and social media. Stallholders must be respectful of neighbouring stallholders and must not photograph or film other stallholders' products, displays or materials without their express permission. PMM takes no responsibility for any intellectual property or privacy disputes arising from unauthorised photography or videography between stallholders.
104.  Stallholders may have children accompany them at their stall during trading hours, provided the stallholder accepts full responsibility for the safety and supervision of any children in their care at all times. Children are not permitted at stalls where food or beverages are being prepared or cooked on site. During bump-in and bump-out, children must remain supervised and must not move freely around the market area, as this poses a safety risk to themselves and others. PMM accepts no responsibility for the safety or wellbeing of children accompanying stallholders at PMM events.
105.  Alcohol and drug consumption is strictly prohibited by stallholders for the duration of the market. No smoking is permitted within a stallholder's stall, and all smokers must adhere to smoking locations allocated by host venues.
106.  Due to the variety of venue restrictions and rules, stallholders are prohibited from bringing pets, with the exception of service animals.

### Limitation of Liability

107.  PMM is not liable for any damage, loss or harm that stallholders, or anyone working with stallholders, may encounter as a result of participation in the markets, including physical, psychological and economic harm. PMM is not responsible for any claims, actions, demands or suits that stallholders may face as a result of their conduct.
108.  Where disputes occur between participating stallholders in relation to any matter, including but not limited to Intellectual Property rights, PMM will not be directly involved under any circumstances. We kindly request that any such disputes be resolved offline, outside of market hours, and without the involvement of other stallholders, venue staff or PMM management. PMM is not responsible for the maintenance of copyright or Intellectual Property rights of any of our stallholders at any time.
109.  While all care is given where possible, PMM is indemnified from any theft, loss or damage to persons, money or goods as a result of participating in the markets.
110.  Stallholders will indemnify PMM from any damage, expenses or liability arising from any injury or damage to any person, including the general public, the stallholder or others, occurring in the space occupied by the stallholder, or elsewhere, arising out of or connected with that occupancy. PMM will not be liable for any loss or damage to a stallholder's property due to fire, robbery, accidents or any other cause arising from use and occupancy of the site. PMM assumes no liability for any damages or losses resulting from a stallholder's failure to comply with the provisions of this agreement, and will not be responsible where a current insurance Certificate of Currency has not been forwarded as required.
111.  Stallholders found in breach of any of the terms and conditions outlined within this document risk exclusion from events, determined at the discretion of PMM.

## SALA Awards & Opportunities

Find current and upcoming awards and opportunities here. Some are open to South Australian artists, and some are exclusive to artists & venues that are registered for the 2026 SALA Festival.

Check out the finalists and winners for the 2025 SALA Awards on our [Finalists & Winners](https://www.salafestival.com/finalists-winners/) page, or check out our [archive of winners from past years](https://www.salafestival.com/awards/past-awards/).

### EXCLUSIVE AWARDS & OPPORTUNITIES

The following awards & opportunities are open exclusively to artists and venues who are taking part in a registered exhibition or event in SALA Festival 2026.

## Guildhouse Artist's Choice Award

voting closed

Artists of any medium, age, or skill level are invited to vote for the SALA Award finalist whose artwork impressed them the most during the 2026 SALA Festival.

**Prize**: $1,500 cash + 12 Month Guildhouse Accredited membership.

**Dates**: Voting form will be open from Saturday 1 August  – Monday 31 August 2026 (11:59pm)  

Eligible Artists

Finalists of the 2026 SALA Awards are eligible for the Artist’s Choice award (and will be automatically featured on the voting form).

How to vote

The form will open for voting 1 August and close 31 August. The link to vote will appear on this webpage.

Key Dates 2026

**1 August** / voting opens

**31 August** / voting closes

**September** / Winner announced at SALA Finissage event (invitation-only)

[![](https://www.salafestival.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Guildhouse-Logo-300x79.png)](https://guildhouse.org.au/)

## SALA in Lights Award

applications closed

The SALA in Lights Award aims to illuminate the work of a South Australian visual artist taking part in the 2026 SALA Festival.

**Prize:** The winner’s artwork will be the subject of an after-dark projection on a prominent wall in the CBD during the 2027 SALA Festival with the support of Novatech (valued at $10,000). The winner will also receive $2,500 prizemoney from Foodland, a further $2,500 loaded onto a Foodland in-store Credit Card, and their artwork digitally displayed in Foodland Stores across South Australia in SALA Festival 2027.

**Applications open**: 3 March – Wednesday 13 May 2026 (11:59pm)

Eligible Artists

This award is exclusively open to artists who are participating in a registered SALA exhibition / event in 2026.

How to apply

The application form for the SALA in Lights Award will appear as a button on this page when applications open.

Key Dates 2026

**3 March** / applications open

**13 May** / applications close (11:59pm)

**September** / Winner announced at SALA Finissage event (invitation-only)

*   [Terms & Conditions](https://www.salafestival.com/sala-in-lights-award-terms-conditions/)

[![Foodland](https://www.salafestival.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/Foodland_IGA_TMSA_colour_cmyk_Full_Keyline-300x142.jpg)](https://www.foodlandsa.com.au/)

### Open for Applications

## Unitcare Services Digital Media Award

This award seeks to encourage experimentation in new media and is for artists working in digital art including computer, moving image, virtual, interactive, sound, and internet platforms.

**Prize**: $5,000  
**Applications open**: 1 March – Sunday 12 May 2024 (11:59pm)

Eligibility: 2024 SALA artists

Artists who are registered in the 2024 SALA Festival with work that is considered to be (or be connected to) ‘digital media’ may apply for this award at no cost.

This may include (but is not limited to):

*   computer art
*   moving image
*   virtual art
*   augmented reality art
*   interactive art
*   sound art
*   artwork presented online

Artwork submitted must:

*   have been created/completed since May 2023
*   not have been submitted to the 2023 SALA Awards
*   be displayed at the SALA exhibition/event noted in the form.

How to apply

Artists can apply for this award by logging in to the [SALA Online Portal](https://www.salafestival.com/artfuel/) from 1 March 2024. It is free and easy to create an account. 

Once logged in, click on ‘Awards’ in the left menu. Then click on ‘UnitCare Services Digital Media Award’ to open a new application form.

Draft application forms will appear at the bottom of the page as soon as you log in. Click the ‘edit’ button next to a draft to return to it. 

You will receive a confirmation email after you submit your award application. If you do not receive one, please get in touch with [SALA Festival](mailto:office@salafestival.com) to ensure that your award application submitted correctly.

Application form

The award application form will ask for:

*   The **registration ID number** for the exhibition/event that your submitted artwork will be featured in (eg: R12345)
*   a brief **statement** about your work (max 100 words)
*   an **image** or still of your work
*   **link** to your digital work or a preview of it (optional)

Key Dates

**1 March** / Award opens for applications  
**8 May** / Festival registrations close  
**12 May** / Award applications close  
**Late July** / finalists announced  
**1-31 August** / judging occurs during the Festival  
**September** / winner announced

More information

**Note to galleries**: Gallery staff and curators are encouraged to support their artists to make their own award application, rather than do it for them. 

**Judging**: Finalists will be determined (and announced) prior to the Festival based on the work supplied in the nomination form. Judging of the finalist artwork will take place during SALA 2024 and the winner will be announced at the conclusion of the SALA 2024.

## About the South Australian Living Artists (SALA) Festival

The South Australian Living Artists (SALA) Festival is a statewide festival of visual art taking place across South Australia annually, during the entire month of August.

The SALA Festival was established in 1998 to promote and celebrate the many talented visual artists in South Australia. The aim was -and remains- to extend visual arts audiences, and as an umbrella organisation, we have continued a policy of inclusiveness allowing all South Australian visual artists of any level and working in any medium to be part of our annual SALA Festival every August.

Founded by Paul Greenaway OAM (Director, Greenaway Art Gallery) and Sam Hill-Smith through the Australian Commercial Galleries Association (ACGA) it started as SALA Week in 1998. The Festival now spans the entire month of August, involving over 700 venues across the state and over 10,000 participating artists.

As part of our commitment to building new audiences for the visual arts, SALA began offering art tours. This started in 2002 as an way to encourage office workers to visit galleries in their lunch breaks. Today, SALA presents a diverse offering of tours and events -including bus tours to regional areas and bilingual tours.

SALA Festival also continues its dedication to creating and supporting opportunities for visual artists by liaising with sponsors and partners to offer a series of awards and residencies. 

**Purpose**

SALA is a state-wide showcase and celebration of South Australia’s living visual artists.

It culminates in Australia’s largest and most inclusive visual arts festival, which takes place in galleries and non-traditional arts spaces across South Australia annually, during the entire month of August.

Each year, SALA takes the work of around 8,000 emerging, mid-career and established South Australian artists to more than 500 venues across the state (from sheds, cafés, offices and retail spaces to wineries, schools, public spaces, galleries and major arts institutions) to reach local and inter/national audiences of more than 850,000 people, and many more online.

**Vision**

South Australian visual artists working at any stage of career and in any medium are able to make, share and receive recognition for their work.

South Australian communities and audiences are enriched and inspired by their engagement with South Australian visual art, including the large number of ‘incidental’ arts audiences for whom SALA’s local exhibitions is their first point of engagement with the arts.

SALA is a vibrant and valued part of all South Australian communities, and inter/nationally recognised as a diverse, democratic and inclusive visual arts champion that enhances our own and the world’s understanding of this unique place and our pride in the art it creates.

**Approach**

ARTIST-CENTRIC                
South Australia’s living visual artists are at our heart.

INCLUSIVE                            
Our democratic, open-access model includes South Australian visual artists working at every level, in any medium, from all backgrounds and all parts of the state.

CONNECTED                        
We listen and respond to our artists, connect and engage with our communities, and work in collaboration with our colleagues and partners.

SUPPORTIVE                       
We support and nurture South Australian visual artists and audiences, create pathways, amplify their voices, and advocate on their behalf.

INNOVATIVE   
We are curious and innovative, always learning and evolving.

ETHICAL                                
We are professional, respectful and accountable.
