## Feature Artist

Every year, an established South Australian artist is celebrated as the SALA Feature Artist.   
This artist’s work features on the SALA poster and printed program, and will be exhibited during the SALA Festival. 

The 2027 SALA Feature Artist, **Jane Bowden**, was announced by Sarah Andrews MP, Assistant Minister for Arts, at the 2026 SALA Finissage event.

### 2027: Jane Bowden

Jane Bowden is an established South Australian artist whose practice has helped shape the field of contemporary jewellery for more than 35 years. Since graduating in Jewellery and Metalsmithing from the University of South Australia in 1990, Jane has developed a sustained and evolving practice grounded in material exploration, conceptual inquiry and community engagement.

Her work investigates the adaptability of traditional craft and textile techniques to metalsmithing, opening up jewellery as a space for experimentation, connection and meaning. As co-founder of Zu design, jewellery + objects in Adelaide, Jane has also played an important role in supporting independent makers and strengthening South Australia’s creative landscape.

*   [@janebowden\_zu](https://www.instagram.com/janebowden_zu/)

read more

The awarded 2027 CreateSA Monograph is intended as both a critical reflection and a forward-looking platform. Rather than simply functioning as a retrospective, the publication will trace the evolution of Jane’s practice while illuminating the current and emerging ideas that continue to drive her work. It will accompany two significant exhibitions planned for 2027 and will give curators, collectors, educators, peers and wider audiences a deeper understanding of her contribution to contemporary Australian jewellery.

The monograph will also be a strategic tool for Jane’s future practice: supporting national and international engagement, strengthening future opportunities, and contributing to the visibility of contemporary jewellery from South Australia.

Jane will be working with a thoughtful team of writers, editors and designers. **Rebecca Evans**, Curator of Decorative Arts and Design at the Art Gallery of South Australia, will write on Jane’s work with the depth of knowledge she brings to contemporary jewellery and the AGSA collection. **Dr Eleen Deprez**, philosopher of art, independent curator and writer, will bring a broader philosophical lens, considering materiality, technique and the relationships between making, meaning and connection. **Ingrid Goetz**, Vernon-Roberts Assistant Curator of Decorative Arts and Design at AGSA, will contribute as an emerging writer, supported through mentoring by Rebecca Evans and Leigh Robb. **Penelope Curtin** will bring her experience as a freelance editor, and **Rachel Harris** of Bit Scribbly Design will lead the graphic design, shaping the monograph into a visually engaging and thoughtful publication.

Together, this team will help create a publication that not only documents Jane Bowden’s achievements, but also opens a new space for reflection, dialogue and future development. The monograph marks a significant milestone in Jane’s career and an investment in the next phase of her artistic practice.

![](https://www.salafestival.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/SALA_Finissage-Event_Sep4-2026_-324_LoRes-1024x683.jpg)

Sarah Andrews MP, Assistant Minister for Arts, Jane Bowden, Bridget Alfred, and Alexandrea Cannon OAM. photo: Sam Roberts

### 2026: Troy-Anthony Baylis

Born in Sydney in 1976, Troy-Anthony Baylis is a painter, textile artist, installation artist and performance artist.

A descendant of the Jawoyn people from the Northern Territory and of Irish ancestry, Baylis’ multi-faceted artistic practice is founded in the process of ‘queering’ and unsettling ‘traditional’ ways of representing Aboriginality.

*   [@btroyanthony](https://www.instagram.com/btroyanthony/?hl=en)

read more

Troy-Anthony has exhibited widely across Australia and internationally, having installed, exhibited and performed across New Zealand, the Philippines, Iceland, Spain, and Germany.

His work has been subject of 24 solo exhibitions and numerous group exhibitions, performances, and publications since 1993. Baylis’ work was profiled in The National 2019: new Australian art at Carriageworks, Sydney. Recent institutional solo exhibitions include Nomenclatures (Art Gallery of South Australia, 2020-2021) and I Wanna Be Adorned (QUT Art Museum, 2023).

He has upcoming projects in Adelaide, Brisbane, and Wollongong, and is currently represented by Jan Manton Gallery, Brisbane. He has lived and worked in Adelaide for the past 25 years.

![](https://www.salafestival.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/photo-of-Troy-Anthony-Baylis-by-Daniel-Mudie-Cunningham-supplied-by-Troy-Anthony-768x1024.jpg)

### Celebrating the work

A closeup of an artwork by Troy-Anthony Baylis work is celebrated on the **Official SALA Festival Poster** and on the cover of the **2026 SALA Festival Program.**

Troy-Anthony Baylis will also be the subject of a high quality book about his practice, with contributions from local writers Tikari Rigney and Sasha Grbich. This book will be produced by [Wakefield Press](https://www.wakefieldpress.com.au/) and is an outcome of the [SA Living Artist Publication opportunity](https://www.salafestival.com/projects/south-australian-living-artist-publication/), supported by Create SA.

![closeup of a green and pink textile artwork with a gray background and the SALA logo](https://www.salafestival.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/SALA-26-poster-A2-FA_final-768x1081.png)

#### The Book

_**Troy-Anthony Baylis: Let it bleed  
**_Sasha Grbich, Tikari Rigney, Troy-Anthony Baylis

Troy-Anthony Baylis: Let it bleed represents a long overdue major monograph on the art of Troy-Anthony Baylis, compiling imagery from most major periods of the artist’s oeuvre including rarely seen and unpublished images. By doing so the publication draws interconnections between work that spans more than three decades of continuous practice.

Available from [Wakefield Press](https://www.wakefieldpress.com.au/product/troy-anthony-baylis/) (Hardback, $59.95)

read more

The artistic practice of Troy-Anthony Baylis has included performances, videos, paintings, collages, assemblages, photography, knittings, embroidery, artist multiples, costumes, installations, parade floats and more. His work explores a multitude of themes including colonisation, migration, trauma, racism, sexism, homophobia, sadness, reconciliation, dark and seemingly self-deprecating humour and unbridled joy.

Often employing a bold use of colour and typography, the artist references pop culture, art history, and queer aesthetics across a range of disciplines including visual art, cinema and literature. In addition to art making, his creative practice sometimes involves curating, publishing writing and presenting public talks.

As the recipient of the Arts South Australia South Australian Living Artist Publication grant, Sue’s art practice will be the subject of a high quality book published by Wakefield Press and to be written by Elle Freak (Associate Curator, Australian Paintings & Sculpture, Art Gallery of South Australia), James Tylor (Kaurna & Māori multi-disciplinary visual artist), Andrew Purvis (curator at Adelaide Central School of Art gallery) and emerging artist and writer Nicole Clift.

[![](https://www.salafestival.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/9781923388758-252x300.jpg)](https://www.wakefieldpress.com.au/product/troy-anthony-baylis/)

## Sell your work with Shop SALA

Shop SALA is platform for South Australian visual artists to show and sell their work. 

[Register as a Shop SALA Artist](https://artists.shopsala.com.au/register)

## What is Shop SALA?

[Shop SALA](https://www.shopsala.com.au/) is a new online sales platform for South Australian artists to utilise throughout the year and was created to address the diminishing opportunities for artists to sell and show work in the state. SALA facilitates safe transactions for both buyers and sellers and manages the promotion of the platform to our existing and expanding global audience.

Our platform is not-for-profit which is integral to our mission to support South Australian visual artists to make, share and receive recognition for their work. All sales commissions go back into the maintenance and promotion of Shop SALA and to the organisation’s work in championing South Australian living artists.

## Frequently Asked Questions

How do I sell my work on ShopSALA?

1.  [Create an artist account](https://artists.shopsala.com.au/register).
2.  Upload artwork (to be approved by a member of the SALA team)
3.  Artwork is listed as for sale on ShopSALA, ready to be purchased.

Does SALA take comission on sales?

Artwork sales go to the artist and the commission received goes directly back into the not-for-profit Shop SALA platform, and to support artists in various initiatives led by SALA.

What happens if my artwork is being exhibited while it is on sale on shopSALA?

Shop SALA is a platform for all-year-round, but is extra useful for selling work in your SALA exhibition. You can use the QR codes as shown in the video above, making the work available to buy in person or online, without doubling up! You can also advise how long the exhibition runs for, to manage delivery expectations.

description: WOMADelaide – the World Of Music Arts & Dance in Adelaide – is an iconic open-air festival celebrating cultural discovery in the heart of Adelaide’s stunning Botanic Park/Tainmuntilla. The World’s Festival, since 1992, WOMADelaide is a truly unique part of the Australian festival landscape, showcasing the best, the essential, and the surprising, in music, arts, dance and ideas from around the world.

# FAQs

### Find all the answers to frequently asked questions below.

## About WOMADelaide

**What is WOMADelaide?**  
WOMADelaide is a music, arts and dance festival featuring artists from all around the world. It is held every March long weekend in Adelaide’s stunning Botanic Park/Tainmuntilla and has been enjoyed by generations for over three decades. ‘WOMAD’ is an acronym for ‘World of Music, Arts & Dance’. It is a charitable foundation and group of international arts festivals originating in the UK, now held throughout the world.

**Who’s on the lineup?**  
Please see our **[lineup page](https://www.womadelaide.com.au/lineup/ "Lineup")** for details on the festival lineup. Artist playing days are announced in December, with the full timetable announced in February ahead of the festival in March.

**How can I get involved?**  
Please see our **[apply page](https://www.womadelaide.com.au/apply/ "Apply")** for volunteer, stallholder, artist, media and employment information. If you’d like to support us in achieving our ambitious cultural, community and sustainability initiatives, see our Support page.

## Ticketing Information

**Purchasing tickets**  
1, 2, 3 or full 4 Day Tickets to WOMADelaide can be purchased online and are released in stages whereby the earlier you buy, the cheaper the ticket. Visit our **[tickets page](https://www.womadelaide.com.au/tickets/ "Tickets")** to purchase tickets and find all information on ticket types, gift vouchers, group bookings, companion cards, payment plans, refunds, exchanges and more.

[Book Now](https://www.womadelaide.com.au/tickets/ "Tickets")

**Wristbands**  
Ticket purchasers will be allocated a unique barcoded wristband; this wristband is your entry and exit to the festival and cannot be removed. For all information on wristbands and postage, visit our **[tickets page](https://www.womadelaide.com.au/tickets/ "Tickets")** or see your postage status in your **[account](https://www.womadelaide.com.au/account/ "Account")**.

**Box Office**  
WOMADelaide Box Offices are located at the Hackney Road and Frome Road entrances during the festival dates and are open at the following times. Please have a valid ID and your order number ready when arriving at the Box Office.

*   Friday: 3pm–10pm
*   Saturday–Monday: 12pm–10pm

## Getting to the festival

**Where is WOMADelaide?**  
WOMADelaide is held in the stunning **[Botanic Park/Tainmuntilla, Plane Tree Drive, Adelaide, South Australia](https://maps.app.goo.gl/ZWhiWL274uyWwbvJ7)**. Entry to the festival is through the gates on either Frome Road or Hackney Road.

**When is WOMADelaide?**  
WOMADelaide 2027 is held from Friday 5 to Monday 8 March, with gates open at the following times:

*   Friday: 4pm – midnight
*   Saturday: 12pm – midnight
*   Sunday: 12pm – midnight
*   Monday: 12pm – midnight

**Bike parking**  
Bike parking is made available for patrons adjacent to each entrance. Please ensure that you bring your own bike lock to secure your ride in the allocated parking area. Bike parking will be monitored by security during the following times, please note there is no overnight monitoring: 

*   Friday: 3.30pm – 1am
*   Saturday: 11.30am – 12:30am
*   Sunday: 11.30am – 12:30am
*   Monday: 11.30am – 12:30am

**Public transport**  
The Adelaide Metro Loop Bus service timetable and map can be found **[here](https://www.adelaidemetro.com.au/plan-a-trip/free-and-special-transport/city-connector)**. All other Adelaide Metro tram and train timetables can be found [**here**](https://www.adelaidemetro.com.au/). 

**Car parking**  
There is no on-site car parking available at the festival. We urge patrons to consider reducing their carbon footprint where possible and use public transport.

If driving, you can secure parking with **[UPark](https://www.upark.com.au/)**. Pre-book for night and weekend parking at UPark Rundle and UPark Frome, convenient and affordable parking that’s open 24 hours and only a short walk to Botanic Park/Tainmuntilla.

**Can I come in and out?**  
Yes, pass-outs are available. If you plan to return to the festival on the same day, please make sure you scan OUT when leaving the site, and scan IN at the gates when returning.

**Conditions of entry**  
All conditions of entry can be found **[here](https://www.womadelaide.com.au/terms/ "Terms")**.

## What can I bring?

**What to bring**  
Here’s what to bring on your trip to WOMADelaide:

*   Your wristband (or your booking reference number/confirmation email to show at the Box Office)
*   Valid photo ID
*   Sun protection — hat, sunnies, sunscreen, sun scarf
*   Medication (especially for allergies and asthma, the park can get dusty at times)
*   Clothes that suit the weather
*   Sturdy shoes for walking around the park
*   A reusable empty water bottle
*   Your phone with the **[WOMADelaide app](https://www.womadelaide.com.au/info/app/ "App")** downloaded and a portable charger
*   An open mind, WOMADelaide is full of surprises!

  
**Prohibited items**  
The following items are not allowed in the festival. Please see our Conditions of Entry for more information.

*   Alcohol, liquids, glass bottles and containers
*   High-back chairs
*   Illegal substances
*   Knives and weapons
*   Oversized umbrellas
*   Professional cameras (anything with a detachable lens)
*   Tents (only pop-up sunshades can be used and must not block pathways or views of performances)
*   Your furry family member (except registered assistance and companion animals)

**Structures and seating**  
Tents and high chairs are not permitted in the park and will be confiscated at the gates, unless a pre-approved exemption has been authorised.

Small pop-up shades and low beach-style chairs are permitted at the back and sides of audiences only, unless it’s a ‘seated’ performance. Blocking walkways, obstructing views, and saving spots with chairs, shades, rugs and blankets at a performance that is not ‘seated’ is prohibited. These items can create safety hazards for large crowds and a Crowd Control volunteer may ask you to move.

**Is there camping?**  
There is strictly no camping on site at WOMADelaide as the venue is part of the Botanic Gardens of Adelaide.

**Please take your belongings**  
Your belongings must travel home with you each night. Anything left unattended in the park will be disposed of.

## Families

**Can I bring my children?**  
Yes! In fact we have an entire zone dedicated to them — **[KidZone](https://www.womadelaide.com.au/lineup/kidzone/ "KidZone")**. It’s full of nature-play activities and art for all ages, be sure to check out the program.

Find out more about children and youth tickets on our [**tickets page**](https://www.womadelaide.com.au/tickets/ "Tickets").

**Is there a parenting room?**  
Parents with babies and toddlers can enjoy a shaded, comfortable parenting room next to the Info Booth near the Foundation Stage. Chairs and baby changing facilities are provided. See our [**map here**](https://www.womadelaide.com.au/info/map/ "Map").

**Children’s safety**  
All children aged 3 and over must be wristbanded prior to entering the festival. We advise that you write the responsible adult's mobile number clearly on the wristband and arrange with children to meet at the Info Booth if they get separated.

All lost children/persons are taken to the Info Booth. Parents/guardians, please report a missing child/person at the Info Booth — see our [**map here**](https://www.womadelaide.com.au/info/map/ "Map").

## At the festival

**Map & App**  
Explore the **[WOMADelaide Map here](https://www.womadelaide.com.au/info/map/ "Map")** or download the official [**WOMADelaide App here**](https://www.womadelaide.com.au/info/app/ "App") to plan your trip to The World’s Festival.

**Cashless**  
WOMADelaide is a cashless event. Accepted cards are Visa, MasterCard, or pre-paid debit cards, processing EFTPOS and PayWave/PayPass.

**Bag check-in**  
Bag check-ins are located at both the Frome Road and Hackney Road entrances. A $3 donation is required to use the bag check-in, with all proceeds donated to the WOMADelaide Foundation. All items are left at your own risk, WOMADelaide takes no responsibility for items left behind.

What you can check in:

*   Handbags
*   Small bags
*   Day-packs

What you can’t check in:

*   Valuables (e.g. wallets, purses, phones, cameras, signed Peter Gabriel vinyl)
*   Coats, jumpers and loose items of clothing
*   Prams and strollers
*   Open bags (e.g. shopping bags)
*   Sun shades, chairs and blankets

The bag check-in will close at midnight each day.

**First aid**  
First Aid tents are located between the Foundation Stage and Stage 2. There is also a pharmacy located next to the First Aid tent between the Foundation Stage and Stage 2. **[See the map here](https://www.womadelaide.com.au/info/map/ "Map")**.

**Water**  
BYOB bottle and stay hydrated! Check the [**map**](https://www.womadelaide.com.au/info/map/ "Map") for free water stations located around the park, thanks to SA Water.

**Smoking and vaping**  
In keeping with the South Australian Government health regulations, WOMADelaide is a smoke-free event. Festival-goers wishing to smoke or vape will be able to do so in designated smoking/vaping areas marked on the [**map**](https://www.womadelaide.com.au/info/map/ "Map").

**Info booth**  
Visit the Info Booth for all general enquiries, directions and lost property, located between Foundation Stage and Stage 2 — see the **[map](https://www.womadelaide.com.au/info/map/ "Map")** here.

**Missing persons**  
Please report any lost children/missing persons to the Info Booth. Any lost children/missing persons will be escorted there. We advise parents/guardians to write their mobile number on their child’s wristband and arrange to meet at the Info Booth if separated.

**Flying foxes**  
The grey-headed flying foxes found in the park are a vulnerable species protected by law. Hot weather may cause stress to the flying foxes, so there are sprinklers in the trees in Speakers Corner to help keep them cool. If you see a flying-fox on the ground or in distress, do not approach it. Please tell a WOMADelaide staff member who will assist.

**Care for the park and each other**  
Do not climb, hang on to, or damage the trees or plants in Botanic Park/Tainmuntilla. 

Please be mindful of other people’s enjoyment during performances. If you need a moment to catch up and have a yarn, there are many open spaces and bars nearby.

Any person behaving in an inappropriate manner towards other patrons or staff will not be tolerated. If someone is behaving inappropriately, please talk to the closest security guard, staff member or volunteer.

**Please return your cups**  
Place used cups in the blue cup return bins around the park, or at the bars and exits. All cups are washed on-site and re-used at the festival.

## Accessibility

**Accessibility entrances**  
An accessible parking and drop-off zone is located next to the Hackney Road entrance. Both entrances have a dedicated accessible entrance to assist in a smooth entry for those with mobility issues. The site is very large, and it can take some time and energy to get from one part to another. We recommend you plan your day with this in mind.

**Access platforms**  
Access platforms are provided near the three main stages — Foundation Stage, Stage 2 and Stage 3. These are raised platforms for people with disabilities who may need to sit down while watching a show, or use mobility aids. Please note they can fill up quickly for popular shows, so plan to arrive ahead of time for performances.

**More access information**  
Please visit our **[access page](https://www.womadelaide.com.au/info/accessibility/ "Accessibility")** for our full Access Guide. The guide provides access information about step-free paths, sensory access and facilities, as well as a detailed overview of the event. It is created by Access2Arts in collaboration with WOMADelaide.

**Asthma**  
Botanic Park/Tainmuntilla can become dusty. We advise anyone who suffers from asthma to bring your medication and make note of the nearest first aid tent in case you need assistance. For more information on asthma first aid, please visit [**Asthma Australia's website**](https://asthma.org.au/).

## Lost property

**Lost property at the festival**  
Lost property will be taken to the Info Booth on site. If you have lost anything please check there first.

**Lost property after the festival**  
After the festival, all credit cards will be destroyed and valuable items will be kept for no longer than two weeks.

If you have lost a valuable item, please contact **[info@womadelaide.com.au](mailto:info@womadelaide.com.au)** with your full name, phone number and a clear description of your item. We will get in touch if we have the item.

Flotsam needs volunteers in a range of roles to make the festival all it can be.

Volunteer to be a driving part of Flotsam Festival’s success – can you help out in a ticketing booth at a venue, help direct people on our installation trail, usher at our movie nights, or help us bump in or out of venues?

If you said yes to any of the above (or have completely different skills to bring to the table) we’d appreciate your help!

It’s not all just about work. Volunteers get an incredible insight into what goes on behind the scenes at a festival. You’ll get to watch and enjoy events, meet other locals and visitors, and be a part of a festival that celebrates our beautiful coastal lifestyle through film and photography.

We currently have openings for:

Social Media, PR or Marketing volunteers

Sound like your jam? Come join our fam!

What skills do I need to volunteer?

We encourage people from all backgrounds and ages to apply to volunteer. If you can offer a friendly smile, love to meet + greet people, and have time free that you’d like to dedicate to the festival, then we would like to hear from you. Of course, if you have relevant applicable skills for specific roles during the festival be sure to note them on the web form too.

How do I apply?

Applications to volunteer are open, fill in the web calendar above or hit us through the website contact form and our team will be in touch.

What type of day-to-day roles will volunteers have?

Volunteers will play many important roles – on any given day you could be providing directions and information, recommending installations or events in the program, and ensuring the public have a safe and enjoyable experience. Beyond visitor services, we’re always in need of helping hands for office duties, moving equipment, setting up events, and more – all the moving parts of the festival could always do with extra hands. Join us and get an exclusive behind-the-scenes peek into the inner workings of an event, connect with the local community, make friends with like-minded people and enjoy the ‘feel-good’ factor volunteering brings.

# Faq’s

![#](https://flotsamfestival.com.au/wp-content/themes/flotsam_arts_inc/assets/images/black-square.svg)

Got a question or query? We’ll try answer common ones here, but if you’re still unsure hit the contact button + send us a message.

How is Flotsam Festival taking COVID-19 restrictions into consideration?

All events will be delivered within Queensland Health’s COVID Safe Events framework. Patrons should register using the Check In Qld app when attending events.

Don’t attend events if you are experiencing symptoms. Our COVID safe planning will be modified to align with changing government directives – please check in with us via social and this website for latest updates.

Do I need to wear a face mask at Festival events? What about social distancing?

The rules around mask wearing are ever changing, however please carry a mask at all times, and wear a mask if you are unable to socially distance.

Keep 1.5m between yourself and others. You may attend events in your social or household group. Keep distance between yourself and other attendees.

And please, stay home if you are unwell or have a cough, fever, sore throat, fatigue or shortness of breath.

Will Flotsam Festival refund tickets if I need to cancel due to COVID?

Some events in our schedule are partner events, but for full Flotsam events we will provide a refund or exchange if you advise before the event that you or any other members of your booking party are:

a) required to isolate or quarantine under laws aimed at reducing the spread of COVID-19 (and the event falls withing the isolation/quarantine period)

b) diagnosed with COVID-19;

c) exhibit symptoms of COVID-19 (e.g. fever, chills or sweats, cough, sore throat, shortness of breath, runny nose or loss of sense of smell)

d) have been in close contact with anyone displaying COVID symptoms; or

e) have been tested for COVID-19 and are awaiting results.

Do audience members need to be vaccinated to attend Flotsam Festival events?

Since the **17th December**, visitors to entertainment venues in QLD have been required to be fully vaccinated to attend.

We are working to ensure that our festival adheres to all Queensland Health COVID requirements, as the health and safety of our attendees, volunteers and team is our top priority.

Attendees will be encouraged to check-in using the Queensland Government mobile app, ‘Check In QLD’ this ensures we’re providing a COVID safe environment for not only our attendees but the wider community. Our team will continue to monitor the ever-changing environment and continue to provide updates via our website and social media channels should there be any changes to festival programming.

# About Us

![#](https://flotsamfestival.com.au/wp-content/themes/flotsam_arts_inc/assets/images/black-square.svg)

Flotsam Festival is an annual showcase delivered by not-for-profit association Flotsam Arts Inc.

The festival was devised by local film makers and photographers in 2022.

You see..

Border restrictions during the pandemic affected all industries, but the creative and tourism communities along border regions like the Southern Gold Coast were particularly hard hit.

Creating a festival that could provide a platform to celebrate this coastline, nurture our creatives, and give people a reason to extend their stays in the region seemed like a win-win.

London, Berlin, New York, and Madrid all have surf film festivals. Yet despite being home to many of the world’s most iconic surf breaks and surf-inspired filmmakers, unlike the aforementioned cities the Gold Coast didn’t – until now.

Enter Flotsam, a surf film and photography celebration aiming to explore the creative side of surf culture via an eclectic mix of pop up short film installations, photography exhibitions, movie screenings, workshops and photo meets.

![Flotsam (n.)\_ etymology](https://flotsamfestival.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/Snapper-at-Night-web2.jpg)

### Flotsam (n.)\_ etymology

Emerging in the early 17th century from Anglo-Norman French floteson, from floter ‘to float’.

c. 1600, from Anglo-French floteson, from Old French flotaison “a floating” (Modern French flottaison), from floter “to float, set afloat” (of Germanic origin and cognate with [float](https://www.etymonline.com/word/float?ref=etymonline_crossreference)) + -aison, from Latin -ation(em). Spelled flotsen in English till mid-19c.

The festival name was chosen for it’s ability to convey that even if we feel discarded or get washed overboard by bigger circumstances sometimes, eventually we’ll float.

![Aims](https://flotsamfestival.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/Ted-Grambeau-2.jpg)

### Aims

Flotsam aims to assist the local arts sector by providing a platform to showcase cultural and creative activities and events.

Developed in response to the economic impact that COVID-19 restrictions have had on the QLD border region of the southern Gold Coast, the festival was set up by newly formed Flotsam Arts Inc – a not for profit incorporated arts association.

![The festival has three main goals:](https://flotsamfestival.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/IMG_6891.jpeg)

### The festival has three main goals:

\+ To support surf filmmakers and photographic artists and their work, with a long-term goal to provide ongoing opportunities to retain artists in these fields.

\+ To generate increased economic activity in the southern Gold Coast tourism sector, with flow-on effects for all local businesses.

\+ To celebrate the southern Gold Coast’s iconic beaches and endemic surf culture through creative, visual events that bring together the local community as well as the wider surf and creative communities at large.

![As they say, a rising tide lifts all ships](https://flotsamfestival.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/upcoming-8.png)

### As they say, a rising tide lifts all ships

Playing with the theme ‘to float’, Flotsam aims to raise the profile of ocean-inspired creatives, lift the fortunes of southern Gold Coast traders, buoy the spirits of festival goers from all corners of the globe, and ensure the southern Gold Coast is awash with creativity for years to come.

![Flotsam Arts Inc](https://flotsamfestival.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/ocean-art-print-ted-grambeau-SL.196.4331.jpg)

### Flotsam Arts Inc

Flotsam Art Inc’s Founding members included various photography and film artists, tourism and event specialists to form the initial working committee:

\+ Peter ‘Joli’ Wilson

\+ Trent Mitchell

\+ Simon ‘Shagga’ Saffigna

\+ Dave Emge

\+ Royce Leu

\+ Kath Gourley

\+ Sonya Mroz

\+ Caz Ridings Emge

## Our Events Crew

### Kath Gourley

Event manager

Current Event Manager at Miami Marketta, one of the Gold Coast’s most popular arts venues. Kathy has decades of experience over seeing successful events and tours for international brands and artists.

*   
*   
*   

### Sonya Mroz

Tourism Engagement

Owner of Coolangatta-based Aspect Tourism, Sonya has 20+ years of experience working with businesses such as Minor Hotels, Currumbin Wildlife Sanctuary, Lady Elliot Island and has held board positions for Japan Tourism Gold Coast and the Australian Tourism Export Council.

*   
*   
*   

### Royce Leu

Branding Consultant

Royce, co-owner of Leu Creative, has a slew of related experience shaping surf and event design – Royce was previously a longtime designer at Australia’s Surfing Life magazine and Billabong, with clients including Burleigh Brewing and Blues On Broadbeach. 

*   [](https://www.instagram.com/leucreative/)

# Venue Application Form

Would your business/venue like to apply to be part of FLOTSAM Surf Film and Photography Festival this year?

We’re looking for spaces to hold pop up photography exhibitions, short film premiers, workshops or live music during the lead up to the major surf events in the region.

Staged like a giant interactive arts trail, Flotsam Festival is an exciting two-week season of sea-inspired cinema run by non-for-profit organisation Flotsam Arts Inc. In 2022 the festival saw over 27,000 visitors across 22 event sites. As a platform to support the region’s artists by exhibiting in existing places, Flotsam’s decentralised nature means that your business will be a hotspot during the festival.

By working in collaboration with both your venue and the artist, Flotsam customises each event to facilitate the most effective outcome for both parties.

![Join the Club](https://flotsamfestival.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/3d77dfadfe0bf995a2ee-1682082968.jpg)

For the Flotsam Snapper Snapper Social Club, the fun doesn’t stop when the festival ends – it’s pumping all year round! For just $55 a year, you’ll unlock discounts on tickets, workshops, and exclusive happenings, monthly member-only giveaways and a community of legends who love the coast as much as you do.

![Your membership includes](https://flotsamfestival.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/Flotsam25_Tee-Concept.pdf-e1744592298396.png)

– A limited-edition Flotsam photo tee (valued at $59)  
– Complimentary access to a Flotsam Festival premium ticketed event (valued up to $39)  
–  A collectable membership keyring (valued at $15)  
–  VIP offers + venue discounts  
–  Plus the feel-good buzz of supporting a grassroots, not-for-profit surf festival.

**This offer is for a limited time only. Help us dream big and ride even bigger waves – hit the link and join today!**

Finals Day at the Noosa Festival of Surfing delivered everything — flawless conditions at First Point, a packed beach, and an incredible showcase of surfing across every division.
From the legends to the next generation, the level of surfing across the board was nothing short of world-class.
In the WSL Noosa Longboard Pro, Nic Brewer claimed the men’s title with a 14.50 total in a tight final over Clinton Guest and Kai McPhillips, while Malia Ilagan took out the women’s with a commanding 15.80, continuing her incredible run through the event.
The Logger Pro divisions brought timeless style to the finals stage, with Declan Wyton taking out the men’s with a standout 18.17 total, and Sophia Culhane winning the women’s in a close, high-quality final.
In the Twin Fin, Tim Bain edged a stacked field with a 14.33 total, just ahead of Micha Margieson and Ashton Pignat in one of the most exciting finals of the day.
Across the age divisions, the depth of talent and legacy of the sport was on full display:
Jack Norton took out the Over 40s
Glen Gower claimed the Over 55s and backed it up with a win in the Old Mal (Masters)
Tony Abood won the Over 65s
Wally Allan secured the Over 60s
Earle Page took the Over 75s in a tight tiebreak finish
Chris Prewitt won the Over 50s
Matt Chojnacki edged a close win in the Old Mal (Mixed)
Jon Lavers claimed victory in the Over 70s
The World Surfaris Women’s HP Longboard saw Alana Johnson take the win in a super tight final, while Declan Wyton also doubled down to win the World Surfaris Men’s HP Longboard.
From elite WSL competition to grassroots divisions, this was the Noosa Festival of Surfing at its absolute best — high performance, deep heritage, and a community that shows up year after year.
An all-time day at First Point.

# FAQs

Thank you for your interest in attending the Noosa Festival of Surfing as a competitor or visitor. Below is a list of frequently asked questions. If you’re unable to find the answer to your question below, please contact us with your enquiry.

*   [ALL](https://www.noosafestivalofsurfing.com/faqs/#all)
*   [SURFING COMPETITORS](https://www.noosafestivalofsurfing.com/faqs/#surfing-competitors)
*   [BEACH BAR](https://www.noosafestivalofsurfing.com/faqs/#beach-bar)
*   [GETTING TO THE EVENT](https://www.noosafestivalofsurfing.com/faqs/#getting-to-the-event)
*   [Surfing Dogs Event](https://www.noosafestivalofsurfing.com/faqs/#surfing-dogs-event)
*   [Associated Events](https://www.noosafestivalofsurfing.com/faqs/#associated-events)
*   [General Event Information](https://www.noosafestivalofsurfing.com/faqs/#general-event-information)
*   [Accommodation Options](https://www.noosafestivalofsurfing.com/faqs/#accommodation-options)

## SURFING COMPETITORS

How do I register to compete?

You can register via our official website. Check the home page for the registration link or simply [**REGISTER HERE.**](https://events.humanitix.com/2026-noosa-festival-of-surfing/tickets?_gl=1*9bucf*_gcl_au*MTYzNDEyNzUwNS4xNzYxNTcyOTcxLjEyNDkyOTIxMDcuMTc2NDkwNTUzMi4xNzY0OTA1NTMy*_ga*MTczNDA1OTgyNy4xNzYzMDA3Njkx*_ga_LHKW5FR9N6*czE3NjczMjk4OTEkbzMzJGcxJHQxNzY3MzI5OTQ5JGoyJGwwJGgw)

What divisions are available?

We offer a range of divisions including Junior & Senior age divisions, Masters, Pro, and specialty events such as the Old Mal and Twin Fin. A full list is available on our website or through the registration portal.

When and where are heats posted?

Heat schedules will be published online approximately 7-10 days before the Festival starts. We use Live Heats for our surfing schedule and scoring system. This information will be displayed at the event site. You can also request surfing times from the marshalls or contest director.

What equipment is allowed?

Equipment regulations vary by division. Ensure your board complies with division-specific rules. Contact us for details.

Where can I find the rules and judging criteria?

You can find more information [HERE](https://www.noosafestivalofsurfing.com/terms-conditions/)

What if I need to withdraw from the Festival?

This information can be found in the Festival terms and conditions [HERE](https://www.noosafestivalofsurfing.com/terms-conditions/)

What if I miss my heat?

Unfortunately, due to the number of competitors we can’t make any promises that we can find you another spot. But, our event staff will do their best to place you in an available heat or a repechage round should one exist for your division.

How are competitors seeded in their respective divisions?

Our team of contest directors and head judge will coordinate seedings based on existing domestic or international rankings and previous results in the festival. This approach is in line with Surfing Australia rules.

How is prize money determined?

If prize money applies to your entered division, we will provide this information prior to the Festival commencement. The Noosa Festival of Surfing believes in equal prize money across both mens and womens divisions and pays prize money within 30 days post festival completion.

Where is the best place to stay up to date with surfing conditions, locations and other information?

 Everyday, we will update our social media page with the ‘official call’ for the days surfing activities. We will also share important updates on the [Competitors Forum](https://www.facebook.com/groups/447671223123013) on Facebook.

## BEACH BAR

Where is the Beach Bar located?

The Beach Bar is conveniently located near the main event site in front of the Noosa Surf Club.

What dates does the Beach Bar operate?

In 2026, the beach bar will operate from 13th – 22nd March.

Do I need a ticket to get in?

No! the beach bar is completely free to patrons. There are SOME ticketed events for the beach bar in 2026 but we pride ourselves on making it as inclusive and affordable as possible.

What are the opening hours?

The bar operates daily from 12 PM to 8 PM, with 2 main bars, catering, live music and other entertainment.

Is the Beach Bar family-friendly?

Yes! Families are welcome, but patrons must be 18+ to purchase or consume alcohol.

What drinks are available?

We offer a selection of craft beers, wines, cocktails, and non-alcoholic beverages.

What type of food is available?

We cater to all dietary requirements and have a range of delicious food options from loaded fries, burgers, wraps, salads and more.

Is there an option to book a private area in the beach bar?

Yes. We offer a private lounge experience for up to 12 adults including table service. The cost is $300 to secure your booking.

Is the beach bar wheelchair accessible?

Yes. We recommend that your equipment is suitable for sand. Our bar staff are available to assist in any way to make you comfortable.

Does the beach bar accept cash and card?

Yes. We accept both forms of payment, however, please be aware that our cash float is limited and you may be asked to pay by card.

Does the beach bar remain open if its raining?

We have never closed the beach bar due to rain. There is ample space undercover to escape the odd shower.

## GETTING TO THE EVENT

Where is the festival located?

The primary surfing site is at First Point, Noosa Heads, with the beach bar located in front of the Noosa Surf Club. We also have events occurring at nearby locations. This information can be found [HERE](https://www.noosafestivalofsurfing.com/whats-on/)

Is there parking available?

Limited parking is available around Hastings Street and along Noosa Parade. However, we highly recommend using public transport, ride-sharing services or other forms of transport such as an e-bike.

Are there public transport options?

Yes, local buses service the area throughout the festival dates. Check [TransLink’s](https://translink.com.au/travel-with-us/around-queensland/noosa) website for routes and schedules.

Can I bring my bike?

Absolutely! Bike racks are available near the festival site.

Shuttle Services from airports? If you are flying into Brisbane or Sunshine Coast airports, we recommend using [con-X-ion airport transfers](https://www.con-x-ion.com/) or [Joel’s Journeys Airport Transfers.](https://joelsjourneys.com.au/airport-transfers)

## SURFING DOGS EVENT

When is the Surfing Dogs event?

The famous Surfing Dogs competition takes place on the opening weekend. Check the [‘Whats-On’ schedule](https://www.noosafestivalofsurfing.com/whats-on/) for specific times.

Can my dog participate? 

Yes, but you must register in advance with [VetShopAustralia](https://www.vetshopaustralia.com.au/). Ensure your dog is comfortable in the water and on a surfboard before applying.

What safety measures are in place?

We provide life vests for dogs and have lifeguards on duty to ensure a safe experience.

Is there an entry fee?

There is no entry fee for spectators.

What is the best way to view the surfing dogs?

Get to the beach early, find a nice vantage point on the rocks at First Point or along the shores edge where the dogs zoom past.

## ASSOCIATED EVENTS

What other events are part of the festival?

Expect to see art shows, live music, surf film screenings, surf based trivia nights, health workshops, charity lunches or dinners and community activities such as the [Locals Day](https://www.noosafestivalofsurfing.com/events/locals-day-by-ripcurl/). Details are on our website.

Are these events free?

Some events are free, while others require tickets. Check the schedule for specifics.

Where can I buy tickets?

Tickets are available online and at designated box offices during the festival.

Can I host an event?

We welcome community collaborations. Contact us via email to discuss your idea.

## GENERAL EVENT INFORMATION

When is the Noosa Festival of Surfing?

The festival runs from March 13th to 22nd, 2026.

Is the festival family-friendly?

Yes, the festival is designed for all ages, with activities for kids and adults alike.

Can I volunteer at the festival?

Absolutely! Volunteer applications are open on our website [HERE](https://www.noosafestivalofsurfing.com/volunteers/)

Do you offer paid positions?

Yes, we have a variety of paid hospitality positions available. You can apply to work in the beach bar [HERE](https://www.noosafestivalofsurfing.com/bar-staff-questionnaire/)

I would like to perform at your Festival. How do I apply?

Musicians and other performers are welcome to register an expression of interest on our website [HERE](https://www.noosafestivalofsurfing.com/musician-application/)

What happens in case of bad weather?

We aim to proceed rain or shine, but safety is our priority. Updates will be communicated on our website and through social media.

Who can I contact for more information?

For general inquiries, [Contact Us](https://www.noosafestivalofsurfing.com/contact-us/)

## ACCOMMODATION OPTIONS

What is the best area to stay?

For the best access to the Festival, restaurants, cafes and bars you should definately try and stay around Hastings Street or in Noosa Sound. The Noosa Festival of Surfing works with Ocean Breeze Resort, Bella Casa & Saks on Hastings but there is ample accommodation options around Noosa including Noosaville, Tewantin, Sunshine Beach and Peregian Beach.

Where is the best place to do grocery shopping?

Noosa Junction is the closest area for groceries with a Coles supermarket, bakers delight, butcher, chemist/pharmacies all in close proximity. Noosaville also has access to similar infrastructure.

# ABOUT

From humble beginnings in 1992, the Noosa Malibu Club’s annual ‘Noosa Malibu Classic’ longboarding event had become a fixture on the international longboard contest calendar. By 1996, and in 1998, in partnership with Phil Jarratt Communications Pty Ltd, the Noosa Festival of Surfing made its debut.

![A surfer wearing a blue shirt and black shorts balances on a wave under a cloudy sky, with the ocean reflecting the light of the setting or rising sun.](https://www.noosafestivalofsurfing.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/DSC_6721-6-2.webp)

![Surfers carrying boards on a sandy beach, with many people surfing and waiting in the waves. The sky is overcast, and mountains are visible in the background.](https://www.noosafestivalofsurfing.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/image-about1.webp)

## FESTIVAL ORIGINS

The festival, loosely based on the popular Biarritz Surf Festival in France, was a huge hit, with big contingents of surfers and their families coming from all the great surf centers of the world, including Hawaii, California, New Zealand, Japan, and Europe.

Since 2010, the Noosa festival has attracted record levels of competitors each year, as well as thousands of spectators from near and far who come to see the legends of the sport, as well as the now world-famous surfing dogs. 

## THE FESTIVAL TODAY

Under the guidance of World Surfaris, the Noosa Festival of Surfing has now evolved into a family-friendly, sustainable event that appeals to all kinds of surfers of all ages. A reunion for the veterans and a starting point for the juniors, it is the longest-running and best-loved surf event in the world.

The ever-popular beach bar, live music, art shows, shaping exhibitions, World Surf Reserve activations, and of course world-class surfing are several reasons why this event is a highlight for many around the world every year!

![Three men in tank tops and swim trunks walk along the beach carrying surfboards. Two shake hands while waves roll in behind them under a clear blue sky.](https://www.noosafestivalofsurfing.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/image-about2.webp)

ⓒ Noosa Festival of Surfing 2026

# THE TEAM

Our Festival wouldn’t be possible without the staff and volunteers who make it all happen. With 6+ months of planning and organising in the background to deliver this amazing world-class surf contest, popup beach bar, and all the other Festival activations happening around Noosa. Our team is dedicated and passionate about creating and sustaining this long and illustrious Surf Festival for the community to enjoy.

Originally from Sydney’s Northern Beaches, Josh saw the light and moved North to the Sunshine Coast in 2015.

With a background in Logistics and Marketing, it’s no wonder Josh excels at planning, organising, and managing events for a living.

A larrikin with a well-guided head on his shoulders, Josh is a people person and a professional operator that wants nothing more than to put smiles on people’s faces as they enjoy the events he works overtime to deliver.

Since taking over in 2019, Josh has managed to pull off some of the most memorable Festivals. Despite challenging surf conditions, Covid, managing 400+ surfers and a beach bar, it’s a miracle Josh still has enough time to raise a young family!

![Josh Allen](https://www.noosafestivalofsurfing.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/EG-Google-Listing-16-9.webp)

#### Josh Allen

Festival Director

READ BIO

John is the owner of World Surfaris, who had been a sponsor of the Noosa Festival of Surfing for many years.

When management of the Festival became available at short notice in 2018, John didn’t hesitate to commit and has taken the Festival to new heights implementing several groundbreaking initiatives.

Adamant that long term sustainability was to be a key element in the Festival’s future, John eliminated all single-use plastics in the first year and also introduced a Sustainability Pledge and Report.

More the elder statesman these days, John is never backward in leading by example in all Beach Bar activities and plays an important role in pre-tasting all our suppliers before the Festival.

![John Finlay](https://www.noosafestivalofsurfing.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/NFOSweb.webp)

#### John Finlay

Festival Chairman

READ BIO

Laguna Bay Longboards & Shotgun Surfboards are brands synonymous with the Noosa and Sunshine Coast surfing fraternity since the 1970s.

After traveling Australia and the world, Tully’s father, Mike lured a young Tully back into the shaping bay where the father & son combination began.

In all his spare time, Tully takes the reigns coordinating 400+ competitive surfers for the annual Noosa Festival of Surfing.

For 3 weeks Tully lives and breaths tides, currents, swell, wind, and what the sand is doing to ensure our surfers are surfing the best waves and giving them the greatest opportunity for success.

![Tully St John](https://www.noosafestivalofsurfing.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Copy-of-Tuesday-Highlights-7-scaled-1.webp)

#### Tully St John

Contest Director

READ BIO

Glen Gower is the quintessential Noosa local having grown up on Hastings Street in the 60′s and early 70′s. This upbringing started Glen’s addiction to Noosa and it’s world-famous surf breaks.

Back then, Glen shared his playground of Noosa main beach and it’s world class point breaks with just a handful of his best mates and siblings. Moving to Sunshine Beach in 1974 (thought to be the end of the earth in those days!!), Glen found that surfing the Opens with little or no company was both fun and scary at times. “I am truly grateful and humbled by my blessed surfing life and my biggest thrill is sharing special days in the surf with friends and especially my family”

Surfing perfect Noosa point waves has been described as like having a cup of tea with god, if so then I have had to top up my cup hundreds of times over 40 years of surfing Noosa”.

![Glen Gower](https://www.noosafestivalofsurfing.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Wednesday-Highlights-11-1.webp)

#### Glen Gower

Noosa Malibu Club President

READ BIO

If being a professional surfer is the best job in the world, then being a professional surf contest judge is a likely second?

Keenan is a seasoned judge with several years of experience judging a variety of comps from longboard world tour events on the WSL to local boardriders at a deserted beaches on the weekend.

With arguably the hardest job out of anyone involved with the Festival. Keenan takes it all in his stride and is a true professional.

Over the years Keenan has experienced a pivotal shift in the longboarding scene paying homage to the Noosa Festival of Surfing for being a big reason why innovation and delineation between traditional log events and performance longboarding have become obvious.

![Keenan Roxburgh](https://www.noosafestivalofsurfing.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Keenan-roxburgh-head-judge.webp)

#### Keenan Roxburgh

Head Judge

READ BIO

A multi-talented young entrepreneur from Sydney’s Northern Beaches, Charlotte is no longer a fresh face to the Noosa Festival of Surfing team. After leading the social media for the 2025 festival and supporting across event delivery and content editing, she returns in 2026 to help manage the full marketing campaign. If you saw The Scoop in action last year, you would’ve met Charlotte!

With experience across multiple industries, including a stint in the WSL’s Production Department, Charlotte brings creativity and professionalism to everything she does. Her background in large-scale events and music festivals, combined with her passion for social media and brand storytelling, makes her a natural fit for the surf scene.

If you see Charlotte pointing a camera your way, smile and wave!

![Charlotte Lerpiniere](https://www.noosafestivalofsurfing.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/WhatsApp-Image-2026-03-07-at-17.33.07-e1772865938192.webp)

#### Charlotte Lerpiniere

Marketing Manager

READ BIO

Behind every great livestream is a killer production crew and that’s where Panga Productions comes in. Shaun and Carol Cairns, along with their team, handle everything from onsite videography to the festival’s daily content drops and live stream broadcast.

They’ve become part of the Noosa Festival family, capturing the magic year after year. If you see them chasing winning surfers or coming out of the water post heat, make sure to smile for the camera. You might just make the highlight reel that drops every day.

Also, proud parents to rising surf talent Coco Cairns who competes in the festival.

![Shaun Cairns, Carol Cairns + the Panga Productions team](https://www.noosafestivalofsurfing.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/1-1.webp)

#### Shaun Cairns, Carol Cairns + the Panga Productions team

Production Team

READ BIO

Be nice to Stuey, there’s every chance he could be saving your life one day. Stuey is our resident water patrol, first aid officer and Brad Pitt wannabe, whose job it is to patrol the lineup and keep a safe contest site.

Although Stuey spends more time-saving members of the public than competitors. His presence and a happy smile are appreciated by all.

On a serious note, Stuey is a professional lifeguard patrolling several Sunshine Coast beaches and is a very good surfer himself competing in a handful of the pro divisions and usually doing quite well.

![Stuart Jeays](https://www.noosafestivalofsurfing.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Copy-of-Thursday-20th-8.webp)

#### Stuart Jeays

First Aid & Water Patrol

READ BIO

Every festival team needs a man like Glenn!

Glenn has been our site manager since 2021. Being 6’6″ in stature helps big Glenny with his role at the festival.

A gentle giant, Glen is quite often seen laughing in between jobs around the comp site or making sure the beer is cold in the bar. A super reliable resource for the Festival.

![Glenn Currie](https://www.noosafestivalofsurfing.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/2.webp)

#### Glenn Currie

Site Manager

READ BIO

A name that has become synonomous with Australian longboarding and surfing in general is Matt ‘the waxhead’ Chojnacki or as we like to call him Chonno!

An extremely accomplished surfer and surf coach, Chonno has been competing at the Festival since he was a grommet and has since created a unique and successful career for himself most notably as a regular on the commentary panel at WSL events both shortboard and longboard. What makes Chonno so great to listen to is his way of breaking down surfer styles and analysing their surfing so it makes sense to the purests as well as the newbies.

When he’s not articulating the abundance of surf styles on the mic, Chonno is often smashing heat after heat on his way to another final and podium finish of his favourite events like the Logger Pro and the Old Mal.

![Matt ‘the waxhead’ Chojnacki](https://www.noosafestivalofsurfing.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/DSC_7922-1.webp)

#### Matt ‘the waxhead’ Chojnacki

Head Commentator (& multiple divisional winner)

READ BIO

Hailing from NZ and now a familiar face (and voice) in the Noosa surf scene, Caelen Pitt stepped into the commentary booth in 2025 and immediately made his mark. A protégé of the iconic Matt “Waxhead” Chojnacki, Caelen brought fresh energy, insight and a juniors love of logging to our livestream.

When he’s not on the mic, you’ll find Caelen in the lineup himself, a talented surfer who knows the community from the inside out.

Some of you may know him from his rise to fame in a new segment we call The Scoop which launched in 2025. Interviews with members of the public, festival go-ers, competitors, salty characters and everyone in between made The Scoop the most highly watched social media segments during the festival.

Cone or cup?

![Caelan Pitkeathly](https://www.noosafestivalofsurfing.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/4.webp)

#### Caelan Pitkeathly

Commentator

READ BIO

# SSF Art SESSION

### 26 MAy 2026

## Enjoy the works of Paul Mcneil, Karlee Mackie, Otis Carey, JAKEY PEDRO and more

### Opening Night

We will celebrate the opening night of the SSF Art Session with works from Paul Mcneil, Otis Carey, Karlee Mackie, Jakey Pedro, Peter Webb, Jason Woodside, Adrianne Dimitrakakis, Niah Mcleod, Daniel Watkins, and Bowen Hopper. With art, live music, complimentary drinks and light bites it will an amazing evening.

**When:** 26 may, 6:00 - 9:00pm

**Where:** HOTA CENTRAL, 135 Bundall Road, Surfers Paradise

[rsvp here](https://partiful.com/e/TInMW7GXAJamt5gd2ucG?c=F6fJKqNI)

Don’t worry if you can’t make opening night, the exhibit will be up all week so stop by any time from 10am - 4pm, 27 May - 30 May.

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/67c778602535fe5237cd32af/77328b7a-4d2f-4f0f-9611-9290a94405c0/ARTSHOW_Solento+51.jpg)

## Meet the artists:

### PAUL McNEIL

Born in NZ, now based in Byron Bay. McNeil's career spans over 40 years.

An original Mambo artist, Paul has published several kids books, co-founded The Art Park and designed endless graphics on Surfboards, skateboards, clothing, album covers, merchandise and tour posters including The Clean and The Rolling Stones.

The last two years have seen relentless solo exhibitions in Sydney, Tokyo, San Francisco, Auckland, Hobart, Christchurch, Bali, Byron Bay and Portugal.

Continuing his early humorous and witty Mambo days, simplicity is the backbone to his ongoing works. Personal truths, localism, music, politics, humanity and surfing show up in these vibrant paintings and sculptures.

#### BEAKER STREET FESTIVAL RETURNS AUGUST 2027 TO LUTRUWITA/TASMANIA. MAKE SURE TO [SUBSCRIBE](https://beakerstreet.com.au/subscribe) FOR UPDATES.

![](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/Beaker-Street-Logo.svg)

Beaker Street is a cultural organisation and registered charity in Lutruwita/Tasmania with science and community at its heart.

The brainchild of a fun-loving evolutionary biologist, Beaker Street is pioneering a new model of science engagement, where diverse adult audiences are welcomed into scientific thinking and discovery, with a generous serve of merriment, and a distinctly Tasmanian twist.

Since our launch in 2017, our core offering, [**Beaker Street Festival**](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/festival/), has evolved from a nerdy night out into a prominent two-week festival and Australia’s premier National Science Week event every August.

Beaker Street produces science & art experiences year-round, including [**CoLab**](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/co-lab/), [**Science Photography Prize**](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/photography-prize/), [**Hobartica Cultural Embassy**](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/hobartica/), [**Roving Scientist Program**](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/roving-scientist-program/), and seasonal [**Field Trips & Retreats**](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/seasonal-field-trips/).

##### ABOUT BEAKER STREET FESTIVAL

# A winter festival for curious adults

Imagine a place where scientists grace centre stage, microscopes live on bar tables, and late-night conversations have the potential to change the world. Welcome to Beaker Street Festival, where science brings us together.

Held each August in Lutruwita/Tasmania, Beaker Street Festival brings nearly 20,000 people together across more than 70 events mixing science, art, culture, big ideas, and the best of Tasmanian environments, food, and drink. Returning for its 11th year in 2027, the Festival invites adults from all walks of life to join crucial conversations about the topics shaping our lives through dinners, field trips, performances, talks, experiments, and the chance to have a drink and a chat with nearly 200 participating scientists.

Past participants include Australian astronaut **Katherine Bennell-Pegg**, **Dr Karl**, Nobel Laureate **Prof Brian Schmidt**, **Wendy Zukerman**, **Adam Spencer**, **Tegan Taylor**, **Dr Kirsten Banks**, Mona founder **David Walsh**, and many other leading voices in science and culture.

Beaker Street Festival is presented by [Beaker Street](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/about), a DGR-endorsed not-for-profit organisation based in Lutruwita/Tasmania, working to build community through scientific understanding.

#### [View Previous Programs](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/festival/#prevprograms)

# Do I need to be “into science”?

### Not at all. Most Beaker Street audience members are not scientists.

The Festival is designed for people who are curious about the world, enjoy learning new things, and like experiences that are a bit different from the usual festival offering. The program is created for adults, but there are a few family-friendly events as well.

People come to Beaker Street because it feels different. You can show up with friends for a fun night out, then accidentally leave thinking differently about the Universe, technology, nature, your own brain, or the future of humanity.

If you enjoy good storytelling, fascinating conversations, live events, food, nature, art, music, or clever people saying surprising things in pubs, you’ll feel very much at home.

#### [Subscribe for updates](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/subscribe)

# A truly Tasmanian festival

### Beaker Street Festival could only exist here.

Tasmania has an unusual concentration of scientists, artists, makers, environmentalists, and adventurous people packed into a small island at the edge of the world. Hobart is Australia’s gateway to Antarctica, surrounded by mountains, waterways, wilderness, and some of the clearest skies on Earth. It also boasts more scientists per capita than any other Australian city. 

The Festival draws energy from all of that.

Beaker Street spills out into the city and the landscape itself. Scientists are waiting to mingle in pubs. Events unfold across the waterfront. Regional experiences take you into forests, coastlines, observatories, distilleries, farms, and dark sky locations across the state.

It feels local, atmospheric, and unmistakably Tasmanian.

### GET INVOLVED. We’re always looking for fine folks to support our work and help create the magic.

[VOLUNTEER](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/volunteer/)

[DONATE](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/donate/)

[JOIN OUR CREW](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/jobs/)

## Previous Programs

### [2026](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/festival/#)

At a time of reckoning and reinvention for humanity, our 2026 Festival’s theme, “The Second Act”, is a provocation to interrogate our assumptions, invite debate, ask harder questions, and reaffirm our connection with each other, in real life. Oh, and maybe have some fun too.

[View Program](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/BSF26_Program_V6.0_OP2-screen.pdf)

### [2025](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/festival/#)

Wild Ideas, Curious Adventures, and Nerds. Beaker Street Festival 2025 took a welcome detour into new territory, discovering better ways to live and smarter ways to die, and offering up plenty of opportunities to party (including cameos from entertainment powerhouses Myf Warhurst, Dr Emse Louise James, and Michael Hing). Hobartica also went next-level, with Antarctic rituals, Celestial Concerts, a Cultural Embassy and nightly talks and jazz.

[View Program](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/BSF25_Program_4.0-screen.pdf)

![](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/2025lookback.jpg)

### [2024](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/festival/#)

Introducing: Hobartica! Take a deep-dive into Antarctica, without leaving a trace. Including Polar Plunge pools, Finnish Sauna Tents, Antarctic audioscapes, and loads of Antarcticans to answer all your coldest questions. Plus, a futuristic mashup of space, AI, food and wellness trends, with a healthy dose of nature excursions and an east coast retreat.

[View Program](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/BSF_Digital-Program_V1.0.pdf)

![](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/2024lookback.jpg)

### [2023](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/festival/#)

Psychedelics, Menopause, and Tim Flannery were part of our 2023 Featured Speaker Sessions at Hobart’s Theatre Royal Studio Theatre, with Fungi Expeditions, Bat Tours, and Museum Vaults included in our Field Trips – the best way to experience Tasmania’s hidden secrets and wild places. Seaweed and Vaginas were on the menu at Mona, and our Dark Sky Retreat at Spring Bay Mill was an unforgettable exhale.

[View Program](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/BeakerStreet_ScreenProgram_V8.pdf)

![](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/2023lookback.jpg)

### [2022](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/festival/#)

Is science really for everyone? In 2022 we took at deep dive into the cultural complexities of science, with discussions from the Tasmanian Aboriginal community, the Deaf community, and a musical exposé expressing the wishes of the dead. We also went north, with events exploring the science of stadiums, sparkling wine, and sauerkraut.

[View Program](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Festival-Program.pdf)

![](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/2022lookback.jpg)

![](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Thirsty-Nerd.svg)

# History

## WOMADelaide: The World's Festival since 1992

Over the past three decades, WOMADelaide has evolved from a daring experiment to a unique and essential part of the Australian festival landscape. Held amongst the trees of Botanic Park/Tainmuntilla, WOMADelaide — the World of Music, Arts & Dance in Adelaide — is one of Australia’s most loved festivals. Growing from just three stages to eight, thousands of artists from every corner of the world have performed in the park since 1992.

WOMAD was co-founded in 1982 in England by Grammy-winning musician **Peter Gabriel**; with a dedicated fanbase, the festival became a worldwide name. “It's brilliant to have an audience that cares so much about what WOMAD is, could be, and stands for,” says Gabriel. “In a world in which many bad actors seem to be achieving power by fanning the flames of hatred, racism and division, a meeting place for all the world’s cultures and dreams, built on mutual respect, seems all the more precious.”

This is the basis of a festival that has stood the test of time through multiple iterations around the world — community, cultural celebration, and music.

Initially staged biennially from 1993, in alternate years to the then-biennial Adelaide Festival, WOMADelaide moved to an annual cycle in 2004, and expanded to become a four-day event from 2010. Held over the March long weekend, returning revellers reserve the sun-soaked four days in their calendars every year for a world of discovery, unforgettable moments, and connection. 

Over its 35-year history, WOMADelaide has been home to extraordinary performances, memorable moments beneath the trees, and rich cultural experiences. Masters of their craft have graced the stages, from **Sinéad O’Connor** to **Peter Gabriel**, **Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan**, **Crowded House**, **Florence + The Machine**, **Yothu Yindi**, **Grace Jones**, **PJ Harvey**, **Ravi Shankar** and hundreds more. Beyond the stages and [Around the Park](https://www.womadelaide.com.au/lineup/around-the-park/ "Around The Park"), WOMADelaide has also welcomed dance, theatre, and large-scale performance installations – from **Luke Jerram’s** awe-inspiring inflatable world, _Gaia_ and **Gratte Ciel’s** spectacular _Place des Anges_, to the 4-metre-tall wandering puppets of **Company Archibald Caramantran,** and the visually and musically stunning masterpiece _The Manganiyar Seduction_. 

A pioneer in [sustainability](https://www.womadelaide.com.au/about/initiatives/sustainability/ "Sustainability"), WOMADelaide has led the way in environmental initiatives, becoming the first South Australian festival to achieve all stages powered by 100% renewable energy, among many other milestones. As an independent charitable foundation, WOMADelaide has introduced countless [initiatives](https://www.womadelaide.com.au/about/initiatives/ "Initiatives") to support industry, culture, and local communities.

WOMADelaide is more than just a festival. It’s a celebration of our shared humanity, a meeting place where generations of families, friends and artists return.

## 1992–2002

Botanic Park/Tainmuntilla was acquired by the adjacent Adelaide Botanic Garden in 1866 and developed as a lush arboretum into an extraordinary wonderland: the native plants. The springy couch grass. The oaks, elms and ghost gums, and majestic Moreton Bay Figs.

But in 1992 came further magic, hints of an event so visionary, so spectacular, that it would change the face of a city and open the ears and hearts of a nation.

There amid the 34-hectare expanse were three separate stages. Sound checks charged the air with curious tones: the slap and boom of a West African djembe; the heavenly octaves of Sufi Qawwali singing; the ethereal beauty of a Chinese dizi bamboo flute.

‘WOMADelaide Festival 1992’ read banners decorated with a lion logo and geometric slashes of red and green.

When the gates opened, a crowd of adults and kids poured in for what the Adelaide Festival billed as ‘a spectrum of world sounds in one weekend.’ People knew headliners **Crowded House** and **Paul Kelly**. But **Youssou N’Dour** from Senegal? Pakistan’s **Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan**? A Chinese flautist named **Guo Yue**? This was a voyage of discovery, a leap into the unknown.

Organisers took a punt on that first WOMADelaide. Presented as part of the 1992 Adelaide Festival in a joint venture with the UK-based WOMAD organisation – and with sponsorship from the National AIDS campaign (“Play safe stay safe”) – WOMADelaide was guided by a faith in music’s ability to connect. To promote peace, love and cultural understanding.

![](https://cms.womadelaide.com.au/media/fm4pscvb/web_2560x1440_1992.jpg?anchor=center&mode=crop&width=768&height=340&format=png&quality=90)

_The gates open on history_

### **From England to the World**

WOMAD (World of Music Arts and Dance) had been co-founded in England a decade earlier by the Grammy-winning rock musician **Peter Gabriel**: “Music is a universal language,” said Gabriel early on. “It draws people together and proves, as well anything, the stupidity of racism.”

Not that Rob Brookman, as incoming Artistic Director of the 1992 Adelaide Festival, had heard of WOMAD when he considered programming a mini-festival of music from elsewhere, to be staged outside the confines of the concert hall.

“The Internet didn’t exist back then,” he says. “There was no email. I was flicking through \[British entertainment newspaper\] _The Stage_ when I saw a tiny article about a music festival called WOMAD happening in the UK. I thought, ‘That’s exactly what I’ve been thinking about doing’. So I sent off a fax.

“I flew over and met Thomas Brooman, WOMAD’s Artistic Director, at a WOMAD event in Morecombe Bay in northwest England,” he continues. “I remember how fantastically exciting it was to see an audience embracing music that perhaps they weren’t aware of.”

Brookman was on a mission to take WOMAD to the world. As well as the main festival in Reading outside London (now in Wiltshire) and its now defunct Morecambe Bay event, there were WOMADs in Spain and Singapore and countries yet to come. A WOMAD in Adelaide – WOMADelaide, as subsequently named by festival Marketing Manager Colin Koch – made sense.

Besides, something was in the ether in Australia in 1992. Alongside the inaugural Big Day Out in Sydney, WOMADelaide heralded a new era of large-scale outdoor events with multiple stages and a multiplicity of voices. Festivals that would eventually dispense with the need for headliners, evolving to become brands guaranteeing quality, variety and life enhancing good vibes.

“WOMADelaide was a huge bonus for the Adelaide Festival and so far from the mainstream approach,” says Koch. “Even Neil and Tim Finn from **Crowded House** seemed in awe of all the unknown talent and at the last minute decided to do a stripped back acoustic set.”

Brooman and Brookman created a line-up of artists they sourced from the existing WOMAD circuit and Brookman’s contacts, folding in several acts – **Paul Kelly**, Indian violinist **Dr L Subramaniam**, the **Mapapa Acrobats of Kenya** – booked to play the Adelaide Festival. A site was found at Belair National Park, 13 kilometres south of the city. But with a few weeks to opening, and with the location printed in the program and on the tickets, organisers were told that if the weekend coincided with a Total Fire Ban, the park would stay closed.

Ian Scobie, Administrator of the Adelaide Festival, was tasked with finding a new venue, fast: “I got into my car with a Gregory’s Street Directory and drove around,” he says. “When I passed Botanic Park, which was run by the Botanic Gardens, who we’d already worked with, I thought, ‘Wow.’”

For Paula Henderson from WOMAD, Botanic Park was a revelation. “It was the most beautiful site I’d ever seen, and a vision after the longest flight I’d ever been on,” she says, having obtained visas for, and flown down from London with, artists including Tanzanian singer/composer **Remy Ongala** and **Guo Yue** (“A character; he was so bored on the plane that he washed his socks in the sink”).

WOMADelaide shared similarities with its mothership. There was the official lion logo. The Global Village of food, retail and community stalls. But unlike WOMAD in the UK there was no camping. Arts-based projects – dance, installations, orchestras, roaming performers and large-scale performance – morphed from the Adelaide Festival. Stage crews came with theatre resumes. Things happened on the ground, in the park, not just on the stage.

“It had the feel of WOMAD,” says Henderson. “But it also had its own identity.”

In uniqueness and scale WOMADelaide offered a perfect example of what festivals could achieve. It even wooed the neighbourhood: “One of my roles was to drive out to nearby residential areas like Hackney and St Peters and assess the noise spill,” says Colin Koch. “I’ll never forget the serene sound of **Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan’s** voice floating across the rooftops. People were out in their gardens, rapt.”
