### **Spontaneity Pays Off**

WOMADelaide was only meant to be a one-off, an Adelaide Festival highlight. But with crowd enthusiasm palpable, organisers jumped onstage on closing night and pledged that it would return the next year as a stand-alone festival.

“Which was a bit rash,” says Brookman, who, following his (then customary) biennial stint as director of the Adelaide Festival, became Programming Director of the Adelaide Festival Centre. “A lot of fancy footwork had to be achieved.”

And so it was. “Colin, Rob and I went to see Mike Rann, who was Minister for Tourism at the time and a huge supporter of what we were doing,” remembers Scobie. “He personally wanted **Peter Gabriel** to come and provided a guarantee to help make it happen. It was a major moment in securing WOMADelaide’s future.”

Presented by the Adelaide Festival Centre, WOMADelaide 1993 was buoyed by commitment from government at State, Federal and local levels, sponsors including the International Year for the World’s Indigenous People initiative, and by media who appreciated that great music came from everywhere. Artists that year ranged from British Asian diva **Sheila Chandra** to Malian crooner **Salif Keita** and indeed, former **Genesis** frontman and A-lister **Peter Gabriel**.

“We were so lucky to get Peter,” says Brookman. “He had a rare free date in his diary the weekend before he was attending the Grammys, our weekend, so we shared the travel costs.

“If 1993 hadn’t worked,” he adds, “then WOMADelaide would have been over.”

A village fair atmosphere was part of WOMADelaide’s early charm; ‘Come and meet your neighbours’ was a tagline coined by Koch. Still, its existence depended on meeting box office targets. The small revenue made in 1993 became risk capital bolstering the next WOMADelaide in 1995 – an alternate year to Adelaide Festival (and the year Stage 4 was created).

Those gap years were peppered with often unprofitable, albeit creatively brilliant, events. Most notably, the 1996 WOMAD Indian-Pacific train trip from Perth to Adelaide, an all-aboard adventure with a stop-off concert at the remote settlement of Pimba. Passenger/performers included the **Bauls of Bengal**, Tuvan throat-singing ensemble **Shu-De**, Scottish band the **Well Oiled Sisters** and – collaborating with all en route – **Paul Kelly**.

“I sat down with Australian National Railways and talked them into giving us a train,” says Colin Koch, whose idea it was. “The journey with those musicians was a once-in-a-lifetime experience, a real hoot. The best 50K we ever lost.”

There were one-off projects at, variously, the Sydney Opera House, Melbourne’s Myer Music Bowl, Perth’s Belvoir Amphitheatre and the vineyards of McLaren Vale outside Adelaide. WOMADelaide’s influence continued to spread; in 1997 the first WOMAD New Zealand ‘sister event’ was staged in Auckland on the weekend after WOMADelaide, with the event relocating to New Plymouth in 2005.

By this time events company Arts Projects Australia (APA) had been formed by former Adelaide Festival colleagues Brookman, Brown, Koch and Scobie. For a few years APA presented WOMADelaide in partnership with the Adelaide Festival Centre (then with the Government of South Australia and later, with South Australian Tourism). By 1999, WOMADelaide was part of the fabric of its host city. A glorious cornucopia of sound, sight and taste. A microcosm of a world we all wanted to live in.

A world with a KidZone children’s area, a WoZone nightclub (presented off-site until 2004), giant silk flags by British visual artist **Angus Watt**, a fifth stage and a good-natured ambience that was carefully nurtured: “Part of building the ethos of the festival was establishing a sense of relationship,” says Brookman. “We tried to keep as many musicians as possible onsite across the weekend, even if they had no further performances.” 

One of my favourite moments was the football match that erupted backstage when Irish band **Kila** got out a soccer ball. Members of **Baaba Maal’s** Senegalese band joined in dressed in their flowing robes and before long there were about 35 people playing. No sides, no goals, just lots of passing the ball around.”

A sense of intimacy continued to prevail. Workshops brought artists up close and encouraged people to engage with each other. Shared environmental concerns were seen, heard, and validated by WOMADelaide 2001 – Australia’s first major ‘green festival’. That same year, the United Nations Year of Volunteers, 18 volunteers operated the Information Booth. **Angus Watt** worked with **Anangu Pitjantjatjara Yankunytjatjara** women artists to create new flags that stood, rows and rows of them, fluttering in the golden Adelaide light – as if acknowledging victories won, and heralding spectacular things to come.

## 2002–2012

By its second decade, WOMADelaide was a brand. A byword for quality. A guarantee of good times. An acronym – World of Music, Arts and Dance – that did what it said on the tin. No matter if you didn’t know, or couldn’t pronounce, many of the names on the bill. Each artist was a gift and very often, a discovery. Each opened a window onto a living culture, to stories from near and far, to traditions both ancient and modern.

Having come on board via the Adelaide Festival, critics and journalists had their horizons broadened. Their affection for WOMADelaide, and their understanding of sounds from around the world, developed and grew.

“Lying on the grass in Adelaide’s beautiful Botanic Park, surrounded by huge and ancient fig trees and listening to great music is as close to heaven we can hope for in this lifetime,” wrote Bruce Elder in _The Age_ in 2003 – the year that WOMADelaide went annual.

Like the crowds, back the media came each year. Waxing ecstatic about the music of the planet. About the classical orchestras and dance companies; the roving performers and visual art installations; the workshops and children’s parade and huge al fresco spectacles.

“WOMADelaide’s roots in the Adelaide Festival made the idea of crossovers between western art music, western classical music and music from around the world very attractive,” says WOMADelaide co-founder Brookman. “Bringing the likes of **Bangarra Dance Theatre** or **Meryl Tankard’s ADT** onstage meant you got to experience acts that you wouldn’t ordinarily find at a music festival.

“It helped us make the demographic as broad as possible, which we wanted,” he continues. “You could basically track two independent pathways through the festival. Older people who came for the classical music and dance companies then began exploring world cultures. And another completely different group were there for the drums and bass, the beats and the DJs.”

Annette Tripodi was programming the festival’s Australia-based content, and working with WOMAD in the UK to manage the international artists, when she established the late night WoZone club that ran from 1999 to 2003 inside the Student Union of nearby Adelaide University.

“I didn’t want to go home at 11pm, which was the curfew at the time,” she says. “We had the club run from midnight until 5am on Fridays and Saturdays: three rooms with DJs, live bands and a chill out space with projections.

“In 2004 we teamed up with the Adelaide Festival, running two WoZone nights as part of their Universal Playground club,” she continues. “In 2006 we did a late night DJ set (**Talvin Singh** on Stage 3) to test the waters. It was hugely well received and since 2007 we’ve programmed DJs in Speakers’ Corner – the first new area of the park we expanded into.”

There were those who’d doubted the wisdom of positioning a sixth stage in ‘Speakers' Corner’ amid the tall pine trees on the opposite side of Botanic Park. Said the locale was too remote. Doubted that anyone would want to walk that far.

“We crossed our fingers,” says Scobie. “Partly because the park is so beautiful, people were just really happy to explore different areas. One of the delights of producing the event has been finding new nooks and crannies where people can happen upon a performance. “To walk through the park when the festival is in full swing is to see a whole range of ages and emotions. There are so many animated faces, lots of talk of ‘Wasn’t that amazing?’ It’s this constant live exchange.”

There was just so much to take in: the Artist in Conversation sessions at Speakers' Corner. The food, fashion, art and trinkets in the Global Village area. The Taste the World stage, where artists chatted and cooked up a storm between intimate musical shows – a concept dreamed up for the 2004 festival by then Marketing Manager Sandy Verschoor (who went on to be Lord Mayor of Adelaide) that is now a fixture of WOMADs across the world.

**Watch:** _The Best of WOMADelaide 2004_

![](https://cms.womadelaide.com.au/media/tspjspjz/womadelaide2004_tony-lewis_tinariwen-1280-x-720.jpg?anchor=center&mode=crop&width=480&height=270&format=png&quality=90)Play video

### **Making History**

In 2004, the WOMADelaide Foundation – the non-profit body that now presents the festival – was established, buoyed by a remit to foster cultural understanding within and outside the festival. That same year the festival began an annual cycle of presentation – a move that was subsequently followed in 2007 by the Adelaide Fringe and in 2013, the Adelaide Festival.

In 2005, the first week-long visual arts workshop (featuring Cuban papier-mâché Artists, the **Mora Brothers**) was presented with Adelaide’s Community Arts Network. The Foundation’s outreach programmes became intrinsic to the festival’s identity: in 2007 a local artist visited the Ngaanyatjarra Pitjantjatjara Yankunytjatjara (NPY) lands of the tri-state central desert region to work with the **Tjanpi Desert Weavers**, returning for large-scale workshops with Community Arts Network, creating pieces on-site. In 2010 artists from the Anangu Pitjantjatjara Yankunytjatjara (APY) lands of remote northwest South Australia based themselves at Better World Arts in Port Adelaide, creating a set of sixty hand-painted flags in workshops facilitated by UK ’flag artist’ **Angus Watt**, their creations flying alongside Watt’s iconic flags – as they have done ever since.

WOMADelaide went carbon-neutral in 2005 through an active program of tree planting and reforestation. It was a move that underscored the festival’s commitment to sustainability, nurturing the sort of environmental awareness that saw people picking up what might have been left behind, and leaving the site as pristine as it was at the outset.

“WOMADelaide was the first festival in the country to pay proper attention to simple stuff like separating waste streams,” says Brookman. “We always tried to be inventive in our approach to carbon neutrality – the crazy idea of compostable plates and cutlery, say – and in our efforts to inspire change. It’s something that has gone into the DNA of the organisation.”

In 2010, ostensibly to celebrate the 50th anniversary of the Adelaide Festival, WOMADelaide extended to four days. The festival’s enormous popularity, along with the public holiday on the Monday, has ensured its four-day length ever since.

“The pace of WOMADelaide changed with that extra day,” says Tripodi. “We could schedule two shows by the same artist, who the audience might see on the Friday and again on the Monday; in between they’d do their activities or watch the other artists. There was more chilling, mingling and opportunities for collaboration. One artist likened it to a summer camp.”

By 2011, around 50% of attendees were travelling from interstate or overseas. Buoyed by a reputation for distinguished environmental sensitivity, the one-off three-day WOMAD Earth Station sister event took place later that year at Belair National Park – the site originally planned for the inaugural WOMADelaide before it was abandoned due to the risk of bushfire related fire bans closing the Park.

Earth Station’s focus on sharing concern and ideas for sustainable life on our earth was a catalyst for WOMADelaide’s wildly successful Planet Talks program, which debuted in 2013.

2012 was WOMADelaide’s twentieth anniversary. By which time the festival was entrenched in the national arts calendar as a must-see event, a celebration of our global community in one of the most beautiful locales in the country and possibly the world. Among the historic memories absorbed by Botanic Park that decade were private celebrations: weddings, three of them, complete with marquee, celebrant and flowers, and catering by Global Village stallholders.

There was the generational shift that saw kids who came with their parents in 1992 return over the years as tweens, teenagers and young adults, with or without children of their own. The personal highlights: the excitement of discovery; the glimpses into lesser-known musical traditions; the bursts of on-the-fly creative brilliance.

The sense of belonging. Of being at the centre of a world we would all like to live in.

“People would walk into Botanic Park and immediately their minds and hearts seemed to open,” says Tripodi. “You could almost feel the joy.”

**Watch:** _WOMADelaide 15 Years On: The Story So Far_

![](https://cms.womadelaide.com.au/media/01vpsxix/womadelaide2008_tony-lewis_flags-5-1280-x-720.jpg?anchor=center&mode=crop&width=480&height=270&format=png&quality=90)Play video

## 2012–2022

The joy has continued and even intensified, what with the combination of memories and experiences accrued over the decades and the steady influx of new audiences.

WOMADelaide’s stellar reputation (“Uplifting, political and expansive festival offers hope amidst the doom,” wrote _The Guardian_ in 2020) owes much to the blue-sky thinking of its organisers. A long-time crew for whom WOMADelaideans – the festival-goers themselves – are key.

“Never underestimate the audience,” says Director Scobie. “That’s something that often gets forgotten in the arts. While we are mindful that ideally people have to like what we present, the first questions we ask are, ‘Is the work good?’ ‘Is it enriching and sustaining?’

“Art and music must have meaning,” he continues, “whether it is traditional rhythms (**Master Drummers of Burundi**, 2012), protest dance music (Palestinian Jordanian outfit **47Soul**, 2016) or leftfield French pop (**Christine and the Queens**, 2019). We want people to feel moved, to connect and feel better for the experience of being there.”

WOMADelaide has worked to maintain its optimum vibe: in 2012 ‘Sounds of the Planet’ was replaced with the new WOMAD-wide tagline, ‘The World’s Festival’, and in 2017 the festival extended into neighbouring Frome Park. This increased the possibilities for large-scale performance and presenting _Exodus of the Forgotten Peoples_ – a sprawling immersive fire installation about the plight of refugees by French fire artists **Cie Carabosse**.

In Frome Park in 2018 a multi-storey ‘jewel box’ stage was created for **The Manganiyar Seduction**, an audio-visual feast created by Indian theatre director Royston Abel. In 2019, Stage 6 moved from its position down by the creek near Speakers' Corner to become the bigger, better Frome Park Pavilion.

Elsewhere, the WOMADelaide Community Access Program continued opening doors to those who wouldn’t ordinarily attend the festival. In 2022 over 300 tickets were distributed to a range of community groups including young refugees, Indigenous communities and survivors of torture and trauma.

“Coming to WOMADelaide is a luxury for many, particularly for those on a low income,” says Scobie. “We proactively try and make it as accessible as possible.”

In 2021 came the WOMADelaide x NSS Academy, a training and development programme for emerging SA First Nations and multicultural artists run in partnership with youth-focused Adelaide music hub Northern Sound System, based in Elizabeth in Adelaide’s northern suburbs.

“Over the years we’ve nursed an ambition to help build the future careers of young musicians,” says Scobie of a scheme that has so far welcomed the likes of Kenyan rapper-singer **Elsy Wameyo** and **Sonz of Serpent** Aboriginal hip-hop outfit.

“Professional mentors are paired with the training initiatives NSS have developed, further building WOMADelaide’s connection with local emerging talent and audiences across the community.”

Community projects have remained paramount. In 2013 WOMADelaide was the winner of the Partnerships Project (part of the SA Premier’s Natural Resources Management Award) for its relationship with Greening Australia, with whom it works to offset the festival’s carbon footprint. Two dollars from every ticket sold have to date seen over 149 hectares of native shrubs and trees (she-oak groves, mallee trees) planted in regional South Australia, a WOMADelaide forest like no other.

In 2018, Botanic Park was transformed each night of the festival by the ambitious live art project _Place des Anges_ by French aerial company **Gratte Ciel**. The spectacular overhead ballet involved swirling feathers, brilliant white angels and a giant inflatable cherub. The following year French experimentalists **Le Phun** presented _The Leafies_: sculptures made from tonnes of disintegrating leaves collected from Botanic Park over the previous autumn and stored in a warehouse in purpose-built containers.

“**Le Phun** arrived from France two weeks before the festival began to do workshops in the warehouse then on-site with students from the Adelaide Central School of Art,” says Tripodi. “They created 150 _Leafies_ that progressively populated Botanic Park in different guises then ‘migrated’ across the city for the next few weeks.”

### **Joy Perseveres**

This most recent decade was also the period in which the precedents set early by WOMADelaide – that is, its role as an influencer – were now clearly reflected in the aesthetics of other Australia-based festivals.

Still, no other festival could ever bottle the essence – and resilience – of WOMADelaide. The festival has navigated everything from world politics (caught up in the conflict in Mali, desert blues band **Tinariwen** cancelled 2012 then played in 2018) to unusual artist riders (cigars, cognac and crème brulee for the late Cape Verdean diva **Cesaria Evora**) and the challenges of flying artists in from such far-flung locales as Yakutia in Siberia (**Ayarkhaan**, 2013) and Nouakchott in Mauritania (**Noura Mint Seymali**, 2018).

Not to mention getting equipment and accoutrements past customs officials with almost permanently raised eyebrows. Among the items that have been brought down in flight cases or sourced locally (as requested in 2020 by Belgian metal-rock-electro-Balkan outfit **KermesZ L’Est**) are maracas, megaphones and bouquets of synthetic roses; a goat’s skull, two boar’s teeth and three stuffed martens; human dreadlocks, half a mirror ball, a fishing rod and a bicycle pump.

In 2021, in the midst of a global pandemic and unable to secure permission from SA Health for a full-scale event in Botanic Park, WOMADelaide defied all odds to present a series of reserved seating sunset concerts at King Rodney (Ityamai-itpina) Park over four nights. They featured the same high production values WOMADelaideans have come to expect, with a line-up of domestic icons including **Midnight Oil**, **Sarah Blasko** and **Archie Roach** – whose poignant farewell concert, coupled with his performance at the first Festival in 1992, seemed like a spiritual bookend.

In 2022 WOMADelaide returned to Botanic Park/Tainmuntilla, celebrating the 30th anniversary of the inaugural event in 1992 with the homegrown likes of **Courtney Barnett**, **The Cat Empire** and **Joseph Tawadros** performing a special concerto for oud with the **Adelaide Symphony Orchestra**.

**Watch:** _Highlights of WOMADelaide 2020_

![](https://cms.womadelaide.com.au/media/pubfwkd5/lucy_partington_photography_copyright_2020_womad-212-1280-x-720.jpg?anchor=center&mode=crop&width=480&height=270&format=png&quality=90)Play video

## 2023–2027

Life continues, and WOMADelaide remains a steadfast celebration despite the global uncertainty throughout the pandemic. Following two years of necessarily condensed and modified programs steering through the web of COVID-19 restrictions — the intent for 2023 was to "throw everything at the program,” and as Director Ian Scobie says, “We did.” 

2023 saw an embrace of dance and joy with a packed lineup of artists including the ethereal dance queen **Florence + The Machine**, alongside two-time Grammy-winner **Bon Iver**, Norway’s most streamed female artist of all time **AURORA**, **Youssou N’Dour**, and a return-to-form performance from **Sampa The Great**. The sound emanating from the stages was a draw for a new audience of first-timers, “Between Florence and Bon Iver there were people who it was unlikely had been to WOMADelaide, and that was also part of the intent: to try and bring a new crowd,” Scobie says. The festival has always embraced well-loved artists alongside lesser known. “If you go back to Men at Work in 1999, there were people saying, ‘they are not world music artists; Florence is not a world music artist; Bon Iver is not a world music artist’. But what is a world music artist? Ultimately, it's about a diversity of programming which brings together different tastes and sounds which can cross-fertilise in a way. You hope that the people who come as passionate fans of one particular artist will listen to another and discover and go away with a few more artists than is possible from attending a single concert of the artist they love.”

And it seemed to work in 2023, with the festival creating an innate sense of community celebration, one that carried over in the following years. When the world becomes increasingly isolating, there is always a place in the park, and **Gratte Ciel’s** _Place des Anges_ was a beautiful representation of that. After debuting at WOMADelaide in 2018, the spectacular overhead ballet involving swirling feathers, brilliant white angels and a giant inflatable cherub returned to close each night of the festival in 2023 and left audiences with joyful memories for years to come.

After record-breaking crowds in 2023, the festival site underwent a redesign to create a more comfortable experience and more green space for all. In 2024, the shaded WoMarkets was established along Plane Tree Drive as part of the relocation of infrastructure to free up the park’s green space and to provide more space for patrons. Access pathways were established to make for clearer and easier navigation day and night around the site and support crowd flow and management. The Studio in the Adelaide Botanic High gym also debuted, created specifically for more intimate physical theatre and dance works, including **Compagnie On Off** – _Le Chant de L'eau_, **Hewa Rwanda** – _Letter to the Absent_, **Restless Dance Theatre** – _Seeing Through Darkness_, and **Lewis Major Projects** – _Triptych Redux_. 

Musical acts included reggae royalty **Ziggy Marley**, Grammy-winning singer-songwriter **Corinne Bailey Rae**, Ukrainian ‘ethno chaos’ quartet **DakhaBrakha** and many more. And in 2024, the Malinauskas Labour Government announced it was extending its longstanding partnership to lock in the beloved festival through to 2029. Despite being the hottest year ever, enthusiastic festival-goers still turned up with more four-day passes purchased than ever before. 

The heat stuck around in 2025, but it didn’t stop artists like the formidable two-time Mercury Music Prize winner **PJ Harvey**, avant-pop powerhouse **Roisin Murphy** and Grammy-nominees **Khruangbin**. Crowd favourites **Compagnie Paris Bénarès** presented _Chamôh_ — a giant camel searching for the way home that delighted audiences across the park. 

Breaking the heatwave, WOMADelaide 2026 was forecast for clear blue skies and perfect temperatures, but there’s always a hurdle in events! The week before the 2026 festival was set to begin, conflict in the Middle East escalated, resulting in the closure of multiple international flight paths, disrupting travel plans for 45 groups scheduled to play in a short five days time. Working 24 hours a day, the WOMADelaide team succeeded in re-routing hundreds of artists and ensuring the festival went ahead, and ultimately only three groups were forced to cancel their plans.

Director Scobie describes there being a “great sense of achievement” at the 2026 festival, highlighting the irony being ‘The World’s Festival’, which celebrates the coming together of people, happening at the same time “the world (was) going mad”. The energy was high, and this showed with performances from Italian mega-star **Jovanotti**, feminist idol **Oumou Sangaré**, the return of **Yothu Yindi** after more than 30 years, and the “one and only” Saturday night headliner, **Grace Jones**. 

Sustainability has always been at the forefront of every WOMADelaide festival — leading the way when it came to innovative ways to better manage waste, beginning with the implementation of multiple coloured rubbish bins, removing single use plastics and introducing a reusable cup system — 2026 was the first time a South Australian festival powered all stages with 100% renewable energy.

“It’s proof of concept for the industry,” Scobie says. “Which is the ambition…if you prove the model, it can be done.”

So felicidades again to a festival that has developed alongside its audience: embracing change, enabling discovery and reinforcing connection. Offering food for thought, reasons to dance, incentive to grow and becoming even more beloved along the way. 

Here’s to the next 35 years. See you in the park!

## About Beaker Street

#### **Beaker Street is a cultural organisation and registered charity in Lutruwita/Tasmania with science and community at its heart.**

The brainchild of a fun-loving evolutionary biologist, Beaker Street is pioneering a new model of science engagement, where diverse audiences are welcomed into scientific thinking and discovery, with a generous serve of merriment, and a distinctly Tasmanian twist.

Since launching in 2017, our core offering, [Beaker Street Festival](https://beakerstreet.com.au/festival), has evolved from a nerdy night out into a prominent two-week festival and Australia’s premier National Science Week event. Our groundbreaking Roving Scientist Program has grown into a nationally recognised platform for public engagement and professional development, and our youthful CoLab sci-art experiment continues to shatter misconceptions and promote diversity in STEM.

We’ve grown beyond expectations, capturing and sharing our enthusiasm for science. We’re led by a small and passionate team, governed by a dedicated Board of Directors, and supported by a fabulous community of scientists and volunteers.

Now in our 10th year, we will continue to trailblaze the creation of a new model of science engagement through interactive, immersive experiences. Most importantly, we aim to strengthen our position as an agent of positive change, a place where conversations get started, where voices are heard, and topics and ideas are shared.

## OUR PURPOSE

### Building community through scientific understanding

## In an increasingly divided world, we have more in common than we might think.

We all inhabit the same universe, breathe the same air, and share the same basic human needs.

At Beaker Street, we invite people from all walks of life to find common ground through the lens of science. Here, impossible problems invite ingenious solutions, and uncertainty is a reason to come together — not to take sides.

Together — through eye-opening conversations, mind-expanding experiences, or just over a cold drink — we can uncover our shared reality.

See you at Beaker Street, where science brings us together.

[SUPPORT OUR WORK](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/donate/)

![](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/Untitled-design-67.png)

## Our Values

### Experimentation

We’re a bunch of creative and curious folks. We champion originality, embrace risks, and are comfortable with uncertainty. Science is about asking questions, not reciting facts. By encouraging experimentation, we set the scene for groundbreaking innovation.

### Connection

We’re greater together. We’re privileged to be part of a supportive community, and we strive to extend that sense of belonging to everyone we interact with. We prioritise collaboration, and we are committed to supporting and elevating our local talent.

### Integrity

In a world of fake news, misinformation, and pseudoscience, we’re an independent and trusted source of truth. We ensure our programming checks out, and put ethical and inclusive practices at the heart of our operations. We do what we say we will, and we do it well.

![](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/support.jpg)

Beyond the Festival, Beaker Street brings science and art together all year round. From the Science Photography Prize, Hobartica Cultural Embassy, CoLab and numerous other projects.

# ROVING SCIENTIST PROGRAM

### Looking to sharpen your science communication skills, expand your networks, and engage the public in meaningful, adult-focused conversations about your research? Join the Beaker Street Roving Scientist Program!

### Expressions of Interest Closed

The Beaker Street Roving Scientist Program 2026 has now closed after receiving a record number of applicants. If you missed out this year, we hope to see you in 2027!

The Roving Scientist Program is a free, curated professional development experience for STEM researchers and professionals who want to sharpen their science communication skills, expand their networks, and engage the public in meaningful, adult-focused conversations about research.

Set in Nipaluna/Hobart during Beaker Street Festival, the program combines a full day of professional development workshops, a VIP networking event, and multiple public outreach opportunities throughout the Festival, including at our iconic Roving Scientist Bar — where researchers share their work directly with curious, engaged adult audiences. There are also additional opportunities to engage with family audiences.

![](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/3-2-scaled.png)

[MEET OUR ROVING SCIENTISTS](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/roving-scientists-list/)

## What you get

*   #### High quality professional development and networking opportunities
    
*   #### Hands-on training in science communication and public engagement
    
*   #### Multiple IRL outreach opportunities with adult audiences
    
*   #### A published profile on the Beaker Street website
    
*   #### Inclusion in Beaker Street’s Roving Scientist database, shared with media and partners
    
*   #### Discounted tickets to selected Beaker Street Festival events
    
*   #### Access to partner accommodation offers
    
*   #### Your own amazingly flashy, highly coveted LED-lit name badge
    

## Key details

*   ### Location: Nipaluna/Hobart, Lutruwita/Tasmania
    
*   ### Timing: Each August, during Beaker Street Festival
    

[VIEW 2026 PROGRAM FLYER](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/BS_RSP-Flyer_2.0.pdf)

## What’s involved

### Friday 14 August 2026

### A full day of sci comm professional development

A practical, skills-focused day of workshops in Nipaluna/Hobart covering topics such as:

*   Communicating complex research clearly and confidently
*   Engaging non-expert audiences without watering down
*   Storytelling, framing, and speaking about uncertainty
*   Public engagement beyond the lecture theatre

The workshops bring together experienced science communicators, researchers, and facilitators in a collaborative, peer-based setting.

### Friday 14 August 2026

### The Collider: a VIP networking event

A free ticket to our swanky but nerdy networking evening bringing Roving Scientists together with:

*   Fellow researchers
*   Science communicators and journalists
*   Industry and policy professionals
*   Artists, cultural leaders, and funders

It’s designed to spark conversations, collaborations, and unexpected connections — not awkward small talk.

### 6-9 and 14-16 August 2026

### Outreach during Beaker Street Festival

Roving Scientists take part in multiple public outreach sessions at the Roving Scientist Bar, a pop-up venue inside Beaker Street Festival where the general adult public comes specifically to talk science.

This is a rare chance to test ideas, practice explaining your research, and engage with people who genuinely want to be there.

In 2026, we’ll also be introducing new family-friendly and sensory-friendly sessions.

**6-9 August** is focused on Antarctica, and **14-16 August** is across diverse research areas.

![](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Untitled-design-3.png)

## Who it’s for

The program is open to:

*   PhD candidates
*   Postdoctoral researchers
*   Early and mid-career researchers
*   STEM professionals working across universities, research institutes, government, and industry

We also have a special offering for all Antarctic workers, including researchers, tractor drivers, station chefs, plumbers… and anyone who’s worked on the ice!

You don’t need prior science communication experience — just curiosity, openness, and a willingness to talk about your work with the public.

### Funding your participation

While the Roving Scientist Program itself is free, many participants receive support for travel and on-the-ground costs through their employers or universities, including from:

*    University departments or HDR offices
    
*   Supervisor/ lab funding to support travel and outreach
*   Faculty or school professional development or travel budgets
    
*   Research centres or institutes
    
*   Engagement, impact, or communications teams
    

If you’re planning to request travel support from your institution or workplace, we recommend asking early.

[INFO FOR EMPLOYERS AND UNIVERSITIES](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/BS_RSP-Flyer_2.0.pdf)

### Info for employers, supervisors, and institutions

Supporting staff to participate in the Roving Scientist Program is a low-cost, high-impact investment in professional development and public engagement.

Your organisation benefits from:

*   Staff developing transferable skills through structured professional development in science communication and public engagement
*   Increased visibility of your research and researchers in a respected national festival
*   Positive, real-world public engagement with adult audiences
*   Opportunities for media, industry, and cross-sector connections
*   Clear evidence of engagement and impact activity

The program itself is free. Institutions typically support participants by covering travel and accommodation costs.

### Want to know more?

Email any questions to our team at **[\[email protected\].](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#f897949481b89a9d99939d8a8b8c8a9d9d8cd69b9795d6998d)**

Not quite right for you? Why not be a **[Festival volunteer](https://www.beakerstreet.com.au/get-involved/),** or simply come along to all the Festival fun. Subscribe below to receive updates and the next Festival program as soon as it’s out.

Craft + Design Canberra

Craft + Design Canberra

Craft + Design Canberra is the proud winner of the 2023 Canberra Region Tourism Commendation Award for Major Festivals + Events for the DESIGN Canberra Festival.

Craft + Design Canberra is supported by the ACT Government, the Visual Arts and Craft Strategy - an initiative of the Australian, State and Territory Governments, and the Australia Council for the Arts - the Australian Government's arts funding and advisory body. The work of Craft + Design Canberra is also generously supported by private sponsorship.

We thank our Government funders, Major, Multiyear, Silver, Bronze and Organisational partners for their generous support of Craft + Design Canberra. With their support we are able to achieve our mission to promote and celebrate excellence and innovation in contemporary craft and design.

# MULTIYEAR PARTNERS

[![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/1347/8135/files/Logo_ART_BLK_240x240.jpg?v=1743639835)](https://artgroup.com.au/?utm_source=CDcanberra&utm_medium=SponsorLink&utm_campaign=Sponsorship)

**ART GROUP**

Art Group is a multi-award-winning Canberra based property developer building homes for over 20 years. Dedicated to delivering projects of quality and distinction, Art Group is passionate about making a positive contribution to the nation’s capital by pushing design and architectural boundaries and creating sustainable communities for future generations.

As a truly local developer with an ambition for a rich and prosperous city, Art Group are excited to support Design and Craft Canberra; advocating for the creative community and continuing to cement the city as a creative hub, and achieve a collective ambition for unparalleled innovation and design.

[![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/1347/8135/files/HBH-blue_240x240.png?v=1743643231)](https://homebyholly.com.au/)

**HOME BY HOLLY**

A long-time supporter of Craft + Design Canberra, home.byholly is a dynamic, full-service boutique real estate agency delivering innovative, creative and exceptional outcomes. Creating an emotional attachment through the personal story of homes, home.byholly’s bespoke service is designed to make the process of buying and selling a home unique experience for everyone.

[![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/1347/8135/files/ACT_PCS_logo_CMYK-outlines_2_240x240.png?v=1743643491)](https://www.act.gov.au/environment/parks-and-conservation)

**ACT PARKS AND CONSERVATION SERVICE**

The Parks and Conservation Service is a Branch within the Environment Division responsible for planning and management of parks, reserves and rural lands. It protects and conserves the natural resources of the ACT and promotes appropriate recreational, educational and scientific uses of our parks and reserves.

[![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/1347/8135/files/A-by-Adina-Lockup-Charcoal_CMYK_240x240.jpg?v=1743639808)](https://abyadina.com/)

**A BY ADINA**

A by Adina is where confident travelers enjoy the best of both worlds with world-class dining and bars.  

Step inside, and you’ll find the perfectly suited balance between a hotel and residential experience that’s refreshingly different from the apartment hotels, hotel residences and all suites offered by mainstream hotel chains. Each destination showcases world-renowned architecture that blends seamlessly with its surroundings, complemented by understated yet impactful contemporary Australian interiors. 

[![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/1347/8135/files/ACT_Mono_Pos_1_240x240.png?v=1743641601)](https://www.architecture.com.au/)

**THE AUSTRALIAN INSTITUTE OF ARCHITECTS ACT CHAPTER**

The Australian Institute of Architects is the peak body for architecture.   
They represent over 14,500 members globally, committed to raising design standards and positively shaping the places where we live, work and meet.

Along with members, they are dedicated to improving our built environment and the communities we call home by promoting quality, responsible, sustainable design and advocating on behalf of the profession for the benefit of all Australians.

[![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/1347/8135/files/lawyerbank_logo_-_jpg_240x240.jpg?v=1743640973)](https://craftanddesigncanberra.org/pages/www.lawyerbank.com.au)

**LAWYERBANK**

lawyerbank is an exceptional team of talented lawyers who work on secondment to government and provide pro bono legal services to various not-for-profits.

![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/1347/8135/files/TA_Logo_Horizontal_3Colour_Reverse-01.jpg?v=1782356184)

Tailored Accounts is an award-winning management accounting and business intelligence company specialising in Not-for-Profit organisations, SMEs and start-ups. Our team combines a deep passion for numbers with a personalised service approach to deliver practical insights, strategic support and the best financial outcomes for every client.

We can help with your Accounting & Bookkeeping, Business Advisory, Taxation, and More!

# BRONZE PARTNERS

[![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/1347/8135/files/Zoo_-_Black_Background_240x240.jpg?v=1743644020)](https://nationalzoo.com.au/)

**NATIONAL ZOO & AQUARIUM**

The National Zoo and Aquarium inspires and assists in the conservation of the natural world through exciting and innovative educational experiences.

Their mission is to set world’s best practices for animal care and sustainability while impassioning their guests to protect the natural world. They do what they do to move towards a better future for us, and all living creatures on this planet.

[![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/1347/8135/files/NFSA_Logo_Primary_Black_RGB_1_240x240.jpg?v=1743644310)](https://www.nfsa.gov.au/)

**NATIONAL FILM AND SOUND ARCHIVE**

The National Film and Sound Archive of Australia (NFSA) is Australia’s national audiovisual cultural institution. We collect, preserve and share Australia’s audiovisual culture.  Our Acton home is open daily from 10am to 4pm, in walking distance of Canberra’s city centre.

There’s always something to inspire and delight at the NFSA, whether it’s school holidays, date night or just a quiet afternoon to yourself. Catch a cult classic at Arc Cinema, join us for thought-provoking discussions, explore the curious collection of audiovisual artefacts on display in The Library or simply drop in to enjoy a locally roasted coffee in Mediatheque or our sunny heritage courtyard.    
Sign up to our newsletter to receive What’s On updates and stay in the loop about Canberra screenings, events, exhibitions, special guests and more.

[![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/1347/8135/files/canberra-centre-logo-vector_240x240.png?v=1743644850)](https://canberracentre.qicre.com/)

**CANBERRA CENTRE**

Located in the heart of the CBD. Canberra Centre is the leading destination for fashion, entertainment and dining, offering 200 of your favorite brands including over 50 restaurant and dining options.

# MEDIA PARTNER

[![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/1347/8135/files/HerCanberra_Logo_RGB_1_BLK_240x240.jpg?v=1743645075)](https://hercanberra.com.au/)

**HER CANBERRA** 

HerCanberra is Canberra's premier lifestyle media brand, connecting Canberrans with their city and each other.

Craft + Design Canberra is the proud winner of the 2023 Canberra Region Tourism Commendation Award for Major Festivals + Events for the DESIGN Canberra Festival.

Craft + Design Canberra is supported by the ACT Government, the Visual Arts and Craft Strategy - an initiative of the Australian, State and Territory Governments, and the Australia Council for the Arts - the Australian Government's arts funding and advisory body. The work of Craft + Design Canberra is also generously supported by private sponsorship.

Craft + Design Canberra is the proud winner of the 2023 Canberra Region Tourism Commendation Award for Major Festivals + Events for the DESIGN Canberra Festival.

Craft + Design Canberra is supported by the ACT Government, the Visual Arts and Craft Strategy - an initiative of the Australian, State and Territory Governments, and the Australia Council for the Arts - the Australian Government's arts funding and advisory body. The work of Craft + Design Canberra is also generously supported by private sponsorship.

title: Craft + Design Canberra – Craft + Design Canberra
description: Craft + Design Canberra is a not-for-profit organisation which supports artists, craft practitioners, designers and makers at every stage of their careers. We promote and celebrate excellence and innovation in contemporary craft in everything we do – in our retail space, exhibitions, events and membership programs.

**Supporting local Australian artists, makers and designers**

Craft + Design Canberra is a not-for-profit membership based organisation which supports artists, craft practitioners, designers and makers at every stage of their careers. We promote and celebrate excellence and innovation in contemporary craft in everything we do – in our retail space, exhibitions, events and membership program.  
  
Craft + Design Canberra acknowledges the Ngunawal, Ngunnawal and Ngambri peoples as the Traditional Custodians of the lands on which we meet, make, exhibit and celebrate craft and design. We recognise all First Nations families with enduring connections to this Country and pay our respects to Elders past and present.  
  
We honour the continuing care of Country, its lands, waterways, skies and communities, and recognise the strength, generosity and resilience of First Nations peoples in sustaining and sharing cultural knowledge across generations.  
  
We recognise First Nations peoples as the original artists, makers, designers, storytellers and knowledge holders of this continent.  
  
We extend our respect to the Traditional Custodians of all the Countries from which the artists, makers and communities we work with create and connect.  
  
Sovereignty was never ceded.

* * *

An Australian design classic, Robert Foster’s water jug is F!NK’s signature piece and one the most recognisable objects to come out of Canberra. The coloured anodised aluminium F!NK jug fits perfectly into any household or boardroom and is a must for design collectors.

**Materials:** Anodised aluminium with a cast steel handle. Sandblasted matte finish

**Dimension:** H 30 cm x D 10 cm (base, slightly ovoid).

**Capacity:** 1.45 litres

**Care instructions:** Handwash only, not dishwasher safe.

**Meet the Maker:** [F!nk](https://craftact.org.au/blogs/meet-the-maker/meet-the-maker-fink?_pos=2&_sid=0df29174d&_ss=r) [+ Co.](https://craftact.org.au/blogs/meet-the-maker/meet-the-maker-fink?_pos=2&_sid=0df29174d&_ss=r) is a much loved and respected Australian design company with an international reputation for producing world-class tableware, hollowware, jewellery and lighting. It was established by Robert Foster in 1993 with the aim of creating a design and manufacturing business to support and generate opportunities for Australian designer-makers.  

F!NK challenges the notions that functional is boring, and that useful and visually exciting are mutually exclusive.  Simultaneously supremely functional and totally elegant, no two F!NK pieces are exactly the same. Each article is created in small batches of 20 to 100 units and individually hand-finished in the Queanbeyan studio/workshop.  

When commissioned to create a jug by a prominent Canberra restaurant in the 1990s, Robert took aluminium tubing, an everyday sustainable material, and fashioned it into a sleek economically viable product. The Water Jug was the first F!NK product and is still the mainstay of the company. It is a striking practical object and encapsulates the qualities of F!NK + Co.: distinctive design, function and technical innovation.

* * *

Studio Hacienda (2005–2008) was established in a factory space in Abbotsford by Blanche Tilden and Phoebe Porter following an Australia Council funded mentorship of Phoebe by Blanche in 2005.

The _General Assembly_ brooches were developed as a series of designed and engineered component parts that, when assembled, are redolent of the built structures of Melbourne and Canberra.

Drawing inspiration from the philosophy of serial production demonstrated in the work of craftspeople such as Melbourne contemporary jeweller, Susan Cohn, and German master goldsmith, Friedrich Dau, Studio Hacienda have produced interchangeable components of varying colour, texture, form and material that are laid out in a "production line" ready pick'n'mix. Architectural details and signage found around Melbourne's CBD were starting points from which each design evolved.   
  
_"General Assembly_ exemplifies Porter and Tilden's common ground: working in multiples, exploring the individual impulse to select, combine and adorn, alertness to the ubiquitous street styles that pulse through a city. It is a project that involves people in a lively, intelligent conversation through the object. That's Studio Hacienda." - Merryn Gates  

_General Assembly—Canberra brooch series_ 2007–2008, remade 2021Edition number RE01.

**Materials:** flameworked borosilicate glass, anodised aluminium, titanium, stainless steel

**Dimensions:** 8 cm (h) x 3 cm (w) x 0.5 cm (d)

Wagtail Scoop - Large

Regular price $125.00 Save $-125.00

* * *

Individually hand hammered handles make each piece truly unique, capturing the hand of the maker and the showcasing our traditional craft.   

Inspired by their much-loved, sell out, limited-edition Brass Wagtail Scoops, the stainless steel wagtail scoops are a new addition to Ferro Forma's Signature Flatware Collection. Robust and sturdy, ready for years and years of use in your home, they need little to no maintenance to keep them looking as good as new.

Choose between the _**small**_ or _**large**_ Wagtail Scoop - both perfectly suited to your daily rituals and little moments in your kitchen.

Whether you're scooping flour for baking brownies or measuring out tea leaves for a hot cuppa - a Ferro Forma wagtail scoop will no doubt be a favourite you reach for again and again for all manner of things! Keep out on a shelf as a beautifully crafted object to admire whilst being within reach for whenever you need it. 

**Material:** Stainless steel, sold individually

**Dimensions:** 11cm long, 7cm wide across the bowl

**About the Makers:** Ferro Forma is the culmination of a long-standing partnership between Alison Jackson and Dan Lorrimer. They are a metalsmithing workshop specialising in handcrafted small batch edition objects that capture the hand of the maker and the heritage of our craft.

[Alison Jackson](https://craftact.org.au/blogs/membership-directory/alison-jackson?_pos=1&_sid=d9e912b94&_ss=r) is a designer, maker and contemporary Silversmith based in Braidwood, Australia. Completing a Gold and Silversmithing degree at the Australian National University, Alison holds over two decades of artistic and technical metal forming expertise.

With an aesthetic best described as elegant, timeless, and minimal, Alison showcases her work through her fine jewellery, tableware, large scale installation, limited editions and exhibition work.

Alison’s work is held in both public and private collections, including a large acquisition by the Canberra Museum and Gallery. A recipient of numerous notable awards and grants,  Alison’s work has been exhibited widely within Australia and also internationally, including at Inhorgenta (Germany) and Milan Design Week (Italy). 

[Dan Lorrimer](https://craftact.org.au/blogs/membership-directory/dan-lorrimer-1?_pos=1&_sid=0a4514b91&_ss=r) is a contemporary sculptor, machinist, fabricator and toolmaker. With a degree in Sculpture from the Australian National University, Dan has since diversified his work, significantly developing his skills across a wide range of technical areas, specialising in metal forming.

Dan’s sculpture practice explores notions of movement, energy, solidity and illusion through minimalist sculptural forms, often located between the artificial and natural world. He has exhibited widely across Australia and has work held in private collections across the country.

Craft + Design Canberra

Craft + Design Canberra is the proud winner of the 2023 Canberra Region Tourism Commendation Award for Major Festivals + Events for the DESIGN Canberra Festival.

Craft + Design Canberra is supported by the ACT Government, the Visual Arts and Craft Strategy - an initiative of the Australian, State and Territory Governments, and the Australia Council for the Arts - the Australian Government's arts funding and advisory body. The work of Craft + Design Canberra is also generously supported by private sponsorship.

Craft + Design Canberra

Craft + Design Canberra is the proud winner of the 2023 Canberra Region Tourism Commendation Award for Major Festivals + Events for the DESIGN Canberra Festival.

Craft + Design Canberra is supported by the ACT Government, the Visual Arts and Craft Strategy - an initiative of the Australian, State and Territory Governments, and the Australia Council for the Arts - the Australian Government's arts funding and advisory body. The work of Craft + Design Canberra is also generously supported by private sponsorship.

# About Us

###### ![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/1347/8135/files/CACT-2048px_online-18_1024x1024.jpg?v=1690512201)Image Tim Bean Photography

## We Love Craft and Design.

Craft + Design Canberra is a not-for-profit membership based organisation which supports artists, craft practitioners, designers and makers at every stage of their careers. We promote and celebrate excellence and innovation in contemporary craft in everything we do in our retail space, exhibition gallery, public membership program, events and throughout our biennial Craft + Design Canberra Festival. Read about the [**history of  Craft + Design Canberra.**](https://craftanddesigncanberra.org/blogs/history/50-years-of-craft-act) 

  

## **Meet the team**

![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/1347/8135/files/2026_Headshots-17.jpg?v=1776677182)

**Jodie Cunningham | CEO + Artistic Director**

Email | [ceo@craftanddesigncanberra.org](https://craftanddesigncanberra.org/pages/ceo@craftanddesigncanberra.org)  
  

Jodie Cunningham is CEO and Artistic Director of Craft + Design Canberra, one of Australia’s leading creative centres for the development of visual art, craft and design. Jodie manages the overall operations and resources, acting as the main point of communication between the board of directors, staff, members, sponsors and government bodies. She is the public face of the organisation, curating a vibrant program of exhibitions, residencies and cross-disciplinary collaborations including the Craft + Design Canberra Festival.

  

Jodie is a highly creative arts leader, visual artist and educator with extensive experience in developing and delivering innovative exhibitions, public programs in museums, galleries and art contexts. She also has an extensive background in visual art and design education and a commitment to mentoring developing artists and fostering collaboration. Jodie advocates for the power of creativity, the arts and cultural activity to provide hope to our communities, strengthen our local and national cultural identities, and facilitate social change.

  

Five fun facts about Jodie

1.  Wore a hole in her carpet when she was little from drawing all the time on the floor of her room
2.  Is a chromaphile - loving, living and wearing saturated colour
3.  Is a bowerbird for colourful vintage objects, filling up her studio with rainbow aluminium picnic cups and makes assemblage sculptures from them
4.  Loves to fly fish but rarely catches a fish
5.  Can put her red lipstick on without looking in the mirror and while talking

  

![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/1347/8135/files/2026_Headshots-20.jpg?v=1775790841)

**Gillian Morrison | Deputy Director**

Email | [gillian.morrison@craftanddesigncanberra.org](https://craftanddesigncanberra.org/pages/gillian.morrison@craftanddesigncanberra.org)

Gillian Morrison is an arts and education professional with over a decade of experience spanning community arts, higher education and creative technology. She led Learn For Yourself, a Melbourne not-for-profit delivering digital literacy and art therapy programs to vulnerable communities, and has coordinated international exhibitions and symposia with the Australian Network for Art and Technology (ANAT). As Research Manager for the TALi Detect project, she oversaw an interdisciplinary collaboration between Monash University, industry and government developing digital tools for childhood cognitive assessments.

Gillian has taught literature at Swinburne University of Technology and holds a PhD in Game-based Learning, a Masters in Creative Media and a Bachelor of Science. She is deeply committed to the role of the arts and the artist in fostering meaningful social change.

  

**Five fun facts about Gillian**

1.  Loves a boogie
    
2.  Buys more books than she will ever read 
    
3.  Would love to own a Fontana (the artist, not the water spout)
    
4.  Super keen on all things Neuroscience
    
5.  Will never say no to a good Op Shop outing
    

  
  
![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/1347/8135/files/2026_Headshots-9.jpg?v=1775791334)

**Kelsie White | Marketing Coordinator**  

Email | [kelsie.white@craftanddesigncanberra.org](https://craftanddesigncanberra.org/pages/kelsie.white@craftanddesigncanberra.org)

Kelsie White has worked in marketing for the last ten years across many sectors from Education to the Arts. Kelsie moved to Canberra in 2023, after relocating from Ballarat and is originally from Perth. Kelsie is a qualified Graphic Designer and holds a BA in Political Science and International Relations.

Five fun facts about Kelsie  

1.  In 2017, Kelsie went on a round the world trip travelling from Australia to Asia, Europe and the USA.
2.  Kelsie is a painter and can be found painting abstract landscapes inspired by the hills of the ACT and her experiences of motherhood.
3.  In 2020, Kelsie coordinated a main street activation through the City of Ballarat and Ballarat Evolve allowing over 20 local makers to present their work in high street shops that sat empty during COVID lock downs.
4.  Currently, Kelsie is pushing her limits and hitting PB's in power lifting.
5.  While living in Ballarat, Kelsie had her own shop and workshop space where she would stock her own products, run workshops in many mediums and have other artists use her space for their events and classes.

![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/1347/8135/files/2026_Headshots-27.jpg?v=1776678145)

**Saori Brooks | Membership Officer  
**Email | [saori.brooks@craftanddesigncanberra.org](https://craftanddesigncanberra.org/pages/saori.brooks@craftanddesigncanberra.org)

Saori has been involved in the arts sector since she began as a gallery assistant in 2023. She studied a master's degree in Art History and Curatorial Studies at the ANU. Originally from Japan, Saori relocated to Australia in early 2022.

Five fun facts about Saori

1.  Loves vintage op shopping.
2.  Is obsessed with cat motif objects.
3.  Collects woodblock prints, fridge magnets and CDs.
4.  Has a phobia of worms.
5.  Holds an 8-dan qualification in Japanese calligraphy.

**![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/1347/8135/files/2026_Headshots-7.jpg?v=1776677220)Jenny Edwards | Retail Officer**  

Email | [jenny.edwards@craftanddesigncanberra.org](https://craftanddesigncanberra.org/pages/jenny.edwards@craftanddesigncanberra.org ) 

Jenny Edwards is not shy about her love of craft + design. She was a board member of CDC from 2019 to 2025 when the organisation's constitutional limit of six years required her to step down; a collaborator on various festival programs over the last decade, and possibly the most frequently occurring customer name in ‘sales’ over that period!   
  
Jenny is the owner of Light House ArchiScience, Canberra’s largest residential architecture practice, until she restructured and down-sized to prioritise her health in 2024, and the only architecture business to makes science and sustainability integral to everything they do.

Five fun facts about Jenny

1.  A scientist, not an architect
2.  Has had three hip replacements and loves to work them by walking
3.  Daughter of a West Aussie Olympian and world record holder known as the Como Comet
4.  A FixItChick with well-known Canberra local Lish Fejer
5.  Has sold her own creations at Salamanca Markets and Fremantle Arts Centre

**![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/1347/8135/files/2026_Headshots-12.jpg?v=1776678203)  
Brittany Dale | Program Coordinator**  

Email | [brittany.dale@craftanddesigncanberra.org](https://craftanddesigncanberra.org/pages/brittany.dale@craftanddesigncanberra.org)

Brittany has a background in community engagement, public program development and arts education and has held roles in arts organisation across Australia and the UK. She holds a Master of Museum Studies and a Bachelor of Arts (Art History)  and is passionate about creating vibrant, inclusive arts experiences through thoughtful program design. 

  

Five fun facts about Brittany

1.  Has travelled to 40 countries but remembers them mostly by what she ate rather than what she saw. 
    
2.  Collects tea towels. 
    
3.  Loves a trivia night and takes it very seriously. 
    
4.  Is an expert parallel parker. 
    
5.  Enjoys distance running and is currently training for her second marathon. 
    

![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/1347/8135/files/2026_Headshots-5.jpg?v=1776677342)

**Stacy Jewell | Exhibition Coordinator**

Email | [stacy.jewell@craftanddesigncanberra.org](https://craftanddesigncanberra.org/pages/stacy.jewell@craftanddesigncanberra.org)

Stacy brings extensive experience managing exhibitions across festivals, commercial galleries and artist-run initiatives. Most recently was the Managing Gallery Administrator at Trocadero Projects where she led programming and strategic development. Stacy has strong project management skills and experience with installation, stakeholder engagement and all aspects of exhibition delivery. She's worked at Next Wave Festival, Sutton Gallery, The National Gallery of Victoria, KINGS Artist-Run, No Vacancy, and Heide Museum of Modern Art. Stacy holds a Master of Arts (Arts Management) from RMIT and has a passion for supporting artists at all levels. Stacy relocated from Melbourne to join us in Canberra.

Five fun facts about Stacy

1.  Stacy runs a small film club dedicated to screening debut features or independent shorts by female identifying directors whose films explore desire, identity and power from a female gaze. This group was started in Covid and has since branched out to include artist films and discussions around social justice and aesthetic drive.
2.  She is a secret pool shark.
3.  She played netball for Victoria in the reserves under 16 team.
4.  Has never seen the snow, but hopes that will change very soon.
5.  Is a triple Gemini.

Craft + Design Canberra

Craft + Design Canberra is the proud winner of the 2023 Canberra Region Tourism Commendation Award for Major Festivals + Events for the DESIGN Canberra Festival.

Craft + Design Canberra is supported by the ACT Government, the Visual Arts and Craft Strategy - an initiative of the Australian, State and Territory Governments, and the Australia Council for the Arts - the Australian Government's arts funding and advisory body. The work of Craft + Design Canberra is also generously supported by private sponsorship.

# DAAF 2027

5-8 AUGUST  
LARRAKIA COUNTRY & ONLINE

Experience the rich diversity and strength of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander art, design and culture, at the 21st Darwin Aboriginal Art Fair on Larrakia Country and Online.

Mark your calendars from the 5-8 August 2027, part of an action packed week of events from DAAF Foundation in the Top End!

[Donate to Support](https://daaf.com.au/support-us)

# Mimili Maku Arts﻿

## "DAAF is about connection, celebration and creating strong futures for artists and communities on their own terms. We absolutely love it. "

**_It’s such a special gathering place_**_, a chance to reconnect with friends, family and colleagues from Art Centres across the country, while sharing everything that has been happening back home in Mimili. We get to celebrate the artists who travel with us, but also tell the bigger story of our studio: the exhibitions, special projects, community initiatives and cultural work happening throughout the year._ **_There’s something incredibly energising about having so many Aboriginal Art Centres together in one place_**_, sharing what we’re doing and learning from one another. And importantly, it’s a fantastic payday for the artists and Art Centre, people return home feeling proud, excited and supported by the response to their work._

_\-_ Mimili Maku Arts

## "Beyond the sales, sharing our stories through art fair program and the masterclass, is what keeps our culture strong."

﻿_DAAF 2026 felt like a true gathering place for our communities. Being one of the 68 Art Centres on the ground gave our artists a rare chance to connect directly with over 12,800 visitors. The reach of the hybrid model meant even our artists back home were part of the 75 centres represented. Beyond the sales, sharing our stories through art fair program and the masterclass, is what keeps our culture strong. The income and opportunities created here flow directly back into our communities, making a real difference. -_ UMI Arts

## WORK WITH US!

## Current Positions

# First Nations Fundraising Internship

**Have you ever considered a career in fundraising?**

Come and join us to build your skills and expertise for a rewarding career! 

You will have the opportunity to hone your skills whilst helping to build business capacity for our amazing network of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Art Centres. This incredible opportunity will support you to:

*   Develop your skills and expertise across all areas of fundraising including completing an online fundraising course.
*   Learn about Australia’s Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Art Centre model
*   Opportunity to travel to the Darwin Aboriginal Art Fair in August 2026!

**Download:** [First Nations Fundraising Internship Position Description\_2026.pdf](https://daaf.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/First-Nations-Fundraising-Internship-Position-Description_2026.pdf)

****_Note that this is STRICTLY an Australian Aboriginal & Torres Strait Islander identified position._****

## About the Internship

There are over 2,000 not-for-profit Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander organisations in Australia. First Nations leadership and agency is critical to ensure that the voices of our First Nations people are heard. However, there are currently very few First Nations Australians engaged and experienced in the area of fundraising and philanthropy to support these organisations and charities.

This 34 week internship program (roughly 8 months!) is designed to offer a holistic understanding of the not-for-profit sector and the intricacies of fundraising and philanthropy activities. Through a combination of education and hands-on experience, the successful intern will gain valuable insights into various aspects of fundraising, including donor and philanthropic engagement, writing and implementing a fundraising strategy, grant writing and strategic campaign development, and more.

The program recognises the importance of cultural competence and safety in fundraising efforts, emphasising the incorporation of traditional knowledge and community values into contemporary philanthropic practices. By doing so, it seeks to ensure that fundraising initiatives align authentically with the diverse needs and aspirations of the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities. This initiative represents a significant step towards fostering inclusivity, diversity and sustainability within the Australian fundraising sector. 

The primary objective of this Internship is to cultivate skilled and experienced individuals within the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander community who can navigate the complexities of fundraising with cultural sensitivity and community-focused perspectives.

At the heart of this internship program is a commitment to providing practical experience, fostering skills development, and ultimately creating tangible pathways into fundraising careers for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people. By doing so, the project aims to empower individuals within these communities to actively contribute to the sustainability and growth of First Nations not-for-profit organisations.

This internship is an initiative of the Darwin Aboriginal Art Fair Foundation, **delivered by Balanced Effect**, and is proudly supported by Creative Australia.

## Description of Internship

The successful intern will work as a paid employee of the host organisation Balanced Effect Pty Ltd, an organisation that provides fundraising and Customer Relationship Management (CRM) support to the not-for-profit sector.

In addition to supporting an exciting fundraising campaign with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Art Centres in remote communities, the internship will also provide support for Art Centre clients and gain insight into non-Indigenous-led clients to gain a comprehensive understanding of the many fundraising roles available to them.

The successful intern will participate in a comprehensive 16-module online fundraising course as an integral part of the program. This course is designed to provide a strong foundation in fundraising principles, donor engagement strategies, campaign management, and ethical fundraising practices. Each module will cover key topics such as grant writing, digital fundraising, donor stewardship, and CRM. By completing the course, the intern will gain valuable industry knowledge and practical skills that can be applied throughout the internship and beyond, preparing them for a successful career in the nonprofit sector.

**Participants will cover fundraising areas such as:**

*   The not-for-profit sector
*   Fundraising strategy creation and implementation
*   Individual giving
*   Campaigns and appeals
*   Community Fundraising
*   Gifts in Will
*   Major donors
*   Regular giving
*   Philanthropic trusts and foundations
*   Digital fundraising
*   Marketing & communications
*   A variety of fundraising software products
*   The importance of data
*   Data collection and privacy
*   Customer Relationship Management (CRM) and software

## Duration, Contact Hours and Remuneration

**Starting:** March 2026

**Duration:** 34 weeks at 0.6FTE - 22.5 hours per week

**Remuneration:** $20,655 + 12% Superannuation

**Location:**

_Wurundjeri Woi-wurrung Country  
_Balanced Effect, SPACES Corner Carrington Rd & Thurston St, Suite 10/1 Main St, Box Hill VIC 3128  
2 days per week at Balanced Effect, 1 day per week study time remote  
Some travel required

_NB: This position is open to candidates from across Australia. Remote working conditions will be considered, however, there will be some intensive time in Naarm with the Balanced Effect team required._

## About the Intern 

**Qualifications, Skills, and Experience:**

First Nations Fundraising Internship candidates should be passionate about the for-purpose and arts sector and want to pursue a career in fundraising for First Nations arts organisations.

The ideal candidate for the First Nations Fundraising Internship position should possess the following qualifications, skills and experience.

**If you are excited about this opportunity, you feel that you have most of the skills and experience required, you are passionate about creating change in the world, and you are a dedicated learner, please apply!**

**Required skills:**

NOTE: _The filling of this position is intended to constitute a special/equal opportunity measure under section 8 (1) of the Racial Discrimination Act 1975 (Cth) and s57 of the Anti-Discrimination Act 1995 (NT)._ **_The position is therefore only open to Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander applicants._**

*   4+ years of general work experience in any industry or sector
*   A basic understanding of fundraising and/or marketing and/or the not-for-profit sector
*   Demonstrated interest in the national and global arts scene
*   Good administration capabilities, with great organisational skills, attention to detail and time management
*   Excellent interpersonal skills, with a cooperative approach and genuine intention to nurture strong stakeholder relationships and an optimal team environment
*   Sound computer literacy skills

**Personal capabilities:**

*   Ability to work independently as well as with a local and remote team to achieve required outcomes
*   Understanding of how to create culturally safe spaces with sensitivity and humility – recognising the importance of Indigenous perspectives, histories and experiences

**Nice to have skills & experience:**

*   A degree or experience in Marketing or Communications (but this is **NOT** essential)
*   Keen interest or experience in the visual arts sector
*   Experience working in remote Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander communities

**Knowledge, Skills and Attributes:**

*   Time Management and Efficiency: Possess good time management skills and efficient work practices
*   Proactive Attitude: Display a proactive approach to all client challenges, constantly seeking ways to solve problems.

**Continued Personal/Professional Development:**

Show enthusiasm for continuous personal and professional growth, have an inquisitive nature and actively seek opportunities to learn.

## Application Process

To apply, please forward your **CV and cover letter** to [\[email protected\]](https://daaf.com.au/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#04706569697d44666568656a6761606162626167702a676b692a6571).

The application process will consist of an initial phone interview, followed by 1-2 in-person interviews located in Box Hill on Wurundjeri Woi-wurrung Country.

A minimum of three referees will be requested and contacted for applicants who are considered for the role.

**This internship is due to begin in March 2026.**

If you are excited about this opportunity, you feel that you have most of the skills and experience required, you are passionate about creating change in the world, and you are a dedicated learner, please apply!

We will actively be contacting people throughout the application period, so please do not delay your application.

**Download:** [First Nations Fundraising Internship Position Description\_2026.pdf](https://daaf.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/First-Nations-Fundraising-Internship-Position-Description_2026.pdf)

Wood-fired sauna cruises in Tasmania

–​  
Kuuma is a mobile sauna boat operating in Southern Tasmania. Departing from Margate Marina near Hobart, we offer communal and private sauna experiences across the seasons, including sunrise sessions, golden hour cruises, and private charters. During winter each June, Kuuma also operates Dark Dip, a series of docked pop-up sauna rituals at Kings Pier Marina in Hobart.

## ABOUT THE FAIR

_**Ngaruwanajirri booth, DAAF, 2025, Photo by Leicolhn McKellar**_

# Darwin Aboriginal Art Fair

### **The Darwin Aboriginal Art Fair, affectionately known as DAAF, is the only national event of its kind and has secured a reputation as one of the country’s most significant internationally recognised arts events.**

Showcasing the contemporary fine art and design of more than 75 Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Art Centres from across Australia, DAAF is held annually each August in Darwin, on Larrakia Country - and online!

#### **Save the Date: 5-8 August 2027**

[About our Foundation](https://daaf.com.au/foundation/)

![](https://daaf.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/54822139814_6e6644f12e_k.jpg "54822139814_6e6644f12e_k")

# **An Art Fair with Impact. DAAF in 2025:**

![](https://daaf.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/7-scaled-e1761790368771.png "7")

![](https://daaf.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/9-scaled-e1761790507564.png "9")

![](https://daaf.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/8-scaled-e1761790528795.png "8")

![](https://daaf.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/6-scaled-e1761790393496.png "6")

![](https://daaf.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/3-scaled-e1761790467432.png "3")

![](https://daaf.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/2-scaled-e1761790487654.png "2")

[DAAF 2025 IMPACT REPORT](https://daaf.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/DAAF_Fact_Sheet_2025-web.pdf)

_**DAAF, 2025, Photo by Dylan Buckee**_

# **a Connection to Country, Community and Culture, through Art and Design.**

**DAAF is the signature event from the [Darwin Aboriginal Art Fair Foundation (DAAF Foundation)](https://daaf.com.au/foundation/), a not-for-profit Indigenous organisation that is owned and governed by the Art Centres it represents, that celebrates the rich cultural and artistic diversity of Australia’s Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Art Centres.**

The Fair offers a unique opportunity for arts industry buyers, and art and design lovers, to purchase works directly from Indigenous owned and incorporated Art Centres. A creative space for connection, where visitors can meet artists in person, learn about Australia’s rich diverse cultural groups and be immersed in our country’s evolving contemporary Indigenous art scene.

Showcasing the work of both emerging and established artists, DAAF features stunning art inspired by Australia’s most varied locations. From remote desert and coastal regions, to rural and urban communities.

A wide range of styles, mediums and products are presented and available for purchase. Discover paintings on canvas, bark paintings, works on paper, limited edition prints, sculpture, didgeridoos, fibre art, cultural regalia and more.

[Meet our Art Centres](https://daaf.com.au/what-is-an-art-centre/)

[Accessibility at DAAF](https://daaf.com.au/daaf-2026/#Access)

# PUBLIC PROGRAM

**Come & engage with the contemporary creations of the world's oldest continuous living cultures!**

Alongside the Fair runs a vibrant **Public Program** of artist workshops, spectacular traditional dance performances, children’s activities, fashion and more… guaranteeing a memorable experience for all who attend.

[Learn more](https://daaf.com.au/public-program/)

# FASHION

**Australia's largest showcase of First Nations fashion! A legacy of contemporary expression, grounded in ancient cultures.**

Preceding the Fair, the Foundation also presents its fashion events from **Indigenous Fashion Projects**, with the renowned **Country to Couture** runways, and **National Indigenous Fashion Awards**.

[Learn more](https://www.ifp.org.au/)

# AROUND TOWN

**A collective of national Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander events in the Top End each August...**

The Fair itself was originally conceived to complement the **National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Art Awards (NATSIAA).** It also celebrates the **National Indigenous Music Awards**, **Garma Festival** and **Salon De Refuse.**

These prestigious events are held in the same period and together, mark the most significant few weeks of national Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander arts in the world.

We acknowledge the Larrakia people, both past and present, as the Traditional Owners of the land upon which the Darwin Aboriginal Art Fair Foundation will present events.
