# Sponsor Darwin Fringe

**Darwin fringe festival is growing, rapidly, into a major arts, social, and economic opportunity for the top end. Every year we present dozens of shows with hundreds of artists to thousands of audience members. We want you to come on the journey with us as a festival partner.**

#### Why partner with Darwin Fringe?

**The Darwin Fringe is a hot house of arts and culture unlike any other festival or event locally.**

**It’s Exciting!** Darwin’s local artists are wonderful and should be seen and supported. We provide an opportunity for young and emerging arts talent to create and present work here, and actively challenge the notion that you need to move to a big city to be able to make it in the arts, and we provocate and challenge our local arts sector to experiment and take risks.

**We’re Passionate about the NT** and for Darwin to be recognised as a place were wonderful events happen. The Darwin Fringe sees the city taken over with art and energy each July, and both artists and audiences from all over the country want to come and bask in it! Growing our city’s appeal for cultural tourism is a biggie for us, and as a Capital city we think it’s only right we have a Fringe Festival to equal our interstate counterparts.

**Our Audiences are incredible.** We know them well, because we share the same values; that Art is vital, that Darwin is unique, and that supporting your community is important.

#### **Partner benefits**

There’s a bunch of benefits to partnering with Darwin Fringe Festival, including all the usual suspects:

**Branding + acknowledgement**

**Activations + events**

**Advertising + exposure**

**Media + publicity**

We have a range of partnership and sponsorship categories with differing benefits,  
and are happy to talk about additional benefits such as:

**Special Events**

**Naming Rights**

**Award Categories**

#### OUR CYCLONIC SPONSOR CATEGORIES

#### Major Sponsor | $20,000+

A disrupter of the everyday as you transform the city, Major Sponsors are keystone to the Fringe ecosystem, wreaking havok on unaccesible systems and establishing fresh new pathways. You are passionate about creating vibrant experiences that bring people together and your contribution powers large-scale opportunities for artists and audiences across the region.

#### Category 5 | $5000+

Your support hits with the full force of a tropical cyclone delivering an extraudinary impact, powering the Fringe to new heights and leaving a trail of creativity and community joy in your wake. You help sustain the creative energy that makes the local arts scene so unique and accessible.

#### Category 4 | $2500+

You’re packing serious winds of change as a driving force behind the Festival’s success. Your sponsorship fuels major impact across the festival by amplifying key programs, helping the arts to travel further.

#### Category 3 | $1000+

A mighty gust of generosity helping to keep the festival in motion! You keep the Fringe spinning strong, energising artists, audiences, and the city alike.

#### Category 2 | $500+

You bring the momentum with your steady support that keeps the creative atmosphere alive and the festival forecast looking bright.

#### Category 1 | up to $500

Lovers of community and culture Category 1 Sponsors are front row fans of creativity and innovation.

Darwin Fringe acknowledges the Kulumbirigin Danggalaba, the Larrakia as the Traditional Owners of Garramilla the land on which we create, play and love.

We recognise your continued connection with the land, water and skies, and pay our respects to your ancestors, elders and community. We extend this respect to all Aboriginal, Torres Strait Island and First Nations people. You are the original artists and creators. We stand in solidarity with your fight for sovereignty and understand that colonisation is ongoing. We at Fringe know that we always have more to learn and do.

# Frequently Asked Questions

## Planning your visit?  
Here is everything you need to know before stepping aboard.  
  
Still have a question? We are happy to help. Email us at [admin@kuuma.com.au](mailto:admin@kuuma.com.au?subject=FAQs%20-%20I%20still%20have%20a%20question) and we will be in touch. 

Before You ArriveYour Kuuma ExperienceBooking Your ExperienceGift CardsCancellation and Policies

### Where is Kuuma?

KUUMA is located at **Margate Marina in Barretta, Tasmania**, approximately 20 minutes south of Hobart.

  

For directions, view [KUUMA – Nature Sauna](https://maps.app.goo.gl/VxA1vb3kh83PhF6VA) on Google Maps.

### When should I arrive?

Please arrive at the designated meeting point **30 minutes before your session’s departure time**. This allows time for boarding and the safety briefing.

  

For example: if your session departs at 10:00 am, you should arrive at the meeting point by 9:30 am.

  

Communal sessions must depart on time. If you miss boarding and the briefing, your booking will be forfeited.

  

For private sessions, where you have booked all session seats, we can wait for late arrivals, however the session will still finish at the scheduled time.

### Where should I park and meet the team?

**PARKING**

  

*   Park **outside** the Marina gate (see map below).
    
*   Do not park within the Marina.
    
*   Once parked, head directly to the designated meeting point.
    
*   **Allow 5 minutes to walk to the meeting point.**
    

  

**MEETING POINT**

  

The Kuuma Skipper/Sauna Master will meet you at the designated meeting point (see map below) and escort you to the sauna boat berth. **Please do not access the berth and remain at the meeting point until Kuuma staff arrive.**

  

![](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/24d751_f951ab468f934c3fa864437d4e6543d1~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_49,h_30,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_auto/24d751_f951ab468f934c3fa864437d4e6543d1~mv2.png)

Parking and Meeting Point Location Map - Margate Marina

  

  

![](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/24d751_31ea34cc9dcc4721bb470c0454b26bad~mv2.jpeg/v1/fill/w_147,h_79,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_auto/24d751_31ea34cc9dcc4721bb470c0454b26bad~mv2.jpeg)

Members Gate & Visitor Gate – Margate Marina

  

  

![](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/24d751_8d4bfee4dccf43d0b1c17e1c9ace1643~mv2.jpeg/v1/fill/w_159,h_159,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_auto/24d751_8d4bfee4dccf43d0b1c17e1c9ace1643~mv2.jpeg)

Kuuma Meeting Point – Margate Marina

  

### What should I bring?

Please wear warm, comfortable clothing and bring the following in a small, closable bag:

  

*   Swimwear (nudity is not permitted)
    
*   A water bottle
    

  

Towels are provided for all Kuuma experiences and filtered drinking water is available onboard.

### What is the best way to get to Kuuma?

KUUMA is located at **Margate Marina, Barretta**, approximately **20 minutes south of Hobart**.

  

We recommend travelling by **car**, as this is the easiest and most convenient way to reach us. Simply search "[KUUMA – Nature Sauna](https://maps.app.goo.gl/VxA1vb3kh83PhF6VA)" in Google Maps for turn-by-turn directions.

  

If you're not driving, taxis and rideshare services (such as Uber) are also available from Hobart.

  

Public transport is available, however travel times are significantly longer. If travelling by bus, we recommend planning your journey in advance using Google Maps or the Tasmanian Government journey planner.

  

Please remember to arrive **30 minutes before your scheduled departure time** to allow for boarding and the mandatory safety briefing.

# About Darwin Fringe

**The biggest platform for emerging, independent and experimental artists in the NT, Darwin Fringe is your 10 day multi arts Festival with bite.**

## What is a Fringe Festival?

Starting in 1947 when 8 artists performed outside of the Edinburgh Festival after not being accepted into the program, the movement has rapidly grown into a network of 300+ independent Festivals world wide. While every Fringe festival is different, we all share a commitment to artistic freedom, experimentation and creating opportunities for artists to present new work. Darwin is proud to house the most northern Fringe Festival in Australia. Read more about the history of Fringes by clicking [here](https://worldfringe.com/history-of-fringe/).

## Our Vision

A supportive, diverse, and exciting local arts sector with multiple opportunities for artistic growth, attracting local and national interest. 

## Our Mission

The Darwin Fringe is a hybrid open-access festival that supports the development of the arts community, providing opportunities for all artists to emerge, experiment, and showcase new and diverse works in Garramilla/Darwin to local and national audiences.

## 2027 Dates

July Friday 16th – Sunday 25th

#### **The Board**

**Chair:** Zoe Scrogings  
**Vice Chair & Public Officer:** Kat Byron  
**Treasurer:** Gina Machado  
**Secretary:** Hannah Illingworth  
**Member:** Claire McNamara  
**Member:** Heather Docker  
**Member:** Marna Paulson  
**Member:** Michaela Nutt  
**Member:** Steve Kyne

Pssst. We’re currently on the lookout for a new volunteer Treasurer. [CLICK HERE](https://darwinfringe.org.au/treasurer-eoi/) to find out more.

#### **Brief history**

Fringe has long been part of Darwin’s cultural fabric, first appearing in the 1980s as a club-style offering within the Bougainvillea Festival (now Darwin Festival). It became a space for experimentation and collaboration, responding to the Territory’s rapidly growing creative landscape. In the early 2010s, a playful misprint saw the Festival briefly rebranded as the “Fridge Festival,” leading to a city-wide program of installations and performances. By 2014, local artists and producers identified a growing need for accessible, career-building opportunities. A group led by CJ Fraser-Bell relaunched Darwin Fringe as an open-access, independent arts festival in 2015, featuring just over 20 events and a dedicated team.

The Festival rapidly expanded, presenting over 180 performances from 100 shows by 2019. At this time leadership transitioned to current Director Hannah Illingworth, who has continued to grow the program while navigating challenges, including two major COVID-19 disruptions in 2020 and 2021. In 2019 Hannah held the role with Tamara Howie who later left town, resulting in the current leadership scenario.

In 2022, DFF became an independent incorporated entity after many years of Auspiced support from Brown’s Mart, and now runs with the guidance of a volunteer board. In 2024 Darwin Fringe Incorporated received Charity status as a Deductible Gift Recipient. Today, Darwin Fringe is a keystone event on the Territory’s arts calendar, recognised for fostering grassroots creativity and providing crucial stepping stones for artists across disciplines, acting as a true showcase of the Top End’s creative heartbeat.

**Nowadays, the Darwin Fringe has become the biggest independent arts platform in the Top End offering audiences 10 days of unique low-cost experiences in July.**

### Darwin Fringe Incorporated Policy

Read our Policies and find out more about how we do things.

[READ NOW](https://drive.google.com/file/d/16uunW7-hDjYTKnxWqCVB4XiJP1OCQP7c/view?usp=drive_link)

### Team

![](https://darwinfringe.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2020/02/director-pic-1-1-336x420.jpg)

# Creative Director and CEO: Hannah Illingworth

**Pronoun:** she / her **Arts I practise:** visual and media arts

Originally from Rubibi, Broome WA Hannah is passionate about empowering people through community arts and cultural development. With a career spanning 10+ years her practice values intention, sustainability, efficient systems, clear communications, adaptive procedures and intuition. Having grown up in regional Northern Australia often on cattle stations, Hannah was brought up knowing that innovation is vital, where sometimes there are no other options other than to give things a go. Early on she learnt the value of relationships and clear communication.

Hannah has acted in leadership positions with local art communities and has held roles across an array of events, services and venues. Beginning her career in Mount Isa QLD as a 16 year old custom shoe illustrator and event support person she has always been passionate about self-expression, learning and healing through creativity. Having lived and worked in Sydney and Broken Hill NSW for 2 years following Mount Isa Hannah returned to Gulumoerrgin, Darwin NT in late 2014 where she has now spent half of her life, having lived here from age 10 – 16.

Hannah’s creative practice explores dialectics, theology, culture and activism.

## FOUNDATION

# **About Darwin Aboriginal Art Fair  Foundation**

### **Where Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Arts and Cultures are strong and celebrated.** 

[Meet our People – the Board and Staff](https://daaf.com.au/foundation/our-people)

[Meet our Art & Culture Centre Members](https://daaf.com.au/what-is-an-art-centre/)

[Join the DAAF Foundation Family](https://daaf.com.au/support-us/)

[](https://daaf.com.au/foundation/#)

# **OUR STORY**

#### **Celebrating the rich cultural and artistic diversity of Australia’s Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Art Centres. The DAAF Foundation is a not-for-profit Indigenous organisation that is owned and governed by the Art Centres it represents.**

#### 2007

In 2006, discussions at the Museum and Art Gallery of the Northern Territory's foundation board explored creating an event that connected Art Centres, art collectors, buyers, and industry specialists who travel from across Australia to attend the annual National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Art Awards (NATSIAA). They proposed that an art fair be established to provide a platform for Art Centres from the NT to showcase and sell artwork while gathered in one location. This concept was spearheaded by Apolline Kohen, former Director of Maningrida Art and Culture, who was also the chair of the MAGNT foundation board at the time.

**The inaugural Darwin Aboriginal Art Fair (DAAF)** was coordinated by the Maningrida Arts & Culture's then Assistant Director, Claire Summers, who brought the event to life with a very humble budget during its first two years of operation.

The first Art Fair hosted 16 Northern Territory based Aboriginal-owned incorporated Art Centres. It was deemed an instant success by the industry.

#### 2008-10

In December 2008, a dedicated steering committee of stakeholder representatives was formed to govern the event, and the event management was outsourced. In 2009 and 2010 DAAF was managed with a memorandum of understanding with To End Arts Marketing. In late 2010 the DAAF steering committee commissioned an organisational review. The aim of the review was to assess the potential directions for DAAF and how to foster a period of new growth, with strengthened governance and an expanded vision.

#### 2011

In 2011 the DAAF steering committee began to implement the recommendations of the review, transitioning to an independent not-for-profit Foundation governed by a board of nine representatives with a minimum representation of three Aboriginal board members. It was agreed that board positions would include cultural leaders, Art Centre managers, peak body representatives and industry directors.

During this transitional year, a partnership with Darwin Regional Indigenous Advancement & Community Development Employment Program (DRIACDEP) was established to assist with opportunities for event delivery, Aboriginal employment and administration support. An event management firm was contracted to manage the event, which included a new program of public forums, workshops and tours.

On the 12th December 2011, the new Board met in Darwin for the Darwin Aboriginal Art Fair (DAAF) Foundation Limited first directors meeting and the organisation was formalised. Dynamic consultations then took place to develop a 2012-2014 strategic plan. DAAF Foundation submitted registration to ASIC in early 2012, with an initial 42 Art Centre members as well as the peak Art Centre associations ANKAAA (now known as ANKA) and Desart.

#### 2012

**On the 2nd March 2012, the Darwin Aboriginal Art Fair Foundation Limited was officially established,** meaning that the Darwin Aboriginal Art Fair was owned and operated by a membership of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Art Centres.

#### 2016-2020

The DAAF Foundation has grown well beyond delivering our annual Darwin Aboriginal Art Fair. In 2016, the Foundation launched the first **Country to Couture** event as part of the Fair's 10th anniversary celebrations. Its instant success swiftly led to the establishment of the **Indigenous Fashion Projects (IFP)** program in 2020. IFP is now the home of Country to Couture, **National Indigenous Fashion Awards**, and a suite of development programs including the **Pathways Program** which culminates in a runway show at Australian Fashion Week.

The Foundation demonstrated its agility and innovation in response to the Covid-19 pandemic in 2020 by developing an **online art fair**. This led to an ambitious digital project which is now known as the **Indigenous Arts Hub.** “The Hub” is comprised of a new online platform to engage audiences about the sector, and a community of practice to support learning, capacity building, and connecting for our Art Centres and fashion community.

# **OUR** **VISION**

#### We envision a future where Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Arts and Cultures are strong and celebrated.

# **OUR** **PRINCIPLES**

## **Centre Culture, Community and Country.**

Honour, sustain, and privilege Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander cultural knowledge, traditions, stories, languages and practices. Understand that culture is living, evolving and enduring. Acknowledge and care for Country, physically and spiritually.

## **Connectedness.**

Approach our relationships with respect and reciprocity. Connect with and serve creatives and communities through our work. Build relationships with depth and longevity in mind. Lead with curiosity and foster collaboration.

## **Continual Innovation.**

Be responsive to change—cultural, technological, social, environmental, market—and proactively explore new ways to increase our impact. Integrate environmental, financial, cultural and organisational sustainability in planning and operations.

## **Co-created Safety.**

Recognise that cultural, physical, emotional and psychological safety are required to innovate and thrive. Actively co-create safe spaces for creatives and the communities we collaborate with.

# **OUR VALUES**

#### Darwin Aboriginal Art Fair Foundation:

*   Acknowledges and values the Larrakia people as Traditional Owners of the land on which the Foundation calls home;
*   Values and respects Indigenous-owned Art Centres in their support of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander art, design and cultural expressions;
*   Values the diversity, integrity and expression of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander artists and designers and will support this through ethical best practice, education and promotional activity;
*   Values the inclusion of diverse opinions and respectful communications;
*   Values the history and significant achievements of the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander art and design industry.

## **ACKNOWLEDGEMENT**

The Darwin Aboriginal Art Fair Foundation acknowledges the value, diversity and integrity of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander art, music and performance as an integral expression of Australian culture. We respect the work of Art Centres in their support of the richness of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander cultural aspirations and expressions.

We acknowledge the Larrakia people, both past and present, as the Traditional Owners of the land upon which the Darwin Aboriginal Art Fair Foundation will present events. We appreciate the opportunity to share this Country and are committed to working together and appropriately consulting with the Larrakia people in presenting the Darwin Aboriginal Art Fair.[](https://daaf.com.au/dashboard)

# About kuuma

Australia’s first floating sauna, handcrafted in Hobart and shaped by the Tasmanian landscape.

[Explore Experiences](https://www.kuuma.com.au/services)

###### The People Behind Kuuma

​

We are Nathan and Chloe, the creators, designers and builders behind Kuuma.

What began as an idea inspired by a sauna experience in Norway became a four-year journey of planning, designing and taking a leap into the unknown. Kuuma was then handcrafted in Hobart over the course of a year.

![Kuuma founders Chloe and Nathan aboard the floating sauna boat](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/24d751_8db4328283024ee1898d97b25e96a32e~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_689,h_450,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/24d751_8db4328283024ee1898d97b25e96a32e~mv2.jpg)

## OUR STORY

​​​​​Kuuma was born from a shared commitment to each other, and to a different way of living. Our story begins long before the boat, on a cold northern coast in Norway. We stepped into a sauna by a frozen fjord and felt something ancient stir. Wrapped in silence and steam, we found more than heat. We found clarity. A ritual as old as fire that brought people back to themselves. We knew then that we wanted to carry this tradition home and share its magic with others. But back in Australia, life pulled us into a familiar current – work that drained us, the mental load of modern life, a growing disconnect between our values and our days. With a young daughter and long-held dreams, we stood at a crossroads. Redundancy came as both a shock and a sign. We could not keep going the way we were. So, we chose to begin again...​ In 2020, we started sketching the blueprint for Kuuma; a floating sauna moored in nature, shaped by Scandinavian wisdom and Australian wildness. Between parenting and planning, hope and fear, we slowly built both a boat and a business. We pitched ideas to National Parks, talked to locals, gathered stories, and adjusted sails. After many hopes and disappointments, leads and dead ends, we found light again in Tasmania. While living in Melbourne and boat building in Hobart, we juggled family, distance, and determination. In 2024, Kuuma was launched – Australia’s first sauna boat. Handcrafted in Hobart, it is a vessel of warmth and care. A space where people come to breathe deeply, feel fully, and reconnect with what matters. Every session reminds us why we began. We see it in the flushed cheeks, the quiet smiles, the friends who return again and again. Kuuma is not just about heat and cold. It is about showing up for yourself, finding presence, and sharing simple joy. To us, success looks like stillness in a fast world. It looks like a growing community of Australians rediscovering the power of ancient rituals, together. This is only the beginning. We dream of Kuuma inspiring a new wave of sauna culture in Australia – rooted in nature, built on connection, open to all.

Read less

![Kuuma | Using the Tasmanian Mark](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/NEdQTMzaNp0/maxresdefault.jpg)

Play Video

[![Brand Tasmania logo "A proud partner of Tasmanina"](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/24d751_2f2cd4d72e2c4c2c9ef5f409b1f3be2b~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_270,h_48,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/Tasmanian-Proud-Partner--Pos-PRIMARY.png)](https://tasmanian.com.au/)

### Designed Around the Ritual

​​

Kuuma’s floating sauna was designed around large windows, generous outdoor space and direct access to the water, allowing guests to move between heat, cold, rest and the surrounding Tasmanian landscape.

![Guest entering the water from the Kuuma floating sauna boat in Southern Tasmania](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/24d751_4830f23cef964bdfbcd4b2d68b589a6a~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_122,h_81,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_avif,quality_auto/24d751_4830f23cef964bdfbcd4b2d68b589a6a~mv2.jpg)

![Wood-fired sauna heater inside the Kuuma floating sauna near Hobart](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/24d751_d46e1c150a434087af541d20bc15c538~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_122,h_81,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_avif,quality_auto/24d751_d46e1c150a434087af541d20bc15c538~mv2.jpg)

### The meaning of Kuuma

​​

Kuuma means “hot” in Finnish.

​

For us, it also represents warmth in a broader sense: fire, care, connection and the feeling of returning to yourself.

### Our Vision

​​

Kuuma was created to offer a slower and more meaningful way to experience sauna.

Our vision is to grow a sauna culture in Australia that values connection, simplicity, nature and the ritual of taking time.

![Guests sharing a quiet sauna experience inside Kuuma’s floating sauna in Southern Tasmania](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/24d751_4228038dc9784cddb4b685d374fe6558~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_123,h_82,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_avif,quality_auto/24d751_4228038dc9784cddb4b685d374fe6558~mv2.jpg)

![Guest arriving at the Kuuma floating sauna at Margate Marina in Southern Tasmania](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/24d751_1937294aa17b47558f99bef2b9289025~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_122,h_81,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_avif,quality_auto/24d751_1937294aa17b47558f99bef2b9289025~mv2.jpg)

### Australia’s First Sauna BOAT

​​

Kuuma is a custom-designed commercial tour vessel, handcrafted in Hobart specifically for sauna cruising.

The boat combines a wood-fired sauna, generous outdoor decks and direct access to the waters of North West Bay in Southern Tasmania.

### our impact

Shaped by the water and landscape around us, we believe caring for both is part of our responsibility.

![Guest cooling down by the water after a Kuuma wood-fired sauna cruise in Southern Tasmania.](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/24d751_ed511767bc5d416eb15ab02db6935378~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_403,h_334,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/Jess%20Oakenfull-Web-KuumaSauna-62.jpg)

caring for the bay

We take practical steps to reduce our impact on North West Bay. Guests are encouraged to minimise sunscreen, perfume and makeup before entering the water, helping protect the marine environment central to the Kuuma experience.

​

Our operations and mooring practices are planned with care to minimise disturbance to sensitive areas of the bay.

![Native bushland and clear coastal waters of North West Bay, Tasmania.](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/24d751_22f892f299214eefb9794c625ef53fc5~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_403,h_334,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/tasmanian-coastline-north-west-bay.jpg)

reducing our footprint

We hold Sustainable Tourism Accreditation and actively measure our emissions, with a Climate and Emissions Reduction Plan guiding how we continue to reduce our footprint.

​

In 2026, we also completed a Plastic Free Places Tasmania Action Plan, reviewing single-use items across our operations and identifying opportunities to avoid, reuse or switch to better alternatives.​​​​​

​

[View our Climate & Emissions Reduction Plan](https://platform.carbonhalo.com/export/memberdashboard/689ab84247ac890729c2e256)

![Volunteer Marine Rescue Kingborough crew with rescue vessel in Southern Tasmania.](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/24d751_fcf771ef111d4c389c537774f9cffe56~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_403,h_334,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/Volunteer-marine-rescue-kingborough.jpg)

supporting our community

We donate 1% of our annual profit to Volunteer Marine Rescue Kingborough, helping the local volunteers who provide search and rescue services across Southern Tasmania’s waterways.

​

We also contribute to local organisations and community initiatives throughout the year.

###### [Explore the Region of Southern Tasmania](https://hobartandbeyond.com.au/)  
 

Plan Your Visit Beyond Kuuma

​

Kuuma is located in Southern Tasmania, just a 20 minutes drive south of Hobart. The region is known for its natural beauty, cool climate produce, and easy access to bushwalks, beaches, and island adventures. Whether you are here for a short visit or an extended stay, there is plenty to explore nearby and further afield.

![View of kunanyi / Mount Wellington across the forested landscape of Southern Tasmania](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/24d751_9f9dcbfd2db449eca22d69445e4c20b2~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_112,h_75,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_avif,quality_auto/24d751_9f9dcbfd2db449eca22d69445e4c20b2~mv2.jpg)

###### Nature & Outdoors​

Close to Kuuma – perfect for before or after your sauna session:

​

*   [Snug Falls](https://tasmania.com/things-to-do/waterfalls/snug-falls/) – A short walk to a hidden waterfall, just 10 minutes away.
    
*   [Coningham Beach](https://hobartandbeyond.com.au/blog/coningham-beach-and-snug-point-track/) – Sheltered, peaceful, and ideal for a refreshing dip.
    
*   [Alum Cliffs Track](https://www.greaterhobarttrails.com.au/tracks/alum-cliffs-track) – Clifftop views and a scenic trail between Kingston and Taroona.
    

​

Worth a detour – for a day trip or a longer stay in the region:

​

*   [Bruny Island](https://www.discovertasmania.com.au/regions/hobart-and-south/bruny-island/) – Beaches, bushwalks, and local produce. Catch the ferry from Kettering, 15 minutes from Kuuma.
    
*   [Hartz Mountains National Park](https://parks.tas.gov.au/explore-our-parks/hartz-mountains-national-park) – Rugged alpine landscapes and glacier-sculpted valleys, around 1.5 hours south-west.
    
*   [Mount Field National Park](https://www.discovertasmania.com.au/regions/hobart-and-south/mount-field-national-park/) – Home to Russell Falls, tall tree forests, and highland hikes—just over an hour north-west.
    

![Forested Tasmanian coastline and clear water on North West Bay](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/24d751_22f892f299214eefb9794c625ef53fc5~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_133,h_75,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_avif,quality_auto/24d751_22f892f299214eefb9794c625ef53fc5~mv2.jpg)

###### Eat & Drink

Close to Kuuma – quick, quality bites just minutes away:

​​​

*   [Peppermint Bay](https://www.discovertasmania.com.au/things-to-do/food-and-drink/peppermintbay/) – Destination dining by the water in Woodbridge, known for Tasmanian produce and wine.
    
*   [Beach Rd. Bakes – Local Margate favourite for freshly baked treats, making it an easy stop before or after a Kuuma session.](https://www.discovertasmania.com.au/things-to-do/food-and-drink/thechannnelcafe/)
    
*   [Woodbridge Village Store](https://maps.app.goo.gl/cqyP96LZivtsSnsb9) – A charming general store turned café with fresh local fare and delicious pies and bánh mì.
    
*   [The Channel Café and Gift Shop](https://www.discovertasmania.com.au/things-to-do/food-and-drink/thechannnelcafe/) – A cosy stop in Margate with excellent bánh mì.
    
*   [Hopfields Brewery](https://www.hopfieldsbrewery.com.au/) – Local craft beer brewed on-site with food trucks and a relaxed atmosphere.
    
*   [Meredith’s Orchard](https://meredithsorchard.com.au/) – A local favourite for fresh apples, seasonal produce, and pantry staples​
    

​

Worth a detour – for a scenic drive and a longer sit-down meal:​​

​

*   [Summer Kitchen Bakery](https://www.summerkitchenbakery.com.au/) – Organic sourdoughs, pies, and pastries in Ranelagh—a Huon Valley gem.
    
*   [The Lost Captain Restaurant & Taphouse](https://www.lostcaptain.com.au/) – A newer spot in Cygnet serving great food, craft beers, and a relaxed pub vibe.
    

![Guests relaxing inside the Kuuma floating sauna overlooking Margate Marina](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/24d751_bfe368ba854e40f0bff47fc4d1669f54~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_113,h_75,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_avif,quality_auto/24d751_bfe368ba854e40f0bff47fc4d1669f54~mv2.jpg)

###### Stay Awhile

Close to Kuuma – unique and restful places nearby:​

​

*   [Poet Ode](https://www.discovertasmania.com.au/accommodation/poetsode/) – Thoughtfully styled studio accommodation tucked in the hills above Margate.
    
*   [Snug Haus](https://www.discovertasmania.com.au/accommodation/snug-haus/) – A peaceful, modern retreat in Snug with views over the D’Entrecasteaux Channel.
    
*   [Gate Keeper’s Lodge](https://www.gatekeeperslodge.com.au/) – A beautifully restored sandstone cottage on North Hobart, full of charm and history.
    

​

Worth a detour – slow stays a little further afield:

​

*   [The Barn at Eden Farmstay (Cygnet)](https://edenfarmstay.com.au/) – Rustic yet refined farmstay with animals, fire pits, and valley views.
    
*   [Little Seed Farm (Pelverata)](https://thelittleseed.com.au/) – Off-grid luxury surrounded by forest—ideal for couples and nature lovers.
    

![View of kunanyi / Mount Wellington across North West Bay from the Kuuma floating sauna](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/24d751_34b8a225cb944b0b8506ddee4b6df6fd~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_112,h_75,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_avif,quality_auto/24d751_34b8a225cb944b0b8506ddee4b6df6fd~mv2.jpg)

## Partnerships

Darwin Festival gratefully acknowledges the generous support from our 2026 partners. We encourage our audiences to support these organisations as generously as they support our Festival.

### Become a Partner

Darwin Festival presents an unparalleled opportunity to connect with your customers or business networks and engage with the local community. We invite you to start a new partnership or to build on your experience as a Festival partner by collaborating with us. Every partnership with Darwin Festival is unique. We welcome the opportunity to work with your team to tailor a partnership that meets your objectives and delivers measurable outcomes against your investment.  
  
Contact our Development team on 08 8943 4200 or send us an email [here.](mailto:kay.crozier@darwinfestival.org.au)

[View our 2025 Annual Review](https://issuu.com/darwin_festival/docs/darwin_festival_2025_annual_review)

# FAQ

## General information

Who is Darwin Festival for?

Everyone! Our Festival is safe, inclusive and welcoming and audiences of all ages and demographics can binge on a fabulous array of artistic offerings. We offer something for absolutely everyone and encourage you to try something you might not normally see –  we promise you’ll be surprised and delighted!

When is the Festival on?

Darwin Festival 2027 runs from Wednesday 5 – Sunday 22 August.

Where is the Festival held?

The beating heart of Darwin Festival is Festival Park, located on the corner of Smith St and Harry Chan Ave in the Darwin CBD. Our other key venues, including Darwin Amphitheatre at George Brown Darwin Botanic Gardens, are in and around the CBD, with visual arts and performance works also held in venues across greater Darwin.

## Festival news

How can I stay in the loop?

Subscribe to our e-news so you don’t miss a thing. You’ll be the first to hear of exciting program reveals, competitions and news. [_Subscribe here.  
_](https://www.darwinfestival.org.au/account/marketing_preferences)  

Like us for event news and exclusive competitions on [_Facebook_](https://www.facebook.com/darwinfestival).  
  

Follow us on [_Instagram_](https://www.instagram.com/darwinfestival/) to see behind the scenes pics, meet our artists and be inspired by all things Darwin Festival.  
  

Subscribe to the Darwin Festival [_YouTube_](https://www.youtube.com/user/DarwinFestival) channel to see sizzle reels and highlight videos.  
  

Use the #darwinfestival hashtag to tag your Instagram and Facebook posts, and tweets.

## Voucher/Credit Note/Promo Codes

I have a voucher or credit note. How do I redeem this?

To redeem a Darwin Festival Gift Voucher, enter the 16-digit code from your confirmation email into the ‘Pay with Voucher’ field at final checkout. The voucher credit will then be applied automatically to your booking. How long is my gift voucher valid for?

Vouchers purchased after 1 January 2023 are valid for three years from the purchase date, as stated in your confirmation email. Vouchers from previous years were only valid for their respective Festival periods and cannot be used for the current Festival. 

## Supporting the Festival

I’d like to donate some money to the Festival

You can find out all you need to know about supporting us financially on our [_Donate_](https://www.darwinfestival.org.au/donate/) page.

## Feedback

I have some feedback I’d like to pass on

All feedback received in writing will be responded to within seven days of receipt. Please email [_hello@darwinfestival.org.au_](mailto:hello@darwinfestival.org.au) or post to GPO Box 570 Darwin NT 0801.  
  

Have a question? Please call the Darwin Festival office on [_08 8943 4200_](tel:0889434200) or email [_hello@darwinfestival.org.au_](mailto:hello@darwinfestival.org.au).

Darwin Festival acknowledges the Traditional Custodians of the lands on which we live, learn and work. We pay our respects to the Larrakia, or Saltwater, Elders and to all Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples.

## FAQ ~ Frequently Asked Questions

#### What are ‘transaction fees’ and how much are they?

Transaction fees help cover some of the associated costs of operating our ticketing system. Currently all transactions come with a fee of $3 except for merch sales at the box office.

#### Do you accept Companion Cards?

YES! The card allows your chosen companion or carer to go with you to participating entertainment, recreation venues and activities without paying for a ticket. Just bring the card with you. For booking select the Companion Card option when checking out and bring the card with you to the show.

#### Who can access concession pricing?

Students of all kinds, pensioners, Seniors Card participants, people on centrelink, those who are unhoused/unwaged and other concession holders can access this ticketing price. If applicable just bring your appropriate card with you.

#### Can I be a volunteer with the festival?

Yes! We love new people joining the Darwin Fringe Family. However you must be over 18. [Sign up here.](https://darwinfringe.org.au/get-involved/volunteers/)

#### When does Darwin Fringe recruit staff?

Our team is made up of only a handful of paid positions, most of which are currently filled. When special project coordinator roles pop-up or box office work becomes available we will post this on our website, newsletter and socials in the lead up to the festival.

#### I’m an Artist, how can I get involved?

Darwin Fringe Festival is proudly open-access, so ANYONE can join in. Sign up to our [creative network](https://darwinfringe.org.au/creative-network-registration/) or newsletter to receive direct updates about this process. Applications generally open in October the year before (about 10 months before the Festival in July).

#### How do I buy tickets?

Tickets go on sale on May1 and can be purchase online or over the phone. The box office will be set up from late May/ early June after the program is released.

#### What does the virtual waiting room mean?

This screen shows up as a defence against hack attacks and usually means the ticketing company we use Ticketsearch is receiving a high amount of traffic. Don’t worry though it doesn’t mean something bad’s happening, it may mean a massive event has gone on sale somewhere else. If you wait a few seconds this screen should go away. We apologise for any inconvenience.

#### When should I arrive to see the show?

At least 15 minutes before the event as doors will usually open around 5-10 minutes before the show so we can have everyone seated in time to begin as the designated time. Want to grabs drinks and snack? Arrive even earlier!

#### How can I find out about accessibility of shows?

As we activate more than 20 venues accessibility varies and is listed in each event on the website. If you would like clarification or have further questions please do reach out. You can also read more about Festival access [here](https://darwinfringe.org.au/access/).

Your questions answered

# Frequently asked questions

## When is the market on?

Mindil Beach Sunset Market always operates from the last Thursday in April until the last Thursday in October annually.

## Can I bring my dog or pet to the market?

Due to the City of Darwin regulations, animals and fur babies are not permitted in the market with the exception of service dogs.

## Can I buy alcohol at the markets?

The Mindil Market is a BYO (bring your own) venue. Alcohol is also served at our Sunset Lounge area. You can book in advance.

[Sunset Lounge](https://mindil.com.au/sunset-lounge/)

## Are there cash or ATM facilities on site?

You'll find ATM's at each end of the market in the Territory Space and Community Space areas.

The majority of food & craft stalls take EFTPOS, some stalls are cash only.

## Does the market open if it is raining?

Mindil will operate unless deemed an unsafe site by the Management Committee and Operational Team. Updates will be posted on our Facebook page.

## Are the Thursday and the Sunday Markets the same?

Thursday is our main market with all stalls trading. Sunday is a smaller market often referred to as the locals night. Stall locations may change depending on the night, please see our information booth located in the craft area to direct you to your favourite stall.

## Can I smoke and/or vape at the markets?

Mindil is a no smoking and/or vaping market. Smoking and Vaping are permitted in the main car park, on the edges of the market next to the toilet blocks and on the public beach.

## Are there facilities for people with different abilities?

Disabled parking is available and whilst access around the market is no problem, there is no direct wheelchair access to the beach. There are disabled toilets in each toilet block (located in the Territory & Community Space).

## How do I get to the market?

Mindil Markets is located less than 3km from Darwin City Centre. Nestled between Mindil Beach Casino and the Botanical Gardens, its an easy walk or hop on bus 4 or 6. Taxis from the city cost about $10 and free parking is available via Gilruth Avenue.

## How many stalls are there?

Mindil has 150+ stalls with approximately 60 food stalls representing cuisines from all over the world. Other stalls include handmade clothing, jewellery, homewares, indigenous product and information stalls.

[Stall directory](https://mindil.com.au/stall-directory/)

## Is there parking available at the market?

Yes we provide free parking within the market area. Additionally, parking is located at the Darwin High School and along the surrounding streets.

## What do I do if I require first aid?

St Johns Ambulance is available at the back of the Craft Space near the Information Booth. If it is an urgent case please grab one of our security personnel for assistance.

## What do I do if I wish to share my experience of the Market?

Mindil Markets welcomes all feedback from patrons and works hard to continually improve all facets of the Market’s operation. Your feedback is appreciated.

[Contact us](https://mindil.com.au/contact/)

## What if I lose or find something?

We have a lost and found register at the Information Booth. For information on lost and found items during office hours please call 08 8981 3454. We also suggest you contact City of Darwin on 08 8930 0300.

## What kind of food is sold at the markets?

There are delicacies from a variety of countries, Vietnamese, Thai, Indonesian, Chinese, Sri Lankan, Malaysian, Indian, Greek, Italian, Mexican, just to name a few. Please see the Information Booth if you have any particular dietary needs. We have Halal & vegetarian stalls & many dishes can be made gluten free.

[Food stalls](https://mindil.com.au/stall-directory/food-and-beverage/)

## What other markets can I visit?

A number of local markets operate from Thursday through to Sunday at various locations throughout the suburbs. More information can be found at City of Darwin's Council website.

[Visit Council Website](http://www.darwin.nt.gov.au/live/your-community/recreation-families-children-and-young-people/markets)

## What time is the sunset?

Sunset during the dry season is approximately 6.30pm but varies throughout the 6 month period.

### About

There’s no better time to be in the tropical Top End than during Darwin Festival each August, where a fabulous festival wonderland awaits you. Balmy nights under twinkling lights provide the perfect backdrop for an unforgettable dry season, the Top End’s tropical winter.

  
Australia’s hottest winter arts festival combines the quintessential spirit and energy of Darwin with warm outdoor festivities and a vibrant program of events for an unforgettable good time. Join in the fun of hot August nights 4-22 August 2027!

### History

Australia’s most northern and only tropical arts festival was born out of the destruction and devastation of a natural disaster over 50 years ago. Cyclone Tracy tore through the Northern Territory’s capital city on Christmas Eve in 1974 leaving behind 68 dead and 25,000 Darwin residents homeless. There was talk from some of abandoning the city site altogether but others were more determined to rebuild.

  
In 1977, Northern Territory Director of Health Dr Charles Gurd suggested celebrating the town’s revival with a festival that would draw the community together and reflect the optimism of those determined to rebuild.

  
Staged in July 1979, the Bougainvillea Festival, held on the first anniversary of the granting of self-government for the NT, was a floral festival aimed at promoting the beautification of the city.

  
The early years of the Festival featured such events as the Bougainvillea Queen of Quests competition, Home Garden contests, the Grand Parade – a floral procession with floats and decorated bikes – sporting events, a billy-cart derby, birdman rally and a mardi gras.

  
The Festival shifted its focus toward community arts in the 1990s, with a vision of becoming a cultural focus for the region through a greater emphasis on cultural performances and arts activities. Artists were recruited to work with community associations and schools to invigorate the Grand Parade, and Indigenous communities and Asia Pacific cultural groups were encouraged to have greater participation. In 1996, Darwin’s annual celebration became known as the Festival of Darwin.

  
In 2003 under the direction of newly appointed Artistic Director Malcolm Blaylock, the Festival was renamed to reflect its international status in the arts. Darwin Festival is a vibrant arts and cultural event with an eclectic and substantial program that takes advantage of Darwin’s delightful dry season weather and spectacular outdoor venues. Darwin Festival reflects Darwin’s position at the Top End of Australia, its unique Indigenous and multicultural population and its close proximity to Asia while at the same time showcasing some of Australia’s finest arts performers.

  
Darwin Festival is held over 18 exciting days and nights, with local and touring performances and events including outdoor concerts, workshops, theatre, dance music, comedy and cabaret, film and visual arts. During the Festival, Darwin buzzes with performers, artists, locals and visitors enjoying the vibrant and colourful atmosphere and festivities.

  
Darwin Festival Artistic Directors have been Malcolm Blaylock (2003 – 2008), Jo Duffy (2009 – 2011), Edwina Lunn (2012 – 2014), Andrew Ross (2015 & 2016), Felix Preval (2017 –2022) and Kate Fell (2023 – 2026). Ben Graetz is the Artistic Director for the Festivals from 2027 to 2030.

![Awards](https://www.darwinfestival.org.au/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6ODMsInB1ciI6ImJsb2JfaWQifX0=--0eb10a43c5ef94a527601e1e7001711bb3edcd04/Untitled%20design%20\(1\).png)

# About Us

## Our Motto

> _Our motto is to **LIVE THE LIFESTYLE**. We aim to give every visitor a taste of Darwin’s carefree, relaxed, and creative lifestyle, especially during the dry season when everyone comes out to play._

## Darwin's Biggest & Best Market!

Mindil Beach Sunset Market is the jewel in the crown of Darwin's market culture, epitomizing what's fabulous about our city. Running along the foreshore of Mindil Beach, come and catch a stunning sunset over the Timor Sea.

*   [History](https://mindil.com.au/about/#history)
*   [A site of significance](https://mindil.com.au/about/#significance)
*   [Mindil Today](https://mindil.com.au/about/#today)

## History

Founded in 1987 by four visionaries, Mindil Beach Sunset Market brought a taste of Southeast Asia's night markets to Australia. From humble beginnings, it now hosts over 150 stalls featuring local and international cuisine, arts, crafts, and services. Operating from the last Thursday in April to the last Thursday in October, it is managed by the not-for-profit Mindil Beach Sunset Market Association (MBSMA).

  

[Contact](https://mindil.com.au/contact/)

## A Site of Significance

Mindil Beach has significant cultural importance for the Tiwi and Larrakia people, with the name 'Mindil' deriving from the Larrakia word 'Min-deel' (sweet nut grass). Historically a popular site for camping, swimming, and socializing, it has evolved from a rest area for military personnel in WWII to a bustling caravan park in the 1960s, and later, an upscale beach-side accommodation area by 2008.

*   [![](/assets/image-cache/Beer%20Can%20Regatta%202019%20-%20Flowpyre.2b8a3154.jpg)](https://mindil.com.au/about/uploads/General%20Use/Beer%20Can%20Regatta%202019%20-%20Flowpyre.jpg)

*   [![](/assets/image-cache/Territory%20Day%203%202019%20-%20Flowpyre.2b8a3154.jpg)](https://mindil.com.au/about/uploads/General%20Use/Territory%20Day%203%202019%20-%20Flowpyre.jpeg)
*   [![](/assets/image-cache/md-57.2b8a3154.jpg)](https://mindil.com.au/about/uploads/General%20Use/md-57.jpg)

## Mindil Today

Today, the Market is a vibrant hub with over 250 small businesses, employing more than 800 locals and contributing over $25 million annually to the Northern Territory economy. It’s renowned for its lively atmosphere featuring local and travelling musicians, street performers, dance groups, and buskers. Visitors can enjoy a sensory feast of sights, sounds, and tastes, all set against the backdrop of spectacular sunsets. Recognized as a national icon by the National Trust in 2000, the Market continues to attract visitors from around the world. We are Darwin's premier tourist attraction. And the locals love us too.

Come and experience the iconic Mindil Beach Sunset Market firsthand, and enjoy the unique blend of culture, cuisine and entertainment.

# Media

## About Handmade Canberra

What seems a lifetime ago now, back in 2008, Julie Nichols launched the very first Handmade Market. Canberra had some great markets, but none that really catered just to Australian Made designers only. Having very little money but a great business plan and vision, Julie launched the first Handmade Canberra market with a focus on local designers and just 35 stalls. Thousands of shoppers came, making Canberra’s new market, The Handmade Canberra Market an instant hit.

The market outgrew [Albert Hall](https://ouralberthall.com/), [The Yarralumla Woolshed](https://www.treasury.act.gov.au/venues-canberra/yarralumla-woolshed) and the [Kamberra Wine Company](https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=100067060457728), before finding a home at the [National Convention Centre,](https://nccc.com.au/) where crowds regularly numbered 15,000. For a while, the Handmade Shop in Canberra’s CBD provided Handmade with a permanent shopfront, but it closed with the regeneration of the area, and Julie’s focus has returned to the markets, whose home is now [Exhibition Park in Canberra](https://www.exhibitionparkincanberra.com.au/) (EPIC). 

Handmade Canberra celebrated it’s 15th birthday in 2023 and continues to grow and flourish, and now offers 260 stalls in two halls at the [Exhibition Park In Canberra](https://www.exhibitionparkincanberra.com.au/) EPIC, along with the central conference centre. Stalls offer Australian Made homewares, gifts, fashion, accessories and food, with a gourmet food hall full of street food vans, creating a feast for the senses and an unbeatable atmosphere of creativity and excitement.

The market regularly attracts over 20,000+ visitors from [Canberra](https://visitcanberra.com.au/) and further afield and has an extensive and growing following on social media.

With a passion for supporting [Australian Made](https://australianmade.com.au/) independent, small and creative businesses and connecting them to their target customers, the market has a nurturing relationship with its designers and producers who bring a high standard in quality, workmanship and sensational customer service, and an interactive relationship with its customers. Handmade Canberra is known nationally as a well-organised, supportive and friendly event, representing the best in Australian handmade design and produce. Many of our stallholders hold the Australian Made accreditation and proudly use the [Australia Made Logo](https://australianmade.com.au/for-business/using-the-logo/).

![Julie Nichols Handmade Canberra Media Contact](https://handmadecanberra.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/Untitled-design-17.png)

## Reach Our Media Team

Our media page hosts a collection of event images, press releases and resources for you to use.

We are always happy to talk to the media about our market, our online markets and our Australian Made designer directory. For interviews, quotes or more information about Handmade Canberra. Please contact:

Mindil Beach Sunset Market currently has over 150 stalls trading on Thursday & Sunday nights throughout the Darwin Dry Season.

New Food Stall Applications for the 2026 season are open from 30th November 2025 and close on January 31st 2026.

## Arts, Crafts & Services Stalls (A.C.S. Stalls)

A.C.S. Stall applications for the 2026 market season are open from January 2026. Please complete a Casual Stallholder Application form and attach all the relevant supporting documentation.

Community Group Stalls are encouraged to apply throughout the Market season as we will continue to accept applications for the duration the season.

![Hi, I'm Julie. The founder, owner and creative director of Handmade Canberra Market](https://handmadecanberra.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/Hi-Im-Julie-1024x1024.png)

What seems a lifetime ago now, back in 2008, Julie Nichols launched the very first Handmade Market. Canberra had some great markets, but none that really catered just to handmade designers. Having very little money but a great business plan and vision, Julie launched the first market with a focus on local designers and just 35 stalls. Thousands of shoppers came, making the Handmade Market an instant hit.

The market outgrew [Albert Hall](https://ouralberthall.com/), [The Yarralumla Woolshed](https://www.treasury.act.gov.au/venues-canberra/yarralumla-woolshed) and the [Kamberra Wine Company,](https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=100067060457728) before finding a home at the [National Convention Centre,](https://nccc.com.au/) where crowds regularly numbered 15,000. For a while, the Handmade Shop in Canberra’s CBD provided Handmade with a permanent shopfront, but it closed with the regeneration of the area, and Julie’s focus has returned to the markets, whose home is now [Exhibition Park in Canberra](https://www.exhibitionparkincanberra.com.au/) (EPIC).

Handmade Canberra celebrated it’s 15th birthday in 2023 and continues to grow and flourish, and now offers 260 stalls in two halls at [Exhibition Park In Canberra](https://www.exhibitionparkincanberra.com.au/) (EPIC), along with the central conference centre. Stalls offer Australian Made homewares, gifts, fashion, accessories and food, with a gourmet food hall full of street food vans, creating a feast for the senses and an unbeatable atmosphere of creativity and excitement.

The market regularly attracts over 20,000 visitors from [Canberra](https://visitcanberra.com.au/) and further afield and has an extensive and growing following on social media.

With a passion for supporting Australian Hand Made independent, small and creative businesses and connecting them to their target customers, the market has a nurturing relationship with its designers and producers who bring a high standard in quality, workmanship and sensational customer service, and an interactive relationship with its customers. Handmade Canberra is known nationally as a well-organised, supportive and friendly event, representing the best in Australian handmade design and produce.

## Our team

The Handmade team is a dynamic mix with expertise in sales, marketing, design, administration, technology, social media and event management – a fantastic combination!

![](https://handmadecanberra.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Julie-Nichols.jpg)

**Julie – Founder Handmade Canberra**

[Julie Nichols](https://www.linkedin.com/in/handmadecanberra/) is the founder, owner and creative director of Handmade. With a background in the RAAF and in hospitality, Julie ran a small millinery business before seeing a gap in Canberra markets for well-run, high quality, Australian made markets. Julie’s innate understanding of how to curate product types to create a buzzing event are combined with her irreverent sense of humour and telling it like it is. Something both designers and customers find refreshing and positive.

![](https://handmadecanberra.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Michelle-Boehm.jpg)

**Michelle**

Michelle Boehm was a stallholder with Handmade for 7 years selling jewellery under the brand [Bok Bok B’Gerk](https://www.instagram.com/bok_bok_bgerk/). With a degree in Computing, her pre-stallholder life included roles as a Business Analyst and Project Manager and her specialty is re-engineering business processes. Michelle currently looks after our website, and streamlines our team processes.

![](https://handmadecanberra.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Alison-Loeliger.jpg)

**Alison**

![](https://handmadecanberra.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Ella-Nichols.jpg)

**Ella**

Alison is the administrative powerhouse behind the market, ensuring seamless coordination between stallholders and our customers. With a sharp eye for detail and a passion for community connection, she plays a key role in the planning and logistics behind the market, helping to create a vibrant, smooth-running market experience every time.

Ella Nichols is our go-to for all things marketing and social media. If you’ve ever spoken to us online you can almost guarantee it was Ella behind the keyboard. Ella also plays a key role in shaping our brand voice and creating content that connects our community. With a degree in Events and Tourism Management, market organising is surely in her future, some might say it’s in her blood.

## Our mission

![Handmade Canberra mission](https://handmadecanberra.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/MISSION-STATEMENT-1024x171.jpg)

### Australian Made Campaign Retail Supporter

![Australian Made Logo](https://handmadecanberra.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/ausmade_logo_aboutus-300x300.png)

We have joined the [Australian Made Campaign](https://australianmade.com.au/) (AMC) as a Retail Supporter, forming a partnership to support and promote handcrafted Australian-made products. We are certified on the basis that our market continues selling all Australian made goods and have one of the largest Australian Made Product Lists in the country through our [Directory](https://handmadecanberra.com.au/directory/).

We are thrilled to be in partnership with a well trusted and widely recognised brand such as Australian Made. We support authentic Australian makers on a national level and being an Australian-made market is what sets us apart from other events.

Australian Made aligns perfectly with Handmade Canberra’s business ethos. We couldn’t be happier to become a Retail Supporter and communicate our Australian-made credentials to our customers. The Australian Made logo is Australia’s most trusted, recognised and widely used country of origin symbol, and is underpinned by a third-party accreditation system which ensures products that carry the logo are certified as ‘Authentically Australian’.

## Handmade Canberra’s Awards

Handmade Canberra is a small business with big ideas and a great philosophy: know your target audience, support local designers and producers by bringing crowds of enthusiastic shoppers and provide amazing customer service. As a result, we have won several awards over the last few years.

# Before you start

When filling out your registration form, you will be asked to provide the following information. Please make sure you have them at hand before starting. This form is best completed on a desktop or laptop rather than a mobile device. If you have any issues, please change your browser and make sure your photos are the correct size.

*   Your **business name** as it will appear in the directory and our marketing
*   Your **full name**
*   Your **contact telephone number**
*   A **postal address**
*   **Your business email** (this will become your username)
*   A memorable **password**
*   Your **Indigenous Country** This is the Indigenous name for the land where your business is located. Refer to the [AISTSIS](https://aiatsis.gov.au/explore/map-indigenous-australia) map
*   Your **website, Facebook and/or Instagram addresses** (we need at least one of these)
*   Your **Australian Business Number (ABN)** if you have one, and details of whether you are **registered for GST**
*   Up to **two designated categories** for your products
*   An **explanation of your brand in 100 words** or fewer
*   A **summary of your business in 5-7 words**
*   Details of **who makes your product and the prices**
*   Confirmation that you can get **Public Liability Insurance** in the business name you have registered with us ($10mil PLI is compulsory to sell at a market)
*   Up to five **professional product shots** that will appear in our directory and represent your business. These images **MUST** be cropped to a square of 800px by 800px and a maximum file size of 2Mb. If you are unsure how to do this, try using the [PicResize Website](http://www.picresize.com/)
*   If you are selling hot food we **cannot take a food van** of any sort as they are too big for our indoor venue.

Your registration is not complete until you receive the **confirmation page.** All steps must be completed at the same time and you are not able to partially complete a registration to be finished later. It is important that you have all the information you are going to need ready to go before proceeding to the next step. Good luck.

CONNECT, CREATE AND CELEBRATE AT AUSTRALIA'S PREMIER FOLK AND CULTURAL EVENT

Welcome to the National Folk Festival, where we honour the rich tapestry of music, dance, poetry, circus, and cultural arts in Australia. Our Festival is a vibrant celebration of diverse folk traditions from around the world, featuring top-quality performances, workshops, and dances, along with immersive experiences that unite artists and audiences. Join us each year on Ngunnawal country in Canberra to experience a welcoming space where everyone can participate in their own way. Together, we ensure that folk and culture will thrive and inspire generations to come.

EXCELLENCE

Showcasing the highest quality in performances, workshops, and community engagements.

INCLUSION

Creating a space where all artists and audiences feel welcome, celebrating a diversity of cultures, backgrounds and stories.

INTEGRATION

Giving opportunity for collaboration between artists and audiences, where anyone can engage, contribute, and co-create.

SUSTAINABILITY

Nurturing a sustainable cultural landscape where folk traditions thrive, evolve, and inspire future generations.

EMPOWERING AUDIENCES, ARTISTS, AND COMMUNITIES TO CELEBRATE AND CREATE TOGETHER

#### ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF COUNTRY

The National Folk Festival acknowledges the Traditional Owners of Country throughout Australia and recognises their continuing connection to land, waters and community. We pay our respects to them and their cultures; and to Elders past and present.  
  
We especially acknowledge the Traditional Custodians of the Lands upon which our annual festival takes place, the Ngunnawal Peoples, their Elders past, present and emerging and their continuing culture and the contribution they make to the life of our region and we recognise any other people or families with connection to the lands of the ACT and region.

# FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

We have compiled a list of answers to commonly asked questions below. We love curious folks, so if you need further information or you would like to ask something else, please use the contact form below or email [info@folkfestival.org.au](mailto:info@folkfestival.org.au)​​

## EMERGENCY AND GENERAL INFORMATIO

### Where is the National Folk Festival held?

The National Folk Festival is located at EPIC (Exhibition Park in Canberra). 10 Flemington Rd. Mitchell ACT 2602

### First Aid

For all major medical emergencies call 000. First Aid services are available near the Flemington Road Ticket Office, in Central Park. All security staff are able to render basic first aid assistance and are available 24 hours.

### Information or Assistance at the Festival

For non-urgent issues, the Festival Office operates between the following hours: Thursday - Sunday: 8am - 10pm Monday: 8am - 8pm For urgent issues, a 24-hour Emergency Control Centre (ECC) operates on site. They assist with emergencies, medical or otherwise, and can coordinate with Security for issues such as offensive behaviour, underage drinking, theft, vandalism, excessive noise in the campgrounds, safety concerns, and unauthorised entry to site.

### Lost Children

Please report all lost children to the Festival Office, Festival Security or Emergency Control Centre. All children at the Festival have a parent or guardian phone number logged against their wristband.

### Conditions of Entry

*   Footwear must be worn at all times whilst in the Festival Entertainment Zone.
    

  

*   No animals are permitted on the Festival site (including the camping areas), with the exception of registered Assistance Animals. All Assistance Animals must be registered with the Festival prior to arrival. For more information on Assistance Animals at the Festival, please visit our Accessibility page.
    

  

*   Offensive behaviour, theft and vandalism will result in removal from the Festival site. In this situation, no refund will be given, per the Festival’s Refund Policy.
    

  

*   The Festival Entertainment Zone is a licensed venue. BYO alcohol is not permitted. Police will be notified of all instances of underage drinking or secondary supply of alcohol. Offenders will have their wristband removed and be escorted off the Festival site.
    

  

*   There is strictly no glass permitted within the Festival Entertainment Zone.
    

  

*   No wristband, no entry. Festival wristbands must be worn at all times on the Festival site.
    

  

*   Discretionary bag checks may be conducted. All patrons are responsible for their own wristbands/tickets.
    

  

*   Lost, damaged or misplaced wristbands will not be reissued unless agreed by the Festival Director.
    

  

*   All vehicles on the Festival site must display a valid vehicle pass.
    

  

### Licensed Bars

Festival Bars are conducted according to ACT licensing regulations. It is an offence to sell or supply liquor to any person who is intoxicated or under 18 years of age. Underage drinking and secondary supply of alcohol to minors will not be tolerated and offenders will be referred to the police. There is no BYO alcohol permitted in the Festival Entertainment Zone. No glass bottles, including water bottles are permitted in the Festival Entertainment Zone. All glass will be confiscated by Security personnel. No alcohol is permitted to leave the Festival Entertainment Zone.

### Smoking

The Festival Entertainment Zone is smoke-free, including e-cigarettes and vapes. Smokers are asked to smoke or vape within one of our unlicensed, designated outdoor smoking areas.

### Bag Checks and Prohibited Items

All patrons carrying bags will be required to present their bags for inspection when entering the Festival Entertainment Zone.

Prohibited items include:

*   Glass (Including food containers and bottles)
    
*   Knives and weapons
    
*   Alcohol and illicit substances
    
*   Fire-twirling equipment, sparklers and flares
    

These items are prohibited for the safety of all staff, volunteers and attendees.

### Ticket Office Locations

1.  **Flemington Road Ticket Office, Gate 2** - Open to members of the public arriving by bus, tram or being dropped off in private vehicles or taxis. Disability and VIP Parking only at this Gate. This ticket office only opens during the festival (Thursday 5pm onwards)
    
2.  **Old Well Station Road Ticket Office, Gate 7** - At the northern end of EPIC, Gate 7. Most Season and Day Ticket holders will use this Gate. Season + Camping ticket holders must use this entrance for initial entry. This ticket office opens from Monday pre-festival for our pre-festival campers and volunteers.
    

### On Foot

Depending on where you’re located, you may like to walk to the Festival. The Flemington Road Entry is the easiest to access on foot, please note this entry only opens at 5pm on Thursday.

You can use the journey planner at [https://www.transport.act.gov.au/getting-around/journey-planner](https://www.transport.act.gov.au/getting-around/journey-planner) to plan your route. Make sure you select ‘Walking’ under the ‘Options’ tab.

## FESTIVAL SERVICES

### Bike Minding

Pedal Power operates a bike minding area with bike racks near the Flemington Road entry (Gate 2). We recommend Festival attendees bring their own bike locks for added security. The Festival takes no responsibility for lost, stolen or damaged bikes.

### Cloakroom

*   Think of it as your festival’s personal concierge for coats and treasures. Whether you’ve brought along a cosy jacket (even though we’ve ordered sunshine for the day!) or scored something fabulous from one of our stalls, we’ve got you covered - literally.
    
*   The Festival takes no responsibility for lost, damaged or stolen property.
    
*   Located in the Quokka Building.
    

### Festival Office

The Festival Office is located in the Entertainment Zone. It’s a hub of on-site information for patrons, performers and volunteers, so if there’s something you need help with or would like to know, please pay a visit and our friendly team will assist you.

It is co-located with our Lost & Found office in the 'Orana Bar' building opposite Gate 2.

### Festival Shop

The best place to get all your National Folk Festival merchandise is the Festival Shop, which is located in the Quokka building.

### Festival Transport

The Festival runs a shuttlebus on site for the convenience of our patrons. The bus runs from Gate 7 (public parking area) to the Quokka and Fitzroy Gates during the festival (Thursday to Monday).

### Instrument Lock Up

*   The Instrument Lock Up is the best place for instrument storage on site, catering to performers and patrons alike. If you have an instrument you’d like to play at the Festival, and need somewhere secure and dry to store it, feel free to pop in and visit our Instrument Lock Up Team, located in the Conference Centre.
    
*   While every effort is made to ensure all instruments are kept safe and secure at the Festival, the National Folk Festival takes no responsibility for lost, damaged or stolen instruments. Those who choose to use the Instrument Lock Up facility do so at their own risk.
    

### Lost & Found Property

*   If you’ve lost an item at the Festival, or found something and want to hand it in, Lost & Found Property is the place to go.
    
*   You can also view found items in real time on our website.
    
*   The Festival takes no responsibility for lost, damaged or stolen property.
    
*   It is co-located with our Festival Office in the 'Orana Bar' building opposite Gate 2.

A collision of art + performance + music | Junction Arts Festival returns to Launceston from 17–20 September 2026.

[ABOUT JUNCTION](https://junctionartsfestival.com.au/about-us/)

## NEED HELP PLANNING YOUR JUNCTION ITINERARY?

We know, there’s a LOT to see and do over the two weekends at Junction this year. So we thought we’d make it easier for you! We’ve developed a quiz that after 5 quick questions will curate an itinerary tailored to the types of experiences you prefer.

Whether you enjoy more community and cultural forward events, or you like to discover something entirely new… maybe you prefer the festival experience that allows you to engage and grow as a person. 

Click the link below to fill out about the  questions and get your very own personalised Junction Arts Festival guide!

[TAKE THE QUIZ](https://bit.ly/yourjunctionguide)

## 15 YEARS.

## SOMETHING NEW.

## TWO WEEKENDS.

###### 12-14th of September 2025 & 18-21st of September 2025

###### WEEKEND ONE: ANNIVERSARY CELEBRATION

12-14th September 2025  
Join us as we celebrate 15 years of Junction with special community events, reflective programming, and moments that honour the incredible journey we’ve shared together.

###### WEEKEND TWO: JUNCTION ARTS FESTIVAL 

18-21st September 2025  
Experience Junction’s signature weekend with bold contemporary art installations, live music, immersive performances, and those unforgettable late-night events you love.

###### WHY TWO WEEKENDS?

This special format lets us properly celebrate our 15-year milestone while delivering the cutting-edge contemporary arts programming Junction is known for.

Whether you want to reflect on our journey together or dive into bold new experiences (or both!), there’s something magical waiting for you.

Mark your calendars. Share the news. Get ready for our biggest celebration yet.

## A COLLISION OF

*   ART

*   PERFORMANCE

*   MUSIC

Junction Arts Festival returns for its 15th year from the 18th-21st September 2025 with a captivating springtime celebration, inviting you to embrace the season’s renewal and revel in Tasmania’s vibrant awakening. As nature bursts into bloom, Junction transforms Launceston into a mesmerising intersection of Tasmanian (lutruwita) art, music, and performance, creating a kaleidoscopic celebration that captures the magic of the spring equinox.

With a diverse program of free and ticketed events, Junction offers something for everyone to discover. From daytime activities to evening entertainment, the city comes alive with the best of Tasmania’s creative talent. While you immerse yourself in the arts, savour the island’s renowned culinary delights, from gourmet local food to distinctive Tasmanian wines, spirits, and craft brews as you celebrate into the night.

# STALLHOLDER APPLICATIONS

#### The Festival has a long tradition of fantastic stalls that folks love to browse and be nourished by, and are an essential part of creating the village atmosphere this long running event is renowned for.  
 

#### First round stallholder applications have now closed. Late applications are still welcome.

#### ​

#### ​

#### We are currently assessing applications and making first round site offers.​​​​

#### Applications received after the first round closing date will be considered once initial offers have been accepted and the remaining available sites have been identified. Further offers will be made to fill any vacancies and ensuring a diverse and balance selection of stalls on site.

#### ​

*   #### Click here to see the 2027 Stallholder [Terms and Conditions.](https://www.folkfestival.org.au/_files/ugd/c9062b_9f1063b8da584a77900f341ccecf3290.pdf)​
    
*   #### For further detail please read the 2027 [Stallholder application supporting information.](https://www.folkfestival.org.au/_files/ugd/c9062b_c72078f9f08f4e23afed751695b19601.pdf)
    
*   #### ​As the National Folk Festival is committed to becoming a No Waste Festival, we require a description of any packaging you intend to use prior to the event. There is no glass allowed on site and no single use plastics. Click on the following [Waste and Recycling info for stallholders document](https://www.folkfestival.org.au/_files/ugd/c9062b_2a307eadb2f748bd986725f3c992de0d.pdf) for guidance. Any updates will be shared with successful applicants.
    

#### ​For more information, please read through our Stallholder FAQs at the bottom of the page

#### To contact the Stalls Team please email [stallholders@folkfestival.org.au](mailto:stallholders@folkfestival.org.au)

#### ​

Join our mailing list and follow the Festival on social media to stay up to date with all the latest information!
