## Stallholder FAQs

### Solving issues on site

The Stalls teams are on hand to help with minor issues.

  

Any issues that require following up with a contractor must be brought to the attention of Festival staff via email.

### Trading dates for stallholders

Event Start: Thursday 25 March, 5pm

Event End: Monday 29 March 2027, 11.59pm (one bar will be open until 4am Tuesday 30 March)

### What we look for in selecting stalls

In selecting stalls, we aim to offer a diverse range of food, beverages, and both Australian-made and general products. We take care, wherever possible, to avoid having multiple stalls selling the same items (with the exception of coffee), to give each stallholder the best opportunity for strong sales. For this reason, it is important that applicants clearly outline the products they intend to sell during the application process.

  

As our festival is volunteer-run and our artists are essential to its success, preference is given to stallholders who offer discounts to both volunteers and artists.

  

Stall presentation also plays an important role in our decision-making. We recognise that patrons are drawn to stalls that are visually appealing and accessible, and many prefer supporting small businesses over larger companies.

### Successful applications

Applications will be assessed, and first round offers will be made by Friday, October 16. Unsuccessful applicants will be informed by Friday, October 23.

  

Those applicants that are being considered for a second-round offer that applied by September 13 will be informed by Friday October 30.

### Trucks and Trailers

There are limited suitable spaces for Food trucks on our site. Most trucks will be placed between the Coorong and Fitzroy buildings, with one or two allocated near the Session Bar for late night trading. No trucks/trailers will be placed in the Coorong or Budawang forecourts in 2027.

### Site Position

We understand that all stallholders want their preferred or the best possible position however unfortunately that is not possible for every applicant. We aim to curate precincts that not only consider power and water needs but also consider the patron flow onsite.

### Site dimensions

Boundaries of the Stallholder’s stall site will be marked out on the event grounds.

  

Stallholders must operate within their allocated stall footprint, including all plant and equipment.

  

As site dimensions determine position, it is important that measurements include all space required for both front and back of house. For trucks and vans this includes tow bars, door openings, and hitches. Our map is quite precise and if these are not included you may find you cannot fit in the site allocated on arrival, at which point adjustments can NOT be made and you may not be able to setup your stall. If we can accommodate changes you will be charged extra accordingly before you setup.

### Contracts

Contracts will be issued upon making an offer. Please check ALL details in the contract are correct and email [stallholders@folkfestival.org.au](mailto:stallholders@folkfestival.org.au) to request any amendments prior to signing.

### Fees and allocated staff passes

See the table below for fees and staff pass allocations. Fees are determined by stall category and trading site sizes. All fees listed below include GST.

  

**Note for larger sites:** There are limited suitable spaces for Food trucks on our site. Most trucks will be placed between the Coorong and Fitzroy buildings, with one or two allocated near the Session Bar for late night trading. No trucks will be placed in the Coorong or Budawang forecourts in 2027.

### Bump in and Bump out

Stallholders must adhere to specified load-in times and rules. These can be found in the Terms and Conditions. Prior to the Festival stallholders are required to book a time with the Stall management team for their arrival for Bump In.

  

All cool rooms must be delivered and positioned on-site by 12pm Wednesday 24 March.

### Staff passes

Staff passes are issued to the primary stall applicant. Each pass permits access to the Entertainment Zone for the duration of the festival (including bump in, bump out, restocking and festival times).

  

Extra passes may be purchased and must be ordered in advance.

  

Staff passes can be passed on to other staff members at shift changeover times.

  

A festival staff pass permits camping in the general camping areas or the designated Stallholders camping area. Note: Stallholder reserved sites, and powered sites must be reserved at an additional fee.

### Electrical

Power onsite is limited and must be requested in the application process as it is taken into consideration when choosing and mapping stalls.

*   Each site fee includes 1 x 15-amp outlet.
    
*   Any additional 15-amp outlets must be ordered and paid for by the Stallholder prior to the event.
    
*   Successful Stallholders must provide a list of all equipment and amp usage.
    
*   Orders for additional power must be placed in advance, as **EXTRA POWER CANNOT BE ORDERED ON SITE.**
    

### Insurance and registrations

Stallholders are required to have the following insurance policies, valid for the duration spent on site.

  

Public Liability - Required for all stallholders - Value of $20 million

Product Liability - Required for Food Stallholders - Value of $10 million

Property Damage - Recommended for all Stallholders - Value of $10 million

  

The National Folk Festival must be listed as an interested party. Copies of these policies must be submitted with your application.

  

  

### Food businesses extra details

Product liability is required for all food stallholders

  

Stallholders who ARE currently registered with the Health Protection Service (ACT) must always display their current food business registration certificate (or a copy) in their stall during the event and supply a copy to the NFF.

*   A food business is exempt from registration if the business:
    
    *   Handles or sells food in or from a food transport vehicle (i.e. Food van) that is registered in another state or territory
        

Only sells pre-packed non-potentially hazardous food (e.g. Muesli bars)

*   Food Stallholders who ARE NOT currently registered with the Health Protection Service (ACT) and are not exempt from registering, need to complete a Declared Event Food Business Registration at least 28 days prior to the event. The National Folk Festival is classed as a Declared Event.
    

  

[Selling food at an event - ACT Government](https://www.act.gov.au/health/businesses/licences-permits-and-registration/food-businesses-and-events-registration/selling-food-at-an-event)

  

Temperature logs must be kept for all potentially hazardous food prepared prior to, and during, the event. Regular temperature checks during transport, storage and display of food must be done and recorded in the log.

  

Food stalls must have the following facilities, and must be indicated on the site plan:

*   Separate sinks for food prep and hand washing.
    
*   Refrigeration (some exceptions for low risk/non-perishable foods).
    
*   A floor of impervious (solid) material such as sealed boards, groundsheets, rubber matting or similar. This covering will ensure that the surface is easy to clean at the end of the event.
    

  

[Food safety for food stalls at declared events - ACT Government](https://www.act.gov.au/health/businesses/food-safety-for-businesses/food-safety-for-market-stalls/food-safety-for-food-stalls-at-declared-events)

### Waste

The National Folk Festival strives to be a no waste and is proud to have received awards in the past. The ACT government has strict guidelines on no single use plastics. We ask all stallholders to adhere to the guidelines in our waste guide.

### Camping

General Camping is included in your fee and allows you to camp in the Stables, Acton Arena, or Oval general campgrounds.

  

_The Stallholder Camp zone is between the Fitzroy building and McDonalds._

  

Reserved sites in the Stallholder Camp Zone are 6m x 8m. Discuss with staff prior if you need a larger site

  

**Please note** there is no option to camp or park your car at or near your stall in the entertainment zone.

  

Reserved (powered) camping is also available in Stables (marked out sites), Bicentennial and Cotter campgrounds. These must be booked through our ticketing system, not via the stall application. These are selling fast and are limited.

## FESTIVAL STAFF TEAM

#### Festival Director: Anne Denzer

Anne brings exceptional leadership and event management skills to her role, along with her knack for efficient systems and cheeky sense of humour. 

#### Volunteer & Business Administration: Demelza Crook

Demelza brings extensive experience as a longterm Festival volunteer to her role co-ordinating the wonderful folks who all pitch in to bring the Festival to life each year.

#### Artistic Directors: Holly Downes & Chris Stone  
 

Holly and Chris bring extensive experience as musicians, educators, artistic directors and community arts leaders. Both have attended, performed and volunteered at the National Folk Festival since their teenage years, and share a deep connection to the Festival community and the broader folk scene in Australia.​

​

Chris and Holly began the Artistic Director role in 2023 alongside Michael Sollis (1985 - 2026). Together they shaped the 2024–2026 Festivals and developed the artistic vision that continues to guide the Festival today. Michael’s creativity, leadership and commitment to community remain an important part of the Festival’s recent history, and his influence continues to be reflected in the Festival’s future through the ongoing work of Holly and Chris.

![NFF 2026 Team Photo.jpg](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/681c4f_be48fb0d4aa14f9b96da654355eb82fb~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_443,h_443,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/NFF%202026%20Team%20Photo.jpg)

## VOLUNTEER TEAM

The National Folk Festival is proud to include over 850 volunteers each year as part of the team responsible for delivering the festival.

[Read More](https://www.folkfestival.org.au/volunteer-teams)

## FESTIVAL BOARD MEMBERS (VOLUNTEERS)

#### President - Emma Cottam

Appointed to the Board: October 2023. Emma is a teacher and student hot air balloon pilot who moved to Canberra in 2020 from Western Australia. She has been attending folk festivals for many years and brings with her a network of connections from Australia and overseas as well as a deep love and connection to music of all kinds. Emma has a storied history with FolkWorld Inc., the organisation that delivers the Fairbridge Festival. Starting as a volunteer, across her time at the festival Emma ran social media, developed community art projects for children with the local First Nation group the Binjarep people, and was eventually the youngest board member in the organisation's history, where she remained on the board for six years. Emma plays the mandolin and the banjo and enjoys spending her time in the Session Bar, particularly when there is an Old Time Session happening!

#### Vice President - John Nicholls

Appointed to the Board: October 2022. John has been involved with festivals and events for over 15 years and has been volunteering with the venue management team at the NFF since 2005. Previous experience also includes Floriade, the Multicultural festival, Reconciliation Day, and other Canberra based events. John is the ICT Director at the National Aboriginal Community Controlled Health Organisation and manages the strategic direction and operational delivery for IT services. John has extensive experience in corporate governance as a Director for the Australian Higher Education Associations Pty Ltd Board and as a business owner at Can Speak Canberra Speech Pathology.

#### Director – David Gilks

Appointed to the Board: October 2018. LLB (ANU), BEc (ANU) David is a manager with experience in strategic policy and operational delivery roles both in Australia and overseas. He is a folk musician, dancer and dance caller. He has participated in the Festival as a patron, volunteer and performer and was the Festival's Ticket Office Area Coordinator for four festivals (2009-12).

#### Director – Roy Volmari

Appointed to the Board: July 2024. Roy is a seasoned finance professional providing financial services to the private and public sectors for nearly 40 years before retiring in 2021. During his working career, Roy has been a Director and Company Secretary for numerous mid-sized companies, and has extensive experience in corporate governance, financial management, HR, and IT. Roy has had past experience in the delivery of events such as horticulture field days, and art shows. Roy has a love for music of all kinds and is looking forward to contributing to the success of The National Folk Festival.

#### Director – Hannah Pelka-Caven

Appointed to the Board: December 2024. B.Mus (UniMelb), Dip.Lang (UniMelb), J.D (UniMelb) Hannah is an experienced employment and industrial relations lawyer, and has advised and represented workers and employers in the Australian cultural arts and live performance sector for many years. Hannah is also an award-winning folk singer and composer, who has performed at folk festivals (including at the National Folk Festival) for over a decade, with her band The Raglins. After attending her first Nash as part of the Folk Alliance Youth Awards, she fell in love with the festival and is keen to ensure that the festival thrives. Hannah also serves on two other arts boards - Happy Haps Productions and Music Theatre Workshop.

#### Director – Zev Aviv

Appointed to the Board: December 2024. Zev Aviv is a personal trainer, interdisciplinary artist, history tour guide and podcaster. They grew up at the National Folk Festival and have been attending for around 35 years where they have been a festival MC, producer and forklift driver. As well as having board experience in the arts, they have produced events, managed artists and stayed up to see the sunrise in the session bar on multiple occasions. They are deeply committed to the festival, its teams and its patrons

#### Director – Stephen Fischer

Appointed to the Board: June 2025. Stephen has recently retired from his role as a consultant, where over the past 18 years he worked with a range of government departments to use technology solutions to improve business outcomes. His areas of expertise include governance, strategic planning, business analysis and ICT systems administration. Outside of work, he has served as treasurer for Canberra Youth Theatre and Canberra Rep Theatre, as well as multiple roles on other not-for-profit boards over the past 20 years.

#### Director – Fred Smith

Appointed to Board: October 2025. Fred Smith OAM, LLB (ANU), BEc (ANU) Songwriter, diplomat, author and raconteur, has had a long and happy association with the National Folk Festival. He has performed at over a dozen Nashes wearing a range of outfits including a seersucker suit, a dinner suit and a safari suit. He was a two times winner of the NFSA National Folk Recording Award, AFMA Solo Artist of the Year in 2022, ACT Artist of the Year in 2023, and more recently awarded and Order of Australia for services to (an improbable combination of) music and foreign affairs. He works at the foreign affairs department when he’s not playing music.

#### Director – Kirsty Greenwood

Appointed to the Board: October 2025. Kirsty Greenwood has been part of the folk festival community since she first discovered it at age 16, and has attended nearly every National Folk Festival in Australia since 1993. A madly keen dancer, you will most often find her at ceilidhs or contras, but she is also a caller, harpist, singer, a proud life member of the Melbourne Scottish Fiddle Club, and a passionate advocate for folk music and dance. Professionally, Kirsty has over 30 years’ experience leading not-for-profits, with expertise in governance, finance, grant writing, and event management. She gladly brings her love of folk and decades of community and leadership experience to the National Folk Festival Board.

#### Director – Ben Drysdale

Appointed to the Board: October 2025. Ben has been attending the National Folk Festival since 1999 and has contributed in many capacities over the years — as a street performer, volunteer MC, and billed act. A songwriter, contemporary folk artist, and educator, Ben has been active in the Australian music and arts community for over two decades. He brings extensive leadership experience as the Founding Co-CEO of Rebus Theatre, where he championed inclusive and socially engaged arts practice, and governance experience through his previous tenure on the Childers Group Committee. Ben is also the founder of Songwriting for Non-Songwriters, helping everyday people discover creative expression through music. Ben is passionate about creativity as a tool for connection, inclusion, and storytelling, and is dedicated to strengthening community through the folk arts.

#### Interested in Joining the Festival Board?

​

The National Folk Festival Board periodically seeks new members to help guide the future of the Festival. We look for people who love the Festival and want to contribute to its long-term success. Previous board experience is welcome but not essential.  
 

We’re especially keen to hear from people with:  
 

*   Governance experience
    
*   Financial or legal expertise
    
*   Funding or grant writing knowledge
    
*   Strong ties to the folk community  
     
    

​If you would be interested in being a member of the board in the future you can send a one-page pitch and your CV to [president@folkfestival.org.au](mailto:president@folkfestival.org.au?subject=National%20Folk%20Festival%20Board%20EOI), please use the subject line "Board EOI".

# VOLUNTEERS

The National Folk Festival engages 850+ volunteers each year to deliver an amazing Festival. It's a big job and a fun one, where you can gain valuable industry experience, meet new people, and learn new skills. We are always looking for enthusiastic, friendly, and motivated people to support one of Australia's key cultural folk events.

​As a thank you for your generous contribution, all volunteers get a Season + Camping ticket for the National Folk Festival and an invitation to the Volunteer Party plus other little perks.​

[​](https://nff.festivalpro.com/form/D64A37235DDFF2656621/55)​​​

​For more information, please read through our FAQs at the bottom of this page and check out the teams below.

​

Still got questions, please email [volunteers@folkfestival.org.au](mailto:volunteers@folkfestival.org.au). ​

​

Applications to volunteer for the 2027 Festival will open on October 1 for returning volunteers.

A link to the application form will be sent to returning volunteers via email.

​

Applications for new volunteers will be available on this webpage from November 1. ​​​​​

​

If you have any questions, please contact [info@folkfestival.org.au](mailto:info@folkfestival.org.au).

![NFF2024 - Scrumpy - Vollies - Group shot - Brian Rosenberg 0B2A6079-Panoa.jpg](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/681c4f_13933ca65afb4d89b799091808e502b1~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_147,h_55,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_avif,quality_auto/681c4f_13933ca65afb4d89b799091808e502b1~mv2.jpg)

## FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

### What does volunteering at the National Folk Festival involve?

Volunteers do everything that needs to be done to make the Festival happen.

  

They check in performers, sell tickets and merchandise, check wristbands, serve drinks, answer phones, manage stages, set up venues – you get the picture.  The fun-loving, community-minded individuals who decide to get involved and become part of the Festival community give our event its heart and soul.

  

With 33 teams to choose from we can find something for everyone, no matter your experience or ability.

### How do I apply to volunteer?

Applications to volunteer for the National Folk Festival are done via the online platform FestivalPro. Applications will open to new volunteers and will be available on our website from November 1. Returning volunteers will be sent a link to the application via email on October 1. [](http://1.as/)[As](http://1.as/) we prepare for 2027 if you wish to volunteer in the office please email [volunteers@folkfestival.org.au](mailto:volunteers@folkfestival.org.au)

### Who can volunteer?

Volunteering is open to anyone aged over 16.

The festival aims to be inclusive and welcoming to its community and has volunteer positions suitable for a wide range of abilities and interests, although these will fill as we get close to Easter.

### What do I get for volunteering?

Adult volunteers who complete 20 hours at the festival, or 30 hours at pre and post-Festival pack down, or more than 40 hours over the rest of the year receive:

*   A Season pass to the festival including Camping and Parking
    
*   An invitation to the volunteer party on the final night at the festival including two complimentary drinks.
    
*   Access to a dedicated Volunteer center with charging facilities, toast, fruit, hot beverages, boiling water, and microwaves.
    
*   Youth Volunteers from 16 years old are welcome with parent/guardian permission. Reduced hours can be arranged for Youth Volunteers.
    

### Why volunteer?

You are not just attending the Festival, you are part of the family making it happen. The friendships, the camaraderie, the sense of community, and the shared laughter that come out of working at the Festival, more than compensate for giving up a few hours out of each day. There are plenty of opportunities to learn new skills or pass on knowledge.

  

Some reasons to volunteer during the festival:

*   It’s fun!
    
*   Try something new, different.
    
*   It’s a manageable commitment.
    
*   Enjoy the social event, meet new people, and make new friends.
    
*   Personal and professional development and fulfillment
    
*   Learn and develop new skills.
    
*   Use existing skills in new and exciting ways.
    
*   Have an active role in a wonderful event.
    
*   Earn a season ticket including camping
    
*   Be recognised as a doer.
    
*   Become a part of the folkie family.
    

### Things to consider before you volunteer

When you volunteer for the National Folk Festival, you are agreeing to work a minimum of 20 hours over the Festival period. Please consider the following before you volunteer:

*   Are you able to commit to a minimum of 20 hours of volunteer work?
    
*   Are you available for the entire Festival period?
    
*   What type of volunteer work are you interested in?
    
*   Do you have any specific skills that you can bring to the festival?
    
*   Are you willing and able to work late nights?
    
*   What do you want to gain from the experience?
    
*   Do you have any physical limitations?
    

  

Consider all the above and the team description when you are selecting your team preferences.

### When will I have to work and for how many hours?

If volunteering during the Festival you will be rostered between Thursday, 25 March, and Monday, 29 March. Pre-festival teams work from Friday, March 19 or Saturday March 20 until the Festival opens on 25 March. The Post Festival cleanup team works from 29 March (Monday of Festival) to Thursday 1st April. Please see the team descriptions above for more information about when the teams operate.

  

Those volunteers working during the Festival are required to do 20 hours and in return will receive a Full Season camping ticket. Pre and Post Festival teams are required to work at least 30 hours, and year-round volunteers are required to work 40 hours.

Volunteers working in the Post Festival clean-up team may be required to purchase their tickets. We will refund the ticket the week after the festival once volunteer hours have been completed.

We aim to have some volunteers that work in both the setup phase and pack down for continuity (30 hours total).

### Which team should I choose?

With a wide range of volunteer teams available, there's something to suit a variety of interests, skills, physical abilities, and availability. We recommend reading the team descriptions carefully and considering:

*   What type of work you enjoy
    
*   Any physical requirements of the role
    
*   Whether you're available before, during, or after the Festival
    
*   Any specific skills, experience, or licences that may be required  
    

If you're still unsure which team would be the best fit, please email [**volunteers@folkfestival.org.au**](mailto:volunteers@folkfestival.org.au). Our Volunteer Manager will be happy to provide more information and help you find a role that suits you.

### Volunteer in the office throughout the year

Volunteers are needed all year round in the festival office. Jobs include answering ticketing and performer enquiries, helping with filing, and archiving of photo’s, auditing and sorting equipment, signage, and storage, and much more.

  

Please email [volunteers@folkfestival.org.au](mailto:volunteers@folkfestival.org.au) for further information.

### If I buy a ticket and then decide to volunteer will I get a refund?

Yes. If you purchase a ticket and later decide to volunteer, you can apply for a ticket refund once your volunteer commitment has been completed.

To process your refund, please email [**volunteers@folkfestival.org.au**](mailto:volunteers@folkfestival.org.au) with proof of ticket purchase and details of your volunteer participation (such as your roster or hours worked). In some cases, volunteers who sign up during the Festival may be asked to complete a refund form.

Where possible, volunteers who have already been accepted and rostered before the Festival may be able to have their refund processed in advance.

We aim to process all volunteer ticket refunds within 72 hours of the Festival concluding. Please note that booking fees are non-refundable.

### Can I volunteer with a friend or family member?

Yes, depending on the team and at the discretion of your coordinator. Please talk to your coordinator about this when they make initial contact.  The Gates team is a very good option to choose if you wish to work with a friend.

### When will I hear from my coordinator?

Our Coordinators are Volunteers also which means that the times that they have available to work on the Festival vary from team to team. For those signing up in the early stages, it may be some time before you hear from your coordinator. Most coordinators will make contact from mid-January and the bulk of rostering in February to early March. If you are concerned that you have not heard from your coordinator, please email [volunteers@folkfestival.org.au](mailto:volunteers@folkfestival.org.au).

### Can I volunteer in more than one team?

We prefer that volunteers do all their hours with the one team as that way we can ensure appropriate training is given and volunteer duties are clear. If you are unsure what team to choose and do not wish to commit to one team for now, please email [volunteers@folkfestival.org.au](mailto:volunteers@folkfestival.org.au) to discuss.

### Are meals provided to volunteers?

During the festival period, volunteers have access to a dedicated Volunteer Centre. Toast and spreads, fruit, and hot beverages are provided to all volunteers. There is also boiled water and microwaves available for use. The volunteer centre is set up with device charging stations for use by volunteers.

  

Meals are the responsibility of the volunteer and with many stalls on site, there is a range of options to choose from. Otherwise please bring your own food and camp kitchen equipment.

  

We aim to organise cheaper alternatives with stall holders again as we acknowledge the rising cost of meals being sold on-site.  Make sure you ask if stalls are providing volunteer discounts when ordering. Those working more than 6 hours in set up and pack down are provided lunch as there are no stalls operating in that period.

  

We ask everyone to please bring a refillable water bottle to help reduce waste on site as we aim for no single-use plastics.

### Does the festival provide accommodation to volunteers?

All Volunteers are provided with the option to camp on-site. The provided camping areas are non-powered. Limited powered spots are available on a first come first served basis and incur a $50 charge. Volunteers must bring their own tent and other camping gear. There is an area for volunteer camping that is unbookable by the public ticket buyers so there is plenty of space. Otherwise, you are free to camp anywhere that is not a pre-booked site in the camping zones. If arriving before mark-out, please check with the camping team before setting up camp to ensure you do not set up in a prebooked site. We have an area for those requiring Access camping with nearby facilities appropriate for those with a disability. These are to be booked at no charge. If power is required for medical reasons this can be accommodated in the Access camping area.

### Inclusivity Statement

The National Folk Festival is an inclusive organisation that is committed to inclusion across race, culture, ethnicity, gender, sexuality, religion, and ability. We encourage all to apply and will work with you to find the right team and duties to ensure a positive volunteering experience.

  

For those volunteers living with a disability that require consideration or modification to support their work, we ask that you give us extra time in the application process to find the right position to suit your needs.

  

Our capacity as a non-profit volunteer organisation is such that we cannot provide the proper levels of care for someone with a serious mental health issue. Participation in any festival can be intense and we advise anyone with any health issue or mental health condition to work out a special health management plan with their current practitioners prior to arriving on site. This plan should be shared with your team coordinator and the volunteer manager so that together we can make sure that volunteering is right for you at this time, and the team you are placed in is the best possible fit to ensure an enjoyable festival.

### The commitment you are making as a volunteer for the National Folk Festival

As a volunteer, you are committing to a minimum of 20 hours of work over the Festival period (Thursday to Monday). If you choose to work pre or post-Festival this time commitment will be more depending on the team.

(Youth volunteers /interns may be engaged for fewer or greater hours depending on whether they are completing volunteering components for training courses, or have other educational requirements requiring minimum hours)

### Volunteer positions

The following options are open to volunteers. The number of positions on each crew is finite, so once all positions on that crew are filled no new applications are taken.

  

Pre-Festival:

Generally, these teams work from the weekend before the Festival through to the Thursday when the Festival opens helping set up the infrastructure that supports the festival and Volunteers teams. Jobs include site decoration, mesh hanging, set up of the shop, ticket office, office, instrument lockup, and similar. Most of the positions (except for Gates) during this period do require a level of physical fitness. People with trade backgrounds, or handyperson skills are of value during this setup period.

  

During:

There are many teams operating during the festival managing everything from ticket offices, general inquiries, stage and venue management, instrument lockup, lost property, festival transport, gates, and much more.

  

Post:

Pack up Tuesday to Thursday: Assist dismantling and packing away festival equipment, and ensuring we hand back the site as clean, tidy and undamaged as possible.

# FAQs

If any burning questions are left unanswered please contact us.

 

[

Do I need to buy a ticket to attend Junction?

](javascript:void\(0\))

We have a range of free and ticketed events as part of the festival - check out our program for more information.

[

Who is eligible for a concession ticket?

](javascript:void\(0\))

We accept: Seniors Cards, DVA Cards, Health Care Cards, Pension Cards, Full-Time Students and Children Under 16.

If you purchase a concession ticket you will be asked to present your valid concession card at the venue.

[

It's kind of cold and wet outside, will Junction still go on?

](javascript:void\(0\))

Yes! Junction is here to liven up Launceston and the show must go on in rain, hail or shine. We would recommend dressing for the conditions - a nice warm coat, scarf, beanie, gloves and wet weather gear is recommended. Rarely will shows be cancelled due to weather, but please check our Facebook page (for live updates).

[

What time does the event start and finish?

](javascript:void\(0\))

Please check the schedule for detailed information about times of show and events.

[

What accessibility provisions are available?

](javascript:void\(0\))

Junction strives to make the festival as accessible as possible. Given the nature of some events, on rare occasions there may be limited access. Further details are listed on our accessibility page as well as the event pages. Feel free to [contact us](mailto:info@junctionartsfestival.com.au) to confirm specific details of performances.

[

Will there be food and drink available at the festival or can I bring my own?

](javascript:void\(0\))

An excellent selection of Tasmanian food vans will be in Prince's Square throughout the festival. Vendors include: Sweet Little Devil Donuts, Stasberry, Savoury Sailor Food Truck, Food of Himalayas, Maesi Thai Kitchen, Greenbean Woodfired Pizza, Fried & Loaded, Malvinas, Pink Buns Coffee, and Tumble Coffee. While we ask that you support our vendors, we understand that children, or those with allergies, may need to bring their own food. As this is a licensed event, you are not permitted to bring alcohol into any of our venues.

[

I love my pet; can they enjoy the art too?

](javascript:void\(0\))

We love pets too, however generally pets are not permitted to attend performances in formal venues. Guide dogs and assistance animals are however permitted in all venues. Please note pet relief areas may not be available.

[

I'm not an arty type, will there still be something at the festival for me?

](javascript:void\(0\))

Absolutely, Junction is about putting everyone at the heart of the action. The program truly features something for every taste, age and disposition. Check out our program and search for something that would interest you. We have music, dance, live performance, installations + more!

[

Is Junction a not-for-profit organisation or charity?

](javascript:void\(0\))

Yes, Junction Arts Festival Inc. is a not-for-profit organisation (ABN 36 414 918 339). 

[

Are your tickets GST inclusive?

](javascript:void\(0\))

Ticket prices include GST. A 3% card fee applies for each transaction.

[

Where does my donation go?

](javascript:void\(0\))

Junction aims to offer a program full of fun events for the general public. Your donation will help us make sure that we can continue to create this great event every year.

[

Who are your funders and sponsors?

](javascript:void\(0\))

Junction is able to operate because of the tremendous financial and in-kind support of government, funding bodies, foundations, corporate sponsors and local businesses. For a full list of Junction partners and supporters, or to find out how you can support the festival, check out our [Partners page.](https://tariks17.sg-host.com/about-us/partners/)

[

I'm an artist. How can I get my work included in the next festival program?

](javascript:void\(0\))

Please [contact us](https://junctionartsfestival.com.au/contact-us) to discuss opportunities with our Festival Team.

[

What kind of work is included in the festival program?

](javascript:void\(0\))

Junction Arts Festival is an international multi-arts festival with a focus on interactive, participatory performance work and site-specific installations. Junction features the work of artists from the local community of Launceston, Tasmania, across Australia and around the world.

[

What do you do with my contact details; do you have a privacy policy?

](javascript:void\(0\))

Junction Arts Festival takes privacy seriously and is committed to protecting privacy of your personal information. The festival endorses fair information handling practices and use of information. Personal information will be used only for the purpose/s intended and where the intention includes confidentiality, information will be treated as such unless otherwise required by law.

Please [contact us](https://junctionartsfestival.com.au/contact-us) for more information regarding JAF's privacy policy.

## A COLLISION OF

*   ART

*   PERFORMANCE

*   MUSIC

Junction Arts Festival returns for its 15th year from the 18th-21st September 2025 with a captivating springtime celebration, inviting you to embrace the season’s renewal and revel in Tasmania’s vibrant awakening. As nature bursts into bloom, Junction transforms Launceston into a mesmerising intersection of Tasmanian (lutruwita) art, music, and performance, creating a kaleidoscopic celebration that captures the magic of the spring equinox.

With a diverse program of free and ticketed events, Junction offers something for everyone to discover. From daytime activities to evening entertainment, the city comes alive with the best of Tasmania’s creative talent. While you immerse yourself in the arts, savour the island’s renowned culinary delights, from gourmet local food to distinctive Tasmanian wines, spirits, and craft brews as you celebrate into the night.

# 2026 Jetty ArtSpace Competition  
Nightcliff Seabreeze Festival  
 Saturday & Sunday May 9-10 2026  
\*\* [Register Your Art for 2026](https://www.nightcliffcommunity.com/jetty-artspace-registration.html) \*\*  
[Apply for School Art Supplies Grant](https://www.nightcliffcommunity.com/jetty-artspace-school-support.html)

Important information for entry

*   Entry is Free
*   Artwork must be registered online **before 5pm Friday 1 May 2026**
*   Only **one (1)** piece of art per artist, per school, per childcare or per group will be admitted.
*   **Unregistered work will be refused** and won't be eligible for prizes
*   All entries must have your **name and contact details** on the back
*   Each entry will be allocated a number for voting purposes 
*   **We will announce the winners and present prizes at the** **Community Bank Nightcliff** **at 10.00am Sunday 24th May 2026  
      
    A 'Door Prize' of a Webber BBQ will be drawn from voters present.** 

[**2025 Jetty ArtSpace winners**](https://www.nightcliffcommunity.com/2025-jettyartspace-winners.html)

### 2026 Categories and Prizes

#### Group Entries

Primary Schools

Ist $1500

2nd $750

3rd $250

Middle/ Secondary Schools

Ist $1500

2nd $750

3rd $250

Open Groups

1st $500

2nd $200

3rd $100

Childcare Centres

1st $500  

2nd $200

3rd $100

#### Individual Entries

Open Individual

Ist $1500

2nd $750

3rd $250

Individual  
Under 16 Years

1st $500

2nd $200

3rd $100

Individual  
Under 12 Years

1st $100

2nd $75

3rd $50

The 2026 Jetty ArtSpace entries will be judged by  Community Votes.

#### Please prepare your work for us to hang

The ArtSpace experiences moderate to severe winds and while the sea breeze is refreshing to feel it can lift even heavy pieces of art and throw them. Art is displayed on fencing panels or on the ground and we've learned that using cable ties to secure it is our safest and most reliable option in the wind.  

We will have hooks and cable ties for registered entries but artists must prepare their own work to hang.

Cardboard and paper are impossible to hang and damage is guaranteed.    

**All artwork is displayed at the owners risk**.

Images of Artworks and Artists may be used in promotional material by  **Community Bank Nightcliff**

### Where can I find the Jetty ArtSpace?

The Jetty ArtSpace will be at the same location at the Nightcliff Jetty

Pick up a flyer from your local cafe / library, [Download it & Print it (PDF)](https://www.nightcliffcommunity.com/support-files/2019-buspass.pdf) at home OR SIMPLY SHOW IT ON YOUR PHONE OR DEVICE  to the bus driver.

# Nightcliff Markets Stall.

A Nightcliff Markets Stall space is available at the front of the **Nightcliff Community Bank** to help local people promote their clubs and charities.

**This space is only available to clubs and other not for profit organizations.**

**All enquiries for general stalls at the markets should be directed to the Nightcliff Markets Manager, Ross Dudgeon on** [**0414 368 773**](https://www.google.com/search?q=Nightcliff+Markets+Manager.&rlz=1C1CHBF_enAU804AU804&oq=Nightcliff+Markets+Manager.&aqs=chrome..69i57.1679j0j8&sourceid=chrome&ie=UTF-8#)

Nightcliff Market Stall

The [Nightcliff Sunday Markets](http://www.enjoy-darwin.com/nightcliff-markets.html) have been a popular destination for both local people and tourists for many years. A variety of arts and crafts, coffee, food and local produce attract visitors to enjoy the pleasant atmosphere provided by live music and the distinctively different stalls and displays.

The Bendigo Bank is a focal point for the markets, especially with the ATM facility, and provides good exposure for stalls located here.

The area along the front of the Bank is available for local groups who wish to promote their favourite clubs, sports or charities during the Sunday Markets.

This is part of the **Community Bank** policy of playing an active supportive role in the Darwin community. Of course it goes without saying that any stalls need to be family friendly and comply with local council regulations.

Please contact Nightcliff bank staff to discuss the possibility of using this space for your community organisation.

Larrakia Stall

**Larrakia Nation** using the bank space to sell tickets for the Moscow Circus opening night for which the proceeds (and discounted tickets) are going to Larrakia Nation and the Retta Dixon Home.

  

SidsnKids Stall

**Sids 'n Kids** using the market stall to raise awareness of support services to those affected by the death of a child that dies suddenly and unexpectedly and to raise some much needed funds.

All around Australia sports clubs, charities, schools and other community groups have benefited from millions of dollars returned to the people through successful community banks

# Nightcliff Community Bank Staff

Nightcliff Community Bank Staff feel they are more than just bank staff because the Bank plays such an important role in the local community.

![Naomi](https://www.nightcliffcommunity.com/images/Naomi.jpg "Manager Naomi Martinson")Naomi

![Amanda Penhall](https://www.nightcliffcommunity.com/images/Amanda.jpg "Mobile Relationship Manager Amanda Penhall")Amanda

![Sam](https://www.nightcliffcommunity.com/images/Sam.jpg "Customer Relationship Officer")Sam

![Best Community Bank® in NT/SA Awards Won by Nightcliff Bank Team](https://www.nightcliffcommunity.com/images/banking-awards.jpg "Best Community Bank® in NT/SA Awards Won by Nightcliff Bank Team")Best Community Bank® in NT/SA Awards Won by Nightcliff Bank Team

As the bank grows and is able to provide support for more and more community groups, the manager and staff of this bank can see they are providing more than just a banking service, and are justifiably proud of their role in the community

The NCEL board also recognises how important professional banking services are for the community and endeavours to provide our staff with the best possible training available.

Board Chairman Jim McDougall encourages local people to come into the bank and meet the staff - "After all, this bank was set up by local shareholders to meet the needs of our community".

![xmas18-childrensward](https://www.nightcliffcommunity.com/images/xmas18-childrensward-l.jpg "Donations for the children's ward RDH")Children's Ward RDH

Within a year, the Community Bank was able to begin support for local clubs and charity organisations.

All around Australia sports clubs, charities, schools and other community groups have benefited from millions of dollars returned to the people through successful community banks.

![Donations to Nightcliff Charities](https://www.nightcliffcommunity.com/images/nightcliff-donations-280.jpg "Donations to Nightcliff Charities")Nightcliff Donations 2009

![Jeff Watson](https://www.nightcliffcommunity.com/images/Jeff-Watson.jpg "Jeff Watson")

After nearly 17 years serving as Branch Manager, Jeff has now moved to Queensland with Janet to begin a new life in the Gold Coast near their daughter.

Jeff made an enormous contribution to both the bank and the community in general.

In September 2009, **Jeff Watson** joined the Bank as our new Branch Manager. Jeff has over 25 years of Banking experience and in recent years was an Mortgage Manager & Regional Manager before joining the Business here. His last role was the Management of the Credit Union for the Australian Defence Force in the NT.

Jeff grew up in Western Suburbs of Adelaide & joined the banking industry straight from Underdale High School after turning down a teaching university placement. His banking career has taken him to several country posting including Naracoorte, Mount Gambier & Penola.

Jeff transferred to Darwin in 1999 & now calls it home after spending the last 21 years here.

Jeff is married to Janet with one child Briana, Janet is employed at local IT Management company CSG where she manages the Help Desk business for NT Government.

Jeff is a keen fisherman & member of the Darwin Flyrodders Fishing Club of which he is the Treasurer, so when not working its likely you will see him out on the water trying to catch the elusive Barra.

As a Branch Manager of the previous bank at this location, Jeff has a long term relationship with the Community of Nightcliff & is closely involved in the many sporting & not for profit groups in the area, he also built up a strong business relationship with many of the local store owners & has assisted many clients in purchasing homes in our Community over the past 11 years.

# Techno Picnic

The fire never really goes out. Old doesn't mean boring. We just pretend parties are picnics and we might make bedtime.

DATE Sunday, November 1

TIME 1PM - 7PM

VENUE ACT Waterski Club, Molonglo River

PRICE Adults $29, Kids $15, Family $69

[Buy tickets](https://events.humanitix.com/techno-picnic-2/tickets?widget=popup)

**Techno Picnic is back!** The event is scheduled for Sunday 1st November by the Molonglo River at the Waterskiing Club. Warm air, unreal sunset, dancing feet that need some practice, and a weatherproof venue on standby.

For years we threw warehouse parties. Late and loud with ridiculous artists. Techno Picnic has the same soul with decorum: earlier, cheaper, a bit more ‘picnic’.

## The Music

Headlining is **D-Nox** with a FOUR-HOUR set. For anyone unfamiliar, D-Nox has been a global mainstay of melodic and progressive techno for decades. Driving beats, rolling basslines, and emotional builds that sneak up and get you when you least expect it. Plenty of you remember 2019, when he turned Verity Lane into a big trampoline. It’s an honour to have him back, now with grass and frisbees.

Playing beforehand is **Waxlily** — an Escape Ferocity warehouse resident who’s been away charming Sydney, now coming home to sprinkle that sparkly energy and seamless mixing across the afternoon. Lunch has never sounded so good.

## The Vibe

Same ethos: a tip-top international artist without the heavy ticket price, and open to all ages.

## The Key Bits

*   Sunday 1 November, 1–7pm, by the water. Home in time to look responsible.
*   Bring your mates or the cute little ratbags.
*   Bring a blanket, snacks and an esky of (any) drinks, or let the bar and food stalls handle it.
*   Micaela’s cocktails, local wines and delicious food.
*   Merch: picnic blankets and competition-weight frisbees.

Questions? Email [connect@technopicnic.com](mailto:connect@technopicnic.com) .

## Find it only at Finders, this October.

The Melbourne Design Market returns 9-11 October to the Royal Exhibition Building with 230+ independent designers and makers for a three-day celebration of mindfully made, good design.

For 18 years, this is where emerging talent has launched, limited editions sell out and design lovers secure what’s next, first. Unique wares, small runs and exclusives you won’t find anywhere else.

Come for the discovery, stay for an Italian feast and collaging workshops, and leave with unique gifts ready for the festive season ahead!

### [Get October market tickets here](https://www.universe.com/events/the-finders-keepers-melbourne-design-market-ss26-tickets-TDRHM2)

Get your tickets online early!

#### $7 daily entry  
$10 weekend pass  
NEW: $13 ticket + [zine](https://www.thefinderskeepers.com/melbourne-markets/found-zine.html) package!  
NEW: $70 [A Feast at Nonna's Table](https://www.thefinderskeepers.com/melbourne-markets/nonnas-table/)!  
Kids under 13 free

_A small booking fee applies._

### Grab a Fan Club membership for a year of market tickets - 

And more! Do you attend as many of our markets as you can? We created [**Fan Club**](https://www.thefinderskeepers.com/melbourne-markets/fan-club/) just for market lovers like you! Sign up for a year of market tickets, bring friends free, discounts, meet-ups and more, all for $30.

![Nonnas Table](img/ss26/Nonnas-Table.jpg)

NEW Pop-up event: [A Feast at Nonna's Table](https://www.thefinderskeepers.com/melbourne-markets/nonnas-table/)

For one Friday night only, The Finders Keepers invites you to join us at Nonna’s Table, a long-table pasta party with [Via Gianlu](https://www.dagianlucacatering.com/) and [Sorry Nonna](https://sorrynonna.com/).

A Feast at Nonna's Table at the Melbourne market

Friday 9th October, 5:15pm for 5:30pm - 7:30pm

Inclusions:

Antipasto & shared pasta feast  
Prosecco on arrival by [Fin Wines](https://finwines.com.au/)  
Dessert by [Cannoleria](https://www.cannoleriaaustralia.com.au/)  
Market entry  
Plus a copy of our new zine [Found!](https://www.thefinderskeepers.com/melbourne-markets/found-zine.html)  
[Full menu and info here](https://www.thefinderskeepers.com/melbourne-markets/nonnas-table/)  
[TICKETS:](https://www.universe.com/events/the-finders-keepers-melbourne-design-market-ss26-tickets-TDRHM2) $70 + booking fee

Very limited seats are available, and once the table is full, it’s full. Get in quick and save your seat at Nonna’s Table!

Missed out on Nonna's feast tickets? Nonna's Table dining room will be at the market all weekend, with Italian flavours from coffee, mains, all the way through to dessert and drinks.

![Zine](img/ss26/The-Finders-Keepers_Zine_Cover-Pink.png)

NEW: Introducing Found, our new mini mag

Slower-paced storytelling for the creatively curious, our choc-a-bloc mini mag ['Found'](https://www.thefinderskeepers.com/melbourne-markets/found-zine.html) is available exclusively at our SS26 markets. [Reserve your limited copy](https://www.universe.com/events/the-finders-keepers-melbourne-design-market-ss26-tickets-TDRHM2) with your market tickets today, or get tickets to [A Feast at Nonna's Table](https://www.thefinderskeepers.com/melbourne-markets/nonnas-table/) and it's included!

![That Paper Joint](img/ss26/That_Paper_Joint-52.jpg)

NEW: That Paper Joint workshops

We're so pumped to be collaborating with artist Maximillian Malone and his team at Brunswick-based collage studio [That Paper Joint!](https://www.thatpaperjoint.com/) Check out the workshop options below and [grab your limited tickets online now](https://www.universe.com/events/the-finders-keepers-melbourne-design-market-ss26-tickets-TDRHM2). The workshops are found in The Playground area of the market, alongside the Mindfulness Mural by Melbourne-based illustrator Emma Winton, and other fun stallholders!

#### **Collage Club Pop-Up: Self-guided Workshop**

Similar to their [Pub Collage Nights](https://www.thatpaperjoint.com/pubcollageclub)! A big communal collage table, join in for self-paced casual collaging for 2 hours, or come and go as you please. All materials provided.

**When**: Friday 9th October, 5:30pm - 7:30pm.  
**[Get Tickets:](https://www.universe.com/events/the-finders-keepers-melbourne-design-market-ss26-tickets-TDRHM2)** $35pp, including entry to the market. 

#### Contemporary Collage Masterclass

A guided masterclass presented by Max Malone, co-founder of That Paper Joint. Collage with pieces from their treasure trove of hand-cut materials, with Max as your guide. Turn your glue-free composition into a digital print to take home!

**When:  
**Saturday 10th October, 10:30am - 12pm  
Sunday 11th October, 10:30am - 12pm  
[**Get Tickets:**](https://www.universe.com/events/the-finders-keepers-melbourne-design-market-ss26-tickets-TDRHM2) $70pp, including entry to the market.

### Indigenous Program and Regional Program

Our SS26 [Indigenous Program](https://www.thefinderskeepers.com/melbourne-markets/indigenous-program.html) recipient is Cooked Concepts, with their "tongue-in-cheek gifts for the non-practising intellectual"! Our SS26 [Regional Program](https://www.thefinderskeepers.com/melbourne-markets/regional-program.html) recipient is [Fluturi](https://www.etsy.com/au/shop/Fluturi), with children's clothing handmade in Castle Forbes Bay, Tasmania by Rebecca Madigan.

### Low Sensory Hour, Sunday 9am

Low sensory hour is on Sunday from 9am to 10am. During this time, we’ll reduce lights, lower or turn off music, and limit capacity for a calmer shopping experience. Those already inside can continue shopping after 10am when we open to the public. Get tickets online now.

### Cash Handling

If you’re buying on the door please come ready with your digital payment device.

Most stallholders accept cash and all accept digital payments. **No ATM's** are available on site.

### Access & Transport

For how to get there, head to our [Access](https://www.thefinderskeepers.com/melbourne-markets/melbourne-markets-directions.html) page.

We highly recommend using public transport. Royal Exhibition Building directions and a 'how to get there guide' is also [available here](https://museumsvictoria.com.au/reb/visiting/).

All areas of the building used by the markets, including toilet facilities, are accessible for wheelchairs. Designated disabled parking is available on level P2 adjacent to the lifts within the Melbourne Museum car park. Wheelchairs are available for use within the venue should they be required.

Assistance animals with identification are always welcome in our market venues. We also always offer complimentary entry to companions and carers, please just show your identification at our entry desk.

The venue has indoor toilets and baby change facilities.

We have also introduced a low sensory hour, Sunday 9am - 10am and your ticket includes general admission so you can stay on afterwards if you wish. Music will be off and lights low. Get your tickets online to save when they go live.

### Market Stall Applications

Applications are now closed for this event, but you are welcome to submit a late application. 

Have questions? Email us on [markets@thefinderskeepers.com](mailto:markets@thefinderskeepers.dsom) and for all the info and to apply, head to our [APPLY page.](http://www.thefinderskeepers.com/applications-overview.html)

# General FAQs

When is the festival?

The Unconformity festival will be held from 16–19 October 2025.

Where is the festival?

The Unconformity festival is held in and around Queenstown, on Lutruwita/Tasmania’s West Coast. Queenstown is approximately a four-hour drive from both Launceston and Nipaluna/Hobart.

When do tickets go on sale?

Tickets go on sale 10am on Friday 29 August. West Coast locals will have access to presale tickets from 10am-5pm on Tuesday 26 August.

Ticketing information and FAQs can be found [here](https://2025.theunconformity.com.au/ticketing-information/).

Are you running a bus service?

This year we are pleased to offer a free bus service running daily from Strahan and Burnie through to Queenstown, with stops in Tullah, Rosebery, and Zeehan. Details on bookings and the timetable can be found [here](https://2025.theunconformity.com.au/bus-service/).

Where can I smoke?

There will be a designated smoking area at Crib Road and Grooved Erratic. All other venues/shows do not permit smoking.

Can I bring my dog to The Unconformity?

The Unconformity is a busy, high-traffic festival with a mix of indoor and outdoor venues, live performance, and food service areas. For the comfort and safety of all visitors (and dogs), we ask that pets are not brought into festival venues, event spaces, or food areas.  
Crib Road and surrounding public spaces remain open to the public, and we understand some people may pass through with their dogs. Please keep dogs on a leash and under control at all times.  
Accredited assistance and service animals are, of course, welcome throughout the festival.

I have lost or found property at the festival. Who can help?

Please take any found property to the Festival Information Booth so it can be logged and kept safe. If you’ve lost an item, head to the Festival Information Booth to see if anyone has handed in your item, or log your details in case it shows up.

What about COVID-19 safety?

The Unconformity’s highest priority is to provide a safe and enjoyable experience for all people involved with the festival. We all have a responsibility to ensure that The Unconformity festival is a safe place for audiences, artists, staff, volunteers and our local community. Please remember to not attend the festival if you are feeling unwell.

# Ticketing Information

## The Unconformity is proud to present the majority of our program free of charge thanks to the support of our collaborators and partners. For ticketed events, please refer to the information provided on this page.

## Booking Tickets

Festival tickets are on sale from 10am, Friday 29 August 2025. For any ticketing enquiries, please contact us via email at [tickets@theunconformity.com.au](mailto:tickets@theunconformity.com.au)

### Pay It Forward

We believe cost should not be a barrier to experiencing the festival. With over 80% of the program free, we're committed to making The Unconformity as accessible as we can. Our No Barriers initiative allows anyone to request a free ticket to ticketed events – no explanation needed. You can also pay it forward when booking your own ticket by making a donation to help cover the cost for others. Every contribution supports broader access to the arts on the West Coast. To request a ticket fill out the [form](https://wkf.ms/3JfE2IO).

### West Coast Presale

West Coasters will have the chance to purchase tickets to festival events on Tuesday 26 August 2025 in person at The Unconformity Hall, 35 Cutten Street, Queenstown. More information can be found [here.](https://2025.theunconformity.com.au/west-coast-presale/)

## **FAQs**

When do tickets go on sale?

Tickets are available to purchase online or over the phone from 10am Friday 29 August 2025.

Will I be charged a booking fee?

Yes, a 3.6% booking fee (BF) applies to each transaction. Listed ticket prices exclude the booking fee.

Why does The Unconformity charge a booking fee?

Booking fees help to cover the costs associated with using our ticketing platform, card-processing fees and the administration of these ticketing systems.

How will I receive my tickets?

Tickets will be emailed to you once you’ve completed your purchase.

What format will my tickets be in?

We recommend that you show your ticket digitally at each event using a smartphone or device. If this is not possible, you may print your ticket and bring it along with you.

Is there a limit on how many tickets I can purchase?

A limit of six tickets per person applies to each event, except Unrise, which is limited to two tickets per person.

Does The Unconformity support Companion Cards?

Yes. Companion Card holders are entitled to a complimentary ticket for their companion. Bookings for complimentary companion tickets can be by made by call **03 6471 1026** or let us know via email at [tickets@theunconformity.com.au](mailto:tickets@theunconformity.com.au)

Am I eligible for a concession/West Coast ticket?

Concession and West Coast-priced tickets are available for West Coast residents, full-time students and children aged 16 year and under as well as Pensioner, Health Care, Seniors and Companion Card holders.

Can I exchange my ticket or get a refund?

The Unconformity does not offer exchanges or refunds on tickets, except in the event of cancellation. See our full [Ticketing Terms and Conditions](https://2025.theunconformity.com.au/ticketing-terms-conditions/) for more details.

I’ve purchased tickets but not received them. What should I do?

First, check to see if your ticket email got caught up in a spam or junk filter. If you still don’t have the email, please contact us on 03 6471 1026 or via [tickets@theunconformity.com.au](mailto:tickets@theunconformity.com.au).

Can I resell my tickets? Can I buy someone else's tickets?

No. The Unconformity does not have a resale facility. Tickets purchased outside of our official ticketing platform may not be legitimate and if you purchase a ticket outside of our ticketing platform, there is a risk it will not be accepted at the door.  
If you are no longer able to attend a free event, please email [tickets@theunconformity.com.au](mailto:tickets@theunconformity.com.au) so the ticket can be given to someone on the waitlist.

Can I book tickets in person?

You can book tickets if they are still available during the festival weekend with our team at the Festival Information Booth.

Please visit the [Festival Information Booth](https://2025.theunconformity.com.au/events/festival-information-booth/) page for opening hours.

Can I book tickets over the phone?

To purchase tickets over the phone, call **03 6471 1026** Monday to Friday, 10am-5pm.  
If you are deaf or hard of hearing, you can contact The Unconformity through the National Relay Service:

TTY users phone **133 677**  
Speak and Listen users phone **1300 555 727**

My ticket says ‘no latecomers’. What does that mean?

Some events have a strict lockout policy, which means that no one will be admitted once the event has started.

Lockouts are advertised on the relevant website event pages, during online ticket purchases and on your ticket. No refunds will be provided for latecomers to strict lockout events.

What does 'no passouts' mean?

If you leave a ticketed event that advertises 'no passouts', you will not be allowed to re-enter the venue, even if you have a ticket.

What is a lockout?

A venue lockout occurs when a venue stops allowing ticket holders to enter after a certain time, even though the event inside is still running. People already inside can stay until the event ends, but any ticket holders who have not yet entered will not be able to do so once lockout begins.

The event I want to see is sold out. Can I join a waitlist?

Yes, you can join the waitlist for sold-out events on the Tickets page. If a ticket becomes available and you are on the waitlist, you may receive an email offering the opportunity to purchase a ticket. We encourage you to purchase waitlist tickets promptly, as the link to claim an available ticket will not last forever.

I have a baby or young child, do they need a ticket?

Children aged two years and under do not require a ticket to most events on the condition they do not occupy a seat and they are carried by, or sit on the lap of, a parent or guardian.

Which events are suitable for kids?

There are targeted youth and kids activities across The Unconformity festival program, such as [The Unconformity Kids Trail](https://2025.theunconformity.com.au/events/the-unconformity-kids-trail/), [Crib Road](https://2025.theunconformity.com.au/events/crib-road/), [Elemental Memories](https://2025.theunconformity.com.au/events/elemental-memories/), [Kani mina milaythina-nanya?](https://2025.theunconformity.com.au/events/kani-mina-milaythina-nanya/) and [The Commonwealth of New Bayswater](https://2025.theunconformity.com.au/events/the-commonwealth-of-new-bayswater/). The broader festival program has been designed to engage a diverse range of audiences. Unless events are marked with an age restriction, we encourage audience members of all ages to explore and discover them.

Where can I find the ticketing terms and conditions?

See our full [Ticketing Terms and Conditions](https://2025.theunconformity.com.au/ticketing-terms-conditions/) page for details.

Melbourne Art Book Fair 2027 runs from 20 to 30 May, with the Stallholder Fair taking place at NGV International, 180 St Kilda Road, Melbourne from 21 to 23 May. Please check the full program when it launches in April for more details. The fair is free and open to the public.

# About

The Melbourne Art Book Fair brings together local and international publishers, artists, and designers, fostering exchange, collaboration, and a shared appreciation for printed matter in all its forms.

Established by the NGV in 2015, the Fair emerged in response to a growing global network of art book fairs in creative hubs such as New York and Los Angeles. Building on Melbourne’s designation as a UNESCO City of Literature in 2008, it continues to highlight the city’s vibrant art publishing landscape and the communities that sustain it.

In May 2027, Melbourne Art Book Fair will enter its thirteenth iteration. The program will feature new voices in art publishing and design, alongside longstanding collaborators. The popular Stallholder Fair will also make a return to NGV’s Gandel Hall across the opening weekend (21–23 May), offering visitors the opportunity to engage with and collect unique publications from leading local and international practitioners.

Melbourne Art Book Fair is presented as part of Melbourne Design Week, an initiative of the Victorian Government.

We are cultural and creative leaders within the Australian dance music landscape. Dedicated to uncovering the full breadth of global underground talent, we bring world-class artists to our community. We champion creatives from across the globe, driven by a deep passion for music, culture and the arts. As key contributors to Australia’s legacy of innovative and immersive dance music experiences, we continually push boundaries, delivering all-encompassing cultural moments. We are Novel. Spanning touring, events, music curation, immersive experience and artist management, we are Australia’s premier curators of contemporary music experiences. The Big Design Market is a wonderland for shoppers, with thousands of distinctive, exclusive goods for sale. For those who place value on ethical production, sustainability, quality, originality and good design, this is a shopping event not to be missed_._

To make sure everyone has a relaxed day of shopping we have ensured there is plenty of room in the aisles with enough space to stop and chat with friends, as well as a dedicated kids area with creative activities to keep them entertained.

### Melbourne event information

#### 2026 DATES + OPENING HOURS

Sunday 6 December, 10am–5pm

#### 2027 DATES + OPENING HOURS

Friday 21 May, 11am–7pm

#### VENUE

**Royal Exhibition Building, Carlton VIC**

The Big Design Market acknowledges the Woi Wurrung (Wurundjeri) and Boon Wurrung peoples of the eastern Kulin Nations where we hold our events, and First Peoples language groups and communities across Victoria and Australia.

### Application information

#### WHO SHOULD APPLY

We're looking for innovative designers and makers of fashion, jewellery, homewares, ceramics, textiles, lighting, fine art, stationery, books, gifts, kid's products and fine food and drinks. Australian distributors for original design brands from overseas are also welcome to apply.

#### APPLICATION ASSESSMENT

The selection committee gives preference to applicants whose products are created using sustainable materials and ethical manufacturing methods. Applicants launching new products and those who are not seen regularly at other markets are highly regarded.

Both the Melbourne and Sydney events are curated, and as such each application will be assessed individually. Please note, previous participation in one or more of our events does not guarantee your application will be successful for future events. Applications will be assessed against our selection criteria which takes into consideration the type and number of similar applications received.  
  

### About The Big Design Market

Since its launch in December 2012 _The Big Design Market_ has brought together leading independent designers and design retailers from Australia and overseas. The event attracts capacity crowds to the Royal Exhibition Building, with over 50,000 shoppers coming through the doors each year.

It's the ultimate shopping destination for those who value original design and ethical production across homewares, fashion, stationery and more. The event provides a great platform for independent design businesses to launch new brands as well as showcase new ranges within existing brands.  
  

* * *

**[Sign up here](https://confirmsubscription.com/h/j/F6CB161C764FCC61) to receive information about all future events.**

If you require further information please contact us at [enquiries@thebigdesignmarket.com](mailto:enquiries@thebigdesignmarket.com)

# FAQs

[

### What is Melbourne Design Week?

](https://designweek.melbourne/faqs/#)

Melbourne Design Week celebrates design in an annual 11-day program of talks, tours, exhibitions, launches, installations, and workshops across Australia’s design capital. The program is driven by ideas through providing a platform for designers, educators, enthusiasts, thinkers, and businesses to come together to share these ideas, show and sell new work, and consider how design can be used as a force for good in an increasingly complex and precarious world.

[

### When and where does Melbourne Design Week take place?

](https://designweek.melbourne/faqs/#)

Melbourne Design Week will take place from 20-30 May, 2027. The program is held across Melbourne in cultural institutions, studios, retail spaces, universities, galleries, gardens and public spaces. Check the Melbourne Design Week program when it launches April 2027 for individual event details and subscribe the NGV eNews for further updates.

[

### Who is behind Melbourne Design Week?

](https://designweek.melbourne/faqs/#)

Melbourne Design Week is led by NGV’s Department of Contemporary Design and Architecture. The design sector contributes to Melbourne Design Week through organising and presenting events within the program.

[

### I want to attend some events at Melbourne Design Week, how can I do that?

](https://designweek.melbourne/faqs/#)

Melbourne Design Week is open to the general public and the majority of Melbourne Design Week events are free but may require bookings and/or have capacity limits. Please check back in when the program is available to plan your visit.

[

### Is Melbourne Design Week free?

](https://designweek.melbourne/faqs/#)

Yes, there are free events to attend during Melbourne Design Week. Please check the program once it becomes available. You can easily identify free events by using the ‘Free’ filter on the programs page. This will help you explore a range of exciting and accessible offerings throughout the week.

[

### Is Melbourne Design Week accessible?

](https://designweek.melbourne/faqs/#)

Melbourne Design week is comprised of over 400 events located at different venues across Melbourne. Each venue will offer varying levels of accessibility. Information regarding accessibility at individual venues will be available when the program is released in April.

For further information about how Melbourne Design Week can support your access requirements in the meantime, please contact our team.
