## Meet the Team

We're a dedicated team of passionate people championing the work of wonderful creatives. We inject goodness into Australia's creative economy on the daily, working to elevate small businesses around the country through our [market events](https://thefinderskeepers.com/markets-calendar.html), [Small Talks](https://thefinderskeepers.com/small-talks.html) online masterclasses, [Creative Business Summits](https://thefinderskeepers.com/creative-business-summit-melbourne.html) and 24/7 [Design Directory](https://thefinderskeepers.com/design-directory-introduction.html).

![](img/staff-2025/Katie.png)

### Katie Smith

#### General Manager

“I’m motivated by elevating the creative community, always balancing a strategic brain with a creative heart.” 

Katie’s role at The Finders Keepers is to bring the biggest, wildest, creative dreams to life – on time and on budget, without comprising the vision.

Katie is a serial do-er. Cutting her teeth as a publicist, she went on to build an event management business and was a part of the founding team who grew Groovin the Moo to a six-state national touring festival. Katie has built her working life in the events industry.

Her passion for all things creative, community and events will ensure the iconic The Finders Keepers events will continue offering a truly unique and carefully curated experience.

When she’s not event-wrangling, you’ll find Katie hanging with the fam, renovating their home and scouring the countryside for mid-century furniture.

![](img/staff-2025/Lindsay.png)

### Lindsay Pepper

#### National Events Manager

"I'm on this earth not only to survive but to thrive! It's my mission to live a full life with passion, compassion, humor and a side dish of style."

Lindsay is one helluva powerhouse that comes to us from a career in managing mammoth events with one of Australia's largest hotel groups. She also grew up within her family's design business. Her skills to support streamlining and success are nothing short of super! Her personality is as big as her heart, and you'll love her as much as we all do the minute you meet her.

Lindsay's the one that makes sure every road trip runs seamlessly with an execution average that sits at the highest end of the calibre scale. From crafting mammoth floor-plans to writing run-sheets, Lindsay steers a tight ship. Best yet, she always does it with enthusiasm and infectious energy that keeps everyone upbeat.

![](img/staff-2025/Roxanna.png)

### Roxanna Chan

#### Creative Projects Lead

“My mission is to share the creative spirit so it sparks the inner you!”

Roxanna is our Events 2IC and is the go-to gal for all things food and beverage. Working alongside our National Events Manager Lindsay, together this powerhouse team ensures the operations of The Finders Keepers is running optimally at all times. Not to mention brainstorming and investigating new, fun ideas for TFK’s evolution!

Roxanna has worked the gamut from product development, publications, teaching and events always finding the creative side to life. She thrives on creating space for thoughtful being, living and doing and in her free time you can spot her using her jewellery skills to spread the good vibes through hands-on workshops.

![](img/staff-2025/erykahsavage.png)

### Erykah Savage

#### Event and Community Coordinator

“I love seeing all the behind-the-scenes planning come to life, turning endless spreadsheets and emails into real-life spaces people can experience and enjoy.”

Erykah’s role at The Finders Keepers is to help bring each event to life, coordinating the operations and logistics while working closely with stallholders, suppliers and contractors to create something truly special.

After first volunteering at festivals as a teenager, Erykah quickly discovered a genuine passion for events. She has since spent five years freelancing across Australia and the UK, working on music festivals, markets and events in everything from front of house and accreditation to bars, staffing and event operations.

Erykah loves the hands-on energy of bump-in, meeting the people behind the emails and watching months of careful coordination transform into a bustling market. Passionate, resilient and creative, she brings plenty of practical experience to the team and is never afraid to pull on her hi-vis and steel caps and get stuck in. When she’s not helping make our events happen, you’ll find Erykah along the South Australian coastline with an oat flat white in hand or having a boogie to live music.

![](img/staff-2025/Ashleigh.png)

### Ashleigh Stallard

#### Communications Manager

"I believe in the power of voting with our wallets. I like to think that I live up to my sustainability values and along the way inspire those around me to do so too!"

Ashleigh has a background in journalism and PR and is passionate about conscious consumerism and supporting small business. She's a vocal advocate for Australian makers & producers, and has launched a directory [_The Fill Market_](http://www.thefillmarket.com/) to help Aussies access more sustainable groceries.

As communications manager, Ash ensures our stallholders, fans, partners and the media are always in-the-know for all things TFK, to build momentum for the conscious shopping revolution. She also heads up our [Indigenous Program](https://thefinderskeepers.com/fk-indigenous-program.html) and the new [Regional Program](https://thefinderskeepers.com/regional-program.html), working with First Nations makers, as well as remote creatives.

![](img/staff-2025/StephJamieson.png)

### Steph Jamieson

#### Brand and Digital Manager

“I love to ask questions and find out what motivates people, I think there’s magic to find in everyone’s story.”

Steph is the Digital and Brand Manager at The Finders Keepers, bringing the market to life online and keeping The Finders Keepers looking as sharp as a freshly ironed market tote. Having run her own business, Steph truly understands the heart of small businesses and loves helping independent makers thrive. When she’s not working on the markets, you’ll likely find Steph with headphones on in her home studio, working on cinematic music projects.

![](img/staff-2025/jane.png)

### Jane Jarecki

#### Social Media and Content Creator

“I resonate with all things interesting, quirky and fun, just like me. It’s essential to stand out, be proud, and be different!”

Jane is the creative force behind the scenes, bringing the values of The Finders Keepers to life with each post, video, and caption. With her expertise in social media, video creation, and community engagement, Jane’s mission is to highlight the magic of ‘thoughtfully made’ freshly and authentically, in a way that fosters deep conversation.

When she’s not behind the camera or on the hunt for the perfect emoji, you can find Jane treasure hunting for vintage gems, exploring the local makers’ market, or busy at her sewing machine, bringing her latest “fantastic idea” to life. If you see her around our markets, don’t hesitate to give her a wave! Jane loves a good ol’ chat, so be sure to stop by and ask her about her next creative adventure.

![](img/staff-2025/EmmaField-.png)

### Emma Field

#### Community and Administration Manager

“I am happiest when I'm around people – I love supporting others and sharing their highs and lows. I think that's why I enjoy creating engagement rings for my clients, what an incredible moment to share!”

Emma is our community support superstar! She's your gal on this end of the email and we're honestly not sure what we'd do without her.

Joining the team in mid-2021, it didn't take long for our stallholders to fall for Emma as she truly walks the stallholder walk with her eponymous [jewellery label](https://www.emmafield.net/). Emma knows the juggle is real, balancing bespoke jewellery making with roles in marketing and customer service.

She knows exactly what it's like to be a small creative business owner, making Em the perfect addition to the TFK fam.

![](img/staff-2025/em.png)

### Em Fogarty (Fogs)

#### Purveyor of Good Times

Lucky for us, Em brings rhythm, fun, and unwavering reliability to everything she touches.

With a diploma in performing arts and a foundation in hospitality management, she moves through the world of event coordination with dancer-like poise, effortless, graceful, and entirely composed.

She marries operational expertise with creative insight: ensuring every event runs smoothly and leaves a lasting impression. As a key member of our events team, Em is the steady beat of our markets the quiet strength that keeps our momentum perfectly in tune

# About

Melbourne Design Week (MDW) is Australia’s leading design festival, held annually over 11 days in Melbourne.

Driven by ideas, MDW provides a platform for designers, thinkers, educators, businesses, and enthusiasts to come together to share perspectives, showcase new work, and consider how design can be a force for good in an increasingly complex world. The program features talks, tours, dinners, exhibitions, launches, and workshops, and will run from 20–30 May in 2027.

Events take place across a wide range of venues – studios, retail spaces, universities, galleries, gardens, sports courts, restaurants and public spaces – celebrating Melbourne’s identity as Australia’s design capital.

Participation is open via an application process. This inclusive approach has helped MDW cultivate an international reputation for promoting design discourse, fostering critical thinking, and encouraging Australia’s design community to shape a better future. It has also supported capacity-building within the sector, offering opportunities for both emerging and established designers.

An initiative of the Victorian Government through Creative Victoria, MDW has grown significantly since its launch in 2017: from just under 100 events in its first year to over 500 in 2026. With more than 120,000 attendees in 2026, MDW is Australia’s most influential design event. It is also one of the Indo-Pacific’s largest design festivals with over 1,300 participating designers.

The festival’s curation is led by NGV’s Department of Contemporary Design and Architecture.

### Application information

#### WHO SHOULD APPLY

We're looking for innovative designers and makers of fashion, jewellery, homewares, ceramics, textiles, lighting, fine art, stationery, books, gifts, kid's products and fine food and drinks. Australian distributors for original design brands from overseas are also welcome to apply.

#### APPLICATION ASSESSMENT

The selection committee gives preference to applicants whose products are created using sustainable materials and ethical manufacturing methods. Applicants launching new products and those who are not seen regularly at other markets are highly regarded.

Both the Melbourne and Sydney events are curated, and as such each application will be assessed individually. Please note, previous participation in one or more of our events does not guarantee your application will be successful for future events. Applications will be assessed against our selection criteria which takes into consideration the type and number of similar applications received.  
  

### About The Big Design Market

Since its launch in December 2012 _The Big Design Market_ has brought together leading independent designers and design retailers from Australia and overseas. The event attracts capacity crowds to the Royal Exhibition Building, with over 50,000 shoppers coming through the doors each year.

It's the ultimate shopping destination for those who value original design and ethical production across homewares, fashion, stationery and more. The event provides a great platform for independent design businesses to launch new brands as well as showcase new ranges within existing brands.

# Getting there

### Royal Exhibition Building, 9 Nicholson St, Carlton VIC

The Royal Exhibition Building is located just north of Melbourne's CBD, next to the Melbourne Museum in Carlton Gardens. Access to the venue is via the main doors on the Nicholson Street side. [_View google map_](https://www.google.com/maps/place/Royal+Exhibition+Building/@-37.8049352,144.9719227,19.21z/data=!4m6!3m5!1s0x6ad642d997ffde71:0x44a0b109393d7537!8m2!3d-37.8046891!4d144.9716502!16zL20vMDJueWZ2) »

#### GETTING THERE BY CAR + PARKING

Located under Melbourne Museum, the car park is open 7 days a week from 5.30am to midnight daily. Enter via Rathdowne Street or Nicholson Street.

**CAR PARK RATES** 

**Monday to Friday**  
Hourly rate: 0–1 hrs/$15.00, 1–2 hrs/$30.00, 2–3 hrs/$45.00  
Maximum daily rate: $60.00  
Flexi bird Monday–Friday: $16.00 (enter between 5.30am-9.30am, exit before midnight)  
**Nights**  
$15.00 flat rate per night (enter after 4.00pm, exit before closing)  
**Weekends**  
Hourly rate: 0–1 hrs/$10.00, 1–2 hrs/$20.00  
Maximum daily rate: $30.00

For more information on parking, please visit _[Museums Victoria](https://museumsvictoria.com.au/melbournemuseum/plan-your-visit/getting-here-and-parking/)_. 

#### PUBLIC TRANSPORT OPTIONS

• Tram 86 or 96 to corner of Nicholson and Gertrude Streets  
• Free _[City Circle Tram](https://yarratrams.com.au/circle-city-tram)[](https://transport.vic.gov.au/route/15834/35)_ to Victoria Parade  
• City loop train to Parliament Station  
• Bus routes 250, 251 and 402 to Rathdowne St  

#### CYCLING

Local bicycle facilities include bike lanes on Rathdowne St and Canning St. There is also a shared pedestrian/bike path on Nicholson St. Bicycle racks on the plaza provide ample bike parking just outside the front door.

## Description

**3 big days. 280+ designers. 80+ foodies. 1 big shopping event.**

Melbourne’s most iconic festive shopping extravaganza is back from **4–6 December 2026** at the Royal Exhibition Building - bringing together **280+ of the country’s best independent designers**, all under one very beautiful roof.

From contemporary fashion and handcrafted jewellery to colourful ceramics, original art, beautiful homewares, innovative lifestyle products, beauty, kids, accessories, pet wares, stationery and much more, discover an incredible lineup of fresh faces and returning favourites from across Australia.

Immerse yourself in a spectacular **large-scale art installation by Guest Artist Em Hatton**, explore a dedicated creative space for kids, and discover the all-new **Curl Club by Wuli Hair x Delilah Hair Studio**, with live styling demonstrations, curl education, giveaways and more.

Come hungry, with **80+ food and drink brands** joining the Market. Indulge in gourmet feasts, sip on delicious drinks and kick off the weekend in style with vibrant **Friday Night Drinks**. Plus, snap up our legendary **Designer Showbags** and enter to win **incredible prizes**.

This is the ultimate festive event - bursting with independent design, creativity, incredible food and plenty of good times. Just in time to tick off your gift list (or totally forget it and treat yourself).

We look forward to sharing The Big Design Market with you for an exquisite shopping indulgence.

**TICKETING INFO:**  

Tickets are available online here and on the door all weekend. Kids 12 and under are free.

All tickets to The Big Design Market are cashless and we accept card-only payments at the door. Some exhibitors will accept cash, but be sure to bring your credit/debit cards too.    

All tickets are non-refundable. Your ticket is valid for entry on any one day of the event.  

**EVENT HOURS:**

Friday 4 December, 11am - 7pm

Saturday 5 December, 10am - 6pm

Sunday 6 December, 10am - 5pm

**EVENT PHOTOGRAPHY & FILMING**

By attending the event, you consent to being photographed and filmed by approved event contractors and consent to the commercial use of the content for advertising, marketing and social media purposes. If you do not want your image to be used, please email a clear photograph of yourself to [enquiries@thebigdesigngroup.com](mailto:enquiries@thebigdesigngroup.com) in advance of the event, detailing your name and the event that you are attending.

# Accessibility

#### DISABILITY ACCESS 

The Royal Exhibition Building is wheelchair accessible. All exhibitors are located on the ground level.  

#### TOILETS  

Toilets are located at multiple convenient points within the venue. Wheelchair-accessible toilets are available in both locations. Staff at the information desk can provide directions to facilities available to visitors within the venue.

### Sensory Information

CHILL-OUT ZONE

We have worked with _[Amaze](https://www.amaze.org.au/)_, the peak body for autistic people and their supporters in Victoria, to undertake an environmental audit of _The Big Design Market Melbourne._ We worked with _Amaze_ to identify ways to improve the visitor experience for individuals with sensory sensitivities. You can find information below about our Quiet Zone along with the best times to visit _The Big Design Market._

For general information about The Big Design Market and what to expect, please visit [About Us](https://melbourne.thebigdesignmarket.com/info/about-us/).

#### WHEN TO VISIT

To enjoy the market in a quieter and more relaxed setting we recommend attending on Friday, after midday. Saturday around lunch time and Sunday tend to be our busiest times.

#### QUIET ZONE

A quiet zone is available within the venue where visitors can sit away from the main thoroughfares and busy eating areas. This area is lit with house lights only, so will be slightly darker and quieter than the rest of the event. Some seating is provided and visitors are also welcome to sit on the floor picnic-style. Please pick up a visitor map at the information desk when you arrive.

#### KIDS AREA

There is a dedicated area for kids activities at the back of the event where children and their families can participate in calming activities including crafts and colouring-in. Coffee and snacks are easily accessible next to the Kids Area.

#### BUYING TICKETS 

Tickets are available for purchase online prior to the event. You can also purchase tickets at the door using credit/debit card. Please note, The Big Design Market is a cashless event. There are several ticket points so queuing will be minimal. 

#### AVOIDING QUEUES

There may be a queue when the doors open but it usually moves quickly and you'll be through the doors within a few minutes. Check event details for opening times each day.

#### FEEDBACK

We'd love to hear your feedback on how we can improve your experience at _The Big Design Market_. Please email us on [enquiries@thebigdesignmarket.com](mailto:enquiries@thebigdesignmarket.com?subject=Sensory-friendy%20event%20feedback)

## Plan your Ballarat weekend

### Getting there

**By train:** V/Line runs from Southern Cross Station to Ballarat Station, in the centre of town, in under 90 minutes.

**By car:** about 90 minutes from Melbourne's CBD, 110km along the Western Freeway.

**From the airport:** about 60 minutes by road from Tullamarine or Avalon.

### Where the venues are

• **Civic Hall:** 300–304 Mair Street, Ballarat Central | approx. 6 minute walk from Ballarat Railway Station  
• **Ballarat Mining Exchange:** 12–16 Lydiard Street North, Ballarat Central |  approx. 5 minute walk from Ballarat Railway Station  
• **Ballaarat Mechanics Institute:** 117–119 Sturt Street, Ballarat Central | approx. 8 minute walk from Ballarat Railway Station  
• **Federation University's Post Office Box Theatre:** Camp Street Campus, corner of Sturt Street and Lydiard Street South, Ballarat Central | approx. 13 minute walk from Ballarat Railway Station  
• **Ballarat Performing Arts Centre:** 501–503 Neill Street, Soldiers Hill | approx. 15 minute walk from Ballarat Railway Station

[More on getting to and around Ballarat](https://www.visitballarat.com.au/plan-your-trip/getting-to-ballarat)

## Frequently Asked Questions

## 

When and where is Fringe Encore: Ballarat?

Thursday 22 to Sunday 25 October 2026, at five venues in Ballarat: Civic Hall, Ballarat Mining Exchange, Ballaarat Mechanics Institute, Federation University's Post Office Box Theatre and Ballarat Performing Arts Centre.

## 

What is Fringe Encore: Ballarat?

A four-day season presented by Melbourne Fringe Festival in Ballarat, the week after the Melbourne season (29 September to 18 October 2026). Twelve shows play, including three that appear only in Ballarat this Festival.

## 

Which shows can I only see in Ballarat?

Degustation (world premiere), Fountain Lakes: Y2K (Victorian premiere) and Sammy J – Hero Complex (one night only).

## 

Do I need a ticket for every show?

Every show is ticketed except Ocker, which is free with no booking. Each show is booked separately on its own event page.

## 

How do I get to Ballarat from Melbourne?

V/Line trains run from Southern Cross Station to Ballarat Station in under 90 minutes. By car it is about 90 minutes along the Western Freeway. 

Check estimated travel times on Google Maps. For more info, contact the Ballarat Visitor Information Centre on 1800 44 66 33 or email [hello@visitballarat.com.au](mailto:hello@visitballarat.com.au)

## 

Is there anything for kids?

Family Friendly Shows:

*   Harold Holt: The Man, The Myth, The Pool
*   Murder in the Market: A Murder Village Improvised Whodunnit
*   Ocker

Please check individual event pages for detailed content and event warnings.

## 

Who do I contact about bookings or access?

Melbourne Fringe box office: 03 9660 9666, Monday to Sunday, 11am to 7pm, or boxoffice@melbournefringe.com.au

## **Axil Coffee x The Big Design Market 'Almost Winter' - Free Coffee for A Year Competition - Terms & Conditions**

#### Giveaway period: 22nd May 2026 - 11:59pm AEST 24th May 2026.

Promoters: This Instagram giveaway is conducted by Coffee Co-Op PTY LTD (ABN 28 967 234 025) trading as Axil Coffee Roasters ("Axil Coffee", "we", "us", "our") and The Big Design Market Pty Ltd ABN 80 443 946 458

### Promotion Period

The promotion commences on 22nd May and closes on 24th May at 11:59pm AEST.  ("Promotion Period").

### Eligibility

*   Entry is open to Australian residents who are currently residing in Australia.
    
*   Entrants must be 16 or older to enter, in compliance with Australian social media regulations.
    
*   Employees, directors, and contractors of Coffee Co-Op PTY LTD (trading as Axil Coffee Roasters) and their immediate families are ineligible to enter.
    
*   By entering, entrants confirm they meet all other eligibility requirements.
    

### How to Enter

To enter the promotion, entrants must:

1.  To purchase any drink from Axil at the upcoming Almost Winter Big Design Market and post a photo of your cup on your stories 
    
2.  Follow both @axilcoffeeroasters and @bigdesignmarket 
    
3.  Like this competition post 
    
4.  Enter during the aforementioned Promotion Period. 
    

Entries made outside the Promotion Period will not be accepted. There are no limits to the number of entries. Every purchase made at the Almost Winter Big Design Market and posted on stories equates to one entry. Entries not captured due to privacy settings are void. Image or video must be taken at the Big Design Market - Almost Winter.

### Prize Details

The prize consists of:

*   Twelve (12) months supply of Axil Coffee, being one (1) x small coffee per day, with alternative milk of choice or full cream/skim dairy milk.
    
*   Coffee can be dine in or takeaway, and must be purchased at one of the 17 Axil Coffee locations across Australia.
    
*   Total prize value: $2,263 approx.
    

Prize Conditions:

*   The prize is non-transferable and non-exchangeable.
    
*   The prize cannot be redeemed for cash.
    
*   The coffee order must be from Axil Coffee's current available range.
    
*   Coffee can be redeemed for 12 months commencing from the day following delivery of the card.
    
*   The Promoter accepts no responsibility for any variation in prize value.
    

### Winner Selection and Notification

*   The winner will be selected via Instagram Direct Messages upon inspection of captured Instagram story.  
    
*   The winner will be notified by instagram DM within (2) business days of the draw.
    
*   The winner must respond within seven (7) days of notification to claim their prize.
    
*   If the winner cannot be contacted, does not respond within the specified timeframe, or does not meet eligibility requirements, the Promoter reserves the right to select an alternative winner by redraw.
    
*   The winner's name and state/territory of residence may be published on Axil Coffee's website and social media channels.
    

### Prize Delivery

*   The Free Coffee VIP card will be delivered to the winning entrant by postal delivery following the communication of their postal address details. The winning entrant may also wish to collect the Free Coffee VIP card from any Axil cafe. 
    
*   The winner is responsible for providing accurate delivery details.
    
*   The Promoter is not responsible for any lost, stolen, or damaged prizes once delivered.
    

### Privacy

*   Personal information collected will be used for the purpose of conducting this promotion and may be used for future marketing purposes in accordance with the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth).

*   The Promoter reserves the right to verify the validity of all entries and to disqualify any entrant who fails to follow Instagram's terms of service or provides false information.
    

### General

*   Entry into this promotion constitutes acceptance of these terms and conditions.

# Information for parents

#### KIDS ACTIVITIES

The kids activities area is open each day of the market. You can find all the details about our fun activities for kids [here](https://melbourne.thebigdesignmarket.com/see-and-do/for-kids/kids-activities/).

#### QUIET ZONE

A Quiet Zone is available within the venue specifically for visitors who require access to a low-sensory space. For directions or a visitor map, please ask one of our staff at the information desk (located at the Nicholson St entrance). [More information >>](https://melbourne.thebigdesignmarket.com/info/accessibility/)

#### FOOD AND DRINKS

A selection of food and beverage stands are located next to the kids' area. More food options are available in the main catering area located at the centre of the venue. See all available food options [here](https://melbourne.thebigdesignmarket.com/see-and-do/eat-drink/).

A microwave is available for baby food and bottle warming in the Parents Lounge. (see below)

#### PARENTS LOUNGE

Parents are welcome to feed their babies wherever they feel comfortable. A private space is available if preferred. You can find the parent's lounge near the toilets close to the Nicholson St entrance to the event. This private space is equipped with comfortable chairs and a microwave for bottle warming.

If you require further information or directions once you arrive at the event, staff at the information desk will be happy to help.

#### BABY CHANGE FACILITIES

Dedicated baby change facilities are located within the accessible toilets to the left of the Nicholson St entrance and next to the toilets at the back of the venue behind the kids area.

INFORMATION

If you require further information prior to the event, please don't hesitate to [contact our team](mailto:enquiries@thebigdesigngroup.com).

Brunswick Music Festival | Melbourne's Iconic Fest Returns in 2027

Navigation

Brunswick Music Festival

Search

Brunswick Music Festival returns from **28 February to 7 March 2027**, bringing a week of live music, community celebration, and unforgettable performances to Merri-bek. Save the date and stay tuned for program announcements. [Sign up to our EDM to stay in the loop.](https://ems.gs/3bclf0kbhiXe)

Special Projects Expressions of Interest Now Open

![](/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.sanity.io%2Fimages%2Fqynhxqky%2Fproduction%2F2c843d972125880090cb3c4cb083d129d52c8933-5000x3333.jpg&w=2560&q=75)

Brunswick Music Festival is now accepting expressions of interest (EOIs) for special projects or events for inclusion in our 2027 Program. We want to hear your big ideas. We’re looking for exciting show concepts, venue take-overs, full concert lines ups, special music projects, the creation of new work, album releases, or other ideas that can happen only in a festival context.

Key Dates

*   Expressions of Interest Open: Monday 10 August 2026
*   Online EOI Information Session: Thursday 20 August 2026, 6:00pm to 7:00pm. [Click Here to Register](https://events.teams.microsoft.com/event/ff8e8dea-679a-4abb-8f24-7a586cdb3e11@fd1e4787-5974-4ae8-ac86-93ab2fd52107)[.](https://events.teams.microsoft.com/event/e6bb3ace-3ba7-4b04-8ffc-d5e6c63fa16e@fd1e4787-5974-4ae8-ac86-93ab2fd52107)
*   Expressions of Interest Close: 11:59 pm, Sunday 13 September 2026

[Learn More](https://merribekcitycouncil.snapforms.com.au/form/brunswick-music-festival-2027---special-projects-eoi)

**Brunswick Music Festival Welcomes New Programmer El Chantry**

![](/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.sanity.io%2Fimages%2Fqynhxqky%2Fproduction%2F5025af6c3011b557f68ecbd9ec32d1480684bb23-1169x886.jpg&w=2560&q=75)

Merri-bek City Council is pleased to announce the appointment of El Chantry as the new Programmer for Brunswick Music Festival.

El Chantry is the Programming Manager at Melbourne Recital Centre, where she has curated the Centre's contemporary music program since 2018.

With more than 15 years' experience across music programming, festival production, partnership development and creative leadership, her career has included roles with Melbourne Music Week, Creative Partnerships Australia and Gertrude Street Projection Festival.

"As both a music programmer and a proud Brunswick resident, I have long admired Brunswick Music Festival for its ability to bring people together and genuinely celebrate the diversity of our community." -**El Chantry**

Event Information

When do Pitch passes go on sale?

\[+\]

\[-\]

The Pitch Collective presale opens Monday October 26th at 6PM AEDT.

The Official Presale follows on Tuesday October 27th at 6PM AEDT.

General public access opens Wednesday October 28th at 12PM AEDT.

What is the Pitch Collective and how do I know if I'm in it?

\[+\]

\[-\]

The Pitch Collective is made for people who back Pitch before anyone tells them to. 

‍

It's a group for _Revellers_ who signed up off the back of our ninth iteration, and _Alumni_ who've signed up ready to reunite with us for our tenth. . If that’s you, you’re in. You’ll have the opportunity to secure your ticket ahead of the Offical Presale. The Pitch Collective Presale opens Monday October 26th at 6pm AEDT.

‍

You should have already received an email confirming your spot. If you can’t find it, check your spam folder as it may have landed there.

‍

If you believe you qualify but didn't receive this, you can contact the Pitch team at hello@pitchfestival.com.au.

‍

A limited allocation of tickets will be available in the Pitch Collective Presale. All ticket types will be available, including bundles. To reward our community’s support and dedication, a small allocation of individual vehicle passes will be available to purchase in this specific Presale only. After the Pitch Collective Presale, Vehicle Passes will only be available to purchase in a bundle. Individual vehicle passes, including GA, Glamping, Premium, and Car Park Passes, may be available to purchase individually in a separate onsale, later in the year.

Who is on the programme?

\[+\]

\[-\]

Arriving soon.

Where is Pitch Music & Arts?

\[+\]

\[-\]

Pitch Music & Arts is located at 1330 Moyston Dunkeld Road, Mafeking 3379.

‍

The coordinates are 37°22'13.0"S, 142°40'14.1"E.

‍

Do you have payment plans available?

\[+\]

\[-\]

Payment plans such as [Afterpay](https://www.afterpay.com/en-AU/how-it-works), [Zip Pay](https://megatix.com.au/about-zip) and Laybuy are available from all Presales. Find out more in the Information section of our website. 

Is Pitch BYO?

\[+\]

\[-\]

Yes, Pitch Music & Arts is BYO alcohol. Please limit yourself to 24 cans or 1 bottle of spirits, and drink responsibly.

‍

Please note, glass is banned, if you are bringing a bottle of spirits this must be decanted into a reusable water bottle.  
‍

For those seeking drink mixers, there will be non-alcoholic and mocktail bar offerings on site.

Does my festival entry pass include camping?

\[+\]

\[-\]

Yes. Your Festival Entry Pass grants you access to the festival and includes access to the general campgrounds.

‍

You're welcome to elevate your stay should a more luxurious experience appeal to you. Camping upgrades are purchased separately, in addition to your Festival Entry Ticket.

‍

The date on your ticket is the earliest you're allowed on site.

‍

What time can I enter Pitch?

\[+\]

\[-\]

The gate times for Pitch Music & Arts are:

‍

Friday 5th: 9:00am - 11:00pm 

Saturday 6th: 9:00am - 10:00pm

Sunday 7th: 9:00am - 8:00pm

Monday 8th: 9:00am - 4:00pm

‍

If you arrive past gate closing time, there will be no guarantee that you will be able to enter. Please plan your journey accordingly to avoid disappointment.

## Acknowledgement

## Pitch Music & Arts is held on the sacred lands of the Djab Wurrung and Eastern Maar peoples. Traditional Custodians of the Country that has held us across ten iterations. We are deeply privileged to gather here, at the foothills of Gariwerd, on a Country of profound cultural and spiritual significance where ancient stories and songlines remain embedded in the landscape.We recognise while Pitch marks ten years here, the culture and custodianship of this Country extends across generations beyond measure.

#### The Grampians

Pitch Music & Arts takes place on the lands of the Djabwurrung people. We ask guests to walk respectively and be humbled by the enormity of their cultural expression.

## Our Story

> We’re redefining how the world shops, one handmade product at a time.

The Finders Keepers is Australia’s most loved design market, dedicated to supporting small, independent makers and championing conscious consumerism.

![](img/page-images/our-story/FK-Melb-AW23-Samee-Lapham-highres-311.jpg)

![](img/staff/team-photo.jpg)

![](img/page-images/our-story/FK-Syd-AW24-Photo-Samee-Lapham_highres-410.jpg)

![](img/page-images/our-story/FK-Syd-AW24-Photo-Samee-Lapham_highres-185.jpg)

![](img/page-images/our-story/FK-Syd-AW24-Photo-Samee-Lapham_highres-064.jpg)

![](img/page-images/our-story/FK-Melb-SS22-Samee-Lapham-HR_332.jpg)

![](img/page-images/our-story/FK-Melb-AW23-Samee-Lapham-highres-311.jpg)

![](img/staff/team-photo.jpg)

Since 2008, we’ve been the go-to destination for unique, handmade wares, where shoppers meet makers and connect over creativity.

Our mission is to empower Australian makers to thrive while building a future where shopping does the least harm to the planet. By offering resources, a platform for small businesses, and an inclusive space to shop sustainably, we’re redefining how the world shops, one handmade product at a time.

> Join us in celebrating creativity, connection, and mindful consumption.

### We've been supporting small since 2008!

### $1.2 million

Average spent by market-goers each year supporting independent creative businesses.

### 2,800+

Australian independent, creative businesses supported by us each year.

Born in 2008 from the side hustle of friends Sarah Thornton and Brooke Johnston, The Finders Keepers has grown into Australia's most-loved design market, each year hosting festival-style markets in Sydney and Melbourne.

In early 2024, Sarah and Brooke handed over the reins of The Finders Keepers to the Winarch Group, gaining a little sister market in the Olive Tree Market based in Newcastle. Winarch Group is very much driven by connecting communities and providing more opportunities and experiences for individuals and businesses through their events and tourism projects.

Want to know more?

Follow The Finders Keepers' journey on [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/thefinderskeepersmarket), [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/theFindersKeepers/) and [TikTok](https://www.tiktok.com/@thefinderskeepersmarket) or sign up to our [mailing list](https://thefinderskeepers.com/mailing-list.html) to see what's next. You can [meet our passionate team here](https://thefinderskeepers.com/meet-the-team.html)!

Ticketing Information

The Pitch™ Essentials

\[+\]

\[-\]

We understand not everyone has time to pore over the finer details, so here's the bottom line on getting yourself to Pitch Music & Arts.

‍

The Pitch Collective presale opens Monday October 26th at 6PM AEDT.

The Official Presale follows on Tuesday October 27th at 6PM AEDT.

General public access opens Wednesday October 28th at 12PM AEDT.

‍

**_EVERYONE_** needs a Festival Entry Ticket. This is your way in. It grants you access to General Camping. The date on your ticket is the earliest you're allowed on site.

‍

You're welcome to elevate your stay should a more luxurious experience appeal to you. Camping upgrades are purchased separately, in addition to your Festival Entry Ticket:

‍

Premium Camp: upgraded toilets, showers, phone charging, express entry & shade

‍

Pre-pitched: pre-pitched tent with a mattress and sleeping bag ready to go, 2–4 people, sold per tent.

‍

Glamping: Classic, Deluxe, Top-Tier tents, 2-4 people, sold per tent

‍

We encourage you to consider renting your camping gear rather than buying it. Wallaroo Camping can furnish you with everything from tents to trestle tables. No need to invest in equipment destined for single use.

‍

**What Megatix will ask you for at checkout - and everyone else's, if you're buying for the group**

*   Full name
*   Email
*   Phone number
*   Emergency contact details

Have this ready and checkout takes two minutes.

‍

**Getting there**

Driving is the most direct option but there are fewer Car Passes than there are campers, on purpose. The land can't hold every single car, and neither can the roads through Ararat and Moyston. So if you're bringing a car, your best shot is grabbing a Festival & Vehicle Pass Package, four Festival passes plus one Vehicle Pass, bundled together. It's the only way to secure a Vehicle Pass in the initial onsale.

‍

Individual Vehicle Passes go on sale later in the year, but they're limited so please don't bank on it.

‍

We implore you to use our Pitch Charter Bus or Ararat Shuttle straight to site. No designated driver to arrange, no fuel to budget for, and no dust to contend with. We'd suggest securing your seat early as buses tend to sell out early.

‍

Mobtix

\[+\]

\[-\]

Pitch Music & Arts is honoured to gather on Djab Wurrung and Eastern Maar Country at the foothills of Gariwerd, paying respect to Elders past and present and the enduring care of Traditional Custodians. In recognition of this unbroken connection to Country, MobTix provides complimentary or discounted tickets to Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander peoples across Untitled Group events, with allocations guided by community connection.

‍

**How to apply?**

‍

This year, we have refreshed the MobTix program to better protect its integrity and help ensure tickets reach the right people. The new Untitled Group MobTix Community introduces a one-time registration and verification process, with memberships reviewed before approval. The change has been carefully shaped in consultation with Aboriginal community representatives from various Nations to support cultural safety and ensure the program continues to work for mob. Verification does not need to be an official certificate, with accepted options outlined in the registration form.

‍

If you have already registered for the Untitled Group MobTix Community through another festival: You do not need to register again. Email hello@pitchfestival.com.au with your first name, last name, mob and MobTix Community ID, and our team will submit your existing profile for consideration as part of the Pitch allocation.

‍

If you have not registered before: Email hello@pitchfestival.com.au with your name and community connection and we will send you the registration form. Once approved, your profile will be submitted for consideration as part of the Pitch Music & Arts 2027 MobTix allocation.

‍

Once approved for the Untitled Group MobTix Community, you will not need to register again for future Untitled Group events. If you have any questions or are unsure whether you have already registered, email hello@pitchfestival.com.au and our MobTix team will be able to help with your enquiry.

‍

From there, for MobTix at any future Untitled Group event, just reach out to the relevant event team directly.

Refund Policy

\[+\]

\[-\]

Pitch Music & Arts has a strict no refund policy. If you can no longer attend, you will have the option to list your ticket on Tixel for resale. Tixel is our only authorised resale platform.

Name On Tickets Policy

\[+\]

\[-\]

To ensure the validity of your ticket, Pitch Music & Arts has a strict name on ticket policy - your ticket details must match your ID. This applies for all tickets including:

*   Festival Pass
*   Vehicle Passes
*   Camping Upgrade Tickets (Premium Camp, Pre-Pitched, Glamping)

You can now update the name on your ticket directly through Megatix for a small fee.

‍

**Important things to note, please read carefully**

*   Each ticket is only eligible for one name change via Megatix.
*   If the name on the ticket needs to be changed more than once, this must be done via Tixel once official resale opens. Resale will open six weeks before the festival, or earlier if the event sells out.
*   Name changes are intended for genuine transfers between friends or family. We strongly discourage using this process for private resale. Funds exchanged privately (via bank transfer, cash, etc.) are not protected in the event of a dispute or event cancellation, as per our Terms & Conditions.
*   If you arrive at the festival with a ticket that does not match your ID, you will be required to pay a name correction fee at the box office.

**How to change the name on your ticket (via Megatix)**

1.  Log in to your Megatix account
2.  Navigate to My Tickets
3.  Select the relevant ticket
4.  Click Update Details
5.  Carefully update the details of the friend or family member you're transferring the ticket to, including their name, DOB, email address, phone number and emergency contact information
6.  Enter payment information
7.  Once payment has been made, you will be redirected to your original order screen and an updated copy of your order, including the newly named ticket, will be emailed to you.

‍

It is your responsibility to forward the newly named ticket to your new attendee.

Accessibility

\[+\]

\[-\]

Pitch sits on flat terrain, a mix of grassed and dirt areas across a working farm, meaning the land can throw up some challenges underfoot, particularly for those with mobility disabilities or impairments, and especially in harsh weather.

‍

Our Accessible Campground puts you close to the main arena, with accessible toilets and showers on hand.

‍

At checkout, flag any accessibility requirements through our custom questions, and we'll follow up with the details you need. Post-purchase, you'll receive a form to let us know who's camping with you, so we can set up your site accordingly, then check in with staff on arrival so we can confirm everything's sorted for you.

‍

Accessible toilets are also available in the Main Arena throughout the festival.

‍

**PEEP**: Please fill in a copy of your Personal Emergency Evacuation Plan prior to the festival. [Downloadable link here.](https://www.first5minutes.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/PEEP-Form.pdf) 

‍

**Accessibility Guide:** Check back here closer to the event for our Pitch 2027 Accessibility Guide.

‍

**Companion Cards**

If you have a carer who would like to attend Pitch Music & Arts with you, they can access a complimentary Companion Card Ticket.

You can take these steps when purchasing your ticket. 

1.  Firstly, select your desired entry ticket.
2.  Proceed to check-out.
3.  After purchasing tickets, please check the provided box, where you’re able to advise whether you have any accessible requirements. 
4.  Agree to the Terms and Conditions before proceeding.
5.  Once you have submitted all your information, your tickets will be emailed to you. 
6.  A questionnaire will be sent to the provided email address, that allows you to outline your accessible requirements. This also allows you to secure a companion card ticket online, by filling in your companion card holder details. 

‍

Please note that if you can not provide Companion Card details at this time, feel free to contact us as [accessibility@untitledgroup.com.au](mailto:accessibility@untitledgroup.com.au) and you’ll be able to secure one at the Box Office on the day of the event.

Health & Wellbeing

\[+\]

\[-\]

**Crowd Care**

Think of our Crowd Care team as your Pitch older siblings; there to look out for you. Trained in health and care, they're equipped to help with anything from feeling unwell or lost, to needing a calm presence when things feel like a lot.

‍

Find them at Helper Hubs or roaming the grounds in purple, or spot our purple star doof stick in the arena if you need support.

‍

**Medical Assistance**

Our Medical Tent is staffed 24 hours a day, judgement-free and fully confidential, there for you or anyone around you, whenever it's needed. Check your site map so you know exactly where to find us.

‍

Your health comes first all weekend. Stay hydrated, eat properly, rest when you need to, and know your limits. Have fun, but look out for each other and yourself.

‍

There will be onsite alcohol and drug testing, helping drivers make safe, informed choices for the journey home. One free test is available for Vehicle Pass holders.

‍

**Where can I find help at Pitch?**

*   The medical tent
*   Your nearest Helper Hub
*   Crowd Care Staff who are roaming the site
*   Lux concierge

**‍**

**Police**

Victoria Police will be present on site and in surrounding areas for the full run of Pitch Music & Arts 2027, working to keep patrons and road users safe throughout the weekend and beyond.

‍

If you need police assistance, approach them directly, or speak to event staff or security, who can arrange it for you.

‍

We'll be actively identifying anyone trafficking drugs on site. If you have information, report it anonymously to Crimestoppers on 1800 333 000, or let police on site know what you've observed.

‍

Booze and drug buses will be operating as you leave the festival. If you've taken anything that could impair your driving, don't get behind the wheel.

‍

**Emergency**

In an emergency, follow instructions from event staff; leave your belongings behind, and anything else that might slow you down.

‍

Keep an eye on the Info Board in the arena for warnings or important updates throughout the weekend.

‍

**Prescription Medication**

You're welcome to bring medication for medical purposes. Please carry a copy of your prescription and photo ID to show staff and security at the gates.

‍

Any medication that needs to be refrigerated can be kept at the medical tent.

Getting There

\[+\]

\[-\]

**Bus**

Every full bus takes approximately 17 cars off the road.  Save yourself the drive, reduce emissions and be a part of the experience by taking the Pitch bus from Melbourne’s CBD.

‍

We have various options, including the Pitch Charter Bus, departing from Carlton Gardens, the Ararat Shuttle Bus running to and from Ararat Station, or Private Bus Passes for those who wish to organise their own private charter with their group. You may purchase your bus pass via Melbourne on the Move.

‍

‍**Driving**

While this will be the most direct way to travel to and from the event, please consider how you can minimise your carbon footprint through your choice of transport, and the responsibility that comes with being a designated driver. It is expected that groups attempt to travel together, rather than in various separate cars.

‍

While each journey will take varying times depending on your starting point, we recommend taking the following route if travelling from Melbourne.

‍

**Melton Highway towards Ballarat, continuing onto Western Highway.**

‍

If you are driving to Pitch and wish to camp next to your vehicle, then you will require a Vehicle Pass. Vehicle Passes must be purchased separately from your festival pass.

‍

With every Vehicle Pass purchased, you’ll receive a complimentary Saliva Drug Test.

‍

*   Those camping in General Camp must purchase a GA Vehicle Pass
*   Those camping in Premium Camp must purchase a Premium Vehicle Pass
*   Those camping in Pre-Pitched must purchase a GA Vehicle Pass
*   Those glamping, must purchase a Glamping Vehicle Pass.
*   If you wish to drive to Pitch, and park your car in the internal car park, you may purchase a Car Park Pass.

If you wish to tow a Trailer or Caravan, you will need a Trailer Pass Add On.

‍

GA Camping and Premium Camping Vehicle Passes will be available during Presale, where you can purchase one of our 4-Day Festival Entry and Vehicle Pass bundles. The bundle includes 4x Festival Entry passes.

‍

With this bundle, we hope to encourage more of our patrons to carpool together, and achieve a more sustainable impact on our environment. This is the only way you’re able to purchase a Vehicle Pass during initial On Sale, and is your best chance at securing one for the festival.

‍

The Festival & Vehicle Pass Bundle allows you and your group to purchase your Car Pass, in conjunction with your GA or Premium Festival Passes. This package is your best chance at securing a Vehicle Pass to Pitch.

‍

**Drop Off/Pick Up**

If you have organised for someone to drop you off/pick you up from Pitch they will be directed to the designated drop off/pick up point upon arrival - you won’t need to purchase a ticket for this.

‍

Please note, the person driving you will not be able to enter the campgrounds with their car - you must carry your belongings from the drop off point to your campsite.

Helper Hubs are the heart of every campground. A central meeting point staffed 24 hours a day, ready to help with whatever you need. Shade, sunscreen, directions, or just a good chat;, they can do it all.

‍

Each Hub is colour-coded to match its campground, and works hand in hand with our Crowd Care team. Need support at any point? Head to your local Hub and find a friendly face.

Passouts

\[+\]

\[-\]

Pitch Music & Arts has a strict no passouts policy. This is to reduce the vehicle movement on site and to ensure a safe experience for all attendees. If you would like to leave the festival early you are permitted to do so. However, once you leave you will not be able to re-enter.

Lost & Found

\[+\]

\[-\]

Lost and found property is managed at your local Helper Hub, with all items transported to the Main Helper Hub near the General Store daily. Please report all lost items to Hub Staff as soon as you can, and check the Main Hub before leaving the festival to reunite with your lost items. Please visit before 12pm on Tuesday March 9, as all lost property will be transported off-site after this time. 

‍

After the festival, a lost property form will become available here and on our socials for you to report any lost items. If your item has been found, you will be contacted to arrange pick up or postage at your expense. Lost items can be picked up in Melbourne or posted from March 12, 2027. Items not collected/claimed by March 23, 2027, will be appropriately disposed of or donated.

‍

Only items of value (phones, wallets, identification and car/house keys) will be held, as well as items containing identification. Clothing items, backpacks/duffel/handbags, accessories, jewellery, makeup, fragrances etc will not be kept after the event. If items are not collected on or before this date, items will be appropriately disposed of or donated.

‍

Banned Items

\[+\]

\[-\]

To ensure the safety of everyone at Pitch Music & Arts the following items are banned:

Glass

*   Glass bottles (whether it be a bottle of alcohol or a reusable water bottle)
*   Glass jars (Vegemite, salsa etc)
*   Any sort of class container used for either food or storage

Fire (throughout the festival there will be a total fire ban)

*   Flairs, fireworks, sparklers
*   Camp fires‍
*   If you are found in possession of these items or a fire has been started at your campsite you will be immediately ejected from the event.

Gas cooking equipment

*   Gas bottles
*   Camping stoves and BBQs

Electronic devices

*   Large sound systems/Speakers bigger than 11 x 5 x 5 inches (we want your campsite to be a vibe, so smaller portable speakers like a UE Boom or JBL Charge 5 are fine)
*   Drones
*   Generators
*   Professional photography equipment/sound and visual recording equipment, recording glasses
*   Lasers

Furniture

*   Couches
*   Non-demountable tables

Illicit substances

*   Illegal and/or dangerous weapons
*   Any items that are deemed dangerous by staff or security will be confiscated and may result in you being ejected from the festival
*   Whipped cream chargers and canisters (otherwise known as ‘nangs’)

‍

When you arrive at Pitch Music & Arts your vehicle will be searched for any of the above items, if any items are found they will be confiscated. There is no guarantee that confiscated item/s will be returned to you upon leaving the event.

‍

For a full list of banned items please refer to our terms and conditions.

‍

Trespassing

\[+\]

\[-\]

As an independent company curating a festival for our community, we find it especially disheartening when community members attempt to trespass at Pitch Music & Arts. Not only is trespassing disrespectful to us as a festival, but also to those who have paid for their ticket,.

‍

Anyone found fence jumping or on site without a wristband will be escorted out of the event and may be prosecuted by Victoria Police and will have a lifetime ban from attending all future events.

FAQs

How do I know if I’m in the Pitch Collective?

\[+\]

\[-\]

The Pitch Collective is made for people who back Pitch before anyone tells them to. 

‍

It's a group for _Revellers_ who signed up off the back of our ninth iteration, and _Alumni_ who've signed up ready to reunite with us for our tenth. If that’s you, you’re in. You’ll have the opportunity to secure your ticket ahead of the Offical Presale. The Pitch Collective Presale opens Monday, October 26th at 6pm AEDT.

‍

You should have already received an email confirming your spot. If you can’t find it, check your spam folder, as it may have landed there.

‍

If you believe you qualify but didn't receive this, you can contact the Pitch team at hello@pitchfestival.com.au.

Is Pitch 18+?

\[+\]

\[-\]

Pitch Music & Arts is strictly 18+.

Do you offer complimentary birthday passes?

\[+\]

\[-\]

We don't offer complimentary birthday passes, but we'd love nothing more than to celebrate yours alongside our own 10th birthday right there with you.

Is Pitch BYO?

\[+\]

\[-\]

Yes, Pitch Music & Arts is BYO alcohol. Please limit yourself to 24 cans or 1 bottle of spirits per person.

‍

Please note, glass is banned, if you are bringing a bottle of spirits this must be decanted into a reusable water bottle.

‍

I’m experiencing ticketing issues

\[+\]

\[-\]

For any ticketing related enquiries, please contact [Megatix Support](https://megatix.com.au/support) and they will be able to assist.

What should I bring to Pitch?

\[+\]

\[-\]

If you're unsure of what to bring to Pitch, please see suggestions below:

‍

*   Tickets printed or downloaded to your device
*   Valid ID 
*   Bank cards (This is a cash-free event) 
*   Any required medication 
*   Sunscreen 
*   Toiletries 
*   Insect repellent
*   A towel
*   Pillow, sleeping bag and air mattress
*   Tent (with extra pegs)
*   Camping chair 
*   Esky/cooler and snacks 
*   Trolley (to transport esky or chairs into the arena, or to move items from the drop-off zone)
*   Handheld fan
*   A torch
*   Ear plugs
*   A reusable water bottle
*   A warm jacket
*   Clothes or hot and cold weather  
*   Extra pairs of socks
*   Closed-toe shoes 
*   Reusable water bottle
*   A hat 
*   Portable phone charger

‍

No tent? Select one of our Eco Camp or Glamping upgrade options, or rent your gear on site [here](https://www.wallaroocampinghire.com/pma.html).

Who is on the programme?

\[+\]

\[-\]

Arriving soon.

Does my Festival Entry Pass include camping?

\[+\]

\[-\]

When purchasing a Festival Entry Pass, you’re also gaining access to the General Camping area. If you wish to upgrade your camping experience, you can do so with our Premium or Glamping add-ons.

What times can I enter the festival?

\[+\]

\[-\]

The gate times for Pitch Music & Arts are:

‍

Friday 5th: 9:00am - 11:00pm 

Saturday 6th: 9:00am - 10:00pm

Sunday 7th: 9:00am - 8:00pm

Monday 8th: 9:00am - 4:00pm

‍

If you arrive past gate closing time, there will be no guarantee that you will be able to enter. Please plan your journey accordingly to avoid disappointment.

‍

Can I arrive later than my Festival Entry Pass permits?

\[+\]

\[-\]

Yes, however, you can not arrive earlier than the date on your Festival Pass.  

Can I get dropped off?

\[+\]

\[-\]

Being dropped off is the least sustainable option to arrive at Pitch. We implore you to carpool, or choose one of our various bus options. If you must be dropped off by a friend or family member, there will be a permitted drop off/pick up point. 

‍

If you are being dropped off by a privately organised bus, you will be dropped off at the bus drop off/pick up point.

‍

Am I allowed to bring a caravan or campervan?

\[+\]

\[-\]

Yes, you may bring a campervan, caravan or RV to Pitch. A vehicle pass must be purchased alongside your festival ticket. If your Campervan is on a trailer, make sure to select the Trailer Pass add on when purchasing your Vehicle Pass.

‍

Please note, your van will not have access to any power or water throughout the weekend, including wastewater dump points.

‍

Any banned items, including gas bottles, must be removed from the vehicle before arriving at Pitch Music & Arts. If you’re hiring a car or campervan, please check with your rental company that they can be removed before selecting your vehicle.

Will there be any rideshare options in the area?

\[+\]

\[-\]

[Ararat Taxi service](http://ararattaxi.com/) will be running transfers from Ararat to the Festival. Please try to book ahead or get in contact with them at [ararattaxiservices@gmail.com](mailto:ararattaxiservices@gmail.com) or Telephone Bookings: (03) 5352 2233 & Telephone Enquiries: (03) 5352 2300

‍

Will there be WiFi/reception?

\[+\]

\[-\]

We'll have a temporary Cell on Wheels to boost connectivity on site. This means improved cellular activity across the grounds, though given our home in the heart of the Grampians, a few patchy pockets are still to be expected.

‍

Wifi will also be available to purchase at the Main Info Hub, with more details to come closer to the event.

‍

Will there be ice available to purchase?

\[+\]

\[-\]

Bags of ice will be sold from the General Store to keep your food & drinks ice cold.

Are plastic water bottles banned?

\[+\]

\[-\]

Plastic water bottles are not permitted at Pitch. We strongly encourage all patrons to bring reusable water bottles for the weekend.

When does the Pitch site need to be vacated?

\[+\]

\[-\]

The Pitch site will need to be vacated by 12PM on Tuesday the 9th of March. We encourage you to stay Monday night if you need more time to rest and recover before your journey home.

What is Pitch doing for the local surrounds, the community and the environment?

\[+\]

\[-\]

If you're interested in community and sustainability initiatives, how to reduce your own footprint at Pitch, and understanding Pitch Music & Arts' connection to Country, please visit the [Respect for Place](https://www.pitchfestival.com.au/respect-for-place) page.

How do I apply for a Community Grant?

\[+\]

\[-\]

Community Grant guidelines for 2027 will be announced shortly. The next round will open on February 1st 2027 and close on March 30, 2027.

‍

Recipients of the grant will be announced on April 30, 2027. 

How can I join the Pitch Music & Arts team?

\[+\]

\[-\]

**Volunteer and Staff Applications will open on November 17.** [Register for Rosterfy](https://untitledgroup.rosterfy.com.au/register) to receive an email when they open.

‍

To learn more about volunteering at Pitch, click [here](https://app.notion.com/p/Pitch-Music-Arts-20ec6246a63a80acba34f914a775fb6e).

‍

To learn more about our paid staff positions, click [here](https://app.notion.com/p/Pitch-Music-Arts-20ec6246a63a80acba34f914a775fb6e).

‍

If you have any questions regarding working at Pitch, read our FAQs [here](https://www.notion.so/Pitch-Music-Arts-20ec6246a63a80acba34f914a775fb6e).

How do I resell my ticket?

\[+\]

\[-\]

If you wish to resell your Pitch Music & Arts passes, you can do so via Tixel, our Official Resale Partner. Tixel resale will open soon.

‍

If you are having trouble with the Tixel platform, please reach out to their team and they can assist you [here](https://tixel.com/contact-form).

‍

If you’re selling your Pitch ticket to a friend through a private sale, we recommend that you list your ticket via Tixel for the full price that you’d like to sell it for. If you know who you’re selling to / buying from, you can process a private sale, however we recommend that all funds are processed through Tixel, as any funds transacted by alternative means (bank transfer / cash) are not covered by the Tixel Guarantee.

‍

**Melbourne’s favourite winter ritual has returned to Queen Victoria Market!**

Until 9 September, the Winter Night Market transforms the historic Market into a vibrant mid-week playground of global street food, warming drinks, specialty shopping and live entertainment. Rug up and wander beneath glowing lights, gather around crackling fire pits and soak up the unmistakable energy of a Melbourne winter night.

With **free** entry, come for the food and stay for the winter magic. Every Wednesdays, 5-10pm at the Queen Victoria Market.

# FAQs

What are the Winter Night Market opening hours? 

The Winter Night Market is held on Wednesday nights June 3 to September 9, 5pm to 10pm. Is there parking at the Winter Night Market?  

Yes, [event parking](https://thenightmarket.com.au/visit-us/) is available in both the Queen Victoria Market Multi-level Undercover Car Park and the Open-Air Car Park. Entry to both car parks is via Queen Street. Parking is a $15 flat rate for entry after 4.30pm. Please note the Open-Air Car Park closes at 11pm, the Multi-level Undercover Car Park is open at all times.  Are pets allowed at the Winter Night Market? 

No animals are allowed at the Winter Night Market, with the exception of registered Assistance and Guide dogs.  Is there an entry fee for the Winter Night Market? 

No, there is no entry fee at the Winter Night Market.  Is alcohol available for purchase at the Winter Night Market? 

Yes, while the Winter Night Market is a fully licensed venue, we encourage the responsible consumption of alcohol and only alcohol purchased on the premises may be consumed.  Are there ATMs available onsite? 

Yes, there are ATMs conveniently located throughout the site. Traders accept both credit card and cash payments, however contactless payment is preferred.

Is smoking or vaping permitted at the Winter Night Market?  

No, smoking or vaping is strictly prohibited within the boundaries of the Winter Night Market.

Can I film or take photographs at the Market? 

Any commercial or professional photography at the Market requires a [permit](https://support.qvm.com.au/hc/en-us/requests/new?ticket_form_id=8855510605977). It usually takes approximately 72 hours for the permit application to be reviewed.

Where are the toilets located?  

Toilets are located along Queen Street and in String Bean Alley at the Peel Street end.

# About the Night Market

For over 25 years, Queen Victoria Market has transformed Wednesday nights into a feast for the senses, with exciting themes and experiences each season. 

until September 9, the Winter Night Market returns to warm up your mid-week with a cosy lineup of Melbourne’s best street food, artisan shopping, and live local entertainment. Cosy up under the iconic Market sheds as fire pits crackle, hot drinks flow, and the city’s best performers roam the sheds and laneways. 

Entry is free! Just rug up, round up your crew, and dive into the magic of Melbourne’s favourite winter tradition. 

# About Queen  
Victoria Market

From its humble beginnings as Melbourne’s wholesale hub, to its transformation into a retail hotspot, [Queen Victoria Market](https://qvm.com.au/) is now a mix of old-school charm and contemporary flair, drawing both local and international visitors.  

For 148 years, the Market remains one of Melbourne’s top destinations for all things fresh produce, food, shopping and fun festivities.  

Seasonally, on Wednesday nights, Queen Victoria Market comes to life with a vibrant cultural extravaganza!

## Our Story

> We’re redefining how the world shops, one handmade product at a time.

The Finders Keepers is Australia’s most loved design market, dedicated to supporting small, independent makers and championing conscious consumerism.

![](img/page-images/our-story/FK-Melb-AW23-Samee-Lapham-highres-311.jpg)

![](img/staff/team-photo.jpg)

![](img/page-images/our-story/FK-Melb-AW23-Samee-Lapham-highres-311.jpg)

![](img/staff/team-photo.jpg)

Since 2008, we’ve been the go-to destination for unique, handmade wares, where shoppers meet makers and connect over creativity.

Our mission is to empower Australian makers to thrive while building a future where shopping does the least harm to the planet. By offering resources, a platform for small businesses, and an inclusive space to shop sustainably, we’re redefining how the world shops, one handmade product at a time.

> Join us in celebrating creativity, connection, and mindful consumption.

### We've been supporting small since 2008!

### $1.2 million

Average spent by market-goers each year supporting independent creative businesses.

### 2,800+

Australian independent, creative businesses supported by us each year.

Born in 2008 from the side hustle of friends Sarah Thornton and Brooke Johnston, The Finders Keepers has grown into Australia's most-loved design market, each year hosting festival-style markets in Sydney and Melbourne.

In early 2024, Sarah and Brooke handed over the reins of The Finders Keepers to the Winarch Group, gaining a little sister market in the Olive Tree Market based in Newcastle. Winarch Group is very much driven by connecting communities and providing more opportunities and experiences for individuals and businesses through their events and tourism projects.

## GET INVOLVED

Rainbow Spirit has always grown from the energy and imagination of the people who help create it – shaped not just by stages and structures, but by the passions and stories each of you bring.

It’s the artist who turns a quiet corner into a world of colour.  
The healer who offers stillness in the middle of the dance.  
The facilitator who sparks learning and connection.  
All of the unseen contributions that weave the story.  
  
Whether you’re sharing art, performance, workshops or helping behind the scenes – every role brings the festival to life.   
  
Applications are opening soon for the following departments:  
  
**Arts**  
**Market Bazaar**  
**Performers (FIASCO & roving)**  
**The Village**

We look forward to seeing how you could help shape this next chapter.

Cooked fresh to order, Lucky Coin delivers a fun and delicious experience that attracts customers of all ages at markets, festivals and events

# ABOUT STRAWBERRY

Strawberry Fields was founded in 2009 by a trio of young dreamers. With less than 1,000 attending the inaugural three day event in East Gippsland, Strawberry Fields has now grown to attract 15,000 patrons from across the globe and has solidified its reputation as one of Australia’s best known art, music & camping festivals. After a decade at various venues surrounding Tocumwal, the festival now takes place each summer at its permanent home “The Wildlands” - a 300ha private property only 15 minutes from Tocumwal township, featuring over 1km of direct frontage to the iconic Murray River. With customised sustainable infrastructure in place, attendees can bask in the revelry of four days of live music, large scale art, workshops, and wild river swimming in one of the most stunning natural environments Australia has to offer.

  

**OUR MISSION**

**Acknowledge traditional owners & facilitate opportunities for First Nations artists**

The land on which the festival occurs forms a sacred part of the territories of the Yorta Yorta Nation. We acknowledge that the sovereignty of the Yorta Yorta peoples was not ceded, and colonial impacts to their people and land continues until this day. As guests on this land, we ask that all visitors to the festival recognise how privileged we are to host the event in such a special place along Dhungala (Murray River) — together we must commit to treat this priceless place with respect. We are also committed to facilitating opportunities for Yorta Yorta & other First Nations artists to perform at the festival, and are privileged to have previously hosted performances by DRMNGNOW, Yothu Yindi, Briggs, Allara, Kee’Ahn & Paul Gorrie.

  

**Celebrate & protect the wild Australian bush**

The end of November marks the beginning of summer, and with it comes an undeniable urge to indulge in a great Australian past time – camping out and enjoying the beauty of the bush. This is an experience that all who attend Strawberry Fields truly value – leaving the trappings of everyday life for a weekend enjoying nature. It also means we have a fundamental commitment to protecting our natural environment and ensuring sustainability is a top priority in all aspects of event design. After implementing 100% composting toilets, grey water filtration systems integrated with permaculture gardens, and [Australia’s first 100% reusable crockery system for 10,000 patrons at a multi-day greenfield festival](https://www.greenmusic.org.au/rewash_revolution_strawberry_fields), Strawberry Fields was been awarded [A Greener Festival’s Water & Sanitation award.](https://www.eventindustrynews.com/news/agf-congratulates-the-only-4-festivals-that-took-place-and-received-a-greener-festival-award-in-2020)

  

**Create a unique environment for showcasing art, music & workshops**

A big part of Strawberry Fields is creating a space that emphasises the unique and exceptional qualities of the art and music displayed at the event. We aim to showcase creative & dynamic experiences in the beautiful setting of the Australian bush – whether it’s a secret beach, a sunken tea lounge, a suspended gallery or the stages themselves, every structure and space is dreamed and designed for exploration.

  

**Provide a platform for young, local & upcoming talent**

Over 150 local and international musicians and artists display their work at Strawberry Fields. We continue to be amazed at the wealth of local musical and creative talent in Australia and believe the focus should be as much on the headliners as the unknowns. From the hundreds of anonymous submissions, we receive each year, our panel carefully selects a series of up and coming artists to expose their work to thousands of their peers.

  

**Deliver ongoing benefits for the local community**

After a decade in Tocumwal we consider ourselves members of the local community and obligated to support it in every way possible, even extending benefits to those who do not want to attend the festival. Each year we set aside a portion of ticket sales for the [Strawberry Fields Community Grants fund](https://www.riverineherald.com.au/@finley-news/2019/01/29/420259/strawberry-fields-donates-funds-to-local-community) - with the fund dispersing up to $35,000 annually in microgrants to local community organisations and not for profits which would otherwise struggle to find other funding. All residents of the Berrigan Shire are entitled to purchase festival tickets at half price. The festival also enables a valuable fundraising opportunity for a coalition of local community organisations via the Chillin’n’Grillin Community BBQ which, staffed by volunteers, raises up to $30,000 annually.

  

**REVIEWS**

Voted Top 10 Festivals in The World (2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2022, 2023, 2024) - **Resident Advisor**

_“Levelling the field: The music festival offering a low-income discount_" **-** [**Sydney Morning Herald**](https://www.smh.com.au/entertainment/music/levelling-the-field-the-music-festival-offering-a-low-income-discount-20180523-p4zh46.html)

_“The atmosphere and arts were constant, with the trees providing the perfect canvas for the projections on darkened leaves at night. Strawberry Fields lived up to its internationally renowned reputation with hundreds from across the globe travelling to Tocumwal just for the event.”_ \- **Southern Riverina News**

_“A perfectly curated escape hidden deep in the bush.” -_ [**Mixmag**](https://mixmag.net/feature/review-strawberry-fields-was-a-perfectly-curated-escape-hidden-deep-in-the-bush)

_“One for the bucket list for sure. Check out our_ _eight reasons why Strawberry has mastered the festival model.__”_ **-** [**Beat Magazine**](https://www.beat.com.au/eight-reasons-why-strawberry-fields-has-mastered-the-music-festival-model/)

_“Organisers have hit on an inclusive approach, through a program offering heavily discounted tickets to music fans who otherwise wouldn’t have the resources to attend.”_ \- [**Industry Observer**](https://theindustryobserver.thebrag.com/strawberry-fields-tara-benney-low-income-ticket-program/)

We acknowledge that we meet and work on Yorta Yorta country and other

indigenous lands across this nation, and the sovereignty of the land was never ceded.

We pay respect to elders, past, present & emerging.

# FAQ

* * *

#### Where is the festival held?

Mullum Roots Festival is held in four different venues in Mullumbimby town. The Mullumbimby High School Auditorium, The Drill Hall, The Courthouse Hotel, The Ex- Services Club and The Civic Hall. A ticket gets you a wristband to enter the venues. \*\* Please note that photo ID is required when entering the bowling club and the ex-services club.

#### Where does the Love Bus shuttle go?

The Love Bus is for shuttling in between venues throughout the weekend. There isn't a timetable for this as it will continuously run. The Love Bus will also pick up and drop back patrons from both camp grounds in Mullumbimby at least 3 times per day. A timetable will be at each campground on arrival .  The cost to travel on the camp ground shuttle bus and the Love Bus is included in your ticket price. 

#### What are the camping options in Mullum?

The Mullumbimby Showgrounds and The Mullumbimby Leagues Club. 

#### When and where can I check in or buy a ticket

The festival box office will be located at the Mullumbimby Civic Hall foyer and will be open st 9:30am Saturday 11th July at 9:30am.

#### What do I do with my ticket if I can't make it to the festival

You are welcome to gift your ticket to someone else. You don't need to change the name of the ticket holder, but they will need to present the ticket to be scanned at the Box Office. There are no refunds for tickets.

#### Do I have to buy a separate ticket if I want to go the Friday night opening concert?

Yes. The Friday night opening concert is a separate event and will be on Friday 10th July. 

#### Where do I park

There is street parking in Mullumbimby plus there are several council carparks, back street parking and parking up near the Mullumbimby tennis courts.  

#### Can I bring my dog into the festival venues?

No. The campgrounds allow pets, but not the festival venues, unless they are service animals.

#### Do you accept companion cards?

Yes. Please present these upon arrival at the Box Office.

#### Can I bring my children?

Yes but they must be in the company of a responsible adult. Children under 15 years are permitted free entry, children over 15 are not.

#### Is there disabled seating and access at all venues?

Yes there is disabled access to all venues and if you require disables seating you must let reception know and you will be ushered to the reserved seating.

# **18th & 19th April 2026**

# The Annual Byron Bay Malibu Classic

The Byron Bay Malibu Classic is an iconic event, and the Clubs main event of the year. Held at Wategos the contest attracts competitors from up and down the East Coast and regularly has a contingent visiting from New Zealand. A **single fin only 9ft** **and over** Malibu contest, it was first held in 1980, making it the longest-running event of its kind in Australia, perhaps the world.

Money raised at the Classic through the generosity of our sponsors and competitors has enabled the club to donate well over three hundred thousand dollars to local community organisations over the years.

Every year we have a competitor draw for a beautifully board hand crafted by Brett Munro here in Byron Bay. Every competitor goes in the draw held on Saturday night the 18th and **you have to be there to win it**.

Limited spaces get in quick…

# About the Club

The Byron Bay Malibu Club is a sporting club that meets on the second Sunday of every month for friendly competition, followed by a barbeque. At these days there is no set competing divisions and the emphasis is on fun on the waves for young and old. The club caters for all levels of surfing ability from beginners to State & Aussie Champions and we are proud to be a family based club. Not all club members surf and we welcome social members.

The club began in the late 70's and early 80's when local surfers who shared a common love of Malibu surfing would meet and hold impromptu contests, keeping the tradition of Malibu surfing alive. 

In 2023, the Byron Bay Malibu Club will be holding its 42nd Annual Malibu Classic, the longest running single fin longboard event in Australia. The event will be held on the 29th and 30th of April, 2023. We expect to have over 150 competitors again this year, together with their families and a large number of spectators.

All money received by the Club from our sponsors goes directly to these organisations. In the past 40 years, with the support of generous sponsors, we have donated well in excess of $300,000 to local organisations and charities.

We will be continuing to donate locally with the proceeds going to the Coastal Patrol, Westpac Rescue Helicopter, The Youth Activity Centre, The Shift Project, The Disabled Surfers Association NSW Far North Coast.
