# Sponsorship Packages

### [Thank you to our sponsors!](https://nimbinmardigrass.com/sponsors/)

MardiGrass is very grateful for the support of [our sponsors](https://www.nimbinmardigrass.com/sponsors/) in helping promote cannabis law reform, as we enter our 34th year of gathering to both celebrate and liberate the amazing cannabis plant! MardiGrass is a grassroots community event running on a non-profit basis and powered by busy volunteers!

Please read below for our MardiGrass Sponsorship Packages.

### **Indica Sponsorship Package $5,000**

*   3m x 3m stall space with power / Or free ranging distribution of promotional items
    
*   1 x banner-sized advert in printed program [**_The Pot Papers_**](https://www.nimbinmardigrass.com/2024/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/MG_23-web-Combined.pdf) \[40,000 copies\]
    
*   1 x banner-sized advert on our [website](https://nimbinmardigrass.com/sponsors/)
    
*   We will announce any sponsor activities or demos during event, as well as list in web/printed program
    
*   Promotional items for Hemp Olympix winner bags
    
*   Carry promotional banner in the parade
    
*   10 x weekend passes \[no camping\]
    

To book or discuss variations on the package, please email:

[head@hempembassy.net](mailto:head@hempembassy.net)

### **Sativa Sponsorship Package $3,000**

*   Free ranging distribution of promotional items around the event
    
*   1 x business card-sized advert in printed program The Pot Papers \[40,000 copies\]
    
*   1 x business-card sized advertisement on our website
    
*   Promotional items for Hemp Olympix winner bags
    
*   Carry promotional banner in the parade
    
*   5 x weekend passes \[no camping\]
    

To book or discuss variations on the package, please email:

[head@hempembassy.net](mailto:head@hempembassy.net)

### Would you like to [**advertise**](https://nimbinmardigrass.com/participate/pot-papers/) instead? [**Please visit this link.**](https://nimbinmardigrass.com/participate/pot-papers/)

# Always Original  
Art & Design

SHOWCASING THE BEST OF HANDMADE SINCE 2003

## Shop directly from Melbourne’s best artists, designers, crafters and makers at Fitzroy’s iconic Rose Street Market.

[Explore](https://www.rosestmarket.com.au/rose-street-market-melbourne)

### Explore Our Markets

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5af5063fe2ccd173b2e5d1c3/514a9825-b34d-4ad6-a0ba-d3d341c4ab2a/rsam-tile.jpg)

Our original market utilising an old junkyard in the heart of Fitzroy to showcase the work of over 120 different makers each Sat and Sun. 

[Explore](https://www.rosestmarket.com.au/rose-street-market-melbourne)

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5af5063fe2ccd173b2e5d1c3/82d78ae8-5e1a-4eb1-8e07-2c8bec43c9fd/heide-tile.jpg)

Set in the beautiful surrounds of the Heide Museum of Modern Art sculpture park, this market is open on the second Saturday of each month

[Explore](https://www.rosestmarket.com.au/heide-market)

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5af5063fe2ccd173b2e5d1c3/8aa019d3-f8e9-41b3-b946-bbc7e2025105/crft-tile.jpg)

The historic meets the cutting edge at CRFT\* WRK, a celebration of contemporary locally made craft under the big sheds at the Queen Victoria Market.

[Explore](https://www.rosestmarket.com.au/crftwrk-market)

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5af5063fe2ccd173b2e5d1c3/662428bb-fc0c-49c6-af62-81411be3cab7/lygon-st.jpg)

Handmade goods in a traditional Italian style piazza! A fun, colourful market with craft and tasty treats in beautiful Argyle Square, Carlton.

[Explore](https://www.rosestmarket.com.au/lygon-street-market)

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5af5063fe2ccd173b2e5d1c3/d83da151-78b7-4e38-8774-07d558bedfb6/trust-tile.jpg)

Enjoy browsing handmade and homegrown artisan products on the sprawling lawns of Rippon Lea Estate

[Explore](https://www.rosestmarket.com.au/trust-market-ripponlea-estate)

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5af5063fe2ccd173b2e5d1c3/292de640-d21e-47d1-813f-0226cd809fd3/young-tile.jpg)

Set in an historic woolshed in Kensington, enjoy the coolest local makers to help you tick off your shopping list. It’s all happening at Younghusband!

[Explore](https://www.rosestmarket.com.au/younghusband-market-kensington)

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5af5063fe2ccd173b2e5d1c3/533e9cf7-c096-448f-9803-075ed442a3a2/district-tile.jpg)

A monthly market in the heart of the Docklands. Totally under cover and full of crafty products, food and entertainment.

[Explore](https://www.rosestmarket.com.au/docklands-district-makers-market)

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5af5063fe2ccd173b2e5d1c3/3624c8eb-19c8-4af4-ba5e-9c1dde1db76f/MMM.png)

A curated monthly market of art, design and local makers in the heart of the CBD - taking place each month at City Square.

[Explore](https://www.melbournemakersmarket.com/)

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5af5063fe2ccd173b2e5d1c3/866240f7-9598-4d07-a376-58c6aaaebee0/pop-tile.jpg)

Discover vibrant pop-up art and design markets across Melbourne, showcasing creativity, community spirit, and unique local treasures.

[Explore](https://www.rosestmarket.com.au/pop-up-markets)

# Advertise in the Mardigrass Pot Papers

### 40,000 copies will be printed and available all year from the Nimbin HEMP Embassy.

# Important

*   40,000 copies will be printed and distributed all year from the [Nimbin HEMP Embassy](http://hempembassy.net/).
    
*   Ads will be automatically included on [MardiGrass website](https://nimbinmardigrass.com/2025/sponsors/) as soon as we receive them.
    
*   The deadline for print is **1st April 2026.**

Byron Writers Festival presents world-class gatherings that enrich and transform the lives of our audiences and community.

# About us

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5af5063fe2ccd173b2e5d1c3/6f26e3ed-b805-409e-9bb1-350d34b760c1/20250406_112858.jpg)

## Shop directly from Melbourne’s best artists, designers, crafters and makers!

Since 2003, a small part of Rose Street has sprung to life each weekend. Found in the heart of eclectic Fitzroy, The Rose St. Artists' Market is a unique outlet where emerging artists and designers showcase their work to Melbourne and the world!

Roughly based on similar projects in London, Berlin and in particular the DUMBO Collective; a market set up by artists under the Brooklyn Bridge in New York - The Rose St. Artists' Market utilises a former junkyard in the back streets of Fitzroy to display the work of up to 120 artists and designers each Saturday and Sunday, some emerging and some more established.

Since its inception, The Market has gained the reputation of being one of Melbourne's hidden treasures, wowing people with the high quality of work on offer. There's no telling what products you might find. From quirky furniture design and stunning fashion through to intricate jewellery and unique paintings. In fact, over 3000 individuals are listed on our growing catalogue of artists and designers here each week selling everything from the wacky to the wonderful!

The Rose St. Artists' Market has taken a fresh approach to the traditional market concept giving you the opportunity peruse the numerous displays, collect, source and commission unique works; and of course meet, greet and speak with artists and designers in person.

##  A bit about us

**"When people die, they end up at department stores."  
****Andy Warhol**

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5af5063fe2ccd173b2e5d1c3/2b1299e4-3586-4cab-8366-58605cdfad4c/adam-ferrante.jpg)

## Adam F

**Founder & Artistic Director**

With a background in the arts (VCA Scholarship), Adam brings a wealth of arts knowledge and creativity to his role at Rose Street. He was the recipient of the top prize of the Melbourne Fringe Festival before founding the market.

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5af5063fe2ccd173b2e5d1c3/bee6753b-f544-4b4d-8837-24069272f45e/christian-ferrante.jpg)

## Christian F

**Co-Founder & Operations Manager**

Holding a degree in Business Marketing, Christian brings a practical knowledge to his role at Rose Street. He loves bringing creative ideas to life and fostering local emerging artistic talent.

# Byron Writers Festival '26

Partners

14—16 Aug

Thanks to all of our partners and supporters. Byron Writers Festival would not be possible without your passion and generosity.

## Principal Patron

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/683feac88071376d0d808b0f_BWF_2025_Partners_TheVasudharaFund.png)](https://www.byronwritersfestival.com/partners#)

The Vasudhara Fund is committed to supporting the arts: when our world is doing it tough, the power of the arts to inspire us; to give us hope; is ever more important. The Vasudhara Fund is delighted to support the Byron Writers Festival.

‍

# Government Partners

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6a41f7574bfd71abb412ef57_2026%20Festival%20Partner%20Logos%20%20-%20WEBSITE%20\(10\).png)](https://www.nsw.gov.au/)

Byron Writers Festival is supported by the NSW Government through Create NSW.

_‍_

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/683fec12507630d948ef1c32_BWF_2025_Partners_AusGov_CreativeAust.png)](https://creative.gov.au/)

Creative Australia is the Australian Government’s principal arts investment and advisory body.

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/683feabbc66d215e86a01a29_BWF_2025_Partners_ByronShireCouncil.png)](https://www.byron.nsw.gov.au/Home)

Byron Shire Council is a local government area located in the northern part of New South Wales, Australia. It encompasses the vibrant coastal town of Byron Bay, renowned for its stunning beaches, arts scene, and eco-conscious community. The council is dedicated to promoting sustainability, supporting local businesses, and preserving the unique natural environment, including the iconic hinterland. It also focuses on community engagement, cultural development, while ensuring Byron Shire remains a welcoming and resilient place for both residents and visitors.

### Major Partners

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6840ed085c293636b7654811_BWF_2025_Partners_SCU.png)](https://www.scu.edu.au/)

As a founding partner, Southern Cross University’s relationship with Byron Writers Festival has grown from a shared commitment to storytelling, ideas and community into a lasting collaboration grounded in creativity and place. Together, we have helped foster conversations that challenge, inspire and connect, amplifying voices from our region and beyond, and celebrating the people and stories that shape our community.

‍

Across three decades, this partnership has been as much about people as it has been about ideas, bringing together writers, students, alumni, partners and audiences, and contributing to the vibrant cultural life we are proud to be part of.

‍

As Byron Writers Festival marks its 30th anniversary, Southern Cross University is honoured to celebrate this milestone, recognising the stories, thinkers and community that continue to shape who we are, now and into the future.

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6a2f49023f9feeabc22e0ca6_All%20Girls%20Logos%202026%20\(2\).png)](https://discover.taswalkingco.com.au/byron-writers-festival-2026?utm_campaign=45848505-2606_Byron_Writers_Festival_2026&utm_source=Website&utm_medium=BWF_website)

Tasmanian Walking Company crafts guided journeys through Australia’s most inspiring landscapes, combining expert-led walks with exceptional food, comfortable lodgings, and genuine hospitality. Designed around the principles of slow travel, each experience offers time to walk, read, write, reflect, and reconnect with what matters most.

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6840ee70b13239397fe622a3_BWF_2025_Partners_TheBookRoom.png)](https://thebookroomcollective.com/)

The Book Room Collective is an independent and locally owned group of bookshops in the Northern Rivers, operating from Byron Bay and Lennox Head. The shops are carefully curated to ensure every opportunity to explore and discover.

‍

#### Major Media Partners

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6840eeb1c2447c888e38d7e2_BWF_2025_Partners_TheGuardian.png)](https://www.theguardian.com/au)

Since launching in Australia in 2013, the Guardian has delivered trusted journalism to help build human connection and hope – holding power to account and giving a voice to the powerless. The Guardian is proudly independent, open to all, funded by many and beholden to no one. Guardian Australia offers national news coverage and has four bureaux, located in Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane and Canberra. The Australian newsroom is also part of the Guardian’s 24-hour global news operation, helping to cover breaking international stories in all parts of the world.

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6840ef1f06093bb70a420b11_BWF_2025_Partners_Echo.png)](http://www.echo.net.au/)

100% Local - 100% Independent - 100% Free  
  
A vibrant, independent community newspaper covering the Northern Rivers, with a particular focus on the Byron Shire and surrounds. Established in 1986 to give a voice to the rise of the counterculture in the area, The Echo has maintained a fierce pursuit of truth, and supported the irreverent, quirky voice of the community ever since.  
  
The website echo.net.au is a fully-established free news platform, covering the Northern Rivers and NSW Far North Coast. With a large reach, it hosts a strong local subscriber base and is a ‘go-to’ reference point for the community.  
  
The voice of the community since 1986.

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6840ef6bda9d44fe5319e320_BWF_2025_Partners_ABCNorthCoast.png)](https://www.abc.net.au/northcoast)

ABC North Coast is proud to have been a media partner of the Byron Writers Festival since its inception. The Walkley-award winning ABC North Coast team produce stories on air and online reflecting the diversity, creativity, news and views of Northern Rivers people.

##### Festival Partners

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6840efa69c2e6e4bc2d686ac_BWF_2025_Partners_FirstNationalByron.png)](https://www.byronbayfn.com.au/)

In the past 30 years, First National Byron Bay has cemented its position as the region’s number one agency, servicing a footprint that extends from Wardell to Byron Bay, Bangalow, the Hinterland, Mullumbimby and New Brighton.

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6840efcdb42f5fbc167c37d2_BWF_2025_Partners_Mud%20LiteraryClub.png)](https://www.mudliteraryclub.com/)

The MUD Literary Club connects their members to the nation's most celebrated writers through outstanding literary events. Through its membership MUD provides exceptional support to Australia's emerging literary talent by presenting a significant annual prize for the best first literary novel by an Australian author.

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6840f0993473bb1dbefd74c2_BWF_2025_Partners_OrganicIndia.png)](https://www.organicindia.com.au/)

ORGANIC INDIA Everyday Wellness: Herbs, Greens & Fibre

True wellness begins with the simple rituals we choose each day. Our certified organic herbal teas, greens and fibre are created to nourish body and mind while supporting a healthier planet.  

Every ingredient is grown with care through transparent seed-to-shelf practices that protect biodiversity, empower farming communities, and honour the connection between people and nature.

**Create moments of everyday wellness, with Organic India**

‍

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6840f0f40a06ce66c074378d_BWF_2025_Partners_BasqHouse.png)](https://basqhouse.com.au/)

Inspired by the grandeur of Moroccan riads, Basq House is a landing pad for those seeking privacy and peacefulness in a tucked-away laneway in the heart of Byron’s village centre. Hotel facilities include a guest Library, living room, roof deck, bathhouse, and fireplaces.

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6a2d1bd40d1b3a1110f3992a_CA_Cultural%20Fund%20Logo_RGB_full%20colour-square.png)](https://www.copyright.com.au/culturalfund)

The Cultural Fund is the philanthropic arm of the Copyright Agency. Our aim is to ensure Australian writers and visual artists are better supported and paid appropriately for their creative endeavours. The Cultural Fund provides grants and Fellowships to benefit Australian writers, visual artists, publishers and organisations working in the Literature and visual arts sectors. Our current priorities are to support significant projects to benefit Australian writers, visual artists, publishers, and creative organisations that create audience development opportunities for writers and artists as well as all-important grants for leadership and diversity through sector development projects.

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6a2d1d21b79970e94d398cbf_marvell-black.png)](https://byronbayoysterbar.com.au/)

Byron Bay Oyster Bar & Seafood Restaurant and Horizon Rooftop Bar offer two distinct experiences under one roof. Enjoy fresh seasonal seafood, oysters and laneway dining downstairs, or head upstairs for cocktails, poolside moments and rooftop views. Whether it’s a long lunch, sunset drinks or a relaxed dinner, Hotel Marvell brings together design, atmosphere and memorable dining experiences.

##### Festival Precinct Partners

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6a2f5d11cdf959c03337389e_All%20Girls%20Logos%202026%20\(11\).png)](https://havengallerybyron.com/)

Haven Gallery is a multi sensory playground for art, sound, movement and human expression. Inside the reimagined former Woolworths building, the entire space has been transformed into a living artwork that shifts with light, colour and atmosphere. Immersive installations blend physical space with digital imagination, while the transformed streetscape of Haven City invites you to wander, interact and discover something new at every turn. The experience is playful, welcoming and immersive, offering a world that invites creativity rather than simply displaying it.

Across the year we host exhibitions, performances, workshops and creative experiences designed to spark curiosity and connection. Haven Gallery is a place for families, adults, couples, travellers and art lovers who enjoy exploring at their own pace. Whether you come to lose yourself in the sensory environment, participate in a creative moment or enjoy the space with others, Haven Gallery offers a cultural experience shaped by community, imagination and the joy of shared discovery.

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6a2f4d741f174bbdeea23065_All%20Girls%20Logos%202026%20\(3\).png)](https://www.beachhotel.com.au/)

Overlooking the golden sands and sparkling waters of Byron Bay's Main Beach is the Beach Hotel. A Byron Bay icon for locals and visitors alike, the Beachy brings together great food, cold drinks, live entertainment and unbeatable ocean views in one of Australia's most celebrated coastal destinations. Whether you're stopping by for a long lunch, catching live sport, enjoying a weekend stay or settling in for sunset drinks, the Beach Hotel offers a relaxed yet vibrant experience that captures the spirit of Byron Bay.

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6a2f4ad9de45e959f3ef0b19_BCC_CENTRED_COOL_.png)](https://www.byroncentre.com.au/)

**The Beating Heart of Byron**

For 45 years, Byron Community Centre has been bringing people together through community services, arts, culture and social enterprise. Known as the beating heart of Byron, the independent charity and not-for-profit operates the **Byron Theatre**, **Byron Markets**, **Byron Spaces,** **Byron Seniors Club,** volunteer program and art gallery, alongside essential community support services including **Fletcher Street Cottage**. Through a diverse range of programs, events and services, Byron Community Centre creates opportunities for connection, creativity and support, helping to build a stronger, more inclusive and resilient community for locals and visitors alike.

‍

###### Supporting Partners

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6a2f4ea2bc0e9d85ec65ce4c_All%20Girls%20Logos%202026%20\(5\).png)](https://www.firesideagency.com.au/)

Fireside is a creative communications agency based between Melbourne and the Northern Rivers. We believe story is the thing that makes complex ideas land – whether that's a campaign, an annual report or a policy document. We start every project there, with the narrative, before any strategy or design gets near it. We work with organisations tackling hard issues, from youth mental health to the renewable energy transition, and we also publish a print magazine, The Story, about the craft of storytelling itself.

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6840f0c24c78174aee5d5faf_BWF_2025_Partners_TheAustraliaInstitute.png)](https://australiainstitute.org.au/)

The Australia Institute is one of the country’s most influential public policy think tanks. Based in Canberra, we conduct high-impact research that combines rigorous fact-driven material with cutting-edge communication strategies.

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6840f132019a7cdda7c950da_BWF_2025_Partners_TheConversation.png)](https://theconversation.com/au)

The Conversation Australia and New Zealand is a unique collaboration between academics and journalists, and is the world’s leading publisher of research-based news and analysis.

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6840f174f311f21909d27781_BWF_2025_Partners_HoneyBeeHomes.png)](https://honeybeehomes.com.au/)

Over 446,000 Australians are living with dementia. If that becomes your reality, will you be happy living in a locked ward for your final years? 

Honey Bee Homes offers a real home, not a facility. No uniforms, no locked doors. It is aged care reimagined.

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6840f19a5ce94df6325db25c_BWF_2025_Partners_NRCommunityFoundation.png)](https://nrcf.org.au/womens-giving-circle)

Northern Rivers Community Foundation (NRCF) helps people give where they live. Since 2003, NRCF has distributed more than $14.7 million to grassroots organisations and community-led initiatives, supporting a stronger, more resilient Northern Rivers. The NRCF Women's Giving Circle brings together women who believe in the power of collective giving. Through shared philanthropy, members support local projects that empower women and girls, address inequality, and create lasting change across our region.

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6840f1b7da9d44fe531ad5e0_BWF_2025_Partners_TheBankHouse.png)](https://www.thebankhousebangalow.com/)

The Bank House is a heritage gem, thoughtfully curated featuring four bedrooms and a studio, located in the heart of Bangalow. Over a century of memories have been created within her walls. Step up from the main street and walk into your own European inspired abode with secret garden, where the outside world rushes by and time stands still.

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6a2f4fca5a4de301ecd1a157_All%20Girls%20Logos%202026%20\(7\).png)](https://thesunseeker.com.au/)

The Sunseeker is 80’s brick motel nostalgia reimagined as a boutique holiday experience for the modern, conscious traveller. Tucked just on the edge of town, The Sunseeker sits nestled in a private tropical oasis alongside the magnificent beaches of Byron Bay, Australia. Explore their diverse range of unique accommodation options, thoughtfully designed to suit every traveller and every occasion. For short stays to extended holidays, The Sunseeker spaces combine comfort, style and convenience to create their uniquely trademarked holiday experience.

###### Media Partners

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6840f1e5a20e4020489fb6ae_BWF_2025_Partners_BangalowHerald.png)](https://www.bangalowherald.com.au/)

The Bangalow Herald is a monthly not-for-profit magazine dedicated to the community of Bangalow and surrounding villages. With historical links going back more than 100 years, the Herald continues to be the focus for cultural, social and environmental concerns of the 2479 community. It is proudly independent and produced mainly by local volunteers.

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6840f20e4fa1662dfcaef39c_BWF_2025_Partners_BayFM.png)](https://www.bayfm.org/)

BayFM is Byron Shire’s own and only community radio station, serving listeners on 99.9FM and at bayfm.org . We are 100% independent, volunteer-run and not-for-profit.

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6840f246b8319d97759ca6a0_BWF_2025_Partners_ByronBay.png)](https://byronbay.com/)

Byron Bay truly is unlike anywhere in the world. So, come visit the wellness capital of Australia and experience the awe-inspiring natural beauty, and lively, welcoming community.

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6840f2851da59fce1b27366d_BWF_2025_Partners_KooriMail.png)](https://koorimail.com/)

Proudly the Voice of Indigenous Australia, the Koori Mail is Australia’s leading fortnightly national newspaper dedicated to reporting on the issues that matter to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people. Established in May 1991, the Koori Mail celebrates 35 years of commitment to giving First Nations Australians a voice missing in mainstream media.

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6840f2afd69e2118181610d7_BWF_2025_Partners_RustysByronGuide.png)](https://rustymillersurf.com/byron-guide/)

Rusty’s Byron Guide magazine is shopping for the mind, through its incisive, quality writing. We ask our readers to Read Think Act.

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6a2f52e15a4de301ecd216ed_Byron%20Edit%20logo.png)](https://www.byronedit.com/)

Byron Edit is a Northern Rivers media platform covering local news, events, food, travel and culture. Reaching thousands of locals and visitors each week, Byron Edit helps people discover what's happening across Byron Bay and the wider region.

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6840f2e162af6b40d94cdf27_BWF_2025_PartnersTheWeekendEdition.png)](https://www.indailyqld.com.au/theweekendedition-brisbane)

The Weekend Edition is your go-to source for planning the perfect weekend, delivering the best of Brisbane, the Gold Coast and surrounds straight into your inbox every Thursday morning. Whether you’re on the hunt for a new restaurant, cafe or bar, eager to know what events are happening or looking for local travel inspiration, The Weekend Edition has you covered. Get your weekly dose of local goodness online.

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6840f2fd08ed9de5d49df32e_BWF_2025_Partners_RadioNational.png)](https://www.abc.net.au/listen/radionational)

ABC Radio National is the home for curious minds. Offering programs on air and on demand that inform, challenge, and inspire - from Radio National Breakfast with Sally Sara every weekday morning to The Radio National Hour with Fran Kelly every weekday evening. Whether it's science, philosophy, culture, religion, or books, every program feeds your curiosity, one conversation at a time. Tune in on your radio or the ABC listen app.

###### Cultural Partners

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6840f315b49f59dfbd703122_BWF_2025_Partners_AustralianPoetry.png)](https://www.australianpoetry.org/)

Australian Poetry, the national poetry body, runs an extensive calendar of publications and festival events. Here, we partner directly with major and emerging literary festivals where many of these poems are then published by AP. These events are presented in partnership via funding from the Copyright Agency Cultural Fund.

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6840f33272c40f1ed64ce6c6_BWF_2025_Partners_Blak-Bright.png)](https://www.blakandbright.com.au/)

Blak & Bright First Nations Literary Festival showcases the diverse expressions of First Nations writers. We celebrate all genres of storytelling from oral stories to epic novels and plays to poetry.

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6840f34b8b00aae0f71da0f6_BWF_2025_Partners_BoldAuthors.png)](https://www.boldauthors.com/)

Bold Authors is a collaborative online course hub. It enables authors and publishing industry insiders to create and/or attend courses on subjects including writing, publishing, book marketing and author business.

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6840f36a23100116fb637490_BWF_2025_Partners_GriffithReview.png)](https://www.griffithreview.com/)

Griffith Review is a literary and current affairs journal that offers fresh takes on big ideas. Each edition responds to a loose theme and features essays, short fiction, conversations, poetry and visual art by emerging and established creatives from Australia and overseas.

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6a30a8eb7ab34eb02b6b4acc_2026%20Festival%20Partner%20Logos%20%20-%20WEBSITE%20\(5\).png)](https://www.musicnsw.com/)

We're the peak body for contemporary music in New South Wales - here for the artists, communities and music businesses that make this state's culture what it is. We exist to build a NSW music ecosystem where artists have sustainable careers, communities are connected and supported, and music culture is properly valued - with the wellbeing of artists at the heart of all we do.

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6840f38543fe9fd48881b9e3_BWF_2025_PartnersIngramSpark.png)](https://www.ingramspark.com/)

IngramSpark is self-publishing company that allows you to print and manage your print and ebooks in one convenient platform. We offer book distribution to over 40,000 booksellers and librarians located throughout the world. Upload your book for FREE today!

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6840f3bec92ddbc6ab4be206_BWF_2025_Partners_PoetsOutLoud.png)](https://poetsoutloud.org/)

Founded by prize-winning poet Sarah Temporal, Poets Out Loud empowers voices of all ages through inclusive cultural projects and performances.

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6840f3e78b00aae0f71dcfd1_BWF_2025_Partners_QuarterlyEssay.png)](https://www.quarterlyessay.com.au/)

Quarterly Essay is the leading agenda-setting journal of politics and culture in Australia. Established in 2001, Quarterly Essay presents the widest range of political, intellectual and cultural opinion, and aims to foster debate. It offers a forum for original long-form investigations, profiles and arguments, and correspondence on previous essays.

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6840f400b42f5fbc167de6b7_BWF_2025_Partners_RedRoomPoetry.png)](https://redroompoetry.org/)

Red Room Poetry is Australia’s leading organisation for commissioning poetry in meaningful ways. Key projects include the national Poetry Month, POEM FOREST, Poetry in First Languages and MAD Poetry.

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6840f43726f6e9f388318a96_BWF_2025_Partners_WordTravels.png)](https://wordtravels.info/)

Word Travels is a not for profit arts organisation, organising literary and literacy programs for festivals, private companies, libraries, schools and cultural institutions around the Asia Pacific with a focus on developing performing writers.

###### Community Partners

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6840ef8f3d2e52546158e62f_BWF_2025_Partners_Elements.png)](https://elementsofbyron.com.au/)

Stay at Elements of Byron during Byron Writers Festival. Immerse yourself in the natural beauty of Byron Bay with a stay at the award-winning Elements of Byron. Set on 22 hectares of beachfront paradise, the resort features 202 standalone villas, thoughtfully designed to reflect the surrounding rainforest, dunes, eucalypt forest and wetlands. Enjoy world-class amenities and a tranquil setting that nurtures creativity, reflection and rest - the perfect base for your Writers Festival experience.

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6840f4984c78174aee5ebfcd_BWF_2025_Partners_FrontlinePrint.png)](https://www.frontlineprint.com.au/)

Frontline Print & Copy Centre is Byron Bay’s premier copy and digital print centre. With state of the art Xerox, Canon and Qce equipment, and knowledgeable staff, they can handle any size print job, located in the heart of Byron Bay for over 15 years.

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6840f4b26cc6d1578ea92d29_BWF_2025_Partners_Bask-Stow.png)](https://baskandstow.com.au/)

Bask & Stow exudes an aura of calm, their suites designed with a chic, yet laid-back vibe. Bright interiors spill onto private decks with lush gardens and a plunge pool to leave you feeling utterly restored. Relaxed coastal living meets mid-century interior design, Bask & Stow luxury guesthouse embodies the ever-charming Byron Bay lifestyle.

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6840f505920180dc4b8922b4_BWF_2025_Partners_Rochdale.png)](https://rochdaleadvisory.com.au/)

Rochdale Accounting & Advisory are all about helping you build a truly successful business. In addition to being reputable accountants in Bundaberg and the Northern Rivers, they are also business strategists and coaches—committed to empowering you with the tools and knowledge needed to achieve lasting growth.

###### Hospitality Partners

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6a2f566e9b060f6e07677bb6_Ink%20Gin_Logo-Strapline_PMS%202756%20C-01%20\(3\).png)](https://www.inkgin.com/)

ink gin is an independent, family-owned Australian gin brand and the original conversation starter. Founded in 2015 in Northern New South Wales, ink was the world's first naturally colour-changing gin, crafted using butterfly pea flower. The gin pours a deep natural indigo and transforms to pink when tonic is added.

Produced at Husk Farm Distillery in the Tweed Valley, NSW, ink is made for simple rituals and shared moments. Whether enjoyed with friends or savoured at the end of the day, ink makes it a moment.

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6a2f56e77a9c7089d9fd5b15_All%20Girls%20Logos%202026%20\(10\).png)](https://jillywines.com.au/)

[![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67c6fc0c4fdc01d0349b4826/6a31d44745e2f0268281baec_Screenshot%202026-06-17%20085451.png)](https://byronbaysurfclub.org/)

# Contact

## For general enquiries, get in touch

## For common enquiries, see below

*   ### I'm a stallholder looking to join a market
    
    You can find out all the specific info for each one of our markets [here](https://www.rosestmarket.com.au/quick-market-guide).
    
    Details you’ll find include stall size, location, what we provide, criteria and applicable stall fees.
    
    To get involved, just click the [Apply Now](https://www.rosestmarket.com.au/applynow) button. All applications are handled via our online portal.
    
*   ### I need to reschedule my stall
    
    [Get in touch](mailto:info@rosestmarket.com.au?subject=Reschedule%20Request&body=Name%3A%0ABooked%20Market%3A%0ACurrent%20Date%3A%0ANew%20Requested%20Date%3A%0AComments%3A) with your details of your current booking including which market and date you’re booked into, and the date you’d like to reschedule to.
    
    Note we can’t reschedule stalls within 7 days of the event date.
    
*   ### I need to cancel my stall
    
    [Get in touch](mailto:info@rosestmarket.com.au?subject=Cancellation%20Request&body=Name%3A%0ABooked%20Market%3A%0ACurrent%20Date%3A%0AComments%3A) with your details of your current booking including which market and date you’re booked into, and the reason for your cancellation.
    
    Note we can’t reschedule stalls within 10 days of the event date.
    
    Any fees refunded are at the discretion of the event organiser and are subject to a $20 cancellation fee.
    
*   ### I'm searching for a specific vendor
    
    Please [email us](mailto:info@rosestmarket.com.au?subject=Vendor%20Search&body=Which%20market%20did%20you%20see%20the%20vendor%3A%0ADate%20you%20visited%3A%0ADescription%20of%20their%20product%3A%0AAny%20other%20information%20you%20can%20share%3A) with the market name, date and product description of the vendor. Any specific details you can share is always useful!
    
*   ### Media Request
    
    If you’re after images, video or content for an article, [click here](mailto:info@rosestmarket.com.au?subject=Media%20-%20Content%20Request&body=Name%3A%0APhone%3A%0AOutlet%2Fpublication%3A%0AContent%20required%3A%0A).
    
    If you’d like to film at one of our markets, [click here](mailto:info@rosestmarket.com.au?subject=Filming%20Request&body=Name%3A%0APhone%3A%0AOutlet%2FPublication%3A%0AMarket%20location%3A%0ADate%20of%20filming%3A%0AComments%3A).
    
*   ### I can't find my requested date on the application
    
    *   **Fully Booked Dates:** Dates that are full will not appear on the online application form.
        
    *   **Joining the Waiting List:** Please sign up for the waiting list for each individual date you would like to attend.
        
    *   **Notifications:** We only get in touch if a spot opens up due to a cancellation, so notification timing will vary.

# FAQ

## Frequently Asked Questions

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67beff1f653304c10c2c4879/67d40adf8de24338a4ed5243_our-history.webp)

Still have questions?

[

Contact Us

Contact Us

Contact Us

Contact Us







](https://www.byronwritersfestival.com/contact)

What are the dates for the 2026 Byron Writers Festival?

Friday 14 – Sunday 16 August 2026.

What is the new location for the Byron Writers Festival?

In 2026, Byron Writers Festival will be held across multiple venues in the township of Byron Bay.

‍

The Festival Precinct will feature two distinct festival hubs – one on the foreshore at Bay St and one in the heart of the town on Jonson St.

‍

The following venues will be hosting 2026 Byron Writers Festival sessions and events: Byron Community Centre (Byron Theatre and Wategos Room), Beach Hotel, Byron Bay Surf Club, Johnson Street Stage, Haven, with more to be announced.

‍

All venues are accessible and full details will be provided closer to program launch.

How far apart are the venues?

The Festival Precinct venues are within walking distance of each other – generally within a five to 15-minutes stroll.

The Festival Precinct is 650m end-to-end – only 250m longer than the previous festival grounds. Venues are clustered together in hubs, connected by the The Book Room on Fletcher Street, with retail and hospitality options along the way.

Are all sessions in the township of Byron, or are some still in Bangalow?

All sessions will be held in Byron township.

What are the closest airports to Byron Bay?

The closest airport to Byron Bay is the Ballina Byron Gateway airport. You can also fly into the Gold Coast airport at Coolangatta.

Will there be parking near the venues?

There will be a festival shuttle between the Cavanbah Centre and the precinct allowing our festival attendees to park and ride. The shuttle will drop off and pick up patrons from the Byron Bus Interchange.

‍

Visit Byron Shire Council’s website for local parking options.

‍

Will there be road closures or traffic changes to the townships?

The festival will have minimal impact on the regular flow of traffic and is working with Byron Shire Council to implement a traffic management plan.

Will I need separate tickets for each venue or is my festival pass valid everywhere?

Single-day and three-day passes are valid for programming between 9am and 5pm _only._ Feature events are separately ticketed and your day pass is not valid for these events.

What are the benefits of Festival Friends passes?

Festival Friends get exclusive first-access to three-day passes ahead of the crowds, and for a discounted price. Festival Friends will also receive priority access to venues, and access to the members-only lounge within the Festival precinct.

What does the three-day or single-day pass give me access to?

The three-day and single-day Festival passes are valid for all Festival programming from 9am through until 5pm daily. This includes all free programming. Evening feature events are ticketed separately and your day pass _is not valid_ for these events.

What does my pass include parking?

Park-and-ride will be available from the Cavanbah Centre, 249 Ewingsdale Rd, Byron Bay. Byron. Daily parking passes are $10 per day and can be purchased via the website at any time. These parking passes are valid for the duration of the day, and include the shuttle into the Festival precinct.

What tickets are available for the Festival in 2026?

In 2026 there are three types of tickets available: three-day passes, single-day passes and feature event tickets. Single-day and feature event tickets are available in adult, Festival Friend, youth, concession and MobTix prices.  
  
The three-day and single-day Festival passes are valid for all Festival programming from 9am through until 5pm daily. This includes all free programming. Evening feature events are ticketed separately and your day pass _is not valid_ for these events.

Do I need to be a writer to enjoy the festival?

Not at all. Byron Writers Festival is about ideas and conversation and is for readers, writers and thinkers of all ages and walks of life. Many attend to hear contemporary writers, engage with new ideas, meet other curious-minded people and fall in love with new books.

What’s changing in 2026?

Byron Writers Festival will return to the heart of Byron Bay in 2026. It will be hosted across multiple local venues in the Festival Precinct and includes exciting free community programming on the iconic Byron foreshore.

What is your ticket refund and exchange policy?

In the unlikely event that Byron Writers Festival 2026 does not proceed, you will be offered a refund for all passes including parking.

‍

Unfortunately we are unable to swap or change passes once they have been issued.

What transport options to the precinct are available?

Getting to the Byron Writers Festival will include a range of transport options including a regular festival shuttle from the Cavanbah Centre to the precinct, as well as the Byron Solar Train from North Beach Station. Carpooling is encouraged and public transport is encouraged where possible to reduce congestion and environmental footprint.

What happens if it rains during the festival?

The majority of festival events are held indoors. In the event of extreme weather conditions the Festival will follow a wet weather plan. Details will be released closer to the event.

Can I volunteer with the festival?

Yes, we love our volunteers, they are the heart and soul of our festival. Applications generally open in May each year.

For more information on how to get involved, see our [volunteer page](https://www.byronwritersfestival.com/get-involved/volunteer). Make sure to sign up to our mailing list and socials to stay in the know.

How can I get on the program of the Byron Writers Festival?

Thanks for your interest, Byron Writers Festival is curated by our Artistic Director and programming committee, in wide consultation with publishers and industry bodies. Participation is by invitation only. The Programming Committee does not accept unsolicited submissions, and due to the large quantity of messages we receive, we are not always able to reply to individual pitches. The program gives a broad definition to the concept of writing and incorporates many genres.

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67beff1f653304c10c2c4879/683d203c833af33b42568f7f_I45A3532%201.webp)

Support us

Byron Writers Festival is Australia's largest regional literature festival and the beating heart of the Northern Rivers' intellectual and cultural life.  
  
Byron Writers Festival is a registered charity with DGR status. All donations over $2 are tax deductible.

# Transport to Nimbin

### Getting to Nimbin by car, bus, train or flying carpet.

## Looking for a lift to Nimbin?

Join our **Facebook** groups and pages:

[Nimbin MardiGrass Rideshare](https://www.facebook.com/groups/748951941867955/)

[Facebook Event](https://www.facebook.com/events/423541350320171/)

[Official Facebook Page](https://www.facebook.com/nimbinmardigrass/)

[Official Facebook Group](https://www.facebook.com/groups/nimbinmardigrass)

## Getting to Nimbin By Car

Located inland of Byron Bay and to the north of Lismore, Nimbin is easily accessed by car. The village is within a 1.5-hour drive of both the Gold Coast and Byron Bay and 30 minutes from Lismore. Recommend that drivers join and check this Facebook group: [**Nth coast RDT locations**](https://www.facebook.com/groups/1592575741045251/)  Or invite a designated driver? MardiGrass is a wonderful experience for non-cannabis lovers too!

[Nth Coast RDT Locations](https://www.facebook.com/groups/1592575741045251/)

## Flying in on your Magic Carpet

*   Nimbin’s closest airport is [**Lismore Regional Airport**](https://www.lismore.nsw.gov.au/Community/Lismore-Regional-Airport), serviced by [Regional Express Airlines (REX)](https://www.rex.com.au/).
    
*   The [**Gold Coast Airport**](https://www.goldcoastairport.com.au/) in Coolangatta is located 81 kilometres to the north, just over the border to South East Queensland. The drive south to Nimbin meanders through some of the [Green Cauldron](http://www.visitscenicrim.com.au/about-us/australias-green-cauldron/)’s most stunning landscapes and picturesque villages.
    
*   Alternatively, the [**Ballina Byron Gateway Airport**](https://ballinabyronairport.com.au/), 65 kilometres east of Nimbin, transports visitors to and from the heart of the Northern Rivers and is just minutes away from some of Australia’s most iconic beaches.
    

## By Bus

*   ### **Lismore-Nimbin**
    
    Operates **Monday to Friday ONLY.** No service on Saturday and Sunday  
    [**Link to Timetable**](https://www.buslinesgroup.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/NR-Nimbin-Timetable-010425.pdf)  
    [Northern Rivers Buslines](https://www.buslinesgroup.com.au/northern-rivers/timetables/)  
    02 6626 1499

    Operates **Monday to Friday ONLY.** No service on Saturday and Sunday  
    [**Link to Timetable**](https://www.goselsbusservice.com.au/bus-timetable)  
    [Gosel’s Bus Service](https://irp.cdn-website.com/3670bb95/files/uploaded/Timetable%20PDF.pdf)0427 149 689

## MardiGrass Day Pass

[Buy Tickets](https://tickets.oztix.com.au/outlet/event/3335c2d5-6bf2-480b-a739-08c49c861154)

## Tickets & Check-in

How to collect your entry armband.

#### [Armband entry](https://nimbinmardigrass.com/attend/tickets/#feb74112da23d03bb)

### **We need your support, please buy your armband for entry.**

Available online or from the Info Desk at the front of Nimbin Town Hall all MardiGrass weekend.

MardiGrass has always been about trust but it doesn’t happen all by itself. Months of preparation and ground work go into the weekend so the village as a whole benefits as well as the thousands of visitors. We’d like it to happen in such a way that everyone who attends it has an uplifting experience. Accordingly, MardiGrass asks that everyone understands the critical importance of buying armbands. Without you buying armbands we are history. Some businesses even give preferential service to armband wearers and we support that. We need your support. Please buy one!!

#### [Camping pass per person](https://nimbinmardigrass.com/attend/tickets/#00f80b76d13dfa1e5)

Camping passes are per-person, NOT per-vehicle or per-tent.

#### [Camping check-in](https://nimbinmardigrass.com/attend/tickets/#5e396b2e85c74b5db)

To collect your armband and claim a camping spot:

*   Go to the Nimbin Showgrounds at [33 Cecil Street, Nimbin.](https://maps.app.goo.gl/qEuBdivWNrbFjPrk9)
*   Identify yourself with your PayPal receipt. (Printed copy or on your phone)
*   Or show identification (eg driver’s licence etc) in the name of the purchaser.

#### [Event only check-in](https://nimbinmardigrass.com/attend/tickets/#c0d1bbda6a0c5fe72)

To collect your event armband:

*   Go to the Nimbin Town Hall at Cullen Street, Nimbin.
*   Identify yourself with your PayPal receipt. (Printed copy or on your phone)
*   Or show identification (eg driver’s licence etc) in the name of the purchaser.

#### [$30 day tickets](https://nimbinmardigrass.com/attend/tickets/#3978c8ba7aa4c8c1c)

During Mardigrass, there are **$30 Day Tickets** available from the Information Desk at the front of the Nimbin Town Hall.  Day Tickets are not pre-sold online, and are only available in-person in Nimbin.

#### [$30 tickets for Nimbin locals](https://nimbinmardigrass.com/attend/tickets/#b7bb5517a8df821ea)

From Monday 29 April, **locals may purchase $30 MardiGrass armbands** from the Nimbin Hemp Embassy, or from the Town Hall Info Desk over the MardiGrass weekend. For our purpose, the definition of “local” is the 2480 post code.  These tickets are not pre-sold online, and are only available in-person in Nimbin.

## Camping Guidelines

Camping at Nimbin Showgrounds

[**Golden Bud pass for $150 per person**](https://nimbinmardigrass.com/attend/tickets/) includes 3-nights camping – Friday, Saturday and Sunday nights at the **Nimbin Showgrounds,** plus entry to all MardiGrass events!

#### [Cost per person](https://nimbinmardigrass.com/attend/tickets/#54abe7deeb5765556)

Camping bookings are **per person**, not per vehicle or per tent.

Camping is also available at the [Nimbin Showgrounds,](http://nimbinshowsociety.org.au/index.php/camping/) before and after MardiGrass.

#### [Children 12 and under](https://nimbinmardigrass.com/attend/tickets/#47684d51135e22108)

Children twelve years and under are **FREE** for both camping and entry to MardiGrass.

#### [Arrival time](https://nimbinmardigrass.com/attend/tickets/#bf4cbe012929ef295)

We do ask that campers **arrive before dark** to ensure the safety of themselves and other campers when setting up.

#### [Camping in designated areas](https://nimbinmardigrass.com/attend/tickets/#cc2527370fb75253e)

Camping only in designated areas. There are three camping areas set aside:

1.  Quiet area
2.  Reasonably noisy area
3.  Family area

Keep your space clean and tidy – garbage bags provided.

#### [Camping in tents and vehicles](https://nimbinmardigrass.com/attend/tickets/#f489705fb9c2f5a30)

Bring your own campervan, caravan or tent.

#### [Powered sites](https://nimbinmardigrass.com/attend/tickets/#3c280a834be8a0130)

There are a small number of powered sites – first come, first served!

Camping is also available before and after MardiGrass. Book with [Nimbin Showgrounds.](http://nimbinshowsociety.org.au/index.php/camping/)

#### [Facilities](https://nimbinmardigrass.com/attend/tickets/#ed628043b5c9cc52f)

Facilities include powered and non-powered sites, a camp kitchen (refrigerator, microwave, kettle, sink, and free electric barbecue), toilets, hot showers, and a rotary clothesline. We also have a dedicated dump point for the benefit of motorhome operators.

#### [Noise restrictions](https://nimbinmardigrass.com/attend/tickets/#d14bfff642e286038)

Please keep noise in camping areas to a respectable level – be considerate of your neighbours.

*   No generators!
*   No loud drumming after midnight!
*   No barking dogs please!

#### [Pets](https://nimbinmardigrass.com/attend/tickets/#7796e64d95e8448c8)

We recommend that you do NOT bring pets, however owners may do so at your own risk.

*   No dogs please!

#### [Canteen](https://nimbinmardigrass.com/attend/tickets/#0860fb368c566b447)

The canteen will be open all weekend!

*   **Friday, Saturday and Sunday**
*   **7:00am to 7:00pm**

#### [Camp fires](https://nimbinmardigrass.com/attend/tickets/#fee20263ef989648a)

Open fires are to be restricted to central communal fire area.

*   No private or individual fires in the camp area.
*   Please refrain from having fires in the day – it’s only wasting valuable firewood.

#### [Emergencies](https://nimbinmardigrass.com/attend/tickets/#422ca659412c24ea3)

*   First aid and fire extinguishers available at the Canteen.
*   Emergency assembly area is at front entrance parking area.

*   **Australia-wide Emergency number:** 000
*   **Hospital:** 6688 1400  
    35 Cullen St, Nimbin
*   **Police:** 6627 6400  
    38 Cullen Street, Nimbin

#### [Camping before & after MardiGrass](https://nimbinmardigrass.com/attend/tickets/#ae46607723557c1d5)

Camping is also available at the [**Nimbin Showgrounds**](http://nimbinshowsociety.org.au/index.php/camping/), before and after MardiGrass.

*   **Address:** 33 Cecil Street, Nimbin NSW 248
*   **Email:** [nimbinshow2@y7mail.com](mailto:nimbinshow02@y7mail.com)
*   **Phone:** 0457 61 44 33
*   **Hours:** An on-site  caretaker is present but it is preferred that you arrive during daylight hours if possible.

# Get Involved

## Join the community

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67beff1f653304c10c2c4879/683d203c833af33b42568f7f_I45A3532%201.webp)

Our mission is to enrich and transform the lives of our community through writing and ideas – and your support is essential.

Byron Writers Festival is Australia's largest regional literature festival and the beating heart of the Northern Rivers' intellectual and cultural life. We present year-round author talks, writing workshops and schools programs in addition to our renowned annual festival.  
  
We invite you to join our community by [subscribing to our mailing list](https://mailchi.mp/byronwritersfestival/subscribe-to-byron-writers-festival), becoming a [Festival Friend](https://events.humanitix.com/festival-friend-membership-2026), volunteering, donating, or becoming a valued partner or patron.

# MardiGrass Market Stalls

### Apply to bring your market stall to MardiGrass

### Thank you for your interest in running a market stall at Nimbin MardiGrass 2026! We encourage any interested stalls to apply as early as possible. MardiGrass always fills our markets area to capacity, and we expect the same for 2026.

ALL market stalls, including food stalls, **are within the ticketed area**: the dedicated MardiGrass venue PLANTEM PARK, behind the HEMP Embassy and Town Hall, featuring the HEMP Olympix, music, comedy and other entertainment in Sativa Stadium; unless otherwise pre-organised. The park also hosts Indica Arena which is an educational space featuring Hemposium talks, the Industrial Hemp Expo, and medican advice and information.

# General Market Stalls – CLOSED

2026 General Stalls Applications CLOSED

# Food Stalls – CLOSED

2026 Food Stalls Applications CLOSED

**We invite vendors of hemp and cannabis related products, services and ideas.** MardiGrass gives priority to stalls showcasing:

*   Hemp food
    
*   Hemp clothing
    
*   Hemp building
    
*   Hemp body care and natural health products
    
*   Industrial hemp technologies
    
*   Cannabis culture
    
*   Gardening
    

**We also welcome educational stalls providing:**

*   Cannabis law reform advocacy
    
*   Medical cannabis advice and information
    

**We invite local vendors to showcase the creative, innovative and alternative spirit of Nimbin and the Northern Rivers region.**

## Information for Stallholders

All the information below is also available as a **[PDF document on this link](https://nimbinmardigrass.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/2025_Market_Stall_Information.pdf).**

[Stallholder Information](https://nimbinmardigrass.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/2026_Nimbin_Mardigrass_Stall_Info-2-Apr.pdf)

#### Deadlines

*   **NOW CLOSED! 15 March 2026** – Food Stall Applications
    
*   **31 March 2026** – Stalls bringing cool rooms must confirm the cool room by this date.
    
*   **NOW CLOSED! 1st April 2026 –** General and Campaign stall applications
    
*   **15th April 2026 –** Payment for stalls
    
*   **15th April 2026** – Showgrounds camping confirmation and payment, if applicable
    
*   Your stall will NOT be confirmed until payment is received. No stall fees will be collected during MardiGrass.
    

#### Stall Fees

#### Extra Staff & Camping Tickets

*   The stall fees include staff as per the numbers in the table above.
*   **Additional** staff tickets are available for $50 per person.
*   We have very little room for camping behind your stall, so we would prefer you either camp inside your stall, or down at the Showgrounds. Any behind-stall camping must be approved in advance.
*   If required, **camping tickets** at the Nimbin Showgrounds are available at $50 per person per night. **Camping** is an **extra/additional charge** to the stall fee. To request camping tickets, please email [\[email protected\]](https://nimbinmardigrass.com/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#5c3235313e3532313d2e38353b2e3d2f2f1c3439312c39313e3d2f2f2572323928) .
*   Deadline for purchasing any additional staff or camping tickets is **15th April**.

#### Arrival time and departure times

*   The market site will be open for setting up on **Friday 1st May from 8am**.
*   Your stall must be set up by **5pm Friday 1st May,** and all vehicles must be offsite by this time. You may only park with your stall if this has been previously confirmed, and if so, your car must remain in the market area until at least **8pm on Sunday night 3rd May** (preferably until **10pm,** after the final act finishes in this area. If you have reasons why you may need to leave early, please discuss this with the market co-operator in advance).
*   Stalls must be packed down and off site **no later** than **10am Monday 4th May,** preferably by **9am** if possible. (The locals would prefer their carparks be accessible again as early as possible!)
*   Please leave your stall site clean. Messy stall sites after the festival will be noted and considered in the selection process in future years.
*   Be aware that Nimbin village is still doing business as usual on Friday, and again on Monday.

#### Running Times / Lighting

*   Standard opening hours are **5pm – 10pm** on Friday; **8am – 10pm** on Saturday and Sunday.
*   This is also a night market, so stallholders must be willing to trade into the evenings.
*   Stalls usually close around **9-10pm**, but you are welcome to trade longer. Noise restrictions apply after 10pm. You may also open earlier for trading that 8am if desired.
*   You **must** organise your own lighting for night time trading, either via battery powered lights or via your pre-organised 10amp power lead.
*   **Power may also be limited after 10pm,** so please bring solar or battery powered lighting if you think you will trade later into the night.

#### Insurance / Site Safety / Dig Limit Policy

*   All stalls must have their own insurance. We prefer $20mil indemnity but will accept $10mil also. We will request that you email us your insurance certificate in advance.
*   No ground piercing items can be placed deeper than 20 cm without management approval. **DO NOT** bring starpickets or posts and pierce the ground. Please bring sandbags or other weighting systems to stabilise your marquee from wind etc.
*   You alone are responsible for your property and must ensure that products are secure overnight.
*   No dogs or other non–native animals are allowed on site. Please leave your pets with a carer for the weekend.
*   Market Stall holders **must** follow any additional directives from MardiGrass staff during the festival to keep everyone safe.

#### Stall Space

*   No changes are permitted to General/Non-Food stall space **after 15 April** as we have to report all details to council.
*   The size of the stall you have indicated in your application is important! This is the size of the total space allocated to you, including your back of house space. **The space we have for stalls is limited.** If you arrive and want more space, we **won’t** be able to help.
*   Stall spaces will be marked out and tagged for each stall holder to outline your allocated space.
*   Please do not encroach on your neighbour’s stall site. Any special placement requests must be made to the market stalls coordinator before the event.

## Food Stalls

*   Lismore City Council requires a list of food stalls 6 weeks before event, so the application deadline for food stalls is **15 March 2026**.
*   Stalls bringing cool rooms must confirm that you are bringing a cool room by **31 March 2026.** If you turn up on the day with a cool room without telling us, you won’t be able to set up the cool room.
*   Please also let us know in advance if you will have an internal fridge that requires power overnight.
*   Food stalls **must** hold both a **[NSW FSS certificate](https://www.foodauthority.nsw.gov.au/retail/fss-food-safety-supervisors/fss-certificates)** and **[Lismore City Council Food (LCC) Permit](https://lismore.nsw.gov.au/regulations-for-temporary-food-stalls-mobile-vendors-and-market-stallholders)** in order to operate a food stall at Nimbin Mardigrass. We will not accept applications from food stalls without these NSW permits.
*   QLD or other state FSS certificates are **not** relevant and out of area food stalls take time for LCC to process. Please organise these in advance.
*   Food stalls **must bring** at least 4 x20L wastewater containers, which are emptied as needed by waste crew into designated commercial grease traps.
*   There is a **no glass policy** for all food stalls.
*   Food stalls should provide biodegradable tableware only.

We also prefer food stalls which use hemp ingredients. With many more food stall enquiries than sites available, preference will be given to those applicants that fulfill the following criteria:

*   Promote and use hemp seed, oil and other hemp ingredients (now legal!)
    
*   Locally owned (or containing locally grown produce) within the Northern Rivers region
    
*   Doesn’t duplicate permanent Nimbin village food businesses
    
*   Promotes healthy food
    
*   Self contained/ no power or very low power consumption
    
*   Regular Nimbin market stallholders
    
*   Returning/ regular MardiGrass supporters
    
*   Zero or minimum waste. Only compostable/ recycled packaging
    
*   No Coca Cola/Amatil/Pepsi Co. products or bottled water.  
    _We are planning to have a water refilling station on site, and would prefer healthy alternatives such as kombucha and coconut water, etc, for our patrons, and for the Earth!_
    

#### Power Supply and Electrical Safety

*   Stalls with cool rooms are charged more for their stall space to compensate for significant energy consumption.
*   If you’re also using other high-current items like fryers or bain maries, **please make sure that you let us know in the application form.** There may be additional upfront costs if necessary.
*   Generator power will be switched off from 10pm – 7am. **Only cool rooms are guaranteed to have power from 10pm-7am**, if you require power for lighting or other reasons outside of these times, you may have to use your own batteries, etc. (This includes internal **fridges** that require overnight power – you **must** organise this in advance.)
*   As a standard safety measure, all appliances and leads **must be tested and tagged** before use at the event. Please do this before you arrive! Our onsite electrician will not have time to assist you.
*   Any electrical appliances not compliant with the test and tag process must be removed from the market stall site.
*   Failure to comply with this requirement will lead to discontinuation of your power supply.
*   Please make sure that you minimise the amount of electricity you use. Choose lower electricity lights rather than spotlights. Halogen lights or flood lights will **not** be allowed as there are plenty of alternatives.

**IMPORTANT – PLEASE BRING**

*   **50m of extension lead per line** of power you need and any required power boards for your stall.
*   Please make sure that you have **large cable ties** to affix cords to your stall. Power leads cannot be threaded through marquee frames, but must be loosely suspended by cable ties so they can be easily removed in an emergency.

#### Sound Systems / Amplified Music

*   Market Stalls are permitted to set up small sound systems to create a good vibe in their stall.
*   Volume and music choice should be respectful to stall neighbours.
*   Permitted running times of sound systems are **8am to 10pm**. No amplified music is permitted in market stalls after 10pm.
*   Market Stall holders **must** follow any additional directives from MardiGrass staff during the event regarding amplified music running times and volume levels.

#### Products that are NOT allowed

*   Any Coca-Cola Amatil (Sprite, Fanta etc), or Pepsi Co. product.
    
*   Bottled water (unless pre-approved)
    
*   Toy guns or other child’s pretend weapons
    
*   Please be aware that this list is not complete. If there are any issues, the markets coordinator will contact you upon receipt of your application.

# About Us

## Australia’s favourite regional meeting place of storytelling and ideas

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67beff1f653304c10c2c4879/683af3aef6c82555d8b15b96_DSCF7468.jpg)

Byron Writers Festival is the largest regional writers festival in Australia.  
  
We showcase writers from around the world, representing all aspects of contemporary literature, especially First Nations writing and ways of knowing, environment, politics, philosophy, art, history and society.  
  
We are proud of our regionality, and ambitious in our approach to creating transformative experiences for artists and audiences.

## What We Do

Established in 1995, at the heart of the Northern Rivers, the festival and year-round programs engage tens of thousands of audience members annually to develop and promote literature from and in the region.  
  
Our artistic vision is to deliver world-class programs that provide transformative experiences for authors and audiences, and to ensure everybody is able to enjoy a life enriched by books, stories and ideas.  
  
Byron Writers Festival delivers profound cultural, social and economic impact to NSW and Australia. We present a major cultural event in regional NSW, which 50% of our audience travels to attend. We support the careers of writers, a culture of literature and literacy, and experience tourism in our region.  
  
Through our vibrant year-round program, we celebrate diverse Australian writers and stories, engage audiences with new ideas, and enhance access to literature and literacy for people regionally and nationally.  
  
Join our [mailing list](https://mailchi.mp/byronwritersfestival/subscribe-to-byron-writers-festival) and stay up to date on festival news and competitions.

## Our Vision & Mission

Lives transformed by writing and ideas.  
  
To present world-class gatherings that enrich and transform the lives of our audiences and community.

## Our Values

Connection

We connect writers with their readers in powerful gatherings, and emerging writers with the publishing industry. We are active agents in the cultural ecosystem by partnering widely, connecting our home in Byron Shire with the world.

Ambition

We are proud of our regionality and believe in presenting world-class literary gatherings for all audiences to enjoy. We host the best local, national and international writers at an impressive and unique festival. We develop a love of storytelling and literacy for future generations.

Nature

Our site-specific festival connects readers and writers to the spectacular natural environment of Bundjalung Country. We are deeply committed to place and the honouring of Country, and to furthering environmental causes, climate justice, and sustainable practices.

Authenticity

Our festival is identifiably 'Northern Rivers' in nature and style, reflecting our respect for the environment, community, and artistic practice, and we seek out partners with aligned values. We create genuine moments of human connection and provide the highest level of artist and audience care.

# Legal Advice

### Legal advice including roadside drug testing and medicinal cannabis in NSW

![Legal Advice](https://nimbinmardigrass.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/hempsoim-legal-advice.jpg)

_Steve Bolt, Solicitor & Author_

### In Summary

Cannabis is still an illegal drug in NSW – mostly.

The “mostly” is because many people are now able to access medicinal cannabis on prescription, which is obviously lawful. That is the only exception. But then you have to comply strictly with the terms of the prescription. Otherwise, your possession and use of cannabis remains against the law.

Having a prescription for example does not entitle you to possess cannabis from the black market, only cannabis that has been provided by your doctor.

So, mostly, it is a criminal offence to possess or use or supply or cultivate cannabis.

Cannabis is listed on the schedule of “prohibited drugs” under the NSW drug law (proper name the Drug Misuse and Trafficking Act 1985). It is listed separately for leaf (which includes flowers and buds), resin, oil and growing plants. There are different offence categories based on weight (or number of plants), ranging from “small quantity” to “large commercial quantity”.

So, except as allowed under prescription, any activity involving cannabis – possessing it, using it, growing it or supplying it – is illegal.  Supply and cultivation offences are considered more serious than possession. And the larger the quantity involved, the higher the likely penalty.

Police can issue a caution for possession of 15 grams or less. A caution means that there is no charge, so no court and no criminal conviction. You have to give the police your name and address. There are some rules about who qualifies to receive a caution – such as not having a prior record, and not having more than 2 previous cautions – but even if you “qualify”, giving a caution rather than laying a charge for possession is a discretionary decision for the police officer.

### Medicinal cannabis

There is no blanket rule that allows cannabis use for medicinal purposes. If you do not have a prescription, the same laws apply to cannabis used for medicinal purposes as for cannabis used for other reasons. Sometimes Courts will apply some leniency to cases involving non-prescribed medicinal cannabis; sometimes they won’t.

### Driving and saliva testing

It is an offence to drive a vehicle with the presence of THC (or methamphetamine, MDMA or cocaine) in your saliva.  It does not matter how much or how little. The penalty is a fine and probably what’s worse, disqualification of your licence for a period of 3 months.

The police do not have to prove that you were impaired by the drug, only that the drug was present. (There is a separate offence of driving under influence.) THC can be detected in saliva for days after using it.

The police can legally stop and drug test drivers randomly- that is, without having any particular reason. If the saliva swab shows positive, you are required to undergo a second test. The police take a saliva sample and use a machine for preliminary analysis. If the machine shows positive, the police give you a notice not to drive for 24 hours. If negative, you are simply free to go.  But either way, that sample is sent to the government laboratory for analysis – and almost always comes back as positive.

Offenders with good driving records might have no conviction recorded, and so keep their licences. However, you can only receive the benefit of that provision once every 5 years.

If the result is positive to THC, police will issue an on the spot fine and 3 month disqualification.  You then have to elect to take the matter to court if you want to challenge the penalty or guilt. Offenders with good driving records might have no conviction recorded, and so keep their licences. However, you can only receive the benefit of that provision once every 5 years.

It is a defence to this charge if the Court accepts that you had an honest belief that you did not have THC present in your saliva at the time you were driving, and that belief was held on reasonable grounds.

### Possession

To prove possession, the police must prove beyond reasonable doubt that you had the cannabis in your custody or under your legal control, and you knew you had it.

Depending on the circumstances, it might (or might not) be difficult for the prosecution to prove that you knew about the presence of the drug.

That is why the police will always try to get you to talk – to get you to make admissions that you knew you had the cannabis in your bag or whatever – things they otherwise might find difficult to prove.

In cases where more than one person has access to the cannabis – for example, in a communal area in a shared house or in a car with several passengers – the police must rule out, beyond reasonable doubt, the possibility that someone else might be the person in possession.

### Supply

Supply includes selling, giving away and agreeing to supply. Sharing cannabis is supply. Supply is treated as a serious offence and of course the penalties get quite severe for supply on a commercial scale.

If the police prove that you were in possession of 300 grams or more of cannabis, you are “deemed” to be in possession for supply and you must prove otherwise (for example, that it was for your personal use).

Charges involving higher amounts are dealt with in the District Court where higher penalties apply and jail is more likely.

### Cultivation and possession of plants

Cultivating means some activity to assist growing or harvesting the plant. Cultivating cannabis can include planting or watering or fertilising. But there is also an offence of possessing cannabis plants, where for example, the plants were grown on your property with your consent. The same penalty range applies for cultivation or possession of plants.

There are higher maximum penalties – and trial by judge and jury – for cultivating or possessing more than 250 plants (outdoors). Cases involving fewer than 250 plants are heard by a magistrate in the Local Court.

### Growing hydroponically

There is a separate offence in NSW law of cultivating “by enhanced indoor means” (that is, hydroponically). The maximum penalties are a lot higher than for cultivating an equivalent number of plants outdoors.

For offences involving between 5 and 50 plants grown indoors, the maximum penalty is the same as for commercial cultivation, but the police must prove the indoor cultivation was “for a commercial purpose”. If there are more than 50 plants, the commercial purpose is basically assumed and the maximum penalty is the same as for large commercial outdoor cultivation.

### More about cautions

Police have a discretion to issue a caution (instead of taking you to court) for small possession charges only. If you are found in possession of less than 15 grams of cannabis “leaf” (but not oil or resin) AND you have no prior convictions AND you admit that the cannabis is yours, you might get a police caution (which is not recorded as a conviction). If you are cautioned a second time, you must attend compulsory drug counselling. On the third occasion, you must go to court.

The cautioning guidelines for young people under 18 are slightly more generous.

### What can the police do?

You do not have to say anything to the police, whether you have been arrested or not.

You might say something like, ‘I do not wish to say anything until I get legal advice”. Beware of small talk and being lured into a conversation. Just tell them your name and address.

If you admit anything (or say something that sounds like you’re admitting something), the police can use that in evidence against you.

### Searches

Police are legally entitled to enter and search private property only if they have a search warrant, or if they are invited in by one of the occupiers – not necessarily and owner or tenant.

The police have the power to search you personally, or search your vehicle, without a warrant, if the police believe on reasonable grounds that you might be in possession of cannabis (or other prohibited drug).

### Sniffer dogs

The police sometimes use sniffer dogs for drug detection. In some places (in licensed premises, at dance parties and music festivals, on trains and buses, and on or near railway stations and bus terminals), the police can use sniffer dogs without a warrant.  Otherwise – for example for general street operations – police need to get a warrant to use a sniffer dog.

If a dog indicates to the police handler the presence of drugs, the police will then use that as the basis to search you and your bag.

### Likely penalties

The law sets out maximum penalties for the different offences, but the actual penalty imposed in a particular case depends on the circumstances of the case. The most significant factors are usually the type of offence (that is supply, cultivation or possession), the quantity of cannabis involved and whether you have any prior convictions. You should expect a reduced penalty for pleading guilty.

The penalties available includes fines, good behaviour bonds, intensive corrections orders and jail. The court can also decide to find someone guilty of an offence but record no conviction (under a provision known as “section 10”). This might be applied where the quantity is small and the person’s record is very good.

Generally speaking, supply and cultivation offences are considered more serious and are punished more heavily than possession offences.

A first offender pleading guilty to possession of a small amount of cannabis might have no conviction recorded, or get a fine. Someone convicted of supply for profit, especially if it is not their first supply offence, would be looking at jail terms of years.

**The best advice? TAKE CARE !!**
