Beer, music and community spirit are coming together as we throw open the gates to our Murwillumbah brewery for a family-friendly Open Day on Saturday, 29 August.

From 11am–5pm, we’re inviting the Northern Rivers community to join us at Murwillumbah for an afternoon of fresh beer, live music, local food, brewery tours and plenty of fun for the whole family.

Entry is free and all ages are welcome, with free buses running from Murwillumbah and Tweed Heads to help you get to and from the brewery.

This year, we’re celebrating the hometown launch of Northern Rivers Lager – right here at the brewery where it’s made.

We’ll also be pouring an extremely limited Swamp Beer Pilot Batch, available exclusively on tap at Murbah.

Swamp Beer pays tribute to one of Murwillumbah’s great local stories. This year marks 25 years since a beer truck ended up in the Tweed River over a long weekend, prompting a group of cheeky locals to dive in and swim the precious cargo back to shore.

There’ll be live music throughout the day, featuring TV Misery, Hayley Grace Trio from Bay Collective, O and Shae, and emerging local artist Ike.

Want to see what happens behind the brewery doors? Guided brewery tours will run at 12pm, 1pm, 2pm and 3pm, with our crew on hand to answer questions about brewing, packaging and some of the recent upgrades to our Murwillumbah brewery.

Come hungry too. 2020 Smokehouse BBQ and Gunter’s Flammkuchen will be serving up food throughout the day.

For the little ones, there’ll be face painting, kids' activities and Malt Disney entertainment, making it a day the whole family can enjoy.

Raising a glass for our community

Most importantly, Murbah is about celebrating and supporting the community we call home.

The event will help raise funds for local organisations Tweed Palliative Support & Wedgetail Retreat and The Family Centre, supporting the important work they do across our region.

So round up your family and mates, jump on one of the free buses and come spend the day with us.

Murbah  
Saturday, 29 August | 11am–5pm  
Stone & Wood Brewery, 35 Kite Crescent, South Murwillumbah  
Free entry | All ages welcome

Come for the beer, stay for the yarns.

Another Festival of the Stone has come and gone, and what a weekend it was.

Festival of the Stone has always been more than a beer festival. It's a celebration of community, creativity and the people who make this place what it is. [![Hells Bells and High Lines: Easter Awakens at Bells Beach](//stoneandwood.com.au/cdn/shop/articles/bells2.jpg?v=1745296572&width=533)](https://stoneandwood.com.au/blogs/all/hells-bells-and-high-lines-easter-awakens-at-bells-beach)

![Hells Bells and High Lines: Easter Awakens at Bells Beach](//stoneandwood.com.au/cdn/shop/articles/bells2.jpg?v=1745296572&width=533)

For surfers, Bells Beach at Easter conjures images of cold Southern Ocean, long lines of swell, and fresh northwest offshores blowing off the adjacent farmland and through the moonah trees.

Well not so much this year.

The opening day of the Rip Curl Pro at Bells felt positively sub-tropical. Walking down the hill toward Bells, the sea breeze had a warm wash to it and the sun, when it caught you, bit hard. Even the water temp is currently sitting around 18 degrees – boardshorts for the brave, three-two full suits for the rest. If you weren’t facing due south staring out at the Antarctic sub latitudes, you could swear you were back on the North Coast.

![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0256/5498/4783/files/Stone_Wood_AfternoonDelight_Bells25_TC_1Z9A0724.png?v=1745292507)

Bells Beach has been known as Djarrak for tens of thousands of years to the Waddawurrung people, Djarrak meaning ‘elbow’, the headland appearing as a bend in the coastline. It was a place to gather shellfish and gather, generally. In more modern times, the small beach today known as Bells has been held in reverence by surfers who travel here to surf its icy lines.

That reverence rings out on Good Friday morning, shortly after first light as the bell tolls and the first notes of AC/DC’s _Hells Bells_ echo around the beach. The ceremonial playing of _Hells Bells_ to start the morning’s first heat at Bells began a couple of decades ago and has become iconic in its own right. An ancient landscape, a modern dance in the elements, a killer riff played by a grown man from Adelaide dressed as a schoolboy. Surfers in the water when it’s played have spoken about being lost out there in a powerful moment, forgetting they’re even surfing a heat.

The reality of course is that the annual Easter contest is a big deal, a stop on the world tour and a major sporting event that draws thousands of people from all over Victoria and beyond. Over the Easter weekend, Bells hums.

After parking on the adjacent farmland, you walk down the hill past the grandstands, coffee vans, the big screen and the gift shop, the air filled with the smell of deep fryers working overtime.

A full house will see 5000 Victorians fill the place. Many of them don’t know much about the sport of surfing, but as Victorians they know sport and they love sport, and they understand that Bells is the saltwater equivalent of an AFL final. They’ll sit on the beach all day, or at least until the high tide washes them away, applauding each wave and cheering on local favourites.

![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0256/5498/4783/files/Bells.jpg?v=1745291786)

The difference however is that at an AFL game you can’t run onto the ground and start kicking your own ball around. You can here. While the contest runs at Bells, a couple of hundred metres to the east the reef at Winkipop serves as a practise pitch. Punters can paddle out and mix it with the pros warming up for their heats.

On Good Friday, just before lunch, Jordy Smith took off up the top of the point at Winki. He soon hit top speed, pushing hard on his rails as he chicanes down the line, running a slalom course around several surfers watching the show and drifting into his line. No stress. Jordy is cool. On the way back up the point several people congratulate him on winning the last tour event, over in El Salvador. “Thanks, bru.”

After lunch, the crowds on the hill at Bells kick back.

It’s the first year Stone and Wood have come on as the official beer of the WSL world tour in Australia, but in their own relaxed way have billed themselves as the tour’s “unofficial” official beer. The open-air Stone & Wood bar sits halfway up the hill and feels unofficial. Surf fans from Prahran, Preston, Nunawading and Fitzroy tilt Pacific Ale cans as the sun drops lazily into the farm paddocks behind the contest.

![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0256/5498/4783/files/Stone_Wood_AfternoonDelight_Bells25_TC_1Z9A0724.jpg?v=1745292304)

Out in the Bells Bowl, the high tide has seen the contest go on hold but on the hill, nobody seems too bothered. It’s Friday afternoon with a full Easter weekend ahead. In place of contest heats, they’ve sent out a Stone & Wood “Afternoon Delight” twin-fin expression session. It’s supposed to be some lo-fi fun, but the reality is the modern twin is perfectly suited to the sloping walls of Bells, and some hi-fi surfing goes down. Some of it would win heats in the contest.

![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0256/5498/4783/files/Stone_Wood_AfternoonDelight_Bells25_TC_1Z9A0762.png?v=1745292573)

Bells is between weather systems right now, so the waves disappeared on Easter Saturday, and nobody seems to know when they’re due to return. Again, with a full Easter weekend in prospect, and a full town, nobody seems too concerned for now. The waves will turn up when they’re ready.

Words by Sean Doherty.

## Why do we celebrate [Festival of The Stone](https://stoneandwood.com.au/pages/festival-of-the-stone) every year?

Festival of the Stone 2024 will raise money for Byron Shire homeless hub, [Fletcher Street Cottage](https://www.byroncentre.com.au/fsc/fletcher-street-cottage). Byron Shire’s homelessness rate is currently the highest in NSW and Fletcher Street Cottage provides support, information, referral and advocacy to people at risk of homelessness and those already sleeping rough.  
  
Festival of the Stone began as a celebration of Stone & Wood’s annual release of Stone Beer and the first tapping of the keg. The 2024 Stone Beer brew is a wood-fired porter ideal for chilly winter nights. A nod to medieval brewing, it’s a tradition held dear since Stone & Wood’s humble beginnings, seventeen years ago.  
  
Every May since Stone & Wood began, alongside others in the brewing industry, Stone & Wood brews its woodfired porter [Stone Beer](https://stoneandwood.com.au/pages/stone-beer) in preparation for winter. This is called Stone Brew Day. A decadent porter with dark roasted malts is brewed to give coffee and dark chocolate flavours to the beer. Then, on an open fire, volcanic stones sourced from the nearby hinterland are heated, before being lowered, glowing-red into the kettle, which lends smoky caramel notes to the beer. The moment the woodfired stones touch the wort with a loud hisss is a moment for celebration. A month later, Stone Beer is tapped at the annual Festival of the Stone, where the community comes together to enjoy fresh beer, live music, good food and winter cheer.

## What food will be at Festival of The Stone?

Those in need of sustenance at Festival of the Stone are in for a treat with some very tasty options available. From handmade and freshly baked Byron Bay Pretzels to artisan pizza from Gunter’s Flammkuchen and delicious wurst from The Kranski Sisters food truck, you won’t go hungry! Plus, masters of the grill, Traegar will be on ground doing BBQ demos and sampling.

## Festival of The Stone is Family Friendly!

Bringing the ankle biters along? Festival of the Stone has that covered too with Malt Disney Art & Craft Zone. Malt Disney is a free style creative area where kids can let their maker imagination run wild with paints, collage, mask making, drawing, crown creating, play doh and more. Plus there’s garden games galore to keep them engaged and burning up that energy!  
  
For the easiest access to Festival of the Stone, catch the Festival Shuttle Service. For up-to-date information about road closures, parking and bus services check out the FAQ section on the website.

One of Australia’s most loved singer-songwriters [Dan Sultan](https://www.dansultan.com/)’s trophy shelf holds an incredible 7 ARIA Awards, alongside NIMA Awards, Top 5 ARIA-charting albums, and an ARIA-certified gold record. With countless sold-out headline shows in his wake, he’s also toured with the likes of Bruce Springsteen, Midnight Oil and Vance Joy, and played Australia’s biggest festivals including Splendour in the Grass, Blues Festival and Falls to name a few. He’ll add Festival of the Stone to that list on 1 June!

![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0256/5498/4783/files/10_dce830b9-af82-4f93-8abd-7c91a8d1362e_1024x1024.png?v=1716439650)

  
It’s almost impossible not to recognise a [Beddy Rays](https://open.spotify.com/artist/4qn6hSO1qLlaAW8jiyOw18?si=UpnfmYNjSfml_5FxxxW5SQ) track, a carefully curated recipe involving all the right ingredients: heartfelt lyrics, huge hooks, mosh-worthy riffs and a lingering sense of comradery and good vibes that underpins everything they create. It’s seen them land plays on triple j’s Hottest 100 and Hottest 100 Like a Versions of all time, an ARIA nomination for ‘Breakthrough Artist’ and spots on festivals around the country. With a knack for knowing how to have a bloody good time, everyone wants to be friends with Beddy Rays.

![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0256/5498/4783/files/12_8b67291d-27a9-4612-9d5b-6ed9a288139e_1024x1024.png?v=1716439650)

  
Ultimate purveyors "pub-pop" goodness, [The Beefs](https://www.thebeefs.com.au/about) founded their musical haven in 2018 when frontman Sammy Smith decided to round up some talented mates and cook up a musical feast for the ages. In the kitchen of their tunes, you'll find a dash of infectious pop melodies and a sprinkle of rock 'n' roll charm. Marinated together with catchy hooks and relatable lyrics, and voilà - you've got the signature sound of The Beefs. It's the kind of music that'll make you want to hoist a pint in one hand and dance with a mate in the other.

![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0256/5498/4783/files/14_1024x1024.png?v=1716439649)

  
Hailing from Perth, [VERGE COLLECTION](https://open.spotify.com/artist/1aQcyDr9KqWk7CIiv87E3o?si=MUsjngAaT86pGRoThN4akQ&nd=1&dlsi=0ab237ae5fb74c10) balance classic pop sensibilities with working class poetry to channel the collective conscious of suburban Australian milennials. Songwriter and front-man Ben Arnold’s songs have the ability to hoist you high to the point of chills and a stupid grin, before making you plummet just as quickly into an existential nosedive.

![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0256/5498/4783/files/FOTS_blog_1024x1024.png?v=1716439981)

  
[AKA Lui](https://open.spotify.com/artist/4ZCvesZqn6v6oJRBtvR5xx) seamlessly fuses disco and psychedelia to create a sound that is uniquely his own. His debut single catapulted him into the spotlight, earning critical acclaim and over 2 million streams on Spotify alone. Recent tracks like "Kick It", "Lighthouse", and "Fool" have continued to captivate audiences both in Australia and abroad and with the upcoming release of his debut EP Sapphire Blue on June 21st, AKA Lui is set to confirm his status as a rising star in Australian music.

![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0256/5498/4783/files/11_9c83e44c-8e76-47e8-99f8-7b179b5e5489_1024x1024.png?v=1716439650)

  
Bursting with sun-soaked melodies and an electric live set it’s no surprise that Brisbane (Meanjin) indie-pop 5-piece [Mid Drift](https://open.spotify.com/artist/6D1ONv6dkTpWhFK4Sfsf8F?si=ynkrei82RW6s4DreWktCpg&nd=1&dlsi=475210e4a5ef41f8) have quickly become a crowd favourite in their hometown and are gaining a loyal fan base interstate. Get a sneak preview of their debut EP Lemon, Lime and Tanlines when they open the stage at Festival of the Stone.

## Are DJs more your scene? Don't worry...Club Raiders has you covered!

[Cashew](https://soundcloud.com/djcashew-nut)’s infectious sounds are ready to take you on a joyous journey through house, tech house, deep house, RnB, hip-hop, funk and disco. Uplifting and exciting, each set from this party-starting pro masterfully weaves a mix of old school and new school. Cashew’s ability to read the room has dancefloors up and down the east coast pumping, delivering satisfaction every time.

Versatile, distinctive and relentlessly fun, a night with Cashew is one you won’t want to miss.

Bringing the heat, we've got [Yazmin](https://soundcloud.com/djyazmin_aus) on the lineup. With a career spanning back to 2013, Yazmin has rocked dance floors across Australia, Indonesia, and the UK. Now, back on home soil, she’s here to share her love for dance music and club favourites!

Her journey has taken her to some of London's hottest clubs and events, including Printworks with Amnesia Ibiza, Ministry of Sound, Egg Club, South West Four Festival and Electric Brixton, to name a few.

With additional sets from Bean Dip, Dan Muz, Reiflex, Mase vs. Kane, and Sammond, the vibes will be high amongst the brewing tanks...so if you're ready to get sweaty, the DJs will be spinning just the tunes to get you grooving. 

## Come celebrate the annual Release of Stone Beer

With meticulous care, we’ve created this limited-edition winter brew using the best ingredients we could find, including select Australian malts. Stone beer boasts aromatic notes of brewed coffee, rich dark chocolate, and hints of subtly smoked barley.

![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0256/5498/4783/files/4_cd77c7b6-787d-4d9b-a99b-62405e049e1b_1024x1024.png?v=1716436968)

## Grooving for a good cause

Festival of the Stone 2024 will raise money for Byron Shire homeless hub, Fletcher Street Cottage. Byron Shire’s homelessness rate is currently the highest in NSW and Fletcher Street Cottage provides support, information, referral and advocacy to people at risk of homelessness and those already sleeping rough.

![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0256/5498/4783/files/3_e800395d-0c81-4110-9ddb-cc6e4e58f6de_1024x1024.png?v=1716436968)

  
  
“We believe it’s a really important time to support Australian music, events and our community. With Splendour and other festivals having a year off, we’re injecting a little more love into the music side of things this year. Live music in Australia ain’t going anywhere. And with Byron having one of the highest homeless populations in the nation, now is as important as ever to support those sleeping rough. We’re happy to support Fletcher St Cottage’s incredible work in this area for the 10th year in a row.” – James Aris, Stone & Wood Marketing Manager.

![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0256/5498/4783/files/5_53fb43cd-b215-451f-b117-581448194750_1024x1024.png?v=1716436968)

We are so proud to be supporting our mates over at Pony Rider and The National Project as we bring to life the inaugural Wild For Wilderness Van Life festival. The goal of Pony Rider’s #TheNationalProject is to raise funds to support a ‘Land Buy Back’ scheme, where areas of land are bought to protect, regenerate, grow and create new Aussie National Parks.

Based in the Glenworth Valley and spread over two days, the Van Life event features adventure films and IRL adventures by day and live music under the stars by night. For the keen ones, there’s kayaking, hiking, mountain biking or horse riding, and for those feeling more zen, we’ve got breathwork, yoga and native food walks. Heading back into the campsite, there’s food trucks, cold beers, live music and good times.

Tickets are $150 per person and if sleeping in your wheels isn’t your thing, there’s a limited number of glamping sites too. 20% from ticket sales and all proceeds from the bar will be donated, along with other initiatives throughout the weekend.

We’re pumped to announce our mini beer festival, Murbah Open Day, is back for another year at our [Murwillumbah Brewery](https://stoneandwood.com.au/pages/murwillumbah "Stone & Wood Murwillumbah Brewery") on Saturday, 5 August. 

Welcoming locals and beer frothers from all over, Murbah Open Day is a celebration of community, great music, good food and of course, fresh beer straight from the source. 

The only day of year our brewery opens to the public, the festival gives punters the chance to peek behind the curtain of the Stone & Wood engine room, with staff guided tours of the brewery throughout the day.

Running from 11am - 5pm, Murbah Open Day is an event for the whole family and a chance to give back to the amazing community that supports us. 

Entry to the festival is by gold coin donation with all profits going towards an amazing local cause: [Wedgetail Retreat](https://www.tweedpalliativesupportandwedgetailretreat.com/ "Wedgetail Retreat").

Wedgetail Retreat provide free palliative care to the Northern Rivers community, giving locals and their families a warm and welcoming environment to call home. Operating without government funding, Wedgetail relies on the support of its community to keep its doors open and continue with the excellent care they provide.

# Festival Overview

[Winter Skate & Street Festival 2026](https://www.winterskatefest.com/) is a multi-weekend experience bringing together sport, culture and community at Noble Park Skatepark.

Taking place every Saturday and Sunday across June 2026, the event begins from 4:00 PM to 9:00 PM.

We welcome youth, families and the local skate community to enjoy an exciting lineup of skate competitions, a vibrant night market and vibing with live performances!

# **🎉**Sponsor Perks

Sponsors gain a chance to increase brand exposure to an estimated **50,000** visitors who will join in the festival. Sponsor activities may be and not limited to:

1.  Brand exposure (banners, signage)
2.  Booth or activation space
3.  Social media features
4.  On-site engagement opportunities
5.  Product placement or giveaways
6.  Naming rights for specific segments (e.g. competition days)

For further discussion, do [contact us](https://www.winterskatefest.com/visit-us/contact-us)!

### Digital Presence

Inclusion in event marketing campaigns

# Stone & Wood is the official beer partner of the World Surf League

Last updated: February 5, 2025

2 Mins Reader

We’re stoked to announce that Stone & Wood is the official beer partner for all major World Surf League events in Australia! 🍻

From the WSL Championship Tour stops at Bells Beach (VIC), Snapper Rocks (QLD), and Margaret River (WA) to the Newcastle Challenger Series and the World Longboard Tour at Bells, we’ll be pouring fresh, cold beers right next to the action.

But that’s not all. We’re also introducing the Stone  Wood Golden Hour—a sundowner session featuring a specialty heat where surf icons ride alternative boards shaped by local legends. Expect live music, panel talks, epic surf films and giveaways.

_“Coming from Byron Bay, Stone & Wood and surfing have always gone hand in hand. We’ve been part of the local surfing community from the outset and partnering with the WSL gives us the opportunity to take that natural connection to the beach lifestyle to coastal communities right across the country,”_ said Stone & Wood Head of Strategy  Creative, Paul Tansley.

The partnership will also be brought to life through broadcast integration, including the ‘Stone & Wood Post Show’ and the ‘Stone & Wood Slow-Mo’, as well as a content series titled ‘Stone & Wood Real Talk’ which will take fans behind the scenes of the competitor’s area and event village. This content will be distributed across WSL and Stone & Wood’s social channels.

_“WSL is thrilled to have Stone & Wood join as the official Beer of WSL Australia from 2025,”_ said Andrew Stark, WSL APAC President. _“They’re a brand that was born at the beach and lives and breathes the coastal lifestyle. That, coupled with their passion and focus on community, makes them a perfect partner for WSL. We look forward to seeing Stone  Wood bring this partnership to life at each of our events around Australia by creating moments and places where we can come together through surfing.”_

  
We can’t wait to bring good vibes, great beers, and unforgettable moments to the Australian leg of the WSL tour. See you on the sand. 🌊

## **Mud Trail 2026**

### Open Ceramic Studios - 22 & 23 of August

### **NEW!** Workshop Days - 21 & 24 of August

The North Coast Mud Trail invites you to explore the work and processes of 35 ceramic artists across 26 studios in the Northern Rivers region. 

New to the Mud trail, two additional days will be devoted to workshops at select studios on Friday 21st & Monday 24th. Details and registration for workshops is below.

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/623433d28e28f959fbacc840/f291729a-acc6-41d7-b329-38021522b4cc/benjamin_ruble_studio_2.jpg)

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/623433d28e28f959fbacc840/4249b4a1-9619-4cb5-bc6e-992c72a90ec6/NC+Mudtrail+Logo+V1.png)

#### **NEW WORKSHOP DAYS‍**

#### Friday 21 & Monday 24

#### Step inside the creative world of clay with 20 ticketed hands-on workshops across a diverse range of techniques and skill levels.

[2026 MUD TRAIL ARTISTS](https://www.northcoastceramics.com/2025-mudtrail-members)

[2026 WORKSHOP DETAILS & TICKETS](https://www.northcoastceramics.com/group-events)

This August, the much-loved North Coast Mud Trail expands into a four-day celebration of ceramics, creativity, and connection — giving art lovers even more reason to hit the road and explore Bundjalung’s thriving maker culture.

Traditionally known for its iconic open studio weekend, the Mud Trail now includes two additional days dedicated to specialised hands-on workshops, offering visitors the chance to step beyond observing and into creating. Across four inspiring days, ceramic enthusiasts, collectors, weekend wanderers and curious beginners can immerse themselves in the region’s rich clay community.

**What to Expect**

*   **Studio Open Days :** Get a rare look behind the scenes as artists open their working studios to the public. Get to know the people behind the pots — their techniques, inspirations, and studio secrets.  [View all participating potters profiles.](https://www.northcoastceramics.com/2025-mudtrail-members)
    
*   **NEW!** **Workshops:** Get hands on and take part in creative workshops with participating potters on Friday 21st and Monday 24th. Registration is required. [View the workshops schedule.](https://events.humanitix.com/north-coast-ceramics-mud-trail-2026)
    
*   **NEW!** **Exhibitions:** For the first time, the Mud Trail extends into gallery spaces across the region - four exhibitions, opening events and artist talks, showcasing the depth and calibre of ceramic practice in the Northern Rivers. [View the exhibition details here.](https://events.humanitix.com/north-coast-ceramics-mud-trail-2026)
    
*   **Demos & Artist Talks:**  Watch live demonstrations and artist talks to learn more about your favourite potter. [View the free event schedule.](https://www.northcoastceramics.com/group-events-1)
    

**Stay in the Loop & Plan Your Muddy Adventure**

*   **Plan Your Trail :** Pick up a hard copy of the 2026 Mud Map from local cafes, stores, galleries and tourist information centres (available in early July). An interactive map will be available soon to plan your route in advance.
    
*   [**Register now**](https://events.humanitix.com/north-coast-ceramics-mud-trail-2026) **to receive updates :** Register with Humanitix and go in the running to win three nights accommodation in the beautiful town of Bangalow, including access to a full ceramic studio (redeemable within 12 months).
    
*   **Stay in the know:** Check out our [facebook page](https://www.facebook.com/NorthCoastMudTrail) for details
    
*   **Subscribe:** to our newsletter (below) for all updates.

> The North Coast Ceramics Mud Trail is committed to creating an inclusive, welcoming and accessible experience for all visitors. We celebrate the diversity of our ceramics community and believe everyone should have the opportunity to connect with artists, explore studios and experience the creativity and joy of clay.
> 
> Our studios are unique working spaces, and accessibility varies across locations. Many studios offer wheelchair access; however, some have limited physical access due to natural terrain, steps, narrow spaces, or building constraints.
> 
> The following studios currently do not have wheelchair access: **Rainforest Ceramics, Safir Studio, Keramika, Jay Ceramics, The Hill Pottery and Sasa Ceramic Studio.**
> 
> We encourage visitors to check individual studio listings for accessibility details. If you have any questions or specific access requirements, please contact studios directly; our artists will be happy to assist wherever possible.

### North Coast Ceramics (NCC) is a vibrant community of professional ceramic artists living and working along the stunning North Coast of New South Wales.

Dedicated to promoting and sustaining the art of ceramics, NCC offers members valuable opportunities to connect with the public, exhibit their work, and grow their artistic practices.

NCC hosts three-four major annual events: the [NCC Surface Award exhibition (January)](https://www.northcoastceramics.com/award), an Easter Ceramic Market (March/ April), the celebrated [Mud Trail (August)](https://www.northcoastceramics.com/mud-trail), now in its thirteenth year, which opens studios to visitors, and the [Pre-Christmas Ceramic Market (November).](https://www.northcoastceramics.com/markets)

Alongside these events, NCC supports members and the public with professional development programs and exhibition opportunities year-round, fostering a thriving community passionate about clay and creativity.

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/623433d28e28f959fbacc840/f6c66b3f-e8a1-4899-a0d2-268ed4d34089/portrait+by+kiln.jpg)

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/623433d28e28f959fbacc840/1740801760934-CGKJ7WK0XUXHQXM4DL31/unsplash-image-ZSgWcW70cTs.jpg)

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/623433d28e28f959fbacc840/2bbfe5df-b82a-4020-bba2-f84869c5eaf1/IMG_1341.JPG)

### NCC Membership

North Coast Ceramics (NCC) is the peak body for ceramics in the Northern Rivers, representing professional and semi-professional ceramicists committed to excellence in their craft. Our rigorous membership criteria ensure that the public can trust they are purchasing from educated, experienced, and professional ceramic artists.

**For just $50 per year you can become an NCC member** and gain your own [dedicated space on this website](https://www.northcoastceramics.com/members-gallery). **Membership is valid from 1st January to 31st December** each year and is open to ceramicists with studios located in the **Byron, Ballina, or Lismore shires**.

To apply, please complete the [membership form](https://www.northcoastceramics.com/join-2), ensuring you have all required information ready before you begin. Your application will be reviewed by the NCC committee, and you will be notified once a decision is made. **Membership fees are payable upon approval.**

Applications are assessed individually on merit, but please note that NCC is a volunteer-run organisation led by practising artists. As a result, response times may vary depending on committee availability. However, all applicants will receive feedback as part of the process.

[apply now](https://www.northcoastceramics.com/join-2)

### Building Community Through Creativity

At NCC, we believe in fostering grass-roots connections and meaningful conversations across our diverse community. At the heart of our identity is our logo—a simple, timeless bowl. A bowl is more than just an object; it is a symbol of holding and giving. NCC embraces this spirit, holding space for **creativity, community, and respect for place**.

#### **Giving Back**

NCC proudly supports two local charities:

*   **Federal Loves Refugees**
    
*   **Country Women’s Association (Bangalow Branch)**
    

At our **two annual markets**, members create and donate handcrafted bowls, which are sold to raise funds for these causes. **100% of proceeds** go directly to charity, transforming each purchase into an act of generosity. This initiative reflects the values of our region—**community, inclusivity, and giving back**.

### **Our Commitment to the Arts**

We believe the arts are essential to a **healthy, connected community**. Through our work, we aim to not only celebrate ceramics but also inspire mindful action and support those in need.

[Join us](https://www.northcoastceramics.com/join-2) in shaping a community where creativity and generosity go hand in hand.

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/623433d28e28f959fbacc840/710524b6-a120-4465-84af-8a4985b94e5b/RAINFOREST+CERAMICS+MUGS.JPEG)

# FAQs

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/623433d28e28f959fbacc840/7f85259f-7d10-4397-85b8-8f9d49fc9860/YXrah3GkRNuYLON0Iiv47A_thumb_45f2.jpg)

*   What events does NCC organise?
    
    NCC hosts **three to four major annual events**, including:
    
    *   **NCC Award Exhibition** (January)
        
    *   **Easter Ceramic Market** (March/April)
        
    *   **Mud Trail Open Studios** (August)
        
    *   **Pre-Christmas Ceramic Market** (November)
        
    
    These events provide opportunities for artists to showcase their work and engage with the public.
    
*   Does NCC offer support beyond exhibitions and markets?
    
    Yes! In addition to our events, we offer **professional development programs and exhibition opportunities** year-round to support ceramic artists in growing their practice.
    
*   Who can become a member of NCC?
    
    Membership is open to **professional and semi-professional ceramicists** who have **studios located in the Byron, Ballina, or Lismore shires**.
    
*   What are the benefits of NCC membership?
    
    Members receive:
    
    *   A **dedicated profile space** on the NCC website
        
    *   Opportunities to **exhibit and sell work** at NCC’s markets and exhibitions
        
    *   Access to **professional development programs**
        
    *   A supportive network of ceramic artists in the region
        
    
*   How much does membership cost?
    
    Membership costs **$50 per year** and is valid from **1st January to 31st December**.
    
*   How do I apply for membership?
    
    To apply, complete the [**membership form**](https://www.northcoastceramics.com/join-2) on our website. Ensure you have all required information before submitting.
    
*   How is my application assessed?
    
    Applications are reviewed by the **NCC committee** based on merit. As NCC is a volunteer-run organisation, response times may vary, but all applicants will receive feedback.
    
*   If I join mid-year, is my fee reduced?
    
    Yes, new members pay a **pro-rata membership fee** based on the quarter they join:
    
    *   **January – March:** $50 (Full-year membership)
        
    *   **April – June:** $37.50 (¾-year membership)
        
    *   **July – September:** $25 (½-year membership)
        
    *   **October – December:** $12.50 (¼-year membership)
        
    
*   Can I participate in NCC events if I’m not a member?
    
    Some NCC events are open to non-members, but membership is required for the Mud Trail, certain **exhibitions, markets, and promotional opportunities**.
    
*   How can I stay updated on NCC events and news?
    
    Follow us on [**Instagram**](https://www.instagram.com/northcoastceramics/) and subscribe to our **newsletter** (link below) for the latest updates on exhibitions, markets, and opportunities.

You can find Pacific Ale in the United Kingdom. To find your nearest stockist, follow and message our UK crew on Instagram @stoneandwooduk.  
  
Pacific Ale, Green Coast Lager and selected merch is also available Hong Kong; visit [https://www.winebrothers.com.hk  
  
](https://www.winebrothers.com.hk/search?q=stone+%26+wood&type=product "https://www.winebrothers.com.hk/search?q=stone+%26+wood&type=product")For everywhere else, sorry beer lovers, at this stage, we don’t stock our beers anywhere else or ship internationally.

Can I buy a keg of beer from you guys?

For quality and safety reasons, we only sell kegs to licensed venues.

Can I refill a keg of beer?

Once again, for quality and safety reasons, we only sell and exchange kegs to licensed venues.  
  
You can visit our [Byron](https://stoneandwood.com.au/pages/byron-bay "https://stoneandwood.com.au/pages/byron-bay") and [Brisbane](https://stoneandwood.com.au/pages/brisbane "https://stoneandwood.com.au/pages/brisbane") Breweries and grab refillable [1L Sharers](https://stoneandwood.com.au/pages/the-sharer "https://stoneandwood.com.au/pages/the-sharer").

Do you guys have job positions available?

You can check out our job openings, or submit an expression of interest, [here](https://stoneandwood.com.au/pages/join-the-team "https://stoneandwood.com.au/pages/join-the-team").

Do you have gift vouchers available for online store/tours/food at your Breweries?

Yes! Here’s where you’ll find them.  
  
[Online purchase gift cards](https://stoneandwood.com.au/products/gift-card "https://stoneandwood.com.au/products/gift-card") – These gift cards can be used for any purchases on our online store.  
  
[Brewery tour gift cards](https://stoneandwood.com.au/pages/breweries-listing "https://stoneandwood.com.au/pages/breweries-listing") – Click on this link then click ‘book now’. This one allows you to buy 1 or more brewery tour at our Byron Brewery.  
  
Tasting room vouchers – Email our Brisbane team at [brisbane@stoneandwood.com.au](mailto:brisbane@stoneandwood.com.au "mailto:brisbane@stoneandwood.com.au") or Byron team at [tours@stoneandwood.com.au](mailto:tours@stoneandwood.com.au "mailto:tours@stoneandwood.com.au")

 

COMMUNITY

Do you have a dress code?

Yes, if you’re doing a tour please wear sturdy enclosed shoes.

What if the date I want to attend isn’t on the drop-down list?

That means it’s sold out. Tours sell out a few weeks in advance.

What is the legal age to do a tasting tour?

You must be over 18 to participate in our tours.

I can only see one tickets available for the date I want? Does this mean I have to book tickets individually?

No, it simply means there is only one ticket left for the tour on this date.

Can you release additional ticket for the date I want so I can book with a friend?

As we work in an operating brewery, we must limit tours to a maximum of 12 people so we can ensure everyone in the group is safe and has a great time on our brewery tours.

What if I need to get a refund?

If it’s more than 48 hours before the tour, we can refund. If not, then we won’t be able to.

My friend would like to come but doesn’t have a ticket. Can I bring them?

If the tour is sold out then, unfortunately, we can’t take anymore due to space restrictions. However, they can always come over to the Tasting Room for a tasting paddle while you’re on tour.

Can I change dates?

Maybe. Give us a call and we’ll see what we can do (this is usually only possible if there are spaces on another tour).

Is your brewery pet-friendly?

Yes! We welcome doggos to both our Tasting Room in Byron Bay and our Brissy brewery.

Can I bring my kid to the brewery and on brewery tours?

While kids are absolutely welcome to our brewery Tasting Room, they aren’t permitted on brewery tours for safety reasons.

Can I have my function/wedding at your brewery in Byron or Brisbane?

For queries about hosting your function/wedding at our brewery, please email our team at [functions@stoneandwood.com.au](mailto:functions@stoneandwood.com.au)

Do your breweries sell food?

Yes! If you get hungry while you’re with us, our canteens are available for a bite to eat. Check out our menu for the Byron Brewery [here](https://stoneandwood.com.au/pages/byron-bay "Byron Bay").  Brisbane’s menu changes frequently, [check in directly](mailto:brisbane@stoneandwood.com.au) for more info. Both breweries offer vegetarian options and can modify for vegans.

Can I make a reservation at either of your breweries?

We don’t take bookings at our breweries. If you are bringing a group of 10 or more get in touch with the team so they can look after you.  
  
Brisbane Brewery – [brisbane@stoneandwood.com.au](mailto:brisbane@stoneandwood.com.au)

Byron Brewery – [tours@stoneandwood.com.au](mailto:tours@stoneandwood.com.au)

Can I visit the Brewery in for my best mate’s bucks/hens?

Unfortunately we aren’t able to accept hens or bucks parties. Our licensing restrictions and family friendly vibe just don’t offer the right space for pre-wedding parties.  That said, while you here, if you personally wanted to quietly pop in for a tour and a tasting paddle you’ll find all the details here: [https://stoneandwood.com.au/pages/breweries-listing](https://stoneandwood.com.au/pages/breweries-listing "https://stoneandwood.com.au/pages/breweries-listing"). If you get hungry, you can grab a bite from our canteen while you’re in.

Do you do tours of your Brisbane Brewery?

Not at the moment.

Why can’t I book in for a tour on the date that I’m after?

We only make 4-5 weeks available at any one time so that the tasting room team can get an idea of the working production requirements of our brewery and plan the tours around events, special brew days etc.

We recommend booking your tour at least 2 weeks out. You can book [here](https://stoneandwood.com.au/pages/breweries-listing "https://stoneandwood.com.au/pages/breweries-listing").

Can I use the $20 discount voucher that I got on your website when I’m at the brewery?

Any vouchers or offers available on our website can only be used for [online store](https://stoneandwood.com.au/ "https://stoneandwood.com.au/") purchases.

 

COMMUNITY

I’m interested in whether you could support my community fundraiser – who do I contact?

As part of our community program, we’re keen to get behind your community/grassroots/not-for-profit event or initiative. Please contact [marketing@stoneandwood.com.au](mailto:marketing@stoneandwood.com.au "mailto:marketing@stoneandwood.com.au") with information on your organisation, its location and your event, and our team will be in touch. 

 

ONLINE ORDERS AND DELIVERY

I ordered from your online store and I am yet to receive a confirmation email with tracking?

Thanks for making a purchase on our online store! Orders are dispatched within 24hrs of when you placed your order, on business days. You will receive a confirmation with tracking information once the package has left our warehouse. If you have not received your tracking information within 48hrs of making a purchase, please feel free to email us at [online@stoneandwood.com.au](mailto:online@stoneandwood.com.au)

I ordered two cartons, but only 1 has arrived?

Multiple carton orders can sometimes be split. Please wait an additional day for your other carton/s to arrive and if they haven’t arrived by then, please email [online@stoneandwood.com.au](mailto:online@stoneandwood.com.au) and we will chase them up for you.

Can I use multiple discounts for the same purchase?

We will not be offering a combination of discounts to be used through our online store during the same purchase.

Can I order cartons through your online store for my wedding/bucks/event?

If you need a bulk order consider that your order may be split up and arrive on different days. Please allow ample time for your order to arrive (at least 7 days prior, plus shipping time). As with all courier services, sometimes we experience delays, so if you need the stock urgently please reach out to our friendly Customer Service team at [online@stoneandwood.com.au](mailto:online@stoneandwood.com.au) and ask us to provide you with a recommendation for a local bottleshop.

Fastway left me a card to arrange redelivery, what do I do?

Visit the Fastway website and follow the instructions on this link to arrange a redelivery – [Aramex Australia | Calling card left](http://www.fastway.com.au/card)

I am having trouble making a purchase on your online store. Why am I receiving an error?

Sometimes if you try again it will succeed the second time, or please try refreshing and/or trying in a different browser, sometimes Chrome will get it done where Explorer might not.  
  
If all else fails. Get in touch with us on [online@stoneandwood.com.au](mailto:online@stoneandwood.com.au "mailto:online@stoneandwood.com.au") or 02 6685 5173.

Can I order your beer from overseas?

Outside of Australia, you can enjoy our Original Pacific Ale in select Countdown stores and [online](https://shop.countdown.co.nz/shop/productdetails?stockcode=363579&name=stone-wood-beer-pacific-ale) in New Zealand. You can also order it [online](https://biercraft.myshopify.com/products/stone-wood-pacific-ale-case-24-bottles) and find it at Majestic Wine Stores in the UK. It’s also available in Hong Kong and Singapore. Unfortunately, we don't have the set up yet to deliver our beers to other countries. Maybe we'll get over there one day though!

Still have questions?

# our History

See how three guys from the beer business took a chance on something different and created a craft beer like no other.

# our History

See how three guys from the beer business took a chance on something different and created a craft beer like no other.

*   ## Early 2008
    
    ![](//stoneandwood.com.au/cdn/shop/files/Early-2008_1.png?v=1678352284)
    
    ## Early 2008
    
    Founder Ross, Brad & Jamie quit working for CUB and take the keys to an old soft drink factory in Byron’s Industrial Estate
    
*   ## SEP 2008
    
    Shiny new tanks arrive from Canada, the brewery starts to come together.
    
    ## SEP 2008
    
    ![](//stoneandwood.com.au/cdn/shop/files/SEP-2008_1.png?v=1678352315)
    
*   ## NOV 2008
    
    ![](//stoneandwood.com.au/cdn/shop/files/NOV-2008.jpg?v=1678927152)
    
    ## NOV 2008
    
    The First kegs of draught ale rolled out of our Byron Brewery on the back of a ute to local pubs.
    
*   ## APR 2009
    
    The first lager bottles rattle down the bottling line
    
    ## APR 2009
    
    ![](//stoneandwood.com.au/cdn/shop/files/SEP-2008_1_1.png?v=1678352384)
    
*   ## SEP 2009
    
    ![](//stoneandwood.com.au/cdn/shop/files/Early-2008_1_2.png?v=1678352439)
    
    ## SEP 2009
    
    The first batch of Stone Beer was brewed using the ancient methods adding burning hot rocks to the to the kettle, to rouse the boil.
    
*   ## NOV 2010
    
    Our Flagship Beer, The Original Pacific Ale is born. Draught Ale is renamed Pacific Ale
    
    ## NOV 2010
    
    ![](//stoneandwood.com.au/cdn/shop/files/SEP-2008_1_2.png?v=1678352475)
    
*   ## MAY 2011
    
    ![](//stoneandwood.com.au/cdn/shop/files/Early-2008_1_3.png?v=1678352670)
    
    ## MAY 2011
    
    Festival of The Stone is established, our annual festival that celebrates community, live music and Stone Beer
    
*   ## SEP 2013
    
    First employees become shareholders under our employee ownership plan, 72% of employees become owners in the business
    
    ## SEP 2013
    
    ![](//stoneandwood.com.au/cdn/shop/files/SEP-2008_1_3.png?v=1678352507)
    
*   ## JUL 2014
    
    ![](//stoneandwood.com.au/cdn/shop/files/Early-2008_1_4.png?v=1678352513)
    
    ## JUL 2014
    
    We open our second brewery in Murwillumbah at the base of Mt Wollumbin (Cloud Catcher). Releasing Cloud Catcher Australian Pale Ale to celebrate
    
*   ## MAR 2015
    
    100kw solar panels are installed at our Murwillumbah Brewery to reduce our footprint, a stepping stone in dialling up our sustainability
    
    ## MAR 2015
    
    ![](//stoneandwood.com.au/cdn/shop/files/SEP-2008_1_4.png?v=1678352516)
    
*   ## NOV 2016
    
    ![](//stoneandwood.com.au/cdn/shop/files/Early-2008_1_5.png?v=1678352518)
    
    ## NOV 2016
    
    B-Corp Certified – We join a growing community of companies dedicated to being agents of positive change through conscious sustainability practices.
    
*   ## FEB 2017
    
    Northern Rivers Flood Relief – Our crew hit the streets of Murwillumbah to help victims of the devastating 2017 floods donating over $30k
    
    ## FEB 2017
    
    ![](//stoneandwood.com.au/cdn/shop/files/SEP-2008_1_5.png?v=1678352521)
    
*   ## MAR 2017
    
    ![](//stoneandwood.com.au/cdn/shop/files/Early-2008_1_6.png?v=1678352597)
    
    ## MAR 2017
    
    Murwillumbah Open Day is established, we open the gates to our community for live music and good food to raise money for Wedgetail Retreat palliative care
    
*   ## MAR 2018
    
    Our ingrained Foundation is born, Stone & Wood’s not-for-profit that support grassroots, environmental and social charities in the local areas where funds are donated.
    
    ## MAR 2018
    
    ![](//stoneandwood.com.au/cdn/shop/files/SEP-2008_1_6.png?v=1678352591)
    
*   ## NOV 2018
    
    ![](//stoneandwood.com.au/cdn/shop/files/Early-2008_1_7.png?v=1678352586)
    
    ## NOV 2018
    
    We open the doors to our new spiritual home, relocating our original Byron Brewery around the road to Centennial Circuit
    
*   ## JAN 2019
    
    Stone & Wood launch Counter Culture series – Beers that go against the grain
    
    ## JAN 2019
    
    ![](//stoneandwood.com.au/cdn/shop/files/SEP-2008_1_7.png?v=1678352580)
    
*   ## MAR 2019
    
    ![](//stoneandwood.com.au/cdn/shop/files/Early-2008_1_8.png?v=1678352575)
    
    ## MAR 2019
    
    The inGrained Foundation launch annual large grants round donating $100k to local not-for-profits in the Northern Rivers
    
*   ## OCT 2019
    
    We officially open our Brisbane Brewery to the Brisbane community in Fortitude Valley with 8-hectolitre brewhouse
    
    ## OCT 2019
    
    ![](//stoneandwood.com.au/cdn/shop/files/brisbane.jpg?v=1687478699)
    
*   ## OCT 2019
    
    ![](//stoneandwood.com.au/cdn/shop/files/Early-2008_1_9.png?v=1678352570)
    
    ## OCT 2019
    
    Beer Club is born, a Stone & Wood community for beer lovers and enthusiast
    
*   ## SEP 2021
    
    Fermentum Join the Lion Beverages group alongside iconic craft breweries Little Creatures and New Belgium
    
    ## SEP 2021
    
    ![](//stoneandwood.com.au/cdn/shop/files/SEP-2008_1_9.png?v=1678352567)
    
*   ## MAR 2022
    
    ![](//stoneandwood.com.au/cdn/shop/files/Early-2008_1_10.png?v=1678352561)
    
    ## MAR 2022
    
    2022 floods devastate the Northern Rivers, our crew volunteer in the community to help out in affected areas. Stone & Wood donate $100k to flood relief
    
*   ## JUL 2022
    
    We pledge our commitment to more sustainable practices, implementing regenerative malt sourced from certificated sustainable farmers into limited release brews
    
    ## JUL 2022
    
    ![](//stoneandwood.com.au/cdn/shop/files/SEP-2008_1_10.png?v=1678352557)
    
*   ## AUG 2022
    
    ![](//stoneandwood.com.au/cdn/shop/files/Early-2008_1_11.png?v=1678352553)
    
    ## AUG 2022
    
    The inGrained Foundation expands large grants round to Brisbane donating $100k to local not-for-profits in the Brisbane region

# Vision & Mission

![VISION STATEMENT FINAL](/images/VISION_STATEMENT_FINAL.png)  
  
The Tropical Fruits Inc, established in 1988, is the premier LGBTIQ+ community group in the Northern Rivers in NSW. We are a not-for-profit, incorporated association that holds regular events for our diverse members and guests. We are a self funding, independent and voluntary organisation.

**Our mission is to:**

1.  To promote friendship, respect, acceptance and understanding within the lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, intersex and queer (LGBTIQ) community and of the LGBTIQ community within the Northern Rivers region in which members can enjoy all the benefits of the association without any political affiliation, 
2.  To be a not-for profit, charitable organisation, 
3.  To support any other organisations and institutions charitable at law who share the objects of the association,
4.  To assist in overcoming the isolation of LGBTIQ members,
5.  To relay appropriate information through a regular newsletter, 
6.  To hold regular events and activities to achieve the objects of the association,
7.  To promote the social development of LGBTIQ community in the Northern Rivers region, 
8.  To assist members of the LGBTIQ community in the Northern Rivers region through community disbursements.
9.  The Tropical Fruits Inc. acknowledges that this organisation operates on the land of the Widjabul-Wiabal Peoples of the Bundjalung Nation. 
10.  A First Nations LGBTIQ Subcommittee shall guide the Tropical Fruits Committee with regards to ensuring that respect is always given to First Nations perspectives.

We hold regular [**events**](https://tropicalfruits.org.au/17-events/7-events "Events") throughout the year, providing opportunities for our diverse members and guests to get together and celebrate in the beautiful "Rainbow Region". 

Tropical Fruits prides itself on being a **Fun, Safe & Inclusive** social club and invites all it's members and guests to come and enjoy our events in a safe and respectful environment that embraces all the diversity of our community.

We have made a home at our **[Clubhouse](https://tropicalfruits.org.au/about-us/club-house "Club House: The Fruitbowl"),** the "Fruitbowl", located in the colourful heart of the Rainbow Region, Lismore (lovingly dubbed Lovemore, Lesmore, Livemore). 

Each year we elect a nine-member [**Committee**](https://tropicalfruits.org.au/about-us/committee "Committee"), which meets fortnightly throughout the year to manage our club.  Our [**Volunteers**](https://tropicalfruits.org.au/nye/volunteer "Volunteering") work hard year-round in preparation for parties, during events, running the office and looking after the Fruitbowl.  Since 1988, it is the commitment of many thousands of these dedicated people that has enabled Troppos to become one of the largest regional LGBTIQ+ organisation in the country.  Check out our [**History**](https://tropicalfruits.org.au/about-us/history "OUR STORY") page for more.

# Frequently Asked Questions

*   ### What is Sticky?
    
    Sticky is one of the only shops in the world dedicated entirely to zines. It opened in April 2001, inspired in no small part by the artist bookstore Boekie Woekie in Amsterdam, and its objective ever since has been to ardently defend zine culture.
    
*   ### What can you do at Sticky?
    
    As a zine distro, we provide a safe space for zine makers to create, buy and sell zines. Sticky has stocked 20,000 titles since opening, both from local creators and artists all over the world. Zine makers are welcome to come down to our shop to use our photocopier, long-armed staplers, guillotines and typewriters. They can also speak to our expert zine-making volunteers about anything zine related!
    
    On top of offering a retail and working space for zines, Sticky also offers badge making facilities. You’re not able to book in a time to come down to Sticky to use the space but you’re more than welcome to drop by whenever we are open!
    
*   ### How does Sticky operate?
    
    Sticky is entirely volunteer-run; nobody you see working there gets paid. It takes a 20% commission from the zines it sells to help with bills and that, but otherwise relies on fundraising efforts and donations to survive.
    
*   ### How can I become a volunteer?
    
    If you’re interested in volunteering, in-store or at one of our fairs, please fill out the [Volunteer Expression of Interest form](https://stickyinstitute.com/volunteer).
    

## About

* * *

## Events and workshops

*   ### Does Sticky Institute run zine making workshops?
    
    We do! We don't have a strict workshop schedule so we recommend signing up to our mailing list and keeping an eye our Events Calendar to see what's coming up.
    
    If you are interested in Sticky running a workshop at your school/workplace/event, [get in touch with us](https://stickyinstitute.com/contact) so we can discuss it further!
    
*   ### Do you only run zine making workshops?
    
    No, we run all kinds of workshops! Check out our [Event Calendar](https://stickyinstitute.com/event-calendar) to see what’s coming up.
    
*   ### Can you run a private workshop for my school/workplace in the shop?
    
    We sure can but workshops held inside the shop can only accommodate 10 attendees!
    
*   ### Can you come to my school/workplace to run a workshop?
    
    Yes, we can!
    
    [Please get in touch with us](https://stickyinstitute.com/contact) so we can discuss this further.
    
*   ### Can I host/run an event or workshop at Sticky Institute?
    
    Maybe, it depends on what you want to do!
    
    We’re not looking to host additional zine making, badge making and collage as they are already included in our workshop program.
    
    [Send us an email with an outline of your ideas](https://stickyinstitute.com/contact) and we'll see if we can make it happen!
    

* * *

*   ### The Festival of the Photocopier
    
    Sticky’s original zine fair, and the largest in the Southern Hemisphere, Festival of the Photocopier runs in February of each year.
    
    Applications for FotP open in December and close in January.
    
    [Sign up to our mailing list to be notified of any updates!](https://stickyinstitute.com/faq#sign-up)
    
*   ### Hallozeen
    
    Run in collaboration with [Alex E Clark](https://www.instagram.com/lexlotl/?hl=en), Hallozeen celebrates all things spooky and scary in October of each year.
    
    For more information, [visit the Hallozeen website](https://hallozeen.rip/).
    

## Zine Fairs

* * *

*   ### Where is Sticky?
    
    Sticky is located at [Shop 1 & 2, Campbell Arcade in Melbourne/Naarm.](https://maps.app.goo.gl/hnNDtGZdTxJrXmzHA)
    
    Entrances to the underground arcade are located on Flinders Street (stairs), Degraves Street (stairs) & via Flinders Street Station (stairs/lift).
    
*   ### What time is Sticky open?
    
    Sticky is currently open from 12pm to 5pm, Tuesday to Saturdays.
    
*   ### Is Sticky wheelchair accessible?
    
    There is a lift on each of the train platforms to get down to Campbell Arcade.
    
    Unfortunately our store is too small for electric wheelchairs but smaller, manual wheelchairs are able to fit.
    
*   ### Do you accept credit card / EFTPOS instore?
    
    We are only able to accept EFTPOS payments in store, sorry. We are no longer able to accept cash payment.
    
*   ### Is there a public bathroom available?
    
    We do not have public bathroom facilities. The closest public toilets are at Flinders Street Station.
    
*   ### Can I stock my zine at Sticky?
    
    All information about stocking your zine with us is on the [Stock with us page](https://stickyinstitute.com/stock-with-us).
    

## In-store

* * *

*   ### Can I buy zines online?
    
    You sure can! We have an online mail department here that ships internationally. Due to time and space constraints, we aren’t able to put all zines that come in onto our online shop, but if you let us know what you’re after we can try and make that happen.
    
*   ### I want to buy a specific zine but it’s not listed in the online shop.
    
    We have hundreds of zines in our shop at any time so it's be impossible for us to list them all online individually!
    
    If you’re looking for something specific, [get in touch with us](https://stickyinstitute.com/contact) and we can check the shelves to let you know if we have it.
    
*   ### Do you ship internationally?
    
    Yes! The shipping costs for your order will be displayed on the checkout page.
    
*   ### Do you ship to the US?
    
    Australia Post has recently stopped delivering packages to the United States, so we are unable to process to any zine orders to our state side friends. We hope this changes soon but it is out of our hands.
    
*   ### Why is shipping so expensive?
    
    That just seems to be how it is. If you’re feeling very strongly about this topic you could [send some feedback to Australia Post.](https://auspost.com.au/about-us/corporate-information/complaints-compliments-and-feedback)
    
*   ### When will my order be shipped?
    
    Orders will be shipped out within seven (7) days. If there are any delays with getting your order out, we'll let you know!
    
*   ### I didn’t receive my order!
    
    Uh oh, that's not cool.
    
    [Please get in touch with us](https://stickyinstitute.com/contact) so we can look into this for you.
    

## Online store

* * *

*   ### How can I make a monetary donation to Sticky Institute?
    
    Wow, you’re lovely!
    
    [You can make a monetary donation to Sticky Institute online through Raisely](https://donate.stickyinstitute.com/).
    
    We also accept donations in store.
    
    If you are stock a zine with us, you can opt to donate 50% or 100% of your zine sales (instead of the standard 20%).
    
    All donations over $2AUD are tax deductible in Australia!
    
*   ### Do you accept donated zines?
    
    We sure do!
    
    Donated zines are given a new life by going into our [Mystery Bags](https://stickyinstitute.com/shop/p/mystery-bag).
    

## Donations

* * *

*   ### Can I bring a school group to Sticky Institute for an excursion?
    
    Yes, we love school groups!
    
    [Please get in touch with us to let is know what date you want to visit!](https://stickyinstitute.com/contact)
    
*   ### Can Sticky Institute run a  workshop at my school?
    
    Yes, we can!
    
    [Please get in touch with us](https://stickyinstitute.com/contact) so we can discuss this further.
    
*   ### Can my school purchase zines?
    
    You sure can!
    
    The easiest way to buy zines is by purchasing an I[nstant Zine Hit](https://stickyinstitute.com/shop/p/instant-zine-hit) from our online store.
    
    If you need an invoice with a purchase order number, [get in touch with us](https://stickyinstitute.com/contact) and we'll organise one for you.
    
*   ### Do you offer workshop experience for students?
    
    If you are a high school student looking to do your work experience with us, [get in touch with us](https://stickyinstitute.com/contact) so we can see if we can accommodate you.
    
    Please keep in mind that due to the way Sticky operates, we cannot accommodate the solid two week period that normally applies to work experience projects.
    

## Schools

* * *

*   ### Can I buy one of the typewriters?
    
    No, sorry, they aren’t for sale. You are welcome to come in and use them any time we are open.
    
*   ### Do you sell replacement typewriter ribbons?
    
    [We sell universal typewriter ribbons for $8 a pop.](https://stickyinstitute.com/shop/p/typewriter-ribbon)
    
*   ### I have a broken typewriter. Help!
    
    We can't help you out, sorry!
    

## Typewriters

* * *

*   ### I have a cool idea for a comic, do you know any artists who would want to work with me?
    
    We can’t connect you to anyone, no, but the cool thing about zines is that they’re a great opportunity to develop your own skills! The best thing about self-publishing is only being limited by your own creativity, so don’t be afraid to try (and fail at) new things while trying to find your groove!
    
*   ### Do you offer residencies?
    
    Sticky does not offer residencies but anyone is welcome to visit during opening hours to use the space and use facilities in an ad hoc fashion.

### Why is there sediment in my beer?

Fear not- your golden nectars are perfectly safe to drink. What you're explaining sounds like coagulated yeast!

All of our beers at Stone & Wood are unfiltered which means there is a natural yeast present, as we like the cloudiness and the natural flavours that come with unfiltered beer.  Kind of like Coopers, if they sit for too long in the same position, this yeast can settle to the bottom/side/top of the bottle, and essentially clump up and not distribute evenly. This isn't a bad thing; it just means the beer needs a good swirl or vigorous roll prior to opening for even distribution, which we recommend doing prior to opening anyway! At times I've copped slightly more stubborn deposits of yeastafter they've been stored upside down, in which case I'll just pour them into a glass. 

We actually made a little video about how to pour the perfect Pacific Ale, yeast and all! Check it out, [https://stoneandwood.com.au/hand-hand-pouring-beer/](https://stoneandwood.com.au/hand-hand-pouring-beer/ "https://stoneandwood.com.au/hand-hand-pouring-beer/")

# We are ardent defenders of zine culture.

Sticky Institute is an Artist Run Initiative in Melbourne/Naarm dedicated to zines. Part open-resource working space and part non-profit retail space, we’re your one-stop-shop for all things zines!

Since 2001, we've been supporting the local zine community and culture, leading us to become a pivotal resource for zine makers around the globe. We’ve stocked nearly 20,000 zine titles and pride ourselves on supporting zine makers by offering a space to make, showcase and sell their work. 

At the heart of Sticky Institute is our commitment to the zine community. Our space is more than just a store; it's a creative sanctuary equipped with essential tools like typewriters, long-armed staplers and a photocopier— all there to help bring your zine ideas to fruition. 

![A  wall covered with various posters and flyers. Among them are event announcements, artistic illustrations, and photos.](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/6610cdfcd9a9ce56ef703a8d/0ba26259-eea2-40fe-b350-459c273b17d6/campbell-arcade-on-jackson-street+%2810%29.jpg)

We host two annual zine fairs:

*   **The Festival of the Photocopier** - Australia's largest and longest running zine fair operating since 2010.
    
*   [Hallozeen](https://www.hallozeen.rip/) - A collaboration with [Alex e Clark](https://www.instagram.com/lexlotl) celebrating zines and all things spooky.
    

Both fairs are free to attend for stallholders and the public. They stand as a testament to our dedication to celebrating the art and craft of zine making, drawing enthusiasts from across the nation and beyond.

Sticky Institute is run by a dedicated team of volunteers who are committed to the zine community, DIY ethics and the enduring spirit of punk.

[Read: A history of Sticky written in 2011, when Sticky became a fully volunteer-run operation.](https://stickyinstitute.com/false-diary)

[![Radler vs Shandy: What’s the Difference?](//stoneandwood.com.au/cdn/shop/articles/250507_S_W_Randler_CSearl_Lifestyle_2212_websize_3f33ebe6-e792-473c-8b08-543c2a9c76fb.jpg?v=1756778480&width=533)](https://stoneandwood.com.au/blogs/all/radler-vs-shandy-what-is-the-difference)

![Radler vs Shandy: What’s the Difference?](//stoneandwood.com.au/cdn/shop/articles/250507_S_W_Randler_CSearl_Lifestyle_2212_websize_3f33ebe6-e792-473c-8b08-543c2a9c76fb.jpg?v=1756778480&width=533)

You know how it goes. You’re standing around the esky, crack open a cold can of our new [Citrus Radler](https://stoneandwood.com.au/products/citrus-radler), and someone throws it out there:

“So... it’s just a fancy shandy, right?”

Fair question. At first glance, they might seem similar, both easy-drinking, citrusy and built for hot arvos. But when you dig a little deeper, you’ll find that a Radler and a shandy are more like distant cousins than twins. They might show up to the same [backyard BBQ](https://stoneandwood.com.au/blogs/all/how-to-host-the-ultimate-aussie-bbq-this-christmas?srsltid=AfmBOorRs30SBaGuMtKg4J7C-ueWaDMSZA3-VF9p0MN2RfIZhjIW5Hcw), but they’ve definitely taken different roads to get there.

Let’s unpack it.

## What’s a Shandy?

A shandy is your classic mix, usually one part beer (like a lager or light ale), one part lemonade or lemon squash. It’s blended on the spot, whether it’s your local bartender pouring it from the tap, or you mixing one yourself at home. 

It’s casual, nostalgic and has its place. But here’s the key, a shandy isn’t brewed. It’s a half-half combo. Part beer. Part soft drink.

So, while it’s refreshing, the flavour is usually sweeter, less structured, and definitely not designed for beer lovers chasing real depth or balance.

## And a Radler?

A [Radler](https://stoneandwood.com.au/products/citrus-radler), on the other hand, is a purpose-brewed style of beer that’s been around for over a century. It was first poured in Germany for cyclists looking for something cold, light and sessionable post-ride. (Fun fact: “Radler” actually means “cyclist” in German.)

But unlike a shandy, a true Radler is brewed from the ground up. It’s not beer mixed with lemonade, it’s beer infused with real citrus during the brewing process. The result? Something light, fruity, naturally zesty and still proudly beer.

## Enter: Our Citrus Radler

We’ve always brewed with the Northern Rivers lifestyle in mind, long summer days, salt in the air, backyard hangs that roll into the evening. So, when we decided to create our take on a Radler, we knew it had to tick a few boxes:

*   Light and easy on the palate
*   Full of fresh citrus character
*   Brewed with intention, not mixed after the fact
*   Mid-strength, sessionable, and undeniably refreshing

Our [Citrus Radler](https://stoneandwood.com.au/products/citrus-radler) is all that, and then some. We brew it with Galaxy hops, regenerative malts, and add 100% Aussie lemon purée during the whirlpool. Once fermentation’s done, we finish it with natural orange and grapefruit flavours to dial up the citrus.

At 4.0% ABV, it’s crisp and refreshing without compromising on taste, with just enough zing to make you want another.

And unlike a shandy, there’s no lemonade or soft drink in sight. Just beer, crafted with care, and a little citrus twist.

Feature

Shandy

Citrus Radler

Made with

Beer + lemonade or soft drink (post-pour)

Brewed beer + real fruit additions during and post-ferment

Sweetness

Sweet from lemonade

Lightly citrusy, dry and refreshing

Brew process

Mixed after brewing

Citrus integrated into the brew itself

Alcohol

Variable, often lower

4.0% ABV, balanced and consistent

Flavour

Soft drink-forward

Beer-forward, with real citrus character

Vibe

Classic Aussie pub mix

Thoughtfully brewed, bright, modern and beer-first

## Same Purpose, Different Path

Both Radlers and shandies exist for the same reason: to quench thirst. They're made for summer, for sweaty afternoons, for post-surf chill outs and backyard hangs with the crew.

But where a shandy leans on lemonade, a Radler is brewed with integrity, it’s real beer, made with real fruit, and built from the ground up to be bright, citrusy and sessionable.

At [Stone & Wood](https://stoneandwood.com.au/), we don’t just want to make something “like a shandy.” We want to make something that’s uniquely us, something brewed with the same purpose and care as everything else we make. And we want it to reflect who we are and where we’re from.

That’s why we use locally grown fruit, regeneratively farmed grains, and why we’re proud to be a [Certified B Corp](https://stoneandwood.com.au/pages/impact), committed to leaving the Earth better than we found it. From our solar-powered brewery to our community-focused [inGrained Foundation](https://stoneandwood.com.au/pages/impact), we believe good beer should do good too.

## The Verdict?

Next time someone asks if our Citrus Radler is just a fancy shandy, feel free to smile and say:

“Nah mate, it’s a proper beer with a citrus twist.”

Same thirst-quenching vibe, different story in every can.

![Radler vs Pacific Ale: Cousins or Just Mates?](//stoneandwood.com.au/cdn/shop/articles/250507_S_W_Randler_CSearl_Lifestyle_2212_websize_b67dd0d0-fe89-4c7f-befc-9f47f797af76.jpg?v=1756778637&width=533)

We get it, when a new beer drops, especially one with citrus in the name, the first thing you want to know is how it stacks up against the original. And around here, there’s no beer more iconic than our [Pacific Ale](https://stoneandwood.com.au/products/pacific-ale-bottles). Born from the salt, sun and laid-back energy of the Northern Rivers, it’s been pouring in pubs, beachside bars and backyard eskies since day one.

So, when we brewed up [Citrus Radler](https://stoneandwood.com.au/products/citrus-radler), we figured some of you might be wondering: is it like Pacific Ale? Is it sweeter? Is it for beer drinkers or more for the “just-a-splash” crew? And the big one, what even is a Radler?

We’ve got you. Here’s the lowdown.

## A Shared DNA

Let’s start with what they have in common. Think of Citrus Radler as having Pacific Ale’s good bones, a similar malt base made up of pale malt, regen malt, malted wheat and rolled wheat, bringing a smooth, slightly biscuity foundation that you’ll recognise straight away.

We’ve also kept our favourite hop in the spotlight, Galaxy, which gives both beers that distinct hit of tropical fruit, especially passionfruit. If Pacific Ale is your go-to, the first sip of Radler will feel familiar. Comforting even.

But that’s where the paths start to split.

## Radler’s Citrus Twist

Here’s where things get interesting.

[Citrus Radler](https://stoneandwood.com.au/products/citrus-radler) brings something extra to the table, a bright, zesty kick of real fruit, thanks to 100% Australian lemon purée added during the whirlpool stage of brewing (that’s the hot side). Post-fermentation, we layer in natural orange and grapefruit flavours, all derived from actual fruit. Nothing artificial. No syrupy sweetness. Just crisp, natural refreshment that lifts the whole experience.

It pours a golden hue, a little brighter and clearer than Pacific Ale, with a gentle citrus aroma that hits you as soon as the can cracks. And at mid-strength, it’s the kind of beer that doesn’t demand too much, light on the palate, low on alcohol, and perfect for long sessions under the sun.

In short: it’s summer in a can.

## For Pacific Ale Fans Wanting Something Fresh

If you love Pacific Ale’s easy-going charm but feel like mixing it up, Citrus Radler could be your new weekend staple. It brings the same relaxed attitude, just with a citrusy twist and a slightly lighter body.

It’s also a great way to bring someone new into the fold, that friend who’s not quite into “beer beer” but wants something flavourful and sessionable. Radler is approachable, refreshing and brewed with care, no shortcuts, no sugar bombs, just real ingredients and a clean finish.

Perfect for post-surf cool downs, fish tacos at sunset, or that second round you didn’t think you had in you.

## The Bigger Picture

At [Stone & Wood](https://stoneandwood.com.au/), beer has always been more than what’s in the glass. For us, it’s about bringing people together, sharing stories, moments, and a sense of place. That place for us is the Northern Rivers, and it shows up in everything we do, from the ingredients we choose to the way we brew.

We're proudly [Certified B Corp](https://stoneandwood.com.au/pages/impact), which means we hold ourselves to higher standards around sustainability, community and transparency. It’s not just a badge, it’s a commitment. We source regenerative malts that are better for the soil, use Australian-grown fruit, and we give back through our inGrained Foundation, supporting grassroots organisations that make our region thrive.

When we brewed [Citrus Radler](https://stoneandwood.com.au/products/citrus-radler), we wanted something that reflected that same ethos: something light, refreshing, made with real ingredients and brewed with care, for the people who drink it and the planet we live on.

So, whether you're loyal to [Pacific Ale](https://stoneandwood.com.au/collections/beers), curious to try something new, or just after something easy to sip when the sun’s still high, Citrus Radler is ready to roll.

You’ll find Citrus Radler wherever you pick up Stone & Wood, or better yet, swing by our Byron Tasting Room and enjoy one fresh off the tap.

See you soon, legends.

[![Hells Bells and High Lines: Easter Awakens at Bells Beach](//stoneandwood.com.au/cdn/shop/articles/bells2.jpg?v=1745296572&width=533)](https://stoneandwood.com.au/blogs/all/hells-bells-and-high-lines-easter-awakens-at-bells-beach)

![Hells Bells and High Lines: Easter Awakens at Bells Beach](//stoneandwood.com.au/cdn/shop/articles/bells2.jpg?v=1745296572&width=533)

For surfers, Bells Beach at Easter conjures images of cold Southern Ocean, long lines of swell, and fresh northwest offshores blowing off the adjacent farmland and through the moonah trees.

Well not so much this year.

The opening day of the Rip Curl Pro at Bells felt positively sub-tropical. Walking down the hill toward Bells, the sea breeze had a warm wash to it and the sun, when it caught you, bit hard. Even the water temp is currently sitting around 18 degrees – boardshorts for the brave, three-two full suits for the rest. If you weren’t facing due south staring out at the Antarctic sub latitudes, you could swear you were back on the North Coast.

![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0256/5498/4783/files/Stone_Wood_AfternoonDelight_Bells25_TC_1Z9A0724.png?v=1745292507)

Bells Beach has been known as Djarrak for tens of thousands of years to the Waddawurrung people, Djarrak meaning ‘elbow’, the headland appearing as a bend in the coastline. It was a place to gather shellfish and gather, generally. In more modern times, the small beach today known as Bells has been held in reverence by surfers who travel here to surf its icy lines.

That reverence rings out on Good Friday morning, shortly after first light as the bell tolls and the first notes of AC/DC’s _Hells Bells_ echo around the beach. The ceremonial playing of _Hells Bells_ to start the morning’s first heat at Bells began a couple of decades ago and has become iconic in its own right. An ancient landscape, a modern dance in the elements, a killer riff played by a grown man from Adelaide dressed as a schoolboy. Surfers in the water when it’s played have spoken about being lost out there in a powerful moment, forgetting they’re even surfing a heat.

The reality of course is that the annual Easter contest is a big deal, a stop on the world tour and a major sporting event that draws thousands of people from all over Victoria and beyond. Over the Easter weekend, Bells hums.

After parking on the adjacent farmland, you walk down the hill past the grandstands, coffee vans, the big screen and the gift shop, the air filled with the smell of deep fryers working overtime.

A full house will see 5000 Victorians fill the place. Many of them don’t know much about the sport of surfing, but as Victorians they know sport and they love sport, and they understand that Bells is the saltwater equivalent of an AFL final. They’ll sit on the beach all day, or at least until the high tide washes them away, applauding each wave and cheering on local favourites.

![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0256/5498/4783/files/Bells.jpg?v=1745291786)

The difference however is that at an AFL game you can’t run onto the ground and start kicking your own ball around. You can here. While the contest runs at Bells, a couple of hundred metres to the east the reef at Winkipop serves as a practise pitch. Punters can paddle out and mix it with the pros warming up for their heats.

On Good Friday, just before lunch, Jordy Smith took off up the top of the point at Winki. He soon hit top speed, pushing hard on his rails as he chicanes down the line, running a slalom course around several surfers watching the show and drifting into his line. No stress. Jordy is cool. On the way back up the point several people congratulate him on winning the last tour event, over in El Salvador. “Thanks, bru.”

After lunch, the crowds on the hill at Bells kick back.

It’s the first year Stone and Wood have come on as the official beer of the WSL world tour in Australia, but in their own relaxed way have billed themselves as the tour’s “unofficial” official beer. The open-air Stone & Wood bar sits halfway up the hill and feels unofficial. Surf fans from Prahran, Preston, Nunawading and Fitzroy tilt Pacific Ale cans as the sun drops lazily into the farm paddocks behind the contest.

![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0256/5498/4783/files/Stone_Wood_AfternoonDelight_Bells25_TC_1Z9A0724.jpg?v=1745292304)

Out in the Bells Bowl, the high tide has seen the contest go on hold but on the hill, nobody seems too bothered. It’s Friday afternoon with a full Easter weekend ahead. In place of contest heats, they’ve sent out a Stone & Wood “Afternoon Delight” twin-fin expression session. It’s supposed to be some lo-fi fun, but the reality is the modern twin is perfectly suited to the sloping walls of Bells, and some hi-fi surfing goes down. Some of it would win heats in the contest.

![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0256/5498/4783/files/Stone_Wood_AfternoonDelight_Bells25_TC_1Z9A0762.png?v=1745292573)

Bells is between weather systems right now, so the waves disappeared on Easter Saturday, and nobody seems to know when they’re due to return. Again, with a full Easter weekend in prospect, and a full town, nobody seems too concerned for now. The waves will turn up when they’re ready.

Words by Sean Doherty.
