## NATI FRINJ FESTIVAL DIRECTOR 2026/27

We are seeking a visionary and dynamic **Nati Frinj Biennale Director (2026–27)** to lead the next chapter of one of regional Australia’s most exciting arts festivals. This is a unique opportunity to shape a bold, community-connected program that brings together contemporary performance, visual arts, and experimental practice in the heart of Natimuk.

As always, we’re looking for an inspiring leader with strong artistic vision, excellent collaboration skills, and a passion for regional arts. If you’re ready to create an unforgettable festival that celebrates creativity, place, and community, we’d love to hear from you.

Previous applicants are welcome to apply.

[**Click here**](https://natifrinj.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Nati-Frinj-Biennale-Festival-Director-PD-26-27.pdf) for the full position description.  
Applications close 15th May 2026.

## Volunteer with Frinj

Volunteer roles vary in time commitment and skill levels – there’s something for everyone. Roles during the Frinj include: 

*   Selling tickets at the Frinj hub 
*   Venue Door person 
*   Assisting with events incl. queue management, ticket scanning and seat-ing 
*   Running a licenced bar or working at a bar 
*   Setting up spaces, deco-rating or chair moving 
*   Setting up street sign-age or temporary fencing 
*   Assisting artists to run community workshops 
*   Assisting with event production, sound and lighting.

# Host an Event

## Expression of Interest guidelines to host a fringe event as part of the 2027 Benalla Street Art Festival

### About the Festival

Our annual Benalla Street Art Festival will be celebrated over three days on

### 2 – 4 April 2027

The Benalla Street Art Festival promises a captivating experience for art enthusiasts and visitors alike. This annual event transforms the city into a vibrant outdoor gallery, showcasing the talents of local and internationally renowned street artists. The Benalla Street Art Festival is run by Benalla Rural City Council and overseen by the community-based Benalla Festival Advisory Committee.

The Benalla Street Art Festival Advisory Committee is now accepting applications to host events or activities as part of the Benalla Street Art Festival. We want to hear from interested businesses, community groups, social groups, sporting groups, schools, and service organisations. Our aspiration is for the Benalla Street Art Festival to evolve into a nationally renowned celebration of contemporary arts and culture.

**Expressions of interest close Friday 29 January 2027.**

### We’d love fringe event applications to align to our aspiration:

● Celebrate Street Art, host live painting demonstrations, feature graffiti artists from diverse backgrounds, and integrate the existing street art as a backdrop for music, performances, or temporary art installations.  
● Enhance Benalla Rural City’s reputation as a leading regional destination for world-class street art and public art, generating positive media attention.  
● Direct visitor spending towards local cafes, restaurants, and retail, and provide a platform for local artists, creatives, and artisanal vendors to sell their work or offer creative workshops and experiences.  
● Draw a greater number of art enthusiasts, visitors, and families to Benalla Rural City and encourage them to explore the broader High-Country region by offering unique, compelling street art experiences and tours.

### WHAT WILL the Benalla Street Art Festival provide for your event?

Events will be promoted through the Festival’s program, highlighting activities across Benalla and surrounding townships during the festival.

 Those interested in hosting an event can apply for a $750 Quick Response Grant or a Major Event Funding of up to $3,000 to help bring their ideas to life. 

For more information on eligibility and how to apply, visit Council’s website. 

[Community Grants and Funding – Benalla Rural City Council](https://www.benalla.vic.gov.au/community/get-involved/community-grants-and-funding/)

### Marketing

We provide marketing, advertising and media opportunities that promote each of the events that comprise the Festival. Event organisers are encouraged to take out their own additional advertising or sponsor the Festival for additional benefits (download the Sponsorship Prospectus).  
Events will be promoted through the Benalla Street Art Festival’s digital channels which includes the Festival’s website and Socials (i.e. Instagram, Facebook).

### Support

We support organisers to obtain Council permits required to deliver events.

### Economic and social returns

The Benalla Street Festival offers a host of economic and social benefits to the community. Those who participate help showcase the many facilities and attractions that make Benalla Rural City a great place to live and to visit. Well-managed events create opportunities for financial returns to the event facilitator.

### What is my role if I am part of the Benalla Street Art Festival?

As a host of an event or activity, you are responsible for managing your own activity or event and associated costs. You are responsible for organising the necessary venue and equipment, ticket sales, bookings enquiries, Public Liability Insurance and permits if necessary. Events are self-managed, self-funded, self-staffed, and will not be part of the official printed program if submitted after Monday 1st December. Benalla Street Art Festival will aid with the marketing and promotion of events via digital channels.

Once your event is approved and published, if for any reason you are considering the cancellation or postponement of your event you must liaise with the Benalla Street Art Festival Advisory Committee in the first instance to discuss alternate options. The Benalla  
Street Art Festival program of events is distributed widely.

### How do I get involved?

Complete the Expression of Interest form online by **Friday 29 January 2027.**

### What do I need to submit?

At this initial stage, the Benalla Street Art Festival Advisory Committee is only seeking a completed Expression of Interest form. Every effort will be made to accommodate requests for inclusions. Priority will be given to those proposals that best fit the Benalla Street Art Festival program and aspirations. If successful, we will then require you to submit the following:  
▪ A signed MOU approving the inclusion of your event  
▪ A copy of your Public Liability Insurance certificate  
▪ Working with children and police clearance if hosting a children’s activity  
▪ A community event application may be required pending the scope, location and size of the event. The Events Department can assist with support and advice.

### More information

For more information contact the Council’s Events Coordinator on 03 5760 2600 to discuss your event proposal.

## Submit your Expression of Interest

# **Blazing Swan 2027: Side Quest**  
**(24th – 30th March 2027, Jilakin Rock City, Kulin)**

## **Tickets for Swan 2027 are expected to be released in mid-to-late November 2026**

## **Volunteering for Blazing Swan 2027 event is expected to open in early to mid-November 2026**

Please stay tuned to our website and social media for updates

Life rarely follows the path imagined. We discover new avenues, change direction and sometimes get a little lost.

But so often, when we arrive, we find the people, places and pieces of ourselves quietly waiting for us to arrive.

Thirteen detours and somehow you land exactly where you needed to be.

Sometimes, the best parts of a journey are the ones you never planned.

Sometimes, it’s about the journey rather than the end destination.

Blazing Swan 2027: “Side Quest” invites you to embrace the adventure, wander without a destination and find a familiar soul in an unfamiliar face. To deviate to find undiscovered art, or wander into the camp you hadn’t planned to visit. To immerse yourself in creativity, participate, play and perhaps…. say “YES” a little more often.

We encourage you to live our 11 Principles. To embrace your curiosity, release your self-expressions, share your gifts and pick up some MOOP along the way as you get wonderfully lost amongst the community. Meet friends you don’t know yet, welcome the stranger into your adventures, and stay up just long enough to welcome a sunrise.

Nothing planned, but something wholesome, unplanned and magical experienced.

Between the dust, dancing, creating, gifting and the people we meet along the way, you might find yourself wondering…

Is Blaze the Side Quest? Or is everyday life simply the Side Quest that brings us home to the paddock, one more time?

Every path leads somewhere, but when the Side Quest becomes part of our story that matters most….it transforms into the ultimate adventure

**Blazing Swan 2027**  
**Side Quest**  
**_~Take the Scenic Route_**

![](https://blazingswan.com.au/wp-content/uploads/BLAZE-ART-27-scaled.jpg)

The Blazing Swan annual event is dedicated to RADICAL SELF-EXPRESSION and RADICAL SELF-RELIANCE for seven days of community over the Easter Long Weekend, from Wednesday 24th 2027 (noon) to Tuesday 30th March 2027 (noon).

Blazing Swan is an official Burning Man Regional Event. We practice DECOMMODIFICATION, placing ourselves and our relationships at the centre of our own lives, GIVING and receiving openly, being IMMEDIATELY present, and acknowledging that everything we have ever accomplished, everything we will ever accomplish, only happens through COMMUNAL EFFORT. We will be RADICALLY EXPRESSIVE and RADICALLY INCLUSIVE and ask only of ourselves and others that we respect and value each other and practice kindness and caring.

Blazing Swan is not a spectator event. Every participant is a performer, every act is a performance. Find your best self, your creative self, and play it out on the stage that is Blazing Swan.

Blazing Swan gives absolute priority to CONSENT, CIVIC RESPONSIBILITY and LEAVING NO TRACE. When you purchase a ticket you sign-up to say you understand what all these things mean, and you will follow our rules which are there to keep everyone safe. People do ask, “Why do you have so many rules? More than any other event I’ve ever been to!” It’s because we care. And a week in the Australian outback is not a naturally safe space. Be prepared.

Read the Ticket FAQ and the Event FAQ on the Website, read the Survival Guide, read about the Principles and our Statement of Inclusion. Get your head around our Blazing Swan Tickets and Event Attendance Terms and Conditions. PARTICIPATION and CIVIC RESPONSIBILITY starts here.

We acknowledge the traditional custodians of the land where our event is held – the Njaki Njaki, Ballardong, and Wiilman Noongar peoples and their Elders past and present. We acknowledge and respect their continuing Culture and the contribution they make to the life of this country and region.

Much more information about Blazing Swan, our culture, our people and our art can be found on this website.

# GIPA Public access to information

The Government Information (Public Access) Act (GIPA) requires Council to proactively release information where possible.

On 1 July 2010, new legislation came into effect, replacing the former Freedom of Information Act and Section 12 of the Local Government Act.

This legislation requires Council to proactively release information where possible, acknowledging the right of members of the public to have access to our information providing there is no overriding public interest against disclosure.  At all times, the presumption is in favour of disclosure.

The GIPA Act:

*   ​Creates rights to information that are designed to meet community expectations of more open and transparent government; and
*   Encourages government agencies to proactively​ release government information.

For more information on types of applications and how to apply, visit [Council's access to information/GIPA guidelines page.](https://www.cbcity.nsw.gov.au/node/12500)

The [**Access to Information Policy**](https://www.cbcity.nsw.gov.au/your-council/policies-and-codes/access-to-information-policy) outlines Council's principles regarding public access to information.

The [**Government Information (Public Access) Act 2009**​](https://legislation.nsw.gov.au/view/pdf/asmade/act-2009-52) provides for Council information to be released in four ways:

### GIPA Informal Release

Informal applications are generally suitable for 

*   Property or development-related matters 
*   Information that is already publicly available that you can’t locate yourself; and 
*   Other information held which may be authorised to be released in response to an informal request 

Release is subject to any reasonable conditions that Council may wish to impose.

[Access for information form (Open Access - Informal Application)](https://www.cbcity.nsw.gov.au/your-council/forms/informal-gipa-application-form)

### GIPA Formal Release

The release of all other information not made available by either mandatory, proactive or informal release can be made by way of an Application for Information (Formal Application). 

Standard fees and charges and time frames are applicable for such applications.

[Application for Information (Formal Application)](https://www.cbcity.nsw.gov.au/your-council/forms/formal-gipa-application-form)

### GIPA Internal Review Form (fo​rmal appli​cation)

You have the right to request a review of certain decisions made by government agencies about the release of information under the _Government Information (Public Access) Act 2009 (GIPA Act)_. ​ You have 20 working days from the date of the decision to ask for an internal review.  Standard fees and charges and time frames apply.​

[Internal Review Form (Fo​rmal Appli​cation)](https://www.cbcity.nsw.gov.au/your-council/forms/internal-review-application-relating-to-formal-gipa)

### Mandatory Disclosure

This information is made available on Council’s website and is available free of charge, for example Council policies, meeting agendas and minutes, media releases and annual reports etc - Open Access Information (Sec 18 GIPA 2009 and Schedule 1 Part 2 of GIPA Regulations). ​

### Voluntary Disclosure

Council is encouraged to make as much information of public interest as possible publicly available, free of charge or at minimal cost. Examples include frequently requested information or information of public interest. ​

[GIPA Informal Release](https://www.cbcity.nsw.gov.au/your-council/gipa-public-access-to-information#) [GIPA Formal Release](https://www.cbcity.nsw.gov.au/your-council/gipa-public-access-to-information#) [GIPA Internal Review Form (fo​rmal appli​cation)](https://www.cbcity.nsw.gov.au/your-council/gipa-public-access-to-information#) [Mandatory Disclosure](https://www.cbcity.nsw.gov.au/your-council/gipa-public-access-to-information#) [Voluntary Disclosure](https://www.cbcity.nsw.gov.au/your-council/gipa-public-access-to-information#)

Informal applications are generally suitable for 

*   Property or development-related matters 
*   Information that is already publicly available that you can’t locate yourself; and 
*   Other information held which may be authorised to be released in response to an informal request 

Release is subject to any reasonable conditions that Council may wish to impose.

[Access for information form (Open Access - Informal Application)](https://www.cbcity.nsw.gov.au/your-council/forms/informal-gipa-application-form)

The release of all other information not made available by either mandatory, proactive or informal release can be made by way of an Application for Information (Formal Application).

## Attending the Frinj  

![](https://i0.wp.com/natifrinj.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/20221028_natifrinj_0039.jpg?fit=1024%2C683&ssl=1)

Nati frinj 20222. Photo : Suzanne Phoenix

##### Natimuk is a small regional township in a unique setting

We are a small population of approximately 510, which grows to around 3,500 people during the festival weekend. Natimuk is located several kms from the Mt Arapiles-Tooan State Park on the lands of the Wotjobaluk Nation.

The Nati Frinj Biennale ignites the town with activity as art and performance events are spread across various town venues and in the ‘Verj’ parkland. Walking between venues and outdoor locations for high-quality art experiences or just kicking back with friends is all part of the festival experience.

##### **Here is some useful information to help you have the best festival experience including travel, day visits or overnight/weekend stays, access and food options.** 

## How to get here

#### Transport Options

**Natimuk is located 324 kms north-west of Melbourne on the Wimmera Highway.**

**Driving** through the country side and small towns makes a wonderful half a day journey.

**Travelling via public transport** is via V/Line bus/train travels which run daily from Melbourne’s Spencer St Station and arrive in Horsham or from Adelaide to Horsham. Allow a little more time for transport connections.  
  
[For a V/line timetable Click here](https://www.vline.com.au/Timetables/Train-coach-timetables) 

##### Visit the Grampians ranges

![](https://i0.wp.com/natifrinj.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/BBD-SUMMER23-24-Posters_Grampians.jpg?fit=724%2C1024&ssl=1)

**For accommodation options and things to do** go to [www.visitgrampians.com.au](http://www.visitgrampians.com.au/)

## Where to stay

#### In town

**Natimuk Lake Caravan Park –**Camping by Lake Natimuk (5mins out of town) Address: 357 Lake Rd, Natimuk VIC 3409 Call : 0407 800 753  
Camping and caravan sites are available. Sites with power start at $35, Site without power start at $26

**Natimuk Show Grounds – Pop-up Camping** – hosted by Natimuk Show Grounds Committee of ManagementUnpowered sites available $50 per night

[NSGC Camping INfo](https://natifrinj.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Natimuk-Show-Grounds-Pop-up-Camping-Information-sheet.pdf)

[BOOK here](https://events.humanitix.com/natimuk-show-grounds-pop-up-camping/tickets)

##### Mt Arapiles – Tooan State Park

![](https://i0.wp.com/natifrinj.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Mt-Arapiles-image.jpg?fit=1024%2C768&ssl=1)

 **Mt Arapiles – Tooan State Park** Camping approximately 8kms west of town. Popular with rock climbers and bushwalkers, Centenary Park Campground at the base of Mt Arapiles (Dyurrite) offers three camping areas with toilets and picnic tables. One overnight site for two people starts at $6.20. Follow this link to book a camp site here   [Camping in Mount Arapiles-Tooan State Park](https://www.parks.vic.gov.au/places-to-see/parks/mount-arapiles-tooan-state-park/where-to-stay/camping-in-mount-arapiles-tooan-state-park) 

##### Visit Horsham and surrounds

**Airbnb accommodation in the region includes in** Natimuk, Mitre and Horsham, Dimboola and other locations in the region. Go to [Natimuk Holiday Rentals & Homes – Victoria, Australia | Airbnb](https://www.airbnb.com.au/natimuk-australia/stays)

**Other accommodation options** can be explored via [www.visithorsham.com.au](http://www.visithorsham.com.au/)

## Getting around

#### Access as you move around the festival

Natimuk is a small town, but after you have walked from one end to the other and back again in the pursuit of high-quality art experiences your feet may be feeling it. Bring a bike (and lock if your bike is precious) and/or some comfy shoes.

Access around Natimuk will require navigation across cracked and sometimes non-existent footpaths, please be aware of this as you plan your festival experience.

Venues : performances and events happen in all sorts of unique and quirky places, small halls, the rotunda, parks, sheds, even historic gaol cells! That’s part of what makes the festival special, but it also means that physical access can vary from venue to venue.

This year each event/venue has physical accessibility information:

![](https://i0.wp.com/natifrinj.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Access-info-image.jpg?fit=1024%2C557&ssl=1)

If you have any questions or need more detailed information about events or venues, we’re here to help.

Get in touch via

[Contact us](https://natifrinj.com/contact/)

## Dining and Food options across the festival weekend

##### Natimuk Hotel

Our local pub offers mouth-watering counter lunch and bistro evening meals, plus pizza available at the bar.

Open Friday – Sunday 11.30am till close

##### **Nati Milk Bar**

Perfect for a quick pie or sausage roll and cold drink, it also doubles as our fish n Chips

Open 8am -8pm

## LOOM | You move. It responds.

#### Artist’s collaboration : Dave Jones I Greg Pritchard I Beau Ladlow I Russell Goldsmith

![](https://i0.wp.com/natifrinj.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/LOOM_previs2B.jpg?fit=1024%2C768&ssl=1)

###### Step into an immersive world of sound, light, and movement. Inside the towering Grain Shed, digital art comes alive in real time, shaped by your presence. LOOM is an unmissable sensory experience where architecture, technology and creativity collide. Created by acclaimed regional artists and collaborators, LOOM is a bold experiment in digital theatre — where your presence becomes part of the artwork.

This project has been assisted by the Australian Government through the Festivals Australia program.

UTMB INDEX PRIORITY REGISTRATION

Holders of a valid [UTMB Index](https://utmb.world/utmb-world-series/runners/utmb-index), will have 48-hour priority access to a limited allocation of entries, starting at 11 AM AEST on 15 September 2026.

Priority registration gives UTMB Index Holders first access and the best chance to secure their spot at the start line!

If you have completed a [UTMB Index Race](https://utmb.world/index-races) (there’s over 4,000 worldwide) in the past two years, you will have a valid UTMB Index. To see if you have a valid UTMB Index and to set up your My UTMB account click here: UTMB Index.

**HOW TO ACCESS PRIORITY REGISTRATION**

For UTMB Index holders, to ensure you have a smooth registration process here’s a few tips:

1.  Ensure you have set-up your free [My UTMB Account](https://utmb.world/my-utmb/my-dashboard).
2.  During registration for UTA, enter your first name, last name, and date of birth exactly the way it appears in your My UTMB Account – the system will recognise your details and allow you to progress your registration.
3.  There is only a limited allocation of priority registrations available for UTMB Index holders, and they may sell out before 48hrs is up – first come, first served! If you miss out, please try again when general registrations open.

The priority entry link for UTMB Index holders will be emailed to runners and available by clicking enter now on the website. Only runners with a valid index will be able to access registration.

If you aren’t eligible for priority registration, you can register from 11 AM AEST on 17 September 2026 when General Entries go on sale.

## TERMS & CONDITIONS

See the 2027 terms & conditions below

2027 Terms and Conditions of Entry & Participation

](https://pdf.utmb.world/image/upload/v1787689235/uta/Event%20Waiver%20and%20Terms%20And%20Conditions/2027_Ultra_Trail_by_UTMB_Waiver_MC_08072026_1_8c517a97a3.pdf.pdf)

2027 Athlete Withdrawal Policy

](https://pdf.utmb.world/image/upload/v1787689236/uta/Event%20Waiver%20and%20Terms%20And%20Conditions/2027_Ultra_Trail_Australia_by_UTMB_Terms_and_Conditions_DRAFT_eb0316aa1f.pdf.pdf)

### UTAMILER QUALIFICATION

Completing a UTA Miler is a physically and mentally challenging event, and participation in it requires significant training and preparation. For your health and safety, we require evidence of your ability to take part by meeting this qualification criteria below:

*   A result from an official 50 km or longer trail race completed between 28 March 2025 and 28 March 2027 must be uploaded to your event registration, either when you initially register or later via your Participant Dashboard. Results must be submitted by 11:59 pm (AEST), 28 March 2027.
    
*   Official result: You must be an official finisher of the full course and have completed it within the advertised cut-off time.
    
*   Backyard Ultra: Results will be accepted where you have completed 50 km or more (8 yards or more) and your result is supported by official race results.
    
*   Race management reserves the right to reject any result deemed not meeting the above criteria.
    

You will only be contacted should your result not meet the above criteria. You will be provided an opportunity to re-submit your result prior to the cutoff date of 11:59pm (AEST) 28 March 2027. In the event you do not meet the criteria by the cutoff date, you will be notified and automatically moved into the UTA 100. Standard athlete withdrawal options apply prior to the 28 March 2027.

### UTA100, UTA50, UTA22, UTA11

There is no pre-requisite of competing or finishing any trail running event to participate in the UTA100. However, participating in UTMB World Series events, trail running events and half/marathon distance road running events will assist with your start group seeding.

All participants of the UTA100 should be experienced in trail running, including sufficiently skilled and trained to undertake a trail run event. The course is tough, demanding and is remote in sections that can result in slower first aid / rescue response times. It is a combination of fire trail, narrow walking tracks, some very steep sections on staircases, ladders, river/creek crossings, dirt, on rock and sections that are rough under foot.

It is the participants responsibility to ensure you are physically fit enough to complete the distance you have entered and monitor your health and condition during the event, including knowing when to withdraw from the event if you are no longer fit enough to continue.

### ATHLETE WITHDRAWAL POLICY

**ELIGIBLE ATHLETE WITHDRAWAL REFUNDS**

This Athlete Withdrawal Policy forms part of the Event’s Terms and Conditions of Entry & Participation and provides you with withdrawal options which are in addition to any existing entitlements you may have under applicable consumer protection law.

**Requests:** Without exception, all requests must be received on or before the below dates to be eligible for withdrawal options. All requests must be requested through the official form that can be found here: [Ultra-Trail Australia Withdrawal Form](https://in.njuko.com/2027-oceania-ultra-trail-withdrawal-form1775600273409)

Where eligible, please allow up to 30 business days for your refund to be processed. The refund is automatically issued to the credit card originally used to pay for the registration.

**Partial Refund:**

*   Requests received before 21 February 2027
    *   All athletes - 45% refund of entry fee
*   Requests received before 4 April 2027
    *   All athletes - 22% refund of entry fee
*   Requests received after 4 April 2027
    *   All athletes - No refunds under this Athlete Withdrawal Policy

**Additional Purchase Refunds**

Additional purchases paid for at the time of entry (if any) which are paid by the Event Operator to a third-party are not refundable or transferable.

These non-refundable additional purchases include:

*   Nirvana packages and accommodation (contact Nirvana directly)
*   Training packages (contact supplier directly)
*   Transport\*
*   Pre-purchased photo packs\*
*   Medal engraving tag\*
*   Bib Postage\*

\*May be refundable prior to the event where Event Operator has not incurred the cost

**Merchandise**

Your options regarding refunds for merchandise purchased during registration are outlined in the Online Store Terms and Conditions available via [https://utmbstoreoceania.myshopify.com/pages/terms-conditions](https://utmbstoreoceania.myshopify.com/pages/terms-conditions). Please note that refunds are not offered for change of mind merchandise purchases.

**Please note:** This event takes place in Katoomba, NSW, Australia. It is each athlete’s sole responsibility to ensure that they can attend (including Race Check-In during specified times) and compete in the event on the day. Other than as provided for in the Athlete Withdrawal program set out above or the Enter with Confidence deferral options below, no further remedies will be provided for change of mind, change of personal circumstances, or injury.

### TRANSFER TO A DIFFERENT DISTANCE

Athletes can request to transfer their entry to a lesser or greater race distance up until such time as that race distance is **sold out**, subject to the following terms: 

*   To request a transfer from one race distance to another, athletes must log into their **Participant Dashboard** and follow the necessary steps before 5:00pm (AEDT) on 13 May 2027.
*   **Transferring to a greater distance:** Where an athlete requests to transfer to a greater distance and space is available, the athlete is required to pay the difference in entry fees between the two distances. 
*   **Transferring to a shorter distance:** Where an athlete requests to transfer to a shorter distance and space is available, the difference in entry fees will not be refunded.

### TRANSFER TO A FRIEND

Athletes can transfer their race entry to a friend subject to the following terms:

*   Transfer request is submitted via original athlete’s Participant Dashboard before 5:00pm (AEST), 13 May 2027.
*   The transferred registration must be for the same distance.
*   The transfer is complete when the receiving athlete registers and pays (at the current advertised price on the [Event website](https://uta.utmb.world/runners/entry-info)) using the transfer registration link.
*   A full refund of the entry fee will be processed, less a $55 transfer fee, once the new transferred registration is completed.
*   Additional purchases and merchandise cannot be transferred to another athlete. The above Additional Purchase and Merchandise terms will apply.

As stated in the Athlete Terms of Entry and Participation, under no circumstance are you permitted to give your bib to another person. The safety of our athletes is paramount; therefore, we need to ensure we have correct details of all our athletes on course.

### PATH TO PARENTHOOD

UTMB have released the _UTMB World Series Path to Parenthood_, which applies to this event.

The full [UTMB World Series Path to Parenthood](https://utmb.world/inclusion) is available. A summary of this policy is included below for guidance. The full policy will apply to the extent of any inconsistency.

Eligible athletes (as outlined below) are able to request a full refund OR defer their entry for up to 2 years to the same race and distance as originally entered.

ELIGIBLE ATHLETE

MINIMUM DOCUMENTATION REQUIRED

Pregnant Athlete

a dated doctor’s note confirming the pregnancy.

Athletes pursuing Medically Assisted Reproduction (MAR)

a dated doctor’s note or note from a fertility clinic confirming that the Athlete is undergoing medically assisted reproduction (MAR). No medical diagnosis or treatment details are required. For sake of clarity, MAR includes in vitro fertilization (IVF), intracytoplasmic sperm injection, intrauterine insemination (IUI), egg retrieval, embryo transfer (fresh or frozen), donor cycles, ovulation-induction treatment, and medically indicated egg freezing.

Athletes with a pregnant partner with a due date within three months before or after the race

a dated doctor’s note confirming the pregnancy and proof of relationship if available (eg. marriage certificate, civil union documentation etc).

Athletes adopting a child or birthing via surrogacy

adoption or birth certificate dated within six months before the race.

**Note:** no particular outcome of the pregnancy or MAR is required; miscarriages and failed cycles remain covered, and do not need to be disclosed. Recognizing that one’s individual Path to Parenthood may be unpredictable, athletes may benefit from the policy if they meet the eligibility requirements at any point from the registration period up until race day. Athletes may be pregnant, already undergoing MAR, or in the process of adopting or welcoming a child through surrogacy at the time of registration, and they will still be entitled to a deferral or refund before race day if they choose to take advantage of those options.

**Policy Options**

*   A full refund of the registration fee (excluding service fees and additional purchases such as donations, photos, or accommodation & if the request is made at the latest, the date of the race). OR
*   Deferral up to 2 years to the same race category or shorter.

**Repeated Deferrals:** Athletes can repeat the deferral process for an additional deferral if they meet the Paths to Parenthood eligibility again during the deferral period. For instance, if an athlete defers a race due to MAR and then becomes pregnant during that period, they can then shift onto the pregnancy part of the policy without losing their place.

**Additional Requirements for Using a Deferred Entry Spot**

*   **Request Deadlines**: All requests made prior to the opening of registrations will be accepted. Requests made after registration is open cannot be guaranteed and are based on availability. No requests will be accepted after registrations for the event are closed.
*   **UTMB Index:** For events requiring a valid UTMB Index, runners should ensure it is valid at the time of registering for the deferred race.
*   **Verification:** The organizer may reasonably request additional proof if required, respecting the privacy and confidential nature of the Athlete’s personal situation, and deny requests at their discretion.

### DEFERRALS

No deferral option available.

### WHEELCHAIRS AND PRAMS ON COURSE

The safety of all athletes on course is our priority. Our event team considers each race/event individually to determine the entry requirements. Due to course conditions, Ultra-Trail Australia by UTMB is not suitable to be completed using wheelchairs or with prams across all distances. While this race is not suitable, our goal is to make everyone's racing dreams a reality so if you would like information on other events where the course is able to accommodate wheelchair participation or any other course accessibility needs, please email us at [ultratrailaustralia@service.byutmb.world](mailto:ultratrailaustralia@service.byutmb.world).

### ADAPTIVE ATHLETES

As part of UTMB's ongoing efforts to increase and encourage the participation of athletes with disabilities in trail running races, UTMB has implemented a new policy for all UTMB World Series events. Participants need to apply to UTMB to be approved prior to entering the Adaptive Athlete Open Division of Ultra-Trail Australia by UTMB. Please visit the UTMB website for further information and the process for Adaptive Athletes: [Inclusion & Diversity (utmb.world)](https://utmb.world/inclusion).

Once approved by UTMB, you can register for Ultra-Trail Australia by UTMB in the Adaptive Athlete Open Division. Please contact us directly at [ultratrailaustralia@service.byutmb.world](mailto:ultratrailaustralia@service.byutmb.world) after completing your entry.

Please Note: Due to course conditions, Ultra-Trail Australia by UTMB is not suitable to be completed using wheelchairs.

## RACE RULES

To the extent of any inconsistency between the 2027 Ultra-Trail Australia by UTMB Race Rules and the UTMB World Series Race Regulations, the UTA Race Rules will prevail. These UTMB World Series Race Regulations apply to the extent permissible under the laws of Australia.

# Safety Information

# Safety Is Our Highest Priority

The Distinguished Gentleman's Ride is an automotive fundraising event. We endeavour to make the ride as safe as possible for all participants of the ride as well as those around us. We have enlisted the help of [https://riskysoftware.io/](https://riskysoftware.io/) to highlight safety issues and address them.

They have also been set up with an email address [safety@gentlemansride.com](mailto:safety@gentlemansride.com) for any queries or feedback.

[

![](https://media.gentlemansride.online/tenant/0c3bf7ee-6d5e-4386-b329-a84c7b694c41/image/tenant/acb931f3-5b41-4d85-aef2-a9c3cc941cc6-riskysoftware.png)



](http://riskysoftware.io/)

## **How a DGR Ride Works**

Once you have registered your profile, prepared your bike & outfit and the day has arrived, It is time to ride dapper!

There are many components to a DGR ride including volunteer corner markers, mid group markers, first aid riders and support vehicles.

The most important points are:

*   To follow instructions
    
*   Ride behind the ride leader
    
*   No Overtaking
    
*   Follow the speed of the ride. It’s not a race.
    

## **What is the role of a Ride Host?**

A Ride Host is the person/team that is officially authorized from DGR to organize the event in their respective city.

While passionate and enthusiastic, it is important to remember all ride hosts are volunteers. They are there to represent The Distinguished Gentleman’s Ride and work alongside us to achieve our mission in changing men’s lives.

**How does one become a Ride Host?**

We require all Ride Hosts to apply to host a ride in their city. Once initially approved they are required to complete a set of Guidelines and Modules that encompass the core rules and responsibilities of becoming a Ride Host. Only once complete, DGR will approve the ride online.

**Organizing the Ride**

The main responsibility of a Ride Host is to organize the ride route, event times and the start & finish venues. Without our Ride Host’s this event would not be possible, they deserve your gratitude and respect.

## **Riding Safely: Important Points**

**Low-Speed Limits**

The ride takes part through the heart of each city to ensure low speed limits while riding dapper.

**Helmets Are Mandatory**

All riders must wear helmets that are legally compliant within their state/country.

**Obey Signs & Street Lights**

*   Do not block any roads without the consent of local authorities.
    
*   Do not run red lights.
    
*   Giveaway signs to be followed.
    

**Strictly No Burnouts! We Are Gentlefolk!**

Do not do stunts, burnouts, bike surfing or ride recklessly. This is not appropriate behaviour for this event. We ask all riders to set the best example. This event is a great way of combatting often negative motorcycling stereotypes.

## **Ensuring Safety: What safety procedures does DGR use?**

**Rides are required to be short in length and slow in speed**

A DGR ride is not a typical motorcycle ride. We are raising awareness in your city for men’s health. Limit the length of your ride to 30-40km / 20-30mi. Rides should stay off freeways and high speed roads.

**Don't forget to listen to the Ride Safety Speech**

It is required that our Ride Hosts give a ride safety speech. It is ideal to arrive as early as possible to the Ride Start Time to ensure you listen in to the Ride Safety Speed. Your Ride Host should cover the details of the ride, introducing the volunteer riders helping and most importantly the safety points of the ride. These vary across each city, state and country.

**Motorcycle Breakdowns**

Each ride will endeavour to have a support vehicle that has the capability to load up a broken down motorcycle. The DGR Support Vehicle stays at the back of the ride so they can sweep up any motorcycles along the way. They will drop the bike off either somewhere safer than it was collected or at the final destination where it is the participant’s responsibility to pick up the bike.

To report any incidents please [**click here and complete the incident report form**](https://www.surveymonkey.com/r/DGR_Incident_Report)

For any other information send an email to [safety@gentlemansride.com](mailto:safety@gentlemansride.com)

## Safety FAQ

What does DGR do to ensure there are no collisions?

The Ride Host for your particular city is reminded to give a safety briefing prior to the start of the ride to remind all participants that bikes should maintain a slow speed and safe distance. DGR will also send an email reminder to all registered participants to highlight the risks and information on how to ride safely.

What happens if I have a malfunctioning motorcycle as a result of poor maintenance or age?

Control - Organisers will attempt to have a sweeper vehicle with the capacity to safely move broken down vehicles. The vehicle should contain a tool kit, first aid kit (or a first aid certified provider riding at the rear of the pack with a first aid kit). This may not be possible in each domicile. Please ensure your bike is in working and safe order before joining us on the event. DGR will create imagery throughout the campaign to promote to participants that their bike needs to be in a roadworthy state. This will be included in the safety memo emailed to all registered participants.

Infringement of local law as a result of inappropriate riding behavior?

Control - Inappropriate riding is not accepted. Organisers will announce that inappropriate riding behaviour will not be accepted and anyone who attempts to ruin the event will have their number plate details given to local authorities. We communicate this via email and on social media.

What does DGR do to ensure everyone is wearing the minimum personal protective equipment?

We continuously inform all riders that they must wear personal protective equipment that meets local legislation requirements especially helmets and goggles. We communicate this via email and on social media.

What if the weather is inappropriate to ride?

In the interest of safety and bad weather, the organiser can postpone rides if the weather appears unsuitable. DGR will give access to ride hosts to communicate this via email and facebook to all participants.

What happens if the ride is too large? What controls does DGR implement?

We encourage the use of loudspeaker (if possible) to ensure participants can hear the pre-ride safety briefing. Organisers are to monitor and record numbers of actual participants in order to safely estimate the next year’s numbers. In case of the ride hitting capacity, there will be a limit set on registrations for that ride. DGR will continue to promote itself as a classic styled bike event to keep the number of attendees down. Riders should also print out the details of the ride to ensure they have them on hand at the event.

What to do when there is excessive sun exposure resulting in dehydration, fatigue and sunburn contributing to incident or accident.

Rides are encouraged to start at places that offer shelter, food and drinks. The event is short and usually only goes for approx. 3 hours. If it is expected to be extremely sunny or hot, we will encourage riders to bring and apply sunscreen.

Riders speeding to catch up with group if the group is separated at intersections.

Part of our guidelines are that the route should be well mapped out and published in advance. This is a suggested route with participants choosing alternative routes if they feel unsafe. The route will be covered at the safety briefing by your ride host. Each ride may have multiple re-group points to ensure people do not rush to catch up to other riders.

How do you stop excessive speeding and thus resulting in an incident?

The speeds on the ride will be low, managed by lead riders and marshals. DGR is a slow-paced, short event that takes place in busy locations to ensure the speed is limited.

Intoxicated while riding resulting in an incident.

If someone is deemed intoxicated they must be removed from the ride and the local authorities informed. We take this very seriously and we will communicate this with all participants via email and social media.

What to do in the event there is inadequate parking at the start, finish and stop locations resulting in traffic congestion, illegal parking and traffic hazards.

Organisers are advised to select areas suitable for the numbers they are expecting. Some rides may have unexpected riders join through friends. We ask that all riders register to ensure we can provide adequate space for these riders.

Deliberate or unexpected incursion by motorists into the ride group.

We remind all participants of our gentlemanly ways and if the vehicle does not cause injury or damage to a participant regardless of how it intrudes, give it room and let it carry on.

What happens if a vehicle causes injury or damage to a participant?

We encourage riders to ensure that the welfare of the rider(s) is attended to immediately and that the safety of all other participants and the general public is maintained. We encourage riders to ensure the welfare of the motorcycle is seen to and obstruction of traffic flow is minimized. If the motorist fails to stop, DO NOT pursue them, simply ensure that all details of the vehicle (make, model, colour, license plate number) are recorded to pass on to police. If the motorist stops to assist, DO NOT threaten, abuse or attempt to engage the motorist. Instead, have them wait in a safe place until police arrive.

What happens if local law enforcements cancel the ride?

We will do our best to work with ride hosts and communicate with local law enforcement prior to and during the event if required (each country has different rules). If the ride is shut down, we will accept the request. Ensuring the safety of participants is our utmost priority.

## MINI JCW X Deus

Deus Ex Machina and MINI JCW present a partnership that celebrates both brands storied legacy of automotive enthusiasm - a collaboration that seamlessly merges racing heritage and contemporary design sensibility.  
  
[See More](https://deuscustoms.co.id/pages/mini "MINI JCW x Deus")

![](//deuscustoms.co.id/cdn/shop/files/2260x1350_specterdeus_04_d9455284-4878-4201-ab6d-13e6f4d8eec1.jpg?v=1743053641&width=640)

## Specter Design x Deus Customs

A full circle moment, the longstanding creative partnership between Specter Design and Deus Ex Machina culminates in a limited edition capsule range - an ode to both brands’ deep appreciation for craftsmanship and design principles that extend beyond the bounds of any one discipline or practice.

[See More](https://deuscustoms.co.id/blogs/magazine/specter-design-x-deus-customs "Specter Design x Deus Customs")

![](//deuscustoms.co.id/cdn/shop/files/Bob_and_Beau.png?v=1743054697&width=640)

## Bob Moore x Beau Foster

We're thrilled to introduce a special artist collaboration with Robert 'Bob' Moore and Beau Foster. Bob's adroit brushwork is deftly applied to a series of six hand-shaped boards custom-built by Beau for the project.  
  
[See More](https://deuscustoms.co.id/pages/bob-moore-x-beau-foster "Bob Moore x Beau Foster")

![](//deuscustoms.co.id/cdn/shop/files/YT_cover.png?v=1743054218&width=640)

## Matt Willey x Deus Customs

If you haven't heard Matt Willey's name, you've certainly seen his work. Following five years as art director of New York Times Magazine, the English born, Brooklyn based designer became a partner at the renowned design firm Pentagram. Our collaboration project and capsule collection which has Monte Carlo Rally winning Mini Coopers in its DNA

[See More](https://deuscustoms.co.id/blogs/magazine/deus-x-matt-willey "DEUS X MATT WILLEY")

![](//deuscustoms.co.id/cdn/shop/files/BREITLING_DEUS.png?v=1743054861&width=640)

## Deus x Breitling 2023

Hot on the heels of two sold-out limited editions, Breitling and Deus have joined forces on a third installment of the Top Time Deus, set to become part of Breitling's core collection.  
  
[See More](https://deuscustoms.co.id/pages/deus-x-breitling-2023 "Deus x Breitling 2023")

![](//deuscustoms.co.id/cdn/shop/files/Slowtide.png?v=1743054964&width=640)

## Deus x Slowtide

We’re thrilled to introduce the latest iteration of our ongoing collaboration with Slowtide featuring two new towels dripping in style (pun fully intended) and a full restock of our previous collabs.  
  
[See More](https://deuscustoms.co.id/pages/deus-x-slowtide-2023 "Deus x Slowtide 2023")

![](//deuscustoms.co.id/cdn/shop/files/ArkAir.webp?v=1743055163&width=640)

## Deus x ArkAir

We’re thrilled to introduce our latest collaboration with ArkAir, a military-grade capsule collection that's equal parts pit-stop and paratrooper.  
  
[See More](https://deuscustoms.co.id/pages/deus-x-arkair "Deus x ArkAir")

![](//deuscustoms.co.id/cdn/shop/files/Solido_d6c8677d-3023-460c-a8b2-069349074a3b.webp?v=1743055540&width=640)

## Deus x Solido Porsche 356

The Deus Three Five Six started life as a screen-printed art edition of our dream outlaw hotrod, we tapped the model car maestros at Solido to immortalize this four-wheeled paragon that stirred our loins in two dimensions and bring it into three.  
  
[See More](https://deuscustoms.co.id/pages/deus-x-solido-porsche "Deus x Solido Porsche")

![](//deuscustoms.co.id/cdn/shop/files/Cariuma.png?v=1743055604&width=640)

## Deus x Cariuma

Inspired by life on the road and the pursuit of fun, our latest collaboration with Cariuma is all about a free spirited existence and admiration for the planet in which we traverse. We’ve teamed up to create a simple and timeless design crafted to live with you and in harmony with our planet.  
  
[See More](https://deuscustoms.co.id/pages/deus-x-cariuma-2023 "Deus x Cariuma 2023")

![](//deuscustoms.co.id/cdn/shop/files/Bleach.png?v=1743055750&width=640)

## Deus x Bleach Design Werks

Introducing Deus x Bleach. A shared desire to celebrate the fundamental pursuits of fun takes form in this collaboration. We let Mikey Ojeda of Bleach Design Werks loose on tees, hoodies, jerseys and more, all made in the USA. Inspired by his love of motocross and the city of Los Angeles these threads showcase the same freestyling flavor of Mikey’s custom machines.  
  
[See More](https://deuscustoms.co.id/blogs/magazine/deus-x-bleach-design-werks-collection-launch "Deus X Bleach Design Werks Collection Launch")

![](//deuscustoms.co.id/cdn/shop/files/Breitling2022.png?v=1743055822&width=640)

## Deus x Breitling 2022

Co-Designed with Swiss luxury Watchmaker Breitling, the Top Time Deus is a nod to their original 1960s watch and a true tribute to the nomad spirit.  
  
[See More](https://deuscustoms.co.id/pages/deus-x-breitling-2022 "Deus x Breitling 2022")

![](//deuscustoms.co.id/cdn/shop/files/FCS.png?v=1743055889&width=640)

## Deus x FCS

The ethos of the collaboration was to take the things we use everyday in the surf and make them better - in design, style and function.  
  
[See More](https://deuscustoms.co.id/pages/deus-x-fcs-2023 "Deus x FCS 2022")

![](//deuscustoms.co.id/cdn/shop/files/eastpak.png?v=1743055916&width=640)

## Deus x Eastpak

A collection that celebrates the pure joy of motion, no matter what your choice of machine: from planes, trains and automobiles to motorcycles, surfboards or your own two feet.  
  
[See More](https://deuscustoms.co.id/pages/deus-x-eastpak-2022 "Deus x Eastpak 2022")

![](//deuscustoms.co.id/cdn/shop/files/100.png?v=1743055997&width=640)

## Deus x 100%

This is the fifth goggled formed through our shared experiences in motorcycling, design and fashion, while exploring the culture, creativity and special sauce that make both 100% and Deus Ex Machina tick!  
  
[See More](https://deuscustoms.co.id/pages/deus-x-100-barstow-2023 "Deus x 100% Barstow 2023")

![](//deuscustoms.co.id/cdn/shop/files/Gramicci.png?v=1743056026&width=640)

## Deus x Gramicci

At it's core, Deus and Gramicci's mission statements revolve around a passion and enthusiasm for outdoor activities. So we've teamed up with Gramicci for the second time on a limited edition capsule spanning mens and womens.  
  
[See More](https://deuscustoms.co.id/pages/deus-x-gramicci "Deus x Gramicci")

![](//deuscustoms.co.id/cdn/shop/files/Solido_Mini.jpg?v=1743056091&width=640)

## Deus x Solido MW Mini

If you haven't heard Matt Willey's name, you've certainly seen his work. Following five years as art director of New York Times Magazine, the English born, Brooklyn based designer became a partner at the renowned design firm Pentagram. He invited us into his home and studio to discuss the collaboration project and capsule collection which has Monte Carlo Rally winning Mini Coopers in its DNA.⁠.Headlining the collaboration is a historic racing Mini Cooper S with custom livery designed by Willey. The design references the Mini's storied and winning history at the Monte Carlo Rally including the Monte Carlo coat of arms, rally pace note hieroglyphics and period (in)correct advertising copy lines.

[See More](https://deuscustoms.co.id/blogs/magazine/deus-x-matt-willey "DEUS X MATT WILLEY")

# Pre Race Info

[](https://www.facebook.com/ultratrailaustralia)[](https://instagram.com/ultratrailaustralia)[](https://www.youtube.com/user/AROCSport)

Runner ListsRunner GuideCheck InEvent AppStart/Finish Village

## RUNNER LISTS

Race week runner lists can be found on the event app from 4 weeks out from race day.

2026 Runner Guide

The runner guide contains everything you need to know for the event. It is a very important document which all runners must read.

Please find the 2026 Runner Guide below (last updated 21.04.26)

[

2026 Runner Guide

](https://uta.utmb.world/runners/runners-guide)

RACE CHECK-IN

Race check in for UTA is done at KCC Auditorium, located on the corner of Cliff Drive and Violet St, opposite Scenic World in Katoomba. Please refer to the  [event schedule](https://uta.utmb.world/runners/event-schedule)  for the exact times of UTA race check-in.

At race check-in you will collect your race pack which includes your race number and other items of mandatory equipment such as maps, course descriptions and emergency instructions. Also included in your race pack is also a bag timing tag. This is a separate timing tag to be attached to your backpack.

Only the person registered can pick up their race pack, and can only be collected during check-in opening hours. They will not be posted out prior to the event.

**What to bring to check-in:**

*   Photo ID (driver’s licence or passport):
*   Mandatory gear check certificate (UTA100 & UTAMiler Only): Gear check will be available during the same time as check-in at KCC, or you can also perform an early gear check in the months prior to the event.

DOWNLOAD THE APP

To help ensure you have the best possible UTA experience, please download the latest version of Ultra-Trail Australia app. It has the full event schedule, course maps and other key event information you need ahead of arriving in Katoomba.

Your family & friends will also be able to follow you on race day so make sure they download it too!

[

DOWNLOAD FOR APPLE

](https://apps.apple.com/nz/app/ultra-trail-australia/id1103940357)

  

[

DOWNLOAD FOR ANDROID

](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=nz.netproject.ultratrailaustralia)

## START/FINISH VILLAGE

We're headed back to Scenic World for our start lines and finish line for 2025. Scenic World has been home to so many iconic UTA memories, and we can't wait to create many more at this years UTA. Here's what you can expect:

**Start Lines**

For the UTA100 and UTA50, your start line will return to being under the big finish arch. We will flow you into chute as you line up pre-start, before then heading out through recovery, turning right and then left onto Cliff Drive.

UTA11 - runners are so speedy that there will be finishers in this distance before all runners have even started, which means we will have a separate start line set up for you, as shown on the map. You'll roll straight out and left onto Cliff Drive.

UTA22 - you will start at Queen Victoria Hospital in Wentworth falls before running down Kedumba Pass into the Kedumba valley.

UTAMiler - you will begin you 100 miles at Govetts Leap (subject to change)

**Finish Line**

The finish line will be in a slightly different location to previous Scenic World finish lines, however runners will still make their way right to the top of Furber Steps, along the boardwalk, past the entrance to Scenic World, through the hoards of cheering spectators, and underneath the finish arch. There's more opportunity for high-fives and pictures, for you to soak up the emotion of your amazing achievement. Remember, you can have friends and family join you in the finish chute - they'll be able to do so just next to the Scenic World entrance. Please be courteous to other finishers - this is their moment too!

After you cross the finish line and have your medal placed around your neck, you'll flow through recovery - with food and beverage options for you to peruse, as well as medical on hand. When you're ready, you can exit recovery and join your friends and family, kick back and cheer on other runners.

**Drop Bags**

Finish line drop bags will be located in the newly re-furbished CMS, to the south of the venue. Massage can also be found here.

**Food & Drink**

A range of Food Vendors will be operating within the venue, in case you're feeling peckish. All of these are local vendors from the Blue Mountains region.

A bar will be operating, on the north side of the finish chute. You can crack a cold one and cheer on runners, but please only do so within the licensed area.

**Merchandise**

Pick yourself up some sweet merch to commemorate your finish, and even get your medal engraved at the merch tent.

**Scenic World Event Lounge**

If you've got crew hanging around waiting for you to finish (especially during the early hours when it gets nippy) send them into the Scenic World Event Lounge, where there will be a live feed of the finish line, and food and drink available.

CheckpointsDrop BagsCourse Markings Spectators

CHECKPOINTS

Please note we are a cup-less event. In an effort to cut down on waste, we will have no drinking cups at checkpoints. You will need to carry a cup or hydration pack with you. Limited stock of cups and hydrations packs will be available for sale at the event expo, but we encourage you to purchase one in advance and use it in your training.

First Aid will be available at each checkpoint, the Emergency Aid Station and the finish. There will also be roving first aid crews on the course.

There will be port-a-loos at the start, all checkpoints except CP 1: Narrow Neck, and the Emergency Aid Station. There will be flushing toilets at Katoomba Aquatic Centre, Fairmont Resort and the Finish.

Checkpoints are stocked with a mixture of:

*   Naak Nutrition (including drink mix, gels, and waffles)
*   Gels
*   Water
*   Hot water, tea, coffee, soup
*   Soft Drink
*   Lollies
*   Fruit
*   Bakery goods

Note - not all items listed above will be available at every checkpoint. Exact checkpoint stocks will be available to view in the Runner Guide.

If you are using a support crew you must also read the [UTA100 Support Crew](https://uta.utmb.world/races/uta100) section.

DROP BAGS

A drop bag service will be available which allows you to have your own personal supplies (gels, food, change of socks, shoes, shorts, lubricant, etc.) available at certain check points or at the finish. Please see the time charts above for information on which checkpoints have drop bags.

Your bag needs be closable and soft and a reasonable size. Cool-bags from the big supermarkets are perfect! In line with our commitment to sustainability please don’t use plastic bags or plastic boxes – these will not be accepted. One drop bag per runner is allowed for each locations.

Checkpoint drop bags must be delivered to the checkpoint trucks at race check-In on the Friday between 10:00am and 7:00pm. Please don't be early, as if not placed directly into the correct checkpoint trucks they may go missing!

Finish line drop bags can be left in the designated Drop Bag area near KCC on Friday ONLY from 10:00am - 7:00pm.

Drop bags will be returned to the drop bag marquee at Scenic World within 4 hours after the relevant checkpoint cut-off time. **Drop Bags must be collected from Scenic World by 2:00PM on Sunday 18th May.** Collect by showing your race number. Any drop bags not collected by 10am Monday will be donated if appropriate or disposed of.

*   Please don’t use glass bottles/jars
*   Clearly mark your drop-bag using the provided stickers in your race pack. These will be colour coded based on the CP location, have the name of the CP on and your bib number.
*   At checkpoints and the finish line - drop bags will be lined up numerical order. Any bags without or clearly written/visible with a name and race number, will placed at the end of the number range.
*   Only the runner can collect their drop bag at the drop bag locations. Once each checkpoint drop bag is finished with it must be taken to the used drop bag pile.
*   Please don’t use the drop bag service for any checkpoints where your support crew will meet you.

## RACE DAY COURSE MARKINGS

All UTA course will be marked with red directional arrows on a white background '→', dark blue crosses on white background 'X' and pink flagging tape. There will also be reflective tape and arrows on night-time sections.

There will be course markings at least every 500m and at every track junction. At all track junctions there will be an arrow indicating the direction of the route as well as confirmation pink flagging tape along the correct route. There will also be a cross on the tracks that you should not take. There will be a distance sign every 5km.

## SPECTATORS

We encourage spectators to get out on course and support their runners!

Spectators can see runners at many points along the Ultra-Trail Australia by UTMB courses. We ask that you please respect private landowners and do not cross any private property. If spectating on course, please respect runners and support crews and do your best to spectate in a supportive, safe manner. Any on course spectating outside of supported checkpoints can only be moral support – no material or physical supporting is allowed.

For more helpful information please visit the [Transport Services](https://uta.utmb.world/runners/transport-parking) page and [Spectators](https://uta.utmb.world/get-involved/spectators) page.

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/59c0a6f1221db50001e7e23f/5a37047b781e400001e0c20b_Astral-People-Vichara-Edirisinghe-1200.jpg)

Vichara Edirisinghe

OUR STORY

After a late night meeting at Dimitri’s Pizza in 2011, Astral People was born

**Astral People** is one of Sydney’s most influential independent music companies, whose multi-faceted approach to the music industry is matched only by their eclectic taste.   
  
Formed after a late night dinner at Dimitri’s Pizza in 2011 between directors **Tom Huggett** and **Vichara Edirisinghe** (alongside Lee Danilewitz), **Astral People** now finds itself a team of many across their distinct management, touring, events, publishing, and label arms: all of which stay true to the company’s original philosophy of community investment and trust in the Astral People vision.  
  
Artist-focused at its core, **Astral People’s** management roster covers some of the most forward-thinking in Australian music. With a family of local artists including multi-instrumentalists **Cosmo’s Midnight**, **Winston Surfshirt**, **Wave Racer**, **GL**, **Milan Ring**, and **Collarbones**, DJs & producers **Ayebatonye**, **Basenji**, **Memphis LK**, **moktar**, **Sam Alfred, Tseba,** and **Willo**, rapper **Arno Faraji**, and audio engineers **George Nicholas** and **Doug Wright**, **Astral People’s** management net is cast wide: and looks to be cast wider in time.  
  
**Astral People’s** taste is emphasised in their touring roster, a melting pot of subcultures from across the world. First finding footing bringing grime to Australian and New Zealand shores in the mid-2010s, the company continues to push boundaries and is now a touring staple of the region.  
  
In 2015, **Astral People** merged with **Handsome Tours** to build one of the largest independent rosters in Australia, covering pioneering electronic producers **Ross From Friends, Fred again..,** and **Bicep**, the cutting-edge experimenters **100 gecs** and **Injury Reserve**, soul adventurers **Arlo Parks** and **Masego**, stadium grime acts **Stormzy, AJ Tracey**, and **Dave**, UK jazz artists **Yussef Dayes**, **Kokoroko**, and **Alfa Mist**, underground kings **Freddie Gibbs** and **Yung Lean**, and world-class DJs like **Jyoty, Shanti Celeste, Folamour, John Talabot, Moxie,** and **Yung Singh**: lists far from exhaustive.   
  
Staying curious curatorially, **Astral People’s** boutique events arm have shown off a multitude of international and local talent. From their own festival endeavours including **OutsideIn Festival, Last Dance NYE** and **Summer Dance**, to curating stages for **Red Bull, Splendour** **in the Grass, Strawberry Fields,** and **Vivid LIVE** for the company’s 10th birthday party, **Astral People** have been partymakers for well over a decade now.  
  
2017 saw **Astral People** launch their own publishing arm with the world’s largest independent publisher BMG, harbouring artists such as **CLYPSO, moktar, Winston Surfshirt,** and **Young Franco**. Soon after, **Astral People Recordings** began in collaboration with \[PIAS\], becoming the first Australia co-op label under their wide international umbrella, releasing disparate music from **Stevan, Wave Racer, Bumpy, Milan Ring, Skeleten,** and **Club Angel**, with more in the pipeline.  
  
**Astral People** stay leaders in the Australian and New Zealand music scene, with a twelve year history dedicated to community investment and staying true to their vision. Every member of the team a fan of music first, **Tom** and **Vichara** find opportunities in untouched corners.  
  
Putting on the first shows for management act **Cosmo’s Midnigh**t (who now sell venues across the world), debuting **Stormzy** to Australia in 2015 to less than 500 early-adopters, bringing New York to Sydney with a Belmore Park day party for **Mister Sunday** (notwithstanding some torrential downpour)... their attention to and fandom of niche, up-and-coming scenes globally and locally, with potential often only they can hear, has made them one of the most trusted voices across their music industry disciplines.   
  
Today, **Astral People’s** unique touch can be felt in virtually every space imaginable. From clubbing institutions to cherished festivals, the prestigious **Sydney Opera House** to local DIY spots, calendars are filled across the country with **Astral People’s** curative taste.   
  
With an eye to genuine growth and more creative output, **Astral People** remain multi-hyphenate and curious, staying leaders for the years to come.

Global Partner

The Distinguished Gentleman's Ride is proud to have Triumph join us for an 13th consecutive year of bringing classic and vintage style motorcyclists together. 2026 marks the continuation of this important partnership of what has been a great success story.

In 2026, the Top 3 Fundraisers and the Gentlefolk Prize Winner for the year will each receive a modern classic Triumph motorcycle. 

The Triumph Modern Classic motorcycle family represents the quintessence of The Distinguished Gentleman’s Ride spirit: elegant, iconic, characterful, and built for the ride.

[Find out more about our partnership with Triumph Motorcycles.](https://gentlemansride.com/about/triumphmotorcycles)

[Visit Hedon for more details.](https://hedon.com/en-au)

The Distinguished Gentleman's Ride is proud to continue our partnership with ELF Lubricants, which started in 2018, and now marks 9 incredible years.

Committed to meeting the needs of all motorcycle riders, ELF is an iconic brand with a legendary history, and stands out for bringing passion and emotion to riders’ daily life. With this philosophy in mind, ELF showcases an exclusive range of lubricants specially formulated for motorcycles and scooters: ELF MOTO.

[For more information visit ELF.](http://elf.com/)

Technical Partner

Bring tech to your fingertips with Quad Lock’s smartphone motorcycle mount and case this is now fast becoming an essential for all motorcycles globally.

To help reward fundraisers in this year’s event, Quad Lock will be offering a range of prizes available only to registered fundraisers in the event.

[To see more about Quad Lock click here.](https://www.quadlockcase.com.au/)

Brett will be offering a range of rewards to top fundraisers, gentlefolk competition winners and more.

title: Sydney Contemporary
description: Australasia's premier art fair returns to Carriageworks from 3–6 September 2026. Discover 100 galleries, contemporary art, installations, talks and more.
markdown:
Sydney Contemporary

 [![Sydney Contemporary](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/2015/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/untitled-design-1.png) ![Sydney Contemporary](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/2015/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/untitled-design-1.png)](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/)

9 – 12 September 2027

9 – 12 Sept 2027

Carriageworks

# Sydney Contemporary is Australasia's premier art fair, the place to discover and buy exceptional contemporary art from over 100 galleries and 500 artists.

Thank you to the galleries, collectors, partners, artists and art lovers who joined us at Carriageworks for Sydney Contemporary’s 10th edition!

To the thousands of visitors who came through the doors, thank you for showing up, discovering new artists, buying art, starting conversations and celebrating with us. Your enthusiasm, curiosity and energy are what bring the Fair to life.

For four days each September, Carriageworks fills with ambitious gallery presentations, large-scale installations, inspiring encounters, and spectacle. We can’t wait to welcome you back in 2027!

Stay connected for the latest gallery news, artist stories, exhibitions and announcements as we look ahead to Sydney Contemporary 2027.

Sydney Contemporary   
9–12 September 2027  
Carriageworks, Sydney  
Principal Partner MA Financial Group

[Subscribe and Stay Connected](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/sign-up/)

## What collectors said about Sydney Contemporary 2026

“Sydney Contemporary is, in our opinion, the art event that we simply will never miss. The range of artists and galleries and the manner in which it is presented is without peer in this country, in our view. The majority of the art we have acquired in the last 5 years has understandably been sourced from this week each year.”

**Craig and Chrissie Hart, Collectors, Melbourne**

“This year’s Sydney Contemporary was, for us, the best we have attended, and we have attended all 10! The fair has improved consistently over the years, however this year was next level! As collectors we will continue to come to Sydney especially for Fair week and the increasing number of activities built around the event across Sydney. A really important calendar event for the visual arts in this country!”

**Stephanie Grose, Collector, Adelaide**

“Sydney Contemporary is always one of the highlights of the year for my Melbourne collector group! We love coming together and spending a few days in Sydney immersed in the excitement and energy of the fair. It’s always such a fun few days of discovering, connecting, and sharing our love of art.”

**Elle Zoltak, Collector, Melbourne**

## Sydney Contemporary returns to Carriageworks  
9–12 September 2027

Save the date and join us for four days of contemporary art, discovery, conversation and collecting! Applications to exhibit at Sydney Contemporary 2027 will open in late 2026. 

Until then, stay connected for artist stories, gallery news, exhibitions, and announcements from Sydney Contemporary.

[Subscribe and Stay Connected](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/sign-up/)

![](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/2015/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/4-1.png)

![](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/2015/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/3.png)

## What gallerists said about Sydney Contemporary 2026

“Had we forgotten how to have fun in all the gloom? Sydney Contemporary 2026 showed us how to celebrate inclusively. Massive crowds every day of enthusiastic art lovers confirmed how important artists, emerging and established and their galleries are in our lives.”

**Beverly Knight  
Alcaston Gallery, Melbourne**

“This year’s 10th edition of Sydney Contemporary was extraordinary. The energy felt explosive, ambitious, dynamic and impossible to ignore. It was a landmark edition that reflected the growing confidence and international reach of Australia’s contemporary art scene. We couldn’t be more thrilled to have been part of it.”

**Cassandra Bird  
CASSANDRA BIRD,** **Sydney & Paris**

“This year’s fair was one of the strongest on record. The atmosphere was vibrant, and there was a real sense of energy and momentum throughout the entire event. It was also exciting to see the collector base continuing to grow, creating an even greater level of engagement with the galleries and artists. As a new Sydney gallery owner, I think having Sydney Contemporary energise and activate the city’s art world in this way is absolutely priceless.”

**Danielle Renshaw  
The Renshaws’,** **Brisbane & Sydney**

DISCOVER, EXPERIENCE, COLLECT

## The Galleries

At the heart of Sydney Contemporary is an exceptional line-up of galleries from across Australia, New Zealand, Asia and beyond, filling the Fair with ambitious presentations.

Explore works across painting, sculpture, photography, ceramics and more. From iconic names to the next generation of artists shaping contemporary practice, every corner of the Fair offers something unexpected, with every artwork available to buy.

[![](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/2015/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/social-solo-duo-819x1024.png)](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/artwork-sydney/)

### Galleries

Leading galleries present standout contemporary art across every medium, and at a range of price points.

[](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/artwork-photo-sydney/)

### Photo Sydney

Discover contemporary photography, from documentary and conceptual work to large-scale experimental practice. 

[](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/artwork-futures/)

### Futures

Meet the artists and galleries shaping what’s next, with emerging talent and fresh ideas that are often the first to watch.

[](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/artwork-paper/)

### Works on Paper

From prints and drawings to watercolours and artist books, discover works on paper that make collecting contemporary art accessible and endlessly varied.

IN THE PRESS

"The art fair that's become the exact event that Sydney needs"

Sydney Morning Herald

"The largest and most diverse art fair in the country – and it's brilliant"

Time Out Sydney

"After nine years, Sydney Contemporary is still a hub of innovation and imagination"

Broadsheet

"Sydney Contemporary continues to cement itself as Australasia's premier art fair"

Harper's Bazaar Australia

"… pivotal art fair shaping an Asia-Pacific art circuit"

Ocula

"Affordable or significant? Sydney's biggest art fair offers both"

Australian Financial Review

“This democratising of art is perhaps Sydney Contemporary’s greatest success.”

ArtsHub

## Fair Program

Alongside the gallery presentations, Sydney Contemporary’s program brings together artist talks, panel discussions, live performance, large-scale installations and workshops across Carriageworks. The 2027 program will be announced in 2027.

[](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/installations/)

PANEL DISCUSSIONS

### Let's Talk Art

Conversations with artists, curators, collectors and thinkers exploring the ideas, debates and trends shaping contemporary art.

[](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/friday-night/)

IMMERSIVE LARGE-SCALE WORKS

### Installations

Discover ambitious installations that take contemporary art beyond the gallery booth and into the wider Fair and city.

EXPLORE WITH EXPERTS

### Guided Tours

Explore contemporary art through expert-led tours offering fresh perspectives on artists, artworks and gallery presentations.

AT GALLERY BOOTHS

### Artist Talks

Hear directly from artists about their work, ideas and practices, and gain insight into the thinking behind the art.

OVER A DECADE AT THE CENTRE OF CONTEMPORARY ART

## Australasia's Premier Art Fair

Over ten editions, Sydney Contemporary has grown from a bold idea into one of the most significant contemporary art fairs in the region.

Bringing together leading galleries from Australia, New Zealand, Asia and around the world, the Fair has established itself as Australasia’s premier art fair and a major fixture on the international art calendar.

It is where collectors, artists, gallerists, curators, advisors and first-time buyers come together to discover new work, build collections, exchange ideas and make connections across the art world.

Its strength lies not only in its scale, but in the breadth and ambition of its program. Alongside gallery presentations, Sydney Contemporary commissions large-scale installations, presents live performance, talks, tours and educational programs, transforming Carriageworks into a vibrant cultural hub each September.

More than an art fair, Sydney Contemporary is a defining moment in Sydney’s cultural calendar – bringing the art world together and opening it up to new audiences.

# Rip Curl Cup Padang Padang

Now celebrating “23 Years of Tubes,” The Rip Curl Cup Invitational at Padang Padang is Indonesia’s longest-running and most prestigious surfing competition, one of the best invitational contests on earth featuring the world’s greatest tuberiders alongside Indonesia’s best.

# Rip Curl Cup Padang Padang 2026

![SponsorBanners\_samudera-600x241px.png\_\_PID:94954a20-7d71-461d-9e5c-e3f35c03fe57](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0570/6124/5081/files/SponsorBanners_samudera-600x241px_500x.png?v=1718762181)

### Main Event Window:

### 1 - 31 August 2022

The Rip Curl Cup Padang Padang is the highlight event of the year for us, providing an amazing opportunity to be able to showcase the best Indonesian surfers against some of the world’s most renowned and talented tube riders in pumping conditions at Padang-Padang.

In 2026 the Rip Curl Cup celebrates its 23-year anniversary with one of the most exclusive fields in professional surfing: just 24 invited surfers – twelve of Indonesia’s finest and twelve of the world’s elite. The limited number of surfer invitations ensures this will be a “one-day, one-swell” event, increasing the likelihood of spectacular conditions and incredible performances. When contest directors determine an ideal Padang swell lining up in the Indian Ocean, the green light will be given and competitors will have 48 hours to make it to Bali’s Bukit Peninsula.

The waiting period for the 2026 Rip Curl Cup spans an entire month, from 1 – 31 August, during the peak of Indonesia’s prime swell season, providing the event with the highest chance of scoring the spitting green barrels the Balinese Pipeline is world-famous for.

Bol Winning 2005

Exactly 20 years ago, Bol claimed his second title as Rip Curl Cup Padang Padang Champion. Battling it out with local legends Rizal Tandjung, Pepen Hendrik, and Betet Merta, they turned Padang Padang into the ultimate surf battlefield.

Jack Robinson 2018

“It was worth the wait” - Jack RobinsonAt 20, Jack Robinson claimed a monumental victory at Padang, dazzling with three 9s and a perfect 10. His unbeatable 19.90 Finals score sealed the win.The victory was a long time coming after his first invitation back in 2013 at the age of 15, but never got to cash in his golden ticket until 2018, when Padang awakened with treacherous 8-foot square barrels. The wait was worth it, the waves delivered, and Jack made history. Padang magic at its finest!
