Garut Winning 2014

An unforgettable moment in Rip Curl Cup history: Kuta Beach cousins Garut Widiarta and Raditya Rondi faced off in a thrilling Final in 2014. Rondi opened strong with 9 and 8-point rides, but Garut clinched victory with an epic 8.3 tube on a near-dry reef in the final minutes.

From growing up surfing together to representing Indonesia on the world stage, this was more than a competition. It was a celebration of family, friendship, and Indonesian surfing.

Bruce Iron 2016

Back at Padang for the first time since his 2008 WCT victory, Bruce Irons proved his magic was far from gone. During his Round 1 heat at the 2016 Rip Curl Cup, Bruce delivered a mind-blowing tube ride that not only stole the show but also set the record for the longest barrel in event history. 🏆

Bol's Hurdless Jetski

Back in 2018, Semifinal 1 delivered the heaviest set of the day. Made Bol Adi Putra went all in, taking off deep, threading through a massive barrel, then stalling perfectly into the inside bowl.⁠

As the wave exploded behind him, a drifting jetski nearly blocked his exit. But Bol, with catlike reflexes, launched over it mid-ride and stuck the landing.⁠

The crowd went wild. Judges dropped a 9.55. And Bol punched his ticket to his record-fourth Rip Curl Cup Final. Iconic.⁠

Erin Brooks 2022  

Fresh off a gold medal at the ISA World Juniors in 2022 and a dream trip to the Mentawais, 15-year-old Erin Brooks of Hawaii just made history. As the only female and the second-youngest surfer ever to compete in the open field, Erin charged through to the final, earning 4th place and cementing her spot among the world’s best tube riders. 

She also took the win in the first-ever women’s Super Heat, a major moment for women’s surfing.

# History

History

## What is Mural Fest?

Internationally renowned as Australia’s Town of Murals, Sheffield’s first mural ‘Stillness and Warmth’ was painted in 1986 by John Lendis. Since then, more than 130 murals have been added to the collection, highlighting the region’s rich history of stories, pioneering families, farmers, community leaders and the beauty of this idyllic part of Tasmania.

Visionary Brian Inder believed the mural theme in Sheffield needed another string to its bow and created Mural Fest which over the years has evolved to provide unique and contemporary public artworks that complement the Town of Mural’s colourful landscape and ensure that visitors have something new to see each year.

Held annually since 2003, Mural Fest is a truly unique, annual event comprising of a mural painting competition and other arts-related activities, attracting mural artists from Australia and around the world.

Conducted in Mural Park, Sheffield’s very own ‘Outdoor Art Gallery’ in the heart of Tasmania’s Cradle Mountain touring region, Mural Fest tests an artist’s skills, endurance, and tenacity while subjecting them to public scrutiny, time constraints and sometimes unpredictable Tasmanian weather!

Historically, nine artists have been selected to compete in full public view over a seven-day period using the same poem or theme as their mural’s central theme and inspiration. The murals are 2100mm x 4800mm in size with the Inder Prize and People’s Choice Prize being awarded.

All murals remain on display in Mural Park until the following Mural Fest, providing visitors to the area the opportunity to delight in viewing the completed murals and learning about this unique competition.

Over the years, interesting mural-based activities have been introduced including street art competitions, painting murals by helicopters and unicycles and painting murals with the public.

With the backdrop of magnificent Mount Roland, and nestled in rich farmlands, Sheffield is centrally located and on the main touring route to Tasmania’s iconic Cradle Mountain, West Coast, Devonport and the North West Coast, Launceston and Northern Tasmania.

# Charity Bib

[](https://www.facebook.com/ultratrailaustralia)[](https://instagram.com/ultratrailaustralia)[](https://www.youtube.com/user/AROCSport)

New for the 2027 HOKA Ultra-Trail Australia by UTMB is the Charity Bib Program; an exclusive opportunity to support one of our official charities and earn an inaugural Charity Bib.

Charity Bib Program

**Charity Bib benefits:**

*   Entry into 2027 HOKA Ultra-Trail Australia by UTMB (UTA100, UTA50, UTA22)
*   Exclusive charity race bib
*   Charity start group
*   Charity medal

**How to gain an exlcusive Charity Bib:**

1.  Apply for a Charity Bib with one of the official UTA charities below
2.  Start fundraising
3.  Be invited to claim a Charity Bib by your chosen charity
4.  Complete your Charity Bib registration for 2027 HOKA Ultra-Trail by UTMB.

Each charity has a limited allocation of entries for the UTA100, UTA50 and UTA22. To be considered, applicants must apply for a Charity Bib and meet the minimum fundraising requirement; however, meeting this requirement does not guarantee a Charity Bib. Successful applicants are selected by the charity and awarded places at their discretion.

Australian Cancer Research Foundation

Our mission is to back brilliant research by giving scientists the technology and equipment they need to find new and improved ways to prevent, detect and treat ALL types of cancer.

See more

Aspect (Autism Spectrum Australia)

Aspect (Autism Spectrum Australia) is one of Australia’s largest autism-specific service providers, with one of the world’s most extensive autism-specific educational programs. A not-for-profit organisation, we work in partnership with people of all ages on the autism spectrum to co-develop, co-produce and co-deliver supports and services that are individualised, goal-driven and grounded in evidence-based practices.

Our services help people on the autism spectrum realise their individual potential and provide much-needed support for their families, carers, friends and colleagues. Aspect’s vision is to provide the best possible opportunities for Autistic people. We believe that people on the autism spectrum are a different brilliant!

See more

Beyond Blue

Our Vision is that all people in Australia achieve their best possible mental health.

Our Role is to work with the community to improve mental health and make it easier for people to feel better earlier, get well and stay well.

See more

Kids with Cancer Foundation

When you fundraise for Kids with Cancer Foundation you will be supporting young families of pre teen children (0-12 years old and under) that are experiencing financial difficulties due to their child being treated for cancer, along with doctors,  nurses, social workers, and cancer research.

See more

PanKind Pancreatic Cancer Australia

Our mission is to triple the pancreatic cancer survival rate by 2030 and dramatically improve the quality of life for those impacted by the disease. We aim to achieve this through a strategic focus and collaborative approach.

See more

## With Thanks To Our Fair Partners

Sydney Contemporary is made possible through the support of an exceptional group of partners who share our commitment to contemporary art, culture and creative excellence.

From our Principal Partner MA Financial Group to our hotel, beverage and presenting partners, these organisations play a vital role in bringing the Fair to life each year.

Partners integrate into the many facets of Sydney Contemporary, including lead-in events, Fair activations, bespoke programming, retail opportunities and artist collaborations. To discuss opportunities please contact Erin Kent, Head of Partnerships, [erin@artfairsaustralia.com.au](mailto:erin@artfairsaustralia.com.au)

## Principal Partner

![](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/2015/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Website-Partner-Hero-Image.png)

### MA Financial Group

MA Financial Group is a global alternative asset manager specialising in private credit, real estate and hospitality. The firm lends to property, corporate and specialty finance sectors and provides corporate advice. MA Financial invests and manages $15 billion on behalf of clients, is responsible for $179 billion in managed loans and has advised on more than $135 billion in advisory and equity capital market transactions. The firm has over 900 professionals across locations in Australia, China, Hong Kong, New Zealand, the Philippines, Singapore and the United States.

[Learn More](https://mafinancial.com/)

## Presenting Partner

![](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/2015/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/12.png)

### Carriageworks

Carriageworks is a prominent multi-arts center located in Sydney, Australia, renowned for its dynamic exhibitions, performances, and cultural events. Housed in a historic railway workshop, it offers a vibrant platform for contemporary art, theater, dance, and music. Carriageworks collaborates with leading local and international artists, fostering innovation and creativity in a distinctive industrial setting.

[Learn More](https://carriageworks.com.au/)

## Major Partner

![](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/2015/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Polestar.png)

### Polestar

Sydney Contemporary’s luxury electric vehicle partner. Based in Gothenburg, Sweden. Born out of the need for sustainable change, we combine performance parts and materials with an obsessive attention to detail, creating cars we believe will make a difference. It’s in our Nordic genes to solve challenges through design. It’s what makes our cars unique, and not just from the outside. No decorations, no distractions. Minimalism is never about giving something up or doing less, it’s about removing anything that’s not necessary to create a pure experience. These are the reasons why Polestar exists. But the best reason to drive one is perhaps the most important reason of all. For the thrill of it.

[Learn More](https://www.polestar.com/au/)

## Strategic Sponsor

![](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/2015/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Website-Partner-Hero-Image-4.png)

### Destination NSW 

Destination NSW is the lead agency, champion and voice for the visitor economy within the NSW Government. Working with various departments and agencies Destination NSW influences and shapes the visitor economy in marketing NSW as a destination, to secure and deliver major events, invest in visitor economy infrastructure and support the diverse ecosystem of visitor economy businesses and experiences that operate throughout the state.​

###### **Image Credit: Destination NSW**

![](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/2015/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/2-2.png)

[Learn More](https://www.destinationnsw.com.au/?utm_source=EO&utm_medium=website&utm_campaign=SydneyContemporary25%E2%80%8B)

## Supporting Partners

![](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/2015/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Website-Partner-Hero-Image.png)

### BresicWhitney

As Sydney’s leading property group, we’re ambitious for our clients, our communities, and our people. For over twenty years, our approach has recalibrated the ways homes are bought and sold, where opportunity is found, and how homes are brought to life. Our commitment to our values and creative ethos amplifies our ambition to lead in all that we do; seen in the diverse communities we’re proud to serve, the results we’re trusted to deliver, and the stories that shape us.

[Learn More](https://bresicwhitney.com.au/)

### Artwork Transport

One of Australia’s leading domestic art transportation providers and trusted partners of leading artists, commercial galleries, collectors and public fine art institutions Australia wide.

[Learn More](https://artworktransport.com.au/)

### Art Galleria

Art Galleria builds the systems that keep collections organised and histories intact, from the artists who make the work, to the galleries who exhibit it, to the collectors who take it home. We’re proud to support Sydney Contemporary and to power ArtPass, the digital discovery companion for visitors, helping the work exhibited here find its way to the collections where it belongs.

[Learn More](https://www.artgalleria.com/)

### AON

Aon Australia specialises in fine arts and antiques insurance, catering to art dealers, private collectors, and major galleries across the country. As the largest insurance broker in Australia and a global industry leader, Aon offers tailored insurance solutions without exclusive ties to single insurers. This flexibility ensures clients access the best options available, whether domestic or international. Endorsed by the Australian Antique and Art Dealers Association (AAADA) and the Australian Commercial Galleries Association (ACGA), Aon stands out for its comprehensive support and expertise in protecting valuable collections.

[Learn More](https://www.aon.com.au/australia/fine-art-insurance.jsp?utm_source=online-publications&utm_medium=paid-banner&utm_campaign=b_0_ri__all_csl_ap-lp_apac_au&utm_content=r__re&utm_term=sydcontemporay_2025_fineart)

### Harry the Hirer

Harry the Hirer is Australia’s leading event and exhibition hire partner, offering a premium range of furniture, exhibition solutions, structures, signage, audiovisual, production and custom-build solutions, all delivered in-house under one roof. For more than 50 years, Harry the Hirer has partnered with businesses, government organisations, event professionals, and private clients to deliver end-to-end solutions for events of every scale. Our experienced in-house teams provide a personalised approach, ensuring seamless coordination, consistency, and exceptional quality at every stage. With operations across, Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane and Adelaide, Harry the Hirer delivers projects nationwide, supporting events, exhibitions, conferences, brand activations, and private celebrations at any scale.  

[Learn More](https://www.harrythehirer.com.au/#)

### Copyright Agency

Copyright Agency collects and distributes copyright fees for writers, artists and publishers under collective licensing arrangements to its 40,000 members. Talk Contemporary and Kid Contemporary is supported by Copyright Agency’s Cultural Fund. The Cultural Fund provides grants for visual artist commissions, including Copyright Agency Partnerships (CAP) – an annual collaboration with Australian art galleries and institutions to commission and present new work. CAP is partnering with UNSW Galleries to present Heather B Swann: The Forests of Symbols, 3 September – 22 November 2026, and with ECU Gallery to present an exhibition by Sarah Contos from 12 February – 7 May 2027. Gertrude Contemporary is partnering with CAP in 2027-28, with applications opening early in 2027.

[Learn More](https://www.copyright.com.au/)

## Beverage Partners

### Yalumba

Established in 1849, in the Barossa, Yalumba has flourished under six generations of family ownership.​ Throughout three centuries, it has been a symbol of ambition, inclusivity, and collaboration.​ Generations of the Hill-Smith family’s values and traditions have nurtured a sense of unity, welcoming wine lovers to a realm of joy and appreciation.

[Learn More](https://www.yalumba.com/)

### Champagne Pommery

The dedication of Pommery Champagne to Contemporary Art is an integral part of the House’s identity, constituting a fundamental element of its essence. Pommery Champagne was the first House to open its doors to the public in 1874. The Domaine has welcomed visitors from all over the world and since 2003, the most iconic curators of their generation have been brought together in the extraordinary cellars carved out of the Gallo-Roman crayères (chalk pits), opening up to the emerging international scene alongside established artists.

[Learn More](https://www.champagnepommery.com/home)

### Four Pillars Gin

  
Established in 2013 in the Yarra Valley near Melbourne, Four Pillars Gin has become a global leader and Australia’s top craft spirit. Recognized as International Gin Producer of the Year in 2019, 2020, and 2023 by the IWSC, it also received the inaugural IWSC Green Spirit Initiative Award in October 2022. Based in Healesville, Four Pillars offers a range of gins including Rare Dry, Olive Leaf, Spiced Negroni, Bloody Shiraz, and Navy Strength, with a second location in Sydney’s Surry Hills. Founded by Cameron Mackenzie, Stuart Gregor, and Matt Jones, the distillery continues to innovate in the spirits industry

[Learn More](https://fourpillarsgin.com/)

### Saison Aperitifs

Saison is a seasonal aperitif company that obsessively crafts non-traditional vermouth and amaro from peak-season Australian ingredients. Brighter, fresher, and more singular than old-world styles, Saison captures seasonal moments and bottles them. Each Australian aperitif begins with a single core ingredient harvested at its peak: layered with hand-picked wild herbs, fruit, and flowers from small-scale growers. No essences, no shortcuts. Shaped by a chef’s palate honed over 25 years in professional kitchens, this precision shapes every bottle.  From Melbourne to Copenhagen to Hong Kong, since 2020, Saison has grown quietly and is now poured in some of the finest bars and restaurants around the world. Drink what a bitter could be.

[Learn More](https://saisonaperitifs.com/)

### ST. ALi

ST. ALi is the exclusive coffee partner of the Fair and will be served in all Fair bars and cafés. ST. ALi is Australia’s largest independent specialty coffee roaster, founded in 2005 in a South Melbourne warehouse. Nearly 20 years on, they continue to lead and push boundaries, shaping how Melbourne drinks coffee through direct farmer relationships, in-house roasting, and food that matters. Now operating across four countries with over 1,000 partners, ST. ALi goes beyond the cup with signature blends, cans, capsules, and innovative cold brew formats. From laneways to global stages, including the Australian Grand Prix, they sit at the intersection of coffee and culture. Melbourne-born, globally minded, and still crew-owned – ST. ALi is defining what comes next.

[Learn More](https://stali.com.au/)

## Hotel Partners

### Ace Hotel Sydney

Ace Hotel Sydney is a sweeping reimagination of a historical building, nestled in the vibrant neighbourhood of Surry Hills, and close to all that Sydney has to offer. 

Ace Sydney’s communal spaces, guest rooms and dining venues are a deep homage to Australia’s boundless creativity, and the hotel experience was awarded a 2025 MICHELIN Key. The hotel is designed with careful consideration by Flack Studio, drawing inspiration from architect Robin Boyd’s paradigm-shifting book, _The Australian Ugliness_, the paintings of Indigenous Australian artist Albert Namatjira and the building site’s legacy of pottery and ceramic creation. Inside the hotel, find an extensive art program that includes original pieces by celebrated Australian artists, including Nadia Hernandez, Nell, Julia Gutman, Jason Phu and more. Rising 18 stories, Ace Hotel Sydney includes a lobby bar, ground-floor restaurant and laneway cafe, as well as award-winning restaurant and bar Kiln, currently helmed by Culinary Director Isobel Whelan-Little, and offering a singular Sydney dining experience.

[Learn More](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/accommodation)

### Capella Sydney

  
Capella Sydney, the first Australian property in the Capella Hotels and Resorts portfolio, redefines luxury in Sydney’s vibrant heart. Originally the Department of Education building, a heritage-listed icon designed by George McRae, it debuted as Capella Sydney in March 2023. Featuring 192 guestrooms and suites, the hotel blends historic charm with contemporary elegance, highlighted by curated artwork and bespoke furnishings. Ground-level amenities include Brasserie 1930, McRae Bar, and versatile event spaces. Exclusive experiences await at The Living Room for cultural immersion, complemented by world-class health and spa facilities on level six, marking a new pinnacle in luxury accommodation and hospitality.

[Learn More](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/accommodation)

[](https://reservations.tfehotels.com/?adult=1&arrive=2026-08-31&chain=14687&child=0&config=CORP_SBE&currency=AUD&depart=2026-09-10&end=2026-09-10&event_name=Sydney%20Contemporary&hotel=44887&level=hotel&locale=en-US&productcurrency=AUD&promo=TH17264505&rooms=1&src=ZDAwNjY4Ym&start=2026-08-31&theme=SBE_NPR&utm_medium=link&utm_source=corporate)

### The EVE Hotel Sydney

  
Winner of a Michelin Key 2025, The EVE Hotel Sydney is a 102-room design-led luxury hotel in Redfern where art, culture and exceptional hospitality converge. Conceived in collaboration with leading Australian architects, designers and makers, the hotel celebrates creativity and craftsmanship through thoughtful interiors, commissioned artworks and immersive guest experiences. Home to acclaimed dining destinations Lottie and Bar Julius, a 20-metre rooftop pool and the seasonal Art House cultural programme, The EVE offers a distinctly contemporary stay within Wunderlich Lane – one of Sydney’s most vibrant neighbourhoods, where guests are moments from some of the city’s most exciting dining, wellness and retail experiences.

[Learn More](https://reservations.tfehotels.com/?adult=1&arrive=2026-08-31&chain=14687&child=0&config=CORP_SBE&currency=AUD&depart=2026-09-10&end=2026-09-10&event_name=Sydney%20Contemporary&hotel=44887&level=hotel&locale=en-US&productcurrency=AUD&promo=TH17264505&rooms=1&src=ZDAwNjY4Ym&start=2026-08-31&theme=SBE_NPR&utm_medium=link&utm_source=corporate)

## Media Partners

### Art Collector

  
Every quarter, Art Collector magazine profiles the region’s leading artists, gallerists and collectors. You’ll also find art news, analysis of important issues affecting collectors and previews of forthcoming exhibitions across Australia and New Zealand. Subscribe to Art Collector and save up to 40% on newsagency prices. Plus, you’ll never miss an issue.

[Learn More](https://artcollector.net.au/)

### Current

_  
Current_ art magazine is an independently published contemporary art magazine covering art and ideas from the Moana-nui-a-Kiwa region — including Aotearoa, Australia, and the Pacific.

[Learn More](https://currentartmagazine.com/)

### VAULT

  
Published for over ten years, VAULT focuses on the most engaging Australian and international visual arts, with a parallel interest in fashion, architecture, design, writing and other outstanding and engaging forms of creative expression. VAULT is invested in placing Australian discourse in an international context. Offering a curated perspective and insight into the world of artists and creative practitioners, VAULT seeks to foster a new sense of appreciation, a desire to learn and explore the industry in the context of a community of readers who are passionate about ideas in the arts and culture.

[Learn More](https://www.vaultmagazine.com/)

### Artist Profile 

Since 2007, Artist Profile has been a leading quarterly journal delving into artists’ studios and critical discussions shaping their reception. By commissioning original work from writers, artists, and scholars, the publication provokes debate on the contemporary visual arts landscape. Focused on Australasia, Artist Profile engages established and emerging artists in conversations about their practices and the personal, social, and cultural influences behind them. The publication features exclusive artist portraits and includes reviews, previews, essays, poetry, and firsthand artist perspectives, offering a profound critique of visual culture past, present, and future.

[Learn More](https://artistprofile.com.au/)

### GalleriesNow

  
The world’s top invitation-only art guide for over a decade. Discover international exhibitions via our Instagram (350K followers), website, city-wide print maps, app and weekly newsletters.

[Learn More](https://www.galleriesnow.net/)

### Art Almanac

  
Established in 1974, Art Almanac is Australia’s longest-running monthly art guide, offering comprehensive exhibition previews, listings, and artist opportunities nationwide. Online, the publication provides real-time coverage of art events. Approaching 50 years, Art Almanac remains shaped by art enthusiasts—from artists and critics to gallery professionals and educators. Dedicated to supporting the arts community’s sustainability, it serves established and emerging artists, commercial and not-for-profit galleries, and a diverse readership of all ages with a commitment to promoting the arts in all its forms.

[Learn More](https://www.art-almanac.com.au/)

### est living 

  
est living is a leading design platform and resource for exceptional architecture, interiors and products. Through its digital magazine, curated Product Library, daily publishing and annual print edition, est living connects and inspires designers, architects and design-discerning consumers worldwide.

[Learn More](https://estliving.com/)

### Art Guide Australia

  
Art Guide Australia is a print and online magazine capturing the best of contemporary Australian art. What started as a guide to exhibitions and galleries across Australia has grown into the destination for discovering the latest in arts features, profiles, interviews, opinions and studio visits, alongside our podcast. Visit our ‘What’s On’ to find the exhibitions near you, grab a copy of the magazine at bookstores, newsagents or by subscribing—and sign up to our much-loved weekly newsletter.

[Learn More](https://artguide.com.au/)

About | Sydney Contemporary

 [![Sydney Contemporary](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/2015/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/untitled-design-1.png) ![Sydney Contemporary](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/2015/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/untitled-design-1.png)](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/)

9 – 12 September 2027

9 – 12 Sept 2027

Carriageworks

![Hero Banner](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/2015/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/website-top-banner-resize-1.png)

## Sydney Contemporary is Australasia's premier art fair - the largest and most diverse gathering of leading contemporary art galleries from Australia, New Zealand, Asia and around the world. 

Sydney Contemporary is Australasia’s premier art fair – the largest and most diverse gathering of contemporary art galleries from Australia, New Zealand, Asia and around the world. The Fair has grown from a bold idea into one of the most significant events on the international art calendar.

Staged at Carriageworks in Sydney, one of Australia’s most extraordinary cultural venues, the Fair brings together over 100 exhibitors and more than 500 artists across four days each September. It is the highest concentration of art sales in Australasia annually, and a vital meeting point for collectors, artists, gallerists, curators, advisors and new art buyers from across the region and beyond.

Sydney Contemporary began in 2013 with a clear conviction: that Australia deserved a world-class contemporary art fair, and that Sydney, a city with a thriving art scene, a sophisticated collector base and an international reputation, was the right place to build it. Over the years, that conviction has proven right. The Fair has welcomed over 250,000 visitors, generated over $154 million in art sales, launched careers, built collections and brought the best of contemporary practice in the region to a genuinely broad audience.

Alongside the gallery presentations, Sydney Contemporary presents an ambitious curated program, large-scale installations, live performances, talks, guided tours, educational workshops, and Art Night, one of the great evenings on Sydney’s cultural calendar. It is, in the words of those who cover it, much more than an art fair.

THE TEAM

## The People Behind the Fair

![](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/2015/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Tim-1024x1024.png)

### Tim Etchells

##### Founder

Tim Etchells has spent the last 30 years creating and managing Events and Fairs all over the world. From The Good Food Shows to London Fashion Week to Art HK, Tim has worked in numerous different industry sectors across different countries. In 2008 Tim developed the idea to stage Art HK which became the largest art fair in Asia, and is now under the ownership of MCH and renamed Art Basel Hong Kong. In 2013 Tim launched Sydney Contemporary initially on a biannual basis. Having established itself as the largest international art fair in Australasia, Sydney Contemporary moved to an annual cycle in 2017. Tim’s art fair portfolio includes ART SG (Singapore), Taipei Dangdai (Taiwan) and Art Central (Hong Kong).  In 2016 Tim received two separate Lifetime Achievement Awards from the UK Exhibition industry.

### Jo Duncan

##### CEO

Jo Duncan brings extensive experience to Sydney Contemporary from launching and working across a range of high-profile consumer events. Jo helped to successfully launch a range of events in new markets globally including the Good Food and Wine shows nationally across Australia and has worked on a range of other events across Australia, the UK and Asia including London Fashion Week, Melbourne Art Fair, Fashion Week Sydney, Taste of Sydney and Melbourne, the Affordable Art Fairs and Better Homes and Gardens Live. Jo oversees all operational, marketing and gallery needs for Sydney Contemporary.

### Zoe Paulsen

##### Fair Director

Zoe Paulsen is an experienced arts professional with a demonstrated history of successfully delivering multiple contemporary art fairs in Australia, including The Other Art Fair (Sydney, Melbourne), Can’t Do Tomorrow (Australia’s largest street art festival – Melbourne), the Affordable Art Fair (Sydney) and the Incognito Art Show (Sydney). Zoe has a Bachelor of Arts, Media and Communications from the UNSW and began her professional career as a TV Producer in the advertising industry. Zoe has been an MCA Next committee member since the group’s inception in 2010. The program advocates for the institution, encouraging philanthropic engagement and support for the contemporary art sector. Zoe believes that a supported cultural sector is key to building a more resilient and well-rounded society. Motivated by the success of past creative endeavours, Zoe is excited to continue with her contribution to this all-important sector.

### Lyn Moran

##### Finance Director

Lyn Moran has more than 20 years’ experience delivering and leading events across international markets, with expertise spanning finance, partnerships, and operations. She began her career in film and television, contributing to the production of multiple series of _The Amazing Race_ and _The Real Housewives_ franchises before moving into large-scale live events. In Australia, Lyn produced major events with Single Market Events and IMG Events, later expanding her portfolio in the United States to include The World MMA Awards and Trail Hero Music Fest. From 2018 to 2022, she served as General Manager of Sydney Contemporary, overseeing the company’s strategic direction, financial performance, and operational delivery. Now based in the United States, Lyn leads business and financial strategy across the company’s Australian and New Zealand portfolio, while also partnering on the financial strategy of fairs in Singapore, Taiwan and Tokyo. She brings a collaborative leadership style and a clear, commercially focused approach to every project.

### Rowena Talacko

##### Head of VIP Relations

With a background in film production, working for the Australian Film Commission and on internationally renowned feature films such as Muriel’s Wedding and Strictly Ballroom. Rowena then went on to establish a career in the visual arts. Alongside her work for Sydney Contemporary, Rowena manages The Laverty Collection, one of Australia’s most significant private art collections; She also runs a consultancy service, The Art Collection Manager. Rowena has also worked as an Art Consultant at Artbank, working with clients to showcase carefully chosen artworks.

### Ali Hillman

##### VIP Relations Manager

Ali has worked extensively across the international contemporary art sector, programming exhibitions and cultural engagement initiatives in the UK, Europe and the United States. For over a decade Ali was responsible for the delivery of Microsoft founder Paul Allen’s art program at locations in London and Los Angeles. During the Pandemic Ali launched a UK nationwide art competition, securing support from Concord Music, the largest independent music publishing organisation globally. Since returning to Australia Ali held development roles at the Museum of Contemporary Art Australia and Artspace. Within those organisations Ali supported initiatives to drive attendance, with a particular focus on revenue generation, strategic partnerships, and audience engagement. An active philanthropist Ali supports the work of living artists, partly through patron programs and projects that create visibility for early career practitioners and amplify their work to new audiences.

### Erin Kent

##### Head of Partnerships

Erin is a business development and partnerships expert with a career launching global collaborations and scaling brands across the luxury fashion, art, interiors, and lifestyle sectors in both the Australian and U.S. markets. As a Director at WME/IMG in New York, she led designer recruitment for eight international fashion properties. Her leadership was demonstrated during her tenure at the Council of Fashion Designers of America (CFDA). Most recently, Erin led her own consultancy for nascent fashion and lifestyle brands while serving as Director of Marketing & Partnerships for von Holzhausen. Today, Erin leads the partnership strategy for Sydney Contemporary, transforming traditional sponsorship into thoughtful creative integration.

### India Ford

##### Fair Manager

India joined Sydney Contemporary as VIP Relations Liaison before transitioning to the role of Fair Manager. She holds an MA in Art History from the University of Edinburgh, complemented by a background in contemporary and Indigenous Australian art, including her previous work with Utopia Art Sydney. India has also held a range of sales and administrative roles across the events, luxury hospitality, not-for-profit and financial services sectors.

### Bonnie Lee

##### Marketing Executive

Bonnie works across the marketing for both Sydney Contemporary and the Aotearoa Art Fair in Auckland. Since completing her Fine Arts degree, she has held curatorial and communications roles within public galleries and arts organisations. Through creative campaigns, Bonnie has helped grow audiences and deepen engagement at art fairs on both sides of the Tasman. Passionate about expanding access to the arts, she is particularly interested in creating meaningful pathways for people to engage with contemporary art.

### Diana Chen

##### Operations Manager

Diana is an event specialist with 18+ years of experience in B2B and public events, exhibitions, and experiences. With tertiary qualifications in design, her career began in the art departments of film & television productions. She then transitioned her skills to events and exhibitions and has been involved in productions across Australia and Asia, in industries including automotive, telecommunications, not-for-profit, and the arts. Diana is a problem solver with a passion for creativity and tackling new challenges.

### Sophia Mavris

##### Fair Coordinator

Sophia first joined Sydney Contemporary as VIP Relations Liaison and later transitioned into the role of Fair Coordinator. A graduate of the Australian National University with a Bachelor of Art History and Curatorship, she has experience in the Indigenous Art Centre sector and has a strong passion for Contemporary Australian art. Sophia has held a range of sales and administrative roles across the commercial gallery sector and the events industry.

# 2026 Advisory Council

The Advisory Council of Sydney Contemporary brings together leading figures from the arts, business, philanthropy and cultural sectors to provide strategic guidance, industry insight and advocacy for Australasia’s premier art fair. Through their expertise and networks, our Council members help strengthen Sydney Contemporary’s role as a vital platform for artists, galleries, collectors and audiences across the region.

### Sue Cato

Principal, Cato & Clive

Sue has been a leader in corporate communications and issues management for over 20 years and is an avid art collector. She is a board member of Carriageworks and is a member of Chief Executive Women. Sue is a regular panelist on ABC TV’s The Drum and on the 2UE Breakfast Show and is a commentator on business issues for the national press.

### Kym Elphinstone

Founder + CEO, Articulate Advisory

Kym is an arts advocate and advisor with more than two decades experience championing the work of contemporary artists. Kym is the founder of Australia’s leading cultural communications agency Articulate Advisory, through which she has advised on and launched hundreds of arts initiatives for public and private museums, galleries, biennales, art fairs and foundations. An avid art collector, Kym was a founding board member of Art Month Sydney, founding member of the MCA Young Ambassadors, sits on the board of Ngununggula and is the Chair of Firstdraft.

### Alexie Glass-Kantor

Executive Director, Art Dubai

Alexie Glass-Kantor is a curator, cultural producer, and advocate for the arts. She is the Executive Director at Artspace, Sydney. As an advocate for the cultural sector she is on several boards, including Contemporary Art Organisations Australia (CAOA); Academic Board, National Art School, and Sydney Culture Network. 

### Mark Hughes

Mark Hughes Art Advisory

Mark Hughes is a leading art advisor with over two decades experience working in commercial galleries in Sydney and New York. Mark has represented artists from all over the globe and collaborated on exhibitions with many of the world’s leading museums including the Museum of Contemporary Art, Sydney, Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, The Whitney Museum of American Art New York, Centre Pompidou Paris, and the Tate Gallery London.

### Nick Tobias

Principal, Tobias Partners

Nick Tobias, a renowned architect and interior designer, boasts over two decades of delivering acclaimed projects globally. He is currently on the Board of Directors of the MCA, Chairman of the MCA Foundation, and has been an Advisory Council member of Sydney Contemporary since its inception. Nick was on the Commissioner’s Council for the 56th Venice Art Biennale.

### Lucy Turnbull AO

Former Lord Mayor of Sydney

Lucy is a businesswoman, philanthropist, and former local government politician. She served on the Sydney City Council from 1999 to 2004, becoming the city’s first female Lord Mayor in 2003. Lucy has also contributed to urban planning bodies, including as chief commissioner of the Greater Sydney Commission from 2015 to 2020. Her husband, Malcolm Turnbull, was Australia’s prime minister from 2015 to 2018.

### Evan Williams

CEO, Williams Land Limited

Evan founded Williams Land Limited after a successful career as a commercial lawyer with one of New Zealand’s preeminent law firms. Williams Land is a land development firm committed to preserving the legacy of the environments it develops. A passionate advocate for arts, culture and heritage, Evan sits as Chair of the Board of the Museum of New Zealand, Te Papa Tongarewa.

# 2026 Ambassadors

The Sydney Contemporary Ambassador Program brings together influential advocates for contemporary art and culture whose deep engagement with the arts, meaningful connections across the contemporary art community, and ongoing support of Australia’s cultural landscape help champion and strengthen the sector.

### Benjamin Chong

Founder, Right Click Capital

Benjamin Chong is a Partner at Right Click Capital, with more than 20 years’ experience investing in and building technology businesses. He is passionate about innovation, entrepreneurship and supporting the next generation of founders.

### Miffy Coady

Managing Director, EST Living

Miffy Coady is Managing Director of est living, a global design platform showcasing architecture, interiors and design. She is passionate about championing both established and emerging creative talent.

### Eva Galambos

Director, Parlour X

Eva Galambos is the Founder and Director of Parlour X. A longstanding supporter of the arts, she has played an active role in Sydney’s cultural landscape through her involvement with leading arts organisations and initiatives.

### Nikita Le Messurier

GTM, OpenAI

Nikita Le Messurier works in GTM at OpenAI, where she advises some of Australia and New Zealand’s most innovative technology companies on generative AI. Alongside her work in technology, Nikita is an active investor and contemporary art collector. She is committed to supporting the next generation of Australian artists and helping broaden engagement with contemporary art.

Nikita is Chair of the Arts Centre Melbourne Contemporary Foundation and an Ambassador for The Australian Ballet. Through her collecting and advocacy, she is committed to supporting the next generation of Australian artists and helping broaden engagement with contemporary art.

### Liana Rossi

Creative Consultant

Liana Rossi is an award-winning advertising creative, keynote speaker, panellist and MC. A panellist on ABC’s Gruen, she is known for her engagement with art, fashion and contemporary culture, and contributes regularly to creative and cultural conversations across Australia.

### Stephen Todd

Design Editor, The Australian Financial Review

Stephen Todd began his writing career in Paris in the early 90s where he was immersed in the worlds of fashion, art, architecture and design. He has contributed to papers such as The New York Times and The Guardian. Today he is the Design Editor of the Australian Financial Review and the Head of Publishing at Powerhouse Museum.

title: Visit | Sydney Contemporary
markdown:
Visit | Sydney Contemporary

[](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/)

9 – 12 September 2027

9 – 12 Sept 2027

Carriageworks

## Plan Your Visit

Sydney Contemporary, Australasia’s premier art fair, returns to Carriageworks from 9–12 September 2027, with a VIP Preview on Wednesday 8 September (by invitation only). Whether it’s your first visit or you’re a returning collector, here’s what you need to plan your trip. Galleries, programme and ticketing details will be announced in 2027.

[Sign Up](http://sydneycontemporary.com.au/sign-up)

OPENING

## Fair Days

**Wednesday 8 September**  
VIP Preview  
_VIP Pass and Premium+ Pass only_

**Thursday 9 September**  
Fair Open and Art Night 

**Friday 10 September**  
Fair Open and Friday Night 

**Saturday 11 September**  
Fair Open

**Sunday 12 September**  
Fair Open

TICKETS

## Tickets and Passes

Tickets for the next edition of  Sydney Contemporary will go on sale in June 2027. Choose from the unlimited-entry Premium+ Pass, Any Day session tickets, or a ticket to Art Night or Friday Night. Concessions are available on day tickets. Sign up to be the first to know and access special offers.

[Sign Up](http://sydneycontemporary.com.au/sign-up)

THE VENUE

## Carriageworks, Sydney

Sydney Contemporary takes place at Carriageworks, one of Australia’s most extraordinary cultural venues. A vast 19th century railway workshop transformed into a world-class contemporary arts institution, the scale and drama of the building is part of the experience. It’s the perfect setting for ambitious art.

Carriageworks  
245 Wilson Street  
Eveleigh, Sydney

GETTING HERE

## Finding Your Way

Sydney Contemporary is a short walk from several train and bus stops, and a 20-minute drive from Sydney Airport. We recommend arriving by public transport.

**Trains**  
Carriageworks is easily accessible by train. Walk eight minutes from Redfern Station, ten minutes from Macdonaldtown Station or 15 minutes from Newtown Station.  
More info [transportnsw.info](https://transportnsw.info/)

**Bike  
**There are bike lanes on nearby streets and bike racks on Wilson Street at the the top of the stairs to Carriageworks, near the main entrance.

**Buses  
**Nearest stop is at Codrington Street at City Road, approximately a 5 minute walk to Carriageworks.  
Buses: 422, 423, 426, 428, 370, 352  
More info [transportnsw.info](https://transportnsw.info/)

**Taxi and Rideshare  
**Taxi and rideshare pick-up address is Carriageworks Way, via 229 Wilson St. 

**Parking  
**Valet parking will be available for visitors, guests and staff and can be booked through Gieves. Flat rate of $48.00 pre-booked (and pre-paid) per space per day or $59.00 pay-on-arrival. All pre-paid bookings are to be finalised by 3pm the day prior to your booking. Call 1300 880 839 or email [\[email protected\]](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#d1b8bfb7be91b6b8b4a7b4a2ffb2bebcffb0a4)

Additional parking may be available at South Eveleigh, 2 Central Avenue, a 15-minute walk to Carriageworks via the Redfern footbridge and Little Eveleigh Street. For more details, visit the **[South Eveleigh website](https://www.southeveleigh.com/getting-here?utm_source=carriageworks&utm_medium=referral)**. We encourage using public transport whenever possible.

EXPLORE THE CITY

## Visiting Sydney

Make the most of your time at Sydney Contemporary with our Sydney City Guide, your insider’s guide to where to eat, stay and explore while you’re in town. From world-class dining and harbour-side hotels to cultural hotspots and hidden gems, discover the best of Sydney beyond the Fair.

Our hotel partners, Ace Hotel Sydney, Capella Sydney, and The EVE Hotel Sydney, will offer exclusive rates for Fair visitors. All are excellent bases for Fair week, whether you’re coming from afar or simply want to make the most of the city.

[Sydney City Guide](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/sydney-city-guide/)

ACCESSIBILITY

## A Welcoming Space for All

Carriageworks is a fully accessible venue. All entrances have wheelchair ramps and level access, and toilets are fully accessible throughout. Complimentary wheelchairs and motorised scooters are available for visitors who need them, please ask at the information desk on arrival.

Please note that dogs are not permitted inside Carriageworks, with the exception of accredited service and assistance animals. Please ensure identification is clearly displayed and animals are kept on a leash or harness at all times.

If you have any specific accessibility requirements or questions ahead of your visit, please [contact us](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/contact) and we’ll do our best to help.

FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

## Good to Know

**Can I bring children?  
**Absolutely. Kid Contemporary offers a dedicated hands-on creative space for young visitors.

**Can I buy art?**  
Yes – every work in the fair is available for sale. Gallery staff are on hand throughout the fair and are always happy to talk you through.

**How long should I allow?**  
Most visitors spend between two and four hours, though many come back for multiple sessions across the four days. The Premium+ Pass gives you the flexibility to come and go as you please. 

**Is there food and drink?**  
Yes, a range of food and drink options are available throughout Carriageworks during the fair.

### In the Beginning  
In March of 1969 two surfing friends Doug "Claw" Warbrick and Brian "Sing Ding" Singer bumped into each other in Gilbert Street, Torquay.

![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0570/6124/5081/t/3/assets/pf-347cce30--InTheBegining01.jpeg?v=1625541650)

![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0570/6124/5081/t/3/assets/pf-7cce30d7--InTheBegining02.jpeg?v=1625541664)

The Beginning

In March of 1969 two surfing friends Doug "Claw" Warbrick and Brian "Sing Ding" Singer bumped into each other in Gilbert Street, Torquay. Claw had just finished a summer shaping stint with Fred Pyke and Brian was a science teacher. As the conversation progressed, and no doubt thinking about how they could stay surfing Bells in the pumping months ahead, Claw posed the question that started something great...

"Do you want to start making surfboards together?" he asked. Brian immediately figured this would mean a lot more time surfing, so on the spot said, “Yes!” and resigned from teaching a couple of days later.  
  
The timing was perfect and just like that... Rip Curl was born...  
  

![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0570/6124/5081/t/3/assets/pf-b2c1abb7--InTheBegining03.jpeg?v=1625541809)

The Garage

While Claw could mow foam, Brian’s main attribute was that he had a tail-planer for shaping and a garage at 35 Great Ocean Road (towards Jan Juc) to work from and soon the sound of cold chisels could be heard hammering into the garage’s concrete floor to build stands as they set up over the next month.  
  
In April 1969 the first boards were made with Claw doing four boards a week for the best surfers in Torquay and Brian doing the “shittiest job in the world” sanding and making fins in the yard.

![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0570/6124/5081/t/3/assets/pf-ac75571c--InTheBegining04.jpeg?v=1625541880)

The Old Bakery. Left to right: Brewster Everett, Claw, Terry Goldsworthy, Chagga the dog, Tony Ellis, Gary Crothall

The Bakery

They had enough work to keep them going through the winter, which was one of the best for surf on the reefs in memory, so product-testing was free-flowing with a lot of time spent in the water at Bells Beach.  
  
In November of that year they realised they needed a better spot than the garage. So they went and found the Old Torquay Bakery at 5 Boston Road and for the princely sum of $10 a week rent they moved on up.  
  
Inside they set up a proper shaping bay, glassing and sanding rooms and lifted production to 12 boards a week.

![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0570/6124/5081/t/3/assets/pf-106a75ed--InTheBegining06.jpeg?v=1625541980)

![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0570/6124/5081/t/3/assets/pf-32106a75--InTheBegining05.jpeg?v=1625541976)

Wetsuits

In December 1969 another local surfer, Alan Green, joined the duo and they started making wetsuits to complement the boards in the basement of a house in Beale Street behind the Torquay Pub.  
  
Greeny had spent some time at a wetsuit dive company "Australian Divers" and they found a sewing machine, a "Pffaf 138 zig zag", which worked on thick rubber sourced in Clayton in the back-blocks of Melbourne.

Outsourcing much of the work at first, they soon realised that to keep up with orders and get the quality they wanted, they needed to do it all themselves so the wetsuit operation moved into Claw's flat at 66 Zeally Bay Road.

![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0570/6124/5081/t/3/assets/pf-272ef24e--InTheBegining07.jpeg?v=1625542063)

Rip Curl Crew: Back row: Lesley, Sparrow, Claw. Front row: Sjarn Garner, Magooer The Gluer, Sue Muller and Nancy Milikan.

Focus

Change was rampant back then, such was the flower power and anti-establishment mood of the time. Business was no different to life in general and Greeny left Rip Curl in April 1970 to do his own thing, forming Quiksilver, with Claw and Brian as equal partners in the new venture.  
  
Eventually it was time for them all to focus on one thing or the other and the partnership dissolved. Brian recalls that he swapped his Quiksilver shares for Greeny’s half of the land at the back of Bells Beach 

where he still lives today. "There was a bit of a difference in opinion over the value of the land, $5000 or so," he recalls "So we tossed a coin for it, I don't remember who won, but the deal was done."  
  
Claw later sold his shares to Greeny so they could be issued to his new partner John Law. When asked now, Claw has no clue how much he got for them!

![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0570/6124/5081/t/3/assets/pf-16f46523--InTheBegining08.jpeg?v=1625542385)

Rip Curl store and HQ, Geelong Road, Torquay 1980

Along the way

Pretty soon Rip Curl was firing and the Old Bakery was a hive of activity. The pair took over the adjoining house and that became the wetsuit factory. A new machine, a "1910 Singer Up The Arm Zig Zag", which had been used to sew flying boots for airmen in World War II, was found. This was used to sew the legs of the new “long John” style the boys were developing using the comfortable Rubatex neoprene from the US.  
  
At the Old Bakery Claw and Brian had created a headquarters of sorts - with surfers naturally gravitating to the scene.  
  
"It was a house for all the drop-outs that came down from Melbourne surfing and they'd degenerate further and move to the Krishnas looking for the next thing," recalls Brian, laughing.

"But when that wore off and their final degeneration happened, they came to work at the Rip Curl wetsuit factory!"  
  
Times were good and with surfing as the catalyst the company progressed and they eventually moved out of the Old Bakery in 1976 into a new facility up the Geelong Road, (which is currently the medical centre), with Quiksilver opening next door soon after.  
  
In 1980 the move was made across the road to the current Rip Curl HQ at 101 Surfcoast Highway, Torquay.

# About

## Celebrating 15 Years of Riding Dapper

**The Distinguished Gentleman’s Ride unites classic and vintage styled motorcycle riders from all over the world to raise funds and awareness for prostate cancer research and men’s mental health.**

The Distinguished Gentleman’s Ride was founded in Sydney, Australia, by Mark Hawwa. It was inspired by a photo of TV Show Mad Men’s Don Draper astride a classic motorcycle and wearing his finest suit. Mark decided a themed ride would be a great way of connecting niche motorcycle enthusiasts and communities while raising funds to support the men in our lives.

### Rip Curl - The Ultimate Surfing Company about in 1967.

### FOUNDED IN 1969 BY BRIAN SINGER AND DOUG “CLAW” WARBRICK, RIP CURL IS ONE OF THE WORLD’S MOST RECOGNIZED AND RESPECTED BRANDS. IT HAS BEEN AT THE FOREFRONT OF THE SURF AND SNOW SCENES SINCE ITS CREATION.  

Rip Curl is a company for, and about, the crew on The Search. The Search is the driving force that led to the creation of Rip Curl, and it lives in the spirit of everything the Rip Curl crew do. It's what makes Rip Curl unique. It defines who we are. The products we make, the events we run, the riders we support and the people we reach globally, are all a part of that Search that Rip Curl is on.  
  
Rip Curl remains a company built by surfers for surfers, and we’ve been market leaders in surfing for over 50 years. We endeavour to make the best products, run the best events, support the best athletes, deliver the best customer service, communicate the best brand message and have the best crew of people. This helps Rip Curl hold a vision of being regarded as The Ultimate Surfing Company.  
  
As a part of that vision, Rip Curl has forever prided itself on having the world’s best surf team. That statement is none truer than today. Rip Curl athletes are World Champions. They are innovators, dreamers, role models and Searchers. 

From global elite athletes to regional rising talents, no matter where you are in the world the best surfers will be riding with a Rip Curl sticker on the nose of their board.  
  
Rip Curl also has an extraordinary events platform, headlined by WSL World Championship Tour surfing contests, the global GromSearch Series and an array of international events across surf and snow. We were the first company to sponsor a professional surfing event, the 1973 Rip Curl Pro at Bells Beach, and we’re committed to continue the tradition of supporting and showcasing the best surfing to fans across the globe.  
  
Rip Curl will continue to stick by the grass roots that helped make us the market leader in surfing, but we'll also charge on into the future and push riding to a new level. We know what we are doing and we will be around for a long time

# FAQ

## General

What is The Distinguished Gentleman’s Ride?

The Distinguished Gentleman’s Ride is an annual motorcycle charity event that fundraises for Movember. Movember is the leading global charity changing the face of men’s health through prostate cancer research and men’s mental health initiatives. The Distinguished Gentleman’s Ride looks to connect all riders around the world who own and ride classic and custom style motorcycles and scooters, to dress dapper and unite in a parade through the heart of their city to raise funds and awareness for men’s health. Each ride is organised by volunteer ride hosts, and each city is limited to one ride. To find out if there’s a ride in your city, or a city near you, visit our rides page. If you don’t have a suitable vehicle but are passionate about our event, you can still sponsor a participant or donate to the event, which will contribute towards our charitable goals and benefit all men around the world.

Is The Distinguished Gentleman’s Ride opened to all genders?

Yes, The Distinguished Gentleman’s Ride is opened to everyone.

Can I still ride if I don't have a classic-inspired motorcycle?

DGR is about the classic styled motorcycling community, consisting of motorcycles that are either classic in age or in style. If you don't have a motorcycle that fits within the DGR Style Guide, you can borrow or rent a suitable motorcycle. If this is not possible and you’d still like to support the event, you can volunteer your time to help your local host, or make a donation.

I understand the ride is for classic-styled motorcycles, but why can’t we open it up to all?

DGR is a classic themed event, so modern-designed motorcycles, sports motorcycles, dirt/adventure motorcycles and cruiser motorcycles that do not fit within the classic style are not eligible to participate with. We aim to keep events manageable for our volunteer ride hosts, and to ensure the safety of all participants that take part in each event. Many of our key events expect over 1,000 participants throughout city centres, and significant growth in numbers will increase the risk of incidents and road closures, which will have a negative effect on the success of The Distinguished Gentleman’s Ride.

I am having technical problems with the website. Help!

Click here to go to the contact us. Send us a message and we will get back to you.

I can’t seem to find a DGR in my area. Who do I contact to start one?

Click here to the ‘Host a Ride’ form to fill in the details and we will aim to have you hosting as soon as possible.

## Registration

How do I sign up?

To sign up, click here to go to the Registration Page. Follow the registration process to select the city you will participate in. Please ensure all details are correct, including your address, as you may find yourself being the lucky winner of one of our many rewards, so we’ll need to know where to reach you!

How do I find my DGR ride city details?

The local details will be made available after you register. These details must be kept private to ensure that only registered participants have access to important event information. If these details are shared publicly, it can put the event at risk of being shut down. All participants must be registered in order to take part. You can check out any updated city details from within your Dashboard.

Do I have to pay to participate?

Some cities may have a required minimum donation amount for participants to take part. This will be highlighted to you during the first step of registration and give you the option to continue if you wish to make a minimum donation. The amount will vary for each city, and will be applied to your profile as a donation.

## Fundraising

Do I have to fundraise to take part?

While The Distinguished Gentleman’s Ride is a charitable event it is not compulsory to fundraise or donate unless you are taking part in a city with a required minimum donation.

Can I donate to another charity?

Movember is the sole beneficiary to DGR, and donating to other charities through DGR is not possible or permitted. We have deliberately partnered with Movember as they are the leading global charity committed to changing the face of men's health and therefore are uniquely positioned to take action and spend the funds strategically. Movember finances a diverse range of global and local initiatives, ensuring that the knowledge gained is shared. They utilise research findings to inform policies, programs and practice, and improve health outcomes for men around the world.

Can I make a cash or cheque donation?

Cash contributions or donations are not accepted on event day unless there are representatives from Movember present. We will alert the participants at the event beforehand if this is taking place. These funds will not count towards your online total, so it is best you donate to yourself online. If you are being asked by anyone who is not from Movember to make a cash donation, please contact us immediately via our contact page. If you wish to make a cheque donation, visit https://gentlemansride.com/donate to download the cheque donation form, fill in the fields, and mail it to the relevant address. Movember will inform DGR once a cheque has cleared and we will update accordingly.

Will I receive a tax-deductible receipt?

Through Movember's charitable status the countries where you can receive a tax-deductible receipt include: USA, Canada, UK, Australia, New Zealand, Germany, Netherlands, Spain and Sweden. For all other enquiries please contact: movember@gentlemansride.com

Where does my fundraising go?

Movember invests funds donated by the participants of The Distinguished Gentleman’s Ride into approved programs in line with the founding principles of both parties. 100% of funds donated go directly to Movember. The Distinguished Gentleman’s Ride is then reimbursed for costs relating to the delivery and running of the actual event. These costs relate to a maximum of 20% of total fundraising. Our priority will always be to run a safe event and ensure its delivery on a global level for all participants involved. Funds donated in 2025 will be invested in prostate cancer clinical research, prostate cancer health services and men’s mental health and suicide prevention projects. Find out more about Movember's investment with The Distinguished Gentleman's Ride on our Programs We Fund page.

Why have you chosen to support Movember?

Movember is the world’s largest men’s health organisation. The Distinguished Gentleman’s Ride strives to select health partners that are focused on universal, game-changing and realistic outcomes, so Movember and their purpose to create positive change so men live healthier & longer lives is a perfect fit for what we are trying to achieve. With an official presence in over 10 countries and a truly global community, Movember has already funded over 1300 men’s health programs with a unique focus on global collaboration, some of which have been supported by The Distinguished Gentlemen’s Ride in the past. More needs to be done to tackle the specific issues that affect men's health. As the leading global organisation committed to changing the face of men's health, Movember is uniquely positioned to take action.

## Safety

What happens if it rains?

Safety is always the priority. If a city is experiencing extreme conditions, we will postpone the event if necessary and as decided by the Ride City Host. The local host of your registered city will send an email alert including an SMS or WhatsApp regarding events that are postponed or cancelled.

Is it unsafe to wear dapper clothing on a motorcycle?

Riding a motorcycle is a risky exercise, regardless of what you are wearing. Our event is always low speed and takes place through the slowest streets of each city. This is a safety feature of our event to minimize the risk to our participants. Any participants concerned about safety are encouraged to wear armor underneath their suits for added protection. Information regarding safety for all events can be viewed through our Safety Information page.

## Prizes

What do I get for participating?

All registered participants that fundraise over $250 USD receive a commemorative patch, exclusive to 2025, which can be only be earned, not purchased. Fundraising over $250 USD also gives you an opportunity to take part in a global competition to win amazing prizes, including a brand new Triumph motorcycle. For those who fundraise over $1000 USD, a limited edition Pin Pack will be sent through. This can only be earned. To view all prizes on offer for DGR 2026, visit our prize page.

Where is my sticker or fundraising reward?

Movember will be managing the distribution of these globally. Stickers - The Movember x DGR Sticker purchased during registration or through your dashboard is sent weekly (Monday - Friday) from set Movember offices and postal services. Please allow up to 4 weeks to receive these, however, we have experienced significant delays in postage so please be patient. Patches - The $250 USD Commemorative patches are sent weekly. Please allow up to 4 weeks for your patch to arrive. Pin Pack - The $1000 USD Pin Packs are sent weekly. Please allow up to 4 weeks for your pin pack to arrive. If you feel the postman may have misplaced your package, please contact us at the below email address: fulfilment@gentlemansride.com Shipping Estimate: All items will begin shipping at the end of March.

title: Installations | Sydney Contemporary
markdown:
Installations | Sydney Contemporary

 [![Sydney Contemporary](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/2015/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/untitled-design-1.png) ![Sydney Contemporary](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/2015/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/untitled-design-1.png)](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/)

9 – 12 September 2027

9 – 12 Sept 2027

Carriageworks

![Hero Banner](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/2015/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/installations.png)

![Ident](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/2015/wp-content/uploads/elementor/thumbs/ident-rqfai409gdfpmfthjmzmn5v0f9oepfc61eytjlp8h4.png "Ident")

At Sydney Contemporary, art doesn’t stop at Carriageworks. Installations extend beyond the Fair, bringing large-scale works into some of Sydney’s most iconic public spaces.

Browse the 2026 Installations program below. Details for 2027 will be announced next year.

THE 2026 PROGRAM

## 14 Ambitious Projects

Curated by José Da Silva, the 2026  Installations program spans sculpture, textiles, painting, photography, kinetic forms and public interventions, with works that are generous and immediate but also ask us to look more closely at the social, ecological and cultural systems shaping our world.

Artists use spectacle, material invention and public address to explore some of the defining questions of contemporary life: how histories inhabit place, how images circulate, how materials carry memory, and how audiences gather, move, participate and reflect.

BEYOND CARRIAGEWORKS

## Installations Extend Across the City

Installations extends beyond Carriageworks to offsite locations across Sydney, creating unexpected encounters with artists who transform public spaces into powerful contemporary experiences. These projects invite audiences to experience contemporary art in public spaces before, during and after their visit to the Fair.

[![8](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/2015/wp-content/uploads/elementor/thumbs/8-1-rsk9y684vmaa9oi3yrayuqan1sawl0iybxqe4ufur4.png "8")](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/installation-rekorennie/)

SYDNEY FISH MARKET

## Reko Rennie

Reko Rennie questions the politics of visibility and brings histories of Aboriginal culture and identity to the iconic Sydney Fish Market. Presented by Ames Yavuz with the support of Destination NSW and Placemaking NSW. 

[Learn More](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/installation-rekorennie/)

[![1](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/2015/wp-content/uploads/elementor/thumbs/1-4-rsk98qpbyzh05hfygrkce5boghnebtke62bgpc5b3k.png "1")](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/installation-joanross/)

PIER PAVILION, BARANGAROO

## Joan Ross

Joan Ross’ video animation transforms Pier Pavilion into an encounter with a critical eye on colonial history. Presented by N.Smith Gallery with the support of Destination NSW and Placemaking NSW. 

[Learn More](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/installation-joanross/)

THROUGHOUT SYDNEY CONTEMPORARY

## Leading Contemporary Artists at Carriageworks

The scale and history of Carriageworks make Installations a compelling experience. Visitors enter a site marked by its industrial past and encounter some of the most current ideas being explored by contemporary artists.

[](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/installation-billy-apple/)

# Billy Apple®

Presented by 1301SW | STARKWHITE with the support of Destination NSW.

Billy Apple® (1935-2021) was a pioneering artist in the pop and conceptual art movements.  His art remains one of the most incisive commentaries on the unspoken economic structures that underpin contemporary art. Sydney Contemporary celebrates his legacy with three related projects. 

[Learn More](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/installation-billy-apple/)

[](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/installation-mikehewson/)

# Mike Hewson

Presented by Roslyn Oxley9 Gallery

Mike Hewson takes over the Sydney Contemporary Café and turns it into a shared sculptural setting, alongside a new fountain assembled from industrial and organic materials.

[Learn More](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/installation-mikehewson/)

[](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/installation-alexseton/)

# Alex Seton

Presented by Sullivan + Strumpf

Alex Seton transforms the everyday puffer jacket item into a vessel for contemporary anxieties around protection and truth. 

[Learn More](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/installation-alexseton/)

[](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/installation-jemimawyman/)

# Jemima Wyman

Presented by Sullivan+Strumpf

Jemima Wyman transforms protest smoke into an immersive textile, considering camouflage, collective action and the political charge of pattern.

[Learn More](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/installation-jemimawyman/)

[](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/installation-gracelillianlee-drkenthaidaysnr-allangeorgelee/)

# Dr Grace Lillian Lee, Dr Ken Thaiday Snr & Allan George Lee

Presented by CASSANDRA BIRD

Dr Ken Thaiday Snr, Dr Grace Lillian Lee, and Allan George Lee bring together Zenadth Kes weaving, ceremony and mentorship through kinetic contemporary form.

[Learn More](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/installation-gracelillianlee-drkenthaidaysnr-allangeorgelee/)

[](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/installation-choiyoungwook/)

# Choi Youngwook

Presented by Gallery LNL 

Choi Youngwook’s pavilion featuring his Moon Jar paintings offers viewers a serene retreat from the bustle of the fair.

[Learn More](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/installation-choiyoungwook/)

[](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/installation-kirtikakain/)

# Kirtika Kain

Presented by Roslyn Oxley9 Gallery

Kirtika Kain brings together material intensity, darkness and luminosity to consider caste, ancestral memory, labour and the charged politics of surface.

[Learn More](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/installation-kirtikakain/)

[](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/installation-remyfaint/)

# Remy Faint

Presented by CASSANDRA BIRD

Remy Faint’s sculptures bring together vessels, limbs and animal forms, creating strange hybrid objects that appear excavated, reassembled and alive.

[Learn More](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/installation-remyfaint/)

[](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/installation-williamkentridge/)

# William Kentridge

Presented by Annandale Galleries

William Kentridge reveals animal and botanical forms through bronzes poised between drawing and theatre.

[Learn More](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/installation-williamkentridge/)

[](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/installation-nabilahnordin/)

# Nabilah Nordin

Presented by Neon Parc

Nabilah Nordin turns steel into gestural, enigmatic forms that bend, lean and hover between drawing, sculpture and movement.

[Learn More](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/installation-nabilahnordin/)

[](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/installation-ingvarkenne/)

# Ingvar Kenne

Presented by day01.

Ingvar Kenne’s photographs slow our perceptions of landscape through scale and spatial rhythm.

[Learn More](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/installation-ingvarkenne/)

[](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/installation-louisgrant/)

# Louis Grant

Presented by SABBIA

Louis Grant’s new sculptures stage glass and found materials in intimate tableaux exploring queer embodiment and relations of support.

[Learn More](https://sydneycontemporary.com.au/installation-louisgrant/)

Sydney Contemporary is proudly supported by the NSW Government through its tourism and events agency, Destination NSW.

## Meet The Curator: José Da Silva

José Da Silva is an Australian curator and the Director of Sydney’s UNSW Galleries, where he has led a dynamic program of contemporary Australian art and design since 2018. In 2024, he curated the 18th Adelaide Biennial of Australian Art and became Chair of University Art Museums Australia.

# Partner With Us

Partner With Us

Each year Kentish Arts Commerce and Tourism seeks sponsorship support from the Kentish Municipality and surrounding areas for Mural Fest. If your business is passionate about local art events and providing emerging and established artists with an opportunity to showcase their talents in a public forum, several sponsorship packages are available.

The generous support received over the years has enabled Mural Fest to grow and develop while promoting mural art as a valued art form. By sponsoring Mural Fest, in addition to assisting artists in their artistic growth and development, you will be contributing to the unique interest of ‘The Town of Murals’.

As we look forward to this year’s event, we can’t help but be excited to welcome back international artists to Sheffield in person or via a digital platform embracing new interactive technology.

For more information on how you can become a sponsor, please phone [**0427 475 113**](tel:0427 475 113) or email [**info@muralfest.com.au.**](mailto:info@muralfest.com.au.)

# Vanlife diaries began with a van ...

## Surprised, eh?

Vanlife Diaries was initially a concept. Jared and Sam were fitting out vans into campers at an affordable price for fellow travelers. Travelers don’t have a lot of money and are usually happy just to blaze their own trail. If this involves hiring a campervan, funds can hemorrhage. Jonny, one of Jared's long-time brothers, came to stay at Jared and Sam's rental property in Collingwood. Like most old friends, the pleasantries dissolve rapidly and questions of direction and struggle bubble to the surface. Jonny had some skills he wanted to bring to the table and over the next four hours, they created a team and project. After six months, Vanlife Diaries Instagram following spiked to 30,000. The friends orchestrated two vanlife gatherings, fitted out several vans and expanded the Vanlife Diaries network of facilitators to five countries and four continents. This included hiring Kathleen to come on board as our American representative and part of our vanlife crew.

## We need your help!

Vanlife Diaries can't happen without you. We'd like to share your story.

Need ideas or help for a new van set up? Want to start a vanlife gathering in your neck of the woods or have some feedback we could use to make your experience more enjoyable? Are you a brand that wants to reach the vanlife community? Reach out to us in your region below.

# AUSTRALIA, CANADA & EUROPE

## **JONNY DUSTOW**

Dusty (Jonny Dustow) is co-founder of Vanlife Diaries. He lives in his van (Mercedes Sprinter) full time on the east coast of Australia sharing music and stories in his home country and the world. He is the lead member of a six-person band called Dusty Boots.

Send in your stories and photos if you are living the vanlife in Australia, Canada or Europe.

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/547a7a53e4b0b93ff702af56/1492170504352-NNATKGWJDWC1QCQS3PN7/image-asset.jpeg)

## **JARED MELROSE**

Jared is co-founder of Vanlife Diaries. He lives with his girlfriend Ashleigh in a van on the East Coast of Australia full time. He is also the singer-lyricist and fronts the band, The Evening Son. He works as a tradesperson and helps produce an array of community projects.

Reach out if you need a friendly professional hand fitting out your van or need ideas.

Contact Me

## **SAM PETERSON**

Sam is co-founder of Vanlife Diaries. When he’s not living on the road he has a base at Bells Beach Victoria Australia. Surfing is integral to his life and his connection to the surf coast community. He plays music, in three acts: The Evening Son with Jared, Boatfriends and Kira Puru. Sam works freelance in events, mostly music festivals, and promotes the community and charity channels though these events.

Converting vans into little homes is a real passion with his background in building it's worthwhile contacting Sam for a camper conversion.

## **KATHLEEN MORTON**

Kathleen is a co-founder for Vanlife Diaries and the creator of [Tiny House, Tiny Footprint](http://www.tinyhousetinyfootprint.com/). Both organizations share stories of people living alternative lifestyle, encourage others to get outdoors, promote environmental initiatives and host gatherings all across the world.

Kathleen started living small in '69 camper trailer (140 sq. ft.). Now, she lives out of a built-out '87 Toyota van with her dog, Peaches, and travels primarily around the west, connecting with fellow travelers and the land. You might often find her backpacking in national forest, working on organic farms or climbing canyon walls in the desert.

Contact Kathleen for all things U.S. Share your tiny living story or help her organize a local vanlife gathering.
