[![](https://theyogabarn.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/BSF-tickets-coming-soon-button-blue.png)](javascript:;) 

### Yoga For Nature

Yoga For Nature(TM) is a registered charity and a community led approach to achieving sustainability and peace.

Whether it’s our wildlife, marine life or human life, founder [Philip Dickenson](https://balispiritfestival.com/programs/presenter/phil-dickenson) believes that an interconnected world calls upon a connected community and Yoga should be helping to transform the world. “Our ultimate goal is to achieve sustainability and peace through effective partnerships and the teaching of yoga.”

![](https://www.balispiritfestival.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/yoga-for-nature-bali-festival.jpg)

![](https://www.balispiritfestival.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/bali-kids-yoga-for-nature.jpg)

With the support of Yoga studios from all over the world, Yoga For NatureTM classes create a growing network of teachers & students, who are aware of specific environmental, humanitarian and animal rights causes. Our monthly memberships and charity classes help educate Yogis from all over the world and empower us to support effective action and advocate for change.

![](https://www.balispiritfestival.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/yoga-save-elephants.jpg)

![](https://www.balispiritfestival.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/bali-water-yoga-for-nature.jpg)

In the spirit of Yoga, our work inspires yogis to co-create peace with people, animals and nature.

Yoga For Nature is a proud partner of the BaliSpirit Festival, for more info visit [www.yogafornature.org](http://www.yogafornature.org/)

# FAQs

### Account Area

* * *

#### What are the benefits of getting an account?

An account is absolutely FREE. With an account you'll be among the first to receive exclusive offers, event promotions / announcements and ticket sales details. You need to have an account to buy tickets, so keep your account details up to date to ensure you don't miss out on any breaking news. [Click here](https://www.greazefest.com/account/new/) to register an account now.

* * *

#### Is the Account Area safe and secure?

Yes, the Account Area is a password protected environment. If you are concerned that you have lost your password, or wish to change your password, you can reset it [here](https://www.greazefest.com/account/forgot_password.aspx) (or navigate to the Account Area login page and click the Forgot Password button).

* * *

#### How do I update my contact details?

Login to the Account Area and click on “My Details” in the Account Area sidebar.

* * *

#### What do I do if I can’t remember what email address I used to register?

Try logging in and see if you can remember what email address you might have used; our system will tell you if the email address you enter does not exist in our system. Otherwise you can [contact us](https://www.greazefest.com/contact/) and we can look up your email address in our system; before doing this we will need to verify your identity.

* * *

#### What do I do if I have forgotten my Password?

Passwords are case sensitive, so check whether you have the Caps-Lock key on and try entering your password again. If this still doesn't work or you think you have forgotten your password, you can reset it [here](https://www.greazefest.com/account/forgot_password.aspx) (or navigate to the Account Area login page and click the Forgot Password button).

* * *

#### Why is an email confirmation required after I have registered an account?

You should receive an email within a few minutes of submitting your online Account registration form. This email includes a link which must be clicked in order to validate your registration. Clicking on this link double-checks that your email address has been correctly recorded and ensures you will receive important news and exclusive offers about the event/s.

When a large number of people are registering at once it may take up to half an hour to receive the confirmation email. If you do not receive a confirmation email, contact us and we'll ensure your registration is completed.

* * *

#### How do I download my E-tickets?

Once e-tickets are available to download from the Account Area the tickets will be stored and remain safe and secure for the life of the ticket, and therefore there is no rush to download. To download these tickets, just login to the Account Area, click on “My Tickets” in the Account Area sidebar. From this page you can choose to Download or Email your E-tickets.

To download your ticket/s you must have Adobe Acrobat Reader installed on your computer. If you do not have it installed, you can download it for free from: [www.adobe.com/products/acrobat/readstep.html](http://www.adobe.com/products/acrobat/readstep.html)

* * *

#### How do I print my E-ticket's in hard copy?

You can print your E-tickets on your home printer in black and white or colour, on standard A4 paper. Please ensure that the barcode has printed correctly, otherwise we might be unable to scan your ticket correctly at the gate. Once printed, please read the terms and conditions.

* * *

#### Why do I need to “name” my E-tickets?

If you have purchased more than one E-ticket, you will need to name the tickets you purchased for the other patrons that will accompany you. This is because in order to gain entry to your event, the name of your ticket must match the name of your ID. To name your tickets, login to the Account Area, click on “My Tickets” in the Account Area sidebar. From this page you can click the “Name” button next to each ticket and enter the name of the person it will belong to. Once you are done you can use the “Download All” to download your individually named tickets as a single PDF ready for printing.

* * *

#### I haven't received my E-Tickets to my email address. What should I do?

If you haven't received your E-Tickets via email within half an hour, please check to see if your mailbox is full or if the email is in your spam folder.

You can also check that your email address is entered correctly in your Account Area, by clicking the My Details button in the Account Area sub-menu. Alternatively, you should [contact us](https://www.greazefest.com/contact/) and we will be able to help you work out why you didn’t receive your tickets and assist in ensuring you receive these as soon as possible.

Note, that you can also download your E-Tickets from your Account Area by going to My Tickets and then click the View Order Details link.

* * *

#### How do I use my E-ticket to gain entry to the event?

On the day of the event simply take your E-ticket/s with you as you would for any event ticket. Please present your E-ticket on arrival at the entry gate. The name on your E-ticket must match the name on your ID.

* * *

#### How do I unsubscribe from the mailing list

Click here to [unsubscribe](https://www.greazefest.com/account/unsubscribe.aspx).

* * *

#### How do I review your Privacy Policy and Terms and Conditions?

Click [here](https://www.greazefest.com/privacy/) to read our Privacy Policy.

Click [here](https://www.greazefest.com/terms/) to read our Terms and Conditions.

* * *

#### Need further help?

If you have been unable to find what you need in the Frequently Asked Questions section, and need further help, please complete an online help request by clicking [here](https://www.greazefest.com/contact/).

### Keep Bali Beautiful

The once idyllic island of Bali, Indonesia is drowning in plastic, and it’s killing our land, water and wildlife. Keep Bali Beautiful is a grassroots recycling program which partners with local schools, churches and villages to build a sustainable recycling network and to change the beliefs and habits that lead to this pollution. # Become a Partner

[](https://www.facebook.com/ultratrailaustralia)[](https://instagram.com/ultratrailaustralia)[](https://www.youtube.com/user/AROCSport)

Become a PartnerPremier PartnersOfficial Suppliers

TITLE PARTNER

OFFICIAL PREMIER FOOTWEAR AND APPAREL PARTNER

HOKA® is one of the fastest-growing performance footwear and apparel brands in history.

Conceived in the mountains, HOKA footwear delivers an unprecedented combination of enhanced cushioning and support for a uniquely smooth ride. Every day, HOKA pushes the innovation and design of its footwear and apparel by teaming up with a deep roster of world champions, taste makers and everyday athletes.

From finish lines to everyday life, HOKA fans love the brand for its bold and unexpected approach, and its belief in the power of humanity to create change for a better world. HOKA empowers a world of athletes to fly over the earth.

[

Discover

](https://www.hoka.com/en/au/)

DESTINATION PARTNER

New South Wales offers adventures around every corner, with diverse terrains, beautiful beaches, famous surf breaks, underwater worlds, and magnificent national parks, including the UNESCO World Heritage-listed Blue Mountains.

An outdoor adventure playground, where you can trek through ancient rainforests, discover stunning waterfalls and gaze at awe-inspiring rock formations like the iconic Three Sisters. The regions offers a world of spectacular experiences, from challenging hikes and thrilling mountain biking trails to exploring hidden caves or simply enjoying a peaceful lookout to take in the breathtaking views and tranquillity.

Come and be entertained at world-class events and leave satisfied after dining at some of the finest restaurants and bars in the region.

[

Visit NSW

](https://www.visitnsw.com/destinations/blue-mountains)

OFFICIAL TECHNICAL SPORTS NUTRITION & HYDRATION PARTNER

As a Technical Partner for sports nutrition and hydration in the trail running events of the UTMB World Series circuit, NÄAK will provide Ultra Energy™ bars, waffles, drink mixes, purees and gels to the aid stations at a large majority of the circuit's events, including during the flagship event of the season, the HOKA UTMB Mont-Blanc, as well as nutrition plans to all runners prior to their races.

Made for trail and ultra-runners, NÄAK Ultra Energy™ products were created with the insights of elite runners like Mathieu Blanchard and Marianne Hogan. NÄAK’s tagline, ‘Fuel your ultra, preserve your playground’ perfectly embodies the brand's approach to nutrition. As Certified B Corp, everything NÄAK does is designed to help trail runners achieve their full potential while preserving their playground.

[

Learn More

](https://www.naak.com/)

OFFICIAL TECHNICAL GPS WATCH PARTNER

Suunto have supported adventurers since 1936 and have been involved in trail running since its inception. Their legacy in the sport is enriched by a strong team of elite runners, including UTMB Mont Blanc winners Courtney Dauwalter, Francois D’Haene and Pau Capell. Suunto watches feature award-winning design, industry-leading battery life, reliability, and purpose-built features for training and racing.

As Official GPS Watch and Technical Partner of the UTMB World Series, Suunto will support runners in navigating the trails and achieving their dreams across the 45 UTMB World Series Events, by bringing its heritage and experience with GPS sports watches. Athletes with a Suunto Vertical or Suunto Race watch will be able to download intuitive GPS maps in three different map styles with important landmarks, contour lines, water, paths and different sorts of terrain highlighted.

[

Discover

](https://www.suunto.com/)

DARING PARTNER

TUDOR is an award-winning Swiss-made watch brand, offering mechanical watches with sophisticated style, proven reliability and unmatched value for money. The origins of TUDOR date back to 1926, when “The Tudor” was first registered as a brand on behalf of the founder of Rolex, Hans Wilsdorf. He officially set up the Montres TUDOR SA company in 1946 to produce watches that respect the traditional Rolex philosophy of quality at a more affordable price point. Throughout their history, thanks to their robustness and affordability, TUDOR watches have been chosen by some of the boldest adventurers, on land, in the air, underwater and on ice. Today, the TUDOR collection includes iconic lines such as Black Bay, Pelagos, 1926 and TUDOR Royal. Since 2015, TUDOR has also offered models with mechanical Manufacture Calibres with multiple functions and superior performance.

A TUDOR is a durable testament to the daring commitment that it takes to tackle something like the UTMB World Series. It’s a totem to the unbreakable spirit that defines every single athlete who has ever stepped foot on the UTMB World Series trail. It’s a watch that’s earned by those who wear it, perpetuating the legend of its owners. Simply competing in the UTMB World Series doesn’t happen by accident. There are no walk-ons. A TUDOR marks every step of the journey there. Every win. Every finish. Every achievement and the hardship that comes with it.

[

DISCOVER

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How do I view my event information?

For all key information, please log into your [participant dashboard](https://in.au.byutmb.world/2026-ultra-trail-australia-by-utmb-14-17-may-1752698256868/my-registration).

### Withdrawal/Cancellation

To view the agreed entries policies please visit our [entry info](https://uta.utmb.world/runners/entry-info) page to view all terms and conditions.

Please note as of 4th April 2027, the only withdrawal option is to complete a transfer to a friend. For more information on how to complete a transfer please **[click here](https://uta.utmb.world/runners/entry-info)**

### Can I change distances?

Athletes can request to transfer their entry to a lesser or greater distance up until such time as that race distance is sold out. For more information on how to complete a transfer please **[click here](https://uta.utmb.world/runners/entry-info)**

### Do I need to get my mandatory gear checked?

All runners in UTA100 and UTAMiler need to have their mandatory gear checked before they can collect their race pack at race check-In.

UTA50/22/11 are not required to get their mandatory gear checked, but must carry all items throughout the race.

Athletes will be advised at the following times if the items marked as "weather dependant" listed above must be carried on the day:

UTA11: 10:00am on Wednesday 12 May UTA22 and UTAMiler: 9:00am on Thursday 13 May UTA100: 10:00am on Friday 14 May

### Where/When do I collect my race bib?

Athlete check-in is located at **KCC Auditorium, Katoomba**

Thursday 13th May 2027 9:00am - 7:30pm Friday 14th May 2027 10:00am - 7:00pm

You will need to provide photo ID (preferably a drivers licence or passport) and your mandatory gear/pre-inspection certificate to be issued with your race pack.

### How do I find more information on shuttles?

For all key parking information please view our [bus guide](https://pdf.utmb.world/image/upload/v1778051433/uta/Runners%20and%20Spectators%20Guide/UTA_26_Bus_Guide_v3_060526_a08b165126.pdf.pdf)

### Which locations have spectator access?

For all key information about spectator movements on race day, please view our [spectator guide.](https://pdf.utmb.world/image/upload/v1778051515/uta/Runners%20and%20Spectators%20Guide/UTA_26_Spectator_Guide_v3_Published_060526_50ec0ab1fd.pdf.pdf)

**The IRONMAN Group Office**

Phone: (+61) 1300 761 384

Please note our office hours are 9:30am AEDT to 4:00pm AEDT Monday to Friday, so there will be a delay in responding to calls or emails received outside of these hours. During event weekend, please visit the Event Information desk for onsite support.

## The Nati Frinj Biennale is a three-day visual art and performance festival in Natimuk, deep in the wheat-belt of Western Victoria.

###### Held in late October to early November Nati Frinj Biennale has forged a reputa-tion for making outstanding, innovative and often audacious art projects.

It is an important platform to showcase local artists, and invite other artists to come and play, to experiment and collaborate. 

From the opening parade to aerial performances, visual art exhibitions to street installations, new theatre works to walking tours, the Nati Frinj is a chance to celebrate and express the creative energy of Natimuk and our invited artists. 

## Since 2002

#### History of Nati Frinj Biennale

With a reputation that dates back to 2002, Nati Frinj is well established in the hearts and minds of our township, the boarder arts community, local and state government stakeholders as well as significant community and arts organisations. 

[view our history](https://natifrinj.com//history/)

## Frinj 2025

#### 2025 Curatorial sub-committee

For Frinj 2025, the festival program will be developed by the festival Director with a small group of volunteers who will act as a sounding board and help formulate ideas for the open and curated program. The Curatori-al Sub-committee makes recommendations and guides the festival footprint. 

## Volunteer

#### Frinj 2025 Volunteer with Frinj

We’re on the lookout for volunteers for the next Nati Frinj Biennale. 

If you have skills you’d like to share or a space to host an artist we’d love to know about it. 

[GET INVOLVED](https://natifrinj.com//get-involved/)

## Some of our objectives

##### Respectfully working with First Nations people of the Wotjobaluk Nation:

ACT Natimuk and Nati Frinj acknowledges and respects the integral knowledge, strength and resili-ence of Australia’s First Peoples – the world’s oldest living and evolving continuous culture. We acknowledge the special relationship that Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people have with their traditional lands and waters, as well as their unique history, diverse culture, customs and circum-stances. When working on Wotjobaluk Country, ACT Natimuk acknowledges that it is vital to be inclu-sive of Indigenous perspectives at the very beginning of a project through to the end. This inclusivity is embedded in all our activities and reflects the organisations understanding of its role in supporting positive actions towards Reconciliation. 

##### And safe for the youngest of us:

ACT Natimuk and the Nati Frinj is committed to promoting and protecting the interests and safety of children in all of our project activities. View our Child Safe Policy HERE 

##### Let’s try and keep things clean:

The Nati Frinj has the stated target of reducing waste produced at the event and becoming a “no single use plastic” event. This includes the following objectives: 

*   No single use plastic bags or plastic packaging to be given out or sold at the event. We encourage eve-ryone to refrain from the distribution of single use plastic bags, cutlery, straws and plastic bottles and avoid all unnecessary plastic packaging. 
*   We seek a commitment from all participants at the festival to reducing waste, recycling and the use of reusable products (e.g. reusable bags/cups/cutlery/etc) 
*   The Frinj commits to celebrate and promote the reduction of waste and recycling. 

![](https://i0.wp.com/natifrinj.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Tower_Moment_MMP-0008-Pano-cropped-1024x989-1.jpg?fit=1024%2C989&ssl=1)

## Who are we

The Nati Frinj is developed by the Festival Director who is governed by a committed group of volunteers on the ACT Natimuk Executive Committee. Nati Frinj is a major program for ACT Natimuk who’s vision is to support arts over a broader range of disciplines, including dance, visual arts and film. 

The Nati Frinj Biennale takes many creative minds and lots of hands, so in the lead up to the Frinj, other roles join the small dedicated Frinj team including a Production Officer and Community Engagement Officer. Our festival relies on a dedicated and passionate volunteer base who bring essential skills and surprising talents while making a vital contribution to the Festival team. The festival could not happen without them.

# 富士グラベルエクストラ2026 ー 出店・ブランドライドのご案内

富士グラベルエクストラは、富士山がもっともくっきり見える12月に開催する、上級者向けのグラベルイベントです。約68km・獲得標高1,800mのロングコースに、グラベルに本気で向き合うライダーが集まります。

2026年は、メイン会場（富士山こどもの国）での出店に加え、コース上のエイドでの出店や、ブランドが参加者を率いて走る「ブランドライド」をご用意しました。熱量の高いライダーと、走りながら・話しながら、ブランドを体験してもらえる場です。

各種お申し込みは、下記のプランをご購入のうえ、フォームに情報をご入力ください。内容の確認が必要な場合のみ、事務局よりご連絡いたします。

出展の詳細（スケジュール・会場図・エイド通過時刻など）は、[出展マニュアル（PDF）](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1nBuLmTYbMA-GNtvt5zPXjLRDBdxAMd2w/view)をご覧ください。

※出店日時：12月5日（土）午後〜12月6日（日）（両日込み）  
※お問い合わせ：contact@fujigravel.com

# Who is Deus Ex Machina?

![](//deuscustoms.co.id/cdn/shop/files/nicklapaglia-_diditprasetyoadiwibowo-_U7U3884_LOWRES_39ca0ace-2c8a-4136-9ade-caf2abc78b2f.jpg?v=1707201430&width=640)

![](//deuscustoms.co.id/cdn/shop/files/AR1I3715_a32fa09d-c88b-47f3-b05d-c32baaaccbbb.jpg?v=1707201433&width=640)

##### 1

Deus ex Machina (god from the machine) roared into Australia’s cultural consciousness in 2006, with some neatly customised motorcycles and a quaint notion that doing something is more fun than just owning something.

Deus ex Machina is a step bigger than a brand: it’s a culture. Our openness and enthusiasm strike a chord with people, wherever they are…

Deus (“day-us”) didn’t set out only to sell custom parts and hand-built motorcycles, but to celebrate a culture of creativity.

The Deus ex Machina Temple of Enthusiasm followed in 2010, the showroom/cafe/workshop/surfboard bay/art gallery in Canggu immediately became a shrine to ‘run-what-you-brung’ resourcefulness and street-honest industrial art.

![](//deuscustoms.co.id/cdn/shop/files/B46T8037_64d88836-bcbd-432a-bf7e-2a10efef1121.jpg?v=1707201433&width=640)

##### 2

The Deus philosophy recalls an era before the various pursuits of fun – motorcycling, surfing, skateboarding, whatever – were marketed into fundamentalist factions.

All are welcomed under the Deus roof, where there’s simply respect for the honesty and enjoyment of the machine. Inclusiveness, authenticity, enthusiasm. It’s a simple and sincere pitch that has winged Deus ex Machina across the world. Deus ex Machina says simply there’s no ‘right way’ to do individualism, its all the same juice.

![](//deuscustoms.co.id/cdn/shop/files/L1008341_0d92239e-9dbe-4c84-a089-4ebc8bff468a.jpg?v=1707201433&width=640)

![](//deuscustoms.co.id/cdn/shop/files/salt_flats.jpg?v=1705901573&width=640)

##### 3

Since opening the doors of the Camperdown Deus House of Simple Pleasure and then the Deus Temple of Enthusiasm in Bali, Deus has spread its own flavour of internally combustible postmodernism around the globe. The way forward is one down, four up.

![](//deuscustoms.co.id/cdn/shop/files/ORN9851_64d06070-b3cb-4518-9c01-a1b6ef77a00b.jpg?v=1707201432&width=640)

##### 4

Deus Ex Machina is a sum of parts, it’s not just one idea, it’s more of a philosophy than a brand. Like a big ole cornucopia of fun embracing every flavor of enthusiasm.

# 富士グラベルやまなし2026 ー 出店のご案内

## ■ 開催概要

名称　　：富士グラベルやまなし（初開催）  
日程　　：2026年10月11日（日）  
　　　　　※10月10日（土）に前日受付・ウェルカムライド・前夜祭を予定  
会場　　：アルカディア南部総合公園（山梨県南部町）  
主催　　：株式会社テラインコグニタ  
後援　　：南部町／山梨県／やまなしスポーツエンジン  
併催　　：アルカディアスポーツフェスタ（南部町のスポーツ＆文化の例祭・11日のみ）

###   

### ■ 本大会の特徴 ― 2つの来場層に同時にリーチできます

富士グラベルやまなしは、南部町で長年開催されてきた地元の例祭  
「アルカディアスポーツフェスタ」との併催です。そのため会場には、

（1）全国から集まるコアなグラベルライダー（ライド定員 150名）  
（2）スポーツに関心の高い地元のファミリー・ライト層（フェスタ来場者 〜500名）

という性質の異なる2つの層が同時に滞在します。  
既存顧客への訴求と新規タッチポイントの創出を、一度の出展で両立できる構成です。

## ■ 出店プラン

**ゴールドプラン**　30,000円（税込）  
・テントスペース 6m × 3m  
・会場内でも特に視認性と導線の良いエリアをご用意  
・試乗車の展開が可能（メイン会場内に常設予定の試乗コースを使用）  
・物販、製品展示、ブランド訴求を余裕をもって展開いただけます

**シルバープラン**　15,000円（税込）  
・テントスペース 3m × 3m  
・製品展示・ブランド紹介・コミュニケーションを中心とした出展に  
・試乗車の展開はご利用いただけません

※初開催のため、今年は試験的な位置づけとして通常より抑えた（参加者数の定員と）価格設定としております

## ■ 出店可能日時

10月10日（土）12:00 〜 任意  
10月11日（日）任意 〜 16:00

両日出展・単日出展のいずれもお選びいただけます（11日のみの出展も可能です）。  
なお併催の「アルカディアスポーツフェスタ」は11日のみの開催です。

### ■ 搬入・搬出

10月10日（土）　搬入：12:00まで（12:00までに搬入を完了してください）  
10月11日（日）　搬入：6:30まで、または 8:00〜9:00  
　　　　　　　　搬出：16:00以降

11日は 6:30〜8:00 の時間帯、および 9:00 以降は搬入車両の乗り入れができません。

### ■ 主催者側でご用意するもの

・区画（ゴールド 6m×3m／シルバー 3m×3m）  
・メイン会場内の試乗コース（常設予定・ゴールドプランのみ利用可）  
・公式サイト出店者一覧ページへの掲載（ロゴ／企業紹介文／HP／SNSリンク）  
・会場マップ上へのブース掲載  
・イベント公式SNS・写真・動画での露出  
・雨天決行（大雨や台風等の場合は中止）  
・会場内宿泊プラン（車中泊 4,000円／テント泊 5,000円）もご用意しています

2025年富士グラベルエクストラ・協賛・出店

2025年12月7日（日）、富士山の麓を舞台に開催される「富士グラベルエクストラ」。未舗装率60%、獲得標高1,870m。そして、五感で感じる“富士の冒険”。ただ走るだけではなく、「人とブランド、自然が交わる場所」として、全国のグラベルライダーが集う特別な一日です。

### スポンサー募集について

今回の富士グラベルでは、イベントを共につくり上げてくださるスポンサー様・ブランドパートナー様を募集いたします。各ブランドの世界観を、走るライダーの体験と結びつける──それが、富士グラベルのスポンサーシップの特徴です。

企業様・個人様問わずご参加いただけます。

### 協賛メニュー

プラン名

内容

価格（税込）

① コースネーミングライツプラン

コース上の印象的な区間に「presented by 貴社名」を掲出。パネル・フラッグ設置、撤収費込み。

33,000〜44,000円

② エイドステーションプラン

各エイドにて食材やドリンク提供、販促物設置が可能。参加者との直接接点を持てる人気プラン。

22,000円  
または補給食等のご提供にて充当可能

③ 会場出展プラン

16,500〜22,000円

④ ソファ＋フォトブース区間

全参加者が立ち寄る撮影スポットにロゴ掲出・展示可。SNS拡散効果が高いフォトゾーン。

33,000円

⑤ ブランドライドプラン

試乗車やオーナーライダーによる20kmショートコース体験ライド。ガイド帯同・募集ページ作成含む。

55,000円

※パネル製作費は別途（22,000円）で対応可能です。

### 開催概要

**開催日：**2025年12月7日（日）  
**会場：**富士山こどもの国（静岡県富士市桑崎1015）  
**参加人数：**150名（※エントリー開始から1日で満員御礼）  
**走行形式：**ガイド付きグループライド（ロングコース68km）

### スポンサー特典

・富士グラベル公式サイト・SNS・リーフレットでのロゴ掲載  
・公式フォト素材の二次利用可（SNS発信・広告利用など）  
・当日運営チームによる設営・撮影サポート

### メッセージ

富士グラベルが目指すのは、単なるグラベルイベントではなく、“走ることでブランドが記憶に残る”体験型イベントです。富士の大地を舞台に、ブランドの想いとライダーの冒険をつなぐ。そのパートナーとして、ぜひご参画ください。

# 富士サイクルフェスティバル2026・出店／協賛プラン

富士サイクルフェスティバルには、2日間にわたって延べ2000名のお客様の来場が見込まれています。  
自転車はもちろん、アウトドア、キャンプ、食、子供向けや体験コンテンツを横断する複合型イベントとして、出店者様を募集いたします。

各種お申し込みについては、下記にてチケットをご購入頂き、情報をご入力ください。  
ご購入後はスタッフがお持ち込みイベントのご希望や出店計画などヒアリングを行い、最適な形でご出展頂けるように尽力いたします。　

※チケットは、5月16日（土）＆17日（日）の二日間有効です。単日のご出店も可能です。  
※申し込み期限：**4月26日（日）まで**

# CubaDupa 2027 Vendor Applications Now Open!

By [cubadupa](https://www.cubadupa.co.nz/author/cubadupa/ "Posts by cubadupa") October 6, 2026 October 8th, 2026 [No Comments](https://www.cubadupa.co.nz/vendor-applications-open-for-cubadupa-2027/#respond)

### **Vendor Expressions of Interest for CubaDupa 2027!**

The businesses who participate in CubaDupa play a huge role in our festival. _\*Please note: If you are interested in a stall but do not sell food or do not already have a business on Cuba Street, please reach out to Foxtail Events regarding the Craft Market next year._

CubaDupa 2027 is taking place on Saturday 20th & Sunday 21st of March. Please read the information below and click the relevant form for your business. Each expression of interest form also has an information sheet with details, timelines and frequently asked questions. It is important you read this information sheet **_before submitting an application._**

**All applications except food trucks are still open. Food truck applications close 20 Nov. All other applications are due 1 December 2026.**

*   [**CubaFoods EOI Form**](https://airtable.com/appS263MXcm8rRWDC/pagDBfCGEPYF8aET1/form) **–** This form is for **_existing food businesses within the CubaDupa event footprint_** that would like extend their operating area onto the footpath outside their premises. Please read the [CubaFoods Information Sheet](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1R9rngqOiTrVLa3tbsWEcIV_7_RUBU4D2/view) before completing this form.
*   [**CubaMarkets EOI Form**](https://airtable.com/appS263MXcm8rRWDC/pagjgFETY3KzAExjR/form) **–** This form is for **_existing retail (non-food) businesses in within the CubaDupa event footprint_** that would like extend their operating area onto the footpath outside their premises. Please read the [CubaMarkets Information Sheet](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1WPdCH82WcAPKvLgz4WsmIuIec9kuctDE/view) before completing this form.
*   [**Special License Area EOI Form**](https://airtable.com/appS263MXcm8rRWDC/pagNJ82ODR1Pqmcuv/form) **–** This form is for **_existing businesses within the CubaDupa event footprint that would like to apply for an outdoor liquor license area for the event._** Please read the [Special License Area Information Sheet](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1lTy5OCQAO7ISKSol3roHeCAfqbeCU17u/view) before completing this form.
*   [**Food Trucks EOI Form**](https://airtable.com/appS263MXcm8rRWDC/pagxi9nGx5BwJ9fWa/form) **–** This form is for **_any mobile food vendors_** who would like to apply for a place in the Food Truck area for CubaDupa 2027. Please read the [Food Truck Information Sheet](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1qjul1MWGdngcBqTTvnCyqBFn_hcRPI4f/view) before completing this form.

We are excited to see all the businesses buzzing in the Cuba Quarter next year and thank you again for playing such an important role in the festival. If you have questions, flick us a message at vendors@cubadupa.co.nz.

#### 03-4550-1191

**Business Office**  
(Non-Counseling inquiries only)

Since its establishment in Japan in 1973, TELL has been dedicated to providing world-class, effective support and counseling services to Japan’s international community and helping to address the country’s growing mental health care needs.

An accredited and certified non-profit organization, TELL’s vision is to be a leader in services and education by practicing state-of-the-art standards of care in the mental health field. Services include free phone counseling, professional face-to-face evaluations and therapy, and community-wide programs.

東京英語いのちの電話は、主な三つの活動をとおし、地域社会のメンタルヘルスケアのニーズに応えます

1973年の設立以来、在日外国人コミュニティにおいて必要とされる国際レベルのサポートやカウンセリングサービスを提供し、国内で高まるメンタルヘルスケアの需要への対応に努めています。東京都より認定を受けた特定非営利活動法人として、メンタルヘルスの領域において最高水準のサービスと教育の両面でリーダーになることを目標に、無料電話相談や専門家による面談カウンセリングを提供するとともに、メンタルヘルスに関する様々なワークショップも開催しています。

東京英語いのちの電話は、1977年に日本いのちの電話連盟に加盟しました。

## Reach Out to TELL

The Lifeline

Have comments about the TELL Lifeline? Contact [lifeline.assist@telljp.com](mailto:lifeline.assist@telljp.com).

Learn more about joining TELL’s Lifeline training program at **[supportworkerapp@telljp.com](mailto:supportworkerapp@telljp.com)**.

Outreach

Ask about our various internship opportunities  – [outreach@telljp.com.](mailto:outreach@telljp.com)

Volunteer in a non-Lifeline role

Join TELL as a non-Lifeline based or short term volunteer – [volunteer@telljp.com.](mailto:volunteer@telljp.com)

TELL @ Work

Reach out to TELL @ Work at [development@telljp.com](mailto:development@telljp.com).

Clinical Placements and Training

\*Please note TELL Clinic is currently not accepting applications for our practicum program.

Reach out about clinical placements and training – [clinical.assist@telljp.com.](mailto:clinical.assist@telljp.com)

Please know the TELL Counseling line is not live which means you will most likely need to leave a message.

We will try to return your call in a timely manner, however, please note that the best way to reach us will be through email.

Clinic - Okinawa

For Okinawa, please contact [okinawa.intake@telljp.com](mailto:okinawa.intake@telljp.com).

For Tokyo and all other locations please email,  [clinical.assist@telljp.com.](mailto:clinical.assist@telljp.com)

グラベルとは

近年、自転車の新しいキーワードとして注目を浴びている「グラベル」。

「グラベル」とは「砂利道」のことで、自転車文化の原点を思い起こす自転車の新しい遊び方を指しています。その中心にあるのは「グラベルバイク」という、長距離を走れるロードバイクと自由度の高いマウンテンバイクの強みを組み合わせた自転車で、旅行、キャンプやその他アウトドア活動との相性が良いことから、ここ数年で大きな広がりを見せています。

![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0737/8672/0476/files/NBX02644.jpg?v=1738223242)

国内最大のグラベルイベント、「ニセコグラベル」の様子

## 日本における「グラベル」の現状

発祥の地である米国に続いて、日本にも定着しつつあります。国内でもっとも大きなグラベルイベントは、2020年から北海道ニセコ町で行われている「ニセコグラベル」です。毎年2回ほど、500名前後のサイクリストが北の大地に集まり、北海道ニセコ町周辺の未舗装路を繋げる60kmから125kmのいくつかの特設コースを駆け抜けます。他にも、宮城県で2023年に発足した「グラベルクラシックやくらい」や、昨年から長野県で行われる「白馬グラベルミーティング」など、100名規模を超えるイベントは近年、全国各地で立ち上がっています。

一方で、広大な土地が広がるアメリカやヨーロッパとは異なり、日本のサイクリストにとっては、活動の場をどう確保するかが大きな課題となっています。日本の場合、未舗装路といえば、農道や林道がほとんどですが、多くの場合地域との調整が必要で、気軽に楽しめる環境が整っていないことも現状です。

![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0737/8672/0476/files/24901.jpg?v=1738223449)

## 「富士グラベル supported by Panaracer」立ち上げの背景

日本のシンボルである富士山の南麓では林業が盛んで、多くの林道が存在しています。中には、自由に走行できる路線や、許可申請手続きが必要な路線、ゲートが閉まっている路線など、扱いは様々ですが、関東圏からも関西圏からも日帰りでアクセスでき、グラベル走行に最適なフィールドが整っています。

林道の管理者である富士市の後援のもと、この富士山南麓で26kmのショートコースと66kmのロングコースを構成し、2025年5月18日（日）に「富士グラベル supported by Panaracer」を開催します。会場は家族連れに大人気な「富士山こどもの国」で、本イベントの他にも、出店イベントや地域団体、事業者との連携を図り、家族で楽しめるコンテンツを組み合わせる予定です。また、5月といえば新茶の季節で、コース上のエイドステーションで地域の美味しいお茶や食材を参加者に振舞います。「グラベル」の楽しさに触れる本格的なイベントでありつつ、初心者でも参加しやすいイベントとして間口を広げることが「富士グラベル」の趣旨のひとつです。

# General Collective Lifestyle & Design Market

Get ready to immerse yourself in a winter market experience ✨

General Collective’s flagship event returns this Christmas — the [**General Collective Lifestyle & Design Market - Christmas Edition**](https://www.facebook.com/events/1038708002103365/ "General Collective Lifestyle & Design Market - Christmas Edition | Sunday 29 November 2026"), taking place on **Sunday 9 August 2026** at **Auckland Showgrounds**.

![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0284/8545/1850/files/GCLD_Nov_2025_a_012.jpg?v=1786455302)

This much-loved market is the ultimate destination for discovering thoughtful pieces and locally made treasures. From ethical New Zealand fashion and design-led homewares to unique jewellery, children’s products, art, and gourmet treats — there’s something special for everyone.

Whether you’re refreshing your space for the season, sourcing meaningful gifts, or simply love beautifully crafted New Zealand-made goods, this market is one not to miss.

![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0284/8545/1850/files/GCLD_Customers_2.png?v=1784679989)

###### [**General Collective Lifestyle & Design Market — Christmas Edition**](https://www.facebook.com/events/1038708002103365/ "General Collective Lifestyle & Design Market - Christmas Edition | Sunday 29 November 2026")

###### **Sunday 29 November 2026, 9am – 3pm**

###### Auckland Showgrounds, 217 Green Lane West, Greenlane, Auckland

•••

Entry: $5 per person | Kids under 12 FREE

Online tickets at [iTICKET.co.nz](https://www.iticket.co.nz/events/2026/nov/general-collective "Get Tickets | General Collective Lifestyle & Design Market | Sunday 29 November 2026")

Door sales available — Cash & Eftpos. Credit cards & Paywave incur a surcharge

**Visit our [blog](https://generalcollective.co.nz/blogs/news "Blog | General Collective")** for the latest market updates, featured vendors and visitor information ahead of the event.

**Planning to visit?** Click "Going" on our [Facebook event](https://www.facebook.com/events/1038708002103365/), then add it to your calendar so you don't miss out.

### **![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0284/8545/1850/files/GCLD_May_2025_GCLD_May_2025_a_018_2048x2048.jpg?v=1779409467)****Discover something truly special**

With over a hundred incredible vendors, this curated showcase brings together the very best of New Zealand’s small and emerging brands. Explore a considered mix of homewares, jewellery, skincare, fashion, art, and children’s products — all thoughtfully designed and made.

It’s a chance to shop with intention, support local, and discover pieces that will be loved well beyond the season.

More than just a market, the Christmas Edition offers a relaxed day out — with a welcoming atmosphere, great food and drink, and the opportunity to connect directly with the makers behind the brands.

### ![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0284/8545/1850/files/GCLD_Nov_2024_a_066_2048x2048.jpg?v=1747111005)**Meet the makers**

Connect with talented New Zealand creatives and hear the stories behind their work. Many will be joining General Collective for the first time — offering something fresh to discover with each visit. ![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0284/8545/1850/files/GCLD_Nov_2024_a_131.jpg?v=1746622496)**Street food & festive flavours**

A winter market calls for something warm and delicious.

Enjoy a selection of Auckland’s favourite food vendors — perfect for a mid-shop break, a warm drink in hand, and a moment to soak in the atmosphere.

![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0284/8545/1850/files/GCLD_Nov_2024_a_163_1024x1024.jpg?v=1757782501)

###  **Join Us**

This winter edition brings together creativity, community, and design in a one-day experience filled with inspiration and connection.

✨ Mark your calendar for [**Sunday 29 November 2026**](https://www.facebook.com/events/1038708002103365/ "General Collective Lifestyle & Design Market — Christmas Edition | Sunday 29 November 2026, 9am – 3pm") — and experience the best of New Zealand creativity, all under one roof.

## The TELL Board

_The demand for compassionate mental health support is more pressing than ever._ _Japan is navigating a complex landscape of mental health issues, from rising isolation to the multifaceted pressures faced by our youth in a hyper-connected world. We aim to welcome and serve the global English-speaking community in Japan. Our commitment extends to supporting people from all backgrounds, including those relocating for work or family, individuals seeking refuge from conflict, women on their paths towards equality, and LGBTQ+ individuals pursuing acceptance and fulfilment._

_We recognise our responsibility to set and uphold exemplary standards in mental health services in Japan. Through our LifeLine, public awareness initiatives, and clinic offerings, we aim to encourage open conversations about mental health. By fostering understanding and providing essential support, we believe we can cultivate a stronger, more resilient community._

_For over 51 years, TELL has been a beacon of hope and a source of practical assistance. Together, we can confront life’s challenges, dismantle barriers, and build a society where quality mental health care is accessible to everyone in need. Remember, you are not alone. We are here, and together, we are stronger._                                                                   

_– Joshua Bryan, TELL Chair_

## Joshua Bryan

#### Chair

Joshua Bryan, Senior Director at Robert Walters Japan, leads the Financial Services, Legal, HR, and Support division in Tokyo. With over two decades of experience in Japan, he has become a leading figure in search and talent acquisition across various sectors within Tokyo’s global business community.

He is passionate about equality, human rights, and mental health. He was a founding member of the Robert Walters Group Global Diversity & Inclusion Council, and remains an active contributor to the work of Lawyers for LGBT & Allies Network (LLAN), a Japanese NPO promoting LGBT rights and marriage equality.

Joshua has a Postgraduate Diploma from Centro de Arte & Comunicaçao Visual in Lisbon and a BA in Painting from Edinburgh College of Art.

## Tsuyoshi Akiyama, (M.D., PhD)

#### Chair Emeritus

Tsuyoshi Akiyama graduated from Tokyo University in 1979 and has been practicing psychiatry in Japan ever since. In addition to his service for TELL, he currently serves as Secretary of Finances for the World Psychiatric Association, and as a board member for the World Federation of Mental Health, the Japanese Society of Psychiatry and Neurology and the Japanese Society of Transcultural Psychiatry.

In 2008, Tsuyoshi Akiyama received the Tokyo American Club Distinguished Achievement Award and in 2010 the Certificate of Honor from the Samaritan Institute. He received these awards on behalf of everyone who has been at TELL.

## Philip Turner

#### Secretary

 Philip Turner is a former New Zealand diplomat (Ambassador to South and North Korea 2018-2023) and business executive (with Fonterra), with more than twenty years’ experience living and working in Japan, South Korea, and China. He now lives in Tokyo, where he balances business consulting, media writing, university teaching, and undertaking a PhD at Waseda University.  He is an official Beachheads Advisor to the New Zealand Embassy in Tokyo, a Senior Fellow of the Centre for Strategic Studies at Victoria University, Wellington, and a member of the Executive Board of the Australia New Zealand Chamber of Commerce in Japan. 

## Mika Matsuo

#### Vice-Chair

Mika Matsuo, the former CHRO of AIG Japan, is a transformational HR Professional with vast experience in culture transformation, business restructuring, and post-merger integration. Mika was born and raised in Japan but was educated in an International School. Her multicultural background as well as her experience as a successful female executive in Japan, provides her with the unique skillset in supporting Japanese leaders to excel in the global context; and in supporting global leaders to quickly assimilate into the Japanese business environment. Mika is well-known for her empathic leadership style and has coached many Japanese businesspeople to become globally-minded, successful leaders. Mika is a graduate of Tufts University and earned her MBA from the University of San Francisco. Currently, Mika is Executive Advisor at Asahi Group Holdings. She also sits on the board of Manulife Insurance Company and two other listed companies.

## Simon Mather

#### Treasurer

Simon is a Partner in Deloitte in their Tokyo office, focused on financial advisory services for Japanese and global clients.  He has around 15 years of experience living and working in Japan, working in both English and Japanese languages.  In addition to his work, Simon is passionate about education, diversity, equity and inclusion, and mental health matters.

Simon holds a Masters’ degree in Philosophy Politics & Economics from the University of Oxford and is a Chartered Accountant with the Institute of Chartered Accountants in England & Wales.

## Colette Rogers

Hailing from Ireland and traveling for the past 30 years, Colette finds herself back in Tokyo for the second time and assuming the role of Head of Seisen International School since 2015. Her background as an experienced international school counselor, mother of two teen third culture kids ( TCKs), and her experiences as a “trailing spouse” reinforce her advocacy of holistic education.

Colette has a firm focus on social and emotional wellbeing, student voice, a global mindset, and a belief in cultivating the existence of a strong network of qualified professionals working in collaboration with international families. As a Head of School, top of Colette’s priorities is adhering to the international standards of Student Safeguarding and ensuring her faculty and staff are trained in child protection and advocacy. A proud and respected member of the Japan Council of International Schools ( JCIS), Colette represents JCIS on the TELL Board.

## Tiziana Alamprese

Tiziana came to Japan the first time as a fellow student of the Japanese Ministry of Education at Kyushu University, where she obtained her Master in Economics. The years spent in Japan as a student were fundamental to growing her respect for the Japanese culture.

Since 2005, when she returned to Japan from Italy as a top executive in the automotive business, she has been combining her knowledge and love for the local culture with her creative approach. Her focus, in her current role as Marketing Director at FCA Japan is to connect the value of each Brand she manages to a responsible cause marketing strategy. Since 2011, she has promoted consistent support to 13 NPOs active in Japan in the field of women empowerment, LGBT rights, environment & animal protection, support to hospitalized children and to persons with diverse abilities.

Tiziana is a passionate lecturer and is often invited as a speaker by the Academia, at business associations networking events, other companies’ seminars and as an energetic testimonial to encourage women empowerment in Japan.

## Maurice Rabb

Maurice L. Rabb has been a TELL Japan Executive Board Member for several years. He is a California licensed attorney, professional development and strategy consultant, diversity & inclusion strategist, career coach, and legal tech evangelist.

He has been living and working in Asia for more than 15 years. During his time in Asia, Maurice has worked for U.S. and Japanese law firms as an international business lawyer and human resources professional and for a global education Non-Profit Organization. Currently, Maurice is the Senior Manager for Recruitment in Asia for Baker McKenzie, a leading global law firm.

## Jin Montesano

Jin Song Montesano is Executive Officer and Senior Managing Director of LIXIL Corporation. As Chief People Officer, Jin oversees a broad range of functions including Human Resources and General Affairs, Communications, Corporate Responsibility, Investor Relations, and External Affairs.

Prior to joining LIXIL, Montesano held various senior positions around the world, including Vice President, Global Public Affairs at GSK Vaccines; Vice President, Corporate & Government Affairs, Asia Pacific in Kraft Foods; Vice President, Communications, Asia Region in GE Money and Corporate; Government Affairs Director, Asia Pacific in GlaxoSmithKline plc. She received a Bachelor of Arts degree in English Literature from Columbia College of Columbia University and a Master of Public Affairs from Princeton University’s School of Public and International Affairs.

## Minako Abe, M.D.

Dr. Minako Abe serves as Vice President and Director of Lifestyle Medicine at the Tokyo Cancer Clinic, where she leads programs integrating personalized immune cell therapy, regenerative medicine, and evidence-based lifestyle interventions to support cancer patients.

She holds a B.A. from the University of California, Berkeley, and an M.D. from the State University of New York at Stony Brook. Dual board-certified in Emergency Medicine and Lifestyle Medicine, Dr. Abe practiced in the United States for over 15 years.

Recognizing the profound impact of mental health on physical health, Dr. Abe is dedicated to addressing psychological well-being as a core aspect of patient care. She leads initiatives that empower individuals to take charge of their health through evidence-based lifestyle changes, emphasizing the mind-body connection.

Outside of work, she enjoys spending time in nature, exploring the culinary arts, and engaging in community wellness initiatives.

## Kirsten O’Connor

Originally from the UK, and with almost three decades of teaching and senior leadership experience in international education, Kirsten is now the Director and Founder of QUEST TOKYO KK, an educational consultancy and tutoring company established in 2018. Her life in Tokyo since 2001, has included 17 years at The British School in Tokyo, the final six of which serving as Head Teacher – Primary. As a British qualified teacher, Kirsten has a BA Hons QTS  from Canterbury Christ Church University, UK, an MEd from University of Southern Queensland, Australia, and the NPQH (National Professional Qualification for Headship) from UCL, UK.

Kirsten’s background as a seasoned educator, her involvement with international school opening and development in Tokyo, alongside her individualised educational consultancy, emphasise her commitment to tailored educational solutions. A long term and vocal supporter of inclusive education practices in Tokyo and beyond, Kirsten is dedicated to fostering safe, positive and productive learning environments for both pupils, staff and families.

## Sean King

Sean is a digital and cybersecurity focused partner in PwC Consulting LLC, where he advises clients in the areas of IT strategy, IT risk, cyber/information security, and IT governance. He has extensive experience helping large domestic and multinational organizations in Japan navigate complex, cross-border issues. Sean is on the Diversity, Equity and Inclusion leadership team in PwC Consulting, where he is focused on the theme of nationality and committed to improving cross-cultural engagement across the firm.

Sean graduated from Northwestern University with a Joint Bachelor of Arts in Mathematics and Economics. He has resided in Japan for 25+ years and is well versed in local business culture and the Japanese language.

## Koji Iizuka, MD

Koji Iizuka, MD was raised in Japan and moved to the United States at the age of 18. He earned his medical degree from Loma Linda University School of Medicine in 2010 and completed his psychiatry residency at the University of Hawaii. Dr. Iizuka served as a psychiatrist in the U.S. Air Force for six years and has continued to serve as a reservist since 2020. He currently operates a private telepsychiatry clinic based in Hawaii and also works part-time with the Guam SDA Clinic. In addition, Dr. Iizuka serves as a contract examiner for veterans’ compensation and pension evaluations. He is also a school counselor for two schools in Japan, where he supports the emotional and mental well-being of students and their families. Deeply committed to culturally informed care, Dr. Iizuka integrates clinical expertise with faith-based values to promote resilience and healing across diverse communities.

## Rune Sølvsteen

Rune Sølvsteen is a strategic advisor and digital commerce expert with a focus on organizational growth and digital disruption. He is the co-founder of Ginto Asia and Defacto Partners, with current business activities centered on Consulting, HR software solutions, and managing the distribution of Trollbeads jewellery in Japan.

Rune’s governance experience includes serving on the TAC board as Treasurer, demonstrating his commitment to financial stewardship and non-profit oversight. His career includes leadership roles at global companies like Nike, where he was part of the e-Commerce founding team for 21 European countries, and as Industry Leader Retail & Board Member at Google Benelux.

Rune holds a BA in Marketing & Economics and an MBA from INSEAD. Rune speaks English, Dutch, Spanish, and Danish. He studies Japanese and lives in Tokyo with his family.

## Akiko Mega

Akiko Mega is the founder of Faro (The Mega Center), a transformation advisory working with global organizations and their leaders across Asia on organizational change and leadership effectiveness.

A graduate of the Rhode Island School of Design, she began her career in Tokyo with Issey Miyake before serving as Co-General Manager of Maison Margiela Japan, in joint venture with Mitsubishi Corporation. Raised in Texas and shaped by Tokyo and Paris, she is based in Hokkaido.

Akiko is passionate about normalizing mental health care in Japan, a committed ally of the LGBTQ+ community, and an advocate for women and girls, including those affected by gender-based violence.

Our Mission and Vision

**Mission**

TELL is a not-for-profit organization dedicated to providing world-class, effective support and counseling services to Japan’s international community as well as helping to address the country’s growing mental health care needs.

**Vision**

TELL will be a leader in services and education, practicing state-of-the-art standards of care in the field of mental health. We will:

*   Create a vibrant, sustainable organization
    
*   Foster growth and development of all staff and stakeholders
    
*   Embrace diversity with compassion and respect
    
*   Communicate with outside organizations to bring value and talent into TELL
    

**使命**

東京英語いのちの電話（TELL）は、国際化に伴って発生するこころの問題に対し、ハイレベルのカウンセリング・サポートの提供を目指すとともに、日本において高まっているメンタルヘルスケアへの必要性に応えていくことを目的として設立された非営利団体です。

**目標**

メンタルヘルス（精神衛生）分野の先駆けとなり、最高のサービスを提供することを目指します。

*   持続可能で活気のある組織
    
*   団体の活動に関わるすべての人の成長と向上を促進する
    
*   慈しみと尊敬の心で多様性を受け入れる
    
*   他団体との情報交換を通じて、組織に価値と才能を取り入れる
    

### A Message from TELL's Executive Director

_It is a great honour for me to be involved with TELL. Since its inception in 1973, TELL has been saving lives for nearly half a century through its Lifeline, Clinic, and Outreach services. TELL relies entirely on the support of its kind and compassionate donors (you), a superb staff, and its unrivaled volunteers and clinicians. TELL, its Chairman and the Board are impassioned about what we do, and we will continue to be so for the next 50 years and more. You don’t have to be alone. Together, we can make a difference._

_– Royanne Doi, TELL Executive Director_

_私はTELLに関わることができ、大変光栄に思っています。1973年の設立以来、TELLはライフライン、クリニック、アウトリーチサービスを通じて、半世紀近くにわたって人々のいのちを救い続けてきました。TELLは、親切で思いやりのある寄付者（皆様）、優れたスタッフ、そして比類なきボランティアや臨床医の支援に頼ってきました。私たちTELLとその会長・取締役会は、次の50年、さらにその先の50年も、いのちを救う活動に情熱を注ぎ続けます。一人でいる必要はありません。_

_– TELLエグゼクティブディレクター_ 

# TELL's History

TELL is a nonprofit organization that has been serving Japan’s international community since 1973. TELL offers free, anonymous, and confidential lifeline support via phone and chat, professional face-to-face counseling, and an extensive outreach program.

The inspiration for TELL’s founding came from _Inochi-no-denwa_, the Japanese-language suicide prevention helpline. The research into the need for a similar English-language service and the work to make a start-up possible fell mostly to missionaries and members of the various English-speaking congregations in Tokyo. **The first training (of some 50 volunteers with just 7 trainers) took place in 1972 with TELL taking its first call on April 1****st, 1973.**

In the first eight months of TELL’s operation, we answered just over 1,000 calls. By contrast in 2013 – the year of our 40th anniversary – that number had risen almost sevenfold. And of course, the nature of those calls has changed significantly. In this internet age, there are far fewer “information calls” and many more demands on our volunteers to help people deal with depression, anxiety, and a host of other issues. Consequently, our training program for volunteers has evolved accordingly.

By 1988 TELL was able to extend the Lifeline service to three shifts a day and, by 2003, to four. But we still miss a worrying number of calls in the hours when the line is not manned (23:00-09:00) and our goal going forward is to provide a 24-hour service. To this end, we are considering various ideas to attract more volunteers and – while maintaining the very high standards expected in our training – make such training easier to manage for both trainers and trainees.

In the years between our founding and now, TELL has become a member of the Federation of Inochi-no-denwa; created a dedicated TELL/HIV helpline (now incorporated into the general Lifeline); created a Filipino Lifeline (now spun off); is affiliated with Lifeline International, and has received accreditation from the Samaritan Institute in the US. This latter accreditation is essential for the face-to-face counseling service we began offering in 1991.

From the late 1990s, TELL began offering a number of services for children and adolescents and we have continued to build our portfolio of offerings for Children and Families, including assessments. In 2009, we opened our medical clinic, which allowed us to provide a full menu of psychiatric and counseling support for our community.

We are particularly pleased that in our 40th anniversary year, in 2013, TELL was granted certified NPO status.

TELLは1973年に設立された日本の国際コミュニティに奉仕する多面的な非営利組織です。設立されて以来、日本の国際コミュニティに匿名かつ秘密厳守の無料電話相談と情報、専門家による対面カウンセリング、幅広いアウトリーチ活動などを提供しています。

TELL設立のきっかけは、日本語の自殺予防電話である「いのちの電話」でした。英語での相談窓口の必要性のリサーチや立ち上げの作業は、主に宣教師や東京の英語圏のメンバーに任されました。1972年に最初のトレーニング（約50人のボランティアとわずか7人のトレーナー）が行われ、1973年4月1日に最初の電話相談を受けました。

最初の8カ月間では、TELLは1,000件強のコールに対応しましたが、40周年を迎えた2013年には、相談件数が約7倍にもなりました。もちろん、相談の内容も大きく変わっています。インターネットが普及している中、「情報提供」の電話が少なくなり、「うつ」や「不安」など、さまざまな悩みを抱えた人たちからの相談が多くなりました。そのため、ボランティアのトレーニングプログラムも進化しています。

1988年から2003年にかけて、ライフライン相談員のシフトを1日3枠から1日4枠に拡大しました。しかし、相談窓口が閉まっている時間帯（23時〜9時）には、まだ多くのコールがあり、今後は24時間体制のシフト作成を目指しています。そのため、より多くのボランティアを集め、研修に求められる高い水準を維持しながら、研修者と講師にとって運営しやすいよう、さまざまなアイデアを考えていくつもりです。

設立から現在までに、TELLは、日本いのちの電話連盟とライフライン・インターナショナルと提携し、TELL/HIVヘルプライン（現在はライフラインに統合）とフィリピンライフライン（現在は分離）を作成し、米国サマリタン研究所からの認定を受けました。特に後者は、1991年に開始した対面式カウンセリングサービスにおいて重要な意味を持ちます。

1990年代後半から、子どもと思春期の若者を対象としたサービスを開始し、アセスメントを含む「子どもと家族のためのサービス」のポートフォリオを構築してきました。2009年にはメディカルクリニックも開設しました。

2013年、40周年を迎えたTELLは、認定NPO法人として認定されました。

## HOW WE SELECT BRANDS TO SHOWCASE

We review each application and carefully select vendors to ensure a high-quality balance of the right products and brands.

We encourage **every** applicant to put their best foot forward in their application. When assessing your application we place a high value on:

*   Your story and passion for what you do.
*   How you feel you can make a difference to the General Collective events.
*   How well your brand will fit with our audience (see our customer demographics.)
*   Beautiful professional photography - applications will not be accepted without images of your products.
*   How you plan to create an outstanding product display.

The most competitive categories are those with jewellery, soap, and candles. If your business is one of these categories tell us how you stand out from the rest. 

Due to the popularity of each General Collective market we often receive more applications than we have physical space for. This means not everyone who applies can be accepted. Make your application shine for your best chance.

# Frequently Asked Questions for Vendors

![Ecology & Co at General Collective](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0284/8545/1850/files/191020GC_084_lowrez_600x600.jpg?v=1694016811)

###   FAQs for Vendors Interested In Showcasing Their Brand With General Collective

**When is the next General Collective event?**

*   Check the [What's On](https://generalcollective.co.nz/pages/whats-on "What's On | General Collective | Auckland Events & Markets") page for our event line-up.

**How do I take part in a General Collective event?**

*   To participate in a General Collective event, vendors must [apply](https://generalcollective.co.nz/pages/apply-for-general-collective-market "Apply for Events & Markets | General Collective") for each specific event they’re interested in. Applications open 3 weeks to a few months in advance of each event.
    
    Here’s how to get started:
    
    *   Create a vendor profile on the General Collective vendor portal [here](https://generalcollective.co.nz/pages/vendor-login "Vendor Portal Login | General Collective").
    *   Once your profile is set up, apply for the specific event you’d like to take part in.
    *   As applications open for each event we email vendors who have created a profile and have opted in to receive emails. Notification of applications opening and new events is also published on our social platforms.
    

Please note:

*   Signing up on the portal does not automatically register your interest for every event.
*   A separate application must be submitted for each event.
*   Vendor applications are carefully reviewed, and all applicants will be notified of the outcome once the application period closes. 

**What is General Collective, and what type of products are showcased?**

*   General Collective showcases talent from New Zealand's creative community through in-person events, markets, and social channels.
*   General Collective welcomes vendors who design, make, create, curate and assemble high-quality homeware, artwork, jewellery, skincare, food, fashion, and more.
*   General Collective is not a platform for businesses who purely import and re-sell products. We're looking for products belonging to a brand, brands that can share an inspiring story. 

**What are the benefits of taking part in General Collective events as a vendor?**

*   Showcasing your brand at a General Collective event offers several advantages ([Showcase your brand with General Collective](https://generalcollective.co.nz/pages/showcase-your-brand-with-general-collective "SHOWCASE YOUR BRAND WITH GENERAL COLLECTIVE")), including:
    *   Boosting awareness of your brand.
    *   Connecting with a wider audience and growing your customer/fan base.
    *   Gaining valuable feedback and ideas for your brand.
    *   Attracting potential retailers looking for wholesale opportunities.
    *   Generating sales.
    *   Exposure and/or promotion through popular social media channels & a large email list.
    *   Having your brand listed on the General Collective online customer [portal](http://www.generalcollectivemarket.co.nz/ "General Collective Online Customer Portal, Vendor Line-Up & Market Map"), specific to the event booked.
    *   Building in-person relationships with visitors at market day events.
    *   Connecting with a community of like-minded creatives through a dedicated [vendor support group](https://www.facebook.com/groups/generalcollectivevendors/ "General Collective Vendor Facebook Group").

![General Collective](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0284/8545/1850/files/GCLD_May_2023_0021_1024x1024.jpg?v=1694065847)

**How does General Collective select brands to showcase?**

*   We review each application carefully to ensure a balance of high-quality products and brands.
*   When assessing applications, we consider:

*   The product offering.
*   Your story and passion for what you do.
*   How you believe you can contribute to General Collective events, and make a difference.
*   The product offering.
*   The fit of your brand with our audience (please refer to our [customer demographics](https://generalcollective.co.nz/pages/showcase-your-brand-with-general-collective "Showcase your brand with General Collective")).
*   The quality of professional product photography - this is your chance to really sell your brand and products visually.  
*   Your plan for creating an outstanding product display.
*   For competitive categories like jewellery, soap, & candles, we look for what sets your business apart from the rest.

**How competitive is the application process?**

*   Due to the popularity of General Collective markets, we often receive more applications than we have physical space for. While we strive to showcase a diverse range of vendors, not everyone who applies can be accepted. It's essential to make your application shine for the best chance of being selected.

![The Joy Make Club at General Collective](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0284/8545/1850/files/GCLD_May_2023_0017_600x600.jpg?v=1694043946)

**Where can I find more information and apply to become a vendor?**

*   You can find detailed information on showcasing your brand with General Collective [here](https://generalcollective.co.nz/pages/showcase-your-brand-with-general-collective "General Collective Vendor Portal").
*   Access the [vendor portal](https://portal.conventionforce.com/?aid=103 "General Collective Vendor Portal") for the online application for each event. 

**What is the cost associated with becoming a vendor at General Collective markets?**  

*   Stall pricing starts from $150 + GST and varies based on the type of event and location.
*   For specific information about stall pricing, stall sizes, and any additional costs and options, refer to the individual application for each event on our [vendor portal](https://portal.conventionforce.com/?aid=103 "General Collective Vendor Portal").

![Dirty International](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0284/8545/1850/files/GCLD_May_2023_0075_600x600.jpg?v=1694066201)

**How can I stay updated on General Collective events & announcements?**  

*   Check out our event line up & What's On [here](https://generalcollective.co.nz/pages/whats-on "What's On").
*   To stay informed about upcoming events, applications opening, & announcements, create a profile for your biz/brand on our [vendor portal](https://portal.conventionforce.com/?aid=103 "Vendor Portal"), & follow us on our social media channels ([Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/generalcollective "Facebook - General Collective") & [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/generalcollective "Instagram - General Collective")).

 **Can I apply as a food vendor, and are there specific requirements for food-related businesses?**

*   Yes, we welcome food vendors at the [General Collective Lifestyle & Design Market](https://generalcollective.co.nz/pages/glasshouse-market "Glasshouse Market by General Collective") and the [General Collective Kids Market](https://generalcollective.co.nz/pages/kids-market "General Collective Kids Market"), & for special events.
*   Our boutique markets - [Glasshouse Market](https://generalcollective.co.nz/pages/glasshouse-market "Glasshouse Market") & [Ponsonby Cental Market](https://generalcollective.co.nz/pages/ponsonby-central-market "Ponsonby Central") - don't allow vendors to serve food prepared onsite, for consumption at the event.  Food vendors offering baked goods or similar, or those intended to take home, may be considered.
*   Please ensure to provide details of your food offering in your application and include photos, each with a title & brief description.
*   Food-related businesses must comply with all relevant food safety regulations
*   Food certificates/grades must be loaded onto your profile in the vendor portal at time of application. 
*   Food providers for the [General Collective Lifestyle & Design Market](https://generalcollective.co.nz/pages/lifestyle-and-design-market "General Collective Lifestyle & Design Market") at Auckland Showgrounds must hold a minimum of $5 million public liability.

**![Koko Body](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0284/8545/1850/files/190505GC_027_lowrez_1024x1024.jpg?v=1694065239)**

**Are there any restrictions on the geographic location of vendors?**

*   General Collective primarily showcases New Zealand-based talent and small businesses. 
*   There is no restriction on geographic location within New Zealand and we regularly welcome vendors from across both north and south islands.
*   Overseas applicants will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis.
*   Please include your location information in your application.

**What is your cancellation policy?**

*   The cancellation policy is outlined in our Terms & Conditions, found [here](file:///Users/rosebarbarich/Library/Mobile%20Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/GC/MASTER%20Docs/Terms%20&%20Conditions/Terms%20and%20Conditions%20-%20General%20Collective.html "General Collective Terms & Conditions").

![Tides Out Maps](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0284/8545/1850/files/a_77_lowrez_e25a442b-637c-488c-907f-bd676cf0f5be_1024x1024.jpg?v=1692089541)

**How can I contact General Collective if I have additional questions?**

*   For further inquiries or assistance, you may contact [Sarah](mailto:sarah@generalcollective.co.nz "Sarah@generalcollective.co.nz") or [Rose](mailto:rose@generalcollective.co.nz "Rose Barbarich | General Collectiv") [here](https://generalcollective.co.nz/pages/contact "Contact General Collective, Rose Barbarich & Sarah Langstone-Ross").

Worried About Someone?

If you have noticed changes in the behavior and mood of someone you know; if they have told you that they are feeling suicidal; or if they are talking on social media about ending their life, it can be hard to know what to do. If you are worried, don’t ignore what you are feeling. Trust your instincts. There are things you can do to support them.

Reach out to the **TELL Lifeline**, 03-5774-0992 or **Toll Free 0800-300-8355** or via [chat](https://telljp.com/lifeline/?swcfpc=1)**.** TELL Lifeline volunteer support workers offer confidential support every day of the year, from **Saturday 09:00 – Monday 23:00** (continuous service), Tuesday – Thursday 09:00 – 23:00, and Friday 09:00 – 02:00. Please check out our [weekly hours](https://telljp.com/tell-hours/?swcfpc=1) to find out whether we are currently available on chat or phone.

# Emergencies

##### If you think it may be an emergency and the person could be in immediate danger:

##### **If you are in Japan:**

*   Call 119 for an ambulance or 110 for the police 

For emergency services to be able to act, you need to be able to give:

*   Their name
*   Their phone number
*   Their address

##### **If you are located outside Japan:**

*   Call 81-3-3501-0110 (M-F 8:30 – 17:15 JST). Outside of these hours the service is not available. 
*   If it is outside of these hours, try to locate a police station near the person’s address and ask for translation (TSUYAKU) when you call.
  

For emergency services to be able to act, you need to be able to give:

*   Their name
*   Their phone number
*   Their address

PLEASE NOTE: TELL IS NOT ABLE TO CONTACT THE EMERGENCY SERVICES ON YOUR BEHALF.

Listen and offer support

If you think that someone you know might be struggling, find an opportunity to talk to them directly about your concerns. For most people listening and showing you care will help.

*   Listen carefully to what is troubling them.
*   Ask questions about how they are feeling.
*   Talk gently about your concerns and the things you have noticed.
*   Give them time and space to tell you about what they are going through.
*   Listen without being judgmental or offering solutions.
*   Encourage them to get professional support.

Recognize [Warning signs and risk factors](https://telljp.com/lifeline/suicide-prevention/)

Encourage and support them to make a safety plan

Many people feel such relief that someone has noticed they are struggling and have taken the time to ask them about it. However, if you are still worried about them, then getting help and support is very important.

*   You can help by encouraging them to make a [Safety Plan](https://telljp.com/safety-plan/) and offer to work on this together. 
*   You can help by encouraging them to make an appointment with a doctor or [counselor](https://telljp.com/counseling/).
*   If they are already seeing someone, encourage them to stick with their treatment plan, or to seek different treatment if no improvement occurs.

今年は10月。秋空の下、裸足で芝生を踏みしめるパークヨガが気持ちいい。  
ヨガを深めるアカデミーエリアに、ショッピングやヨガ友との再会も。  
100を超えるプログラムを1日リトリートとして堆能しよう♪

# About Us

![Genera Collective](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0284/8545/1850/files/Auckland_Market_1024x1024.jpg?v=1587984364)

We’re known for our contemporary market experiences that showcase the incredible talent of New Zealand’s creative community.

Where the brands and products on offer are in a league of their own.

Where we celebrate clever ideas and the hard yards required to turn these creative ideas into reality.

Where the values of our vendors are as important as their products.

We champion small New Zealand makers and creators far and wide with their New Zealand made and designed products. 

Because celebrating creativity, connection, and collaboration is what makes the General Collective unique.

 ![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0284/8545/1850/files/GCLD_Nov_25_-_Rose_a_160.jpg?v=1763469857)

## OUR STORY

Hello, welcome to General Collective.

I’m Rose Barbarich, founder of General Collective. 

In 2012, General Collective started from a small seed of an idea.

A friend and I needed an outlet to sell our boutique New Zealand handmade products. 

We found a unique space and invited friends who made beautiful products to join us. 

From the start I wanted to create something different - a fresh take on traditional markets.

Something highly-curated and well thought out to showcase outstanding local creative talent.

Word got out and General Collective took off, quickly attracting a strong following.

Our first market had 14 stalls. Our second jumped to 30, and the third to 50.

General Collective now has markets throughout the year in beautiful venues throughout Auckland. 

Our flagship event is held at the Auckland Showgrounds in Auckland with 150+ stalls showcasing New Zealand made or designed products, amazing street food vendors, and thousands of visitors.

![](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0284/8545/1850/files/General_Collective_191201_035_lowrez_235d3d43-7be0-416d-835d-35cdbceb92fd_480x480.jpg?v=1588681364)

## SHOWCASING NEW ZEALAND TALENT FAR AND WIDE

We're passionate about helping hard-working and talented small businesses to increase brand awareness.  
   
By showcasing brands at our in-person events and on our engaged social platforms, we help small businesses to gain exposure to fellow kiwis and further afield.   
   
This supports New Zealand small business owners, makers and creatives to build connections with new fans and customers who may otherwise never get to experience their wonderful talents.

title: FAQ - ヨガフェスタ横浜 2026
markdown:
FAQ - ヨガフェスタ横浜 2026

# FAQ

ヨガフェスタ横浜 2026 よくあるご質問

## ヨガフェスタ横浜について

Q. ヨガフェスタ横浜ってどんなイベントですか？ ▼

様々なヨガと出会える10月10日～12日にパシフィコ横浜で開催される日本最大級のヨガイベントです。有料のアカデミークラス、無料のトライアルクラス・パークヨガ、ショーケース（出展ブース）など、多彩なコンテンツを3日間にわたり開催します。YOGAWeeKや各地で開催されるサテライトイベントとは少し異なりますのでご注意ください。

Q. 誰でも参加できますか？ ▼

はい、どなたでもご参加いただけます。ショーケースエリアやパークヨガは入場無料・予約不要です。アカデミークラスは事前にチケット購入が必要、トライアルクラスは事前に無料予約が必要です。

Q. どんなクラスがありますか？ ▼

全100クラス以上の多種多様なヨガクラスを、国内外の著名インストラクターが担当します。初心者向けからアドバンスまで、ハタヨガ・ヴィンヤサ・アシュタンガ・陰ヨガ・瞑想など幅広いジャンルをご用意しています。

Q. ショッピングはできますか？ ▼

はい。ショーケースエリア（アネックス館内）にて、ヨガウェア・グッズ・コスメなど様々なブースが出展しています。入場は無料です。

Q. 更衣室はありますか？ ▼

男性用・女性用の無料更衣室をご用意しています。場所は会場内の案内をご確認ください。

Q. クローク・託児所はありますか？ ▼

クローク、託児所はございません。パシフィコ横浜のコインロッカーをご利用ください。お荷物は最低限（ヨガマット・タオル・貴重品・飲料程度）でお越しいただくことをおすすめします。

Q. 子どもと一緒に参加できますか？ ▼

ショーケースエリアやパークヨガは年齢制限なくご参加いただけます。アカデミークラス（有料クラス）については、お子様も大人と同様にチケットが必要です（未就学児は保護者のマット内でお過ごしいただける場合がありますが、クラスにより異なります）。

Q. ヨガマットは必要ですか？ ▼

どんなクラスを受けるかによって異なりますが、有料のアカデミークラスには、ヨガマットのご持参を推奨しています。お持ちいただけない場合は会場でヨガマットレンタル（1日1,000円）のサービスがご利用いただけます。その他トライアルクラスではマットをご用意しています。パークヨガは、数に限りはありますが無料貸し出しマットもご用意しています。

Q. 会場へのアクセスは？ ▼

パシフィコ横浜アネックスホール（神奈川県横浜市西区みなとみらい1-1-1）が会場です。最寄駅はみなとみらい線「みなとみらい駅」から徒歩約5分です。

Q. 駐車場・駐輪場はありますか？ ▼

パシフィコ横浜の駐車場・駐輪場をご利用いただけます（イベント割引はございません）。公共交通機関でのご来場をおすすめします。

## アカデミークラス（有料）

Q. アカデミークラスの参加方法は？ ▼

公式サイトからチケットを購入してください。当日はクラス開始30分前から受付を開始しますので、スマートフォンでチケット画面を提示して入室してください。初回クラスは15分前からの受付となります。

Q. チケットはどこで買えますか？ ▼

公式チケットサイト（store.yogafest.jp）にてクレジットカードまたはPayPayでご購入いただけます。当日会場でも空きがあればご購入いただける場合がありますが、事前購入をおすすめします。

Q. 売り切れたクラスの再販売はありますか？ ▼

基本的に売り切れ後の再販売は行っておりません。お早めにご購入ください。

Q. キャンセル・返金はできますか？ ▼

購入後のキャンセル・返金は一切お受けしておりません。チケット購入時点でスペースの確保（サービスの提供）が開始されるため、体調不良・交通機関の遅延等の場合も返金の対象外となります。主催者都合による中止の場合のみ全額返金いたします。

Q. チケットを他の人に譲渡できますか？ ▼

チケットの転売は禁止しております。ただし、代理購入（購入者が他の参加者のために購入し、チケットを送付すること）は可能です。

Q. 途中入場・途中退出はできますか？ ▼

原則としてできません。クラス開始前にご入室ください。

Q. 撮影・録音はできますか？ ▼

クラス中の撮影・録音・スクリーンショットは一切禁止です。違反が確認された場合は、データの削除・機材の没収・強制退場となる場合があります。

Q. 服装の指定はありますか？ ▼

特に指定はありません。動きやすい服装でお越しください。

Q. クラスの時間はどのくらいですか？ ▼

アカデミークラスは1クラス90分です（クラス間に30分の休憩があります）。

Q. オンラインでも受講できますか？ ▼

有料のアカデミークラスのビジネスクラスのみZoomによるオンライン配信を行います。ビジネスクラスはアーカイブ視聴（期間限定）もご利用いただけます。オンラインチケットは公式チケットサイトで販売します。その他のオンラインクラスはございません。

Q. 連続して複数クラスを受講できますか？ ▼

はい、同じ教室での連続という意味では可能です。ただし、クラス間に一度退出していただく必要があります。次のクラスの受付時間に再度お越しください。 違う教室でしたら、前のクラス後、次の希望クラスの教室へご移動いただきます。

Q. 時間が重なっているクラスはどうするのですか？ ▼

数多くのクラスがあるため、時間が重なるクラスは発生して受講したい方にはストレスを感じさせてしまう可能性がございますが、時間に対して物理的に1クラスで選択いただくようにお願いいたしいます。途中でクラスを退室してもう一つの希望クラスへ途中から参加する方法はご遠慮ください。

Q. チケットは送られてきますか？ ▼

チケットは購入された瞬間に購入された方のログインされたサイトに格納されていますので、別途メールなどで送られることはありません。購入後自身のサイトで確認ください。

Q. スマホが無い場合はどのように購入すればよいですか？ ▼

チケットはスマホをお持ちの方で当日にスマホを対象教室入口で見せることで入場が可能です。そのためスマホが必須となっております。 スマホが無い方は、パソコンで事前に購入して、会場入口すぐのinformationでその情報を伝えていただき確認が取れますと紙のチケットをお渡ししてその紙のチケットで受講は可能です。

Q. 購入したのですがメールがきません。 ▼

メールが来ない理由は様々あるケースがあります。登録メールアドレスが 間違っているや登録のメールアドレスが購入メールを拒否しているなど、ヨガフェスタのチケットは購入した時点で自身のログインされたサイトにチケットが入っていますので、購入メールを探すより自身のサイトを確認された方が解決になるかと思います。購入メールの履歴も自身のログインされたサイトで確認もできます。

Q. 知人がスマホ持っていません。どのようにチケットを購入すればよいですか？ ▼

大変お手数をおかけしますが、ヨガフェスタのチケットはスマホで利用する前提で作られております。そのスマホで受講希望の教室入口でチケットを見せていただきスタッフが操作（もぎり）をすることで入室可能となります。 そのため、知人の方がスマホが無くて参加する場合は、パソコンなどで予約購入していただきその情報（ログイン情報必要）を会場入口のinformationでお伝えいただき、確認が取れますと紙のチケットをお渡しして、その紙のチケットで希望教室の入口でスタッフに渡すことで参加が可能です。 最後に知人の方が同じクラス受講で一緒に動く場合は変わりに自身と一緒に同じクラスのチケットを複数枚買うことは可能です。ただし入口にその複数枚のチケットを確認しますので、ご一緒に入室をお願いします。 その際の購入トラブル、購入者が会場に来れないなどのトラブルには責任は負いかねますのでご注意ください。

Q. 連続した時間で受けたいのですが違う教室なので違う教室の距離感はどのくらいですか？ ▼

どの教室間なのかにもよりますが、クラスの間のインターバルは30分設けており遠い教室間でも5分程度に移動かと思いますので、事前にHPや会場の案内なのど確認いただくとよりスムーズかと思います。

Q. 当日券はありますか？ ▼

事前のネット発売の数量がすべてとなりますので、当日は空きのあるクラスの販売は行いますが、当日券としての独自の枠はありません。

Q. 当日でもチケットは買えますか？ ▼

事前購入と同じネットシステムが当日まで稼働しますので、売り切れてしますと終了となりますが空きのあるクラスは当日まで購入は可能です。

Q. チケットは買ったのですが、チケットが反映されません。 ▼

会員情報を複数お持ちでは無いですか？（過去登録したなど） 同じメールアドレスの登録はできませんが過去のメールアドレスが間違えていたり 今回新たに登録したが、端末がメールアドレス・パスワードを記憶していて違う登録情報で購入されているという状況があります。すべての購入情報は事務局で把握できますのでinfo@yogafest.jpにお問合せください。

## ショーケース

Q. ショーケースとは何ですか？ ▼

ヨガウェア・グッズ・コスメなど、ヨガに関連する様々なブランド・ショップが出展するエリアです。今年はアネックス館内にゆったりとしたスペースをご用意しています。お買い物はもちろん、休憩スペースとしてもくつろいでいただけます。

Q. 入場料はかかりますか？ ▼

入場は無料です。どなたでもお気軽にお立ち寄りいただけます。

Q. 営業時間は？ ▼

各日の営業時間は公式サイトでご確認ください。

## トライアルクラス（無料・予約制）

Q. トライアルクラスとは？ ▼

ヨガワークス協賛による無料のヨガクラスです。1クラス45分で、初心者の方にもおすすめです。ヨガマットはこちらでご用意しています。

Q. 参加するにはどうすればいいですか？ ▼

事前に公式HPのトライアルクラスのページより予約（0円購入）が可能です。無料のため、人気クラスは売り切れになる場合がありますが、再販・追加などは行いません。ただし、当日はキャンセル待ちを設けますので、当日トライアルクラスの受付へお問い合わせください。

Q. ヨガマットは必要ですか？ ▼

トライアルクラスではヨガマットをご用意しておりますので、手ぶらでご参加いただけます。

## パークヨガ（無料）

Q. パークヨガとは？ ▼

屋外の開放的な空間で行う無料のヨガクラスです。1クラス45分で、予約不要・先着順でご参加いただけます。

Q. 予約は必要ですか？ ▼

予約は不要です。直接会場にお越しいただき、先着順でご参加いただけます。

Q. ヨガマットは必要ですか？ ▼

ヨガマットのご持参を推奨していますが、多少の無料貸し出しマットもご用意しています。

Q. 雨天の場合はどうなりますか？ ▼

荒天の場合は中止となる場合があります。当日の開催状況は公式SNSまたは会場でご確認ください。

## その他

Q. 開催日程を教えてください。 ▼

2026年10月10日（土）・11日（日）・12日（月祝）の3日間です。

Q. 会場はどこですか？ ▼

パシフィコ横浜アネックスホール（神奈川県横浜市西区みなとみらい1-1-1）です。

Q. 会場内での写真撮影は可能ですか？ ▼

ショーケースエリアや共用スペースでの個人的な撮影は可能ですが、クラス受講中の撮影・録音は一切禁止です。また、会場での公式撮影映像・写真が公式サイト・SNS等で公開される場合がありますのでご了承ください。

Q. お問い合わせ先は？ ▼

ヨガフェスタ事務局（info@yogafest.jp）までメールにてお問い合わせください。

## ヨガフェスタについて

Q. ヨガフェスタについて教えてください ▼

ヨガフェスタは毎年秋に開催される様々なヨガに触れるイベントです。 10月10日～12日パシフィコ横浜で行われるヨガフェスタ横浜を中心に事前オンラインイベントYOGAWeeKや各地で行われるヨガフェスタの名の基にサテライトイベントが開催されます。詳しくはHPをご確認ください。

Q. 〇〇先生のクラスはどのように受けられますか？ ▼

ヨガフェスタは複数のイベントで構成されています。公式サイトで講師をお探しいただき、どのイベントに属しているかご確認ください。 【主なイベント】 - \*\*ヨガフェスタ横浜\*\*（10月10-12日、パシフィコ横浜）：アカデミークラス（有料）、トライアルクラス（無料）、パークヨガ（無料） - \*\*YOGAWeek\*\*（オンライン無料） - \*\*サテライトイベント\*\*（全国各地）

Q. オンラインのクラスはありますか？ ▼

10月10日～12日にパシフィコ横浜で開催のヨガフェスタ横浜は実際に会場にお越しいただき参加されるリアルイベントです。ただし、アカデミークラスのビジネスカレッジクラスに関しましては、Zoomでの配信とアーカイブを期間限定で行います。ヨガフェスタでのオンラインクラスはヨガフェスタ横浜以前に行われるYOGAWeeKは全てオンラインで行われます。各HPをご確認ください。
