# ABOUT:

## How The Show Came To Be

**![](https://boardroomshow.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/timmy-shaping-sanding-block-300x188.jpeg)**

**In 2005 Clark Foam abruptly closed its doors, with no warning, essentially shuttering the surfboard industry. Clark Foam was the only surfboard foam blank supplier – a monopoly. Vanished in a day. The surfboard industry was shocked. All of these surfboard shapers I grew up with, and I had been surfing with for decades, were more or less out of work, or struggling to find foam. It was a tough time. Everyone struggling to get orders, struggling to find foam, and struggling to build surfboards — and that was industry wide.**

**That disruption created fallout, but from my perspective, it meant that the craftsmen that I knew, and the craftsmen up and down the coast of California and in Hawaii, and everywhere, that sourced Clark Foam to build boards, were being left behind. Especially in the retail surf shop space. They needed an outlet. They needed a place to showcase their wares.**

**Frankly, these guys were my heros. As a grom in Southern California the surfboard shapers and the surfboard factories was where all the magic happened. And it was sort of a hands-off place too. You didn’t just roll up to the surfboard factory and hang out like you would at a surf shop. The shapers, the builders, the sanders, laminators, the crew…they were sort of mystical … or magical. The doors were closed. They had a Wizard of Oz curtain. They had stories. They had authenticty that you weren’t going to get from Missy selling bikinis and Madras shorts. The smells were… the smells were great. I always liked the smell of resin. The stories and lore that came out of the surfboard factory crew had a lot more legitimacy. From my perspective, these guys lived the life. Moonlight Glassing for instance (Peter, Kenny, Mark, Gary, I feel like I’m missing one more?) worked at night so they could surf during the day. As a young surfer, this made a ton of sense. So I had a certain affinity. To this day, I believe that this is where authentic surf culture germinates. From the hands of those that build our craft.**

**So much more than a tool, the surfboard is the philosophical icon, a sacred craft, a culturally pervasive symbol of freedom, adventure and enduring youth. This is why the surfboard builder was once the primary arbiter of surfing culture, from those early Hawaiian kahunas to the first wave of board manufactures. Think back: Blake, Downing, Brewer, Hobie, Hansen, Bing, Weber, Larkin, Noll, Jacobs, Haut, et al. These surfboard builders shaped surf culture, both literally and figuratively. It was all about the ride–what you wore came second. Since 2007 THE BOARDROOM SHOW (aka Sacred Craft) has reasserted and maintained this philosophy. To put the surfboard — and the modern day kahunas who craft and design them — back at the forefront of surf culture. Today the international surfboard building community places surf culture, its influence, its importance, its responsibility, back in the hands of the artisans who shape our sacred craft – and ultimately our future.**

**![](https://boardroomshow.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/BestInSHow-430x250-1-300x174.jpg)**

**Late 2006. It’s been about a year since Clark closed. All sorts of crazy foams were showing up in the marketplace, but perhaps more importantly, the retail surf shops had started to bring in overseas surfboards to fill out their retail space. They just simply didn’t have surfboards. It’s hard to validate a surf shop without surfboards. By the time the dust settled in 2007, it was just way easier and the terms were much softer for retail surf shops to bring in overseas surfboards — and they did. I don’t blame the surf shops for doing that, but it certainly didn’t help the local board builders and it was a catalyst for the show.**

**I thought, “hey, let’s put on a surfboard show for the real guys, the real deal.” These shapers, these craftsman, these builders, these laminators. No fashion. All passion.**

**In 2006 I had gone to Australia and spent a few days traveling with Chris Christenson. I told him what I was planning to do and I told him I wanted to honor the shapers. Chris was adamant that it can’t be an art contest. It had to be something that highlights the quality of hand shaping surfboards. He gave me his opinions on what that might look like. I threw out ideas at him and Chris either shot them down or suggested a better way.**

**Chris‘s insight was incredibly helpful in regards to how the shape-off competition unfolded.**

**Believe me, I had some horrible ideas. For example, I told Chris, “what if I get a huge block of foam, like an 8’ x 4’ block of foam.” I wanted to see who can craft a board out of a big chunk. Just like the Polynesians in the 1400s. They would identify a huge Koa tree and chop it down and build a board out of it. So I thought a huge chunk of foam was the best way to test the craftsmanship of the shapers. Chris immediately shot that down. He realized that wouldn’t be practical, and it wouldn’t test the shapers skill. He suggested other ways to test the shapers ability, like picking a blank that challenges the shaper to find rocker inside of the blank, ideas like that. I queried him about know how much time would they need to finish the board, what kind of tools should I allow them to use… all of these type of things. Chris gave me his insights and I built the shape-off around this insight. Chris is a legendary shaper and his insights we’re invaluable.**

**![](https://boardroomshow.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/christenson150x200.jpg)****A few months go by and I’m about to pull the trigger so to speak. I’m getting ready to send the big rent check over to the fairgrounds facility people. I’m pretty nervous — my children are eight and nine years old.  I’m sending over a significant amount of my money. I called two people: Rusty Preisendorfer and Matt Biolos. I wanted to get their opinion on doing something like this, and to see if I could in fact count on their participation. Luckily both Rusty and Matt enthusiastic about the idea and told me I could count on their participation. After those two phone calls I sent in the rent check — and crossed my fingers.**

**So those three guys Chris, Rusty and Matt were foundational exhibitors at the show. Chris was a judge in the very first Icons of Foam Tribute to the Master Shape off along with Steve Pezman and John Kies. That first year in 2007 we honored Mike Diffenderfer. Pez new Diff well, and more importantly knew Diff’s boards. John Kies had a shaping bay next to Dif for years and played golf with him. They were good friends.**

**That’s how the Boardroom Show started, in 2007, as Sacred Craft, in Del Mar, California.**

**This is just the quick history. There is much more to tell, but you’d have to be pretty bored to pull up chair and listen. We have a great friends, who turned into great staff, and my immediate family is involved.**

**If you’re interested in the Icons of Foam shapers whom we have honored over the years, and the contemporary shapers who have honored the icons, there is a page for that [here](https://boardroomshow.com/icons-of-foam/).**

**The goal of the show, when it started out in 2007 – and to this day – was to highlight the surfboard: the incredible designs, ideas, and craftsmanship of the modern day kahunas who engage in this creative space.**

**We’ve produced shows at the San Diego Convention Center, in Del Mar, in Huntington Beach during the U.S. Open, in Ventura, in Santa Cruz, in Orlando, Florida, in Costa Mesa, California and in 2019 we went to Tokyo and did a show right before COVID. We’ve had exhibitors go to fame at Shark Tank. Each year other core authentic surfing hardgoods brands exhibit alongside the surfboard builders. – artists too! Surfers love the shows because people love surfboards. They love what the surfboard builders bring to the show, incredible, high-quality, state-of-the-art craftsmanship. Authentic builders that live this life, that live this culture, that surf, and that shape. We realize that the surfboard is a philosophical icon of enduring youth. Pick up a new surfboard, put it under your arm and you will be 15 years old again. — SB**

faq

## Common Questions

How can I Donate or Volunteer?

All donations help fund our skate programs, equipment, facilities and staff. Go [here](https://exposureskate.networkforgood.com/projects/102469-exposure-skate-main-giving-page) You can either make a one-time donation or a monthly reccuring donation.

To volunteer, please visit our [volunteer page](https://exposureskate.org/volunteer/) to learn more how to get involved.

How can I sponsor an event?

Contact amelia.brodka@exposureskate.org 

exposure 2026 vendor information

Setup for all vendors and sponsors at Exposure 2026 is on Friday, November 5th, 12:00-4pm at 425 S. Santa Fe Ave . You can leave your booth overnight on-site until Monday, November 9th at 8:15 am. There will be overnight security but we recommend packing up any valuables. _If you are already registered as a vendor you will receive information such as the sitemap by October 27th._ Your booth location will be determined by your level of sponsorship, you cannot choose your location.  If you are interested in becoming a vendor, please contact amelia.brodka@exposureskate.org by October 25th. 

Media Passes for Exposure 2026

Interested in a media pass for Exposure 2026? Please reach out to info@exposureskate.org to learn more.

Attending exposure 2026

Exposure 2026 is free to attend. [Click Here](https://exposureskate.org/event/exposure-2026/) for information such as the schedule, location and available activities.

Exposure 2026 Competitor information

Stay tuned to learn more information about registration for Exposure 2026. Encinitas Community Park is a public park – you can practice on the street course or bowl at any time prior to November 4th. There will be scheduled practice days November 4th and 5th. If you want to skate vert locally, we recommend Clairemont Skatepark or LVLUP USA. You can choose any division you want based by your ability level. Do not register for more than one ability level in the same discipline. (I.e: “intermediate street” AND “advanced street” ) , If the judges see your same tricks repeated they may score you lower the second time around! We encourage you to challenge yourself. 

More information regarding registration & practice times can be found on [The Boardr](https://theboardr.com/events/4299/Exposure)

**Lodging** – we currently do not have a recommended hotel block.

Trans inclusion

Exposure is an inclusive community of women, trans and nonbinary individuals. We recognize and value the contributions that our non-traditional community makes to skateboarding and it is our intention to provide safe and inclusive spaces for competition and coming together.

IF YOU CHOOSE TO COMPETE IN OUR EVENT, YOU WILL BE COMPETING WITH OUR WHOLE COMMUNITY.

Public relations and Media relations Information

Contact info@exposureskate.org for media information

What are the age requirements for your clinics?

We have taught individuals ranging in age from 18 months to 86 years. Our instructors are trained to work with individuals of all ages and ability levels. Skateboarding has no age restrictions! 

How do I get a tax write-off?

Donate [HERE](https://exposureskate.networkforgood.com/) and you will get a tax receipt automatically. Sponsorships are tax-deductible as well, contact amelia.brodka@exposureskate.org for sponsorship information.

Inclusive spaces

## Build Community Skateboarding

At Exposure Skate, we believe skateboarding is more than just a sport—it’s a powerful tool for building community and creating positive change. Our mission is to provide opportunities for individuals of all ages, backgrounds and skill levels to come together, share their passion, and grow through the culture of skateboarding.

[Learn More](https://exposureskate.org/about)

Whether you’re a beginner, a seasoned pro, or somewhere in between, Exposure Skate fosters an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive. Our Sesh(E) program creates spaces where skaters 16 & over can connect and support one another.

Exposure Skate's youth program provides classes that build empowerment through skateboarding and compassion through service for girls age 4 - 12.

Your generous donation helps Exposure Skate provide life-changing opportunities for skaters of all ages and backgrounds. # ABOUT:

## How The Show Came To Be

**![](https://boardroomshow.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/timmy-shaping-sanding-block-300x188.jpeg)**

**In 2005 Clark Foam abruptly closed its doors, with no warning, essentially shuttering the surfboard industry. Clark Foam was the only surfboard foam blank supplier – a monopoly. Vanished in a day. The surfboard industry was shocked. All of these surfboard shapers I grew up with, and I had been surfing with for decades, were more or less out of work, or struggling to find foam. It was a tough time. Everyone struggling to get orders, struggling to find foam, and struggling to build surfboards — and that was industry wide.**

**That disruption created fallout, but from my perspective, it meant that the craftsmen that I knew, and the craftsmen up and down the coast of California and in Hawaii, and everywhere, that sourced Clark Foam to build boards, were being left behind. Especially in the retail surf shop space. They needed an outlet. They needed a place to showcase their wares.**

**Frankly, these guys were my heros. As a grom in Southern California the surfboard shapers and the surfboard factories was where all the magic happened. And it was sort of a hands-off place too. You didn’t just roll up to the surfboard factory and hang out like you would at a surf shop. The shapers, the builders, the sanders, laminators, the crew…they were sort of mystical … or magical. The doors were closed. They had a Wizard of Oz curtain. They had stories. They had authenticty that you weren’t going to get from Missy selling bikinis and Madras shorts. The smells were… the smells were great. I always liked the smell of resin. The stories and lore that came out of the surfboard factory crew had a lot more legitimacy. From my perspective, these guys lived the life. Moonlight Glassing for instance (Peter, Kenny, Mark, Gary, I feel like I’m missing one more?) worked at night so they could surf during the day. As a young surfer, this made a ton of sense. So I had a certain affinity. To this day, I believe that this is where authentic surf culture germinates. From the hands of those that build our craft.**

**So much more than a tool, the surfboard is the philosophical icon, a sacred craft, a culturally pervasive symbol of freedom, adventure and enduring youth. This is why the surfboard builder was once the primary arbiter of surfing culture, from those early Hawaiian kahunas to the first wave of board manufactures. Think back: Blake, Downing, Brewer, Hobie, Hansen, Bing, Weber, Larkin, Noll, Jacobs, Haut, et al. These surfboard builders shaped surf culture, both literally and figuratively. It was all about the ride–what you wore came second. Since 2007 THE BOARDROOM SHOW (aka Sacred Craft) has reasserted and maintained this philosophy. To put the surfboard — and the modern day kahunas who craft and design them — back at the forefront of surf culture. Today the international surfboard building community places surf culture, its influence, its importance, its responsibility, back in the hands of the artisans who shape our sacred craft – and ultimately our future.**

**![](https://boardroomshow.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/BestInSHow-430x250-1-300x174.jpg)**

**Late 2006. It’s been about a year since Clark closed. All sorts of crazy foams were showing up in the marketplace, but perhaps more importantly, the retail surf shops had started to bring in overseas surfboards to fill out their retail space. They just simply didn’t have surfboards. It’s hard to validate a surf shop without surfboards. By the time the dust settled in 2007, it was just way easier and the terms were much softer for retail surf shops to bring in overseas surfboards — and they did. I don’t blame the surf shops for doing that, but it certainly didn’t help the local board builders and it was a catalyst for the show.**

**I thought, “hey, let’s put on a surfboard show for the real guys, the real deal.” These shapers, these craftsman, these builders, these laminators. No fashion. All passion.**

**In 2006 I had gone to Australia and spent a few days traveling with Chris Christenson. I told him what I was planning to do and I told him I wanted to honor the shapers. Chris was adamant that it can’t be an art contest. It had to be something that highlights the quality of hand shaping surfboards. He gave me his opinions on what that might look like. I threw out ideas at him and Chris either shot them down or suggested a better way.**

**Chris‘s insight was incredibly helpful in regards to how the shape-off competition unfolded.**

**Believe me, I had some horrible ideas. For example, I told Chris, “what if I get a huge block of foam, like an 8’ x 4’ block of foam.” I wanted to see who can craft a board out of a big chunk. Just like the Polynesians in the 1400s. They would identify a huge Koa tree and chop it down and build a board out of it. So I thought a huge chunk of foam was the best way to test the craftsmanship of the shapers. Chris immediately shot that down. He realized that wouldn’t be practical, and it wouldn’t test the shapers skill. He suggested other ways to test the shapers ability, like picking a blank that challenges the shaper to find rocker inside of the blank, ideas like that. I queried him about know how much time would they need to finish the board, what kind of tools should I allow them to use… all of these type of things. Chris gave me his insights and I built the shape-off around this insight. Chris is a legendary shaper and his insights we’re invaluable.**

**![](https://boardroomshow.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/christenson150x200.jpg)****A few months go by and I’m about to pull the trigger so to speak. I’m getting ready to send the big rent check over to the fairgrounds facility people. I’m pretty nervous — my children are eight and nine years old.  I’m sending over a significant amount of my money. I called two people: Rusty Preisendorfer and Matt Biolos. I wanted to get their opinion on doing something like this, and to see if I could in fact count on their participation. Luckily both Rusty and Matt enthusiastic about the idea and told me I could count on their participation. After those two phone calls I sent in the rent check — and crossed my fingers.**

**So those three guys Chris, Rusty and Matt were foundational exhibitors at the show. Chris was a judge in the very first Icons of Foam Tribute to the Master Shape off along with Steve Pezman and John Kies. That first year in 2007 we honored Mike Diffenderfer. Pez new Diff well, and more importantly knew Diff’s boards. John Kies had a shaping bay next to Dif for years and played golf with him. They were good friends.**

**That’s how the Boardroom Show started, in 2007, as Sacred Craft, in Del Mar, California.**

**This is just the quick history. There is much more to tell, but you’d have to be pretty bored to pull up chair and listen. We have a great friends, who turned into great staff, and my immediate family is involved.**

**If you’re interested in the Icons of Foam shapers whom we have honored over the years, and the contemporary shapers who have honored the icons, there is a page for that [here](https://boardroomshow.com/icons-of-foam/).**

**The goal of the show, when it started out in 2007 – and to this day – was to highlight the surfboard: the incredible designs, ideas, and craftsmanship of the modern day kahunas who engage in this creative space.**

**We’ve produced shows at the San Diego Convention Center, in Del Mar, in Huntington Beach during the U.S. Open, in Ventura, in Santa Cruz, in Orlando, Florida, in Costa Mesa, California and in 2019 we went to Tokyo and did a show right before COVID. We’ve had exhibitors go to fame at Shark Tank. Each year other core authentic surfing hardgoods brands exhibit alongside the surfboard builders. – artists too! Surfers love the shows because people love surfboards. They love what the surfboard builders bring to the show, incredible, high-quality, state-of-the-art craftsmanship. Authentic builders that live this life, that live this culture, that surf, and that shape. We realize that the surfboard is a philosophical icon of enduring youth. Pick up a new surfboard, put it under your arm and you will be 15 years old again. — SB**

About

# About

*   [Home](https://exposureskate.org/about/#)
*   About

![](https://exposureskate.org/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/Bodhi-Boul-Amelia.jpg)

OUR MISSION

## WHAt EXPOSURE Does

Exposure Skate is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit dedicated to empowering women and girls through skateboarding and teaching compassion through service. We offer a range of classes, camps, retreats, college scholarships and events for all ages which incorporate social and emotional learning through skateboarding, mindfulness and community service. Exposure’s unique programming creates an outlet for women, girls and nonbinary individuals to build confidence, community, education and healthy mental and physical well-being.

![](https://exposureskate.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/ornament-3.png)

![](https://exposureskate.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/ornament-4.png)

ORIGIN

## WHERE WE CAME FROM

Exposure 2012 was inspired by the **[Underexposed](https://www.amazon.com/Underexposed-Skateboarding-Documentary-Amelia-Brodka/dp/B00J49PLNE)** documentary, created by Exposure co-founder and Olympian Amelia Brodka, which highlighted the lack of opportunity for female skateboarders. At the time, women’s divisions had been cut from all major skate events, and the best female skateboarders in the world lacked support. The need to create space was crucial for both professional and amateur female skateboarders, as well as those looking to be introduced to skateboarding. Hosting competitions in park, street and vert disciplines, Exposure started as an annual skateboarding competition inclusive to women and girls from all over the globe. As the event grew, skaters traveled from as far as Japan, South Africa, Australia, Brazil, and across Europe to compete in the annual competition, growing the initial field of 32 female competitors to 230 competitors by 2020. The prize purse also saw substantial growth, and by 2016, Exposure offered the largest prize purse in women’s skateboarding. Legends such as Tony Hawk, Andrew Reynolds, Steve Caballero and Christian Hosoi regularly show their support on deck. Each year, the event supports survivors of domestic violence by spreading awareness and raising funds for the issue that disproportionately affects the girls, women and LGBTQ+ identifying communities we serve.

![](https://exposureskate.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/LesliInterview3-1024x683.jpg)

![](https://exposureskate.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/smiles-hand-in-the-air-group-pic-1-1024x665.jpg)

Storys

## MORE THAN COMPETITION

Lesli Cohen and Amelia Brodka created the nonprofit in order to feature year-round programming dedicated to empowerment through skateboarding and compassion through service. In addition to skateboarding, Exposure’s programs include elements of giving back to at-risk communities, social and emotional development, inclusion, leadership, service and college scholarship opportunities.

In 2016, Exposure’s youth program **[Skate Rising](https://exposureskate.org/skaterising/)** was launched, a program created to teach girls ages 4-18 a combination of skateboarding, mindfulness and community service. Each event includes a teachable moment where girls learn about communities in need or a way to practice self-case, participate in a project either dedicated to alleviating the community need or a mindfulness activity and enjoy a Learn-To-Skate Clinic taught by local and visiting Olympians and Pros. Nearly 100 girls attend each event, with each individual girl’s service project serving 1-3 individuals in need.

The adult **[Sesh(E)](https://streaklinks.com/B1T9mEk0dPxLYPo4DAktNqR8/https%3A%2F%2Fwww.exposureskate.org%2Fprograms%2F%23adult_skate_clinics)** program addresses the need to make skateparks inclusive spaces by offering free skateboarding guidance to women, trans and nonbinary skaters age 16+ in exchange for goods donated to the local domestic violence shelter. Exposure provides personalized instruction with professional skate coaches, skate gear and safety equipment at every youth and adult clinic.

In 2020, Exposure introduced its two annual $5,000 [**College Scholarships**](https://streaklinks.com/B1T9mEsRUZUHgpZHdw6eeAW9/https%3A%2F%2Fwww.exposureskate.org%2Fexposure-college-scholarship%2F) for skaters who actively contribute to the wellbeing of their communities. 

Exposure also brings community activations to schools, camps as well as existing events around the globe including X Games, Rockstar Energy Open, Vert Attack (Sweden) and Monster Skatepark (Australia). 

![](https://exposureskate.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/ornament-8.png)

![](https://exposureskate.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/ornament-4.png)

VIDEO PARTS

## SKateboard Media

In 2020 & 2021 Exposure partnered with Thrasher Magazine to create a first-of-its kind women’s video part competition, with a $50,00 prize purse (watch the **[2020 winners](https://streaklinks.com/BxtB_OeOjhjh61BwyApxNsGp/https%3A%2F%2Fwww.thrashermagazine.com%2Farticles%2Fvirtual-exposure-2020-video-winners%2F)** and **[2021 winners](https://streaklinks.com/BxtB_OapacGumML7ZwuoEjBV/https%3A%2F%2Fwww.thrashermagazine.com%2Farticles%2Fvideos%2Fvirtual-exposure-2021-video-winners%2F)** featured on Thrasher’s website). A field of 230 submissions from 23 different countries were judged by skateboarding legends Vanessa Torres, Elissa Steamer, Alex White, Mimi Knoop and Jamie Reyes. For the tenth anniversary of the flagship event, 2021’s Exposure X featured a red-carpet premiere of the video competition and an awards ceremony.

[2020 Winners](https://streaklinks.com/BxtB_OeOjhjh61BwyApxNsGp/https%3A%2F%2Fwww.thrashermagazine.com%2Farticles%2Fvirtual-exposure-2020-video-winners%2F)

[2021 Winners](https://www.thrashermagazine.com/articles/videos/virtual-exposure-2021-video-winners/)

![](https://exposureskate.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/E9B16D10-BAF2-4889-8D87-106E9B8C0769-1024x1024.jpg)

Skateboarding

## OLYMPIANS

The inclusion of Women’s Skateboarding in the 2020 Olympics has created a rise of non-male participants and supporters in and around the world. 60% of Women’s Skateboarding Olympians got their got their competitive start at Exposure. Today, a number of these individuals continue to compete in Exposure’s events as well as volunteer to teach at our Skate Rising and SeshE Programs.

![](https://exposureskate.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/ornament-3.png)

ABOUT

## THE BORN-FREE MOTORCYCLE SHOW

The Born-Free Motorcycle Show started back in 2009 when a couple of friends, MikeDavis and Grant Peterson, wanted to throw a get-together of vintage choppers in Orange County, California. Believe it or not, there weren’t any shows for bikes like ours back then!  
  
Born-Free’s meteoric rise quickly made it “the” place for old and young from all over the world to ride in, see, and talk about old iron for one day. Now, over 14 years later, it brings together over 25,000 eager spectators, participants, and over 200 vendors/sponsors, live music, Ives Brothers Wall of Death, the highly anticipated Invited Builder show, Special Guest Area, AMCAregional swapmeet, and more! The Born-Free Show is a back-to-basics show built on this impromptu action of people building and riding their vintage Harleys, Hondas, Indians, Triumphs (and more) into the show which then becomes “the show”.  
  
The show is open to all makes and models and is laid back with voluntary registration and a handful of awards and prizes, but this December, Best In Show gets a trip for themselves and their motorcycle to the Mooneyes Hot Rod & Custom show in Yokohama, Japan!  
  
Inside the show, there is a special Invited Builder area where 32 up-and-coming motorcycle builders from all around the world will be debuting the bikes they’ve been building just for this event over the past year. These builders are not cable TV stars but craftsmen, small shop owners, and garage builders who are doing their best to push themselves to build something unique, well thought out, and finely finished.  
  
Did we mention we have given away over 30 motorcycles in the history of the show? Yep, that’s right! Each year, we give away two or three new and old Harley-Davidsos to lucky show attendees who enter our drawing. A poster and ticket combo are for sale online. Must be present to win!  
  
For more info, visit our Facebook and Instagram for daily updates, Invited Buildervideos, and more. Born-Free is family-friendly, but there are no pets, coolers, or club colors allowed. Thanks for all the years of support and fun!  
  
—Mike and Grant

## FAQs TEXAS

Does Admission include camping?

Yes it does for Thursday, Friday, and Saturday nights. You find a suitable spot in the acres and acres of designated camping land and setup your own gear.

Will there be food available onsite?

Yes! We will be upping all food and drink quantities by 300 percent this year! We want for there to be no real reason to have to leave the property if you don’t need to. There will be some amazing BBQ smoked and prepared onsite by chef Rino! He’ll also be cooking breakfast and coffee. We will have food trucks during the day again as well, that fried boudin and the chicken strips were AMAZING!

Is there alcohol for sale or can I bring my own in?

Yes and yes! There will be a full bar menu at the Red Thorn Tavern as well as ice cold beer well into the night each night. The Red Thorn and also the “bowl” area of the property are considered a “private club” by the TACB so no outside alcohol is allowed in those areas, but the rest of the property is BYOB.

How do I reserve an RV space or a cabin?

You need to contact the staff at Yellow Rose Canyon to reserve these, www.yellowrosecanyon.com

THE BORN FREE MOTORCYCLE SHOW

## About our California show

The Born-Free Motorcycle Show started back in 2009 when a couple of friends, Mike Davis and Grant Peterson, wanted to throw a gathering of vintage choppers in Orange County, California. Believe it or not, there weren’t any shows for bikes like ours back then! Born-Free’s meteoric rise quickly made it “the” place old and young from all over the world to ride in, see, and talk about old iron for one day. Now, over 14 years later, it brings together over 25,000 eager spectators and participants and over 200 vendors/sponsors, live music, Ives Brothers Wall of Death, the highly anticipated Invited Builder show, Special Guest Area, AMCA regional swapmeet, and more!  
‍  
The Born-Free Show is a back-to-basics show built on this impromptu action of people building and riding their vintage Harleys, Hondas, Indians, Triumphs (and more) into the show, which then becomes “the show”. The show is open to all makes and models and is laid back with voluntary registration and a handful of awards and prizes, but Best In Show gets a trip for themselves and their motorcycle to the Mooneyes Hot Rod & Custom show in Yokohama, Japan, this December! Inside the show, there is a special Invited Builder area where 32 up-and-coming motorcycle builders from all around the world will be debuting the bikes they’ve been building just for this event over the past year. These builders are not cable TV stars but craftsmen, small shop owners, and garage builders doing their best to push themselves to build something unique, well thought out, and finely finished.  
  
Did we mention we have given away over 40 motorcycles in the history of the show? Yep, that’s right! Each year, we give away two or three new and old Harley-Davidsons to lucky show attendees who enter our drawing. A poster and ticket combo is for sale online. Must be present to win!  
‍  
For more info, visit our Facebook and Instagram for daily updates, Invited Builder videos, and more. Born-Free is family friendly, but there are no pets, coolers, or club colors allowed.  
  
Thanks for all the years of support and fun!  
\-Mike and Grant

# Flash Foxy Climbing Festival • BISHOP, CA

## March 13-15, 2026

Bishop is located within the lands traditionally known as Payahuunadu, which is the traditional ancestral homeland of the Nuumu and Newe.

Learn about the local [Bishop Paiute Tribe here.](https://www.flashfoxy.com/climbing-fest/bishop-paiute-tribe)

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/60dcd6d7fa1dbe2cd786c81b/56e98984-7d7a-49d8-ba21-9023866e3e84/peabodys+buttermilks.jpg)

#### For festival updates, [subscribe to our newsletter](https://www.flashfoxy.com/subscribe-newsletter) \+ follow us on Instagram [@heyflashfoxy](https://www.instagram.com/heyflashfoxy/).

Nestled in in beautiful Payahuunadu in the Eastern Sierras, Bishop not only offers world-class bouldering but also provides hundreds of sport climbing routes nearby. We work hard to make the Flash Foxy Climbing Festival a welcoming space for [women and genderqueer climbers](https://www.flashfoxy.com/about) of all levels to come together and celebrate all that climbing has to offer! This event is open to climbers of all ages and abilities.Our goal is to create and maintain a safe and diverse space where consent and respect are our first priorities. Harassment of any kind (unwanted contact, verbal or physical abuse, racism, homophobia, transphobia, body-shaming, etc.) will NOT be tolerated and will lead to being asked to leave. 

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/60dcd6d7fa1dbe2cd786c81b/916e6a2f-1dcf-4484-9eea-76bd513bb190/2024_FFCFBishop_LorClinic_%40jennflemm_1.jpg)

# Goals Achieved

#### CREATING COMMUNITY

We’ve reached more than 2,500 climbers since the start of the festival. Climbers have traveled from 36 states and territories and 3 countries. They’ve ranged in age from infants + children to folks over 70 years-old! Our festivals have sold out within minutes and have had over 500 climbers on the waitlist.

#### SUPpORTING THE TOWN OF BISHOP

We partner closely with 20 local small businesses and organizations as well as the Bishop Chamber of Commerce. Excluding the payment given to athletes, facilitators, panelists, photographers and other professionals involved with the festival, we are also able to spend ~80% of our budget locally, giving back into the local economy.

#### WOMEN + GENDERQUEER CLIMBERS TEACHING EACH OTHER

Each year we host outdoor clinics at the festival, all are led by women and genderqueer athletes and guides. In addition, we host multiple workshops, yoga sessions and panels, all led by women and genderqueer facilitators, instructors, and panelists.

#### CONTRIBUTING TO INCREASE ACCESS AND MINIMIZE IMPACT

With generous raffle donations from our sponsors, we raise money at every festival for local conservation organizations, Indigenous Tribes and our scholarship fund. We also partner with local conservation organization, Friends of the Inyo, to co-host a stewardship day on Sunday at every festival.

Since 2016, we've raised a total of **over $30,000** at our festivals! These funds have gone to Friends of the Inyo, the Access Fund, Bishop Area Climbers Coalition, Bishop Paiute Tribe, and the Flash Foxy Scholarship Fund.

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/60dcd6d7fa1dbe2cd786c81b/147499e9-0cd6-4b5e-bd39-56a8a49d8464/2024_FFCFBishop_ASSIGNMENT_%40pterrellyn-.jpg)

# Climbing Areas

**FREE access to KAYA Digital Guidebook!** [Fill out this link](https://kayaclimb.typeform.com/to/vW8jDe09) by March 12th!!

*   Happy Boulders
    
    **Google Maps:** [Happy Boulders](https://www.google.com/maps/place/Happy+Boulders/@37.4136384,-118.4498369,17z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m5!3m4!1s0x80be1724ed0d748d:0x87b6e022100d8048!8m2!3d37.4136384!4d-118.4476482)
    
    [**Mountain Project Link**](https://www.mountainproject.com/area/105799640/happy-boulders)
    
    The Happy Boulders has climbs of all shapes and sizes on friendly volcanic rock. This is a great place for newer boulderers to explore Bishop climbing!
    
    **Approach + Trail Surface:** moderate-steep uphill 0.5-1.0 miles on _soft sand._ Trails between climbing areas are mixed terrain including low flat boulders, packed sand and soft sand.
    
    **Directions:** The Happy Boulders can be accessed by two different routes out of Bishop. From Main Street (395) you can take the junction for Highway 6. Then turn left onto Five Bridges Road and continue until you reach the intersection at which you will turn left onto Chalk Bluff road. Continue down Chalk Bluff road for 2.3 miles until you reach the Happy Boulder parking. From Main Street (395) continue north out of Bishop as if you were driving to Mammoth. Turn Right onto Pleasant Valley Dam Road and continue on it until you get past the County campground. Turn right onto Chalk Bluff road and continue for about 3.6 miles until you reach the Happy Boulders parking area.
    
*   Buttermilk Boulders
    
    **Google Maps:** [Buttermilks](https://www.google.com/maps/place/Buttermilk+Boulders/@37.3273988,-118.5777763,17z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m5!3m4!1s0x80be18a567a5c6f7:0xd19904fdcac7b5a7!8m2!3d37.3273988!4d-118.5755876)
    
    [**Mountain Project Link**](https://www.mountainproject.com/area/106132808/buttermilks-main)
    
    The Buttermilks hosts iconic boulders beneath large beautiful mountains. The rock is sharp, the landings are flat, and the boulders tend to be pretty tall. This area is best for folks with a bit more bouldering experience.
    
    **Approach + Trail Surface:** mild-moderate uphill 0.25-0.5 miles on packed dirt/sand/gravel mix. Trails between boulders are packed dirt/sand/gravel mix
    
    **Directions:** Turn off State Route 168 about 7 miles west of Bishop onto Buttermilk Road. There is parking available along the roadside. The Department of Water and Power land is closed to camping. Inquire at the White Mountain Ranger Station for camping information and a map. DRIVE SLOW on Buttermilk Road, it has been known to crack oil pans of low clearance speeding vehicles
    
*   Owens River Gorge
    
    **Google Maps:**[Owens River Gorge](https://www.mountainproject.com/area/105843226/owens-river-gorge)
    
    [**Mountain Project Link**](https://www.mountainproject.com/area/105843226/owens-river-gorge)
    
    The Owens River Gorge has sport climbs on volcanic tuff that shines in the 5.10 and up grades, although there are also ample options in the lower-grade ranges. The approach can be arduous and steep, and often includes river crossings. The central and upper gorge are better suited to intermediate/advanced climbers. The lower gorge has better options for newer climbers.
    
    **Approach + Trail Surface:** mild-steep terrain 0.5-1.0 miles. Length and difficulty of approaches vary. Trail surfaces include: packed dirt roads, large steep gravel stairs, scrambling over large boulders on steep terrain and crossing rivers using logs as bridges.
    
    **Directions:** From Bishop go North on 395 to the Paradise Swall Meadows exit and turn right. Go approximately 1/2 mile and at the T intersection turn left (Gorge Rd). There are 3 parking areas to choose depending on where in the Gorge you wish to climb. The first parking area is 3.3 miles from the intersection of Gorge road and 395. Adjacent to the parking area you will go through a gate and follow the paved central gorge power station road for 1 mile down to the Central gorge power station. The second parking area also accesses the central gorge and ends just uphill from the central gorge power station. You will find a trail adjacent to the parking area that goes down a steep 2nd/3rd class loose gully. Be careful not to dislodge anything because there are climbs below the gully. This parking area is 4.8 miles up the Gorge road from the intersection of Gorge Road and 395. The last parking area is for the upper gorge. This parking area is 6.4 miles up Gorge Road from the intersection of Gorge Road and 395. You will park off the pavement and walk through a gate down the paved upper power plant road approximately 1/2 mile then drop into a 3rd class gully. There is a trail along the entire length of the bottom of the gorge so you can use any of the access points to access all climbs at Owens.
    
*   Alabama Hills
    
    **Google Maps:** [Alabama Hills](https://www.google.com/maps/place/Alabama+Hills,+Lone+Pine,+CA+93545/@36.5677108,-118.0985859,15z/data=!4m6!3m5!1s0x80bf860c0b2bf5ad:0xfef098e3ab75953d!8m2!3d36.5677116!4d-118.0898097!16s%2Fm%2F048b1yq)
    
    [**Mountain Project Link**](https://www.mountainproject.com/area/105876822/alabama-hills)
    
    The Alabama Hills sits beneath Mount Whitney and hosts gorgeous views of the Eastern Sierra. You’ll find sport bolted granite climbing on beautiful, brown patina with minimal approaches. This area is excellent for beginner and intermediate climbers!
    
    **Approach + Trail Surface:** many areas can be approached within 100ft of parking. Some areas may have longer approaches and may depend on road conditions. Trail surface is packed dirt/sand with occasional scrambling to access specific climbs.
    
    **Directions:** Take Whitney Portal Road off US 395 to this area. Most of the climbing is accessed from Movie Road, which heads north from the Whitney Portal Road.
    

# Venues

## \+ Accessibility

*   Accessiblity
    
    All primary festival event venues (opening party, open air market, film screenings, panels) will be held at wheelchair accessible venues and will have accessible bathrooms. The Opening Party and Foxy Fair take place outside in a flat grassy field with paved paths. Film screenings, panel, dinner and other activities will take place in the Heritage Arts Building at the [Tri-County Fairgrounds](https://tricountyfair.com/wp/) - this building is ground-level. The Community Slideshow will take place at [Mountain Rambler Brewery](https://www.mountainramblerbrewery.com/) \- this building is ground-level. Seating will be available during all events.
    
    All films will have captions in English. ASL interpreters can be coordinated upon request. Please email events@flashfoxy.com to discuss your needs.
    
    Approaches differ by climbing area. Details about approaches can be found below, or can be found on [Mountain Project](https://www.mountainproject.com/area/106064825/bishop-area).
    
    **Have an accessibility concern? Reach out to events@flashfoxy.com** and we’ll see how we can help!
    
    We are always working to make the Flash Foxy Climbing Festival a more inclusive and welcoming space, please let us know what we can do to make our event more accessible for you. Unfortunately, we are not always able to arrange accommodations, but we will do our best and will provide honest answers about the our event spaces, staff capabilities and the activities that take place at our festivals. Thank you for learning and growing with us!
    
*   Tri-County Fairgrounds (Primary venue)
    
    **Google Maps:** [Tri-County Fairgrounds](https://www.google.com/maps/place/Eastern+Sierra+Tri-County+Fair/@37.3730618,-118.4018057,17z/data=!4m6!3m5!1s0x80be1605e29691ff:0x262875cedcfe1fac!8m2!3d37.3733062!4d-118.3990173!16s%2Fg%2F1tcxdg6d?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI0MTEwNS4wIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D)
    
    **About the venue:** All of our Saturday programming, with the exception of clinics, and our Sunday morning programming will take place at the Eastern Sierra Tri-County Fairgrounds. The Open Air Market and Workshops will take place in a grassy field, other outdoor programming takes place in parking lots. Film screenings, panel, dinner and other activities will take place in the Heritage Arts Building - this building is ground-level and has accessible bathrooms.
    
    **Directions:** Turn west on to Sierra Street from US 395 in Downtown Bishop, drive 2 blocks and turn right into the Fairgrounds under the front gate arch. There is a large parking lot with marked accessible parking spaces available.
    
*   Eastside Student Center (Friday morning)
    
    **Google Maps:** [**Eastside Student Center**](https://maps.app.goo.gl/B2BrF6suVm6ZoSx16)
    
    **About the venue:** Friday Climber Coffee will take place at The Eastside Student Center. This building is ground-level. Bathroom is not wheelchair accessible.
    
    **Parking:** There are multiple parking lots and street parking.
    
*   Owens Valley Paiute-Shoshone Cultural Center (Sunday morning)
    
    **Google Maps:** [Owens Valley Paiute-Shoshone Cultural Center](https://maps.app.goo.gl/ga7LrCfVumcnkwdf9)
    
    **About the venue:** All Sunday morning programming will take place at The Owens Valley Paiute-Shoshone Cultural Center. This building is wheelchair accessible with wheelchair accessible bathrooms.
    
    **Parking:** Accessible parking is available in the parking lot.
    
*   Mountain Rambler Brewery (Sunday evening)
    
    **Google Maps:** [Mountain Rambler Brewery](https://www.google.com/maps/place/Mountain+Rambler+Brewery/@37.3606119,-118.3945062,15z/data=!4m2!3m1!1s0x0:0xd5942f9aab9c9939?sa=X&ved=1t:2428&ictx=111)
    
    **About the venue:** Friday Climber Coffee and our Sunday Community Slideshow will take place at Mountain Rambler Brewery. This building is ground-level and has accessible bathrooms. The venue is often dark, loud, and crowded. Seating is available both indoors and outdoors.
    
    **Directions:** Located on Main Street near the traffic light at the intersection of E/W Line Street. The brewery is located in a small parking lot which can be accessed via Short Street.
    
    **Parking:** Accessible parking is available in the parking lot. All other Flash Foxy participants should use street parking. The parking lot is very small and needs to be shared with local patrons of all businesses in the parking lot. Thank you for your cooperation!
    

#### EVENT PERMITS

*   Flash Foxy Climbing Festival Clinics operate under permit on the Inyo National Forest.

(Not all prohibited bases apply to all programs.) Persons with disabilities who require alternative means of communication for program information (e.g., Braille, large print, audiotape, American Sign Language, etc.) should contact the responsible State or local Agency that administers the program or USDA’s TARGET Center at (202) 720-2600 (voice and TTY) or contact USDA through the Federal Relay Service at (800) 877-8339. Additionally, program information is also available in languages other than English.
    
    To file a complaint alleging discrimination, complete the USDA Program Discrimination Complaint Form, AD-3027, found online at http://www.ascr.usda.gov/complaint\_filing\_cust.html, or at any USDA office or write a letter addressed to USDA and provided in the letter all of the information requested in the form. To request a copy of the complaint form, call (866) 632-9992. Submit your completed form or letter to USDA by: (a) mail: U.S. Department of Agriculture Office of the Assistant Secretary for Civil Rights, 1400 Independence Avenue, SW, Washington, D.C. 20250-9410; (b) fax: (202) 690-7442; or (c) email: program.intake@usda.gov.

## FAQs California

Do I need a Grass Pass? How do I enter my bike in the show?

If you want to park your bike inside the show on the grass either or both days you need a “Grass Pass” wristband for the days you want to be there. If you have a passenger they need a Grass Pass as well. You also get in early with a Grass Pass so you can get a great place to park. Get them online from us HERE or in person at events. Stay tuned to our socials to see what those events might be. If your bike is on the grass inside the show it is also eligible to win any awards, including Best in Show!  
‍  
Grass Pass Wristbands sell FAST! We only can sell a fixed amount due to the size of the property, so they absolutely DO sell out each year. We have been releasing them in batches online and in person, usually starting in January. They can go in a matter of minutes online, so plan accordingly. Watch our socials or sign up for our mailing list for alerts HERE.

Do I need a “ticket”?

There is no entry “ticket” for walk-in spectators, simply pay at the gate. If you want to enter to win any of the motorcycles being given away at the show please read on. We do not presell general admission and it DOES NOT sell out, just Grass Pass Wristbands.

Does General Admission sellout?

No, you simply show up and purchase onsite. Cash is highly recommended at the gate! There is an ATM, but can’t always count on it and digital currency is not accepted for this.  
Kids 12 and under are FREE.  
‍  
Active and retired military are FREE with ID, this is for general admission only.

How do I win a motorcycle?

To have a chance to win any or all of the (generally 2-4) motorcycles being given away at Born-Free each year, you need to purchase a poster that comes with a free ticket to enter, must be present to win! They are $20 each and you can buy as many as you’d like to raise your already good odds of winning. Get your poster/ticket combo(s) online from us HERE until mid June each year. Please note, this is not admission to the show, just entering you in the giveaways.

What can I win?

We generally give away at least one vintage Harley-Davidson, such as a Knucklehead, Panhead, or Shovelhead, sometimes two! We also usually have a fully built to the hilt custom FXR by San Diego Customs. We will update the site and socials when we have the current giveaways.  
‍  
If you can’t make it for some reason and have entered, please give your ticket to a friend that will represent you. If you are not present, we will wait 5 minutes before pulling another potential winner for each motorcycle until someone is there. We will also have many giveaways online during the year via our Instagram page as well as more consolation prizes at the show.

What is not allowed at Born-Free?

You cannot bring: coolers, alcohol, pets of any kind, weapons, MC club colors (patches or shirts), or outside food.

Participate in local and year-round Burning Man events — in your home community, and in more than 30 countries around the world. Start small, or go big — whatever works for you.

## A Global Movement

[Join a Session](https://burningman.org/black-rock-city/black-rock-city-2027/#important-dates)

### Apply for a BRC Art Grant

[Learn About Grants](https://burningman.org/black-rock-city/bring-your-art/art-grants-programs/brc-honoraria/)

### Join a Fly Ranch Nature Walk

[Register for a Walk](https://events.ticketleap.com/tickets/blackrockdesert/fly-ranch-nature-walks-2026)

### Burning Man is Built By You

Burning Man is not something you attend — it’s something you do. Your support for the nonprofit funds Honoraria art, makes Black Rock City tickets accessible to more people, and nurtures a more creative, connected world.

# About Us

**flash fox·y** \\‘flash ˈfäk-sē \\ - to flash or send a climb on your first try but to do it with your own style and swagger

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/60dcd6d7fa1dbe2cd786c81b/a02487ad-a245-441a-8ae4-d4370b9cdb63/2022_FFCFNorthConway_Affinityclimb14_%40jennflemm.jpg)

Flash Foxy originated to empower women climbers and offer a virtual space to connect over climbing, being outside together, and building community. The inaugural Women’s Climbing Festival in 2016 helped us establish an alternate climbing space in real life that did not center cisgender men. 

The climbing community is not static and Flash Foxy has adapted over the years to meet the needs of its membership as they grow, change and continue to self-actualize. **Presently, Flash Foxy stands with women and genderqueer climbers** - including trans and gender non-conforming folks - who need a space to pursue their love of the sport without having to deal with historic barriers to access.

_Still not sure if Flash Foxy is for you? Check out our_ [_FAQs._](https://www.flashfoxy.com/faq)

## Our Mission

Our Mission is to provide accessible resources, opportunities and welcoming spaces for our climbing community through events and education programs. Originally created to celebrate women climbing with women, our community has grown to include a range of gender expressions and gender identities amongst our membership and leadership teams.

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/60dcd6d7fa1dbe2cd786c81b/94c8ff36-6ca6-487c-b489-50f731f0d114/climbing+rope.png)

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/60dcd6d7fa1dbe2cd786c81b/a389e02f-9552-406b-9336-b768252e8e5a/2026_FFCFBishop_FRIDAY+MEETUPS_catlikeacat-1.jpg)

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/60dcd6d7fa1dbe2cd786c81b/4649f871-0caa-4025-b8c8-d6c232992dd6/2026_FFCFBishop_MULTIPITCH+MAGIC_catlikeacat-13.jpg)

## Our Vision

Flash Foxy is committed to uplifting all community members that disrupt normalcy and need a space to connect away from narratives that tell them they don’t belong. We will continue to build sustainable spaces for women and genderqueer folks and use climbing as a means for change. We hold the belief that no one is “self-made” and therefore Flash Foxy is committed to being in conversation with other anti-oppressive organizations to disseminate knowledge and power, work collaboratively and normalize being transparent in the outdoors industry.

If you want to climb and work on building intentional community, this can be a space for you and your voice to matter, to be present, seen and heard.

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/60dcd6d7fa1dbe2cd786c81b/abe876e0-87da-469a-963b-aa8f66ecfb3e/mammoth.png)

### No Wasted Days: Flash Foxy

A 2024 Arc’teryx short film about how Flash Foxy is making space for women and genderqueer climbers at the crag.

When they first started climbing, Lou (they/he) and Marian (they/them) didn’t see opportunities for those within the genderqueer community to go into the outdoors. So, they decided to become guides, share their knowledge, and open doors for others to experience the exhilaration of moving freely.

They also plan some climbing festivals along the way ;)

# GENERAL INFORMATION ⚡️ TICKETS ⚡️ VENUE ⚡️ PROGRAM ⚡️ SCHEDULE ⚡️

### GENERAL INFORMATION

*   What is The One Motorcycle Show?
    
    The One Motorcycle Show is an annual celebration of motorcycles, art, and community. It’s a vibrant gathering that showcases unique and custom motorcycles from builders across the globe alongside art installations, live music, and a diverse array of vendors.
    
*   When and where does the show take place?
    
    **The One Motorcycle Show PORTLAND** is happening Friday, May 1st - Sunday, May 3rd, 2026 at the historic Zidell Yards located at [3121 S Moody Ave Portland, OR 97239](https://maps.app.goo.gl/GG4qvMvaTXH381r67). This will be our sixth year at this venue.
    
    **Portland Show Hours**
    
    5/1/2026: 9 AM - 10 PM
    
    5/2/2026: 9 AM - 10 PM
    
    5/3/2026: 9 AM - 3 PM
    
*   Is the show family-friendly?
    
    Yes, the event is open to all ages. There's a diverse range of activities and displays suitable for motorcycle enthusiasts of all ages. Kids aged 10 and under receive free admission when accompanied by an adult. Day time sessions are recommended for families, but the show allows all ages at all hours of the event.
    
*   Are pets allowed at the show?
    
    Pets, with the exception of service animals, are generally not allowed inside the event venue due to safety and space considerations.
    
*   Will there be food and drinks available at the show?
    
    Yes, there are food vendors offering a variety of options, along with beverage options to keep attendees refreshed throughout the event.
    
    If you’re interested in applying to be a market or food vendor at one of our shows, check out the latest info at [**the1moto.com/get-involved**](https://www.the1moto.com/get-involved) or click [**HERE.**](https://www.the1moto.com/get-involved)
    
*   Are there accommodations nearby for out-of-town visitors?
    
    There are several hotels, motels, and Airbnb options in the vicinity of the show venues. It's recommended to book accommodations in advance due to high demand.
    
    Check out the latest hotel partner info for Portland [**HERE**](https://www.the1moto.com/hotels).
    
*   Is there parking available at the event?
    
    Parking availability can vary. Attendees are encouraged to consider riding their bike, carpooling or using public transportation if possible, as parking spaces may fill up quickly. Motorcycle parking is free, first come first served and located near the main entrance. Check back closer to the show dates for an up-to-date map.
    
*   Is the venue ADA accessible?
    
    Yes, although it is not an ideal space for wheelchairs as there is not any sidewalk. There are ramps to all elevated spaces within the venue, but due to the nature of the industrial building and the outdoor areas around it, please be aware that there are many areas at the event venue with uneven ground.
    
*   Do you have ADA / handicap parking available?
    
    Limited accessible parking options are available on site near the main show entrance, first come first serve. Our parking attendants will help get you there. We will also have ADA-compliant restrooms available.
    
*   Are there any prohibited items?
    
    **Prohibited Items**
    
    NO WEAPONS OF ANY KIND – Including Firearms, Pocket Knives, Pepper Spray, tasers, etc.
    
    These items will be confiscated via Local Authorities and Security. 
    
    ❌ Backpacks, Purses, or Bags larger than 14″ x 14″ 
    
    ❌ Illegal Substances, Drugs or Drug Paraphernalia
    
    ❌ Unsealed Over the Counter Medications or Vitamins
    
    ❌ Animals (except service animals)
    
    ❌ Outside alcohol
    
    ❌ Fireworks, open fires, flammable products, projectiles, or explosives
    
    ❌ Drones or Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs).
    
    ❌ Glass of any kind
    
    ❌ Lasers or pointer devices
    
    ❌ Tactical Gear, Walkie Talkies, etc.
    
    ❌ Items deemed as posing a threat to the safe enjoyment of the One Motorcycle Show by management.
    

### SUBMISSIONS

*   Can I bring my motorcycle to display at the show?
    
    The show welcomes submissions from builders who want to display their custom motorcycles.
    
    More information for how to submit your bike for consideration can be found [**HERE**](https://www.the1moto.com/get-involved) or visit [**the1moto.com/get-involved**](https://the1moto.com/get-involved).
    
*   When will I hear back about my bike being accepted or not?
    
    We will be making our official decisions in the next coming weeks and will communicate bikes that will be accepted to display in the show via email. Official physical invites will be sent via the ol' postman. We will get back to you with our decision and official invites as soon as we can!
    
*   How can I submit a helmet for the 21 Helmets showcase?
    
    For those interested in showcasing their helmet in the 21 Helmets showcase, drop a message to [**thor@theonemoto.com**](mailto:thor@theonemoto.com?subject=21%20Helmets) & he’ll provide further details and guidelines on how to submit your helmet for potential display.
    
*   How can I submit my band?
    
    If you think your band belongs on our radar, please reach out to [**mahala@theonemoto.com**](mailto:mahala@theonemoto.com?subject=One%20Moto%20Music%20Inquiry).
    
*   Is photography allowed at The One Motorcycle Show?
    
    Yes, general photography is permitted. However, out of consideration for other attendees, please be mindful when taking photos. By entering The One Motorcycle Show, attendees consent to being photographed, filmed, and/or recorded. Official photographers and media representatives can apply for an official press badge, granting access to exclusive events. More information [HERE](https://www.the1moto.com/media) on how to apply or at [**the1moto.com/media**](https://the1moto.com/media).
    

### SHOW SCHEDULE

*   Will there be any offsite events, parties or racing?
    
    Yes, offsite events and after parties will be listed in the full weekend schedule. Check back closer to show dates! If you’re interested in partnering on a good time, hit up [**info@theonemoto.com**](mailto:info@theonemoto.com?subject=Inquiry%20-%20Offsite%20Events%2C%20Parties%2C%20Racing)!
    
*   What bands will be playing at The One Motorcycle Show this year?
    
    Check back soon!
    

### TICKETS

*   How can I attend The One Motorcycle Show?
    
    Tickets for The One Motorcycle Show can be purchased online [**HERE**](https://www.tixr.com/groups/1moto) or at the door (ticket prices increase at the door).
    
*   Can I get a refund?
    
    Refunds are available until the day of the show. For assistance with refunds, please send an email to [**support@tixr.com**](mailto:support@tixr.com?). They will be able to assist you with the refund process.
    
*   Can I change the name on my ticket?
    
    Unfortunately, name changes on tickets are not allowed at this time.
    
*   Can I transfer my ticket to another person?
    
    Currently, ticket transfers to another individual are not permitted.
    
*   Can I resell my ticket?
    
    We do not support the resale of tickets.
    

### ONLINE SHOP

#### Refund Policy

*   What is your policy on refunds, returns, and exchanges?
    
    We accept returns within 30 days after delivery if the item is unused and in its original condition. We will refund the full order amount, minus the shipping costs for the return. In case your order arrives damaged, please contact us at info@theonemoto.com with your order number and a photo of the item's condition for a case-by-case assessment.
    
*   Are there any items that cannot be returned or exchanged?
    
    Products on sale are not eligible for return or exchange.
    
*   Who covers the return shipping costs?
    
    The buyer is responsible for return shipping costs. Original shipping fees are non-refundable.
    
*   How long does it take to process a refund?
    
    Refunds may take 2-7 days to process after we receive and approve the return, depending on your payment method and credit card company.
    

#### Shipping

*   How long does it take to process and ship my order?
    
    All orders are processed within 2 to 5 business days, excluding weekends and holidays. After your order is confirmed, you will receive a shipping notification. Delivery times vary but typically take 5-10 business days, depending on your location.
    
*   What are the shipping rates and how are they calculated?
    
    We offer free shipping for orders over $50. For orders under $50, shipping charges are calculated and displayed at checkout based on your order size and shipping destination.
    
*   How can I track the status of my order?
    
    Once your order has shipped, you will receive an email with a tracking number. You can use this number to check the status of your delivery. Please allow 48 hours for the tracking information to become available.
    
*   Do you offer a local pick-up option?
    
    Yes, we offer local pick-up at One Moto Cafe, 1642 NE Sandy Blvd., Portland, OR 97232. Select the local pick-up option at checkout, and we will notify you by email when your order is ready for pick-up, usually within 2 to 5 business days.

# festival FAQ

#### What festivals does flash foxy offer?

We have THREE 2026 climbing festivals:

*   [Flash Foxy Climbing Festival in Bishop](https://www.flashfoxy.com/climbing-fest), CA (March)
    
*   [Flash Foxy Mini Fest in Red River Gorge](https://www.flashfoxy.com/mini-fest-ky), KY (May)
    
*   [Flash Foxy Mini Fest in Gunks](https://www.flashfoxy.com/mini-fest-ny), NY (October)
    

#### do you have event specific faqs?

Yes! Please follow the links below:

*   [FAQ - Flash Foxy Climbing Festival in Bishop](https://www.flashfoxy.com/climbing-fest/faq)
    
*   [FAQ - Flash Foxy Mini Fest in Red River Gorge](https://www.flashfoxy.com/mini-fest-ky/faq)
    
*   [FAQ - Flash Foxy Mini Fest in Gunks](https://www.flashfoxy.com/mini-fest-ny/faq)
    

#### Do I have to be an experienced rock climber to attend flash foxy festivals?

**Not at all!** We welcome women and genderqueer folks of all climbing experience levels – including none. There will be several intro and beginning clinics and workshops. The festival will be a great opportunity to try out climbing in a safe and supportive environment.

#### Do I need to register to attend flash foxy festivals?

**Yes.** Registration is required to attend Flash Foxy festivals. Learn more about specific event registration:

*   [Flash Foxy Climbing Festival in Bishop](https://www.flashfoxy.com/climbing-fest/registration)
    
*   [Flash Foxy Mini Fest in Red River Gorge](https://www.flashfoxy.com/mini-fest-ky/registration)
    
*   [Flash Foxy Mini Fest in Gunks](https://www.flashfoxy.com/mini-fest-ny/registration)
    

#### Why are there different levels of ticket pricing?

We strongly believe in keeping the festival affordable so that folks of all situations who love climbing can attend which is why we have a **“pay more if you are willing and able”** model.  Each event has a “Standard” ticket price as well as options for Pay-it-forward and Lower-cost tickets. If you feel that you can afford the higher price and would like to help offset the costs for other participants, please select a Pay-it-forward Festival Pass. Lower-cost Passes are directly funded by Pay-it-forward Passes and are released as funded. Each event also has full scholarships available and opportunities to volunteer.

#### Are scholarships available for flash foxy festivals?

**Yes!** A limited number of full scholarships, and occasionally travel stipends, are available for Flash Foxy festivals. See individual event registration pages for more details.

*   [Flash Foxy Climbing Festival in Bishop](https://www.flashfoxy.com/climbing-fest/registration)
    
*   [Flash Foxy Mini Fest in Red River Gorge](https://www.flashfoxy.com/mini-fest-ky/registration)
    
*   [Flash Foxy Mini Fest in Gunks](https://www.flashfoxy.com/mini-fest-ny/registration)
    

#### Who can attend flash foxy festival?

Flash Foxy welcomes **women and genderqueer climbers** to join us at the Flash Foxy Trad Fest. We use “genderqueer” as an umbrella term for all folks of non-dominant genders. Still not sure if this space is for you? We’ve got [more FAQs about who Flash Foxy is for](https://www.flashfoxy.com/faq).

This is an **all-ages** event and young children are encouraged to attend with a guardian! If you are a guardian for a young climber who wants to attend, please email us at events@flashfoxy.com.

Our goal is to create and maintain a safe and diverse space where consent and respect are our first priorities. Harassment of any kind (unwanted contact, verbal or physical abuse, racism, homophobia, transphobia, body-shaming, etc.) will NOT be tolerated and will lead to being asked to leave.

#### Can I get a refund if I can't attend the event?

**Unfortunately, we can NOT offer refunds.** However, we truly understand that circumstances can change and that you probably want your money back. **While we cannot offer refunds, we strive to facilitate ticket transfers whenever possible!** You must find someone who wants your ticket (tag us in your stories or post in our Facebook group for help finding someone!). If tickets sell out and a waitlist forms, we can offer ticket transfers to folks on the waitlist. Please note that as the festival date approaches, processing refunds and ticket transfers becomes more challenging.

The deadline to request a ticket transfers is Friday, March 7th. If you've purchased a pass but find yourself unable to attend, please contact us right away at events@flashfoxy.com.

#### are festivals rain or shine?

**Yes, our festivals are rain or shine!** Regardless of the weather, we will have a good time! We cannot guarantee access to climbing or any specific climbing areas. Part of climbing outdoors is respecting the land and learning to make the best of whatever Mother Nature throws our way!

We cannot guarantee weather conditions, crag conditions, or any other element of climbing, road, or trail access. There are **no refunds**.

#### Where can I find information about the accessibility of venues + programming?

Information about venues and accessibility can be found at the bottom of individual event pages.

*   [Flash Foxy Climbing Festival in Bishop](https://www.flashfoxy.com/climbing-fest)
    
*   [Flash Foxy Mini Fest in Red River Gorge](https://www.flashfoxy.com/mini-fest-ky)
    
*   [Flash Foxy Mini Fest in Gunks](https://www.flashfoxy.com/mini-fest-ny)
    

ASL Interpretation can be coordinated upon request. All films will have captions in English. Please email [events@flashfoxy.com](mailto:events@flashfoxy.com?subject=ASL%20Interpreter%20Request%20-%20Trad%20Fest) to coordinate.

**Have an accessibility concern? Reach out to** [**events@flashfoxy.com**](mailto:events@flashfoxy.com?subject=Accessibility%20Question%20-%20Trad%20Fest) and we can discuss your needs and see how we can help!

We are always working to make the Flash Foxy festivals more inclusive and welcoming spaces, please let us know what we can do to make our event more accessible for you. Unfortunately, we are not always able to arrange accommodations, but we will do our best and will provide honest answers about our event spaces, staff capabilities, and the activities that take place at our festivals. Thank you for learning and growing with us!

#### What’s your Covid-19 Plan?

All festival attendees **must have received a minimum of 1 dose of any COVID-19 vaccine** to attend any Flash Foxy event. **To request a vaccine exemption\* please email events@flashfoxy.com.**

\*Vaccine exemptions will only be granted to those with medical conditions preventing them from receiving a vaccine. Vaccine exemptions must be requested within 48 hours of ticket purchase and at least 2 weeks prior to the event. All unvaccinated attendees with approved exemptions must present proof of a negative COVID-19 test (PCR or at-home test) within 24 hours of the event at registration.

**Face masks will be optional at all indoor programs. Face masks will be available on-site.**

Additionally, we request that if you are sick - even if it’s not Covid - that you stay home. We don’t like missing events any more than you do, but we also really don’t like being sick. We especially don’t like putting our immunocompromised community members at risk. If you’re recovering from illness or think you might be getting sick… consider wearing a mask in all group settings <3

**If we have to cancel** any Flash Foxy event or program due to rising Covid-19 cases or other national emergency ticket holders will have the following refund options:

*   50% Refund (standard policy if no action taken by ticket holder)
    
*   100% Refund (by email request to events@flashfoxy.com)
    
*   Donate full ticket price to Flash Foxy
    

We ask ticket holders who have the financial ability to keep in mind that the majority of our festival expenses are fixed and non-refundable (employee salaries, insurance, perishable goods, deposits, etc). We greatly appreciate our community and your on-going support. 

**If changes in your personal circumstances** related to Covid-19 affect your comfort levels with attending the festival, we may be able to facilitate a ticket transfer. We cannot guarantee ticket transfers. No Refunds.

**If you have a positive Covid-19 test or contact** with someone with a confirmed or suspected case of Covid-19 within one week of the festival we ask that you do not attend. Please inform us immediately and we will do our best to facilitate a ticket transfer. We cannot guarantee ticket transfers. No Refunds.

**Our Covid-19 plan may be updated at any time.**

* * *

**If you've gone through everything and still can't find what you're looking for, no problem!**

Just drop us an email at [events@flashfoxy.com](mailto:events@flashfoxy.com?) or fill out our [**Contact Form**](https://www.flashfoxy.com/contact)
