# FESTIVAL FAQ

#### Flash Foxy Climbing Festival • BISHOP • March 13-15, 2026

#### What is the Flash Foxy Climbing Festival?

**Flash Foxy Climbing Festival is a three-day event that brings together and celebrates the growing community of women and genderqueer climbers.** The inaugural Women’s Climbing Festival in February 2016 helped us establish an alternative climbing space in real life that did not center cisgender men. After a two year hiatus due to COVID-19, we came back in 2022 as the Flash Foxy Climbing Festival with an expanded mission to serve women and gender non-conforming (GNC) folks ! We hope that the Flash Foxy Climbing Festival will not only reach experienced climbers but also provide a safe space for beginner climbers to come and learn more about all that climbing has to offer! Check out [**OUR PHOTO ALBUMS**](https://www.flashfoxy.com/climbing-fest/photos) to see what it looks like when hundreds of women and genderqueer folks gather in the desert for a weekend of community + climbing.

\*_The Flash Foxy Climbing Festival was formerly known as the Women’s Climbing Festival_

#### When is the festival?

The 2025 Flash Foxy Climbing Festival will take place the weekend of **March 15-17, 2024**.

#### Where is the festival located?

The festival is located in **Bishop, California**. If you’ve never been to Bishop, check out our recommendations for [Lodging + Local Beta](https://www.flashfoxy.com/climbing-fest/lodging). We even made you this sample [Desert Packing List](https://www.flashfoxy.com/desert-packing-list) to help make sure you’re warm enough, cool enough, and watered enough out here!

Festival events will be occurring in several locations throughout the town of Bishop as well as at several climbing areas. Specific event locations will be listed on the [Schedule of Events](https://www.flashfoxy.com/climbing-fest/schedule) when finalized.

#### Do I have to be an experienced rock climber to attend the festival?

Not at all - **beginners are welcome**! We welcome women and genderqueer folks of all climbing experience levels. There will be several intro and beginning clinics and workshops in addition to intermediate and advanced offerings. The festival will be a great opportunity to try out climbing in a safe and supportive environment.

#### Do I need to register to attend the festival?

**Yes! Registration is required** to attend the festival and the number of participants is limited to 350. Learn more about [Registration](https://www.flashfoxy.com/climbing-fest/registration)!

#### What is included in the cost of registration?

*   **FRIDAY**: Opening Party, Happy Hour, Arts & Crafts, Welcome Presentation, DJ Dance Party
    

*   **SATURDAY**: Breakfast, Climbing Demos, Arts & Crafts, Evening Yoga, Dinner, Panel, Film Screenings
    

*   **SUNDAY**: Morning Workshop, Breakfast, Stewardship Project, Community Slideshow
    

*   **SWAG** from our generous sponsors!
    

Please see the [](https://www.flashfoxy.com/registration)[Registration](https://www.flashfoxy.com/climbing-fest/registration) page for more detail.

#### What is not included in the cost of registration?

*   **Clinics:** $125/clinic. Registration is open only to festival ticket holders. Unfortunately, we are unable to offer refunds or transfers for clinics. [More info here.](https://www.flashfoxy.com/climbing-fest/clinics-workshops)
    
*   **Lodging:** see [Lodging + Local Beta](https://www.flashfoxy.com/climbing-fest/lodging) for our recs
    
*   **Climbing Equipment Rental:** Shoe + harness demos will be available from our sponsors, however access to demos is not guaranteed. All participants are responsible for their own climbing equipment. Check out local gear shops, [Sage to Summit](https://sagetosummit.com/collections/crash-pads?srsltid=AfmBOorTizjiSrNcW1PPD-IBJABL3-Lld9n_MvvzHsCC1zVul2y31FDJ) and [Eastside Sports](https://eastsidesports.com/pages/rentals?gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=21641062538&gbraid=0AAAAA-JD0qmiFfgB-y4mjRq9zB-gu0kUf&gclid=CjwKCAiAqKbMBhBmEiwAZ3UboJ4DjfDE8WP18tI0PN07RQ15RC3BB6F82xaMrkXE8EZuj0ihs6-G3xoCsIgQAvD_BwE) for gear rentals and guidebooks!
    
*   **Transportation:** All festival ticket holders will receive a link to a ride-share spreadsheet to help coordinate transportation. This link can be found in the festival linktree (it’s in your Eventbrite confirmation email, save it!!). All participants are responsible for their own transportation to/from the festival and to/from venues throughout the weekend. Grocery stores and restaurants are within walking distance (less than 1 mile) from the festival venue. Camping, hotels, and hostels are available within walking distance from the festival venue. Access to a vehicle is necessary for getting to climbing areas independently. We highly encourage festival participants to carpool!
    
*   **Refunds:** This event is rain or shine. We cannot guarantee weather conditions, crag conditions or any other element of climbing, road or trail access. There are no refunds for this event.
    

#### Do you need to be registered for the festival to sign up for a clinic?

**Yes, clinics are only open to registered festival participants.** Clinics are subject to limited attendance. Purchase of a festival pass does not guarantee that you will be able to register for a clinic. Our most popular clinics often sell out within minutes! Early Bird Festival Pass holders will receive the registration link on February 14 (24hrs early!). Registration link will be sent to all other ticket holders on February 15.

#### Are scholarships available?

**Yes!** Please see more information on our [Registration Page](https://www.flashfoxy.com/climbing-fest/registration) (scroll down!).

#### Who can attend the festival?

Flash Foxy welcomes all **women and genderqueer climbers** to join us at the Flash Foxy Climbing Festival. We use this as an umbrella term for all folks of non-dominant genders, including all trans and gender non-conforming folks. Still not sure if this space is for you? Check out our [FAQs about who Flash Foxy is for](https://www.flashfoxy.com/faq).

**This is an all-ages event - children and elders are welcome!** Special pricing is available for families with young children. To learn more about Family Festival Passes, including bringing your kiddos with you to the festival or supporting a young climber who wants to attend, please email us at events@flashfoxy.com. Pricing for children is as follows: Under 6 = free to attend with adult; 6-12 years = $50 with adult; 12-18 years $90 with adult.

Our goal is to create and maintain a safe and diverse space where consent and respect are our first priorities. Harassment of any kind (unwanted contact, verbal or physical abuse, racism, homophobia, transphobia, body-shaming, etc.) will NOT be tolerated and will lead to being asked to leave.

#### Can I bring my dog?

As much as we love dogs, they are **not allowed** at primary festival programming including the opening party, film screenings, presentations, clinics, workshops and stewardship projects. Our events are jam packed with both humans and activities and can be an overwhelming experience for our canine friends. Additionally, dogs can be a safety hazard at the crag. To avoid conflict, we would prefer that you leave your pup at home. Thank you for understanding!

Dogs **are welcome** to come hang outdoors at the Foxy Fair on Saturday at the Tri-County Fairgrounds!

Service dogs are allowed at all festival programming. If you will be bringing a service animal to your clinic or workshop please email events@flashfoxy.com so that we can ensure that the venue can accommodate dogs. Some approaches involve delicate scrambling and are not safe for dogs.

#### I have a food allergy, can I still participate in event dinners?

Gluten free and vegan options will be available for breakfast and dinner. Catered food is not prepared in a celiac/gluten free kitchen, however community member with celiac have reported eating the catered food and feeling OK. It is up to individuals to make their own decisions regarding sensitivities. Nut-free food will always be available, but again we cannot guarantee that there is no cross contamination. At this time, no refunds or discounts will be given for those with allergies. We apologize for any inconvenience and thank you for your understanding!

#### What if I purchased a festival pass and no longer can attend?

**Unfortunately, we can NOT offer refunds.** However, we truly understand that circumstances can change and that you probably want your money back. **While we cannot offer refunds, we strive to facilitate ticket transfers whenever possible!** You must find someone who wants your ticket (tag us in your stories or post in our Facebook group for help finding someone!). If tickets sell out and a waitlist forms, we can offer ticket transfers to folks on the waitlist. Please note that as the festival date approaches, processing refunds and ticket transfers becomes more challenging.

The deadline to request a ticket transfers is Friday, March 7th. If you've purchased a pass but find yourself unable to attend, please contact us right away at events@flashfoxy.com.

#### Is this event rain or shine?

**Yes, our event is rain or shine!** Regardless of the weather, we will have a good time! We cannot guarantee access to climbing or any specific climbing areas. Part of climbing outdoors is respecting the land and learning to make the best of whatever Mother Nature throws our way!

We cannot guarantee weather conditions, crag conditions, or any other element of climbing, road, or trail access. There are no refunds for this event.

#### Where can I find information about accessibility of venues + programing?

All primary festival event venues (opening party, open air market, film screenings, panels) will be held at wheelchair accessible venues and will have accessible bathrooms. The Opening Party and Foxy Fair take place outside in a flat grassy field with paved paths. Film screenings, panel, dinner and other activities will take place in the Heritage Arts Building at the [Tri-County Fairgrounds](https://tricountyfair.com/wp/) - this building is ground-level. The Community Slideshow will take place at [Mountain Rambler Brewery](https://www.mountainramblerbrewery.com/) \- this building is ground-level. Seating will be available during all events.

All films will have captions in English. ASL interpreters can be coordinated upon request. Please email events@flashfoxy.com to discuss your needs.

Approaches differ by climbing area. Details about approaches can be at the [bottom of the Schedule](https://www.flashfoxy.com/climbing-fest/schedule), or can be found on [Mountain Project](https://www.mountainproject.com/area/106064825/bishop-area).

**Have an accessibility concern? Reach out to events@flashfoxy.com** and we’ll see how we can help!

We are always working to make the Flash Foxy Climbing Festival a more inclusive and welcoming space, please let us know what we can do to make our event more accessible for you. Unfortunately, we are not always able to arrange accommodations, but we will do our best and will provide honest answers about the our event spaces, staff capabilities and the activities that take place at our festivals. Thank you for learning and growing with us!

#### What’s your Covid-19 Plan?

All festival attendees **must be fully vaccinated** to attend the Flash Foxy Climbing Festival in Bishop. To request a vaccine exemption please email events@flashfoxy.com. Exemptions will only be granted for those with medical conditions preventing them from receiving a vaccine. 

If you are unvaccinated and have purchased a ticket please email events@flashfoxy.com and we will do our best to accommodate a ticket transfer. Please refer to our refund policy (above) for more details - although, we hope you’ll choose to get vaccinated instead!

Face masks will be optional for all events (indoors and outdoors). Disposable face masks will be available on site.

**If changes in your personal circumstances** related to Covid-19 affect your comfort levels with attending the festival, we may be able to facilitate a ticket transfer. We cannot guarantee ticket transfers. No Refunds.

**If you have a positive Covid-19 test or contact** with someone with a confirmed or suspected case of Covid-19 within one week of the festival we ask that you do not attend. Please inform us immediately and we will do our best to facilitate a ticket transfer. We cannot guarantee ticket transfers. No Refunds.

Additionally, we request that if you are sick - _even if it’s not Covid_ - that you stay home. We don’t like missing events any more than you do, but we also really don’t like being sick. We especially don’t like putting our immunocompromised community members at risk. If you’re recovering from illness or think you might be getting sick… consider wearing a mask in all group settings <3

**If we have to cancel** any Flash Foxy event or program due to rising Covid-19 cases or other national emergency ticket holders will have the following refund options:

*   50% Refund (standard policy if no action taken by ticket holder)
    
*   100% Refund (by email request to events@flashfoxy.com)
    
*   Donate full ticket price to Flash Foxy
    

We ask ticket holders who have the financial ability to keep in mind that the majority of our festival expenses are fixed and non-refundable (employee salaries, insurance, perishable goods, deposits, etc). We greatly appreciate our community and your on-going support. 

**Our Covid-19 plan may be updated at any time.** If you have any questions please email events@flashfoxy.com.

#### Insurance

Flash Foxy is not responsible for covering additional trip expenses, including change or cancellation fees for travel, lodging accommodations, rental cars, or other arrangements. For your protection, we strongly recommend purchasing trip insurance. Trip insurance can compensate you in the event that you’re no longer able to attend a program. Check out [this article](https://blog.weighmyrack.com/3-top-travel-insurances-rock-climbing-trip/) for more information about finding and choosing travel insurance.

Climbing is dangerous. Especially if you don’t have regular health insurance, we recommend getting some kind of medical coverage such as accident insurance. [Global Rescue](https://www.globalrescue.com/landing-pages/travelinsurance/) is one such service.  

#### Don’t see your question? Please email us at events@flashfoxy.com or fill out our [Contact Form.](https://www.flashfoxy.com/contact)

### GENERAL INFORMATION

*   What is The One Motorcycle Show Portland?
    
    For 17 years, The One Motorcycle Show has been celebrating motorcycles, art, and community. Held annually at Portland’s historic Zidell Yards, it brings together custom bikes from around the globe, moto-inspired art, cars, helmets, live music, vendors, demos, and loads of FUN. There’s something for everyone. 2026 TICKETS LIVE DEC 1ST!!
    
*   When is The One Motorcycle Show Portland?
    
    Year 17 of The One Motorcycle Show is happening Friday, May 1st - Sunday, May 2nd, 2026.
    
    **Portland Show Hours**
    
    5/1/2026: 9 AM - 10 PM
    
    5/2/2026: 9 AM - 10 PM
    
    5/3/2026: 9 AM - 3 PM
    
    **_Online ticket sales end April 30th at 11:59 PM! General Admission available at the door (prices increase). Weekend & Day Passes are available online only._**
    
*   Where is The One Motorcycle Show Portland?
    
    It’s happening once again at the historic [**Zidell Yards - 3121 S Moody Ave, Portland, Oregon 97239**.](https://www.the1moto.com/venue) Our fifth year at this rad venue. Don’t miss it!
    
    **_Online ticket sales end April 30th at 11:59 PM! General Admission available at the door (prices increase). Weekend & Day Passes are available online only._**
    
*   How can I get tickets to The One Motorcycle Show?
    
    Tickets to The One Motorcycle Show are available for purchase [**HERE**](https://www.tixr.com/groups/1moto/events/the-one-motorcycle-show-portland-166660).
    
    **_Online ticket sales end April 30th at 11:59 PM! General Admission available at the door (prices increase). Weekend & Day Passes are available online only._**
    
*   Is The One Motorcycle Show Portland family-friendly?
    
    Heck yeah! The show’s open to all ages and fun for the whole fam. Kids 10 and under get in free with an adult. Daytime’s great for families, but everyone’s welcome anytime during the event!
    
    **_Online ticket sales end April 30th at 11:59 PM! General Admission available at the door (prices increase). Weekend & Day Passes are available online only._**
    
*   Are pets allowed at the show?
    
    Pets, with the exception of service animals, are generally not allowed inside the event venue due to safety and space considerations.
    
*   Will there be food and drinks available at the show?
    
    You bet! We’ve got food vendors serving up tasty eats and plenty of drink options to keep you fueled all day. Wanna join the lineup? Click [**HERE**](https://www.the1moto.com/get-involved) to apply to be a vendor at the PORTLAND show! Or reach out to [**vendors@theonemoto.com**](mailto:vendors@theonemoto.com).
    
*   Are there accommodations nearby for out-of-town visitors?
    
    There are lots of hotels, motels, and Airbnb spots near the venue, but they fill up quick so book early! Check [**HERE**](https://www.the1moto.com/hotels) for all the latest & preferred hotel recommendations.
    
*   Is there parking available at the event?
    
    Parking is limited, so we recommend riding your bike, carpooling, or using public transit when you can. Motorcycle parking is free, first-come, first-served, and right near the main entrance.
    
*   Is the venue ADA accessible?
    
    Yes, although it is not an ideal space for wheelchairs as there is not any sidewalk. There are ramps to all elevated spaces within the venue, but due to the nature of the industrial building and the outdoor areas around it, please be aware that there are many areas at the event venue with uneven ground.
    
*   Do you have ADA / handicap parking available?
    
    Limited accessible parking options are available on site near the main show entrance, first come first serve. Our parking attendants will help get you there. We will also have ADA-compliant restrooms available.
    
*   Are there any prohibited items?
    
    **Prohibited Items**
    
    NO WEAPONS OF ANY KIND – Including Firearms, Pocket Knives, Pepper Spray, tasers, etc.
    
    These items will be confiscated via Local Authorities and Security. 
    
    ❌ Backpacks, Purses, or Bags larger than 14″ x 14″ 
    
    ❌ Illegal Substances, Drugs or Drug Paraphernalia
    
    ❌ Unsealed Over the Counter Medications or Vitamins
    
    ❌ Animals (except service animals)
    
    ❌ Outside alcohol
    
    ❌ Fireworks, open fires, flammable products, projectiles, or explosives
    
    ❌ Drones or Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs).
    
    ❌ Glass of any kind
    
    ❌ Lasers or pointer devices
    
    ❌ Tactical Gear, Walkie Talkies, etc.
    
    ❌ Items deemed as posing a threat to the safe enjoyment of the One Motorcycle Show by management.
    
    Please check out our [Community Code of Conduct](https://www.the1moto.com/code-of-conduct) for more info.
    

### SUBMISSIONS

*   How can I submit my build to be in the show?
    
    Got a custom bike you’re ready to show off? The One Motorcycle Show wants to see it! Click [**HERE**](https://www.the1moto.com/get-involved) for all the details on how to submit your ride.
    
*   When will I hear back about my bike being accepted or not?
    
    Accepted builds will know before or by March 7th, 2026, via email. Once accepted, we'll send you a physical invite via the ol' postman (in the mail) by April 1st, 2026.
    
*   How can I submit my art?
    
    Wanna get your art in the mix? Click [**HERE**](https://www.the1moto.com/get-involved) to learn more about getting involved.
    
*   How can I apply to be a vendor?
    
    Fresh oysters? Cool wares? Moto Gear? We’re into it. Locals get dibs. Check out how to get involved [**HERE**](https://www.the1moto.com/get-involved).
    
*   How can I participate in the 21 Helmets showcase?
    
    Shoot an email over to [**thor@theonemoto.com**](mailto:thor@theonemoto.com) for more info!
    
*   How can I submit my band?
    
    Thanks for your interest! Band submissions aren’t currently open, but if you think your band should be on our radar, drop a line to **mahala@theonemoto.com**.
    
*   Is photography allowed at The One Motorcycle Show?
    
    Yes, general photography is allowed, but please be mindful of others while snapping photos. By attending The One Motorcycle Show, you agree to being photographed, filmed, or recorded. Official photographers and media can apply for a press badge to access exclusive events. Click [**HERE**](https://www.the1moto.com/media) for more info.
    
*   How can I apply for a media pass?
    
    Interested in covering the show? Media credentials are limited. Apply [**HERE**](https://www.the1moto.com/get-involved) to be considered! Questions? Email [**media@theonemoto.com**](mailto:media@theonemoto.com?).
    
*   How can I apply to volunteer at the show?
    
    Click [**HERE**](https://www.the1moto.com/get-involved) for more info!
    

### SHOW PROGRAM

*   Is there an event schedule for the show?
    
    Yep! Check it out above! Keep checking back for the latest info & updates!
    
*   Will there be any offsite events, parties or racing?
    
    Check out the full weekend schedule for off-site after parties you can’t miss! Interested in teaming up for a good time? Hit up **marian@theonemoto.com**.
    
*   Will there be a bike showcase?
    
    Yup!! Custom bikes from all over the world. It’s what The One’s all about.
    
*   What bands are performing?
    
    We’ve got a killer lineup brewing! Check back soon!
    
*   Will there be demos?
    
    Of course! Demos are a staple. We’ll share more info on what’s lined up closer to the show.
    
*   What activities will be at the show?
    
    Bikes, bands, cars, art, food, stunts, vendors... you name it. The One Motorcycle Show is a wheelie wonderland.
    
*   Are there activities for kids?
    
    Yep! Bring the whole fam. There’s something for everyone (and kids 10 and under are free when accompanied with an adult!). We have plenty of fun for the whole family!
    
*   What kind of vendors will be there?
    
    From moto gear to vintage fashion, jewelry, art, and tasty eats, our vendors cover it all.
    
*   Will there be food and drinks available?
    
    Plenty! We’ve got food trucks, drinks, and all the good stuff to keep you fueled for the day.
    
*   Is there a map of the venue?
    
    Check it out above! Keep checking back for the latest info!
    
*   Tips for The One Motorcycle Show first-timers?
    
    Get ready for a good time! Wear comfy shoes, bring a charged phone for pics, and don’t rush… there’s A LOT to see. Arrive early, grab your tickets online to save a few bucks, and snag a [**Weekend Pass**](https://www.tixr.com/groups/1moto) so you don’t miss a single drop of the fun!
    
    **_Online ticket sales end April 30th at 11:59 PM! General Admission available at the door (prices increase). Weekend & Day Passes are available online only._**
    
*   Will there be The One Motorcycle merch for sale at the show?
    
    Oh yeah—plenty of it! Grab some world-famous One Moto gear, posters, hats and maybe even a few surprises you won’t find anywhere else! In the meantime, check out our online merch shop [**HERE**](https://the1moto.com/shop) for the latest drops!
    
    **_Online ticket sales end May 1st at 11:59 PM! General Admission available at the door (prices increase). Weekend & Day Passes are available online only._**
    

### TICKETS

*   How can I attend The One Motorcycle Show?
    
    Tickets for The One Motorcycle Show are available [HERE](https://www.tixr.com/groups/1moto). Grab yours early—this event sells out fast! Prices go up at the door, so save by purchasing in advance. Day and Weekend Passes available online only.
    
*   Can I get a refund?
    
    Refunds are available until the day of the show. For assistance with refunds, please send an email to [**support@tixr.com**](mailto:support@tixr.com?). They will be able to assist you with the refund process.
    
*   Can I change the name on my ticket?
    
    Unfortunately, name changes on tickets are not allowed at this time. 
    
*   Can I transfer my ticket to another person?
    
    Currently, ticket transfers to another individual are not permitted.
    
*   Can I resell my ticket?
    
    We do not support the resale of tickets.
    

### ONLINE SHOP

#### Refund Policy

*   What is your policy on refunds, returns, and exchanges?
    
    We accept returns within 30 days after delivery if the item is unused and in its original condition. We will refund the full order amount, minus the shipping costs for the return. In case your order arrives damaged, please contact us at info@theonemoto.com with your order number and a photo of the item's condition for a case-by-case assessment.
    
*   Are there any items that cannot be returned or exchanged?
    
    Products on sale are not eligible for return or exchange.
    
*   Who covers the return shipping costs?
    
    The buyer is responsible for return shipping costs. Original shipping fees are non-refundable.
    
*   How long does it take to process a refund?
    
    Refunds may take 2-7 days to process after we receive and approve the return, depending on your payment method and credit card company.
    

#### Shipping

*   How long does it take to process and ship my order?
    
    All orders are processed within 2 to 5 business days, excluding weekends and holidays. After your order is confirmed, you will receive a shipping notification. Delivery times vary but typically take 5-10 business days, depending on your location.
    
*   What are the shipping rates and how are they calculated?
    
    We offer free shipping for orders over $50. For orders under $50, shipping charges are calculated and displayed at checkout based on your order size and shipping destination.
    
*   How can I track the status of my order?
    
    Once your order has shipped, you will receive an email with a tracking number. You can use this number to check the status of your delivery. Please allow 48 hours for the tracking information to become available.
    
*   Do you offer a local pick-up option?
    
    Yes! You can pick up your order at One Moto Cafe, 1642 NE Sandy Blvd., Portland, OR 97232, daily from 7 AM to 3 PM. Just select local pick-up at checkout, and we’ll email you when it’s ready—usually within 2 to 5 business days. Questions about local pick-up? Email info@theonemoto.com.

# Frequently Asked Questions

#### What opportunities are available through Flash Foxy Education?

Flash Foxy Education is a new and growing program, we’re adding new locations and new courses as our capacity increases. Current programs are listed on the main [Education Program](https://www.flashfoxy.com/education) page. You can find all our course offerings on our [Types of Courses](https://www.flashfoxy.com/education-courses) page.

#### Can I participate if I’m not a woman or genderqueer individual?

**Currently Flash Foxy Education courses are only open to participants who identify as women and genderqueer climbers.** Not sure if this includes you? Please check our our [FAQs.](https://www.flashfoxy.com/faq) Please keep in mind that our organizational roots call us to center the experience of women and genderqueer folks and create a program that responds to the unique needs of _all_ marginalized genders. Our goal is to create and maintain a safe and diverse space where consent and respect are our first priorities. Harassment of any kind (unwanted contact, verbal or physical abuse, racism, homophobia, transphobia, body-shaming, etc.) will NOT be tolerated.

#### How does sliding-scale pricing work? How much should I pay?

It’s up to you how much you pay, but here are some things you can keep in mind when deciding what price is best for you.

*   The average cost of a 2-day guided course is about $350.
    
*   All the tuition payments go right back into this program so that we can run more courses and provided more full scholarships!
    

Here’s a loose guideline to help you decide where you might fall on the sliding-scale:

*   It can be hard to pay rent and cover other basic necessities > _Apply for a scholarship!_
    
*   I can pay for basic necessities, but I do not have extra income for things like a climbing gym membership > _Apply for a scholarship!_
    

*   I can pay for basic necessities and some luxury items like a climbing gym membership > _$50-$100_
    
*   I am able to afford or save up for occasional weekend trips and the costs associated with that (rental car, park fees, owning gear, etc) > _$100-$200_
    
*   I can afford regular weekend trips and the costs associated with that (rental car, park fees, owning gear, etc) > _$200-$300_
    
*   I am financially comfortable and able to help support scholarships for future course participants > _$300-$400_
    

\*Please also consider that income is not the same as wealth. Income is the amount of money you make. Wealth is passed down from generation to generation and usually takes the form of inheritances, land ownership, and/or earning power. We ask that you take into account not only your income but also your wealth when choosing your price point within our sliding scale.

#### Is transportation included?

Transportation is **not** included. However, your instructor may be able to help coordinate carpooling options among the group or help you navigate public transit. Reach out to education@flashfoxy.com and we’ll see what we can do to help!

#### Is lodging included?

Lodging is **not** included. However, we have some recommendations for accommodations near our course locations:

*   **Bishop, CA** > Camping at the [Tri-County Fairgrounds](https://tricountyfair.com/bishop-climbers-campground/) , [the PV Pit](https://www.blm.gov/visit/pleasant-valley-pit-campground) or [Pleasant Valley Campground](https://www.inyocounty.us/services/parks-recreation/campgrounds/pleasant-valley-campground); stay indoors at [The Hostel California](https://www.thehostelca.com/)
    
*   **Mammoth Lakes, CA** > Camping in [Mammoth Lakes](https://www.visitmammoth.com/trip-ideas/camping-mammoth-lakes/)
    
*   **Joshua Tree, CA** > [Joshua Tree Crash Pad](https://www.joshuatreecrashpad.com/): A community space for climbers, [Black Rock Campground](https://nps.gov/jotr/planyourvisit/black-rock-campground.htm): A National Park campground
    
*   **New Paltz, NY (aka The Gunks)** > Camping at the [AAC Gunks Campground](https://americanalpineclub.org/gunks-campground); stay indoors at [New Paltz Hostel](https://www.newpaltzhostel.com/)
    
*   **North Conway, NH** > Stay indoors or camp at [CoHo](http://www.cohohostel.com/) (**call or email booking@cohohostel.com for 10% off** you stay during any Flash Foxy course!!); stay indoors at [The Bunkhouse](https://www.nemountaineering.com/about-nem/bunkhouse/)
    

#### What about food/drinks?

Flash Foxy does not provide food or drinks for Education Program participants.

#### I don’t know if I can afford to participate. What are my options?

Thanks to our generous sponsor Arc’teryx, all Flash Foxy Education Courses are offered on a sliding-scale. To ensure our programs are financially accessible, full scholarships are also available for most education courses. [**Apply for a scholarship here**](https://www.flashfoxy.com/scholarships). Scholarship application is only required for those unable to afford the lowest tier ticket available on the registration page.

#### What difficulty do I need to climb to participate?

Flash Foxy programs are open to climbers of **all** **ability types and levels**, including people who have never climbed before. If a course’s venue or content requires you to have certain skills or abilities, they will be clearly outlined in the “CLIMBER REQUIREMENTS” section of the course description. If you have a disability that you’re not sure if we can accommodate, please reach out to education@flashfoxy.com.

#### Do I have to bring my own climbing gear?

Nope! Flash Foxy and our guide service/climbing school partner can provide you with any and all necessary climbing gear, including a helmet, harness, climbing shoes, belay device, etc. If you do own your own gear, please feel free to bring it. You may use it at the discretion of your instructor(s).

Other general outdoor gear, such as backpacks or camping gear, may be available upon request. Reach out to education@flashfoxy.com about availability and to get suggestions on where you might be able to rent/borrow equipment from.

#### What should I bring?

Your instructor will reach out to you about the specifics of your particular course, but you can check out our [Packing List](https://www.flashfoxy.com/education-packing-list) for a general overview.

#### Do I have to be a certain age to participate?

Flash Foxy Education programming is geared towards adults. However, young adults and kids are welcome! Those ages 12 and under must be accompanied by an adult. Seniors and elders are also welcome and encouraged to join! All of our courses, top roping tends to be the least impactful and risky style of climbing and is a great option for those concerned about participating.

#### I don’t see any options in my area. When will Flash Foxy offer something near me?

We’re perpetually trying to meet more folks where they’re at and plan to increase the number of locations where we offer programs as our capacity increases. If you’d like to help bring a Flash Foxy Education Program to your local area, please let us know! We are always looking for guide service partners, guides and climbing organizations to work with as this new program grows. If you don’t see any options near you, please feel free to reach out and let us know where you’d like to see courses offered next! The only way we can do better in the future is to hear from you.

#### Is climbing dangerous?

Yes, climbing is dangerous and at Flash Foxy, your safety is our primary concern. As with all things in life, rock climbing exposes us to risk—both physical (scrapes and bruises) and emotional (fear and anxiety). We strive to provide an experience where you are:

*   Aware and informed of the risks you’re undertaking by participating
    
*   Cared for by trained risk managers—our seasoned Flash Foxy instructors
    
*   Given the skills to manage the risks you will encounter
    
*   Able to choose the amount and types of risk you’re willing to tackle
    
*   Not exposed to any unnecessary or unproductive risks
    

#### Should I tip my instructor(s)?

Flash Foxy aims to compensate instructors well so that they don’t need to rely on additional gratuity, and you don’t need to think about extra budgeting after you’ve paid your course fee. However, if your instructor has given you an exceptional experience, and you and/or your fellow students would like to show appreciation, please feel free to tip. Groups of students often pool a tip for instructors and the use of Venmo, Paypal, or other electronic payment is common. Gratuity is always appreciated.

Other forms of gratuity are also welcome! If you don’t have the funds to provide a monetary tip, please consider sending your instructor a handwritten card or homemade gift. Our instructors often take bookings outside of Flash Foxy courses as well, so sharing their website or social media platform with your networks can help generate work and income for them.

#### If I was waitlisted, how will I know if/when my status changes?

You will receive an email from Flash Foxy (via Eventbrite) as soon as possible if a spot becomes available, and you are eligible.

#### Are Flash Foxy courses rain or shine?

As much as is practical, we try to run courses rain or shine. Your instructor will communicate with you about any potential inclement weather and what to expect. If for some reason we need to cancel, you can see what your options are in the next section down.

#### I can’t make it to the program I booked. Can I get a refund?

On occasion, Flash Foxy may need to cancel a program for a variety of unforeseen reasons including weather, instructor availability, low enrollment, etc. In the event that Flash Foxy is forced to cancel a program, all participants will be eligible to either reschedule to a program occurring in the next year (subject to availability) at no additional cost to you or receive a full refund. Otherwise, our refund policy is as follows:

_30 Days or More Prior to Program_

*   Reschedule to a program occurring in the next 12-months (subject to availability) at no additional cost to you
    
*   Receive a full refund minus a $25 administrative fee
    

_Less Than 30 Days Prior to Program_

*   No refunds are available
    
*   Reschedule to a program occurring in the next 12-months (subject to availability) for an administrative fee. Fee is based upon original payment.
    
    *   Less than $100 = $25 administrative fee
        
    *   $100 - $200 = $50 administrative fee
        
    *   $200 - $300 = $75 administrative fee
        
    *   $300 or more = $100 administrative fee
        

_Less Than 7 Days Prior to Program_

*   No refunds or reschedules are available
    

_Insurance_

Flash Foxy is not responsible for covering additional trip expenses, including change or cancellation fees for travel, lodging accommodations, rental cars, or other arrangements. For your protection, we strongly recommend purchasing trip insurance. Trip insurance can compensate you in the event that you’re no longer able to attend a program. Check out [this article](https://blog.weighmyrack.com/3-top-travel-insurances-rock-climbing-trip/) for more information about finding and choosing travel insurance.

Climbing is dangerous. Especially if you don’t have regular health insurance, we recommend getting some kind of medical coverage such as accident insurance. [Global Rescue](https://www.globalrescue.com/landing-pages/travelinsurance/) is one such service.

#### What is your Covid-19 Policy?

All Flash Foxy attendees **must be fully vaccinated** to attend any Flash Foxy Education Program. **To request a vaccine exemption please email education@flashfoxy.com.** Exemptions will only be granted for those with medical conditions preventing them from receiving a vaccine. Participants are NOT required to wear face masks, except in the instances outlined below, however participants are welcome and encouraged to mask during the course if desired. **If you are feeling sick - whether you think it’s COVID-19 or a cold - please stay home.**

Please refer to the guidelines below if you have a known or suspected COVID-19 exposure, or generally aren’t feeling well, and are unsure as to whether or not you should attend your scheduled program.

*   If you are symptomatic and are testing positive for COVID-19, please stay home. 
    
*   If you are symptomatic and testing negative for COVID-19, please consider staying home. If you have any symptoms of COVID or a cold please mask during the course!
    
*   If you have a known exposure, but are testing negative for COVID-19, please wear an N95 mask or equivalent for the duration of the course. You may unmask when greater than 6-feet from all participants and instructors.
    
*   If you are recovering from COVID-19, or any other illness, and have followed the CDC guidelines on quarantining after testing positive for COVID-19, please wear an N95 mask or equivalent for the duration of the course. You may unmask when greater than 6-feet from all participants and instructors.
    
*   **We are unable to offer refunds or reschedules for cancellations within 7-days**, including those related to illness or injury. Please refer to our full refund policy above for more details.
    

Our COVID-19 plan is constantly in progress and may be updated at any time.

If you have a question or concern that hasn’t been covered above, please reach out to **education@flashfoxy.com.**

## We Know Adventure

![](https://www.overlandexpo.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/Ralph-Enger-1-1024x768.jpg)

Photo by Ralph Enger

Overland Expo® is the world’s premier event series for do-it-yourself adventure travel enthusiasts, with hundreds of session-hours of classes for 4-wheel-drive enthusiasts and adventure motorcyclists, inspirational programs, speakers & trainers from all over the world, the Overland Film Festival, roundtable discussions, demonstrations, food, and a large expo featuring several hundred vendors of adventure travel equipment, camping gear, bikes, vehicles, and services.

# Mountains to Meadows Endurofest, featuring Grinduro – September 10-13, 2026

10 years later, [Grinduro](http://grinduro.com/) returns to Quincy, back where it all started, to celebrate our birthday with the perfect party to race ratio at the ultimate California gravel race.

Plus, we’re adding the new Mount Hough MTB and eMTB Enduro races into the mix on Sunday. Race Grinduro, the Mount Hough Enduro, or both!

Festivities include two days of excellent food, a handmade bike show, live music and camping.

For full details visit the [Mountains to Meadows website](http://quincymountainstomeadows.com/).

### **2026 Tabler Info!**

**Load in and Set up:**

Tables are _first come, first served._ We will need you to **check in at the PZS info desk** (which is in the Smith Ballroom, you’ll see the line). You can arrive earlier, but we won’t start releasing tables until **10am on each day.** If there’s someone you’d like to table next to, plan to arrive early and arrive together! If you have accessibility requests regarding your table location or other logistics, please let us know this week!   

If you’re running late on the morning of the fest, please text us at the **_PZS Organizer Hotline_**, along with your name and Zine table name. **The _PZS Organizer Hotlin_e number is 503-941-0656.** You can also text or call the organizers during the event if you need urgent support.  _The hotline will only be active the weekend of the fest._  

**If you do not show up by 11:30 am on the day you are tabling, and you don’t text to say you are running late, we will give away your spot to someone waiting for a table.**  

We often have a few last minute cancellations or no-shows each day. If you’re tabling on one day and want to be on the waitlist for the other day, come to the info desk after 10am and we’ll put you on the list to possibly get a table! If we have space for you, half tables will be $20. 

  
**We have lots of new tablers this year! Exciting! Here are some things we recommend having in your Tabler Kit!** 

*   Tablecloth (can be an old sheet! If you bring an extra you can offer it to your table neighbor who might forget)
    
*   Zines! And other merch! Remember, we want at least **60% of your table** to be zines.
    
*   Change bank - it helps to have **one- and five-dollar bills** for making change! 
    
*   Square reader if you have one / Print-out of your Venmo QR code
    
*   Charger and/or external charge block for your phone if you’re taking mobile payments
    
*   Ibuprofen, extra masks
    
*   Water bottle, beverage mug
    
*   Table snacks
    
*   Something to do with your hands, like a handicraft or a sketchbook!
    
*   Paper and pens
    
*   Scissors and tape (to make signage for pricing)
    

We will have tables and chairs set up (one chair per half table), and a **Tabler Kit** for you with a KN95 mask, a PZS sticker, and a PZS program. We will provide you with one(1) KN95 mask in your kit. Don’t forget to bring and wear a mask to the event and in the line to check in! We’ll have surgical masks on-site for free as well.  We ask that you wear your KN95 (or more effective mask) during the fest.  See our [mask policy](https://www.portlandzinesymposium.org/safety) for more details!  

Please review our [**COVID and Safer Space Policies**](https://www.portlandzinesymposium.org/safety) before applying.

For any questions, please contact us at [**pdxzines@gmail.com**.](mailto:pdxzines@gmail.com?)

# About Sierra Buttes Trail Stewardship

### Our mission is building sustainable recreation-based communities through stewardship, job creation and world-class events, and providing quality outdoor experiences through trail construction and maintenance in the Lost Sierra.

# We couldn't verify the security of your connection.

## Access to this content has been restricted. Contact your internet service provider for help.

[_Video Production by Drop Media_](https://www.dropmedia.tv/)

Formed in 2003, the Sierra Buttes Trail Stewardship is a volunteer-driven 501c3 nonprofit dedicated to the maintenance and enhancement of trail systems in the Lost Sierra, a region that offers natural beauty, remote accessibility and diverse multi-use recreational opportunities. Our professional trail crew helps create and rebuild trails that are enjoyable for all user types: hikers, cyclists, dirt bikers, equestrians and anglers.

SBTS employs around 37 full-time and seasonal employees, most of which are Sierra and Plumas County residents, working on [trail projects](https://copper-alligator-9yh3.squarespace.com/trail-projects) across the region in partnership with the U.S. Forest Service. In addition to staffing a paid crew, SBTS has to-date donated 140,000 hours of labor through its dedicated volunteers. Together, we have maintained more than 3,000 miles of  shared-use trails and built 220+ miles of new trails.

## What We've Accomplished Since 2003

# 227

**Miles of New Trail Built**

# 3,082

**Miles of Trail Maintained to Specification**

# 3

**Pro Trail Crews in 2026**

# 40

**Employees in 2025**

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/681e46c994b3ba7455d102a0/c947e782-fd27-4010-b4f5-e14c759531af/sierra-buttes-trail-stewardship-hiking.jpg)

### “What makes Sierra Buttes different? The fact that they can drum up volunteers when they need them, at a moment’s notice,” said Rick Stock, a retired teacher at the Feather River College in Quincy. Stock taught recreation classes and was on the board of Sierra Buttes Trail Stewardship for four years. “People drive up from the bay or Sac to be part of some volunteer event. I don’t want to say it’s unheard of, but Sierra Buttes has a way to do it that’s more prolific than others I would say.”

— SF Gate

### Withstanding The Test of Time

While these trails see more than **200,000** visitors per year, they continue to maintain a level “A” standing, due to the hard work of SBTS staff and volunteers. In a perfect world, the Forest Service would be able to attend to all of these system trails (wilderness, roadless, recreation) as part of ongoing resource management. And that’s where SBTS and our family – our hardworking volunteers and members – come in, partnering with [land managers](https://copper-alligator-9yh3.squarespace.com/partner-with-us) to make dirt magic happen.

Trail bed armoring, grade reversals, drainage reconstruction, and grade reductions are all techniques employed for longevity and erosion control. By minimizing use impact through trail maintenance while not restricting access, the historic and recreational value of these trails has been maintained. And we’ve worked on everything from garden-variety singletrack, to Pacific Crest Trail in wilderness areas, to ADA-compliant paths, to multiple-use flow trails.

### Making Our Effort Count

[Event](http://static1.squarespace.com/static/681e46c994b3ba7455d102a0/681e8b1b538ff676414ffac0/681e8b5a538ff67641500a39/1746832218987/?format=original) income, [membership](http://static1.squarespace.com/static/681e46c994b3ba7455d102a0/681e8b1b538ff676414ffac0/681e8b5b538ff67641500a3c/1746832219014/?format=original), grants (county, state, federal, private), donations, and our bike shop [Yuba Expeditions](https://copper-alligator-9yh3.squarespace.com/yuba-expeditions) in Quincy go directly to trail maintenance and development in the [Lost Sierra](https://copper-alligator-9yh3.squarespace.com/the-lost-sierra). Donations are multiplied by over 500 percent through organized volunteer labor and in-kind contributions. And we have even helped other trail user organizations in South Lake Tahoe, Santa Cruz, the Sacramento Valley and the Sierra foothills with planning, construction and trail improvements. **View our 2025 Annual Report** to learn about our economic impact, partnerships and fundraising we achieved to support Lost Sierra communities.

![Black and white photograph of mountainous terrain with rocky peaks and a forested foreground. Overlaid text reads: "Established 2003 Our mission: Building sustainable recreation-based communities through stewardship, job creation and world-class events. Providing quality outdoor experiences through trail construction and maintenance in the Lost Sierra."](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/681e46c994b3ba7455d102a0/6c72c333-8514-41de-9383-01b078cc1669/SBTS-presentation-1.png)

Click to view the 2025 Annual Report

### The SBTS Family

Our organization is a shining example of what a small group of dedicated, passionate people can do. We are hikers, mountain bikers, motorcycle riders, equestrians and anglers playing in the outdoors. We are the descendants of native tribes and fourth-generation miners. We are the ones with chainsaws in backpacks as the snow melts, doing maintenance and clearing away winter's deadfall. We are the people caring for something very special, and keeping it special for our friends, families, and generations to come. And we have fun too! [Join us](http://static1.squarespace.com/static/681e46c994b3ba7455d102a0/681e8b1b538ff676414ffac0/681e8b5b538ff67641500a3c/1746832219014/?format=original) – become a member, dedicate your time at one of our [Volunteer Epic weekends](https://sierratrails.org/events) and/or [race events](http://static1.squarespace.com/static/681e46c994b3ba7455d102a0/681e8b1b538ff676414ffac0/681e8b5a538ff67641500a39/1746832218987/?format=original), and make a difference!

![Sierra Buttes Trail Stewardship staff](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/681e46c994b3ba7455d102a0/c58ddb53-5f65-4826-bac2-fd4f823ec4b1/sbts-staff-photo-2025-web.jpg)

# Press Kit

### About the Sierra Buttes Trail Stewardship

Formed in 2003, the Sierra Buttes Trail Stewardship is a volunteer driven nonprofit whose primary goal is the maintenance and enhancement of the trail systems in and around Downieville, the Lakes Basin, Graeagle, Quincy beyond. This small group has donated over 140,000 hours of volunteer labor to the Plumas, Humboldt-Toiyabe, Lassen and Tahoe National Forests, maintaining over 3,000 miles of trails in the past two decades, and building 220+ miles of new trails. While these trails see over 200,000 users per year, they continue to maintain a level A standing due to all the hard work of the Stewardship paid crew and volunteers. This organization is not only a shining example of what a small group of dedicated, passionate people can do for an area, it is a demonstration of economic efficiency when no alternatives exist.

All our product sponsors' and volunteer monies go directly to trail maintenance and development. We multiply all donations by over 1500% through organized volunteer labor in-kind contributions.

# SBTS Partners

### Our partners are essential stakeholders and directly responsible for our non-profit’s success.

We firmly believe that responsible enjoyment of the great outdoors is a way to build stronger, more connected communities and boost our economy. This is one of our founding beliefs, and we have formed relationships with organizations and businesses sharing this same belief. Whether you’re a federal agency, a big-time bicycle manufacturer or small mom-and-pop local business, you’re all making a difference. And we thank you.

![1% for the Planet](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/681e46c994b3ba7455d102a0/1746832867013-IM31MHAPQ6212EGS3XNK/one-percent-for-the-planet-logo.png)

## SBTS Partners

### These businesses and organizations have pledged their philanthropic support to SBTS and Lost Sierra trails!

We encourage you to pay it back and buy from these fine people or support their organizations. If you want to support our nonprofit or one of our [race events](http://sierratrails.org/event-partnerships/), contact Marty Scheel at [marty@sierratrails.org](mailto:marty@sierratrails.org).

# A celebration made for the Northwest.

#### The Pacific Northwest’s first large-scale gathering dedicated to the art of sauna, wellness, and community connection.

This two-day celebration invites guests to step into the steam and experience the magic of sauna culture through sauna sessions, cold plunges, live music, and Nordic-inspired food and drinks.

Whether you’re brand-new to the tradition or a seasoned sauna lover, this festival is your invitation to relax, renew, and celebrate sauna culture—Seattle style.

## WHAT TO EXPECT

#### SAUNA CITY

A gathering of unique saunas from across the region. Try them all—each with its own design, heat style, and personality, perfect for warming up on a crisp Northwest day.

#### LIVE MUSIC

Acoustic sets, DJ beats, and cultural performances create a vibrant atmosphere, even when the mist rolls in or the rain taps on the sauna roof.

#### COLD PLUNGE

Cool down the traditional way with invigorating ice baths and enjoy the rain or pray for snow.

#### NORDIC FLAVORS

Fuel your day with hearty soups, fresh baked goods, smoked fish, and craft beverages—comfort food made for cozy weather.

## HOW DOES THIS WORK?

*   #### Purchase a Ticket
    
    Purchase a **General Admission** ticket for a 90 minute timed session.
    
    Purchase a **VIP Experience** ticket for all day access on Saturday or Sunday, as well as festival merchandise and food & beverages.
    
    _All tickets include access to the saunas, cold plunges, and gathering spaces, as well as admission to the museum’s exhibits and galleries on festival dates._
    
*   #### Arrive at the National Nordic Museum
    
    Arrive at the National Nordic Museum freshly showered with a bathing suit and towel for inside the saunas, a robe and flip-flops/easily removed shoes to wear outside of the saunas, and a water bottle to stay hydrated.  We recommend coming already dressed to maximize sauna time, but we will have dressing rooms and small lockers available (just bring your own lock).
    
*   #### Enjoy the Festival
    
    Enjoy the saunas, cold-plunge, hang out around the campfires, and try the delicious offerings at Freya. 
    
*   #### Repeat & Depart
    
    *   _Repeat_ as you like.
        
    *   _Depart_ feeling refreshed and relaxed.

## FAQs

*   #### How much are tickets?
    
    General Admission - $79 each
    
    VIP Experience - $189 each
    
    \*\*Prices above are INCLUSIVE of all ticketing fees/surcharges and city/state taxes.
    
*   #### What is included with my ticket?
    
    **General Admission** includes 90 minutes of access to the sauna sessions, cold plunges, music, and festival programming. 
    
    **VIP Experiece** includes ALL-DAY access to the festival on Saturday or Sunday.  It also includes a festival robe and sauna hat, Nordic snack box, and your choice of beverage. 
    
    **All tickets** include admission to the National Nordic Museum’s exhibits and galleries on festival dates.
    
*   #### Are food & beverage options available?
    
    Food and beverages are available for purchase at **three locations throughout the festival**, making it easy to grab a drink, refuel between sauna sessions, or settle in and enjoy the festival atmosphere.
    
    Inside the museum, **Freya Cafe** is a daytime gathering place inspired by Nordic traditions and local ingredients. Enjoy espresso drinks, fresh pastries, a light lunch of seasonal items, and even handcrafted cocktails.
    
    Located right among the saunas, the **Nordic Flavor Lounge** is your spot to refuel between sessions. Enjoy Nordic-inspired favorites like Finnish salmon soup, Medisterpølse, venison skewers, and local oysters.
    
    Take a break from the heat at the **Terrace Lounge**, a relaxed gathering spot overlooking the festival action. Grab a Finnish Long Drink, warm Glögg, spiced cider, or another favorite from the bar while you soak in the vibes.
    
*   #### What should I bring?
    
    A bathing suit and towel for inside the saunas, a robe and flip-flops/easily removed shoes to wear outside of the saunas and inside the museum, and a water bottle to stay hydrated.
    
*   #### Are there changing rooms available?
    
    Yes. Changing areas will be available, along with small lockers for personal items (bring your own lock).
    
    We recommend coming dressed and ready to sauna.
    
*   #### Is there an age requirement?
    
    By purchasing a ticket or otherwise participating, you must be:
    
    *   At least 18 years of age, medically fit, and in good general health.
        
    *   If accompanying a minor participant (ages 13–17), the parent must confirm the child is medically fit and capable of participating safely in the Activities.
        
    
*   #### Will I "fit in" at the festival?
    
    **The Seattle Sauna Festival strives to create a safe and welcoming space for everyone.** Guests of all races, ethnicities, nationalities, and cultural backgrounds; all faiths, spiritual paths, and belief systems; all gender identities and expressions; all sexual orientations; all body types, sizes, and appearances; all physical, intellectual, sensory, and mental abilities; all socioeconomic statuses and class backgrounds; all immigration statuses, languages, and family structures; including Indigenous peoples, Black and Brown communities, immigrants and refugees, LGBTQIA+ individuals, neurodivergent folks, people with visible and invisible disabilities, people living at the intersections of multiple identities, and every other beautifully unique human being who wants to enjoy sauna culture—**are wholeheartedly welcomed, respected, and valued here.**
    
*   #### Is nudity allowed at the festival?
    
    No. All attendees must wear swimwear and must sit on a towel while in the saunas.
    
    A robe and footwear are required when inside the museum.
    
*   #### Are tickets refundable?
    
    While your tickets are not refundable, you can transfer them to others through your Eventbrite account.
    
*   #### What are the community guidelines?
    
    By attending the Seattle Sauna Festival, you agree to:
    
    *   **Use respectful language** and keep conversations free from offensive, aggressive, or derogatory remarks.  
          
        
    *   **Maintain appropriate behavior** and avoid excessive public displays of affection in shared areas.  
          
        
    *   **Honor personal boundaries** by refraining from uninvited or unwelcome physical contact.  
          
        
    *   **Be mindful of others’ comfort** by ensuring that your gaze, body language, or actions do not make fellow guests feel uneasy.
        
    
    Together, we can make the Seattle Sauna Festival a restorative, inclusive, and enjoyable experience for all.  Thank you!

### BEFORE THE SHOW: MARKETING

SUBMIT APPLICATION FOR EXHIBITOR DEMOS AT YOUR BOOTH

**Apply to Host a Demo at Your Booth** 

Registered exhibitors are invited to present live demonstrations of the products or technologies they are selling at their booth. Product demos are a great way to engage attendees, showcase your expertise, and highlight the value of your offerings. 

All approved product demos take place **within your exhibit space** and may be promoted in **Overland News’ printed show schedule** and the **event mobile app**. 

**Product Demo Rules & Regulations** 

To ensure a safe and positive experience for all attendees and exhibitors, the following rules apply to all product demonstrations: 

**General Guidelines** 

*   Demonstrations must be conducted **entirely within your assigned exhibit space**. 

*   Demos may not block or disrupt aisle traffic, common areas, or neighboring exhibitors. 

*   Exhibitors are responsible for providing appropriate safety measures to prevent injury to spectators. 

**Demo Content Requirements** 

*   Product demos must showcase a **product being sold at the exhibitor’s booth**. 

*   Submissions that are **educational in nature** (e.g., Recovery 101, How to Overland, etc.) will not be accepted, as these topics are part of the curated **general education program**. 

*   Exhibitors interested in teaching a class in the general education area should contact the Director of Programming at [**\[email protected\]**](https://www.overlandexpo.com/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#84e5fef1f6e1c4ebf2e1f6e8e5eae0e1fcf4ebaae7ebe9). 

**Safety, Fire & Compliance** 

*   Exhibitors must comply with **all local fire, safety, environmental, and health regulations**. 

*   Extra caution must be taken when demonstrating equipment with moving parts. 

*   **Wood-burning fires are not permitted.** 

*   Cooking demos using open flames must:  

*   Use propane tanks equipped with an on/off switch 

*   Comply with all local health department regulations 

*   A minimum **3-foot setback** must be maintained, or appropriate hazard barriers installed, to protect spectators. 

*   All demonstrations must be conducted by **qualified personnel only**. 

**Conduct & Approval** 

*   Attention-getting devices, stunts, or gimmicks that detract from the professional, educational, or business purpose of the show are prohibited. 

*   Exhibitors are encouraged to seek approval from Show Management for any activities that may be in question before the event.

**Scheduling & Promotion** 

*   All exhibitor demos must be **pre-approved by the Director of Programming** in order to be included in the event schedule and marketing materials. 

*   While time-slot requests may be submitted, they are not guaranteed. Scheduling priority is determined on a **first-come, first-served** basis based on completed applications.

FIRE PERMIT REQUIREMENTS

**TENTS – LESS THAN 400 SQ FT** 

Portable fire extinguishers REQUIRED (IFC 3104.12) and displayed in tent. 

At Ft. Tuthill, staking is NOT allowed, however all booth tents must be secured.  The weather is unpredictable, and the winds are often gusty. 

Structural stability and anchorage required. Tents must be adequately braced or anchored by manufacturer recommended product specs. (IFC 3103.3.9).  We highly recommend nothing less than 50lbs per each leg, this is a minimum for a 10×10. It is your responsibility to determine what is safe and secure for your own tent needs. 

Bring supplies for securing tents and displays properly.  

Large enclosed water containers (10 gallons or more) make excellent anchors for tents on asphalt and concrete.  Designated water fill stations will be available on-site. Be prepared to take your tent down, as needed, depending on severe weather conditions. 

**TENTS OVER 400 SQ FT** 

All 20×20ft (400sq ft) tent or larger, REQUIRE a tent permit. 

If you have a 20×20 (400sq ft) tent or larger, please [CONTACT US](https://www.overlandexpo.com/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#c7aea9a1a887a8b1a2b5aba6a9a3a2bfb7a8e9a4a8aa) regarding requirements.  

Your tent will be inspected by the Fire Marshall, all below requirements must be met or you may be asked to take your tent down.   

*   700 lbs. ballast on each tent leg 

*   *   A limited number are available for rent – $150 per ballast. Ballast rentals must be added to your order in the portal  

*   Proper way to secure tent to ballast (i.e. ropes/rachet straps)  
*   Fire Extinguisher with current up to date permit 
*   Illuminated Exit Sign (if the tent has walls) 
*   Fire Certification from tent manufacture 
*   Entire tent and weights/ballast must fit in designated booth space 

**COOKING GUIDELINES** 

No cooking is allowed within / under any tents and buildings, no exceptions. 

No cooking or open flame in or within 20 feet if open to the public (IFC 3104.7) 

No heating or cooking equipment within 10 ft. of exits (IFC 3104.15.3) 

Outdoor cooking that produces grease laden vapors or sparks located at least 20 ft. from tents (IFC 3104.15.6) 

**REQUIREMENTS FROM INTERNATIONAL FIRE CODE (IFC)** 

Permanently affixed label indicating size, type of fabric (IFC 3104.3) 

A membrane structure or tent shall have a permanently affixed label bearing the following information: 

1.  The identification of size and fabric or material  
2.  The names and addresses of the manufacturers of the tent or air-supported structure. 
3.  A statement that the fabric or material meet the requirements of section 3104.2 (Flame propagation performance testing and certification) 
4.  If treated, the date the fabric or material was last treated with flame-retardant solution, the trade name or kind of chemical used in treatment, name of person or firm treating the fabric or material and name of the testing agency and test standard by which the fabric or material was tested.   
5.  If untreated, a statement that no treatment was applied when the fabric or material met the requirements of section 3104.2 

**LP GAS CONTAINERS & COMBUSTIBLE LIQUIDS** 

Securing compressed gas containers, cylinders and tanks. (5303.5.3) Compressed gas containers, cylinders, and tanks shall be secured to prevent falling caused by contact, vibration, or seismic activity. Securing of compressed gas containers, cylinders and tanks shall be by; 1. To a fixed object with one or more straps 2. on a cart or other mobile device designed for movement of tanks 3. To or within a rack or framework, cabinet or other assembly designed for such use. 

LP gas containers must be located outside (IFC 3104.16.2) 

Small (under 500 gal.) LP containers at least 10 ft. from tent (IFC 3104.16.2.1) 

Large (over 500 gal.) LP containers at least 25 ft. from tent (IFC 3104.16.2.2) 

LP gas containers secured and protected from damage (IFC 3104.16.3) 

No flammable liquids or liquid fueled equipment shall be stored inside tents; storage of flammable and combustible liquids at least 50 ft. away (IFC 3104.17) 

No refueling within 20 ft. of the tent (IFC 3104.17.3) 

**DISPLAYING OF MOTOR VEHICLES**  

Liquid and gas fueled vehicles and equipment used for display under tents or membrane structure shall be in accordance with sections IFC 3107.15.1 through 3107.15.5.3. This includes any vehicles that are partially displayed under a covering, and they must also abide by the following: 

*   Vehicles or equipment shall not be fueled or defueled within tent or membrane structure 
*   Fuel in the fuel tank shall not exceed one-quarter of the tank capacity or 5 gallons (19 L), whichever is less 
*   The location of vehicles or equipment shall not obstruct means of egress

Overland Expo has partnered with [Showfleet](https://www.showfleet.com/ "https://www.showfleet.com/") to offer Vehicle Detailing for display vehicles.  Please use the [THIS FORM](https://www.overlandexpo.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Overland-West-Order-Form-2026.pdf) to request your services directly with Showfleet.

Please note Overland Expo is not responsible for any arrangement made with Showfleet, and exhibitors must order these services directly.  

NO STAKING YOUR BOOTH TENTS

**All tents must be secured (no staking) – no exceptions.  Weather is unpredictable and winds are often gusty.** 

Please make sure to bring supplies for securing tents and displays properly. Large enclosed water containers (10 gallons or more) make the best anchors for tents on asphalt and concrete. 

If you are using a 20×20 tent or larger, we would request that you let us know, so we can be aware and make sure all requirements are met before the Fire Marshall walkthrough.  Your tent will be inspected by the Fire Marshall, and if all of the below requirements are not met then you may be asked to take it down: 

*   700 lbs ballast on each tent leg. Limited supply available for rent. 
*   Limited number available for rent – $162.50 per ballast/ Forklift delivery additional charge. Must be added to your order before arrival onsite.
*   Proper way to secure tent to ballast
*   Fire Extinguisher with current up to date permit
*   Exit Sign (if the tent has walls)
*   Fire Certification from tent manufacture
*   Tent anchors must fit in designated booth space

FIRE PERMIT REQUIREMENTS

**TENTS – LESS THAN 400 SQ FT** 

Portable fire extinguishers REQUIRED (IFC 3104.12) and displayed in tent. 

At Ft. Tuthill, staking is NOT allowed, however all booth tents must be secured.  The weather is unpredictable, and the winds are often gusty. 

Structural stability and anchorage required. Tents must be adequately braced or anchored by manufacturer recommended product specs. (IFC 3103.3.9).  We highly recommend nothing less than 50lbs per each leg, this is a minimum for a 10×10. It is your responsibility to determine what is safe and secure for your own tent needs. 

Bring supplies for securing tents and displays properly.  

Large enclosed water containers (10 gallons or more) make excellent anchors for tents on asphalt and concrete.  Designated water fill stations will be available on-site. Be prepared to take your tent down, as needed, depending on severe weather conditions. 

**TENTS OVER 400 SQ FT** 

All 20×20ft (400sq ft) tent or larger, REQUIRE a tent permit. 

If you have a 20×20 (400sq ft) tent or larger, please [CONTACT US](https://www.overlandexpo.com/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#8ae3e4ece5cae5fceff8e6ebe4eeeff2fae5a4e9e5e7) regarding requirements.  

Your tent will be inspected by the Fire Marshall, all below requirements must be met or you may be asked to take your tent down.   

*   700 lbs. ballast on each tent leg 
    *   A limited number are available for rent – $150 per ballast. Ballast rentals must be added to your order in the portal  
*   Proper way to secure tent to ballast (i.e. ropes/rachet straps)  
*   Fire Extinguisher with current up to date permit 
*   Illuminated Exit Sign (if the tent has walls) 
*   Fire Certification from tent manufacture 
*   Entire tent and weights/ballast must fit in designated booth space 

**COOKING GUIDELINES** 

No cooking is allowed within / under any tents and buildings, no exceptions. 

No cooking or open flame in or within 20 feet if open to the public (IFC 3104.7) 

No heating or cooking equipment within 10 ft. of exits (IFC 3104.15.3) 

Outdoor cooking that produces grease laden vapors or sparks located at least 20 ft. from tents (IFC 3104.15.6) 

**REQUIREMENTS FROM INTERNATIONAL FIRE CODE (IFC)** 

Permanently affixed label indicating size, type of fabric (IFC 3104.3) 

A membrane structure or tent shall have a permanently affixed label bearing the following information: 

1.  The identification of size and fabric or material  
2.  The names and addresses of the manufacturers of the tent or air-supported structure. 
3.  A statement that the fabric or material meet the requirements of section 3104.2 (Flame propagation performance testing and certification) 
4.  If treated, the date the fabric or material was last treated with flame-retardant solution, the trade name or kind of chemical used in treatment, name of person or firm treating the fabric or material and name of the testing agency and test standard by which the fabric or material was tested.   
5.  If untreated, a statement that no treatment was applied when the fabric or material met the requirements of section 3104.2 

**LP GAS CONTAINERS & COMBUSTIBLE LIQUIDS** 

Securing compressed gas containers, cylinders and tanks. (5303.5.3) Compressed gas containers, cylinders, and tanks shall be secured to prevent falling caused by contact, vibration, or seismic activity. Securing of compressed gas containers, cylinders and tanks shall be by; 1. To a fixed object with one or more straps 2. on a cart or other mobile device designed for movement of tanks 3. To or within a rack or framework, cabinet or other assembly designed for such use. 

LP gas containers must be located outside (IFC 3104.16.2) 

Small (under 500 gal.) LP containers at least 10 ft. from tent (IFC 3104.16.2.1) 

Large (over 500 gal.) LP containers at least 25 ft. from tent (IFC 3104.16.2.2) 

LP gas containers secured and protected from damage (IFC 3104.16.3) 

No flammable liquids or liquid fueled equipment shall be stored inside tents; storage of flammable and combustible liquids at least 50 ft. away (IFC 3104.17) 

No refueling within 20 ft. of the tent (IFC 3104.17.3)

**DISPLAYING OF MOTOR VEHICLES**  

Liquid and gas fueled vehicles and equipment used for display under tents or membrane structure shall be in accordance with sections IFC 3107.15.1 through 3107.15.5.3. This includes any vehicles that are partially displayed under a covering, and they must also abide by the following: 

*   Vehicles or equipment shall not be fueled or defueled within tent or membrane structure 
*   Fuel in the fuel tank shall not exceed one-quarter of the tank capacity or 5 gallons (19 L), whichever is less 
*   The location of vehicles or equipment shall not obstruct means of egress  

FOOD PARTICIPATION / SAMPLING

All rules and regulations for sampling at Overland Expo can be found on the Sample Request Form below. **Anyone wishing to sample at Overland Expo West must submit the form by Friday, April 16, 2027**

[SUBMIT SAMPLE REQUEST FORM](https://app.smartsheet.com/b/form/be003ef0584645f8a27f1bdcffcb673e)

### ON-SITE: BOOTH PLANNING

YOUR BOOTH FOOTPRINT

Your booth display **must** fit into your purchased space. This includes any weights that secure your tent down, display items, vehicles, and trailer (if applicable). 

BOOTH ETIQUETTE

**QUIET HOURS:** Quiet hours start at 10 pm and are strictly enforced.  

**MUSIC:** Very low volume music is acceptable, but do not disturb your neighboring exhibitors. 

**DISPLAY:** Your display must be a family-friendly exhibit. Absolutely no profanity, no sexual content (including innuendo), no scantily clad “spokespersons” either in person or in pictures, and no copyright infringement upon the Overland Expo logo / brand is allowed. 

**GENERATORS:** Exhibitor Generators are allowed as long as they are quiet. If your generator is loud, you will be asked to turn it off during show hours. If you are camping in your booth, your generator must be turned off by 10 p.m. If you are carrying extra fuel in your booth for the generator, you are also required to have a fire extinguisher. 

LOAD-IN & EVENT HOURS

**EXHIBITOR LOAD-IN FOR ALL EXHIBITORS:** 

*   **Wednesday, May 13, 2026, Noon to 6pm:** No early arrivals will be allowed in until NOON, other than large semis. If you will be bringing a semi for your booth space or product, then please contact your sales representative before the event so they may expect your arrival. If you have a trailer that is part of your booth display, we highly encourage you to arrive and place the trailer in your booth space on Wednesday. 
*   **Thursday, May 14, 2026, 8am to 6pm:** Load-in will continue.
*   **SEMI RIGS** need to arrive by 9am on Wednesday to get placed before we start load-in at noon.  
*   **Moving in or setting up will not be allowed on Friday before gates open.** All exhibitors must be moved in and set up by Thursday 6:00 p.m. 

**EVENT HOURS:** 

*   Friday – 9am-5pm 

*   Saturday – 9am-5pm 

*   Sunday – 9am-3pm 

Exhibitors are to be in their booths and ready to go before Event opens. We suggest that you arrive no later than 30 mins before Event opening to be prepared for the crowd. 

**DISPLAY VEHICLES:** 

*   Display vehicles are vehicles that are part of a booth display, that fit into the booth dimensions and have been designated with a “Display Vehicle” hang tag. 

*   If the vehicle does not go into your display space, then it does not come into the show area.  All other exhibitor vehicles must be parked in the designated exhibitor parking lot and are required to have a parking pass. If in need of a parking pass, please purchase one in the Show Office.  

*   Display Vehicles will be allowed to enter the show area for booth space placement from 7 a.m. – 8 a.m. on event days.   No other vehicles are permitted to enter the show gate / area on event days other than the display vehicles with display vehicle hang tags.  

*   No vehicles will be permitted to enter the show area after 7 a.m. on any event day.  There will be no exceptions.  Any display vehicles arriving after 8 a.m. on an event days will only be permitted to park in the designated exhibitor parking lot.  

*   Display Vehicles are not permitted to leave the show area until an hour **after** the event has closed to the public due to safety purposes.  

*   It is highly encouraged to leave any Display Vehicle in your booth all weekend (instead of driving this vehicle back and forth into town/hotel) to avoid any issues with getting your Display Vehicle back in your booth space. 

HAPPY HOURS

**THURSDAY, FRIDAY, AND SATURDAY FROM 5 – 7 PM**: All nightly Happy Hour events will take place at the Oasis Bar & Food Court. Show your exhibitor badge to receive a free drink ticket to the bar. Alcoholic and non-alcoholic options are available.  

ARRIVAL INFO

**Arrival documents will be available approximately 30 days out from the event.** We will send them out to the main contact email that is registered within the exhibitor portal.  

**If you need to change your main contact in the system, please contact your sales representative to take care of that for you.** 

PRODUCT PICK UP & AFTER-HOURS SECURITY PHONE NUMBER: (317) 518-3568

**PRODUCT PICKUP**: If you have sold an oversize item that your customer will need help bringing to their campground / car, then call this number and a member of our staff will be able to assist with a shuttle / cart.   

**AFTER-HOURS SECURITY**: If you are in need of assistance from security after show hours (overnight), then call this number and our roaming security will immediately assist you on-site. 

ALCOHOL / PARTIES / ORGANIZED GATHERINGS

**You must inform Show Management** of any intent to host a gathering that includes the distribution of alcohol on venue premises and obtain a permit. Any serving of alcohol **must** be organized and managed through the event venue.   

Due to liquor licenses and rules set by the Alcohol and Beverage Commission in each state, there are strict rules on distribution of alcohol.  Any organized party not registered with Show Management and not complying with the rules will be considered illegal and dealt with by the County Sheriff and will be shut down immediately.  **There is no distribution of alcohol allowed on venue premises via any other channel other than the event venue’s alcohol provider.** 

PACK IT IN, PACK IT OUT
