# ABOUT US

# JUNCTION ARTS FESTIVAL

Junction Arts Festival is Northern Tasmania’s premier multi-arts festival, transforming Launceston’s unique spaces into extraordinary creative experiences each spring. Since 2010, we’ve been lighting up Launceston with immersive performances, visual arts, music, and unexpected experiences in unusual places.

Born as part of the Regional Arts Australia National Conference, Junction’s immediate success sparked its evolution into an annual celebration that captures the essence of Tasmania’s vibrant arts scene. As an independent, not-for-profit organisation since 2012, we’ve grown from a local initiative into a yearly festival in lutruwita/Tasmania.

We create a kaleidoscope of artistic experiences where the familiar becomes extraordinary. As winter retreats and spring emerges, Junction celebrates the dance between light and dark, inviting audiences to discover art in unexpected places throughout Launceston. Our festival is more than a series of events – it’s a journey that ignites creativity and brings our community together.

# Our Connection to Place

Operating on Kanamaluka/River Tamar, we acknowledge the Palawa/Tasmanian Aboriginal people as the original and ongoing owners of lutruwita/Tasmania. We pay our respects to elders past and present, acknowledge that sovereignty has never been ceded, and actively support Truth Telling and Treaty processes.

# Our FUTURE

With support from Events Tasmania and City of Launceston, Junction continues to evolve. Each September, for four nights and days, we transform our city into a creative hub where locals and visitors alike come together to experience extraordinary moments, forge new connections, and create lasting memories. Our festival brings fresh energy to Launceston’s historic spaces, celebrating the unique spirit of our community while adding another vibrant chapter to our city’s story.

# BOARD OF DIRECTORS

Junction Arts Festival is guided by a passionate, skilled board of directors who volunteer their time and expertise to enrich Northern Tasmania’s cultural landscape. Our board members bring diverse professional backgrounds and deep community connections to help shape Junction’s vision and future.

These dedicated individuals share a common belief in the transformative power of the arts to create a more vibrant, connected, and liveable city. Their combined experience spans arts management, business development, community engagement, and cultural leadership – all vital elements in steering Junction’s growth and success.

Together, they work to ensure Junction continues to evolve as a dynamic force in Tasmania’s cultural scene, supporting local artists, engaging our community, and creating extraordinary experiences that make Launceston shine.

# GET INVOLVED

# volunteer at junction

**Applications for 2026 are now open!** 

Volunteers play such a big role in shaping Junction’s story.

Every year we are overwhelmed by the energy, hard work and passion they bring to the Festival in a variety of roles. 

If you love music, experiencing art, or being involved in your community, theres something to draw your interest at junction.

Check out our Volunteer EOI application

[VOLUNTEER EOI](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSep0C03UsSgWyOZL6kKMqav0jCs0-mXKqB_732bYjwRSk8Fsg/viewform?usp=sharing&ouid=103861042177047371489)

# FESTIVAL EMPLOYMENT REGISTER!

Junction arts festival is on the look out for some excellent people who love a fast paced environment and working across different departments.

**ROLES WE’RE LOOKING TO FILL INCLUDE:**

FRONT OF HOUSE STAFF –

Handle ticket scanning, wristbanding, and guest flow

BAR STAFF –

Run our festival bars with efficiency and good vibes

SITE CREW –

Seliver Junctions production elements during the festival as well as assist in Bump In and Out

[STAFF EOI](https://f331c221015337.au.deputy.com/jobs#/)

# group sax

Got a sax? Got Nerve?

We’re pulling together a group of community saxophone players for something special at this year’s festival, and we want you in it!

The deal:

Saturday 19th September, Prince’s Square

11am – 12pm (rehearsal)

12:30pm – 1:30pm (performance)

Between now and then: learn one simple walking tune and one final banger. We’ll send them soon…

Keen? Fill in the form below. 

Toot toot!

[GROUP SAX SIGN UP](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeSocGqP8KLaF_z_gyfgJ86msujEKI3U2qlnXtRzHzP5sUSHQ/viewform)

# History

The Tropical Fruits Inc, established in 1988, is the premier LGBTIQ community group in the Northern Rivers in NSW. We are a not-for-profit, incorporated association that holds regular events for our diverse members and guests. We are a self funding, independent and voluntary organisation.

**History, Herstory, Ourstory**

**Early Years**

For over three decades, the Northern Rivers region has had an organised gay and lesbian history. In March 1981, the first openly gay and lesbian event was advertised in _Nimbin News_, announcing a bar-be-que at Whian Whian for members of the 'gay and transgendered' communities. In June 1981, a meeting was held at the Bluebird Restaurant in Lismore. The Northern Rivers Gay Group (NRGG) was formed with a committee being elected. NRGG grew quickly, organising pinics, bar-be-ques, beach parties and balls.

From this time through to 1988, the social calendar for the gay, lesbian and transgender (g/l/t) communities was busy. A number of venues and farms operated as meeting places, including the Bluebird and Doubt Dutch Restauarnts in Lismore, Mandala near Uki and Lawrenece Station near Grafton.

Social groups came and went. At the end of 1982, Northern Rivers Gay Group was disbanded. Later, Summerland Gay Women was formed, met at Double Dutch and later metamorphosed into Summerland Gay People, which also folded when Double Dutch was closed.

Political controversies occurred through these years too. In 1984, the then-editor of the _Northern Star_ published a series of homophobic editorials around the gay and lesbian communities and the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV). The local gay radio show was also involved in a debate concerning content of programmes.

**Tropical Fruits is born**

In June 1988, Tropical Fruits was formed following the disbandment of Summerland Gay People. Using bands of faithful volunteers as its organisation principle, Fruits' membership and reputation grew quickly through the later 1980s and 1990s by holding regular parties and picnics at local beaches or members' farms and dances at country halls in the area.

In 1997, the New Year's Eve party was moved from Repentance Creek Hall to the Rugby Union Club in Lismore. Rainbow Circus 1 was created with two marquees, fireworks, luscious sounds, live music and other performances.

2002 was a regenerative time. At the Annual General Meeting (AGM), a new committee was elected with Erif Benham (Saint Erif) emerging as an indomitable community organiser. In 2003, Rainbow Circus was moved to the Lismore Showgrounds, becoming the signature Tropical Fruits' New Years Eve party with two nights of parties in themed auditoriums, live music, cabaret, art exhibition, fire works and performances.

The administration of Tropical Fruits finally moved out of member's loungerooms when the Clubhouse (known as "The Fruitbowl") was opened in December 2004. It rapidly become a de facto community centre with an office, workship space and storage area. It now also functions as a meeting place for local LGBTIQ groups as well as regular activities like Crafternoons.

In 2008, Saint Erif was diagnosed with a terminal illness and tragically passed in January 2009. She was instrumental in establishing the land fund for a future Fruits' home. Later in 2009, it was renamed the Erif Benham Memorial Land Fund. Also in 2009, Fresh Fruits, the most recent youth group within Fruits, was formed and the Queer Fruits Film Festival was added to the end-of-year party, thus making it a festival.

Through all these years, Fruits' has expanded with part-time staff helping with administration and event organisation. By 2011, there were 17 sub-committees, each one working around particular areas like governance or Fruitopia Fair Day. In late 2011, the Fruitbowl was purchased by Tropical Fruits, this being the first time that a regional LGBTIQ group in New South Wales (possibly Australia) has bought its own home.  In 2016, the vacant block next door was purchased, with a view to developing the paddock for much needed parking, storage, craft and meeting spaces.

After several years of discussion and consultation, in 2017 the members voted to change the governing objects of the Tropical Fruits constitution to Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Trans\*, Intersex and Queer (LGBTIQ).

 [![Vanlife Gathering 2026](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/547a7a53e4b0b93ff702af56/2a35f5ef-c2fc-4b27-9a1d-bf95c9982e64/Vanlife2026_Poster.jpg?format=2500w)](https://www.vanlife.com.au/vanlife-gatherings/australian-natural-bridgebundjalung-vanlife-gathering-kpb9f)

A$140.00

**Vanlife Gathering 2026**  
October 2–5, 2026 | Natural Bridge, Yugambeh/Bundjalung Country  
Vanlife Diaries is excited to announce the return of our annual Vanlife Gathering for 2026!  
Join us for three nights and four days of connection, adventure, music, workshops, storytelling and community in one of Australia’s most beautiful natural settings.  
Nestled in the lush hinterland between the Gold Coast and Byron Bay, Natural Bridge offers the perfect off-grid escape. Surrounded by untouched bushland, native wildlife, walking trails and the magic of the Australian outdoors, this unique location becomes our home for the weekend.  
Swim in the natural waterholes, explore nearby Natural Bridge National Park, relax around the campfire, meet like-minded travellers and enjoy the simple things that make life on the road so special.  
This is more than an event — it’s a gathering of people who love adventure, creativity, alternative ways of living and building genuine connections.  
  
**What to Expect**  
We’re bringing together an incredible line-up of workshops, music, activities and community experiences, including:  
Live music and entertainment  Campfire conversations and storytelling  Cultural connection and learning  Solar and off-grid power workshops with @victron\_energy  Conservation education and documentary screenings with @surfridernorthernrivers  Cultural conversations with Uncle Warren from @yarnaustralia  Yoga and wellbeing sessions  Coffee and food trucks  Epic community raffle  Art, creativity and workshops  Shared meals and community connection  
And plenty more announcements are coming soon!  
  
**Community, Connection & Giving Back**  
Vanlife Gatherings have always been about creating a welcoming, inclusive and safe space where everyone belongs.  
A percentage of proceeds from the event and our community raffle will go towards supporting causes that align with our values, including conservation initiatives and our ongoing commitment to cultural connection and education.  
We believe in leaving places better than we find them, supporting local communities and creating experiences that bring people together.  
  
**Tickets & Camping Information**  
Your event ticket includes:  
Three nights of camping.  Access to all event activities and workshops.  Live music and entertainment.  Community experiences.  Catered lunch experience  
Tickets are available online only before the event.  
Early Bird tickets will be available until September 1, 2026 (the first day of Spring).  
Our previous Gatherings have sold out, so we recommend securing your spot early.  
This is a family-friendly event and everyone is welcome.  
Bring your:  
Van  Bus  Truck  Car  Tent  Swag  Motorbike  RV anything you are comfortable in.  
The only requirements are an open mind, a love for adventure and a willingness to meet some amazing people.  
Children under 16 are welcome free of charge.  
  
**Camping Facilities**  
Camping is on unpowered sites.  
Facilities include:  
● Toilets onsite  
● Access to beautiful natural surroundings  
● Walking trails and swimming areas nearby  
Please note:  
● There is no drinking water available onsite — please bring your own supply.  
● Dogs are welcome but must remain on a lead at all times.

This is a leave no trace events so anything packed in with you, needs to leave with you as well.  
**  
Want to Be Part of the Gathering?**  
We’re always looking to collaborate with passionate people, creators and businesses who share our values.  
If you are a:  
Van builder  Outdoor brand  Product maker  Artist or creator  Food vendor  Sustainable business  Workshop host  
and would like to partner, sponsor or have a stall at the 2026 Vanlife Gathering, we’d love to hear from you.  
We only partner with brands and businesses that genuinely connect with and support our community.  
Volunteers are also needed to help bring the event to life. If you’d like to lend a hand and be part of the team, please email us — we’d love to he[ar from you.  
VanlifeDiariesAustralia@gmail.com](mailto:VanlifeDiariesAustralia@gmail.com)  
Financial Hardship Tickets  
We want this gathering to remain accessible to our community.  
If you’re experiencing financial difficulty and would love to attend, please reach out to our team.  
Limited assistance tickets are available.  
[VanlifeDiariesAustralia@gmail.com](mailto:VanlifeDiariesAustralia@gmail.com)  
  
**Come Join Us**  
Make new friends. Reconnect with old ones. Share stories around the fire. Learn something new. Explore the region. Swim, hike, relax and enjoy the beauty of Australia’s outdoors.  
Vanlife Gathering is a place where strangers become friends, stories are shared and memories are made.  
Start planning your Gold Coast / Byron Bay road trip — we can’t wait to welcome you to Natural Bridge in 2026.  
Vanlife Diaries — connecting and building community with our international road-tripping family.

## FAQ

### Frequently Asked Questions

#### How can I become a member of the ESF?

The first condition to become a member of the ESF is to be a recognised national surfing association, accepted as such by the Executive Committee of the ESF. An application should be sent to the ESF with a copy of its charter or constitution and proof that the applicant organisation has been recognised by their governement as the national governing body for the sport of surf riding in that country. Please consult the MEMBERSHIP section of our memorandum: [download](https://www.eurosurfing.org/images/documents/2021-Memorandum-Articles-updated-December-2017.pdf).

#### How do I qualify for a national team?

A competitor may only represent a country if he/she holds a passport or national identification card issued by the national government of that country. A national identification card must clearly show nationality or citizenship of the country. A competitor who is a national of more than one country at the same time may represent any of them, as he/she may elect. More on this in our rule book (pag 29/30): [download](https://www.eurosurfing.org/images/documents/RuleBook_ESF_april2022_update.pdf).

Then of course there is the matter of being selected for the national team. This naturally depends on several factors, "merit" ranked surely as the outstanding one. Please make yourself noted to the national governing body for surf in your country. Consult our [members page](https://www.eurosurfing.org/members) for contact information.

#### How do I become a surfing judge?

To set yourself on the path to become an international surfing judge you normally start at the local level. Join your local surf club and with the help of established names in your club start judging local surf contests. The next step is to consult the national governing body for surfing in your country and attend a judging course to be ranked and registered as a national judge. Consult our [members page](https://www.eurosurfing.org/members) for contact information. With time and dedication we hope you can make it to our European Championship events!

#### What are the requirements to hold an ESF event?

Applications to host a European Championship should be submitted in writing to the Secretary General of the ESF in time to be presented at the AGM of the ESF and at least 3 years before the proposed championships take place.  
2 years prior to the event, the ESF AGM will review the applications and award the Championships to whichever country it so wishes.  
1 year prior to the event, the host nation must make a presentation the ESF Executive showing how their preparations for the event are progressing. They must give details of the contest locations, infrastructure, food and accommodation etc.  
If the ESF is not satisfied that sufficient progress has been made or that there are good reasons to suppose that the organisers will not be able to fulfil their original promises, then the ESF Executive may award the event to another country if another country is able and willing to host the event.

#### Can I sponsor an event?

We absolutely welcome sponsorships to our events. We must of course make sure the product and/or brand does not conflict with any sponsors already on board with the event. Also the product and/or brand must not jeopardize in any way the good name and standing of the ESF. Please submit a query through our online form ([click here](https://www.eurosurfing.org/contact)) and we will get back too you as soon as possible.

#### Can I advertise on your website?

Currently we do not yet have a defined model for online advertising at eurosurfing.org but in the future we will be opening up this possbility and welcome any application already submitted. We must of course make sure the product and/or brand does not jeopardize in any way the good name and standing of the ESF. Please submit a query through our online form ([click here](https://www.eurosurfing.org/contact)) and we will get back too you as soon as possible.

## European Surfing Federation  
The Objects

To establish and maintain a European federation to promote the interests of surfing in all its forms throughout all countries of Europe to which all recognised national surfing associations/bodies concerned with the sport of surf riding, surfing or its related activities may gain affiliation.

[Know More](https://www.eurosurfing.org/our-goals)

![](/images/objects/flag.svg)

To encourage the formation of national surfing associations/bodies in the individual countries to promote, co-ordinate and control the activities of organised surfing within their own countries.

![](/images/objects/book.svg)

To promote uniformity of laws of control and regulation of surfing and surf riding throughout Europe, by encouraging national surfing institutions, organisations and associations to adopt the ESF’s established laws, rules and standards.

![](/images/objects/edit.svg)

To make and amend rules as appropriate for the conducting of surfing contests and other surfing events, programmes and commissioners in Europe.

![](/images/objects/globe.svg)

To co-ordinate the international activities of national surfing associations and bodies providing a forum for arranging international contests and organising the European surfing calendar within the international rules and calendar.

# **Kiwiburn** | New Zealand’s Regional Burning Man Event

Kiwiburn is a participatory festival, where we, the participants, bring and make the things that we want to have here. There are no spectators, no headline acts — just a temporary world built on creativity, gifting, and radical self-expression.

**The next event will be held from 27 January to 1 February 2027 in Hunterville.**

[Wait, what is Kiwiburn??](https://kiwiburn.com/about/about-the-event/what-is-kiwiburn/)

[2027 event theme](https://kiwiburn.com/the-event/at-the-burn/theme/)

## Kiwiburn is built on the ten principles of Burning Man

![](https://kiwiburn.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/wick-radical-inclusion.webp)

## Radical Inclusion

Anyone may be a part of Burning Man. We welcome and respect the stranger. No prerequisites exist for participation in our community.

![](https://kiwiburn.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/wick-gifting-150x150-1.webp)

## Gifting

Burning Man is devoted to acts of gift giving. The value of a gift is unconditional. Gifting does not contemplate a return or an exchange for something of equal value.

![](https://kiwiburn.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/wick-decommodification-150x150-1.webp)

## Decommodification

In order to preserve the spirit of gifting, our community seeks to create social environments that are unmediated by commercial sponsorships, transactions, or advertising. We stand ready to protect our culture from such exploitation. We resist the substitution of consumption for participatory experience.

![](https://kiwiburn.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/wick-radical-self-reliance-150x150-1.webp)

## Radical Self-reliance

Burning Man encourages the individual to discover, exercise and rely on his or her inner resources.

![](https://kiwiburn.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/wick-radical-self-expression-150x150-1.webp)

## Radical Self-expression

Radical self-expression arises from the unique gifts of the individual. No one other than the individual or a collaborating group can determine its content. It is offered as a gift to others. In this spirit, the giver should respect the rights and liberties of the recipient.

![](https://kiwiburn.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/wick-communal-effort-150x150-1.webp)

## Communal Effort

Our community promotes social interaction through collective acts of gifting. We value creative cooperation and collaboration. We strive to produce, promote and protect social networks, public spaces, works of art, and methods of communication that support such interaction.

![](https://kiwiburn.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/wick-civic-responsibility-150x150-1.webp)

## Civic Responsibility

We value civil society. Community members who organise events should assume responsibility for public welfare and endeavour to communicate civic responsibilities to participants. Organisers must also assume responsibility for abiding by national law and district bylaws.

![](https://kiwiburn.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/wick-leaving-no-trace-150x150-1.webp)

## Leaving No Trace

Our community respects the environment. We are committed to leaving no physical trace of our activities wherever we gather. We clean up after ourselves and endeavor, whenever possible, to leave such places in a better condition than when we found them.

![](https://kiwiburn.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/wick-participation-150x150-1.webp)

## Participation

Our community is committed to a radically participatory ethic. We believe that transformative change, whether in the individual or in society, can occur only through the medium of deeply personal participation in experience. We achieve being through doing. Everyone is invited to work. Everyone is invited to play. We make the world real through actions that open the heart.

![](https://kiwiburn.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/wick-immediacy-150x150-1.webp)

## Immediacy

Immediate experience is, in many ways, the most important touchstone of value in our culture. We seek to overcome barriers that stand between us and a recognition of our inner selves, appreciation of the reality of those around us, participation in society, and contact with a natural world exceeding human powers. No idea can substitute for this experience.

## Mission Statement and Brief History

[European Surfing Federation](https://www.eurosurfing.org/about/9-esf "Article Category")

28 February 2021

 Hits: 47287

Share:

*   [Facebook](http://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https://www.eurosurfing.org/about)
    
*   [Twitter](http://twitter.com/share?url=https://www.eurosurfing.org/about&text=Mission%20Statement%20and%20Brief%20History)
    
*   [Google+](https://plus.google.com/share?url=https://www.eurosurfing.org/about "Share On Google Plus")
    

Our mission is to establish and maintain a EUROPEAN SURFING FEDERATION to promote the interests of surfing in all its forms throughout all the countries of Europe.

The ESF was formed in 1972,when surfing in Europe was still a new and undeveloped activity….when each Country was ‘going it alone’ in organising their National Surfing Championships…before communicating became so easy…before even videos of surfing were available never mind live webcasts. Then – as now – it was made up of representatives from its Member Nations, and was the amalgamation of all that early expertise and energy to organise and run the EUROPEAN SURFING CHAMPIONSHIPS, which it has done successfully from 1972 to the present day.

The role of the ESF has expanded to include encouraging the formation of a Surfing Association/Body in each European Country, to promote safety in surfing, and develop coaching and judging strategies and courses alongside its many European Titles and Surfing Tours.

The Championships – known as EUROSURF, was first run by Jersey in 1969, with only Men and Women Champions. It has now grown into Open and Junior Eurosurfs – held in successive years and includes age categories from Under 14, together with Bodyboards and Longboards. There is also a European Tour of Bodyboard –ETB , a European Tour of Longboard – ETL and a European Tour of Surfing – ETS all operating successfully. 2016  saw the introduction of a EuroSUP Championships which includes Surfing, Technical and Distance paddling events.

Details on our mission and role in the "Memorandum of Association of EUROPEAN SURFING FEDERATION":

As we prepare for another exciting edition of the street festival, we are thrilled to welcome our first female director, Bianca Bailey, to lead our festival into its next chapter of vibrancy, community, and celebration.

Bianca brings a wealth of knowledge to the role, having been a part of the CubaDupa team since 2020, with a deep passion for the arts and the Cuba Street community. With her dynamic style and innovative approach, we are confident that she will continue to elevate CubaDupa as a cornerstone of Wellington’s vibrant cultural arts landscape.

Bianca has an extensive background in the arts and event management, having previously held key roles at Stroma, Performance Arcade, Eyegum Music Collective & Ignite Pōneke. We are particularly proud to note that she comes from within our own organisation, exemplifying our commitment to supporting and elevating practitioners who have worked with us before. Meanwhile, she also fosters her own music career with projects such as Wiri Donna, F.A.I.R.Y & Lilith. She has been instrumental in fostering community engagement, curating diverse artistic programs, and driving audience growth. ## Contacto

## BAUM FEST ES UN FESTIVAL REFERENTE A NIVEL EUROPEO DE TENDENCIAS URBANAS

**Baum Fest / Barcelona Tattoo Expo es un festival referente a nivel europeo de tendencias urbanas.**

Nace en 1996 bajo el nombre de Barcelona Tattoo Show en cocheras de Sants, y desde sus inicios integra otras tendencias como el Graffiti y los espectáculos más underground en esos tiempos.

25 años después, bajo el nombre de Baum Fest, por el festival han pasado más de 8.000 artistas de todas las partes del mundo que han tatuado, pintado, bailado o competido en las diferentes zonas que componen el festival. Nos han visitado más de 250.000 visitantes que han podido ver en directo el arte que se respira en Baum Fest.

Este año, celebramos el 28 aniversario con la ilusión de cumplir muchos más y sin perder el objetivo principal que marcó el inicio de este proyecto.

La normalización y profesionalización del sector del tatuaje en España y las diferentes tendencias urbanas.

**El tatuaje ya no es un estigma, pero tampoco una moda.**

**La moda es pasajera, el tatuaje es para siempre.**

## FREQUENT QUESTIONS

We receive many questions before you buy your tickets, so here are the answers to the most frequently asked questions we receive.

If your question is not answered, please contact us!

[contact](https://baumfest.com/en/contact/)

[How can I get a tattoo at the convention?

](https://baumfest.com/language/en/#expand-862db7d)

Go to the artist directory on the website. There you will find all the artists who will attend the 2024 edition. Contact them directly to make an appointment at the event!

[If I get a tattoo at the convention, do I have to pay an entrance fee?

](https://baumfest.com/language/en/#expand-64e6c3b)

Yes, it is mandatory to purchase a ticket to the venue. Depending on your appointment with the artist, you must buy the ticket for the day. In case you have to attend more than one day, since the piece to be tattooed will take many hours, you must purchase the tickets for the days you will attend.

[Can I enter and leave the convention?

](https://baumfest.com/language/en/#expand-0819082)

Yes, when you arrive at the venue and validate your ticket, you will be given a wristband according to the type of ticket you purchase. Without taking it off, you will be able to go in and out of the venue at any time during the convention hours.

[Are children's tickets for all three days?

](https://baumfest.com/language/en/#expand-8cfbab4)

No, the children’s tickets are for one day only. Children under 12 enter for free, and those aged 12 to 16 have a reduced-price ticket.

markdown:
FAQ – Soundsplash

[Tickets](https://soundsplash.flicket.co.nz/)

[![](https://soundsplash.co.nz/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/SS_OG_logo_white@2x.png)](https://soundsplash.co.nz/)

[](https://soundsplash.co.nz/faqs/#elementor-action%3Aaction%3Dpopup%3Aopen%26settings%3DeyJpZCI6IjMyNiIsInRvZ2dsZSI6ZmFsc2V9)

# faq

*   [](https://www.instagram.com/soundsplashnz/)
*   [](https://www.facebook.com/soundsplashnz)

**One of Aotearoa’s longest running all ages festivals, Soundsplash returns for another unforgettable weekend of music, art, and community!** 

**Soundsplash is an all-ages event and runs over two days and two nights in beautiful Raglan, bringing you a world-class mix of musicians, DJs and artists for an UNFORGETTABLE WEEKEND of live music and freedom.**

**For the ultimate Soundsplash experience, stay on site at one of our many campgrounds. From the on site camp store and showers to awesome food stalls in the kai village we have everything you need to cater for an epic weekend with your mates!**

### **FAQ**

## General Info

**Soundsplash Festival returns to Raglan’s Wainui Reserve over the weekend of January 22-24 January, 2027.**

![](https://soundsplash.co.nz/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/SS25-WTB6-2-819x1024.png)

## Getting to Soundsplash

**S****oundsplash Festival is held at Wainui Reserve in Raglan with access via Ngarunui Beach Rd. It is very important to keep the main road up to the festival clear of congestion for emergency services. Please respect the directions given below to ensure the smoothest possible entry into Soundsplash.** 

**Expect traffic delays, potentially lasting an hour or more, when entering through the gates. We appreciate your patience as we strive to expedite the process and get everyone inside as quickly as possible.**

**_Important note: It is crucial that all drop-offs and pickups occur at the Raglan Airfield to prevent traffic congestion and reduce long wait times._**

**Travel times from:**

**Auckland CBD:** 2-2.5 hours  
**Hamilton CBD:** 45 minutes

By Car

Please do not use a GPS system to get to the festival as there are different instructions into the site depending on your ticket (and whether you are being dropped off, parking onsite, or parking off site.) Instead, please refer to the temporary festival road signage on your way to the festival site and follow any instructions from our festival communications team.

[**On site parking**](https://maps.app.goo.gl/wFiGwPgRkxyMwqP69) is limited and only available to on site camping pass holders that have also purchased parking passes. **Don’t forget** to add parking tickets to your purchase when you complete your order.

**Off site parking** is located at the [Raglan Airfield](https://www.google.com/maps/dir//Raglan+Airfield+\(RAG\)+Marine+Parade,+3225/data=!4m6!4m5!1m1!4e2!1m2!1m1!1s0x6d12d4205bc8e9c1:0xf00ef62249b71d0?sa=X&ved=2ahUKEwjtxe2HltyDAxWmr1YBHRLOBHMQ48ADegQIFhAA) and is available for weekend parking for everyone that missed out on an on site parking ticket, day parking for those staying off site or if you’re getting dropped off in Raglan. This year we are introducing booked arrival times for the off site parking shuttle.

Carpool / Share a ride

Car sharing is a fun, easy, cheap and sustainable way to travel! If you’re travelling to the festival by car, check with your friends or other festival goers to see if you can share a ride.

Transport to the Festival from Off site Parking

On site parking is limited and, once sold out, all campers will need to park at the off site park and catch the Raglan Airfield Bus to the festival.

This year we have staggered time slots available for the off site parking Raglan Airfield Bus so you can book your arrival time.

By booking your arrival time, you’ll be ensuring a smoother entry process for everyone which means more time to enjoy the festival.

You’ll only be able to check in to the festival once your designated time slot opens up. Make sure you know what time you’ll be arriving at the festival ahead of buying your ticket for a smooth ticket purchasing experience.

Drop Offs and Pick Ups

All Drop Offs and Pick Ups in Raglan will be at the off site parking site. Please make sure you have booked a Raglan Airfield Bus to the festival site. 

Auckland Road to Raglan Bus Drop Off and Pick up will be at Trusts Arena, Henderson, Auckland.

**NO DROP OFFS AT FESTIVAL SITE PLEASE – WE NEED TO KEEP THE ROAD CLEAR FOR EMERGENCY SERVICES.**

Auckland-Soundsplash return bus service

**Introducing the Road to Raglan Bus!**

Hop on board this **return bus service in Auckland and enjoy a hassle-free ride directly to the festival grounds in Raglan**. No driving required! These buses also have priority entry to the festival site from 9am – that’s before the festival gates open to shuttles from the off-site park.

1.  **Convenient return bus service from Auckland to Soundsplash in Raglan.**
2.  **Priority entry to the festival site from 9am – before the off site park shuttles!**
3.  **Perfect for parents – drop off your kids in Auckland.**
4.  **Skip the off-site parking experience and start the festival experience early.**

The buses will depart the Trusts Arena in Henderson, Auckland on Friday morning and return from Soundsplash on Sunday.

Entry will be staggered, and you’ll only be able to board your bus once your designated time slot opens up. Make sure you know what time you’ll be arriving for your bus ahead of buying your ticket for a smooth ticket purchasing experience.

**Important: During the ticket purchasing process, you will have the opportunity to select your desired bus times. It is essential to book both your departing and returning bus tickets at this time to ensure a smooth journey.**

Splash Bus: Hamilton - Soundsplash Return Bus Service

The Splash Bus is a return bus service that departs Caro St in Hamilton on Friday and returns on Sunday.

There will be two buses departing at 10am – please be ready to board.

The buses will depart from the Soundsplash site at 11am on Sunday morning back to Caro St Bus stop in Hamilton

Book Your Arrival Time via Bus

**Book your arrival time for Soundsplash!**

This year, when you purchase your tickets for Soundsplash, you’ll have the option to book your arrival time in 1-hour slots. This means you can plan your entry in advance, giving you more certainty around how long it will take to get into the festival.

If you are catching a bus or parking offsite (and camping), you will need to select your arrival and departure times when you order your festival and camping tickets.

Entry will be staggered, and you’ll only be able to enter once your designated time slot opens up.

Prior to your bus departure time, you can **check in one hour in advance.** For instance, if your bus is scheduled to depart at 7:00 am, you may check in anytime between 6:00 am and 7:00 am. In Auckland, the check-in process involves collecting your wristband and undergoing a bag search. In Raglan, it entails joining the queue to ensure timely boarding and departure.

Please note that if you fail to check in during your designated check-in time, the Soundsplash team will assist you in boarding the next available bus. However, we cannot guarantee that you will be allocated the subsequent bus slots.

Make sure you know what time you’ll be arriving at the festival ahead of buying your ticket for a smooth ticket purchasing experience.

Leaving on Sunday

**All Pick ups must be made at the Raglan Airfield Offsite Park.**

**We must keep the main road clear for emergency services so please do not drive to site for pick ups.**

Sunday at the festival is designated as a packdown day, and as such, no musical performances are scheduled. Please note that the gates will close to all attendees at 3pm on Sunday. The final Raglan Airfield Bus service returning from the festival to the offsite park is scheduled for 2pm.

Please make sure to leave the site with all your belongings by the designated time. 

Remember, ensuring a safe journey home is an integral part of your Soundsplash experience. Planning your safe return journey well in advance is essential, and it’s never too early to start making these arrangements.

For those travelling back to Auckland, the return bus will depart from the festival campgrounds and will head directly to the Trusts Arena in Auckland.

### **FAQ**

## Tickets

For answers to most ticketing questions head to the ticketing FAQ page [HERE](https://flicketltd.zendesk.com/hc/en-us).

BUYING TICKETS

Tickets available from [Flicket](https://soundsplash.flicket.co.nz/).

You can buy a maximum of 16 tickets in one order. Festival, Camping, Parking, Bus and Pre-pitched Tent tickets are all counted as separate tickets. For example, one person with Festival + Camping in Field of Joy + Onsite Parking would = 3 total tickets.

Please note that a booking fee of 4% applies to the total cost of your order.

FESTIVAL TICKETS

**If you are NOT camping onsite** at Soundsplash, simply purchase your festival admission ticket and Raglan Airfield Bus passes. Make sure to choose the correct age group for your ticket as we can not process swaps for incorrect ticket types.

**\+ YOUTH (16-17) Festival Ticket** – 1 x Youth 16-17 Festival Ticket (Photo ID required.)

**\+ ADULT 18+ FESTIVAL TICKET** – 1 x Adult 18+ Festival Ticket Photo ID required.

_**ALL CHILDREN AGED 15 YEARS AND UNDER MUST BE ACCOMPANIED BY AN ADULT GUARDIAN FESTIVAL TICKET HOLDER. MAX. 4 CHILDREN PER ADULT.**_

**\+ ADULT GUARDIAN 25+ FESTIVAL TICKET** – 1 x Adult Guardian 25+Festival Ticket Photo ID required.

**\+ CHILD 12 & UNDER FESTIVAL TICKET** – 1 x Child aged 12 years & under Festival Ticket 

**\+ GROM 13-15 FESTIVAL TICKET** – 1 x Child aged 13-15 Festival Ticket 

CAMPING PASSES

**If you are planning on camping at Soundsplash** you will need to purchase a camping pass to one of our camp zones as well as a festival ticket. Each person will need their own camping pass to access the camping zone. Please remember that there are no pass-outs for onsite campers.

Fields of Joy Camping Pass  
–  
Comfort Zone Camping Pass  
–  
Neighbourhood Camping Pass  
–  
TePee Village Camping Pass

–  
Road Trippers Camping Pass

(if staying in caravan, campervan, etc.)

**Family Camping Zones**

Family friendly camp zones are One Vibe and Road Trippers. All families staying with children aged 15 years & under will need to stay in these camp zones.

One Vibe Adult 25+ Camping Pass 

–

Road trippers  Camping Pass 

(if staying in caravan, campervan, etc.)

–

Child 12 & Under Camp pass 

Grom 13-15 Camp pass

TePee Life Village Pre-pitched tents

Tepee Life brings an amazing accommodation experience to Soundsplash!

We offer the funkiest, eco-friendly, alternative to pitching your own traditional nylon tent. Let us create the village for you to simply come and enjoy

The waterproof canvas Tepees come with built-in insect screens at all openings and adjustable air vents on top and bottom. Zipped doors that can accept a suitcase padlock and a built-in floor are 5m in diameter and suitable for up to six people.

Their high pitch roofs mean that even the tallest people can stand & stretch. Tepee Life Village Tents are available in either 2-person or 6-person tents.

**Tepee Inclusions**:

**This package includes –**

*   1x Camping Pass **ONLY** must select **additional Tepee life** camping passes for your friends. Up to 5 people for the Large Tepee Tent
*   1x Large Premium Tepee Life Tent zipped doors that can accept a suitcase padlock and a built-in floor are 3m in diameter and suitable for up to two people twin
*   Concierge check-in for you and your tenting friends
*   50mm festival foam single mattress for each person
*   A battery-powered light
*   Coffee Table
*   Thrash Towel for cleaning your feet
*   Access to the Tepee Life Village

Access to the Tepee Life Village Bring your own sleeping bag or duvet and your favourite pillow and whatever else you need to pimp out your tepee.

Parking

Onsite parking is limited and only available to onsite camp pass holders. If sold out or not camping onsite, add a free offsite parking pass and catch the Raglan Airfield Bus. Sleeping in cars is not permitted. If you are staying in Road Trippers, buy an onsite sleeper vehicle pass.

The drop-off and pick-up location will be at the Offsite Car Park  – there will be the Raglan Airfield Bus taking patrons to the event throughout the duration of the festival. It is vital that patrons are dropped off at the Offsite Car Park in order to ensure that the roads remain clear for emergency services.

_**Please note that when you leave your vehicle, you will need to grab all the items you need for your stay as once parked you won’t be able to access your vehicle until the end of your stay – unless it’s an emergency.**_

Onsite Standard vehicle pass: 

Onsite Sleeper STANDARD vehicle pass (Road Trippers only): 

Onsite Sleeper PLUS vehicle pass (Road Trippers only – space for a tent next to vehicle): 

Offsite parking: Raglan Airfield

WHERE'S MY TICKET?

Once you have completed purchasing all of your tickets, you will receive an email confirming your ticket purchase. To minimise fraud for Soundsplash 2027 there will be a print delay on all tickets so you will not receive your actual tickets until early **January 2027.**

You will receive your tickets via the registered email after this date.

DOES MY NAME NEED TO BE ON THE TICKET?

**Yes your name has to match the ticket and your ID.** 

If you want to change the name on your ticket you need to use the official name transfer system.

CAN I CHANGE THE NAME ON MY TICKET?

**Yes, you can change names on tickets. Any name change requests will be subject to an extra charge.**

Complimentary tickets MUST NOT be sold on, and will be canceled if this is done. If someone tries to sell you a comp. ticket, please let us know.

CAN I SELL MY TICKET?

[More Info here](https://flicketfaqs.groovehq.com/help/transferring-tickets)

CAN I ADD EXTRAS TO MY FESTIVAL TICKET?

If you have forgotten to add a pass or need support with ticket enquiries, email soundsplash@flicket.co.nz.

WILL THERE BE GATE SALES?

Gate sales won’t be available.

Going Cashless at Soundsplash

Soundsplash is a cashless event! Soundsplash will operate a digital currency for the festival to ensure speed of service, increased security and ease of transactions at the many bars, food outlets and vendor stalls. Most importantly, there will be reduced need to wait in lines.

When you arrive at the festival, your ticket will be swapped for a wristband which must remain on your wrist for the duration of the event. This wristband will act as your ‘digital wallet’ within the event site, as well as your ticket for remaining event days. You must not remove the wristband or your ticket will become void.

Online top ups are open now. After entering the festival, you will be able to load currency onto your wristband using either cash, debit or credit card at one of our top-up tents.

All food, drinks and merchandise purchased at the event will need to be paid for using the simple, tap-and-go wristbands.

1.  **Go to** [**https://my.wayver.co.nz**](https://my.wayver.co.nz/)

3.  **Select ‘IM GOING TO AN EVENT’ and enter your ticket number**
4.  **Complete the online payment to top up**

Refunds will be available after the event. Hold onto your wristband so you can enter your serial number for the refund.

## Arriving at Soundsplash

GATE TIMES

**This year we are introducing booked arrival times. Please check your tickets to see what time you have booked to arrive at Soundsplash.**

**Onsite Parking:** 8am -8pm

**Raglan Airfield Offsite Parking** : 9am – 8pm

**Trusts Arena Road to Raglan Bus:** 6am

**Festival gates:** 11am

Music usually runs from about 2pm to 1am.

If you are arriving by bus or via the Raglan Airfield Bus – make sure you check your ticket for the arrival time slot that you have booked.

Peak times are expected between 8am and 4pm as we process campers at the camping entrance.

**Please expect to wait in line as we check tickets**, ID and conduct bag searches. Soundsplash is an open-air festival and we expect the temps to be hot so come prepared with food, some water, a hat, sunscreen and good shoes.

**If you want to camp together, arrive together**

The best way to ensure you get to camp alongside your mates is to check in together at the gate.

WRISTBAND TOP UP

1.  **Go to** [**https://my.wayver.co.nz**](https://my.wayver.co.nz/)
2.  **Login with Facebook or create an account**
3.  **Select ‘IM GOING TO AN EVENT’ and enter your ticket number**

Refunds will be available after the event. Hold onto your wristband so that you can enter your serial number.

NO PASS-OUTS

There are no pass-outs for those that are camping on-site at Soundsplash except to access Ngarunui Beach. Once you enter the festival, all campers must stay onsite.

If you are not camping on-site, then you are able to leave and come back to the venue.

FOOD & DRINK

You are more than welcome to bring your own food. Drinks can be brought only in unopened cans. Bring an empty reusable bottle that can be refilled on-site with free water.

Chilly bins are also ok to bring but please don’t bring any single-use plastics or unsealed plastic bag packaging. All food packaging must be sealed (be mindful to use biodegradable packaging as much as possible).  Any contraband found in food, all will be confiscated.

Bags will be searched on entry and contraband items will be confiscated.

No cooking in the camp grounds please. Hot food, drinks and liquids can be purchased from the Kai Village. If your campervan/caravan has a gas cooker attached that will be fine but please don’t bring standalone portable gas cookers.

TOILETRIES

All beauty and hygiene products will need to be in containers 50ml in size or smaller – anything larger will be confiscated during the bag search. Please do not bring large bottles of perfume or cologne as these will be confiscated.

Mirrors that are attached to compacts and palettes will be ok to bring but please do not bring stand alone mirrors. We recommend bringing items like soap and shampoo bars.

The General Store will have toiletries available for purchase as well.

DON’T FORGET

Your tickets & valid ID!

A good-quality, waterproof tent + comfortable bedding and sleeping gear

Warm clothes, some covered shoes, raincoat and gumboots ( if needed)

Sunnies, togs, towel, hat and sunblock

Hygiene items and medication (and prescription too – please have these prepared so you can show security during the bag search)

Your reusable bags, cups, bottles, containers and cutlery

The most important thing is to keep an open heart and bring the good vibes!

LEAVE AT HOME

No alcohol of any kind to be bought on site. Please leave at home.

Illegal drugs or substances: Please don’t bring.

Gas bottles, cookers and barbecues: A fire ban is in place. No cooking or fires at Soundsplash please there’s plenty of yummy food available at the Kai Village

Glass: Very dangerous at Soundsplash so please leave at home. That means mirrors  and perfume bottles too folks.

Tent hammers and mallets. These items will be available onsite for you to use so please don’t bring your own as these will be confiscated during the bag search.

Objects that could harm others: Nothing that can cut, hit or generally be used to harm anybody please. This includes fireworks. Safety first.

Filled bottles: sealed or otherwise, all filled bottles will be emptied during the bag search. Free water stations are available throughout the site.

No fireworks. No fires. No generators. No glass.

**Searches will be carried out at both festival and campground entry points, and items will be confiscated and not returned. To avoid unnecessary delays at the entrance please see our festival terms and conditions for the full conditions of entry.**

If you’re not sure about an item then flick us a message at info@soundsplash.co.nz.
